geometric class need not persist. The exact history decomposition retains
the terms created when ordering fails. The PDE and interval arguments here
are analytic, not new Lean theorems.

### Positive propagators retain the nonlinear parent history

Continue with the preceding axisymmetric whole-space variables. Assume
reflection symmetry about z=0: b and u_r are even in z, u_z is odd, and
eta=omega_theta/r is odd. These parities are preserved by uniqueness of
the smooth unforced NS evolution. Smoothness at the axis and sufficient
decay justify the integrals below. Let

```text
D=R4 times (0,infinity),  beta(r)=1-zeta_rho(r),
f=beta b^2,  F=|b|^(5/2),
(partial_t+v.grad-nu Delta5)eta_core=partial_z f,
eta_core(0)=0,  eta_core|_(z=0)=0.
```

On each available smooth prefix, let U_v(t,s) be the Dirichlet propagator
of `nu Delta5-v.grad` on D with this same complete meridional drift.
The maximum principle makes U_v positive; no bound on its operator norm
or on future drift derivatives is inferred. In particular, this is not
the heat propagator and does not remove parent transport.

Let K_D be the Dirichlet inverse of -Delta5 on D. Its kernel is

```text
G5(X-Y)-G5(X-Y_reflected),  G5(X)=1/(8pi^2 |X|^3).
```

It is positive for X,Y in D because reflection increases their distance.
The full-space potential of an odd function restricts to K_D. Thus
the actual nonlocal reconstruction and history are

```text
q_core=2partial_z K_D eta_core,
eta_core(t)=integral_0^t U_v(t,s) partial_z f(s) ds.
```

The full-space production is consequently

```text
Pcrit_core(t)
 =-4 integral_0^t <partial_z F(t),K_D U_v(t,s) partial_z f(s)>_D ds. (15)
```

The factor four includes the two reflected half-spaces and the factor
two in q_core. The integration-by-parts boundary term vanishes because
K_D eta_core has zero trace at z=0. The receiver F(t) is the actual
evolving swirl at the observation time; it is not frozen at time zero.

Equivalently, full-space adjoint duality uses
`-psi_t=nu Delta5 psi+div5(v psi)+h`, `psi(T)=0`. Here `div5(v)=-q`
must be retained. With `h=w(t)*(-2partial_z K5)F`, it gives
`integral w Pcrit_core=-integral f psi_z`. The checker verifies the
complete local identity, including its diffusive and transport fluxes.

### Ordered histories deplete the critical moment

Suppose `partial_z(b^2)<=0` on D throughout the prefix. Since beta is
nonnegative and radial, the source derivative is nonpositive. Positivity
of U_v implies eta_core<=0, and positivity of K_D then implies
K_D eta_core<=0. The receiver has the same derivative sign, since

```text
partial_z |b|^(5/2)=(5/4)|b|^(1/2) partial_z(b^2).
```

Equation (15) gives `Pcrit_core<=0`. This controls the entire generated
history, including full parent transport and elliptic response. It does
not require small swirl or small drift.

Combining this sign with the preceding paid-parent factor w leaves the
entire critical diffusion available:

```text
(w M)' +(15nu/4)w Dcrit<=0,
integral_0^T S^2 <=(5C5/(12nu))*exp(36M_H/5)*M(0)^(12/5).       (16)
```

Thus persistence of the stated geometric ordering supplies the sufficient
axisymmetric continuation bound. For initially pure swirl one may instead
use beta=1 and the full generated eta, with no paid class: then w=1,
M_H=0 and M itself is nonincreasing while the ordering persists. The same
argument allows initially nonpositive eta on D. These are conditional
physical implications, not a proof that arbitrary initial order persists.

### Which departures from ordering can produce positive work?

Formula (15) also applies without axial monotonicity. Put
`d=partial_z F`, `j=partial_z f`, and split each into positive and negative
parts, `d=d_+-d_-`, `j=j_+-j_-`. For a,b in {+,-}, define

```text
C_ab(t)=integral_0^t <d_a(t),K_D U_v(t,s) j_b(s)>_D ds >=0.
```

The exact identity is

```text
Pcrit_core=4(C_{+,-}+C_{-,+}-C_{+,+}-C_{-,-}).                (17)
```

Matching derivative signs deplete this moment; opposite signs at the
source and its later receiver can increase it. The spatial coupling and
the complete intervening drift remain inside K_D U_v. This is a signed
comparison of compatible histories, not a sum of independent bursts.

In this reflection-symmetric class, the current open allowance is exactly

```text
integral_0^T w[6(C_{+,-}+C_{-,+}-C_{+,+}-C_{-,-})-(15nu/8)Dcrit]
 <= K(u0,nu,H,rho).                                          (18)
```

The negative terms in (18) may matter; discarding them gives a stronger
and still unproved target. No initial bound for (18) is supplied here.

### Initial ordering can fail through internally generated pressure

For n=b_z, differentiating the actual swirl equation and using
incompressibility gives

```text
n_t+v.grad n-nu Delta5 n
 =-(r/2)q_r n+q_z(b+(r/2)b_r).                               (19)
```

The last factor is half the axial vorticity. The term involving q_z is
not sign-controlled by n<=0. The following datum makes it strictly
positive at a flat part of the initial profile, without external force.

Choose a nonnegative smooth a(r), nonzero and supported in 4<r<5.
Choose h(z) smooth and even, equal to one for |z|<=1, zero for |z|>=2,
with h'<0 on (1,2). Set

```text
b0(r,z)=[a(r)+delta exp(-r^2/2)]h(z),
u0=(-x2 b0,x1 b0,0),                        delta>0.
```

This is a Schwartz divergence-free pure swirl with initially nonincreasing
b0^2 on D. Evaluate at r=0,z0=1/2. Initially the meridional velocity is
zero and
`sigma=q_t(0)=2partial_zz K5(b0^2)`, independent of viscosity. Write
`B(r)=a(r)+delta exp(-r^2/2)` and `g(R,w)=(R^2+w^2)^(-3/2)`. Moving one
axial derivative to h^2 gives the nonsingular formula

```text
sigma_z(0,z0)
 =(1/2)integral_0^infinity R^3 B(R)^2 integral_1^2 (h^2)'(s)
     [g_ww(R,s-z0)-g_ww(R,s+z0)] ds dR,
g_www(R,w)=15w(3R^2-4w^2)/(R^2+w^2)^(9/2).
```

For 4<=R<=5 and 1/2<=w<=5/2, `3R^2-4w^2>=23`. Thus g_ww increases
strictly across this interval. The bracket is negative, whereas (h^2)'
is negative. The annular term and the annulus/Gaussian cross term in
sigma_z are both strictly positive.

Let A>0 be the annular contribution and D the absolute Gaussian-only
contribution. Both are finite. Choosing `delta=A/[2(A+D)]` gives

```text
sigma_z[full datum]>=A-delta^2 D>=15A/16>0.
```

This fixes a single smooth datum. Its local axial flatness gives
`n(0)=n_t(0)=0` near the test point: all initial axial diffusion terms
vanish there. Differentiating (19) once in time then yields

```text
n_tt(0,0,1/2)=delta*sigma_z(0,1/2)>0.                         (20)
```

For every fixed nu>0, local smooth NS existence and time differentiability
therefore give n(t,0,1/2)>0 for all sufficiently small positive times.
Continuity gives a neighboring region of increasing b^2 as well. This
is an actual interval argument from a strict initial second derivative;
it assumes no viscosity-free evolution or long Taylor window.

The example refutes preservation of initial axial ordering. It does not
refute the conditional sign theorem, the signed compensation in (18),
a finite original-datum allowance, or regularity. In particular, newly
positive cross terms need not dominate the remaining negative work.
The annulus can be placed within any prescribed core radius by NS spatial
rescaling. The underlying profile may change while its total signed work
remains paid; a quantitative history estimate must allow that possibility.

Indeed this same example has favorable **net** production initially.
Use the full source beta=1; the entire meridional parent starts at zero.
Both `d0=partial_z F0` and `j0=partial_z(b0^2)` are nonpositive on D
and nonzero on sets of positive measure. Strict positivity of K_D gives

```text
Pcrit'(0)=-4<d0,K_D j0>_D<0.
```

Hence Pcrit(t)<0 on a sufficiently short positive interval, and the
complete moment M decreases there. During that same interval the axial
ordering is already broken near the test point. Persistent pointwise
ordering is therefore stronger than the signed payment actually needed.
Controlling the compensation in (18), rather than forbidding every
geometric departure, remains a viable and distinct question.

Run `python3 -O labs/swirl_order_history.py --quadrature`. Exact checks
cover the local equations, complete initial second derivative, full adjoint
flux, Green derivatives, kernel normalization and algebraic margins.
The optional quadrature uses `a(r)=exp[4-1/((r-4)(5-r))]` on (4,5),
zero outside, and `h(s)=1/[1+exp(1/(2-s)-1/(s-1))]` on (1,2), with
the stated plateau, zero extension and reflection. The 64/96/128-point
quadratures give `n_tt(0)` approximately
`0.0003070871013`. It supports the kernel calculation and has no certified
quadrature error; it is not a numerical evolution. Propagator positivity,
PDE existence, physical interval and continuation claims remain analytic.

## Critical parent exchange and the initial allowance it requires

`critical_parent_exchange.py` tests a reserve containing both swirl and
its actual meridional parents at the critical exponent. Its diffusion is
positive and controls the continuation clock. The complete nonlinear
exchange leaves explicit pressure and transport defects. A localized pure
swirl shows that a reserve dominating the critical moment cannot be
automatically nonincreasing if it assigns no extra allowance to any
initially pure swirl. This concerns zero allowance, not the open signed
full-datum budget or indefinite renewal.

### Retaining the actual parent energy at the critical exponent

For a smooth axisymmetric whole-space evolution with the stated
integrability, set

```text
L=(-Delta5)^(-1/2),  h=L eta,  chi=L h,
R_z=partial_z L,    q=2R_z h,
X=b^2+h^2,         Phi=X^(p/2),  W=X^((p-2)/2),
R_p=integral_R5 Phi,             p=5/2.
```

The fractional operators use their homogeneous Fourier multipliers and
the canonical decaying reconstruction. They retain the signed actual eta;
h is not an independently chosen parent. Plancherel and the earlier radial
energy identity give

```text
integral_R5 (b^2+h^2)=pi ||u||_L2(R3)^2.
```

The nonlinear reserve R_(5/2) dominates M, is nonnegative and has invariant
NS spatial scaling. It is finite initially from physical data. For example,
with E_m the meridional kinetic square and Z_m its vorticity square,

```text
integral_R5 |h0|^(5/2)
 <= C5^(5/8) (pi E_m(0))^(5/8) (pi Z_m(0))^(5/8),
R_(5/2)(0)<=2^(1/4)[M(0)+integral_R5 |h0|^(5/2)].
```

Here five-dimensional Sobolev bounds h in L(10/3), interpolation gives
L(5/2), and `||grad h||_2=||eta||_2`. The reserve uses a nonlinear moment
of the joint lifted amplitude. Its h component is nonlocal in physical
space; the quadratic integral, rather than its pointwise density, is
identified with the physical meridional kinetic energy.

### The full evolving-weight identity

Use the commutator convention `[A,B]=AB-BA`. Applying L to the actual
parent equation gives

```text
h_t+v.grad h-nu Delta5 h=L partial_z(b^2)-C,
C=[L,v.grad]eta.
```

The actual streamfunction satisfies `div5(v chi)=0`. Consequently

```text
<h,C>=-(1/2)integral q h^2.
```

Indeed `<h,L(v.grad eta)>=<chi,v.grad eta>=0` by integration by parts,
whereas `<h,v.grad h>=(1/2)integral q h^2`. This is the meridional
kinetic cancellation and uses the physical relation between v and eta.

At a nonconstant W define

```text
T_W=<W h,C>+(1/2)integral q W h^2,
Q_p=((p-2)/2)integral q Phi
       -p<b^2,[R_z,W]h>-p T_W.
```

The complete chain rule yields

```text
R_p' +nu D_p=Q_p,
D_p=integral p W(|grad b|^2+|grad h|^2)
        +p(p-2)X^((p-4)/2)|b grad b+h grad h|^2.               (21)
```

The second integrand is defined by continuity at X=0. For p>=2 the
diffusion is nonnegative. The derivation differentiates Phi in both
evolving components; W is not frozen, and no additional time-weight term
has been dropped. Source transfer is paired using
`R_z(W h)=W q/2+[R_z,W]h`. At p=2, W=1, T_1=0 and Q_2=0, recovering
literal unforced kinetic-energy dissipation. At p=5/2, neither the two
commutator terms nor the remaining `(1/4)integral q Phi` has a claimed
favorable sign.

Since `D_(5/2)>=(5/2)Dcrit` and `R_(5/2)>=M`, a bound K fixed from
the original datum, nu and H, valid on every available prefix T<=H,

```text
integral_0^T Q_(5/2)<=(nu/2)integral_0^T D_(5/2)+K
```

would imply

```text
integral_0^T S^2
 <=(5C5/(4nu)) [R_(5/2)(0)+K]^(12/5).                        (22)
```

This is another explicit sufficient axisymmetric consumer. The signed
Q allowance is open. The original critical-moment history target remains
available; (21) does not establish that this alternative is easier.

### Pure swirl can replenish the critical moment itself

An exact profile tests the missing allowance at its starting state. Put

```text
y=r^2, p0(y)=-120+49y-4y^2, Q(y)=(p0(y)-30)^2+31,
qrad=r^10 exp(-r^2),  hrad=r^8 exp(-r^2)p0,
F=r^8 exp(-r^2)Q^4.
```

Here `(1-Delta_R4)qrad=hrad`. Also Q>=31 and Q>|p0|, so
`|hrad|/F<=31^-3`. The temporary axially periodic source is
`f=F+hrad cos z`, b=sqrt(f). Its generated initial strain is
`sigma=q_t(0)=-2qrad cos z`.

For the critical receiver `b^(5/2)=f^(5/4)`, the phase average is
controlled by the exact radial moment

```text
J=integral_0^infinity r^3 qrad F^(1/4) hrad dr
 =(1/2)integral_0^infinity y^11 exp(-9y/4) Q(y)p0(y) dy
 =-1500298173892001792000/205891132094649.
```

Let A be the same polynomial integral with each coefficient of Qp0
replaced by its absolute value; this bounds the integral with |hrad|.
Taylor expansion of `(1+x)^(5/4)` through degree two, with
`|x|<=epsilon0=31^-3`, gives a phase-averaged remainder bounded by
`(15/512)epsilon0^2 A`. The quadratic term times cos z averages to zero.
The complete negative phase margin is therefore at least

```text
m=-(5/8)J-(15/512)epsilon0^2 A
 =832198796201609419506581504000/182729137619258227902969 >0.   (23)
```

The bound uses `|(d^3/dx^3)(1+x)^(5/4)|/6
 <=(5/128)(1-epsilon0)^(-7/4)<5/64` and the mean of cos^4, which is 3/8.
Thus it retains the entire fractional power, not only its linearization.

### Whole-space localization and the actual viscous interval

Localize with

```text
f_L=exp(-z^2/L^2)(F+hrad cos z),
b0=sqrt(f_L),  u0=(-x2 b0,x1 b0,0).
```

Each finite L gives a smooth Schwartz divergence-free pure swirl. With
`A5=-partial_zz(-Delta5)^(-1)`, partial Fourier transformation in z gives
the operator family `A_xi=xi^2(-Delta_R4+xi^2)^(-1)`. It is bounded by
one on L2(R4), strongly continuous at xi=0 with A_0=0, and continuous
at xi=1 and -1. For the fixed radial profiles, dominated convergence
on the three Fourier packets at 0,1,-1 proves

```text
||A5 f_L-exp(-z^2/L^2)qrad cos z||_L2(R5)/sqrt(L) ->0.
```

The L2 norm of `f_L^(5/4)/sqrt(L)` stays bounded. Cauchy--Schwarz and
periodic averaging therefore give, for the actual full-space response,

```text
I_L=integral_R5 b0^(5/2) q_t(0),
lim_(L->infinity) I_L/L >=4pi^2 sqrt(4pi/9) m>0.              (24)
```

The Gaussian exponent is 9/4: it includes both the receiver's 5/4 and
the strain's additional factor one. This proves I_L>0 for all sufficiently
large finite L. It is an analytic localization argument, not an explicit
numerical bound on the necessary L.

Fix one such finite datum and any viscosity nu>0. Amplify its velocity
by A and write `u_A(t)=A v_epsilon(A t)`, `epsilon=nu/A`. Uniform local
high Sobolev estimates for `epsilon in [0,1]` give C2 time dependence
of b into L(5/2)(R5). To see the lifted integrability, its L2 norm is
sqrt(pi) times the physical swirl L2 norm, and its supremum is controlled by a
physical velocity derivative; the same applies to its first two time
derivatives. One further velocity time-jet bound supplies a common time
modulus for these quantities. The L(5/2) power functional is C2. Thus the
following Taylor expansion has a remainder uniform in epsilon:

```text
M_epsilon'(0)=-(15epsilon/4)Dcrit,0,
M_epsilon''(0)=(3/2)I_L+O(epsilon^2),
M_epsilon(k epsilon)-M0
 =epsilon^2[(3/4)I_L k^2-(15/4)Dcrit,0 k]+o(epsilon^2).
```

At the initial pure swirl the velocity's nonlinear meridional acceleration
produces I_L, while b_t(0)=epsilon Delta5 b0. This accounts for all viscous
terms in the initial jet. No third-derivative bound is assumed for the
fractional-power functional. Choose `k=10Dcrit,0/I_L`; the positive
coefficient becomes `75Dcrit,0^2/(2I_L)`. Hence for sufficiently large A,
at the actual time `t=k nu/A^2`,

```text
M(u_A(t))>M(u_A(0)).                                        (25)
```

This is a finite actual-unforced burst. It asserts no indefinite renewal
or blowup and does not defeat a full-datum allowance.

There is also a fixed rescaled interval. The same uniform continuity
gives tau_*>0 and epsilon_*>0 such that
`M_epsilon''>=(3/4)I_L` on `[0,tau_*]` for `epsilon<=epsilon_*`.
If also `epsilon<=I_L tau_*/(20Dcrit,0)`, integrating this inequality twice
gives

```text
M_epsilon(tau_*)-M0 >=(3/16)I_L tau_*^2,
M(u_A(tau_*/A))-M(u_A(0)) >=c_* A^(5/2),
c_*=(3/16)I_L tau_*^2>0.                                    (26)
```

The constants here are fixed from the unamplified profile; viscosity is
fixed and positive in the actual flow. For all sufficiently large A,
the interval lies below any prescribed positive horizon. This gives a
quantitative necessary allowance of the same amplitude order as M(u_A(0)).

### What the reserve must include initially

Suppose a proposed state or compatible-history reserve dominates M and
equals M initially on every pure-swirl datum. If it were nonincreasing
along every unforced evolution, (25) would imply

```text
M(u_A(t))<=R(u_A(t))<=R(u_A(0))=M(u_A(0)),
```

a contradiction. In particular R_(5/2) from (21) fails automatic
monotonicity, since its parent h is initially zero. The conclusion also
applies to any other nonnegative parent correction vanishing on every
pure swirl, regardless of its particular norm.

A successful dominating reserve must give some of these initial states
an additional allowance for future parent generation, or use a separately
funded signed history cost. This is consistent with an initially allocated
Bellman reserve. By (26), its initial excess on this family must be at
least `c_* A^(5/2)`. This does not refute a finite allowance proportional
to the initial critical moment, show that the necessary allowance is
infinite, or justify further zero-allowance variants of the same test.

Run `python3 -O labs/critical_parent_exchange.py --quadrature`. Exact checks
cover kinetic compatibility, convex diffusion, exchange algebra, rational
phase margins and viscous scaling. Optional radial orders 32/64/96 with
512 phase samples give the negative phase pairing approximately
`-4554282.397419`; this is supporting quadrature, not an error certificate.
The fractional-operator identities, localization, actual interval and
continuation implications remain analytic. No new Lean theorem is claimed.

## A funded critical-history test with bounded coarse resources

`funded_critical_history.py` uses the preceding positive critical burst to
test an allowance that is nonzero initially. The result concerns the
actual signed critical-moment budget, rather than a raw higher moment or
zero-allowance monotonicity. All fluid existence, separation, concentration
and entropy arguments in this section are analytic. The checker verifies
scaling and scalar bookkeeping; it does not certify the PDE limits.

Fix a positive viscosity nu and horizon H. Write

```text
M=int_R5 |b|^(5/2), Dcrit=int_R5 |b|^(1/2)|grad b|^2,
Pcrit=int_R5 q|b|^(5/2),
J(T)=int_0^T [(3/2)Pcrit-(15nu/8)Dcrit].
```

The exact physical balance gives

```text
J(T)=M(T)-M(0)+(15nu/8)int_0^T Dcrit.                       (27)
```

In particular a positive moment increment is a lower bound for J. A bound
`J(T)<=K` would give `M(T)+(15nu/8)int Dcrit<=M(0)+K`: it already includes
the ENTIRE initial critical moment. The question here is whether a further
allowance based only on the displayed coarse resources can pay J.

### The actual-flow separation step

The previous construction supplies one fixed smooth Schwartz pure-swirl
datum u_* and an actual unforced interval [0,t_*] at this viscosity with

```text
delta=M(u_*(t_*))-M(u_*(0))>0.
```

This base is fixed before choosing the number N of packets. For each finite
even N, translate its initial velocity to axial centers a_j in symmetric
pairs, separated by at least R, and sum. For example use centers
`+/-R,+/-2R,...,+/-(N/2)R`. The base and background are even in z, so the
result also retains the reflection symmetry of the signed-order-history test.
The resulting datum is still smooth, Schwartz, divergence free and pure
swirl. As R tends to infinity, its actual evolution satisfies

```text
M(u_N(t_*))-M(u_N(0)) -> N delta.                            (28)
```

Here and below a sufficiently large finite separation is selected; an
infinite collection of independently evolved packets is not a solution.
To justify (28), use the sum V_R of the N translated ACTUAL base solutions
only as an approximate solution. Its projected NS residual is exactly

```text
P sum_(j!=k) [u_*(x-a_j).grad]u_*(x-a_k).
```

For any fixed integer m>=4 this residual tends to zero in H^m uniformly
on [0,t_*]. Products of separated translated H^(m+1) fields tend to zero
in H^m; uniformity follows from compactness of the base trajectory in that
space. The Leray projection is bounded on H^m, so the nonlocal pressure
has not been omitted. The H^m norm of V_R is at most N times a fixed base
bound, which may depend on N but not R. The difference equation, viscous
energy estimate and Gronwall bootstrap therefore construct an actual
solution on this entire interval, approaching V_R in H^m as R increases.
No uniform-in-N local existence time is being inferred from a growing
global Sobolev norm.

For an axisymmetric difference field w, the swirl quotient satisfies

```text
||w_theta/r||_L2(R5)^2=pi ||w_theta||_L2(R3)^2,
||w_theta/r||_infinity<=C||grad w||_infinity.
```

Interpolation and H^m Sobolev embedding give continuity into L(5/2)(R5).
Finally Lp integrals of finitely many separated translates become additive.
This proves (28) for the actual moment, including the generated parents.
Choose R=R_N so the increment is at least `3N delta/4` and the initial
moment differs from N times the base moment by at most `N delta/8`.

The initial profiles also have a uniform circulation maximum. Their axial
Gaussian envelope has width L, fixed by the base. For R>=4L,

```text
sup_z sum_j exp(-(z-(a_j)_z)^2/(2L^2)) <=3/2.
```

Indeed the non-nearest terms are bounded by exp(-2n) on each side, using
`(n-1/2)^2>=n/4`, and exp(2)>=5. The radial envelope is fixed. Thus
`||r u_N,theta(0)||_infinity<=G_*` with G_* independent of N and R_N.
Larger separation also bounds any fixed number of initial derivatives
by the corresponding wider Gaussian envelope, although that uniform
derivative bound is not needed for the preceding H^m stability argument.

### Concentration on a fixed background

Choose a fixed positive Gaussian pure swirl u_B, with b_B(y)=B exp(-|y|^2/2)
and circulation maximum G_B>G_*. It has a smooth actual local evolution.
For the chosen finite packet datum define

```text
u_(N,lambda)(0,x)=u_B(0,x)+lambda u_N(0,lambda x).
```

NS scaling preserves viscosity, M and the time-integrated quantities in
(27). It reduces packet kinetic energy by lambda^-1, and reduces both
its lifted source mass and every finite physical circulation moment by
lambda^-3. Its circulation maximum stays bounded by G_*.

The actual flow exists to `T_lambda=t_*/lambda^2` for sufficiently large
lambda, and

```text
M(u_(N,lambda)(T_lambda))-M(u_(N,lambda)(0))
  -> M(u_N(t_*))-M(u_N(0)).                                 (29)
```

The background is not simply added to a nonlinear solution. In rescaled
coordinates it is `B_lambda(s,y)=lambda^-1 u_B(s/lambda^2,y/lambda)`.
Its W^(m+1,infinity) norm tends to zero. Use the actual u_N+B_lambda as
an approximate solution. Its cross residual tends to zero in H^m: in
each product the background is bounded in W^(m+1,infinity), and u_N in
H^(m+1). The difference energy estimate uses the background's bounded
derivatives and divergence cancellation, not its growing rescaled L2 norm.
Consequently the actual rescaled error tends to zero in H^m on [0,t_*].

For M, the rescaled background quotient is lambda^-2 b_B(s/lambda^2,y/lambda).
It converges pointwise to zero, with bounded L(5/2) norm. The Lp splitting
lemma (or its elementary truncation proof) separates its moment from the
fixed packet field. Its own moment increment tends to zero as physical
time tends to zero. This and the preceding quotient estimate prove (29).
Both approximation steps retain all nonlinear outputs of a single actual
unforced evolution.

For each N choose a finite lambda_N large enough that T_N<=H and

```text
M(T_N)-M(0)>=N delta/2,
J(T_N)>=N delta/2.                                         (30)
```

At the same time the initial coarse resources can be made arbitrarily
close to those of this ONE fixed background:

```text
E0 -> E_B,
C_p(0)=int_R3 |r u_theta(0)|^p -> C_p,B  (any fixed finite list p>=1),
G0=||r u_theta(0)||_infinity -> G_B,
M1=int_R5 b0 -> M1,B>0.
```

The energy conclusion follows from L2 convergence of the added velocity.
Finite circulation moments follow from Lp convergence of its circulation.
For the maximum, the concentrated packet circulation is supported near
r=0 up to a uniformly Gaussian radial tail, where the background circulation
vanishes quadratically. Outside a small axis tube the packet tail tends to
zero. Since G_B>G_*, the maximum tends to G_B as well. The choices are
sequential: fix N, choose R_N, then choose lambda_N. No unproved uniform
separation rate is required.

### The already-paid entropy and action do not repair this allowance

The nonnegative source b0 has a fixed positive background mass. Normalize
it to rho0 and use the standard Gaussian gamma on R5 as reference, exactly
the normalized background. Let m_*=int5 b_*(0), and let K_* be the base
source's finite relative entropy to gamma. The base is even, so it has
zero mean. Entropy convexity and translation/dilation give

```text
theta=N m_* / (lambda^3 M1,B+N m_*),
KL(rho0||gamma)
 <= theta [K_*+(1/(2N))sum_j |a_j|^2+5 log lambda]
 ->0  as lambda->infinity for each fixed N.                 (31)
```

For the dilation formula the omitted term is
`(lambda^-2-1)int |y|^2 rho_N/2<=0`. Thus lambda_N can also be chosen
so that initial KL tends to zero along the sequence. The actual source
action and entropy allowances established earlier remain uniformly bounded:
their constants depend only on G0, E0, M1, nu, H and this initial entropy.

### A precise failure of a funded budget

There is no upper bound for J depending only on these displayed coarse
initial resources through a function locally bounded at their background
values. They converge to one fixed finite vector while (30) tends to
infinity. This refutes such an EXTRA allowance even when the full M(0)
is already included separately in the energy ledger. A positive constant
allowance, or the previously funded scalar entropy/action reserve, does
not remove the obstruction.

This assertion concerns uniform dependence on the listed resources, not
arbitrary discontinuous encodings in exact scalar values. The initial
critical moment itself grows linearly in N. An extra allowance comparable
to M(0), a finer critical source resource, or full-datum dependence is
not refuted. Each example consists of finitely many prepared bursts;
there is no infinite renewal from one datum or blowup claim.

### The paid-parent subtraction leaves the same obstruction

Fix the original radial cutoff rho>0. Every initial datum above is pure
swirl, so eta(0)=0. The earlier paid-parent history estimate, on its
original prefix [0,T], gives the stronger short-time bound

```text
int_0^T ||q_paid||_infinity
 <=2 C_BS T^(3/4)(2nu)^(-1/4) sqrt(T C4(0)/(3nu rho^8))
 =C(nu,rho) sqrt(C4(0)) T^(5/4).
```

This does not restart the history split or its resource. Its original
source cutoff is unchanged. Since w=exp[-(3/2)int_0^t ||q_paid||_infinity],
`1-w(T)<=C'(nu,rho)sqrt(C4(0))T^(5/4)`. For each fixed N, (29) bounds
M(T_lambda) as lambda grows, so the loss `(1-w(T_lambda))M(T_lambda)`
tends to zero. Enlarge lambda_N until it is at most `N delta/4`.

The exact core balance therefore gives

```text
int_0^T w[(3/2)Pcrit_core-(15nu/8)Dcrit]
 >=w(T)M(T)-M(0)+(15nu/8)int_0^T w Dcrit
 >=N delta/4.                                               (32)
```

Thus a bounded coarse allowance fails for the current signed CORE budget
as well. Reflection symmetry is preserved by uniqueness, so equivalently
the left side of (32) is

```text
int_0^T w[6(C_{+,-}+C_{-,+}-C_{+,+}-C_{-,-})-(15nu/8)Dcrit].
```

The matching-sign histories have not been dropped. This addresses the
net history target after removing the already-paid parents, with the
same fixed positive viscosity, horizon and radial cutoff.

### Continuous energy/circulation corrections cannot spend this stock

There is a related state-reserve obstruction, even with one fixed packet
pair. At the short times T_lambda in (29), the endpoint kinetic energy and circulation
moments converge to the SAME background values as their initial values.
This needs an actual PDE argument, since initial convergence alone is
insufficient.

For compactly supported solenoidal velocity tests, the weak momentum
equation bounds the change by T_lambda times a constant depending only
on the test, nu and the uniformly bounded kinetic energy. Pressure drops
by solenoidality. Thus endpoint velocities converge weakly to u_B(0).
Weak lower semicontinuity and the unforced energy inequality sandwich
their squared norms between the same limit E_B.

Likewise, for circulation tests supported away from the axis,

```text
d_t int Gamma phi = int Gamma v.grad phi+nu int Gamma L5 phi.
```

The uniform circulation maximum and physical kinetic energy bound this
rate independently of the concentrated derivatives. Since T_lambda->0,
endpoint circulation converges weakly to Gamma_B. Its nonincreasing
Lp moments and maximum, together with lower semicontinuity, give the same
limits C_p,B and G_B. The positive source mass is conserved. If initial
KL is included, the earlier entropy inequality gives
`KL(rho(T_lambda)||gamma(T_lambda))<=KL(rho0||gamma)+C T_lambda`,
so this value tends to zero too; the reference heat variance tends to one.

Consequently a reserve

```text
R(t)=M(t)+F(E(t),C_p1(t),...,C_pk(t),G(t),M1,KL(t))
```

with F continuous at the fixed background vector has a strictly positive
increment for all sufficiently large finite lambda in that fixed-pair
construction. F may be nonnegative and initially nonzero. It cannot make
R nonincreasing, because its initial and terminal values approach the
same number while the critical moment has a fixed positive increment.
This tests a funded state correction, not only an initially empty one.

The remaining reserve must retain critical initial structure and an actual
mechanism for spending it during parent generation. The original signed
history target remains open; this result does not supply that mechanism.
Run `python3 -O labs/funded_critical_history.py` for the exact scaling,
Gaussian packing arithmetic, entropy limit and signed-budget bookkeeping.

## A critical allowance for the original caloric parent history

`critical_caloric_allowance.py` supplies a nonzero initial allowance for
one complete source/receiver history and retains its exact difference from
the actual fluid. The allowance is critical under NS scaling and covers
all positive times, rather than one local Taylor interval. The remaining
source deformation, receiver deformation and parent transport are explicit
and unpaid. This is an analytic partial payment, not an arbitrary-data
regularity theorem or a new Lean-certified PDE statement.

### The prepared history retains its original source and clock

Fix nu>0, p=5/2 and the original swirl quotient b0 in Lp(R5), with the
smoothness and decay used in the actual-flow application. Set

```text
M0=int_R5 |b0|^p,
B(t)=exp(nu t Delta5)b0,
A5=-partial_zz(-Delta5)^(-1),
q1(t)=-2 A5 int_0^t exp(nu(t-s)Delta5)[beta B(s)^2] ds.
```

For the physical core split beta=1-zeta_rho is its original smooth radial
cutoff. The bound itself only needs a fixed measurable 0<=beta<=1.
The parent q1 contains the complete time history of this diffusing source,
followed by the canonical pressure reconstruction. It is not a new
independently prescribed strain or an actual nonlinear solution by itself.

Let C_R be a fixed L(5/2)(R5) norm bound for A5. Its Fourier symbol is
xi_z^2/|xi|^2; the standard Riesz-transform Lp bound makes C_R finite.
The Gaussian heat kernel and Young's inequality give

```text
||exp(t Delta5)||_(L(5/4)->L(5/2)) <= A/t,
||exp(t Delta5)||_(L(5/2)->L5) <= Bc/sqrt(t),
A=(4pi)^(-1)(5/3)^(-3/2),
Bc=(4pi)^(-1/2)(5/4)^(-2).
```

Split the parent time integral at t/2. On [0,t/2], put the heat smoothing
on the output and use `||B(s)^2||_(5/4)<=M0^(4/5)`. On [t/2,t], use
Lp contraction on the output and smooth the source instead:
`||B(s)^2||_(5/2)<=Bc^2 M0^(4/5)/(nu s)`. The two integrals are
`int_0^(t/2) (t-s)^(-1) ds=int_(t/2)^t s^(-1) ds=log 2`.
Thus neither endpoint is estimated by a nonintegrable time kernel, and

```text
sup_(t>0) ||q1(t)||_(5/2) <= (Cq/nu) M0^(4/5),
Cq=2 C_R log(2) [A+Bc^2].                                  (33)
```

This bound includes the pressure operator. Replacing its multiplier by a
positive heat kernel without an Lp operator estimate is not used.

### A finite reserve for the entire prepared work

The heat entropy and five-dimensional Sobolev estimates are

```text
d_t int |B|^p +nu p(p-1)int |B|^(p-2)|grad B|^2=0,
||B||_(25/6)^(5/2) <=(25/16)C5 int |B|^(1/2)|grad B|^2.
```

They apply to sign-changing B as well, by the usual convex chain rule.
Integrating gives

```text
int_0^infinity ||B(t)||_(25/6)^(5/2) dt
 <=(5 C5/(12nu))M0.
```

Holder with exponents 5/2 and 5/3, followed by (33), now proves

```text
(3/2)int_0^infinity int_R5 |q1(t)| |B(t)|^(5/2) dt
 <= K_cal :=(5 C5 Cq/(8nu^2)) M0^(9/5).                     (34)
```

In particular define a nonnegative remaining stock of this prepared
history by

```text
R_cal(t)=(3/2)int_t^infinity int_R5 |q1(s)| |B(s)|^(5/2) ds.
```

Its future integral uses only the explicit heat evolution of the ORIGINAL
datum; (34) proves finiteness independently of any unknown future fluid
norm. It is not a supremum over uncontrolled future NS solutions.
For every compatible subinterval [a,b] and every actual paid-parent factor
0<w<=1,

```text
(3/2)int_a^b w(t)<q1(t),|B(t)|^(5/2)> dt
 <=R_cal(a)-R_cal(b),
R_cal(0)<=K_cal.
```

The same B, q1 and original clock persist at every seam. Restarting B from
the current actual b, or setting q1 to zero there, would be a different
history and would require a new payment. Under NS spatial concentration,
with beta_lambda(y)=beta(lambda y), or with beta=1 throughout,
R_cal,lambda(t)=R_cal(lambda^2 t): the initial stock is invariant and
its spending time changes at the physical viscous scale. The numerical
upper bound K_cal is independent of beta and remains invariant even when
a fixed physical cutoff is used, although that cutoff does not obey the
displayed exact covariance. The prepared stock retains spatial-scale
information absent from the coarse corrections tested above.

### Exact identification of the unpaid physical remainder

For the actual unforced solution use the existing core history

```text
(partial_t+v.grad-nu Delta5)eta_core=partial_z(beta b^2),
eta_core(0)=0,   q_core=2partial_z(-Delta5)^(-1)eta_core.
```

Eulerian Duhamel gives q_core=q1+qR, where

```text
qR(t)=2partial_z(-Delta5)^(-1) int_0^t exp(nu(t-s)Delta5)
        [partial_z(beta(b(s)^2-B(s)^2))-v(s).grad eta_core(s)] ds.
```

The last term is the NONconservative full advection as written. If it is
integrated by parts, `div5 v=-q` must be retained; physical
three-dimensional incompressibility does not set that divergence to zero.
All generated parents and their pressure reconstruction remain in qR.

With F=|b|^(5/2), F0=|B|^(5/2), the signed physical production is exactly

```text
Pcrit_core=<q1,F0>+P_receiver+P_remainder,
P_receiver=<q1,F-F0>,   P_remainder=<qR,F>.                  (35)
```

Only the first term has been paid by (34). Both other terms may have either
sign. The precise remaining sufficient estimate is an original-datum bound
on every available prefix T<=H:

```text
int_0^T w[(3/2)(P_receiver+P_remainder)-(15nu/8)Dcrit]
 <=K_rem(u0,nu,H,rho).                                     (36)
```

It would supply the previous full core allowance K=K_cal+K_rem and hence
the already stated axisymmetric continuation consequence. Equation (36)
is OPEN. In particular (34) does not control how the actual flow repeatedly
deforms its source, receiver or generated parents.

There is a second, restricted way to use (33). With the ACTUAL receiver,
Sobolev gives

```text
(3/2)|<q1,|b|^(5/2)>|
 <=(75 C5 Cq/(32nu))M0^(4/5)Dcrit.
```

If `M0^(4/5)<=2nu^2/(5C5Cq)`, this is at most `(15nu/16)Dcrit`, so
this entire parent contribution is absorbed without replacing the actual
receiver by heat. The remainder qR is still unpaid; this observation alone
is not a small-data global theorem.

The original-datum allowance in (34) grows as M0^(9/5). It is compatible
with the many-packet lower bound above, where M0 grows linearly in the
packet count. No bound solely from energy, circulation or scalar entropy
is being substituted for this critical initial resource.
Run `python3 -O labs/critical_caloric_allowance.py` for exponent, time-integral,
constant and decomposition checks. The heat/Riesz estimates, nonnegative
reserve construction and actual PDE Duhamel passage remain analytic.

## Paying the caloric parent against the actual receiver

`caloric_parent_strain.py` checks a stronger payment for the same original
prepared parent q1. With initial energy and enstrophy available, its entire
time-integrated supremum is finite. This pays its production against the
ACTUAL receiver, without a separate estimate for receiver deformation.
The nonlinear source and parent transport remain unpaid. The Fourier and
PDE estimates below are analytic, not new Lean theorems.

Use ordinary Lebesgue measure on R5, positive viscosity nu, and a fixed
cutoff beta with `0<=beta<=1` and bounded weak gradient. Let

```text
B(t)=exp(nu t Delta5)b0,
q1(t)=-2 A5 int_0^t exp(nu(t-s)Delta5)[beta B(s)^2] ds,
A5=-partial_zz(-Delta5)^(-1),
F=||b0||_2, G=||grad b0||_2, d=||grad beta||_infinity.
```

Assume b0 belongs to H1(R5). Smooth rapidly decaying axisymmetric data
suffice for this and the subsequent physical identities. Neither a small
initial norm nor an initial L1 moment is required for the parent bound.
For actual-flow use beta=1-zeta_rho from the original core decomposition.

### A Fourier observation paid by two initial norms

Use the unitary Fourier transform with derivative multiplier i xi. For
f in H1(R5), define

```text
I(f)=(2pi)^(-5/2) int_R5 |fhat(xi)|/|xi|^2 dxi.
```

For any a>0, Cauchy--Schwarz and Plancherel give

```text
I(f)^2 <=(a^2 ||f||_2^2+||grad f||_2^2)/(24 pi^2 a).
```

Indeed the other squared Cauchy factor before Fourier normalization is

```text
int_R5 |xi|^(-4)/(a^2+|xi|^2) dxi
 =(8pi^2/3) int_0^infinity 1/(a^2+r^2) dr=4pi^3/(3a).
```

Optimize at `a=||grad f||_2/||f||_2` to obtain

```text
I(f)<=Cp sqrt(||f||_2 ||grad f||_2),
Cp=1/(2 sqrt(3) pi).                                      (37)
```

If either norm vanishes, f=0 in L2 and the result is immediate. All
integrals in this estimate are finite in dimension five, including the
low-frequency endpoint. Fourier inversion followed by Tonelli now gives

```text
int_0^infinity ||B(t)||_infinity dt
 <=I(b0)/nu<=Cp sqrt(FG)/nu.                               (38)
```

The time integration contributes `1/(nu |xi|^2)`. This estimate also
follows by approximation from smooth data; it does not assume that b0
itself has an absolutely integrable Fourier transform.

### The complete first parent has finite accumulated strain

The symbol of A5 has absolute value at most one. Fourier inversion,
the triangle inequality, and Tonelli over t>=s>=0 give

```text
int_0^infinity ||q1(t)||_infinity dt
 <=(2/nu) int_0^infinity I(beta B(s)^2) ds.                 (39)
```

This integrates the output heat kernel in time BEFORE applying (37).
It is not an L-infinity bound for the Riesz multiplier A5 by itself.
Heat contraction and the product rule give, for s>0,

```text
||beta B(s)^2||_2<=||B(s)||_infinity F,
||grad(beta B(s)^2)||_2<=||B(s)||_infinity(dF+2G).
```

Apply (37), then (38), in (39):

```text
int_0^infinity ||q1(t)||_infinity dt <= A_cal,
A_cal=F sqrt(G(dF+2G))/(6 pi^2 nu^2).                     (40)
```

This bounds the full elliptic strain response of the original caloric source,
over all positive times. It does not estimate actual NS source evolution
by heat. The nonnegative remaining clock
`r1(t)=int_t^infinity ||q1(s)||_infinity ds` has `r1(0)<=A_cal` and
spends exactly its decrease on any compatible interval. B, q1 and their
initial clock must persist across seams; they are never restarted from
the current fluid state. Finiteness is proved from the original datum,
without access to an unknown future NS norm.

The resources in (40) have a literal physical interpretation. Writing
`u_theta=r b` and taking E without a factor 1/2,

```text
F^2=pi E_swirl(0), E_swirl=int_R3 |u_theta|^2,
G^2=pi Z_swirl(0), Z_swirl=int_R3 |curl(u_theta e_theta)|^2.
```

The first identity uses `dy5=2pi^2 r^3 dr dz=pi r^2 dx3` for
axisymmetric integrands. For the second, the two nonzero components of
the swirl's curl are `-r b_z` and `2b+r b_r`. Their squared physical
integrand differs from that of the lifted gradient by

```text
r[(r b_z)^2+(2b+r b_r)^2]-r^3(b_r^2+b_z^2)
 =partial_r(2r^2 b^2).
```

The boundary terms vanish at the regular axis and at infinity under the
stated decay; approximation extends the norm identity where these norms
are finite. For beta=1, (40) simplifies to

```text
A_cal=sqrt(2) sqrt(E_swirl(0) Z_swirl(0))/(6pi nu^2).
```

This is initial enstrophy, not an assumed future enstrophy bound. It is
therefore distinct from the coarse energy-only allowances refuted above.
Under `b0_lambda(y)=lambda^2 b0(lambda y)`, F scales as lambda^(-1/2)
and G as lambda^(1/2). The allowance is invariant if beta scales too
(`d_lambda=lambda d`), or if beta=1. At a fixed physical cutoff its
squared resource `F^2 G(dF+2G)` becomes `F^2 G(dF/lambda+2G)`;
exact covariance must not be asserted for that different cutoff choice.

### Paying the actual receiver and retaining the nonlinear remainder

On every smooth actual axisymmetric prefix, retain
`q=q_paid+q1+qR`, with qR exactly as in the preceding Duhamel decomposition.
It is meridional strain reconstructed from vorticity, not the scalar
pressure itself. The earlier paid-parent bound gives
`int_0^T ||q_paid||_infinity<=2M_H` on every available T<=H, from the
original datum and prescribed horizon.
Use the single history weight

```text
W(t)=exp[-(3/2)int_0^t (||q_paid||_infinity+||q1||_infinity)],
W(t)>=exp[-(3/2)(2M_H+A_cal)]>0,  t<=H.
```

Here M_H and A_cal are fixed in advance. The exact critical balance
`M'=(3/2)<q,|b|^(5/2)>-(15nu/4)Dcrit` now implies

```text
(WM)' +(15nu/8) W Dcrit
 <=W[(3/2)<qR,|b|^(5/2)>-(15nu/8)Dcrit].                  (41)
```

Thus the ONLY remaining signed payment in this decomposition is a finite
original-datum constant K_R>=0 such that every available prefix T<=H obeys

```text
int_0^T W[(3/2)<qR,|b|^(5/2)>-(15nu/8)Dcrit]
 <=K_R(u0,nu,H,rho).                                      (42)
```

If (42) holds, the earlier interpolation
`S^2<=(25C5/16)M^(7/5)Dcrit`, `S=int_R5 |b|^3`, yields

```text
int_0^T S^2
 <=(5C5/(6nu)) exp[(18/5)(2M_H+A_cal)](M0+K_R)^(12/5).
```

This is the same analytic axisymmetric continuation consumer as before.
The receiver need not be close to B. Its entire interaction with q1 has
been paid by the weight; there is no separate receiver-difference
obligation in (42). The signed qR work is still OPEN.

For a concrete evolution of this remainder, let eta1 solve the original
heat equation with source `partial_z(beta B^2)` and zero initial value.
Set `e=b-B`, `h=eta_core-eta1`, `T_op=2partial_z(-Delta5)^(-1)`.
The complete actual equations give

```text
(partial_t+v.grad-nu Delta5)e=q b-v.grad B,
(partial_t+v.grad-nu Delta5)h
 =partial_z[beta(2B e+e^2)]-v.grad eta1,
e(0)=h(0)=0,  qR=T_op h.                                  (43)
```

The drift is the full actual meridional velocity and `div5 v=-q`.
In particular the generated source and transported parent cannot be
replaced by independent controls. Initial zero error does not bound
its subsequent growth. A payment for (43) must retain both forcings,
their common evolving drift, pressure reconstruction and diffusion.
No such arbitrary-history payment is established here; general 3D and
periodic continuation remain separate, open obligations.

Run `python3 -O labs/caloric_parent_strain.py` for the Fourier constants,
heat time integral, physical norm algebra, scaling, and continuation
coefficient checks. These exact checks do not certify the analytic
inequalities, physical evolution, or continuation theorem in Lean.

## A relative parent balance with paid supplied terms

`relative_parent_payment.py` derives the critical joint balance after
subtracting the prepared parent. Three supplied terms in this balance
have finite original-datum payments: the original caloric source, the
source outside the axis tube, and transport of the prepared parent by
the FULL actual velocity. The remaining exchange and transport of the
residual parents are explicit and open. These are analytic estimates for
smooth, decaying axisymmetric whole-space flows; the exact checker covers
algebra and constants, not PDE existence or continuation.

### The residual parent retains the complete drift

Keep the original cutoff beta=1-zeta_rho, the original heat source B,
and eta1 from (43). Write

```text
h=eta_core-eta1, L=(-Delta5)^(-1/2), a=L h, R_z=partial_z L,
qR=2R_z a, q0=q_paid+q1, q=q0+qR,
D_v=partial_t+v.grad-nu Delta5.
```

The exact equations are

```text
D_v b=q b,
D_v a=R_z(b^2)-C+f, C=[L,v.grad]h,
f=-R_z(zeta_rho b^2)-R_z(beta B^2)-L(v.grad eta1).          (44)
```

Here f is a term in an exact decomposition of the unforced equation, not
an external force applied to the fluid. In particular the last summand
uses the full actual v. All operators are canonically reconstructed and
`[A,B]=AB-BA`. The identity follows by applying L to (43); no independence
between the evolving source, parent and velocity is introduced.

Set p=5/2 and

```text
X=b^2+a^2, Phi=X^(p/2), w=X^((p-2)/2), R_p=int_R5 Phi,
T_w=<w a,C>+(1/2)int q w a^2,
Q_R=((p-2)/2)int qR Phi-p<b^2,[R_z,w]a>-p T_w.
```

The complete chain rule, `div5 v=-q`, and skew-adjointness of R_z give

```text
R_p'+nu D_p=Q_R
  +int q0 w[(p-1)b^2+(p/2-1)a^2]+p<w a,f>,               (45)
D_p=int p w(|grad b|^2+|grad a|^2)
       +p(p-2)X^((p-4)/2)|b grad b+a grad a|^2.
```

As before, diffusion is defined by continuity at X=0. In particular
`D_(5/2)>=(5/2)Dcrit` and `R_(5/2)>=M`. Since the two coefficients in
the q0 pairing lie between zero and p-1, that pairing is bounded above
by `(p-1)||q0||_infinity R_p`. This is paid by the preceding caloric
and transported-parent clocks. The spatial weight w is fully evolved;
it is different from any scalar time-integrating factor.

### The initial caloric square source is integrable in the needed norm

Let C_R denote a universal L(5/2) norm bound for the single Riesz operator
R_z, and let C5 be the same five-dimensional Sobolev constant as before.
The Gaussian Young estimates give

```text
||B(s)||_5^2 <= min[A_e^2 C5 G^2 (nu s)^(-1/2),
                    A_l^2 F^2 (nu s)^(-3/2)],
A_e=(4pi)^(-1/4)(10/9)^(-9/4),
A_l=(4pi)^(-3/4)(10/7)^(-7/4),
F=||b0||_2, G=||grad b0||_2.
```

The early estimate smooths L(10/3) into L5 and uses Sobolev on b0;
the late estimate smooths L2 into L5. Integrating the minimum, splitting
where its two powers agree, proves

```text
int_0^infinity ||R_z(beta B(s)^2)||_(5/2) ds
 <=C_R int_0^infinity ||beta B(s)^2||_(5/2) ds
 <=Sigma_B=(4 C_R A_e A_l sqrt(C5)/nu) F G.                 (46)
```

Thus this supplied source has a finite all-time norm without an initial
L1 assumption or smallness. No estimate of the actual b by B is used.

### The outside source is paid by physical energy and circulation

Use the actual unforced energy bound `||u(t)||_2^2<=E0` and the
axisymmetric circulation maximum `|r u_theta(t)|<=Gamma0`.
On the support of zeta_rho, r>=rho, so `|b|<=Gamma0/rho^2`. Then

```text
||zeta_rho b^2||_(5/2)^(5/2)
 <=pi int_(r>=rho) r^2 |b|^5 dx3
 <=pi Gamma0^3 rho^(-6) E0.
```

Consequently every available prefix T<=H satisfies

```text
int_0^T ||R_z(zeta_rho b^2)||_(5/2)
 <=Sigma_out=C_R H pi^(2/5) E0^(2/5) Gamma0^(6/5) rho^(-12/5).
                                                               (47)
```

This pays the cutoff mismatch introduced by writing the residual source
as the complete b^2 transfer in (44). It does not assume that initially
outside parents stay outside the tube.

### Actual transport of the prepared parent also has finite payment

Let C_I be a universal norm bound for
`L:L(5/3)(R5)->L(5/2)(R5)`. This is the Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev
fractional-integration estimate at order one; the exponent difference
is `3/5-2/5=1/5`. See
[Tao, Appendix A, (A.10)--(A.11)](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~tao/preprints/chapter.pdf).
Holder with exponents 2 and 10 gives

```text
||L(v.grad eta1)||_(5/2)
 <=C_I ||v/r||_2(R5) ||r grad eta1||_10(R5)
 <=C_I sqrt(pi E0) ||r grad eta1||_10(R5).                  (48)
```

The physical identity is
`||v/r||_2(R5)^2=pi ||v||_2(R3)^2<=pi E0`. The apparent axis singularity
is integrable with the lifted measure. This uses the actual velocity's
energy, not its future gradient or supremum. The other factor is the
explicit original heat history, defined independently of the actual
solution's lifespan.

Here is a conservative finite bound directly in initial norms. Assume
the following quantities are finite, as for smooth Schwartz b0 and the
fixed smooth cutoff. All norms and derivatives here are in R5:

```text
C_beta=max_(|alpha|<=3) ||D^alpha beta||_infinity,
A3=max_(|alpha|<=3) ||D^alpha b0||_infinity,
B4=max_(|alpha|<=4) ||D^alpha b0||_10,
C3=max_(i<=4, |alpha|<=3) ||y_i D^alpha b0||_10.
```

For s<=H, heat contraction and the exact coordinate commutator give

```text
||y_i D^alpha B(s)||_10<=C3+2nu H B4,  |alpha|<=3,
y_i heat(nu tau)g=heat(nu tau)(y_i g)-2nu tau heat(nu tau)partial_i g.
```

Apply the last formula to `g=partial_j partial_z(beta B(s)^2)` in
the Duhamel formula for `partial_j eta1`. Each second derivative has
product coefficient sum 9, and each third derivative has sum 27.
Summing the four horizontal coordinates and five gradient components
therefore gives

```text
||r grad eta1(t)||_10
 <=180 t C_beta A3 (C3+8nu H B4),  0<=t<=H.
```

Integrating (48) yields

```text
int_0^T ||L(v.grad eta1)||_(5/2)
 <=Sigma_adv=90 C_I sqrt(pi E0) C_beta A3 H^2(C3+8nu H B4).
                                                               (49)
```

Only initial derivatives and a prescribed horizon occur in this bound.
Its constants are deliberately conservative; no scale-invariance claim
is made for the maxima of mixed derivative orders. It pays transport of
eta1, not transport of the unknown residual h.

### A finite allowance for all three supplied terms

Define a majorant using the known original heat history,

```text
g(t)=C_R ||beta B(t)^2||_(5/2)
     +C_R pi^(2/5) E0^(2/5) Gamma0^(6/5) rho^(-12/5)
     +C_I sqrt(pi E0)||r grad eta1(t)||_10,
Sigma=Sigma_B+Sigma_out+Sigma_adv.
```

Then `||f(t)||_(5/2)<=g(t)` and `int_0^H g<=Sigma`. This does not
define an allowance through an unknown future fluid norm. Holder and
Young give, if Sigma>0,

```text
p |<w a,f>| <=p g R_p^((p-1)/p)
 <=(p-1)(g/Sigma)R_p+g Sigma^(p-1),
int_0^H g Sigma^(p-1)<=Sigma^p.                            (50)
```

Thus these supplied terms have a finite additive allowance Sigma^p and
an additional multiplicative clock whose logarithm is at most p-1.
If Sigma=0, g=0 almost everywhere and the extra clock is omitted.
This payment is valid for every compatible segment, with the same
original Sigma and elapsed heat history; segmentation grants no refill.

Set `a0=||q_paid||_infinity+||q1||_infinity` and

```text
Omega=exp[-(3/2)int_0^t (a0+g/Sigma)],
Omega>=exp[-(3/2)(2M_H+A_cal+1)].
```

It remains to prove a finite K_joint>=0 from the original datum, nu, H
and rho such that EVERY smooth actual prefix satisfies

```text
int_0^T Omega[Q_R-(nu/2)D_(5/2)]<=K_joint.                 (51)
```

Equations (45)--(50) would then give

```text
int_0^T S^2 <=(5C5/(4nu)) exp[(18/5)(2M_H+A_cal+1)]
                         *(M0+Sigma^(5/2)+K_joint)^(12/5).
```

Here R_p(0)=M0 because h(0)=0, and the stock already includes the
nonzero supplied-term allowance. This connects (51) to the earlier
analytic axisymmetric continuation criterion. It is an alternative to
the direct qR budget (42), not a claim that either open estimate has
been established or that the joint version is necessarily easier.

### The residual transport does not inherit a missing cancellation

The full-parent quadratic kinetic cancellation cannot be applied to the
residual parent alone. Let chi_R=L a and decompose the actual meridional
velocity as `v=v_R+v0`, where v_R is reconstructed from h and v0 from
the subtracted parent. At constant spatial weight,

```text
T_1=<chi_R,v.grad h>=<chi_R,v0.grad h>,
div5(v_R chi_R)=0.
```

The last cross pairing need not vanish. A kinematically compatible check
uses `chi_R=exp(-(r^2+z^2)/2)`, `chi0=z chi_R`, `h=-Delta5 chi_R`,
and the canonical v0 reconstructed from chi0. Exact Gaussian integration
gives

```text
<chi_R,v0.grad h>=(28/9)(2pi/3)^(5/2)>0.
```

This is an algebraic two-field test. It is not a claim that this pair
occurs in the prescribed actual source-history split, and is not a
counterexample to (51). It prevents using a kinetic identity whose
compatibility hypothesis was lost on subtraction. At nonconstant w,
the full T_w and the source commutator in Q_R both remain. Paying the
radial observation q0 does not by itself pay this entire cross transport.

Run `python3 -O labs/relative_parent_payment.py`. Exact checks cover (45),
the diffusion matrix, harmonic-analysis exponents, scalar payment,
constants in (46)--(50), the continuation multiplier and the Gaussian
cross pairing. The analytic inequalities and arbitrary-history target
retain their distinct status. No general R3/T3 regularity theorem follows.

## Prepared transport and the complete residual parent

`prepared_transport_commutator.py` checks the kernel and balance algebra
for a finite payment of transport by the explicitly prepared parent. The
coefficient uses original heat-history norms, not future derivatives of
the actual velocity. Keeping all other parents together then restores
their quadratic self-transport cancellation. The critical weighted
exchange is still open. The physical estimates below are analytic for
smooth, sufficiently decaying axisymmetric whole-space flows, not new
Lean-certified results. Schwartz lifted initial data suffice for the
additional weighted norms used here.

### A homogeneous operator bound, including low frequencies

On R5 set `Lambda=(-Delta5)^(1/2)`, `L=Lambda^(-1)` and
`R_k=partial_k L`. For p=5/2 and a bounded C2 vector field V, define

```text
N(V)=||V||_infinity+||grad V||_infinity
     +||D2 V||_infinity+||D2 V||_5.
```

There is a universal C_op such that, if N(V) is finite,

```text
||[L,V.grad]Lambda a||_p <= C_op N(V)||a||_p.              (52)
```

The operator is initially defined on smooth test inputs and extends by
density. No divergence-free hypothesis on V in R5 is imposed. In
particular it applies to the lifted meridional velocity, whose divergence
is generally nonzero. The norms of mixed derivative orders give a finite
bound at a fixed spatial normalization; no scale-invariance assertion is
made for N.

Here is a proof that retains the homogeneous low-frequency contribution.
Use `Lambda=-sum_k partial_k R_k`, so it suffices to bound
`[L,F]partial_j partial_k` on Lp. The kernel of L is
`K(z)=c5 |z|^(-4)`. Twice integrating by parts gives the kernel

```text
K_jk(x-y)(F(y)-F(x))
 -K_j(x-y) F_k(y)-K_k(x-y) F_j(y)+K(x-y) F_jk(y),
K_j(z)=-4c5 z_j |z|^(-6),
K_jk(z)=-4c5 delta_jk |z|^(-6)+24c5 z_j z_k |z|^(-8).
```

For the first term, fix a smooth radial cutoff equal to one on the unit
ball and zero beyond radius two. Subtract `-grad F(x).z` locally from
`F(x-z)-F(x)`. Its remainder is bounded by
`C||D2 F||_infinity |z|^2`. The resulting local kernel is bounded by
`C|z|^(-4)`, which is integrable in R5. The distant original term is
bounded by `C||F||_infinity |z|^(-6)`, also integrable on its region.

The local linear terms have kernels `z_ell K_jk(z)`. These are odd,
homogeneous of degree -5 and smooth on the sphere. Their principal-value
operators are bounded: their Fourier multipliers, with derivative symbol
`i xi_j`, are those of

```text
-delta_ell,j R_k-delta_ell,k R_j-R_j R_k R_ell.
```

Multiplying the kernel by the fixed smooth cutoff preserves L2
boundedness, since it convolves this bounded multiplier with an L1
Fourier transform. The cut-off kernel has the usual size and smoothness
bounds, so Calderon--Zygmund theory gives Lp boundedness. The integration
by parts introduces no diagonal correction: on an excluded sphere of
radius epsilon, the potentially constant boundary term is odd; its next
Taylor term is O(epsilon), and the other boundary term is O(epsilon).
This also specifies the principal-value interpretation of the formula.

The two middle terms are Riesz operators on `F_k a` and `F_j a` and
cost `C||grad F||_infinity||a||_p`. The last term is the part that cannot
be discarded at low frequency. Holder and fractional integration give

```text
||L(F_jk a)||_(5/2)
 <= C ||F_jk a||_(5/3) <= C||D2 F||_5 ||a||_(5/2).
```

Summing and using Lp boundedness of R_k proves (52). The standard
operator ingredients are [Calderon--Zygmund boundedness and Riesz
multipliers, Corollary 2.10 and Theorem 4.4](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~tao/247a.1.06f/notes4.pdf),
and [fractional integration, Appendix A (A.10)--(A.11)](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~tao/preprints/chapter.pdf).
The imported `NS.Lit.CZ.truncated_Lp_uniform`, `pvOp_Lp` and
`smoothTruncate_Lp_uniform` already cover the positive-dimensional
homogeneous-kernel estimates under their angular hypotheses. No claim
is made here that this new variable-coefficient application or its PDE
consumer has been formalized.

### The prepared coefficient is finite from the original datum

Let `B(t)=heat(nu t)b0` and beta be a fixed smooth function with
`0<=beta<=1`. Define

```text
J(t)=int_0^t heat(nu(t-s))[beta B(s)^2] ds,
eta1=partial_z J, chi1=partial_z(-Delta5)^(-1)J,
v1^i=-y_i partial_z chi1 (1<=i<=4),
v1^5=2chi1+sum_(i<=4) y_i partial_i chi1,
q1=2partial_z chi1, div5 v1=-q1.
```

Write `C_beta,4=max_(|alpha|<=4)||D^alpha beta||_infinity`.
Let N0 be the sum of all

```text
||D^alpha b0||_q, ||y_i D^alpha b0||_q,
|alpha|<=4, 1<=i<=4, q in {1,infinity,5/3,5/2}.
```

The coordinate heat commutator used in (49) implies, for |alpha|<=3,
each indicated q, and t<=H,

```text
||D^alpha J(t)||_q <=27 t C_beta,4 N0^2,
||y_i D^alpha J(t)||_q
 <=27 t C_beta,4 N0^2(1+8nu H).                          (53)
```

Indeed the product coefficient sums through order three and four are
at most 27 and 81. The weighted input heat evolution costs `2nu H`,
and the outer heat commutator contributes the fourth derivative with
coefficient `2nu H`; `27*2+2*81=27*8`.

For completeness, these estimates also control the nonlocal velocity.
If K2 is the Newtonian kernel in R5, `partial_z K2` has order -4.
For each needed derivative,

```text
y_i [(partial_z K2)*D^gamma J]
 =(partial_z K2)*(y_i D^gamma J)
   +(z_i partial_z K2)*D^gamma J.
```

The two kernels have absolute bounds of orders -4 and -3.
Splitting each at radius one bounds the supremum by the input L1 and
Linfinity norms. For `||D2 v1||_5`, fractional integration uses
`I1:L(5/2)->L5` and `I2:L(5/3)->L5`. Thus (53) proves

```text
N(v1(t)) <= C_rec t C_beta,4 N0^2(1+8nu H),
c1(t)=C_op N(v1(t)),
int_0^H c1(t)dt <= C1=C_* C_beta,4 H^2(1+8nu H)N0^2.     (54)
```

C_* is a fixed universal constant absorbing the finite sums and operator
bounds. This bound is deliberately conservative and permits large
initial derivatives. The actual nonlinear flow is never replaced by v1.

### Recombining all unprepared parents preserves kinetic compatibility

For the following alternative balance take beta=1 and set

```text
h=eta-eta1, a=L h, chi_a=L a,
v=v_a+v1, q=q_a+q1, q_a=2R_z a.
```

Here v_a is reconstructed from h by the same meridional rule. This h
includes ALL initial and subsequently generated parents except eta1.
It differs from `eta_core-eta1` in (44); no transported outside parent
is subtracted. In particular `a(0)=L eta0`, not zero in general.
The previous cutoff decomposition remains valid as a separate option.

The actual equations now read

```text
D_v b=q b,
D_v a=R_z(b^2)-[L,v.grad]h+f,
f=-R_z(B^2)-L(v.grad eta1).                              (55)
```

Let p=5/2, X=b^2+a^2, Phi=X^(p/2), w=X^((p-2)/2), and
`R_p=int_R5 Phi`. Define

```text
T_w^a=<w a,[L,v_a.grad]h>+(1/2)int q_a w a^2,
Q_self=((p-2)/2)int q_a Phi-p<b^2,[R_z,w]a>-p T_w^a.
```

Combining the prepared divergence before taking absolute values gives
the exact complete balance

```text
R_p'+nu D_p=Q_self+int q1 w[(p-1)b^2-a^2]
            -p<w a,[L,v1.grad]h>+p<w a,f>.               (56)
```

D_p is the full convex diffusion in (45), with `D_p>=p Dcrit`.
The new decomposition retains `div5(v_a chi_a)=0`, so `T_1^a=0`.
Consequently Q_self vanishes at p=2. At p=5/2, the changing spatial
weight leaves both commutators and `(1/4)int q_a Phi`; no favorable
sign or critical payment has been proved for their sum.

### Paid terms and the remaining signed target

The q1 coefficient in (56) lies between -Phi and (p-1)Phi. Its payment
therefore costs only `(p-1)||q1||_infinity R_p`; there is no additional
prepared-divergence charge. Equation (52) pays the prepared transport
by `p c1(t) R_p`. Use (46), (48)--(50) with beta=1 and

```text
Sigma=Sigma_B+Sigma_adv,
g(t)=C_R ||B(t)^2||_(5/2)
     +C_I sqrt(pi E0)||r grad eta1(t)||_10,
int_0^H g<=Sigma, ||f||_p<=g,
A_cal=sqrt(2) F G/(6pi^2 nu^2).
```

There is no outside-source term in (55). Let

```text
Omega=exp[-int_0^t ((p-1)(||q1||_infinity+g/Sigma)+p c1)],
Omega>=exp[-(3/2)(A_cal+1)-(5/2)C1].                     (57)
```

As before omit g/Sigma if Sigma=0. These are original heat-history
clocks throughout a prescribed window, never restarted on concatenation.
The starting stock contains the actual initial meridional field:

```text
R_p(0)=int5 (b0^2+(L eta0)^2)^(5/4)
 <=2^(1/4)[M0+C5^(5/8)(pi E_m(0))^(5/8)(pi Z_m(0))^(5/8)].
```

This is the initial physical interpolation bound established in the
full-parent balance. It is finite under the stated initial hypotheses.
It remains to prove a finite nonnegative K_full, controlled from the
original datum, nu and H, such that EVERY available smooth prefix T<=H
satisfies

```text
int_0^T Omega[Q_self-(nu/2)D_p] <= K_full(u0,nu,H).        (58)
```

If (58) holds, (50), (56) and (57) give

```text
int_0^T S^2 <= (5C5/(4nu)) exp[(18/5)(A_cal+1)+6C1]
                *(R_p(0)+Sigma^(5/2)+K_full)^(12/5),
S=int_R5 |b|^3.                                         (59)
```

This follows from `S^2<=(25C5/16)M^(7/5)Dcrit`, `M<=R_p`, and
`Dcrit<=D_p/p`, retaining half the weighted diffusion. It connects
the remaining signed target to the same analytic axisymmetric
continuation criterion. It does not control non-axisymmetric defects
or establish arbitrary-data regularity on R3 or T3.

Run `python3 -O labs/prepared_transport_commutator.py`. The checker covers
the derivative kernels, oddness, homogeneity, Fourier symbols,
fractional-integration exponents, scalar coefficients and complete
balance algebra. The operator bounds, actual history estimates and
continuation implication remain analytic. Paying the prepared parent
and restoring the quadratic cancellation do not establish (58).

## Critical parent transport and nodal costs

`critical_parent_transport.py` tests the complete critical transport
remaining in (56). Two smooth, finite-energy, axisymmetric no-swirl
examples distinguish a finite physical history cost from an artificial
singularity in a proposed estimate. The fractional-operator identification,
local NS evolution and interval arguments below are analytic. The script
checks differential identities and exact rational beta moments, with
optional independent quadrature; it does not certify these PDE arguments
in Lean.

### The precise weight-difference identity

Retain `h=eta-eta1`, `a=Lh`, `chi_a=La`, canonical v_a and
`q_a=2partial_z chi_a=2R_z a`. For a smooth spatial weight w, integration
by parts using `div5(v_a chi_a)=0` gives

```text
T_w^a=<[L,w]a,v_a.grad h>
       +int (a^2/2-h chi_a) v_a.grad w.                   (60)
```

To check the boundary terms, put chi=chi_a and v=v_a. The exact local
identity is

```text
w chi v.grad h-w a v.grad a+(q_a/2)w a^2
 =(a^2/2-h chi)v.grad w
   +div5[v(w chi h-w a^2/2)].
```

Self-adjointness of L supplies `L(wa)=w chi+[L,w]a` before applying
this identity. In kernel form `[L,w]a(x)` retains
`K(x-y)(w(y)-w(x))a(y)`. For the other commutator in Q_self, the kernel
is `partial_z K(x-y)(w(y)-w(x))a(y)`. Both use the SAME actual weight.
Formula (60) does not grant permission to estimate its terms separately
without retaining their integrability and cancellation.

For `w=X^((p-2)/2)`, `X=b^2+a^2`, the second part of the complete
diffusion is exactly

```text
p(p-2)int X^((p-4)/2)|b grad b+a grad a|^2
 =(p/(p-2))int X^((4-p)/2)|grad w|^2.
```

At p=5/2 it controls `5int X^(3/4)|grad w|^2`, not the unweighted
gradient norm. The identity is first read where X>0, then through the
original convex-density formula or regularization at zeros.

### A rational unforced parent with positive critical production

Let `s=r^2+z^2` and set the initial swirl b0=0. Define

```text
chi=z/(1+s)^3,
h=eta=-Delta5 chi=6z(7-s)/(1+s)^5,
a=L h=6z/(1+s)^4,
v=(-r partial_z chi, 2chi+r partial_r chi).
```

This is a smooth, divergence-free three-dimensional meridional velocity,
with finite energy and all Sobolev derivatives. It has an actual unforced
local NS evolution. Zero swirl persists, so every prepared-parent term
in (56) vanishes and `Omega=1`. The remaining equation is

```text
a_t=nu Delta5 a-L(v.grad h),
R_p'+nu D_p=Q_self=-p int |a|^(p-2)a L(v.grad h).           (61)
```

The full fractional operator in this formula can be evaluated exactly.
The family `F_tau=(tau^2+s)^(-2)` is its decaying harmonic extension:
`(partial_tau^2+Delta5)F_tau=0`. Fourier transformation in space, with
the decaying branch, gives `Lambda F_tau=-partial_tau F_tau`. Hence

```text
L[(tau^2+s)^(-3)]=(1/(4tau))(tau^2+s)^(-2),
L[(tau^2+s)^(-k-1)]
 =-(1/(2k tau))partial_tau L[(tau^2+s)^(-k)].
```

Commuting L with axial derivatives evaluates odd numerator powers through

```text
z^m(tau^2+s)^(-k)
 =[(m-1)z^(m-2)(tau^2+s)^(-k+1)
    -partial_z(z^(m-1)(tau^2+s)^(-k+1))]/(2(k-1)).
```

Only exponents within this recursion's range are used. The checker
prints the resulting rational coefficients for `L(v.grad h)`. With
the full five-dimensional measure, the required moments are

```text
int_R5 |z|^m(1+r^2+z^2)^(-k)
 =pi^2 Gamma((m+1)/2) Gamma(k-(m+5)/2)/Gamma(k),
m>-1, k>(m+5)/2.
```

At p=5/2 exact evaluation gives

```text
Q =130880331 sqrt(3) pi^3/1446867107840 >0,
D =3928275 sqrt(3) pi^3/11534336 >0,
R_p(0)=1989 sqrt(3) pi^3/262144,
Q/D=855427/3220672000.                                   (62)
```

These values retain the complete signed exchange. The strain piece is
`110925 sqrt(3)pi^3/536870912`, whereas the transport correction is
`-10503909 sqrt(3)pi^3/90429194240`. The latter helps, but does not
cancel the former. At p=2 the same exact moments give zero nonlinear
production, as required by kinetic compatibility.

Multiplying this initial velocity by A>0 multiplies Q by A^(7/2) and D
by A^(5/2). For every prescribed nu>0, take A=4000nu. Then

```text
Q(A)/(nu D(A))-1=50259/805168>0.
```

The actual critical moment therefore increases on a short initial
interval, by local smooth well-posedness and continuity of its derivative.
This refutes universal instantaneous absorption `Q_self<=nu D_p/2`
and (58) with K_full=0, even after all prepared payments vanish.
It does not refute (58) with a nonzero original-datum allowance.

These examples have `omega_theta` integrable in `dr dz`, and belong to
the globally regular no-swirl class covered by
[Gallay--Sverak, Theorem 1.1](https://www.numdam.org/article/CML_2015__7_2_67_0.pdf).
Positive viscosity follows from their viscosity-one normalization by
rescaling. The present calculation is not a new regularity result for
that class. In particular, b and the continuation clock S are identically
zero, despite the growth of the auxiliary parent norm.

### A separate Young estimate has infinite cost on a regular history

Consider another no-swirl initial datum with s=r^2+z^2:

```text
chi=(1+s)^(-2)-(125/16)(4+s)^(-2),
a=Lambda chi=4(1+s)^(-3)-(125/2)(4+s)^(-3),
h=-Delta5 chi, v=(-r chi_z,2chi+r chi_r).
```

The same harmonic-extension identities identify the fractional parent.
On the sphere s=1,

```text
a=0, partial_s a=-9/20, chi=-1/16, h=1/20,
a^2/2-h chi=1/320, v.grad s=4z chi=-z/4.                 (63)
```

Choose a patch with z near 1/2, away from the axis. The zero of a is
transverse, the transport crosses it, and the flux
`B_flux=(a^2/2-h chi)v` stays nonzero. Applying Young separately to
`B_flux.grad w` against the weighted diffusion in (60) introduces a
positive multiple of

```text
J_bad=int |B_flux|^2/X^(3/4),  X=a^2.                    (64)
```

If d is signed normal distance to this nodal patch, then `|a|` is
comparable to |d|. The integrand in (64) is bounded below by
`c|d|^(-3/2)`, so J_bad is infinite. This is not infinite physical
production: the original gradient term is locally of order
`|d|^(-1/2)`, and the diffusion of order `|d|^(1/2)`, both integrable.
The complete initial signed Q_self is zero by axial reflection:
a, h and chi are even in z, whereas `L(v.grad h)` is odd.

The same obstruction holds if only the normal component of B_flux is
charged: it equals `-1/5120` at s=1, z=1/2. Using the FULL diffusion
only changes the constant. When b=0 it is
`D_p=15int |a|^(3/2)|grad w|^2`, so the same singular weight remains.

The obstruction also holds over a physical time interval. Smooth local
evolution gives continuous first spatial derivatives of a; the implicit
function theorem preserves the transverse nodal patch for sufficiently
small positive times. Continuity keeps chi, h and B_flux nonzero there.
Thus J_bad(t) is infinite at every time in that interval, while the
actual smooth solution and its signed critical balance remain finite.
No assertion that the initial reflection makes Q_self zero at later
times is needed.

Replacing the weight by `(delta^2+a^2)^(1/4)` does not give a uniform
separated estimate. A normal strip of width proportional to delta has

```text
int_patch |B_flux|^2/(delta^2+a^2)^(3/4)
 >=c delta^(-1/2).                                      (65)
```

Even the optimal local Young coefficient using the complete regularized
Hessian has this divergence. With `X_delta=delta^2+a^2`, its ratio is

```text
|partial_a w_delta|^2 / partial_aa Phi_delta
 =a^2/[10 X_delta^(3/4)(delta^2+3a^2/2)].
```

On `delta<=|a|<=2delta` this is bounded below by a fixed positive
multiple of delta^(-3/2). That strip has width comparable to delta.

For an integrable regularized density, subtract its constant delta^(5/2)
from `(delta^2+a^2)^(5/4)`; this does not alter the local diffusion issue.
Alternatively add actual initial swirl
`b0=epsilon exp(-r^2-z^2)`. The data converge smoothly to the no-swirl
datum. Uniform local existence, the linear b equation along the actual
velocity, and the same transverse-node argument give a common short
interval with `|b|<=C epsilon`. The separated cost is then bounded below
by `c epsilon^(-1/2)` throughout that interval. The actual complete
production and diffusion remain uniformly finite there. This last
argument is local; it claims no global regularity for the perturbed data.

The rational initial velocities are rapidly enough decaying for all
displayed integrals but are not asserted Schwartz. If Schwartz data are
required, multiply chi by a smooth radial cutoff at large radius before
reconstructing v. The velocity remains exactly solenoidal. Convergence
of chi in high Sobolev norms in R5 gives convergence of a=Lambda chi
on compact sets with first derivatives. It preserves the transverse
node and the nonzero factors in (63). The strict production margin in
(62) also survives sufficiently distant cutoff: the nonlinear source
converges in L(5/3), L maps it into L(5/2), and the displayed diffusion
is continuous under this smooth Sobolev convergence. These localization
arguments are analytic, not numerical cutoff certificates.

### Consequence for the remaining history estimate

The complete observer derivative retains a useful positive estimate.
For p>=2, the convex Hessian gives the exact identity

```text
((p-1)/p)D_p-int (|grad(wb)|^2+|grad(wa)|^2)/w
 =(p-2)int (w/X)|b grad a-a grad b|^2 >=0.                (66)
```

Each integrand is defined by its continuous expression at X=0 when
p>2. To verify it, write `Z=(b,a)` and
`d(wZ)=w[I+(p-2)ZZ^T/X]dZ`; the rank-one projection has eigenvalues
zero and one. Summing the identity over spatial derivatives proves
(66). At p=5/2 the full observer-gradient cost is at most `(3/5)D_p`.
In contrast to grad w by itself, grad(wa) and grad(wb) have no inverse
amplitude singularity at the nodes in (63). The nonnegative remainder
measures variation of the two-component state direction; it is not
identified here with a three-dimensional vorticity-coherence criterion.

The exact identity (60) is valid, but its separated Young cost cannot
fund the critical reserve on arbitrary compatible histories. A uniform
estimate must keep the nonlocal term and the weight-gradient term
together, or change the tested observation. The derivative of the
original convex density, `partial_a Phi=pwa`, remains regular at a
node; splitting off grad w can destroy that useful feature.

One exact expression that keeps this derivative intact is, with psi=wa,

```text
Q_self/p=int wb(q_a b-v_a.grad b)-int b^2 R_z psi
          +int h[v_a.grad L psi-q_a L psi].              (67)
```

It follows directly from the actual b and a equations, self-adjointness
of L, skew-adjointness of R_z, and `div5 v_a=-q_a`. In particular
`grad L psi` is the vector Riesz transform of psi. Formula (67) retains
every nonlocal parent and does not introduce J_bad. Estimate (66) pays
the gradients of its regular observers; it does not yet control the
nonlocal coefficients or establish the physical-time absorption in (58).

There is also a conservative flux form with a finite diffusion estimate.
All vectors in the following display are Cartesian vectors on R5, and L
acts on each Cartesian component. Put chi=chi_a, v=v_a, and

```text
T=e_z |grad chi|^2-2partial_z chi grad chi,
div5 T=-2partial_z chi Delta5 chi=q_a h,
J_b=-v b, J_a=e_z L(b^2)-L(v h+T).
```

Then `div5 J_b=q_a b-v.grad b` and
`div5 J_a=R_z(b^2)-L(v.grad h)`. Thus the SAME complete defect is

```text
Q_self=-p int [grad(wb).J_b+grad(wa).J_a].               (68)
```

In particular the lifted drift's nonzero divergence has not been
discarded. When evaluating L on a radial vector, its Cartesian basis
also has to be retained; applying the scalar radial operator only to
the radial component would change (68).

Define `B_flux_cost=int w(|J_b|^2+|J_a|^2)`. Cauchy--Schwarz, (66),
and Young give the concrete instantaneous bound

```text
|Q_self| <=sqrt(p(p-1)D_p B_flux_cost)
         <=(nu/2)D_p+(15/(8nu))B_flux_cost, p=5/2.       (69)
```

This cost has no inverse-amplitude singularity at the nodes in (63).
It is finite for the smooth, decaying fields here: L maps the relevant
flux inputs from L(10/7) to L2 and w is bounded. For the datum in (62),
its exact value is `7147841286819 sqrt(3)pi^3/37039797960704000`.
The independently reconstructed flux divergence and its pairing in
(68) agree exactly with (61)--(62).

Under NS spatial scaling, B_flux_cost scales like lambda^2, so its
time integral is critical. Nothing here bounds that integral from the
original datum. Formula (68) retains the signed history; using only
(69) can lose useful compensation. This finite diagnostic bound must
not be treated as a proved initial payment or as a replacement of the
open signed history estimate by an already funded absolute-value budget.

The direct swirl-observed budget remains an alternative to the joint
parent budget. A parent norm can grow even when that continuation
observation is identically zero. Neither this extra burden nor the
failure of (64) refutes a finite full-datum signed allowance, a corrected
joint reserve, or unforced regularity.

Run `python3 -O labs/critical_parent_transport.py --quadrature`. The
48/96/192-point quadratures reproduce Q and D in (62). An independent
Riesz-potential integral on the axis at z=0.4 agrees with the rational
formula with absolute errors about `1.08e-8`, `5.29e-11` and `1.97e-13`.
Those quadratures have no certified error bound. The exact moment and
nodal algebra, analytic physical interval arguments, and open full-datum
history estimate retain their separate status.

## Paying the complete far-parent flux from a spatial moment

`far_parent_payment.py` checks the identities and constants below. This is
an analytic payment for one part of the ACTUAL nonlinear history, not only
the prepared heat history. It applies to the smooth, decaying axisymmetric
R3 class of (58), with finite initial second kinetic moment. The moment
estimate itself does not require axisymmetry. None of the new PDE arguments
in this section is Lean-certified.

Keep the complete residual `chi=chi_a`, `h=-Delta5 chi`, `a=Lambda chi`,
the actual b, and the original prepared history from (57). Fix a kernel
distance R>0 before following the solution. This is separation in the R5
lifted Riesz kernel, not a claim that a pair of physical vortices has a
particular three-dimensional separation. Split only J_a in (68); J_b and
the complementary near part of J_a retain their signs.

### A physical moment that remains payable

Use no factor 1/2 in the physical energy. For the FULL unforced velocity,
including swirl, let

```text
E0=int_R3 |u0|^2, I0=int_R3 |x|^2|u0|^2,
Z(t)=int_R3 |grad u|^2, I(t)=int_R3 |x|^2|u|^2.
```

Let C_S be any fixed constant in `||u||_6<=C_S||grad u||_2` on R3.
For every available smooth prefix t<=H,

```text
sqrt(I(t)) <= M_H
 :=sqrt(I0+6nu E0 H)
   +3 C_S^(3/2) E0^(1/4) H^(1/4)(E0/(2nu))^(3/4).       (70)
```

Here the center and H are fixed from the initial problem. The canonical
pressure satisfies `||p||_2<=||u||_4^2`: in Fourier space its tensor
multiplier is contraction with the rank-one matrix `k tensor k/|k|^2`, whose
Frobenius norm is one. Testing the local kinetic-energy identity gives

```text
I'+2nu int |x|^2|grad u|^2
 =6nu E(t)+2 int (x.u)(|u|^2+2p)
 <=6nu E0+6 C_S^(3/2) sqrt(I) E0^(1/4) Z^(3/4).
```

There is no assumed future moment bound in this test. First use
`W_L=|x|^2/(1+|x|^2/L^2)`, which is bounded and obeys
`|grad W_L|^2<=4W_L`, `Delta W_L<=6`. The same differential inequality
holds uniformly for `int W_L|u|^2`. Scalar comparison, the prefix energy
