bound `int_0^t Z<=E0/(2nu)` for t<=H, and Holder give (70). Monotone convergence
as L increases supplies the actual moment. The pressure and Sobolev
estimates use only norms already controlled on each smooth prefix.
This is a standard weighted-energy argument, stated with the constants
needed here; it is not a new general regularity result. For the underlying
Hardy and Sobolev tools, see Appendix A of
[Tao's analysis text](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~tao/preprints/chapter.pdf).

For an axisymmetric meridional potential chi, integration by parts gives

```text
G0=int_R5 |grad chi|^2=pi E_meridional,
G2=int_R5 |x|^2|grad chi|^2=pi I_meridional+4 int_R5 chi^2,
int_R5 chi^2 <=(4/25)G2,
G2 <=(25pi/9)I_meridional.                              (71)
```

The positive correction in the second line matters. In general a weight
W contributes `-2 int_R5 (W_r/r)chi^2` to the physical energy integral;
it cannot be dropped. The third line follows from
`5 int chi^2=-2 int chi x.grad chi` and Cauchy--Schwarz.

Finiteness in (71) need not be assumed circularly. The canonical physical
vector potential is `A=(-x2 chi,x1 chi,0)` in Cartesian R3 coordinates
`(x1,x2,z)`, with `curl A=v`, `div A=0`. Fourier-space Hardy in dimension
three first gives `||chi||_2(R5)^2=pi||A||_2(R3)^2<=4pi I_meridional`.
The bounded weights W_L in the preceding identity then yield finite G2
and its exact identity by monotone convergence. Dimension-five weighted
Hardy improves the constant to 25/9 as displayed. These arguments concern
the decaying canonical potential, not an arbitrary added harmonic field.

### Transport and stress stay together

All indices in the following formula are Cartesian R5 indices. Write
`Y=(y1,y2,y3,y4,0)`, `g=grad chi`,
`S_ik=g_i g_k-delta_ik |g|^2/2`, and
`A_jk=delta_jz Y_k-Y_j delta_kz`. Thus `v=2chi e_z+A g`. Define

```text
F_ij=2 delta_jz chi g_i+sum_k A_jk S_ik,
H_vec=(-3chi_z grad_h chi, 2|grad_h chi|^2-chi_z^2).
```

The exact identity, including derivatives of the coordinate factors, is

```text
v h+T=-div F+H_vec,
T=e_z|grad chi|^2-2chi_z grad chi, h=-Delta5 chi.          (72)
```

The divergence is in F's first index. For example,
`div_i S_ik=Delta5 chi g_k`; differentiating A supplies the remaining
terms in H_vec. The checker verifies (72) for an arbitrary five-variable
function, before imposing axisymmetry. Pointwise Frobenius estimates and
(71) give

```text
|H_vec|<=2|g|^2, |F|<=2|chi||g|+2r|g|^2,
||H_vec||_1<=2G0, ||F||_1<=(14/5)sqrt(G0 G2).              (73)
```

Consequently the transport term v h has not been replaced by a bound
only on T. Its derivative is moved onto the far kernel with all of the
coordinate and stress corrections retained.

### Explicit stocks for the complete residual

Here chi is the residual, not the full potential. The subtraction must
therefore also be paid. In R5 put

```text
A0=||b0||_infinity, F0=||b0||_2, M0w=||x b0||_2,
J0=H A0 F0,
Jw=A0[H M0w+(4/3)sqrt(10nu) H^(3/2)F0].
```

These are original norms; `F0^2=pi E_swirl(0)` and
`M0w^2=pi I_swirl(0)`. For the SAME prepared history through every seam,

```text
B(t)=heat(nu t)b0,
J(t)=integral_0^t heat(nu(t-s)) B(s)^2 ds,
chi1=partial_z(-Delta5)^(-1)J,
||grad chi1||_2<=J0, ||x grad chi1||_2<=(7/3)Jw.        (74)
```

Indeed heat contraction gives `||B||_infinity<=A0`, `||B||_2<=F0`.
The heat displacement estimate
`||x heat(nu t)f||_2<=||xf||_2+sqrt(10nu t)||f||_2`
follows from the Gaussian's second moment and Minkowski. Apply it once
to B and once to the outer heat operator. Integrating the two square
roots gives 4/3 and the bound Jw. The multiplier of grad chi1 is the
vector `m(k)=-k_z k/|k|^2`. Its norm is at most one and

```text
|grad_k m|_F^2=(1+3 k_z^2/|k|^2)/|k|^2 <=4/|k|^2.
```

Plancherel and the dimension-five Hardy constant 2/3 then give
`||x grad chi1||_2 <=(1+4/3)||xJ||_2`. Thus (74) uses no unknown
actual velocity gradients. With chi=chi_total-chi1, (70)--(74) imply
the uniform residual stocks

```text
G0(t)<=Gbar=2[pi E0+J0^2],
G2(t)<=Wbar=2[(25pi/9)M_H^2+(49/9)Jw^2].              (75)
```

All these bounds hold on every available smooth prefix from the same
datum. They require finite I0 and the stated initial heat norms. Smooth
rapidly decaying data satisfy them; no periodic analogue is claimed here.

### A fixed-scale payment with a named remaining consumer

The kernel of L is `K(x)=1/(2pi^3|x|^4)`. Set
`K_R(x)=theta(|x|/R)K(x)`, where theta is zero below 1, one above 2,
and `3(t-1)^2-2(t-1)^3` between them. It is C1 at the seams,
`0<=theta<=1`, and `0<=theta'<=3/2`. Let

```text
s4=8pi^2/3,
cK=(1/(2pi^3))(s4/5)^(2/5),
cD=(7/(2pi^3))(2s4/15)^(2/5).
```

The derivative of the cutoff is included in the constant 7:
`|grad K_R|<=7/(2pi^3|x|^5)` on its support. Radial integration gives
`||K_R||_(5/2)<=cK R^(-2)` and
`||grad K_R||_(5/2)<=cD R^(-3)`. From (72), the complete far part is

```text
J_a,far=e_z K_R*b^2 + sum_i partial_i K_R*F_ij - K_R*H_vec.
```

Young's convolution inequality, (73), (75), and
`||b||_2(R5)^2=pi E_swirl(t)<=pi E0` give the original-data bound

```text
||J_a,far(t)||_(5/2) <= P_R
 :=cK R^(-2)(pi E0+2Gbar)
   +cD R^(-3)(14/5)sqrt(Gbar Wbar).                    (76)
```

This bounds the full nonlinear far contribution, including internally
generated parents, without taking their unknown future norms as inputs.
It is a fixed-scale statement. P_R grows as R tends to zero, and moving
R or resetting the original heat history is not justified by it.

Set `J_a,near=J_a-J_a,far`, and keep

```text
Q_far=-p int grad(wa).J_a,far,
Q_near=-p int[grad(wb).J_b+grad(wa).J_a,near], p=5/2.
```

Holder gives `int w|J_a,far|^2<=R_p^(1/5)P_R^2`, since
`||w||_5=R_p^(1/5)`. Using the COMPLETE observer bound (66), allocate
one quarter of diffusion to this part:

```text
|Q_far| <=(nu/4)D_p+(15/(4nu))P_R^2 R_p^(1/5)
        <=(nu/4)D_p+c_R R_p+d_R,                       (77)
c_R=3P_R^2/(4nu L0^(4/5)), d_R=4L0 c_R.
```

Here any positive stock L0 is chosen from the original datum, viscosity
and H. For nonzero data one may use `L0=R_p(0)+Sigma^(5/2)`; the zero
solution is handled separately. The last inequality is the tangent bound
`x^(1/5)<=(1/5)L0^(-4/5)x+(4/5)L0^(1/5)`.
Thus the payment is a fixed finite linear coefficient and additive
allowance. It is NOT an assertion that `integral |Q_far|` is bounded
independently of the still-unknown reserve and diffusion.

Retain the prepared clock Omega from (57) and set
`Omega_R(t)=Omega(t)exp(-c_R t)`. The OPEN remaining sufficient target is

```text
integral_0^T Omega_R[Q_near-(nu/4)D_p]
 <=K_near(u0,nu,H,R)                                  (78)
```

for every smooth prefix T<=H, with K_near finite from the original data.
Equations (57), (77), (78) would give

```text
Omega_R(T)R_p(T)+(nu/2)integral_0^T Omega_R D_p
 <=R_p(0)+Sigma^(5/2)+d_R H+K_near.
```

In particular the previously established conditional axisymmetric
continuation estimate becomes

```text
integral_0^T S(t)^2 dt
 <=(5C5/(4nu))
   *exp[(18/5)(A_cal+1)+6C1+(12/5)c_R H]
   *[R_p(0)+Sigma^(5/2)+d_R H+K_near]^(12/5),
S(t)=int_R5 |b|^3.                                    (79)
```

The g/Sigma part of the prepared clock is omitted when Sigma=0; the
displayed bound with the extra 1 remains a valid conservative bound.
All clocks retain one original start across compatible segments. The
new coefficient pays the complete distant interaction, while (78) still
contains local swirl transport and the nearby, mutually changing parent
field. A proof of (78), or a better corrected observation with an actual
continuation consumer, remains necessary. Neither a favorable instant
nor the spatial moment estimate proves it. General non-axisymmetric
R3/T3 regularity remains open in this lane.

For the nodal-parent family in (63), including its small-swirl perturbations,
the stocks in (75)--(77) stay uniformly finite as the swirl tends to zero,
at fixed R, nu, H and positive original L0. No division by the evolving
parent amplitude appears. This repairs the particular far contribution
without claiming that the remaining near work is bounded or favorable.

Run `python3 -O labs/far_parent_payment.py --quadrature`. Exact checks
include (71)--(74), bounded moment-test derivatives, kernel exponents,
diffusion allocations and NS scaling. Independent 48/96/192 quadrature
compares the literal and stress forms of J_a,far on the positive-parent
and nodal-parent profiles, with actual initial swirl added, at R=1/2,1,2.
At resolution 192 their differences are below 8e-16. Omitting the cutoff
derivative gives errors between about 2.6e-6 and 1.2e-2. These tests check
the complete integral and expose a real cutoff error; their numerical
accuracy is not a certified error bound or proof of physical evolution.

## An actual no-swirl reference and swirl-seeded parent histories

`noswirl_reference_payment.py` tests an alternative to subtracting the
prepared heat parent. It removes the harmless meridional evolution by
following an actual no-swirl solution, while retaining the full nonlinear
feedback of the target flow. The new estimates are analytic; their PDE,
stochastic and harmonic-analysis parts are not Lean-certified.

Start with smooth, rapidly decaying axisymmetric R3 data u0. Let V be the
unforced NS solution whose initial velocity is u0 with its swirl removed.
This reference is globally regular independently of the target's swirl:
[Gallay--Sverak, Theorem 1.1, Remark 4.6 and Proposition 5.5](https://www.numdam.org/article/CML_2015__7_2_67_0.pdf)
give global no-swirl existence and smoothing when the meridional vorticity
is in L1(dr dz), as it is here. Their viscosity-one result rescales to
any nu>0. Smooth initial data supply regularity at time zero as well.
This uses established no-swirl theory, not an asserted regularity theorem
for the swirling target.

Use the SAME reference from the original initial time through every
compatible segment. Write its lifted fields as V, eta_bar and q_bar,
and set

```text
h=eta-eta_bar, a=Lh, chi_a=La, v=v_a+V,
q=q_a+q_bar, q_a=2partial_z chi_a, p=5/2.
```

The scalar a here differs from the heat-subtracted a in (57). All formulas
in this section use the actual reference just defined. The exact equations
on every available smooth target prefix are

```text
h_t+v.grad h=nu Delta5 h+partial_z b^2-v_a.grad eta_bar,
a_t+v.grad a=nu Delta5 a+R_z(b^2)
              -[L,v.grad]h-L(v_a.grad eta_bar),
b_t+v.grad b=nu Delta5 b+(q_a+q_bar)b,
h(0)=a(0)=0, h_t(0)=partial_z b0^2.                    (80)
```

There is no independent force available in (80). The source uses the
actual b, the drift uses the full actual v, and the reference-feedback
term depends on the actual residual velocity v_a. In particular, the
source cannot be reset as fresh external input at successive segments.

For comparison, an axisymmetric external force would add
`(partial_z f_r-partial_r f_z)/r` to the h equation and `f_theta/r`
to the b equation, with V still chosen unforced. Those are additional
inputs. The internally generated feedback `-v_a.grad eta_bar` in (80)
is retained and is not identified with an independently selectable force.

The first equation has a precise stochastic history representation. For
a fixed available terminal time t and starting point x, let

```text
dX_s=-v(t-s,X_s)ds+sqrt(2nu)dW_s, X_0=x, 0<=s<=t.
h(t,x)=E integral_0^t
        [partial_z b^2-v_a.grad eta_bar](t-s,X_s) ds.    (81)
```

Ito's formula for `h(t-s,X_s)` proves (81); its initial endpoint is zero.
The five-dimensional Brownian motion represents the quotient's lifted diffusion.
The coefficients and source are bounded on each smooth decaying prefix,
so this calculation introduces no extra target continuation assumption.
The drift and source remain coupled to that target solution. This is
stochastic transport of an actual residual, not an identification of an
arbitrary auxiliary control or Schrödinger bridge with a fluid solution.

### Reference feedback has a finite critical coefficient

Put `R_p=int_R5 (b^2+a^2)^(p/2)` and retain its complete diffusion D_p.
The self contribution Q_self has exactly the form (56), with the present
residual. Subtraction gives

```text
R_p'+nu D_p=Q_self+int q_bar w[(p-1)b^2-a^2]
  -p<wa,[L,V.grad]h>-p<wa,L(v_a.grad eta_bar)>,
R_p(0)=M0=int_R5 |b0|^(5/2).                           (82)
```

Both displayed operators matter at the critical exponent. Estimate (52)
bounds the first by `c_bar||a||_p`, where `c_bar=C_op N(V)` and
`N(V)=||V||_infinity+||grad V||_infinity+||D2V||_infinity+||D2V||_5`
uses Cartesian R5 fields. For the second, horizontal Hardy in four
dimensions, followed by the vector Riesz bound C_R, gives

```text
||chi_a/r||_p <=p/(4-p)||grad_h chi_a||_p,
||v_a/r||_p <=(16/3)C_R||a||_p, p=5/2.
```

Indeed `v_a=(-y_h chi_a,z,2chi_a+y_h.grad_h chi_a)`.
The elementary Hardy estimate follows by integrating
`div_h(y_h/r^p)=(4-p)/r^p` against `|chi_a|^p` at each z.
Holder and the R5 fractional integration estimate
`L:L(5/3)->L(5/2)` now give

```text
||L(v_a.grad eta_bar)||_p <=ell_bar||a||_p,
ell_bar=(16/3)C_I C_R ||r grad eta_bar||_5.
kappa_bar=(3/2)||q_bar||_infinity+(5/2)(c_bar+ell_bar),
R_p'+nu D_p <=Q_self+kappa_bar R_p.                    (83)
```

Here the Riesz and fractional-integration constants are fixed, and no
actual future derivative appears in kappa_bar. The underlying operator
results are those cited in (52); the feedback estimate additionally keeps
the radial factor needed for the physical lifted velocity.

The reference integral `Kappa_H=int_0^H kappa_bar` is finite from the
original meridional datum. To justify the weighted part of this assertion,
global smoothness gives bounded physical derivatives on each compact
reference time interval. Weighted L2 derivatives through order two remain
finite: differentiate the physical NS equation, test by W_L times the
same derivative, and use bounded reference derivatives in the transport
products. Integrating pressure by parts leaves only grad W_L, because
each velocity derivative is divergence-free. The unweighted pressure
derivatives are bounded in L2 by product Sobolev estimates and the Riesz
multiplier. The resulting finite triangular Gronwall system, uniformly
in W_L, propagates the weighted derivative norms from their initial values.

For clarity, no weighted estimate at the axis is hidden here. The Cartesian
derivatives of the O(4) lift have the same radial expressions, with fixed
multiplicities, as those of the smooth O(2) physical meridional field.
Thus their second-derivative norm is bounded pointwise by a fixed multiple
of the physical second-derivative norm (sqrt(3) suffices, as the Cartesian
checker verifies). Also
`r grad eta_bar=grad omega_bar,theta-(omega_bar,theta/r)e_r`;
the physical Cartesian derivative of `omega_bar,theta e_theta` includes
both of these terms. It follows that

```text
||D2V_lift||_5+||r grad eta_bar||_5
 <=C ||D2V_physical||_infinity^(3/5)
      [int_R3 (1+|x|^2) sum_(j<=2)|D^j V|^2]^(1/5).   (84)
```

The bound uses `int_R5 f=pi int_R3 r^2 f` for scalar radial functions
and interpolation between L2 and Linfinity. The other terms in N(V) and
q_bar are bounded by ordinary reference derivatives. This proves finite
Kappa_H for the stated initial class, including at time zero.

Kappa_H is a functional of the known globally regular reference. This
section does not give a closed numerical formula for it in initial
seminorms. Its finiteness follows from established reference existence
and the weighted argument above, rather than a supremum over an unknown
future target flow. Computing or formally bounding that reference is a
separate task from proving the remaining target estimate.

### Relative energy supplies a nonnegative history reserve

Let w_phys=u-V be the PHYSICAL three-dimensional velocity difference,
including swirl, and use

```text
E_w=int_R3 |w_phys|^2, Z_w=int_R3 |grad w_phys|^2,
I_w=int_R3 |x|^2|w_phys|^2,
E_s=E_w(0)=int_R3 |u0,theta|^2,
I_s=I_w(0)=int_R3 |x|^2|u0,theta|^2,
L_H=int_0^H ||grad V||_infinity, U_H=int_0^H ||V||_infinity.
```

Use a matrix norm dominating the operator norm in L_H. The literal
difference equation gives

```text
E_w'+2nu Z_w=-2int_R3 w_phys.(grad V)w_phys,
E_w(t)<=Ebar:=E_s exp(2L_H),
int_0^T Z_w<=Ebar/(2nu), T<=H.                         (85)
```

More explicitly, the nonnegative remaining reserve

```text
B_kin(t)=exp[2int_t^H ||grad V||_infinity] E_w(t)/(2nu)
```

satisfies `B_kin'(t)<=-Z_w(t)`. It starts from Ebar/(2nu) and pays
every compatible prefix without a refill. It controls deviation
enstrophy, not the still-open critical stretching history.

The pressure difference is the Riesz contraction of
`w_phys tensor w_phys+V tensor w_phys+w_phys tensor V`, hence
`||p_u-p_V||_2<=||w_phys||_4^2+2||V||_infinity sqrt(E_w)`.
The same bounded moment tests as in (70) give

```text
I_w'+2nu int |x|^2|grad w_phys|^2
 <=2||grad V||_infinity I_w+6nu E_w
   +sqrt(I_w)[6 C_S^(3/2) E_w^(1/4) Z_w^(3/4)
              +10||V||_infinity sqrt(E_w)].
sqrt(I_w(t))<=Mrel
 :=exp(L_H)[sqrt(I_s+6nu Ebar H)
   +3 C_S^(3/2) Ebar^(1/4) H^(1/4)(Ebar/(2nu))^(3/4)
   +5sqrt(Ebar)U_H].                                  (86)
```

This is a conservative bound. Multiply the differential inequality by
`exp(-2int_0^t ||grad V||_infinity)`, use (85), and apply the same scalar
comparison and Holder argument as for (70). It uses only available target
prefixes. The physical estimates (85)--(86) hold for general smooth
divergence-free target/reference pairs when the reference norms are known;
the critical-parent system (80)--(84) uses axisymmetry.

The lifted relative kinetic identities are
`int_R5 (b^2+a^2)=pi E_w` and
`int_R5 |grad chi_a|^2<=pi E_w`. Applying (71) to the residual meridional
velocity yields `int_R5 |x|^2|grad chi_a|^2<=25pi Mrel^2/9`.
Therefore the complete far payment (76) improves in this reference to

```text
||J_a,far||_(5/2)<=P_R
 :=3pi cK R^(-2)Ebar
   +(14pi/3)cD R^(-3)sqrt(Ebar)Mrel.                   (87)
```

This is still at fixed R and uses the complete stress and cutoff
derivatives of (72)--(76). For a fixed meridional reference and
`u0,theta=epsilon times a fixed profile`, Ebar=O(epsilon^2),
Mrel=O(epsilon)+O(epsilon^2), and P_R=O(epsilon^2)+O(epsilon^3).
With `L0=M0>0` in (77), the new far coefficient is O(epsilon^2) and
its additive payment is O(epsilon^(9/2)), at fixed nu,H,R. These are
relative-resource estimates, not arbitrary-amplitude regularity.

### Calibration and the precise unpaid part

If b0=0, target uniqueness gives u=V throughout each existing prefix,
so b,h,a,R_p,Q_self and the relative stocks all vanish. This includes
the no-swirl positive-production example (61): its full parent norm may
grow, but it produces zero DEVIATION from the actual reference.
If b0 is nonzero, the exact initial source in (80) is retained. Thus
the subtraction neither invents new parents nor falsely forbids them.

At quadratic weight the feedback term has an additional cancellation:

```text
<a,L(v_a.grad eta_bar)>=<chi_a,v_a.grad eta_bar>=0,
div5(chi_a v_a)=0.
```

This does not hold at the critical exponent. A kinematic compatible test
with `s=r^2+z^2`, `chi_a=(1+s)^(-2)`,
`a=4(1+s)^(-3)`, `chi_bar=z(1+s)^(-3)` gives

```text
<a,L(v_a.grad eta_bar)>=0,
<a^(3/2),L(v_a.grad eta_bar)>=222816pi^2/1978375 >0.     (88)
```

Reversing chi_bar reverses the second pairing. No reachability of this
particular pair from matched initial parents is claimed. It tests the
operator identity and excludes discarding that term merely because the
quadratic pairing cancels. A separate exact Gaussian test verifies that
the full reference contribution agrees with physical relative strain
work in (85). Neither test is a counterexample to a history allowance.

Set `c_R=3P_R^2/(4nu M0^(4/5))`, `d_R=4M0c_R` when M0>0, and
`Omega_ref=exp[-int_0^t kappa_bar-c_R t]`. Keep all J_b and the near
part of J_a in Q_near. The OPEN sufficient estimate is now

```text
int_0^T Omega_ref[Q_near-(nu/4)D_p]
 <=K_seed(u0,nu,H,R), for every actual prefix T<=H.      (89)
```

If K_seed is bounded from the original datum, (82)--(87) imply

```text
Omega_ref(T)R_p(T)+(nu/2)int_0^T Omega_ref D_p
 <=M0+d_R H+K_seed,
int_0^T S^2 <=(5C5/(4nu))exp[(12/5)(Kappa_H+c_R H)]
                       *(M0+d_R H+K_seed)^(12/5).      (90)
```

This is the same analytic axisymmetric continuation consumer as (79).
There is no prepared-source additive Sigma in this alternative balance;
all reference terms have the finite linear coefficient (83). When M0=0,
uniqueness handles the zero-deviation case instead of dividing by M0.
The near interaction of swirl with the parents it generates remains
unpaid. It can contain repeated renewal, and the estimates here do not
rule that out. General non-axisymmetric R3/T3 closure remains open.

Run `python3 -O labs/noswirl_reference_payment.py`. Exact checks include
the actual residual equation, source at the matched initial state, the
full physical relative-energy equation, both pressure cross tensors,
the critical coefficient exponents, (88), the Gaussian kinetic comparison,
and the small-swirl scaling of the relative spatial stock. The global
reference theory, finite weighted coefficients, stochastic formula and
actual-history estimates have the analytic status specified above.

## The first nonlinear return from an actual swirl seed

`generated_parent_return.py` tests the first closed source--parent--source
interaction of an actual unforced flow. It starts with zero meridional
velocity, so the actual no-swirl reference in (80) is zero. The generated
parents are not independently chosen inputs. A radial identity gives a
strictly negative return for a whole class of seeds, while the source's
next angular component records why this is not an invariant class or an
iterable history bound. The exact algebra is checked; local PDE evolution,
fractional reconstruction and the time-interval implications are analytic.

### The complete initial history and its caloric comparison

Take smooth rapidly decaying pure-swirl data
`u0=(-x2 b0,x1 b0,0)`, with b0 a smooth radial function of
`s=r^2+z^2`. Fix any nu>0 and use the actual local unforced solution.
Let `f=b0^2`, `F=(-Delta5)^(-1)f` be the canonical decaying potential,
and let subscripts denote literal initial time derivatives, not Taylor
coefficients. Then

```text
h1=partial_z f, chi1=partial_z F, v1=velocity(chi1),
q1=2partial_z chi1,
b1=nu Delta5 b0,
b2=nu^2 Delta5^2 b0-v1.grad b0+q1 b0,
h2=nu[Delta5 h1+2partial_z(b0 Delta5 b0)].              (91)
```

Compare with the SAME original caloric forecast
`B=exp(nu t Delta5)b0`,
`(h_cal)_t=nu Delta5 h_cal+partial_z(B^2)`, `h_cal(0)=0`.
The actual and forecast parent jets agree through order two. Their full
third-derivative difference is

```text
f2_nl=-v1.grad f+2q1 f,
h3_nl=partial_z f2_nl-2v1.grad h1,
h3-h3_cal=h3_nl,
h3_cal=nu^2[Delta5^2 h1+2Delta5 partial_z(b0 Delta5 b0)
       +2partial_z((Delta5 b0)^2+b0 Delta5^2 b0)].      (92)
```

Thus no viscosity term is dropped to obtain h3_nl. The two nonlinear
terms retain both deformation of the source and transport of its parent.
Define their signed return into the first generated parent by

```text
C_return=<chi1,h3_nl>
        =-(1/2)int_R5 f[v1.grad q1+q1^2].              (93)
```

To obtain (93), `div5(chi1 v1)=0` cancels the canonical pairing of the
parent-transport term. The remaining integration by parts uses
`div5 v1=-q1`, not zero. These identities apply before imposing radial
symmetry. The sign is not inferred merely from a square or a source norm.

Write `a=Lh`, `a_cal=Lh_cal`. Local smooth evolution and the canonical
kinetic isometry give the Hilbert-space Taylor comparison

```text
||a(t)||_2^2-||a_cal(t)||_2^2
       =(t^4/3) C_return+o(t^4).                      (94)
```

Indeed `a-a_cal=t^3 Lh3_nl/6+o(t^3)` and both first derivatives equal
Lh1. The L2 pairing is `<Lh1,Lh3_nl>=<chi1,h3_nl>`. Smooth physical
L2 time jets justify this expansion on the actual local existence
interval; the forecast has the corresponding smooth jets. The same
positive viscosity appears on both sides. A strict negative return
therefore gives an actual short-time inequality, with an interval
depending on the datum and nu. No uniform Taylor window is asserted.

### A radial sign law for the first complete return

Regard F as a function of squared radius s and put `g=-F'`. The radial
Poisson equation and the regular axis condition give

```text
f=4s g'+10g,
g(s)=(1/(4s^(5/2)))int_0^s y^(3/2) f(y)dy >=0.
q1=-4g-8z^2 g'.                                      (95)
```

The normalized angular mean on S4 of the bracket in (93) is

```text
mean(v1.grad q1+q1^2)
 =(16/35)[42s g g'+4s^2 g g''+28s^2(g')^2+35g^2].
```

This contains the complete transport contribution. The radial integration
by parts can be checked without suppressing any endpoint terms. With
the square bracket called A, its exact integrand identity is

```text
s^(3/2) f A
 =4s^(7/2)(g')^2(26s g'+83g)
  +d_s[8s^(9/2)g(g')^2+40s^(7/2)g^2 g'+140s^(5/2)g^3].
```

The boundary term vanishes: g is smooth at zero, and at infinity a
rapidly decaying f gives `g=O(s^(-5/2))`, `g'=O(s^(-7/2))`.
Since `26s g'+83g=(13/2)f+18g` and `|S4|=8pi^2/3`, this proves

```text
C_return=-(64pi^2/105)int_0^infinity
                  s^(7/2)(g')^2[13f+36g] ds <0        (96)
```

for every nonzero seed in this class. Strictness follows also in the
far radial tail: the nonzero total source gives a positive leading
coefficient of g and a negative leading coefficient of g'. This is a
signed law for the first generated nonlinear return, not an estimate
for an arbitrary instantaneous pair of parent and source fields.

There is a related comparison at the critical observer itself. Radial
averaging gives `mean(q1)=-2f/5`. In the joint critical functional
`R_p(b,a)=int (b^2+a^2)^(p/2)`, the actual and caloric parent contributions
to its second initial derivative agree. Only the retained b2 deformation
differs. Using the full transport divergence yields

```text
R_p(b(t),a(t))-R_p(B(t),a_cal(t))
 =-((p-1)/5)t^2 int_R5 |b0|^(p+2)+o(t^2), p=5/2.      (97)
```

The Lp power functional is C2 for p>2. The lifted L2 and first-derivative
norms of b and a are controlled by the physical velocity and vorticity
norms, including their smooth local time jets. R5 Sobolev and interpolation
therefore give C2 time dependence into L(5/2), justifying this comparison.
Consequently the actual joint critical moment initially lies below its original caloric
forecast. This supplies no monotonicity of that forecast, no comparison
beyond its justified initial interval, and no full diffusion-history
budget on a prescribed arbitrary horizon. The radial hypothesis is absent
from the earlier positive critical-burst family (23)--(26); the two results
concern different seed geometries.

### An anisotropic test and the geometry the next estimate must retain

For `B0=1+r^2+z^2`, the explicitly nonradial potential family

```text
F=B0^(-3/2)+c z^2 B0^(-7/2),
f=-Delta5 F=[(15-2c)B0^2+63c z^2]/B0^(11/2)
```

has f>0 whenever `-12/11<c<15/2`, using `z^2/B0^2<=1/4`.
The associated b0=sqrt(f) gives smooth finite-energy physical data with
all physical L2 derivatives. These particular fixtures have algebraic
tails; the general radial statement above includes Schwartz seeds.
Exact beta integration gives

```text
C_return=(32768pi^2/727840488375)
          [46844c^3-22283310c^2+54483750c-69784875].     (98)
```

This is strictly negative throughout the source-positive interval. A
certificate for the polynomial P in brackets is

```text
P=-21931980(c-1816125/1462132)^2
  -52560048619125/1462132+46844c^2(c-15/2).
```

At c=0, independent radial and angular calculations both give
`C_return=-1015808pi^2/323323`. This robustness test does not make
the family invariant under NS.

In fact, for any radial seed the NONRADIAL part of its second nonlinear
source derivative is exactly

```text
(f2_nl)_nonradial=(12g f'-16g' f)(z^2-s/5).            (99)
```

This is a degree-two angular harmonic; its spherical Laplacian
eigenvalue is -10. For the explicit c=0 fixture, the entire nonlinear
jet is `f2_nl=45(3r^2+2z^2-4)/B0^7`, and its nonradial part is
`-45(z^2-s/5)/B0^7`, which is nonzero. Initial viscous contributions
are radial and do not remove this generated angular component.

Thus the first closed return is depleted, but its own evolution changes
the source geometry. The next necessary estimate is a signed bound on
that evolving angular defect and later parent returns, with diffusion
and the original allowance retained. Replacing every later source by
a fresh radial seed would discard precisely this information. Neither
(96) nor (98) supplies the open allowance K_seed in (89).

Run `python3 -O labs/generated_parent_return.py`. The checker verifies
the full viscous initial jets, both transport divergences, the signed
pairing, angular and radial integration identities, exact anisotropic
moments, strict polynomial sign and generated angular defect. Analytic
local existence and the Taylor remainder are not certified by the
symbolic calculations. No new Lean declarations or axioms are introduced.

## Angular history and a heat-smoothed circulation entropy

`angular_history_entropy.py` tests whether diffusion pays for the angular
change in (99). It identifies a failure of one natural angular measure,
bounds the first angular departure, and derives an alternative entropy
with the complete diffusion retained. The new physical estimates below
are analytic; exact symbolic checks certify their algebra, not their PDE
or continuation hypotheses. The scope here is axisymmetric R3.

### Angular contrast can increase under literal diffusion

Let P denote normalized angular averaging on S4 at fixed radius, p=5/2,
and define the nonnegative contrast

```text
A_p(b)=int_R5 [|b|^p-(P b^2)^(p/2)].                       (100)
```

It vanishes on radial absolute values. For `B=exp(-alpha |y|^2)` and
`h=(z^2-|y|^2/5)exp(-beta |y|^2)`, its second perturbation coefficient
at B is `(5/8)I`, where `I=int B^(1/2)h^2`. Under heat evolution of
BOTH B and h, the exact rate is

```text
I'/(nu I)=(13alpha^2-56alpha beta-72beta^2)/(alpha+4beta).
```

At alpha=6, beta=1 this equals 6, despite the degree-two angular
eigenvalue -10. The radial diffusion of the weight matters.

A compact radial cutoff gives an actual smooth unforced realization
without a nonuniform perturbation argument in the Gaussian tail.
Choose smooth chi(rho) equal to one below 3 and zero above 6, with
`0<=chi<=1`, `|chi'|<=2/3`, and replace h by chi h. For each fixed
cutoff, `b0=B+epsilon chi h` is positive for sufficiently small absolute
epsilon and gives Schwartz pure-swirl physical data. Initially v=q=0,
so the ACTUAL NS rate is exactly `b_t(0)=nu Delta5 b0`.
After integration by parts, the second contrast-rate coefficient is

```text
A_p'(0)=(5nu/8)epsilon^2 J(chi h)+o(epsilon^2),
J(h)=int exp(-3|y|^2)
       [-2|grad h|^2+24h y.grad h+36|y|^2 h^2].             (101)
```

For the uncut h, `I=2pi^(5/2)/5^(11/2)`, `J(h)=6I`, and
`J(h)/|S4|>9/31250`. The cutoff error divided by |S4| is at most
`(3724756896/3125)exp(-45)<116398653/3435973836800000`, which is
less than half that lower bound. To verify the bound, use
`|h|<=(4/5)rho^2 exp(-rho^2)` and
`|grad h|<=(8/5)rho(1+rho^2)exp(-rho^2)`. The error integrand is
bounded by `exp(-5s)(2048s+4672s^2+3968s^3)/25`, s=rho^2;
radial integration over rho>=3 uses `s^(3/2)<=s^2` and e>2.
Thus `J(chi h)>|S4|9/62500>0`. The perturbation is compactly
supported where B is bounded below, so differentiation in epsilon is
legitimate. Smooth local evolution gives an actual interval of increasing
contrast. This refutes heat monotonicity of (100), not regularity or a
full-datum history allowance.

### The first generated angular departure has a finite initial payment

For the radial seeds of (95), put `G=sup_(s>=0) s g(s)^2`, which is
finite from the original datum. The C2 contrast and actual Lp time jets
give

```text
A_p(b(t))=L_ang t^4+o(t^4),
L_ang=(pi^2/420)int_0^infinity
              s^(7/2) f^(-3/4)(12g f'-16g'f)^2 ds,
L_ang<=(18/35)G Dcrit(0)
       +(2/13)||f||_infinity^(1/4)(-C_return).              (102)
```

Here Dcrit is the complete initial weighted gradient in (7).
At zeros of b0 the integrand is interpreted continuously using
`f^(-3/4)(12g f'-16g'f)^2
 =4|b0|^(1/2)(12g b0'-8g'b0)^2`.
The nonradial part of b2 is `(12g b0'-8g'b0)(z^2-s/5)`.
The angular variance is `P[(z^2-s/5)^2]=8s^2/175`.
Expanding about the evolving radial angular mean, whose contrast and
first variation vanish, gives the fourth-order coefficient even though
the functional is only used as C2. The square bound
`(12g f'-16g'f)^2<=288g^2(f')^2+512(g')^2 f^2`
and the positive density of -C_return in (96) prove (102).
This is an initial-order comparison, not absorption with a universal
coefficient or payment for successive returns.

### A fixed heat reference with an exact physical cancellation

The full lifted swirl equation has conservative form
`b_t+div5(v b)=nu Delta5 b`, since `div5 v=-q`.
For any positive fixed heat reference `W_t=nu Delta5 W`, define

```text
e=W|b/W|^(5/2), E=int_R5 e,
D_W=int_R5 W|b/W|^(1/2)|grad(b/W)|^2.
E'+(15nu/4)D_W=(3/2)int_R5 (q-v.grad log W)e.             (103)
```

The Hessian of the perspective `W|b/W|^p` yields the complete
nonnegative square `p(p-1)W|b/W|^(p-2)|grad(b/W)|^2`.
The transport of W and the lifted divergence are both retained.
The formula extends across b=0 since p>2.

There is a reference adapted to physical cylindrical volume. Fix ell>0
from the original datum and horizon, without resetting its clock:

```text
d=ell^2+4nu t,
W(t,r)=(1-exp(-r^2/d))/r^2, W(t,0)=1/d,
x=r^2/d, theta=x/(exp(x)-1), theta(0)=1.
q-v.grad log W=theta q,
E'+(15nu/4)D_W=(3/2)int_R5 theta q e.                     (104)
```

W solves the four-transverse-dimensional heat equation, hence Delta5
heat, and is the heat average of r^(-2) at time
`t+ell^2/(4nu)`. Indeed, integrate the Gaussian heat average of
`exp(-a r^2)` over a>=0 and substitute `a/(1+4nu tau a)`;
the result is `int_0^(1/(4nu tau)) exp(-k r^2)dk`.
This stochastic averaging is a reference construction, not a force
applied to the fluid. The cancellation in (104) uses only
`u_r=-rq/2` and `1+(r/2)partial_r log W=theta`, so it retains
the FULL actual parent field. The lifted scalar density law does not
make the physical three-dimensional fluid compressible.

Since `int5 F=pi int3 r^2 F`, the entropy has physical form

```text
E=pi int_R3 |Gamma|^(5/2)/(1-exp(-r^2/d))^(3/2),
Gamma=r u_theta.                                       (105)
```

The elementary bounds
`0<W<=ell^(-2)`, `W^(-1)<=r^2+d`, `|grad log W|<=2/ell`
follow from `0<theta<=1` and `1-theta<=min(1,x)`.
They give finite original stock and coercivity:

```text
E(0)<=sqrt(2)[pi ||Gamma0||_(5/2)^(5/2)+ell^3 M(0)],
M<=ell^(-3)E,
Dcrit<=2ell^(-3)[D_W+4ell^(-2)E].                       (106)
```

These hypotheses hold for smooth rapidly decaying physical data in
this axisymmetric track. Weighted parabolic estimates on every existing
smooth prefix justify spatial cutoffs in (103); the needed growth of
W^(-1) is polynomial. This local justification is not a bound uniform
up to an unknown maximal time. The factor theta decreases exponentially
away from `r^2` comparable to d but equals one at the axis. The remaining
near-axis production is not eliminated.

### Known and far parents are paid; the near-history estimate remains open

Use the SAME actual no-swirl reference as (80)--(85):
`q=q_bar+q_a`, `a=L(eta-eta_bar)`,
`||a||_2<=sqrt(pi Ebar)`, `Ebar=E_s exp(2L_H)`.
Fix a spatial cutoff R>0 from the datum. With c=1/(2pi^3), let
`K_R(y)=c chi_cut(|y|/R)|y|^(-4)`, where chi_cut vanishes below one,
equals one above two, and has derivative at most 3/2 in absolute value.
Then, including its cutoff derivative,

```text
||grad K_R||_2<=d_R:=7c sqrt(|S4|/(5R^5)),
q_a,far=2partial_z(K_R*a),
||q_a,far||_infinity<=2d_R sqrt(pi Ebar),
kappa_far=3d_R sqrt(pi Ebar),
kappa_ref(t)=(3/2)||q_bar(t)||_infinity.                 (107)
```

The integral of kappa_ref is finite from the known global reference,
independently of the target swirl. In this entropy the exact full-field
cancellation already removed the separate transport term. Thus (107)
pays its complete far contribution without a separate spatial-moment
estimate. It is not uniform as R tends to zero.

Write `q_near=q_a-q_a,far`,
`P_near=(3/2)int theta q_near e`, and
`Omega(t)=exp(-int_0^t kappa_ref-kappa_far t)`.
A precise sufficient, still OPEN estimate is

```text
int_0^T Omega[P_near-(15nu/8)D_W]<=K(u0,nu,H,ell,R)       (108)
```

for every available smooth prefix T<=H, with finite K fixed from the
full original datum and no future target norm. If it holds, setting
`B=E(0)+K`, `Lambda_H=int_0^H kappa_ref+kappa_far H`, yields

```text
Omega(T)E(T)+(15nu/8)int_0^T Omega D_W<=B,
int_0^T S^2 <=(25C5/16)ell^(-36/5)
       [16/(15nu)+8H/ell^2]exp(12Lambda_H/5)B^(12/5).     (109)
```

This follows from (106) and the existing
`S^2<=(25C5/16)M^(7/5)Dcrit`, so it has the same analytic
axisymmetric continuation consumer as (8)--(10), including the finite
initial circulation bound. It is an alternative target, not a proof
of (108) or a replacement of the preceding joint-parent target (89).
All angular changes, surviving parents and subsequent cycles remain
in q_near. A sequence of individually finite payments cannot be summed
without one allowance for its full compatible history.

Run `python3 -O labs/angular_history_entropy.py`. Its exact checks cover
the Gaussian and cutoff signs, first angular coefficient and constants,
perspective Hessian, actual conservative equation, complete heat reference,
physical cancellation, far-kernel constants and conditional consumer
coefficients. No new Lean declarations or axioms are introduced.

## Arbitrarily many finite cellular pattern cycles

`cellular_pattern_cycles.py` constructs a test class in which genuine
spatial patterns undergo repeated approximate cycles under unforced
positive-viscosity NS. The number of cycles is any prescribed finite
integer; the original datum depends on that number and the accuracy.
The construction has a finite original-resource payment. It does not
produce mutually amplifying parents or an infinite concentrating cascade.

### An exact unforced family with a closed parent orbit

On the 2pi-periodic three-torus, fix nu>0 and A>0 and set

```text
v(x,y)=(sin y,-sin x), psi=cos x+cos y,
a(t)=A exp(-nu t),
u(t,x,y,z)=(a(t)sin y,-a(t)sin x,A w(t,x,y)),
p(t,x,y,z)=-a(t)^2 cos x cos y,
w_t+a(t)v.grad w=nu Delta2 w.                            (110)
```

This is the full three-dimensional NS equation with zero force, not a
Galerkin truncation. All fields are independent of z; incompressibility
holds, `Delta2 v=-v`, and `(v.grad)v=grad(cos x cos y)`.
The vertical component cannot affect its horizontal parent because its
only additional advective derivative is in z. The scalar parabolic
equation has a global smooth periodic solution for every smooth w0:
its drift has bounded derivatives on every finite horizon, so successive
Sobolev energy estimates and linear parabolic existence extend it there.
This existence statement is analytic here.

The autonomous flow Phi_sigma of v preserves psi. For c in (0,2),
the connected level psi=c around the origin is a smooth closed orbit.
Choose c=1, away from the central critical point and the separatrix.
Its period P0 is finite:

```text
P0=4 int_0^(pi/2) [cos x(2-cos x)]^(-1/2) dx
  approximately 8.626062589998572.                       (111)
```

The displayed decimal is a numerical illustration. The optional orbit
check evolves `(pi/2,0)` through nine third-period transitions. Its
reported return and level errors are floating-point diagnostics, not
certified enclosures or a fluid simulation.

### A quantitative construction of whole-pattern cycles

On a small fixed annulus of regular levels around c=1, choose a smooth
circle-valued phase theta with `v.grad theta=omega(psi)`, where
`omega(c)=2pi/P(c)`. A transverse section and flow time define this
phase; P is smooth on the compact regular annulus. Only cos(theta)
and its phase shifts are used, so no globally real-valued angle is
required. Let L_omega be a bound for |omega'| there.

Given N>=1 and an error epsilon>0, put S=N P0. Choose a smooth bump
chi supported in (-1,1), with `0<=chi<=1` and chi(0)=1, then choose
delta>0 small enough that the supported levels remain in the annulus
and `L_omega delta S<=epsilon/3`. Define, extending by zero outside,

```text
w0=chi((psi-1)/delta)cos(theta),
w_inv(sigma)=chi((psi-1)/delta)cos(theta-omega(psi)sigma),
Ustar(sigma)=(v,chi((psi-1)/delta)cos(theta-omega(1)sigma)). (112)
```

The seed is smooth and mean-zero. In these coordinates the area measure
is a function of psi times `dpsi dtheta`, and the phase cosine has zero
mean. Ustar is a nonconstant P0-periodic MOVIE of divergence-free fields;
it is a comparison, not itself asserted to be a viscous NS evolution.
w_inv is the exact inviscid passive solution under v, and
`||w_inv(sigma)-Ustar_vertical(sigma)||_infinity
 <=L_omega delta S` for 0<=sigma<=S.

Physical and parent time are related by

```text
sigma(t)=A(1-exp(-nu t))/nu,
t(sigma)=-log(1-nu sigma/A)/nu,
w_sigma+v.grad w=[nu/(A-nu sigma)]Delta2 w.               (113)
```

Take A>=2nu S. The difference w-w_inv solves this last advection-
diffusion equation with zero initial datum and source
`[nu/(A-nu sigma)]Delta2 w_inv`. The maximum principle yields

```text
||w-w_inv||_infinity<=M_S log(A/(A-nu S))<=2nu S M_S/A,
M_S=2(||D2 w0||_infinity+||grad w0||_infinity)exp(2S).     (114)
```

The explicit M_S follows from `||Dv||op<=1`, `||D2v||bilinear<=1`:
the first variation of Phi has norm at most exp(sigma), and its second
variation at most `exp(sigma)(exp(sigma)-1)`. The trace of the composed
Hessian gives (114). These constants are deliberately conservative.
The full velocity, normalized by the SAME original A, obeys

```text
sup_(0<=sigma<=S)||u(t(sigma))/A-Ustar(sigma)||_infinity
 <=sqrt(2)nu S/A+L_omega delta S+2nu S M_S/A.              (115)
```

Thus any finite
`A>=max(2nu S,3sqrt(2)nu S/epsilon,6nu S M_S/epsilon)`
makes this error at most epsilon. First choose N and delta, then A;
M_S is a finite norm of that chosen ORIGINAL seed, not of an unknown
future flow. For normalized torus volume,
`E0=(A^2/2)(1+mean(w0^2))<=A^2`.

Sampling at `sigma=jP0/2` gives A--B--A cycles; sampling at
`sigma=jP0/3` gives A--B--C--A cycles. The ideal two states have sup
distance 2, and the three states have pairwise sup distance sqrt(3),
attained on the central orbit where chi=1. More generally m>=2 phases
give an m-state cycle, with adjacent separation `2sin(pi/m)`; choose
epsilon smaller than a quarter of that separation to distinguish the
actual states. All N circuits use one datum and one evolving solution.
The physical sampling intervals need not be equal. This proves
arbitrarily many finite approximate whole-pattern returns, not an exact
full-state return, a cycle count uniform in initial data, or an arbitrarily
long physical duration at a fixed normalized amplitude and fixed datum.

### The cycles have a finite, nonrenewable original payment

Differentiating the actual passive equation and retaining its complete
diffusion gives, with g=grad w and H=D2 w,

```text
(partial_t+a v.grad-nu Delta2)|g|^2
 =-2a(cos y-cos x)w_x w_y-2nu|H|^2 <=2a|g|^2.
||grad w(t)||_infinity<=||grad w0||_infinity exp(sigma(t))
                     <=||grad w0||_infinity exp(A/nu).   (116)
```

The inequality uses `|cos y-cos x|<=2` and `2|w_x w_y|<=|g|^2`;
the norm conclusion uses the periodic parabolic maximum principle.
The actual curl is `(A w_y,-A w_x,-a(cos x+cos y))`, so

```text
int_0^H ||curl u||_infinity
 <=H A ||grad w0||_infinity exp(A/nu)+2A/nu < infinity.   (117)
```

There is also an all-time absolute receiver-stretching payment. Put
`E=||grad(Aw)||_2^2`, `D=||D2(Aw)||_2^2`, and
`G=-a int (cos y-cos x)(Aw)_x(Aw)_y`. Then
`E'=2G-2nu D`, `|G|<=aE`, and `r(t)=a(t)/nu` satisfies r'=-a.
The nonnegative reserve `R=E(exp(2r)-1)` therefore satisfies

```text
R'+2|G|<=0,
int_0^T 2|G|<=E(0)(exp(2A/nu)-1), for every T>=0.        (118)
```

The same reserve persists at every seam. The parent clock never reaches
A/nu: N full parent circuits imply `N<A/(nu P0)`. Raising the original
energy permits more circuits, but no circuit manufactures a fresh parent
allowance. This example consequently cannot develop the finite-time
vorticity divergence of a singular forced construction. It does not
exclude reproducing selected forced observations on a regular interval,
nor does it control a larger class in which parents replenish one another.

`MettapediaNS.CellularCycleReserve` certifies the horizontal differential
equations with their actual pressure, clock derivatives and bound, seam
payment, finite-turn arithmetic, gradient reaction inequality and envelope,
and the receiver payment under its explicit energy-law hypotheses.
The complete passive PDE construction, annular phase coordinates,
approximate cycles (115), maximum-principle passage (116) and integrated
physical conclusions remain analytic. They are not Lean existence theorems.

Separately, `MettapediaNS.WholeSpaceEnergyReturn` applies the certified
actual whole-space kinetic rate: exact return of the velocity forces
zero gradient energy at every interior time. Positive interior gradient
energy rules out such a return. This formal result concerns smooth
whole-space L2 evolutions with nu>0; it is not a new torus classification.
It excludes neither (115) nor rescaled or concentrating histories.

Run `python3 -O labs/cellular_pattern_cycles.py` for exact symbolic checks
of the full NS reduction, passive-gradient identity, physical curl, clock
and comparison constants. Add `--orbit` for the separate numerical orbit
illustration. The reusable physical specification is: an actual solution,
a retained parent clock, separated comparison states, a quantified tracking
error, and one original reserve. Any extension to interacting parents must
re-establish both tracking and payment for the enlarged actual system.

## A finite-energy finite-time cascade ledger with unbounded stretching

`MettapediaNS.GeometricCascadeLedger` certifies a distinction needed when
interpreting cycles. An exact return of a dissipating full state is
impossible, but finite energy expenditure alone does not exclude an
abstract sequence of successively smaller events. For nu>0, take

```text
ell_n=2^(-n),
energy_n=nu^2 ell_n,
duration_n=ell_n^2/nu,
vorticity_n=nu/ell_n^2,
reserve_n=2nu^2 ell_n.                                  (119)
```

The length, costs, durations, vorticity scales and reserves are positive.
The Lean theorems prove

```text
reserve_n-reserve_(n+1)=energy_n,
sum_n energy_n=2nu^2,
sum_n duration_n=4/(3nu),
duration_n*vorticity_n=1,
sum_(n<N) duration_n*vorticity_n=N.                      (120)
```

In particular the positive stretching partial sums exceed every prescribed
real bound, although both resource series converge. The proof uses
unbounded partial sums, not the value of a totalized real infinite sum
for a divergent series. The reserve never becomes negative or refills.

These numbers match the usual dimensional assignments of a localized
event with velocity scale nu/ell: kinetic energy is velocity squared
times volume, the viscous time is ell squared over nu, and vorticity is
velocity over length. They are a SCALING MODEL, not a sequence of actual
NS fields. No pressure compatibility, incompressibility, nonlinear transfer,
or existence of an evolution realizing them has been established here.
The result refutes the abstract implication from finite energy and finite
time to bounded accumulated stretching. The physical crux is whether the
actual geometry and compatible parent histories permit such a sequence.

## Actual three-dimensional pattern cycles with reciprocal feedback

`reciprocal_pattern_cycles.py` extends (110)--(117) to genuinely
three-dimensional data with nonzero hidden-to-parent transfer. For every
nu>0, finite N>=1, m>=2 and `0<eta<sin(pi/m)/2`, it gives one actual
global smooth unforced periodic solution tracking N complete approximate
m-state whole-pattern cycles to error eta. The initial datum depends on
N and eta. The PDE construction, estimates and continuation below are
ANALYTIC, not new Lean theorems or numerical flow enclosures.

### Reference and full nonlinear stability

Use normalized period-2pi T3, the original annular seed w0, and the
actual reference `U=(a sin y,-a sin x,A w(t,x,y))` from (110).
Write `||f||Hm^2=sum_(|alpha|<=m)||partial^alpha f||2^2`.
Its complete scalar transport commutator is

```text
[partial^alpha,v.grad]w
 =sum_(0<beta<=alpha) binom(alpha,beta)
       (partial^beta v).grad partial^(alpha-beta)w.
```

Only x,y derivatives occur. Each derivative of a nonzero component of v
has supremum at most one. Pair the differentiated equations with their
respective derivatives of w. Principal transport cancels; each remaining
product is bounded by `||w||H4^2`. There are two vector components, j+1
multi-indices at order j, and binomial sum `2^j-1`. Mean zero gives
Poincare for every term in the diffusion. Consequently

```text
C4=2 sum_(j=1..4)(j+1)(2^j-1)=228,
||w(t)||H4<=||w0||H4 exp[-nu t+228 sigma(t)],
||U(t)||H4<=Q exp(-nu t),
Q=A sqrt(5+||w0||H4^2 exp(456 A/nu)).                    (121)
```

The horizontal squared H4 norm is exactly `5a(t)^2`. Regularizing
vanishing norms justifies the scalar comparison. Q is finite from the
original seed and amplitude, with no unknown future target norm.

Let u solve the full NS equation from `U(0)+d0`. Its difference d=u-U
satisfies the actual equation

```text
d_t+U.grad d+d.grad U+d.grad d+grad(p_u-p_U)=nu Delta d,
div d=0.                                                (122)
```

Every differentiated pressure term is orthogonal to its solenoidal test.
It remains in the evolution. The H3 commutator estimate, H3 embedding
into W1,infinity and the H4 reference give a fixed torus/norm constant
C3>0 such that, with `Y=||d||H3^2`,

```text
Y'+2nu D4<=C3 ||U||H4 Y+C3 Y^(3/2),
D4=sum_(|alpha|<=3)||grad partial^alpha d||2^2>=Y.
```

This reuses the standard continuous stability argument in the
[paid reciprocal neighborhood](#returned-parent-work-and-a-paid-reciprocal-neighborhood).
Set `M=C3 Q/nu` and require `sqrt(Y0)exp(M/2)<=nu/(2C3)`.
Inside `sqrt(Y)<nu/C3`, absorb the complete self term with nu D4 to obtain

```text
Y(t)<=Y0 exp[M(1-exp(-nu t))-nu t].                       (123)
```

This stays strictly inside the bootstrap region. Smooth local existence
and H3 continuation therefore construct one global smooth unforced NS
solution with all generated modes retained.
The constants are fixed Sobolev constants and original-data quantities.

Apply (112)--(115) first with error eta/2, choosing the annular seed and
A from N and eta; `S=N P0`, `A>=2nu S`. For a fixed embedding constant
`||d||infinity<=Cemb ||d||H3`, impose also

```text
sqrt(Y0)exp(M/2)<=eta A/(2Cemb).                         (124)
```

Then (123) and the reference tracking theorem give
`sup_(0<=sigma<=S)||u(t(sigma))/A-Ustar(sigma)||infinity<=eta`.
Both A and `t(sigma)=-log(1-nu sigma/A)/nu` remain the ORIGINAL ones.
This is a sampling/comparison clock, not an assertion that perturbed
material trajectories follow the reference streamlines. The samples
`sigma=jP0/m`, j=0,...,mN, give N cycles with adjacent actual states
separated by at least `2sin(pi/m)-2eta>0`. Each return has error at most
eta from its corresponding ideal state. No clock or normalization is
reset. Exact recurrence or an infinite concentrating cascade is not claimed.

### An explicit internal transfer and a reserve for its whole history

The nonzero, real, mean-zero solenoidal perturbation

```text
d0=epsilon[(1,0,-1)cos(x+z)+s(1,1,0)cos(x-y+z)], s=+1 or -1,
Y0=30epsilon^2,
0<sqrt(30)|epsilon|exp(M/2)
 <=min(nu/(2C3),eta A/(2Cemb))                           (125)
```

satisfies both thresholds. Such an epsilon exists after N, eta, w0 and
A are fixed. The threshold may be extremely small; no practical-sized
perturbation or numerical evaluation of that threshold is asserted.

For `v=(sin y,-sin x,0)`, `||v||2=1`, put `alpha=<u,v>`. The projected
equation along the ENTIRE actual history is

```text
alpha'+nu alpha=F,
F=<d tensor d,grad v>=mean (cos y-cos x)d_x d_y,
|F|<=||d||2^2<=Y,
F(0)=s epsilon^2/4.                                    (126)
```

Here `Delta v=-v` and `(v.grad)v=grad(cos x cos y)`. Both cross terms
with the horizontal reference cancel by incompressibility; its vertical
component cannot contract a derivative of v. These identities hold for
the arbitrary evolving vertical reference. Canonical pressure cancels
only in this solenoidal projection. For s=+1, positive nonlinear parent
work persists on a nonempty interval by smoothness. Positivity throughout
a complete turn or growth overcoming viscosity is not asserted.

Let `h=u-alpha v`, the full orthogonal remainder, distinct from d.
Since `<h,v>=0` and `Delta v=-v`, the actual kinetic identities are

```text
(alpha^2/2)'=-nu alpha^2+alpha F,
(||h||2^2/2)'=-nu||grad h||2^2-alpha F.                  (127)
```

The powers `alpha F` and `-alpha F` cancel exactly. This is a modal
energy-exchange interface, not a newly identified spatial boundary port.
The supplying fluid follows its full equation and pays the transfer.

Equation (123) gives a nonnegative reserve on every available interval:

```text
B(t)=Y(t)exp(M exp(-nu t))/nu,
B'+|F|<=0,
integral_s^t |F|<=B(s)-B(t),
integral_0^infinity |F|<=30epsilon^2 exp(M)/nu.           (128)
```

For `beta=alpha-a`, `beta'+nu beta=F`, beta(0)=0. Absolute continuity
gives `(|beta|)'+nu|beta|<=|F|` almost everywhere, including its zero-set
interpretation. Therefore

```text
R(t)=a(t)/nu+|beta(t)|/nu+B(t)/nu>=0,
R'+|alpha|<=0,
R(0)=A/nu+30epsilon^2 exp(M)/nu^2.                       (129)
```

This pays the parent amplitude while allowing replenishment. Duhamel also
gives `|alpha(t)-a(t)|<=Y0 exp(M)t exp(-nu t)`.

The full field has a continuation payment: set `K=Q+sqrt(Y0)exp(M/2)`.
Then `||u(t)||H3<=K exp(-nu t/2)`. For a fixed Sobolev constant Cg,
the actual cubic production `g=mean omega^T grad(u) omega` satisfies

```text
R_g(t)=4 Cg K^3 exp(-3nu t/2)/(3nu),
2 integral_s^t |g|<=R_g(s)-R_g(t).                       (130)
```

The finite-horizon signed renewal allowance may be
`R_g(0)+2|g(0)|H`. These are actual globally paid three-dimensional
cycles in a perturbative neighborhood. The arbitrary-data history
estimate and an infinite-cascade realization remain open.

### Composition and the hidden phase

The opposite phases in (125) have the same alpha(0), total initial energy,
Y0, reference and cycle-error allowance, but opposite F(0). The observed
pattern label and these scalar resources do not determine the next
parent derivative. Exact reconstruction must preserve a compatible
hidden history; a bounding summary may instead preserve a proved envelope.

For `P u=<u,v>v` and `N(u)=-Leray[(u.grad)u]`, P commutes with Delta.
The full remainder consequently satisfies

```text
h(t)=exp(nu t Delta)h0
 +integral_0^t exp(nu(t-s)Delta)(I-P)N(alpha(s)v+h(s)) ds,
F(t)=mean (cos y-cos x)h_x(t)h_y(t).                    (131)
```

The SAME h must supply F and both endpoints. This nonlinear Volterra
constraint cannot be replaced by freely prescribed forcing. The related
`FilteredHistory.hidden_mode_history` is Lean-certified for diagonal
Fourier multipliers; this rank-one P is not asserted to be that instance.

Adjacent physical segments retain full u at the seam, original reference,
time and constants. Equation (128) then telescopes. This is a concrete
analytic consumer of `BoundaryBellman.CostedRelation.Bounds.comp` and
`Bounds.iterate`, together with `PlanarParentReserve.interval_payment`.
Their generic composition algebra is already in Lean; this periodic
physical instantiation is not newly formalized. The actual-solution
gluing in `WholeSpaceHistoryBridge.Segment.comp` has whole-space scope.

Run `python3 -O labs/reciprocal_pattern_cycles.py`. Twelve exact rational
fixtures cover both phases, two parameter choices and three unrelated
vertical receivers. An independent symbolic physical-space integral
checks generic F(0). Every canonical output, including new modes, is
retained. The checks verify full kinetic transfer, H3/H4 sizes and the
reserve/envelope algebra. Smooth PDE existence, bootstrap, continuation
and the full-cycle comparison above remain analytic.
The rational fixture amplitudes test algebra and are not asserted to meet
the conservative global stability threshold (125).

## Reversing internal transfer along an actual cyclic history

`cellular_transfer_reversal.py` gives a finite exact residual certificate
for a change in the direction of energy exchange in the preceding class.
The complete analytic comparison below promotes it to actual nonlinear,
positive-viscosity NS solutions. In one such solution the parent first
receives nonlinear work and later supplies nonlinear work. Both signs
persist on nonempty time intervals. This is not a claim that the parent's
total energy grows despite viscosity, or that the reversal repeats forever.

### The reference and the precise physical claim

Retain the same normalized period-2pi torus and original clock sigma.
Scale the annular receiver by a positive number rho, so that

```text
U=(a v,A rho w), a=A exp(-nu t), v=(sin y,-sin x,0),
w_sigma+v.grad w=mu Delta2 w, mu=1/(Re-sigma), Re=A/nu,
||w0||infinity<=1, G0=||grad w0||infinity,
d0=epsilon[(1,0,-1)cos(x+z)+(1,1,0)cos(x-y+z)], epsilon>0.
```

The new small factor rho permits a controlled comparison with the
cellular horizontal parent. Its pattern is still nonconstant, and the
cycle accuracy below is proportional to rho, so the states remain
distinguishable. Require

```text
Re>=2000,
gamma=6rho(1+3G0)+252epsilon/A<=1/300.                   (132)
```

Also retain the global H3 stability hypothesis (125), with the reference
norm in (121) replaced by
`Q=A sqrt(5+rho^2||w0||H4^2 exp(456A/nu))`.
For the resulting actual global solution put d=u-U and
`alpha=<u,v>`. At `T=3/4` in the ORIGINAL clock, the claim is

```text
F(0)=epsilon^2/4>0,
F(t(T))<=-epsilon^2/16<0,
alpha(t(sigma))>A/3 for 0<=sigma<=T,                    (133)
F=mean (cos y-cos x)d_x d_y, t(T)=-log(1-T/Re)/nu.
```

Thus the opposite nonlinear powers `alpha F` and `-alpha F` in (127)
reverse sign on this same history. No source is prescribed independently
of the supplying fluid. Smoothness gives positive and negative open
intervals and at least one intervening zero of F.

### A finite polynomial with a complete residual

Let P be the Leray projection and define
`L r=-P[(v.grad)r+(r.grad)v]`. Starting from `c0=d0/epsilon`, form
`c_(j+1)=L c_j/(j+1)` and `p(sigma)=sum_(j=0..8)c_j sigma^j`.
Every coefficient includes both conjugate vertical-frequency blocks.
There is no spatial truncation of L or of its generated outputs. In
particular the exact residual is
`p'-L p=-9c9 sigma^8`.

The checker uses rational arithmetic, with outward rational square-root
bounds for norms. Three coefficients are independently checked against
the complete convection and canonical pressure formula. On 0<=sigma<=T
the certified finite inequalities are

```text
||p||2<=3, ||grad p||infinity<=42, ||Delta p||2<=51/5,
integral_0^T ||p'-L p||2 <=1/1000,
||p(T)||2<=7/5,
Fcal(p(T))<=-18/125,
Fcal(r)=mean (cos y-cos x)r_x r_y.                      (134)
```

The gradient bound uses the sum of absolute values of all Fourier
derivative entries and therefore bounds the operator norm. The residual
bound is the exact test `T^18||c9||2^2<=10^(-6)`.
The degree-eight endpoint has 159 modes in the positive vertical block,
with their conjugates retained. The polynomial is an approximation for
comparison, not an invariant finite-mode fluid or an exact solution.

### The actual nonlinear error, including receiver and viscosity

Set `y=d/epsilon`, `q=y-p`, `b=A rho/a` and `c=epsilon/a`.
The actual normalized perturbation obeys

```text
y_sigma=L y+mu Delta y
 -b P[w partial_z y+(y_h.grad w)e_z]-c P[(y.grad)y].
```

All modes generated by the last term are part of y. Since
`W=U/a=(v,bw)` and y are divergence-free, the q equation can be written
with transport `(W+c y).grad q`, which cancels in its L2 energy test.
Its other q terms are `q.grad W+c q.grad p`. Its forcing is

```text
-(p'-L p)+mu Delta p
 -b P[w partial_z p+(p_h.grad w)e_z]-c P[(p.grad)p].
```

The pressure has not been omitted: P is orthogonal, and the equivalent
pressure terms pair to zero against q. Complete diffusion is nonpositive
in this energy test. The maximum principle for the actual reference gives
`||w||infinity<=1` and `||grad w||infinity<=G0 exp(sigma)<=3G0`.
On the interval, `b<=2rho`, `c<=2epsilon/A`, and the polynomial has
only vertical frequencies +/-1, so `||partial_z p||2=||p||2`.
Consequently the last two forcing terms have combined norm at most
gamma, and the q energy growth coefficient is at most `1+gamma/3`.
With z=||q||2 and z(0)=0, regularization at z=0 yields

```text
z' <=(1+gamma/3)z+9||c9||2 sigma^8+mu||Delta p||2+gamma.
```

Because `(1+1/900)T<1` and exp(1)<3, Gronwall and (134) give, uniformly
over the entire interval,

```text
z <=3[1/1000+T(51/5)/(2000-T)+T/300]
  <=3/200+3/400=9/400.                                 (135)
```

This compares the full nonlinear PDE directly with the polynomial.
It needs no assertion that a numerically integrated Galerkin orbit
approximates the unknown flow. The earlier global stability argument
supplies existence; every constant here is fixed from the original data.

The symmetric part of grad v has operator norm at most one. Hence
`|Fcal(y)-Fcal(p)|<=(2||p||2+||q||2)||q||2`, and at T,

```text
Fcal(y(T))<=-18/125+(14/5+9/400)(9/400)
          =-12879/160000<=-1/16.                        (136)
```

Equation (126) says exactly `F=epsilon^2 Fcal(y)`, proving the second
sign in (133). Furthermore (132) implies epsilon/A<=1/75600<1/20.
Since a>=A/2 and `||y||2<=3+9/400`, throughout the interval
`alpha>=A/2-epsilon(3+9/400)>A/3`. This proves the stated power signs,
not just the sign of an auxiliary coefficient.

### Compatibility with any prescribed finite pattern cycles

For fixed nu>0, finite N, m>=2 and `0<eta<sin(pi/m)/2`, first choose
the original annular seed and delta with `L_omega delta S<=eta/6`,
where S=N P0. Then choose rho>0 small enough that
`6rho(1+3G0)<=1/600`. With M_S from (114), choose finite A satisfying

```text
A>=max(2000nu,2nu S,6sqrt(2)nu S/(rho eta),12nu S M_S/eta).
```

The reference has whole-pattern error at most rho eta/2 from
`Ustar_rho=(v,rho chi cos(theta-omega(1)sigma))`.
Finally choose epsilon>0 satisfying both
`252epsilon/A<=1/600` and

```text
sqrt(30)epsilon exp(M/2)
 <=min(nu/(2C3),rho eta A/(2Cemb)), M=C3 Q/nu.            (137)
```

Such an epsilon exists after the original reference is fixed. Equations
(123)--(124) give whole-pattern error at most rho eta along all N turns.
Adjacent sampled states stay separated by
`2rho sin(pi/m)-2rho eta>0`. Their amplitude can be small; no fixed
lower bound independent of the chosen seed is asserted. Since P0>=2pi,
T=3/4 lies strictly within the first turn. Thus both transfer directions
occur in a single actual flow which also makes the prescribed finite
approximate cycles. No claim that every turn repeats this transfer pattern
or that the perturbation is large follows.

The same original reserves (128)--(130) still pay the whole history.
This example excludes a general rule that an initially supplying
component keeps that role. A compositional description may label the
two transfer directions, but it must retain the compatible hidden state
and the original remaining reserve when joining them. The sufficient
arbitrary-data history estimate remains open.

Run `python3 -O labs/cellular_transfer_reversal.py`. All finite bounds
and canonical-pressure checks above use exact arithmetic. The actual
PDE comparison, existence and cycle construction are analytic and are
not newly Lean-certified. No numerical plot or initial-time identity
is used in place of the interval estimate (135).

## Parent refeeding with a paid energy-exchange loop

`cellular_parent_refeeding.py` extends the actual comparison method
(132)--(137) to a different four-mode perturbation. On ONE unforced
positive-viscosity solution, the same parent is fed, supplies the other
modes, and is fed again. These are physical modal power signs, not
independently prescribed controls. The three observations fit inside
the first turn of the preceding finite pattern-cycle construction.

### A fully specified seed and three signed observations

Retain `U=(a v,A rho w)`, the original annular w0, and all notation
from (132). Let `u0=U(0)+epsilon r0`, where epsilon>0 and

```text
10 r0=(1,-2,-1)cos(x+z)+(-4,-2,2)cos(x-y+z)
      +(-3,-5,6)cos(2x+z)+(4,10,2)cos(2x-y+z),
||r0||2^2=11/10, ||r0||H3^2=259/2.                     (138)
```

Each polarization is perpendicular to its own frequency. The field is
real, mean-zero and genuinely three-dimensional. Set `T=3/4` and require

```text
Re=A/nu>=200000,
gamma=8rho(1+3G0)+824epsilon/A<=1/10000.                 (139)
```

Retain global H3 stability as in (123), now with
`Y0=(259/2)epsilon^2` and the same scaled reference Q as in (132).
For the actual parent coefficient alpha and transfer F in (126), the
three claimed observations are

```text
F(t(0))=3epsilon^2/400,
F(t(3/8))<=-epsilon^2/200,
F(t(3/4))>=epsilon^2/400,
alpha(t(sigma))>A/3 for all 0<=sigma<=3/4.              (140)
```

Thus `alpha F` has signs positive, negative, positive on three nonempty
intervals, with at least two intervening zeros. The opposite power in
the full orthogonal remainder has the reversed signs. This is a
recurrence of an observed transfer direction, not an exact return of
the complete fluid state or a proof of indefinitely repeated refeeding.

### Exact residual control of the complete physical history

Use the SAME complete operator `L=-P(v.grad+(.grad)v)` as above, but
start `c0=r0` and take `p=sum_(j=0..16)c_j sigma^j` with
`c_(j+1)=L c_j/(j+1)`. The residual is exactly
`p'-L p=-17c17 sigma^16`. No generated mode is discarded.
The exact rational checks give, uniformly over 0<=sigma<=T,

```text
||p||2<=4, ||grad p||infinity<=103, ||Delta p||2<=31,
integral_0^T ||p'-L p||2<=1/12000,
||p(3/8)||2, ||p(3/4)||2<=11/10,
Fcal(p(3/8))<=-1/100, Fcal(p(3/4))>=1/200.              (141)
```

The checker tests the integrated residual by
`T^34||c17||2^2<=(1/12000)^2`, with both conjugate frequency blocks
included. It independently reconstructs the canonical pressure at
degrees zero, two and four. The observation polynomial has 610 modes
in its positive vertical block and the residual has 682, together
with their conjugates. These are finite exact approximations, not a
closed finite-dimensional invariant subspace.

Apply the full nonlinear q equation preceding (135) to
`q=(u-U)/epsilon-p`. Its unknown-velocity transport still cancels in
L2; the entire viscosity, receiver contribution and nonlinear source
remain. The changed polynomial bounds make the extra forcing at most
gamma and the norm growth coefficient at most `1+gamma/4`.
As `(1+1/40000)T<1`, the same analytic comparison gives

```text
sup_(0<=sigma<=T)||q||2
 <=3[1/12000+31T/(200000-T)+T/10000]
 <=3/5000+9/40000=33/40000<1/1000.                     (142)
```

At either observation the error in Fcal is therefore at most
`(11/5+1/1000)/1000=2201/1000000`. The negative and positive margins
in (141) remain strict and imply (140). The initial value in (140)
is computed directly from (138). Condition (139) also implies
`epsilon/A<=1/8240000<1/30`; hence
`alpha>=A/2-epsilon(4+1/1000)>A/3` on the complete interval.
Every estimate concerns the same actual nonlinear NS solution.

### The exchange loop consumes energy and preserves its original reserve

For the normalized periodic kinetic energy `Ekin=||u||2^2/2`,
the literal unforced energy law and projection onto v yield

```text
Ekin'=-nu||grad u||2^2,
<grad u,grad v>=<u,v>=alpha, ||grad v||2=1,
||grad u||2^2>=alpha^2>A^2/9.
```

Since `dt/dsigma=1/a>=1/A`, each of the two observation intervals
has physical duration at least `3/(8A)`. In particular,

```text
Ekin(t(0))-Ekin(t(3/8))>=nu A/24,
Ekin(t(3/8))-Ekin(t(3/4))>=nu A/24.                    (143)
```

These are bounds for these fixed observation gaps in this constructed
class, not a universal energy price for every possible renewal event.
The repeated qualitative label therefore conceals strictly different
full states with less kinetic energy. Positive nonlinear power is not
asserted to overcome viscous loss in the parent's own total energy.

There is also an explicit payment for the absolute nonlinear exchange
itself. From the retained global perturbation bound set

```text
C_alpha=A+sqrt(Y0)exp(M/2),
B(t)=Y(t)exp(M exp(-nu t))/nu,
R_power(t)=C_alpha B(t),
R_power'+|alpha F|<=0,
integral_s^t |alpha F|<=R_power(s)-R_power(t).           (144)
```

Here `|alpha|<=C_alpha` and `B'+|F|<=0` hold along the entire global
history, by the same proof as (123) and (128). Its initial allowance
is `C_alpha Y0 exp(M)/nu`, finite from the full original datum. To
count the absolute powers of both components, use `2R_power`.
No allowance is restarted when the sign or observed pattern changes.

For any prescribed finite number of approximate m-state pattern cycles,
choose the annular seed and delta as before, then positive rho making
its contribution to (139) at most 1/20000. Choose finite A for the
pattern comparison and `A>=200000nu`. Finally choose epsilon>0 with
`824epsilon/A<=1/20000` and
`sqrt(259/2)epsilon exp(M/2)<=min(nu/(2C3),rho eta A/(2Cemb))`.
This gives the same proportionate whole-pattern accuracy and global
existence as (137), together with all three signs (140). The amplitudes
may be extremely small, and no repetition of the transfer word on
every subsequent turn is claimed.

As a physical consumer for compositional histories, the observed word
`feeding -- returning -- feeding` has an actual smooth witness. A
summary that records only these labels would hide the energy loss
and changing parent correlations. Joining histories must retain their
compatible endpoint fields and remaining reserve, as in the existing
costed-history interface. No general fluid language or arbitrary-history
continuation budget is inferred from this one witnessed word.

Run `python3 -O labs/cellular_parent_refeeding.py`. The residual and
finite inequalities are checked with exact arithmetic. The nonlinear
comparison, global solution and pattern-cycle construction remain
analytic, not newly Lean-certified. Floating-point search was used
only to find the seed; none of its output is a proof premise.

Residual-based validation belongs to the established a posteriori approach;
see [Morosi and Pizzocchero](https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.3832), especially
their Sobolev control inequalities and exact-solution comparison theorem.
Here the L2 error inequality is derived explicitly for the transfer
observable, while the preceding H3 stability argument supplies global
existence for this restricted class. These distinct uses of error control
must not be combined into an unsupported arbitrary-data existence claim.

## Stretching through the parent refeeding loop

`refeeding_stretching.py` connects the actual exchange in (140) to
the cubic vorticity production
`g(u)=mean curl(u)^T grad(u) curl(u)`.
For the same four-mode seed and sufficiently small parameters specified
below, define the physical excess over the ORIGINAL evolving reference:

```text
G(sigma)=[g(u(t(sigma)))-g(U(t(sigma)))]/[a(t(sigma))epsilon^2].
G(0)<=-1/20, G(3/8)>=3/16, G(3/4)>=3/4.               (145)
```

These inequalities concern one actual nonlinear unforced history. They
coexist with the parent-transfer signs positive, negative, positive in
(140). Thus refeeding can accompany either depletion or enhancement of
the excess stretching. When rho=0 the reference is purely cellular and
g(U)=0, so (145) concerns the literal total cubic production. For rho>0
it is the reference-subtracted production; the receiver's own stretching
is retained in g(U). Positive production does not assert net enstrophy
growth after viscous dissipation, or failure of a finite-data budget.

### The quadratic stretching observable

For any smooth solenoidal field r on the normalized torus let

```text
C(r)=<-Delta r,L r>+Fcal(r),
L r=-P[(v.grad)r+(r.grad)v], v=(sin y,-sin x,0).
g(a v+epsilon r)=a epsilon^2 C(r)+epsilon^3 g(r).        (146)
```

Indeed `g(u)=<-Delta u,-P[(u.grad)u]>`, `-Delta v=v`, the
projected self-advection of v is zero, and `<v,L r>=0` by
incompressibility. These facts remove the constant and linear terms.
The checker verifies the complete expansion independently through the
physical curl for the seed and a separate complex Fourier fixture.

After integrating its principal transport by parts, the quadratic form
satisfies `|C(r)|<=3||r||H1^2`. To see the derivative count, the
gradient pairing is bounded by
`2||grad r||2^2+||r||2||grad r||2`, and `|Fcal(r)|<=||r||2^2`.
Consequently its symmetric polarization obeys
`|C(r,s)|<=3||r||H1||s||H1`, and
`|C(r)-C(s)|<=3(||r||H1+||s||H1)||r-s||H1`.
This cancellation is why an H1 comparison suffices for C despite its
displayed Laplacian and first-order operator.

For the SAME degree-sixteen polynomial p used in (141), exact rational
arithmetic gives the additional derivative-level bounds

```text
integral_0^T ||p'-L p||H1<=1/1500,
sup_(0<=sigma<=T)||Delta p||H1<=116,
||p(3/8)||H1, ||p(3/4)||H1<=11/4,
C(r0)=-3/40, C(p(3/8))>=8/25, C(p(3/4))>=9/10.        (147)
```

Here T=3/4 and the complete residual is still `-17c17 sigma^16`.
No later polynomial state has been substituted for an actual solution.

### Original-data bounds for the generated mean and the error

All constants below are fixed from the original annular seed and torus
Sobolev inequalities. Choose fixed positive constants C3,C1,Cb,Ce large
enough for these usual estimates: linearized transport by W has norm
growth at most `C3||W||H4` in H3 and `C1||W||H4` in H1; its nonlinear
H3 energy term is at most `C3 c||y||H3^2` in the norm differential
inequality; `||grad y||infinity<=Ce||y||H3`. For
`B(r,s)=-P[(r.grad)s]`, also require

```text
||B(r,s)+B(s,r)||H1<=Cb||r||H3||s||H3,
||B(r,r)||H1<=Cb||r||H3^2.
```

These are Sobolev product/commutator estimates, not assumptions about
the unknown solution. They use the same multi-index norms as (121);
choose C3 large enough to serve the earlier global estimate as well.
Put delta=epsilon/A, assume 0<=rho<=1 and Re>=200000, and define

```text
Kw=||w0||H4 exp(228T), V=sqrt(5)+2Kw,
K=2sqrt(259/2) exp(C3 V T),
J=2Cb K^2 T exp(C1 V T), Gw=Ce Kw,
delta<=1/(4C3 K T).                                   (148)
```

The actual passive reference has `||w||H4<=Kw`, uniformly in Re,
since its diffusion is dissipative. Thus `W=U/a=(v,bw)` has H4 norm
at most V, with b=A rho/a<=2rho. For y=(u-U)/epsilon its H3 norm z
satisfies `z'<=C3 V z+2delta C3 z^2`. Inside z<=K, integration and
(148) give `z<= (K/2)exp(1/2)<K`. The bootstrap therefore bounds
`||y||H3<=K` on the entire interval. Global existence is still supplied
by the earlier H3 neighborhood theorem; this additional short-interval
bound is uniform in the parameters and contains no future target norm.

Let bar(y) be the average over the vertical coordinate. Its initial
value is zero. Averaging commutes with the Leray projection, diffusion
and linearization about the vertically independent W. Hence bar(y)
solves the SAME linearized equation with the actual source
`c average_z B(y,y)`, where c=epsilon/a<=2delta. The H1 estimate gives
`||bar(y)||H1<=delta J`. This is a bound on a generated parent, not a
freely chosen mean field. Dropping this history would lose the small
factor delta needed below.

More explicitly, with `L_W r=B(W,r)+B(r,W)` and `Pi0=average_z`,
the full equation is
`bar(y)'=L_W bar(y)+mu Delta bar(y)+c Pi0 B(y,y)`, `bar(y)(0)=0`.
The exact checker verifies nonzero mean generation by the seed, commutation
of averaging with the full projected linearization, and the complete mixed
cubic expansion on two fixtures. These checks support the algebra; the
norm estimate for the evolving mean is the analytic argument above.

For q=y-p the H1 growth of the pure cellular operator is at most 5/2;
the proof is the same integrated transport estimate used for (146).
Keep the complete receiver and nonlinear terms as sources and use K
to bound them. In full,
`q'=Lq+mu Delta q-(p'-Lp)+mu Delta p`
`+b[B(w e_z,y)+B(y,w e_z)]+c B(y,y)`.
Since mu<=2/Re and exp(5T/2)<9, (147) yields

```text
Gamma=9T[232/Re+2Cb rho Kw K+2Cb delta K^2],
Gamma<=1/1000
  implies sup_(0<=sigma<=T)||q||H1<=9/1500+Gamma<=7/1000.
                                                               (149)
```

This is a derivative-level estimate for the actual full nonlinear
equation, not an upgrade inferred from the preceding L2 error alone.

### Retaining the receiver terms in the physical stretching

Write `U=a v+A rho w e_z`. Expanding the cubic g with (146), the
terms linear in y against two vertically independent reference factors
depend only on bar(y). Their apparently large factors rho/delta and
rho^2/delta are therefore controlled by `||bar(y)||H1<=delta J`.
For the other terms use `|curl r|<=sqrt(2)|grad r|`, the bound K,
and `||grad w||infinity<=Gw`. Explicitly,

```text
|G(sigma)-C(y(sigma))|<=Xi,
Xi=6rho Kw J+12rho^2 Gw Kw J+12rho Gw K^2+4delta Ce K^3.
Xi<=1/100.                                             (150)
```

The four summands pay respectively for the mixed quadratic form C,
the terms with two receiver factors and one generated mean, the terms
with one receiver and two y factors, and the pure cubic in y. The
factor A/a is at most two. All terms come from the exact physical
cubic expansion, including those involving the retained mean history.

At the two later observations, (147)--(149) bound
`|C(y)-C(p)|` by `3(11/2+7/1000)(7/1000)=115647/1000000`.
Together with (150), this proves the two positive bounds in (145).
Initially y=r0, so `-3/40+1/100<=-1/20` proves the negative bound.
Smoothness gives nonempty intervals with all the claimed signs.

Conditions (148)--(150) are compatible with the entire preceding
construction. After fixing the annular seed, Kw,V,K,J,Gw are fixed
independently of rho, Re and delta. Choose positive rho small enough
for its contributions, then finite A large enough for Re and the
pattern comparison, then positive epsilon small enough for delta and
the original global H3 threshold. Thus the same solution can retain
any prescribed finite approximate pattern cycles as well as the
refeeding and excess-stretching signs. With rho=0 the same estimates
give the pure cellular-reference variant, without an annular movie.

The power reserve (144) remains valid. This test shows why that modal
payment is not, by itself, the missing critical stretching estimate:
the same positive feeding label occurs with opposite signs of excess
stretching. The generated mean can be paid in this small neighborhood;
controlling it and the full critical cost for arbitrary mutually
amplifying histories remains open.

Run `python3 -O labs/refeeding_stretching.py`. The finite Fourier
identities, H1 residual bounds and sign margins are exact rational
checks. The Sobolev bootstrap, averaged evolution, physical interval
comparison and existence are analytic, not newly Lean-certified.

## Bellman control of the actual generated mean

`generated_mean_control.py` supplies an explicit finite-horizon controller
for the generated mean in (148)--(150). It uses linear comparison and an
adjoint cost weight. The costed-history composition laws already available
