in `GSLT.Dynamics.BoundaryBellman` provide the interface; no additional
general control library is needed for this calculation.

The physical class and smallness hypotheses remain those of (145)--(150).
Fix the ORIGINAL clock horizon T=3/4 and all original-data constants.
With `m=average_z[(u-U)/epsilon]`, define

```text
n(sigma)=||m(sigma)||H1/delta, delta=epsilon/A>0,
kappa=C1 V>0, beta=2Cb K^2,
n(0)=0, n>=0, n'<=kappa n+beta.                       (151)
```

The inequality follows from the actual projected mean equation above,
not an independently imposed fluid force. The norm is absolutely continuous
on the compact interval and the inequality holds almost everywhere; a
regularized-norm argument gives the same comparison at its zeros. Viscous
dissipation has favorable sign. Its removal in (151) makes a larger set
of histories, suitable for an upper bound.

### An explicit value function and its physical payment

For h>=0 and n>=0 put

```text
alpha(h)=(exp(kappa h)-1)/kappa,
b(h)=(exp(kappa h)-1-kappa h)/kappa^2,
Vcontrol(h,n)=alpha(h)n+beta b(h).                     (152)
```

Both weights are nonnegative. This is exactly the maximal integral of
the scalar state over the remaining time h among nonnegative absolutely
continuous histories starting at n and satisfying (151). Indeed the
maximizer solves `n'=kappa n+beta`; comparison bounds every admitted
history by it, and direct integration gives (152). Equivalently admit
`n'=kappa n+v-d`, `0<=v<=beta`, `d>=0`, while retaining n>=0.
Then `partial_n Vcontrol=alpha>=0` and

```text
partial_h Vcontrol
 =n+sup_(0<=v<=beta,d>=0)[(kappa n+v-d)partial_n Vcontrol],
d/dsigma Vcontrol(T-sigma,n(sigma))+n(sigma)
 =-alpha(T-sigma)[beta-v+d]<=0.                       (153)
```

The maximizing scalar controls v=beta, d=0 need not be realizable by a
fluid. The valid implication is from each physical history to an admitted
scalar history. This is a control relaxation of an observation, not an
external NS force or a Schrödinger-bridge identification theorem.

The terms in the cubic production that are linear in the perturbation
and involve the reference receiver depend on m. Denote their exact sum
by `g_mean`: in the expansion of `g(a v+A rho w e_z+epsilon y)`, this
is the mixed C pairing and the three terms with two receiver factors
and one epsilon y. The estimates leading to (150) give

```text
ell=6rho Kw+12rho^2 Gw Kw,
|g_mean(t(sigma))|<=a epsilon^2 ell n(sigma),
R_mean(sigma)=epsilon^2 ell Vcontrol(T-sigma,n(sigma)). (154)
```

Since `dt=dsigma/a`, the factor a cancels in the integrated physical cost.
Thus, for any `0<=s0<=s1<=T` in the SAME original clock,

```text
integral_(t(s0))^(t(s1)) |g_mean(r)| dr <=R_mean(s0)-R_mean(s1),
R_mean(0)=epsilon^2 ell beta b(T), R_mean(T)=0.
```

Here t(sigma) denotes the original clock inverse, not a renewed clock.
The initial allowance is finite and explicit from the original datum.
This pays a contribution to actual vorticity stretching, not merely
the quadratic energy exchange with the modal parent.

There is also a complete payment for the reference-subtracted cubic
production on this interval. Equation (146) and ||y||H3<=K give

```text
C0=3K^2+12rho Gw K^2+4delta Ce K^3,
|g(u)-g(U)|<=a epsilon^2[C0+ell n],
R_excess(sigma)=epsilon^2[C0(T-sigma)+ell Vcontrol(T-sigma,n(sigma))],
integral_(t(s0))^(t(s1)) |g(u(r))-g(U(r))| dr
 <=R_excess(s0)-R_excess(s1),
R_excess(0)=epsilon^2[C0 T+ell beta b(T)].              (155)
```

The estimate retains g(U); it does not identify this cost with
`g(u)-g(u0)` in the signed-renewal continuation theorem. The reference
and change of baseline would need their own payment there. The present
class already has global existence from the earlier stability theorem;
(155) supplies a concrete stretching-cost consumer for the history
interface, not a second arbitrary-data regularity proof.

### Exact seams, inherited memory, and the existing GSLT interface

For h1,h2>=0 the weights obey

```text
alpha(h1+h2)=alpha(h1)+exp(kappa h1)alpha(h2),
b(h1+h2)=b(h1)+b(h2)+alpha(h1)alpha(h2).               (156)
```

For a saturating first interval, its ending mean is
`n1=exp(kappa h1)n0+beta alpha(h1)`. Consequently its cost plus
`Vcontrol(h2,n1)` is exactly `Vcontrol(h1+h2,n0)`. For any admitted
first interval the corresponding inequality holds. Repeated composition
uses that same inherited mean and the original terminal time.

If n0=0, restarting each interval with zero mean would retain only
`beta[b(h1)+b(h2)]` and lose the strictly positive term
`beta alpha(h1)alpha(h2)` when beta,h1,h2>0. It represents mean
generated in the first interval acting during the second. The exact
scalar maximum is only a comparison witness, but actual NS mean
generation is independently nonzero for the seed. It cannot be deleted
from an actual endpoint state merely because a pattern label recurs.

The physical boundary state retains the full endpoint velocity and clock,
with the original reference, constants and horizon fixed. Each actual
solution segment in the controlled class maps to its scalar n history;
its cost is bounded by the integral of `epsilon^2(C0+ell n)`.
Pulling this relaxed relation back to those full endpoint states gives
the same-state cost domination required by
`CostedRelation.Bounds.of_domination`. The reserve (155) then has exactly
the form consumed by `Bounds.comp` and `Bounds.iterate`: intermediate
reserves cancel and no new initial allowance appears.

This specifies an analytic instance of the existing formal interface;
the PDE-to-scalar domination is not newly Lean-certified. Matching only
n or a pattern label does not reconstruct matching physical velocities.
The full endpoint witness remains necessary for physically gluing flows.
Scalar summaries may bound a larger family without claiming that each
member reconstructs to an NS solution.

The unresolved extension is explicit: beta and C0 are currently paid by
the proved small-neighborhood bound K. Arbitrary mutually amplifying
parents need a replacement source/stretching estimate from the full
original datum. The Bellman formula and GSLT composition do not provide
that missing physical estimate.

Run `python3 -O labs/generated_mean_control.py`. Exact symbolic checks
cover the adjoint and Bellman equations, complete source/loss slack,
two- and three-interval composition, the zero-growth limit and physical
clock scaling. The actual mean-generation fixtures are reused. The
analytic trajectory domination and interval payment remain distinct
from these finite algebra checks; no new Lean declaration is asserted.

## Reference stretching paid without perturbative smallness

`reference_stretching_control.py` replaces the target H3 cap in the
generated-mean source payment by actual relative kinetic energy. It
pays ALL mixed cubic stretching involving a known evolving reference.
The pure perturbation self-stretching remains explicit and unpaid.
No smallness of the perturbation or bound on its future derivatives
is used in this mixed-term estimate.

### Actual difference and the observed mean

Work either on normalized period-2pi T3 or on R3 with smooth fields
whose derivatives have the required L2 decay. Fix nu>0, H>0 and a
known smooth unforced reference U on [0,H], chosen from original data
independently of the unknown target evolution. For ANY available smooth
unforced target prefix u on [0,S], S<=H, put d=u-U. Then

```text
B(r,s)=-P[(r.grad)s], L_U d=B(U,d)+B(d,U),
d_t=nu Delta d+L_U d+B(d,d),
E=||d||2^2, D=||grad d||2^2,
E'+2nu D=-2<d,(d.grad)U><=2L E,
L=sup_(0<=t<=H)||grad U(t)||infinity.                 (157)
```

The gradient norm here is the Frobenius norm. Pressure is retained by
the Leray projection and vanishes only in its legitimate solenoidal
energy pairing. The complete self-advection has zero relative kinetic
work. The reference need not be small; its smooth existence is a
separate known input, not a claim about arbitrary target data.

There are two observations m used below. For a general reference use
m=d. On T3, if U is independent of z, one can instead use m=average_z d.
Its exact equation is

```text
m_t=nu Delta m+L_U m+average_z B(d,d).                 (158)
```

In particular U(0)=average_z u0 gives m(0)=0. U(t) is its own
unforced evolution, not the instantaneous average of u(t); m records
the actual difference generated by the three-dimensional feedback.
All nonlinear modes remain in d and in the source of (158).

### A negative-Sobolev state retains the needed observation

Use the H3 multi-index norm and its L2-dual H^-3 norm. Let A3 be the
positive constant-coefficient operator with
`<A3 phi,phi>=||phi||H3^2`; then
`||m||H^-3^2=<A3^-1 m,m>`. Derivatives, the Leray projection and
vertical averaging commute with A3. Fix a Sobolev constant c such that
`||grad phi||infinity<=c||phi||H3`.

The dual norm of a solenoidal field can be tested against solenoidal phi:
the Leray projection is an H3 contraction and preserves the pairing.
All test fields in the following pairing identities are solenoidal.

The actual nonlinear source satisfies

```text
<phi,B(d,d)>=<d tensor d,grad phi>,
||B(d,d)||H^-3<=c E.                                 (159)
```

The same estimate holds after vertical averaging. It uses no derivative
of d: incompressibility moves the derivative to the smooth test field.
The projected adjoint of the linearized evolution is

```text
L_U^* phi=P[(U.grad)phi-(grad U)^T phi].                (160)
```

The usual integer-order product/transport estimates give a fixed
constant C such that
`<phi,L_U^* phi>H3<=C||U||H4||phi||H3^2`.
Principal transport cancels; the remaining terms have at most four
derivatives on the known U. Applying this with phi=A3^-1 m and
retaining the nonpositive diffusion gives

```text
n=||m||H^-3>=0,
n'<=kappa n+c E,
kappa=1+2L+C sup_(0<=t<=H)||U(t)||H4.                 (161)
```

This holds almost everywhere for the actual absolutely-continuous norm
path, or follows by regularizing the norm at zero. The source is the
evolving fluid's quadratic source, not an independent control input.

### Complete stretching expansion and its source adjoint

Let `g(u)=integral curl(u)^T grad(u) curl(u)`, with the chosen domain's
measure, and omega_U=curl U. Integration by parts gives the exact first
variation and the complete cubic expansion:

```text
ell_U=P{curl[(grad U+grad U^T)omega_U]
         -div(omega_U tensor omega_U)},
Dg(U)[d]=<ell_U,d>,
g(U+d)=g(U)+<ell_U,d>+Q_U(d)+g(d),
|Q_U(d)|<=6L D.                                      (162)
```

Q_U contains the three terms with two d factors and one U factor.
Each is bounded by `2||grad U||infinity||grad d||2^2`, using
`|curl r|<=sqrt(2)|grad r|`. If U is independent of z, ell_U is too,
so its pairing observes m=average_z d. In the general case m=d.
Thus, with a finite known-reference coefficient

```text
j=sup_(0<=t<=H)||ell_U(t)||H3,
|g(u)-g(U)-g(d)|<=j n+6L D.                           (163)
```

Finiteness of j follows, for example, from the known reference's H5
norm on the compact interval. No future norm of u enters it.

The equivalent backward source formulation retains both endpoints.
For `-psi_t=nu Delta psi+L_U^* psi+theta ell_U`, the exact identity is

```text
d/dt <psi,m>=<d tensor d,grad psi>-theta<ell_U,d>.
```

For the averaged case psi is z-independent. With psi(S)=0, its integral
has the initial term `<psi(0),m(0)>`, which vanishes only when the
initial mean is matched. The checker verifies the plus diffusion,
projected adjoint, nonlinear source and first-variation signs. Equation
(161) is a concrete norm bound for this physical duality.

### A coupled Bellman reserve from original resources

Put a=2L, b=3L/nu. In remaining PHYSICAL time h=H-t define

```text
phi_r(h)=integral_0^h exp(r s) ds,
p(h)=j phi_kappa(h),
r(h)=b exp(a h)+c integral_0^h exp(a(h-s))p(s) ds,
R_H(t)=p(H-t)n(t)+r(H-t)E(t).                         (164)
```

These are nonnegative known-reference weights, with p(0)=0, r(0)=b,
`p_h=kappa p+j`, `r_h=a r+c p`, and r(h)>=b. Since kappa>a,
the second weight also has the closed form
`b exp(a h)+c j[phi_kappa(h)-phi_a(h)]/(kappa-a)`.
For a=0 use phi_0(h)=h. There is no singular zero-growth convention.

The reserve combines the generated observation with its actual source
resource E. Along every available target prefix, (157) and (161) give

```text
R_H'+j n+6L D<=-(2nu r(H-t)-6L)D<=0,
integral_s^t |g(u)-g(U)-g(d)|<=R_H(s)-R_H(t),
R_H(0)=p(H)||m(0)||H^-3+r(H)||u0-U0||2^2.             (165)
```

The constant choice b=3L/nu pays the entire mixed dissipation cost.
Nonnegative terminal stock is retained instead of spent twice. For a
matched periodic mean, R_H(0)=r(H)||u0-U0||2^2: even a large or highly
oscillatory perturbation has this finite mixed-stretching allowance.
These are bounds on every smooth prefix, not an assumption that u
already exists through H. All coefficients use the independently known
reference on [0,H], and the original H is retained at every seam.

This reserve has an explicit control interpretation. Enlarge the actual
histories to nonnegative states with
`n'=kappa n+c E-loss_n`, `E'=a E-2nu D-loss_E`, where D and both
losses are nonnegative. The running cost is `j n+6L D`, and the
terminal cost is b E. Then `V(h,n,E)=p(h)n+r(h)E` is the exact value
of this scalar relaxation. Its Bellman identity is

```text
V_h = j n+kappa n V_n+c E V_n+a E V_E
      +sup_(D>=0) (6L-2nu V_E)D.
```

The supremum is zero since r(h)>=b. Zero losses and D=0 give a
nonnegative saturating comparison history, hence equality for the
relaxation; that optimizer is not asserted to be an NS flow. Actual
NS trajectories supply nonnegative slacks by (157) and (161), so their
costs are dominated. Composition carries the same E, generated m and
remaining horizon across the seam. Reconstructing an actual fluid
still requires the full endpoint velocity, not only these two numbers.

For arbitrary smooth periodic u0, the standard global 2.5D reference
can be chosen from U0=average_z u0: its horizontal velocity solves 2D
NS and its vertical component solves the passive advection-diffusion
equation. Its smooth norms are finite on each finite horizon. This
uses the classical two-dimensional theory; it is not a new Lean
existence theorem. The resulting constants are finite functionals of
that proved-global reference, determined by original data; a closed
numerical expression in initial seminorms is not supplied here.
The earlier cellular reference is an explicit special case. A periodic
reference is not a finite-energy R3 reference and is not used as one.

Relative-energy stability around symmetry-preserving solutions is
established theory; see [Bardos, Lopes Filho, Nussenzveig Lopes, Niu and
Titi](https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.2742). Their Theorem 3.1 treats a
vertically periodic cylinder. The smooth comparison (157) is derived
here on the stated torus/whole-space domains; their boundary hypotheses
and quantitative constants are not silently substituted for these.

### The remaining physical cost and formal status

The paid cost in (165) is the MIXED difference, not all of g(u)-g(U).
Pure g(d) remains. It includes the mean created by d's nonlinear
evolution; d does not stay mean-free and is not a standalone unforced
solution. Its equation still contains L_U d and its full pressure.
Rechoosing U at a cycle boundary would change both d and the reserve;
that operation is not justified by the fixed-reference certificate.

For example, write `D2(v)=||grad curl v||2^2`. A finite original-data
bound, uniform over prefixes, of the form

```text
2 integral_0^t g(d)<= (nu/2) integral_0^t D2(d)+Kself
```

would be sufficient after (165): use
`D2(d)<=2D2(u)+2D2(U)` and retain the known integrals of g(U), D2(U)
and the original g(u0) baseline. More explicitly, the resulting
allowance for `2 integral_0^t [g(u)-g(u0)]` is

```text
nu integral_0^t D2(u)+Kself+2R_H(0)
  +nu integral_0^H D2(U)+2 integral_0^H |g(U)|+2H|g(u0)|.
```

For solenoidal fields the integrated D2 equals the second-order
gradient energy in the existing whole-space signed-renewal criterion.
This is an analytic reduction to that criterion, not a new formal
identification theorem. The displayed self-stretching bound is OPEN;
energy control and the negative-Sobolev observation do not prove it.

For a nonzero force difference F, the observation source additionally
costs `||P F||H^-3` (or its vertical average), and the relative energy
law additionally contains the signed work `2<d,F>`. The reserve defect
is consequently bounded by `p||P F||H^-3+2r<d,F>`. Neither contribution
may be discarded when testing a forced history. This does not itself
exclude a forced singular mechanism: pure perturbation self-stretching
is still unpaid in the unforced comparison too.

`MettapediaNS.ReferenceStretchingReserve` certifies the coupled reserve
calculus, its explicit source defects, observation domination, initial
mean specialization and interval/seam payment under the stated scalar
derivative hypotheses. Its classical interval theorem reuses
`PlanarParentReserve.interval_payment`. The negative-Sobolev PDE bound,
actual norm's a.e. calculus, closed-form weight identification and
physical stretching comparison above remain analytic. Generic GSLT
cost composition remains available; full endpoint states are required
for actual fluid reconstruction.

Run `python3 -O labs/reference_stretching_control.py`. Exact checks
retain canonical pressure, the complete nonlinear difference, actual
relative energy, nonzero first-variation tests, projected adjoint
duality with viscosity, and the coupled weight/payment algebra.

## The evolving planar mean has a finite amplification price

`generated_mean_enstrophy.py` checks a different decomposition which
retains the ACTUAL evolving mean, including its internal forcing. The
estimate below controls every cubic stretching term containing that
mean by an integrable coefficient times total enstrophy and a fixed
viscous share. The coefficient's entire time integral is paid by the
original kinetic energy. No smallness or independently known reference
is required. This is a periodic estimate; no whole-space vertical
averaging operation is asserted.

This is not a finite absolute stretching allowance independent of
enstrophy. It removes the mean-containing terms through an energy
compensation in the enstrophy inequality. Fluctuation self-stretching
remains an explicit open input.

### The mean and fluctuations obey the equation together

On the normalized period-2pi T3, take any smooth unforced NS prefix
with viscosity nu>0. Define M=average_z u, w=u-M, and
`B(v,q)=-P[(v.grad)q]`. Projection and averaging commute. Their exact
equations are

```text
M_t=nu Delta M+B(M,M)+F,
F=average_z B(w,w),
w_t=nu Delta w+B(M,w)+B(w,M)+(I-average_z)B(w,w).       (166)
```

The mean is generally forced by the fluctuations; it has not become
an independently prescribed solution. The two internal kinetic works
cancel, ` <M,F>+<w,B(M,w)+B(w,M)>=0`. Every non-mean output remains
in the second equation. All fields remain solenoidal and pressure is
retained through P.

For `g(v)=integral curl(v)^T grad(v) curl(v)`, put

```text
E=||u||2^2, Z=||grad u||2^2, P2=||grad^2 u||2^2,
Z_M=||grad M||2^2, Z_w=||grad w||2^2,
Z=Z_M+Z_w, P2=P2_M+P2_w,
g(u)=g(M)+Q_M(w)+g(w).                               (167)
```

Here Q_M is the sum of the three cubic terms containing one M and
two w factors. The terms with two M factors and one w vanish by
vertical averaging. In particular, neither g(M) nor the mean forcing
is discarded. The mixed enstrophy identity is

```text
Q_M(w)=<-Delta w,B(M,w)+B(w,M)>+<-Delta M,F>.
```

This displays both sides of the internally generated enstrophy transfer.

### The useful cancellation before estimating

Let A=sqrt(Z_M). Fix a domain constant C_L>=1 for the horizontal
mean-zero Hilbert-valued Ladyzhenskaya inequality

```text
||V||L4(T2;H)^2 <= C_L ||V||L2(T2;H) ||grad_h V||L2(T2;H).
                                                               (168)
```

This follows from the usual two-dimensional inhomogeneous inequality
applied to the scalar norm, the weak derivative bound for that norm,
and horizontal Poincare for V. Regularizing the norm treats its zeros.
The Hilbert space may be `L2(T_z;R^(3x3))`. Its constant is independent
of the vertical Fourier support. All spatial norms use normalized
measure, and Poincare's first nonzero horizontal frequency is one.

For grad M, horizontal mean zero is automatic. For grad w it need not
hold: a vertically varying horizontal shear can have no horizontal
variation. Retain it explicitly by writing

```text
r=average_(x,y) w, s=w-r,
Z_w=Z_r+Z_s, Z_s<=||grad_h grad s||2^2<=P2_w.
```

Since every term in Q_M(r) is linear in grad M and quadratic in the
horizontally constant grad r, horizontal integration gives Q_M(r)=0.
This cancellation must be performed BEFORE taking absolute values.
It removes the spurious horizon-dependent lower-order coefficient
that an inhomogeneous estimate would otherwise introduce.

Let q_M be the symmetric polarization of Q_M, so
`Q_M(w)=Q_M(s)+2q_M(s,r)`. Pointwise curl bounds and Cauchy-Schwarz in
z give

```text
|g(M)| <= 2 C_L A sqrt(Z_M) sqrt(P2_M),
|Q_M(s)| <= 6 C_L A sqrt(Z_s) sqrt(P2_w),
|q_M(s,r)| <= 6 A sqrt(Z_r) sqrt(Z_s)
             <=6 A sqrt(Z_r) sqrt(P2_w).
```

Indeed each polarized mixed term is bounded by twice the product of
the three gradient norms; there are three such terms. Applying (168)
to grad s controls the quadratic term, while the horizontal Poincare
inequality controls the shear cross-term. Orthogonality and
Cauchy-Schwarz now give, with C=12 C_L+24,

```text
2|g(u)-g(w)| <= C A sqrt(Z) sqrt(P2)
             <=(nu/2)P2 + [C^2/(2nu)] Z_M Z.          (169)
```

This retains arbitrary amplitudes and all vertical frequencies. The
kinetic law pays the coefficient's entire history:

```text
E'=-2nu Z,
integral_0^t [C^2/(2nu)] Z_M
  <= C^2 [E(0)-E(t)]/(4nu^2) <= C^2 E(0)/(4nu^2).    (170)
```

The bound is independent of t and uses no future target regularity.
Two-dimensional interpolation in three-dimensional comparisons is
classical; compare the use of Ladyzhenskaya and kinetic dissipation in
[Bardos et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1201.2742).
Their symmetric-reference stability theorem has different hypotheses;
(166)--(170) are derived here for the instantaneous mean of the actual
periodic flow. No novelty priority is asserted for this estimate.

### A concrete energy compensation and its remaining obligation

The exact enstrophy law and (169) imply

```text
Z'+(3nu/2)P2 <= 2g(w)+beta Z_M Z,
beta=C^2/(2nu), gamma=C^2/(4nu^2).
```

Suppose a finite allowance K, fixed by the full original datum, nu
and prescribed horizon, supplied the following remaining prefix bound:

```text
2 integral_0^t g(w) <= (nu/2) integral_0^t P2 + K.     (171)
```

THIS IS OPEN. It is a bound on the w extracted from the full actual
solution, with its evolving mean and all their couplings. It is not
an estimate for an autonomous unforced w equation.

Set `R(t)=K-2 integral_0^t g(w)+(nu/2) integral_0^t P2`.
Under (171), R>=0 and R(0)=K. The compensated reserve

```text
S(t)=exp(gamma E(t)) [Z(t)+R(t)]
```

satisfies

```text
S'+nu exp(gamma E)P2
 <=-beta exp(gamma E)[(Z-Z_M)Z+ZR]<=0,
Z(t)<=S(t)<=exp(gamma E(0))[Z(0)+K].                  (172)
```

Thus an original-data bound on this precise residual would give the
uniform enstrophy bound required for periodic continuation. The same
kinetic stock and residual reserve pass through every compatible seam.
Neither is replenished when a pattern returns. A bound on all prefix
integrals is sufficient: no favorable pointwise stretching sign is
assumed. The exponential price and the reserve are explicit; finiteness
of K in (171) is the missing physical estimate, not a definition by an
unknown-future supremum.

The existing formal periodic consumer is
`FourierLerayRate.one_le_lerayRate`: a maximal tame solution has an
unbounded order-one energy near its endpoint. Its hypotheses retain
positive viscosity, reality, transversality, zero spatial mean and
initial finite order-m energy with m>=7. For smooth zero-mean data,
the bound above together with E<=E(0) controls that order-one norm
after the fixed period/Fourier normalization conversion. This analytic
connection is not a newly certified adapter; the physical estimate
itself does not require zero spatial mean.

For an externally forced periodic flow, (172) additionally retains
`2 exp(gamma E)[<curl u,curl f>+gamma<u,f>(Z+R)]`.
Zero kinetic work does not imply zero vorticity work. This formula
does not transplant a whole-space forced construction onto the torus.

### The first unpaid return is already positive in an actual history

The seed r0 from the previous refeeding example has only vertical
frequencies +/-1. Its self-stretching is initially zero. Split its
complete quadratic source into

```text
F0=average_z B(r0,r0), Nperp=(I-average_z)B(r0,r0).
Dg(r0)[F0] = -3283/10000,
Dg(r0)[Nperp] = 6252773/5460000 > 0.                  (173)
```

All source outputs are retained. The mean first return is depleting
here; the non-mean outputs have the opposite sign. These numbers concern
the quartic return from r0's own source, not the entire derivative of
mean-containing production in a nonzero background. For actual initial
data `u0=U0+epsilon r0`, any smooth z-independent solenoidal U0 and
any positive viscosity, let w(t)=u(t)-average_z u(t). Then

```text
g(w(0))=0,
d/dt g(w(t))|_(t=0)=epsilon^4 * 6252773/5460000 > 0.
```

The viscous and U0-linearized tangents keep vertical frequencies +/-1;
three such frequencies cannot sum to zero, so their cubic variation
vanishes. The non-mean quadratic outputs give (173). Smooth local
existence and time differentiability imply g(w(t))>0 for all sufficiently
small positive t at each fixed nonzero epsilon and viscosity. This
applies in particular to the already constructed actual refeeding
histories under their original parameter restrictions. The sign does
not assert enstrophy growth against viscosity, failure of (171) with a
full-datum allowance, or any singularity.

It also yields an analytic test of the stronger zero-allowance version
of (171). Take u0=epsilon r0 and write
`u(t)=epsilon v(epsilon t)`, with viscosity mu=nu/epsilon for v.
Smooth local estimates for the fixed seed are uniform for 0<=mu<=1.
Thus there is a fixed small tau0>0 for which
`g(v-average_z v)>=c tau/2` and `P2(v)<=2P2(r0)` throughout
0<=tau<=tau0, where c=6252773/5460000. The first bound follows from
the uniform second-time-derivative remainder and (173).
Consequently the residual at t=tau0/epsilon obeys

```text
2 integral_0^t g(w)-(nu/2) integral_0^t P2(u)
 >= epsilon^2 [c tau0^2/2-mu P2(r0) tau0] > 0
```

when mu<c tau0/(2P2(r0)). For every fixed positive nu, a sufficiently
large original amplitude gives an ACTUAL smooth unforced prefix
violating K=0. This is a local analytic consequence of uniform smooth
existence, not a closed Fourier truncation or a statement about later
regularity. It leaves the finite full-datum allowance in (171) open.

### Verification boundary

`MettapediaNS.GeneratedMeanEnstrophy` certifies six scalar compensation
ingredients, including the exact energy price, reserve derivative,
conditional payment and resulting enstrophy bound. R>=0 and its physical
source law remain hypotheses. The anisotropic Sobolev estimate, the
actual projection equations, periodic continuation connection and the
short-time PDE sign argument are analytic, not newly Lean-certified.

Run `python3 -O labs/generated_mean_enstrophy.py`. Exact Fourier checks
cover full pressure-corrected mean and fluctuation equations, both
energy-transfer directions, the horizontally constant cancellation,
complete cubic and dissipation splittings, viscosity, and the positive
first unpaid return. Exact scalar checks retain every compensation
term. The fixtures are independent algebra checks, not simulated
continuum trajectories or a proof of (171).

## A joint parent weight pays transfers that fixed quadratic weights cannot

`shear_fluctuation_reserve.py` tests a certificate for the open fluctuation
budget (171), then supplies a working replacement on the same physical
shear class. This is a limitation of a specified certificate class, not
an obstruction to a full-datum history allowance. The positive result
reuses the triangular mixing mechanism; mutual parent renewal remains open.

### Tested certificate and complete physical transfers

Fix nu>0 and a continuous nonnegative quadratic Fourier-multiplier storage
R(w)=<w,Lw> on smooth fields, differentiable along smooth NS histories
(polynomially growing weights suffice). The multiplier may depend on frequency
and polarization, but is fixed independently of datum and amplitude.
The proposed certificate, at EVERY smooth unforced state, is

```text
R' + 2g(w) <= (nu/2)D, w=u-average_z u, D=||grad^2u||2^2.  (174)
```

It would give (171) with K=R(w(0)). A datum-dependent certificate needed
only on its reachable states is a weaker assertion, not tested here.
On the normalized period-2pi torus, set

```text
p=(1,0,1), q_n=(n,0,n+1), lambda_n=|q_n|^2=2n^2+2n+1,
u=a sin(x+z)(1,0,-1)
       +[b cos(q_n.x)+c cos(q_(n+1).x)] e_y, n>=0.        (175)
```

These are smooth real solenoidal data with zero vertical mean and
constant canonical pressure. Their COMPLETE source N(u)=-P[(u.grad)u] is

```text
N(u)=[-ab cos(q_(n-1).x)+ab cos(q_(n+1).x)
       -ac cos(q_n.x)+ac cos(q_(n+2).x)] e_y/2.
```

The definition q_j=(j,0,j+1) also applies at j=-1. In particular n=0
generates a vertical mean. The outer outputs do not pair with the
initial field in a quadratic derivative, but remain in the PDE source.
The nonlinear kinetic rates at the two occupied receiver modes are
-abc/2 and +abc/2. The parent has zero nonlinear rate, while

```text
Z'_nonlinear=abc(lambda_(n+1)-lambda_n)/2,
g(u)=abc(n+1).                                           (176)
```

Let rho_n>=0 be the multiplier weight on e_y at q_n. The cubic part
of the left side of (174) is

```text
(abc/2)[(rho_(n+1)+lambda_(n+1))-(rho_n+lambda_n)].
```

Scale all amplitudes by a common positive factor and reverse one sign.
Viscosity and the right side of (174) grow quadratically; this term
grows cubically. Thus universal payment forces

```text
rho_(n+1)+lambda_(n+1)=rho_n+lambda_n, every n.
rho_N>=0 then implies rho_0>=2N(N+1).                     (177)
```

No finite rho_0 satisfies every N. For any proposed multiplier, an
adjacent unequal pair supplies a phase and finite amplitude giving a
strict violation on an actual positive-viscosity NS initial tangent.
Local smooth evolution preserves a strict differential violation on
a short interval. This does NOT refute an integrated budget with
additional initial slack, a datum-dependent reachable-state certificate,
or a nonquadratic/adaptive reserve.

On a finite chain, rho_n=lambda_N-lambda_n balances internal edges.
Its increasing initial price and the next unmatched edge explain why
discarding outputs could falsely suggest uniform payment. No closed
Galerkin evolution is asserted. The finite-chain conclusion uses only
its N adjacent equalities.

### A constructive repair on the full receiver system

Take the actual triangular NS class

```text
u=a(t)sin(x+z)(1,0,-1)+theta(t,x,z)e_y,
a(t)=a0 exp(-2nu t),
theta_t+a(t)sin(x+z)(theta_x-theta_z)=nu Delta_(x,z)theta.
```

For ANY smooth periodic initial theta, autonomous shear and a linear
parabolic receiver give a global smooth unforced flow. All generated
modes remain; no amplitude or bandwidth restriction is imposed.
Pressure is constant and this receiver cannot feed its parent.
This rotates the earlier triangular mechanism to test the precise
vertical-fluctuation residual (171).

Put alpha=|a|, Z=||grad u||2^2 and D=||grad^2u||2^2. The parent gradient
has operator norm at most 2alpha. The scalar gradient balance gives

```text
alpha'=-2nu alpha, Z'<=4alpha Z-2nu D,
2g(w)<=4alpha Z, w=u-average_z u.                         (178)
```

For the last estimate, w has the same parent and receiver
phi=theta-average_z theta. Its cubic stretching is scalar-gradient
work against that parent, and orthogonality gives ||grad phi||2^2<=Z.
This spatial identity does not assert that phi obeys the autonomous
receiver equation: theta retains its generated vertical mean.

The nonnegative reserve and enstrophy envelope are

```text
R=(exp(2alpha/nu)-1)Z, S=exp(2alpha/nu)Z,
R'+2g(w)+2nu(exp(2alpha/nu)-1)D<=0,
S'+2nu exp(2alpha/nu)D<=0.                                (179)
```

Integration on any interval of this SAME history yields

```text
R(t)+2 integral_s^t g(w)
     +2nu integral_s^t (exp(2alpha/nu)-1)D <= R(s),
Z(t)<=exp(2|a0|/nu)Z(0),
2 integral_0^t g(w)<=K=(exp(2|a0|/nu)-1)Z(0).
```

Thus (171) is paid even without its extra nu D/2 allowance. The reserve
is quadratic in the receiver for a fixed parent, but nonquadratic in
the joint state. Its bound is uniform in time and the number of generated
modes. The same R passes through every seam without a new allowance.

The stochastic passive-scalar representation uses the actual backward
shear drift and Brownian diffusivity 2nu. The accumulated parent gradient
is at most |a0|/nu; its squared deformation factor is the exponential in
(179). The PDE derivation supplies payment directly and introduces no
stochastic control force.

There is also an exact Bellman interpretation. In the nonnegative two-state relaxation
alpha'=-2nu alpha, Z'<=4alpha Z-2nu D, D>=0, allow a nonnegative cost
q<=4alpha Z. The function R is the infinite-horizon value of this
relaxation: its derivative bounds every admissible cost history, and
D=0, Z'=4alpha Z, q=4alpha Z attains
integral q=Z(0)(exp(2alpha(0)/nu)-1). For a remaining horizon h, the value is

```text
V_h(alpha,Z)=[exp((2alpha/nu)(1-exp(-2nu h)))-1]Z.
```

These maximizing relaxed trajectories need not be realizable NS flows.
Their role is domination: actual triangular trajectories satisfy the
relaxed inequalities, and the physical bound in (178) even holds with
2|g(w)| on the left. Thus this is a finite, explicitly solved control
relaxation identified with a physical cost bound. It does not establish
such an identification for arbitrary mutually interacting parents.

### The exact mutual-renewal defect

If a nonnegative observed amplitude and the full receiver instead obey

```text
alpha'=-2nu alpha+F, Z'<=4alpha Z-2nu D+L,
2g(w)<=4alpha Z+extra,
```

the SAME reserve satisfies

```text
R'+2g(w)+2nu(exp(2alpha/nu)-1)D
 <= (exp(2alpha/nu)-1)L
    +(2/nu)exp(2alpha/nu)F Z+extra.                      (180)
```

For an NS Fourier parent, F comes from its complete nonlinear equation;
L and extra retain other interactions. These are not freely adjustable
controls. An absolute amplitude uses the actual signed source away from
zero and the appropriate one-sided/absolutely-continuous treatment at
zeros. No bound or favorable sign for these defects is asserted.

The compulsory seed r0 from (173) tests this distinction. Observe the
unit-norm parent cos(x+z)(1,0,-1), with coefficient a'=-2nu a+F. The
complete source gives, independently of positive viscosity,

```text
a(0)=1/10, F(0)=0, F'(0)=-22019/546000,
(d/dt)g(u-average_z u)|0=6252773/5460000>0.                (181)
```

Viscous contributions to these nonlinear derivatives vanish by phases
and support. This parent initially depletes while fluctuation stretching
grows: discarding receiver defects and checking only parent return would
be invalid. These are actual initial jets, not a later-history payment.
The next obligation is to control the COMPLETE right side of (180),
or replace the single parent with a jointly funded observation.

### Control-method reuse and verification

Quadratic and polynomial Lyapunov searches for fluid dynamics are
established; see [Kalur, Seiler and Hemati](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.05440)
and [Goulart and Chernyshenko](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.1043).
The former demonstrates quadratic constraints on a reduced transition
model; the latter develops polynomial searches with treatment of
unresolved fluid modes. Neither supplies an arbitrary-data regularity
theorem here. This calculation names an infinite-mode certificate
obligation and an explicit physical nonlinear calibration.

`MettapediaNS.ShearFluctuationReserve` certifies eight scalar/sequence
theorems: positivity, differentiation, complete defect payment, its
decaying-parent specialization and price, plus the weight recurrence,
finite-chain cost and infinite nonnegative-weight obstruction. The
Fourier realization and PDE estimates remain analytic. Interval payment

## Paying the weighted feedback into a fixed smooth parent

`parent_feedback_payment.py` checks the physical source in (180).
Its weighted parent-renewal term has a finite absolute payment for
arbitrary smooth unforced histories and a fixed smooth observation.
No independent decay, smallness, finite Fourier support of the fluid,
or favorable transfer sign is needed. The remaining receiver terms
are not paid by this result.

### The source belongs to the complete fluid

Let u be an actual smooth unforced solution, nu>0, and let psi be a
FIXED smooth divergence-free test velocity with finite L2 norm and
known bound K>=||grad psi||_infinity,op. On R3 use the smooth L2 class
of the imported evolution, with psi in the solenoidal L2 subspace.
On the torus use normalized measure. Set

```text
E=||u||2^2, Z=||grad u||2^2, a=<u,psi>,
F=<-P[(u.grad)u],psi>
 =-<(u.grad)u,psi>=<u,(u.grad)psi>.
a'=nu<Delta u,psi>+F,
|F|<=K E, |a|<=B=||psi||2 sqrt(E(0)).                    (182)
```

Transport skew symmetry proves the source identity. The pressure
pairing vanishes because psi is solenoidal, not because the fluid's
pressure is zero. The source includes all hidden parents and outputs.
The amplitude cap uses the actual unforced kinetic-energy inequality.
For a Laplacian eigenmode on the torus, the viscous term is exactly
-nu lambda a. No L2 Laplacian eigenmode is asserted on R3.

`WholeSpaceParentFeedback.actual_observed_rhs` certifies this source's
place in the actual whole-space NS equation. The advection skew identity,
source bound and original-data amplitude cap are kernel-certified too.
The source bound itself holds for any smooth test; interpreting it as
the entire projected nonlinear force uses the stated solenoidal condition.

### One finite reserve pays every replenishment

Fix c>=0, including the c=2/nu cotangent of (180). Define the constant
A and the nonnegative remaining stock J by

```text
A=c K exp(cB), J(t)=A E(t)^2/(4nu).
q(t)=c exp(c|a(t)|)|F(t)| Z(t)<=A E(t)Z(t),
E'=-2nu Z, J'=-A E Z,
J(t)+integral_s^t q<=J(s).                              (183)
```

In particular integral_0^t q<=A E(0)^2/(4nu), uniformly over every
available smooth prefix and independently of elapsed time. A, c, psi
and the original datum are unchanged across all seams. Refeeding does
not renew this allowance. Its construction is regular at E=0; no
inverse-energy derivative or positive energy cushion is needed.

The mechanism is explicit: a smooth observation cannot see more
nonlinear force than K times the full energy, and the same full energy
decreases at a rate 2nu Z. Multiplication by Z therefore becomes the
derivative of its square. This is a payment for a particular weighted
force channel, not a general bound on vortex stretching.

`actual_feedback_interval` proves (183) on R3 for every subinterval
0<=s<=t<=T of an actual `NSEvolution`, with the weighted source
interval-integrable. This is a technical regularity hypothesis on a
smooth compact prefix, not a future size bound. The initial-allowance
corollary supplies the displayed original stock. The analogous periodic
calculation uses its actual normalized energy law and is analytic here.

### Correction of the parent reserve with actual receiver terms retained

For the fixed normalized periodic parent psi=sin(x+z)(1,0,-1), take
a=<u,psi>, alpha=|a|, c=2/nu and v=exp(c alpha). Its eigenvalue is 2
and K=2 is a gradient bound. Let w=u-average_z u and define the signed
unobserved-strain work, separately for f=u and f=w, by

```text
G_f=integral curl(f)^T grad(f-a psi) curl(f).
```

The parent has zero vertical mean, so its coefficient is the same
whether observed in u or w. Exact splitting and the operator bound give

```text
Z'<=4alpha Z-2nu D+2G_u,
2g(w)<=4alpha Z+2G_w,
alpha'=-2nu alpha+sgn(a)F   almost everywhere.            (184)
```

Consequently the corrected nonnegative reserve is

```text
J_total=(v-1)Z+exp(2sqrt(E(0))/nu) E^2/nu^2,
J_total'+2g(w)+2nu(v-1)D<=2(v-1)G_u+2G_w.               (185)
```

This pays the ENTIRE exponential parent-source term in (180), even
with repeated feeding from arbitrary other modes. The absolute-value
source payment handles both signs and amplitude zeros. G_u and G_w
retain full curl receivers and all unobserved strain; they are not
self-stretching of a closed, independently evolving remainder.

The precise sufficient remaining history estimate for this correction is

```text
2 integral_0^t [(v-1)G_u+G_w] <= (nu/2)integral_0^t D+K_receiver,
```

with finite K_receiver fixed by the full original datum, viscosity and
horizon. It would imply (171) with K=J_total(0)+K_receiver. THIS REMAINS
OPEN. No monotonicity of J_total or payment of the receiver terms is
asserted. Rewriting them as defects has not bounded them.

### Adversarial phases, scale, and observer changes

Use the actual trigonometric datum r0 from (173), its COMPLETE source
N0=N(r0), and the fixed unit parent psi=cos(x+z)(1,0,-1). For
u_delta=r0+delta N0, direct rational calculation gives

```text
<u_delta,psi>=1/10,
||u_delta||2^2=||r0||2^2+delta^2||N0||2^2,
F(u_delta)=-delta*22019/546000.                          (186)
```

The opposite signs of delta give identical parent amplitude, energy
and enstrophy but opposite internal feeding. These are actual smooth
NS initial data, not an assertion that r0+delta N0 is a time-discretized
solution. Their canonical pressure is nonzero. Both signs satisfy the
same source/payment bounds with every generated mode retained.

Dilate periodic coordinates by an integer ell>=1. For the normalized
single harmonic, K_ell=2ell, lambda_ell=2ell^2 and
c_ell=2/(nu ell) give c_ell nu lambda_ell=4ell. Thus

```text
A_ell=(4/nu)exp(2sqrt(E(0))/(nu ell))
      <=(4/nu)exp(2sqrt(E(0))/nu).                       (187)
```

This particular ONE-harmonic feedback payment does not deteriorate
with its frequency. It does not eliminate the cost of changing the
observation or controlling arbitrarily many simultaneous parents.
A fixed finite family can sum its source payments, retaining the sum
of coefficients and the same full energy. No bound for that sum over
an unrestricted family is supplied.

If an observation price A(t) changes, differentiation of its stock adds
A'(t)E(t)^2/(4nu). A changing test field also contributes <u,psi_t>
to the observed equation; changing c and changing the parent reserve
introduce their own derivative or jump terms. The fixed-observer theorem
does not pay these by silently replacing its initial parameters.

### Forced scope and verification

For externally forced flow, E'=-2nu Z+2<u,f> changes the energy-square
identity to

```text
J'+A E Z=(A/nu)E<u,f>.                                 (188)
```

The observed equation additionally contains <f,psi>, which is not the
quadratic source F in (182). A fixed-parent nonlinear source payment
can also hold in a forced evolution if suitable full-energy/dissipation
bounds are available. It therefore does not distinguish or exclude the
imported forced blowup construction. The unobserved high-strain history
and possible changes of observation remain essential.

`MettapediaNS.WholeSpaceParentFeedback` certifies eleven theorems,

It reuses the imported transport cancellation, gradient advection bound,

## Heat-lifetime corrections and the next receiver generation

`receiver_heat_corrector.py` tests a signed correction for the remaining
receiver stretching in (171). Integrating the current interactions over
their viscous lifetimes gives an exact heat cancellation. Its first
nonlinear generation has an explicit quartic initial stock, and this
stock pays the first return on a short interval of an actual flow.
The same correction fails as a universal history certificate, even
where it is strictly positive. All pressure-corrected outputs and the
evolving mean are retained. The PDE arguments below are analytic.

### A signed heat forecast and its actual nonlinear defect

Use normalized measure on the 2pi torus, nu>0, and an available smooth
unforced solution u. Set M=average_z u, w=u-M, Pi=I-average_z,
N(u)=-P[(u.grad)u], and D=||Delta u||2^2. Let S_s=exp(nu s Delta).
For any field v write E(v)=||v||2^2 and Z(v)=||grad v||2^2.
Define the signed cubic functional

```text
H_nu(w)=2 integral_0^infinity g(S_s w) ds,
g(v)=integral curl(v)^T grad(v) curl(v).                  (189)
```

This is a heat forecast from the CURRENT field, not the original
nonlinear history. Every w has zero vertical mean. Exponential heat
decay and Sobolev multiplication make (189) a continuous cubic
functional on sufficiently regular fields. For example, the trilinear
observation is bounded by the two curl L2 norms and the middle gradient
supremum norm; on a high Sobolev space each heated factor decays
exponentially. This also justifies differentiation on compact smooth
prefixes. The infinite auxiliary heat interval does not assume global
existence of the nonlinear target.

The semigroup property gives

```text
D H_nu(w)[nu Delta w]=-2g(w),
d_t H_nu(w)+2g(w)=D H_nu(w)[Pi N(u)].                    (190)
```

Here D H denotes the Frechet derivative, distinct from the dissipation D.
The actual fluctuation equation is w_t=nu Delta w+Pi N(u); replacing its
source by an autonomous N(w) would omit the evolving mean and its pressure.
In Fourier variables each ordered triad k+ell+m=0 receives the exact
weight 2/[nu(|k|^2+|ell|^2+|m|^2)]. Phases and all three differentiated
slots remain. No absolute-value estimate precedes this identity.

### An empty forecast does not pay its own generation

Let r be the four-cosine seed of (173), and N0=N(r). Its input modes
have vertical frequencies +/-1. Hence g(S_s r)=0 for EVERY s>=0:
three such frequencies cannot add to zero. Nevertheless exact arithmetic
gives

```text
C0=D H_1(r)[Pi N0]=46234957/600600000>0,
D H_1(r)[average_z N0]=-4331/75000,
||Delta r||2^2=631/20.                                  (191)
```

The second line records a real generated mean, not a term discarded
from the actual solution. Its contribution to the FULL-velocity heat
forecast differs from the fluctuation forecast's contribution.

For u0=A r with A=16nu, initially H_nu(w0)=g(w0)=0, while
the right-hand side of (190) is A^4 C0/nu. Its ratio to (nu/2)D is
1479518624/1184308125>1. Thus the proposed payment

```text
H_nu(w(t))+2 integral_0^t g(w)
  <= H_nu(w0)+(nu/2)integral_0^t D
```

fails for every sufficiently small positive time of the actual smooth
solution. Local existence supplies that solution, and continuity keeps
the strictly positive initial defect positive on a smaller interval.
The same argument defeats any completion C(w)>=H_nu(w) with C(w0)=0.
This includes H_nu(w)_+ and 2 integral |g(S_s w)| ds: the complete initial
heat forecast vanishes, not merely its signed integral. This does not
refute an additional allowance from other resources of the original datum.

### A first-generation initial stock and its complete next defect

Define the self-generated quartic source and its heat forecast by

```text
Q_nu(w)=D H_nu(w)[Pi N(w)],
K_nu(w)=integral_0^infinity Q_nu(S_s w) ds,
R_nu(w)=H_nu(w)+K_nu(w).                                (192)
```

The smoothness and convergence arguments are as above with sufficiently
many derivatives. K is quartic and is not asserted nonnegative on all
fields. Its Fourier formula retains two distinct denominators: the
inner H denominator uses the generated wave number p+q, whereas the
outer heat integration uses |p|^2+|q|^2+|k|^2+|ell|^2 for the four
ORIGINAL parents. Confusing these heat rates would change the correction.

Let L=Pi[N(u)-N(w)]. It is the complete coupling to M (including its
pressure projection), since Pi N(M)=0. Along the actual flow,

```text
D K_nu(w)[nu Delta w]=-Q_nu(w),
d_t R_nu(w(t))+2g(w)
  =D H_nu(w)[L]+D K_nu(w)[Pi N(u)].                     (193)
```

All generated mean motion remains in this identity. It is not reset
when a new receiver mode appears. At the original seed,

```text
K_1(r)=9212971/2402400000>0,
D K_1(r)[Pi N0]=0.
```

Consequently, for each A>0 and nu>0, the actual flow from A r has
R_nu(w0)=A^4 K_1(r)/nu^2>0 and zero initial right-hand side in (193).
Continuity gives an epsilon>0 on which R_nu(w(t))>0 and

```text
d_t R_nu(w(t))+2g(w(t)) <= (nu/2)D(t),
R_nu(w(t))+2 integral_s^t g(w)
  <= R_nu(w(s))+(nu/2)integral_s^t D,   0<=s<=t<=epsilon.
```

This is a funded FIRST return in the full three-dimensional equation.
Its stretching is genuinely generated: g(w0)=0 and
g(w)'(0)=A^4*6252773/5460000>0. No perturbative smallness of A is required,
but no interval length uniform in A or a prescribed horizon is supplied.
The same state and remaining stock are retained at every seam inside this
interval. This local result alone does not supply arbitrary-history (171).

### Equal recorded resources, opposite next renewal

A sharper test retains the actual cubic observation too. Let v_k be
the pair of modes +/-k in Pi N0, and set

```text
y=v_(2,-1,2)+(559/2376)v_(3,-2,2)-(3311/4335)v_(3,-1,2),
w_+=r+y/10, w_-=r-y/10.                                (194)
```

These are two distinct smooth real divergence-free initial data, both
with zero vertical mean. Selecting their input modes does not truncate

```text
g(w_+)=g(w_-)=H_1(w_+)=H_1(w_-)=0,
K_1(w_+)=K_1(w_-)=kappa>0,
E(w_+)=E(w_-), Z(w_+)=Z(w_-), D(w_+)=D(w_-),
D K_1(w_-)[Pi N(w_-)]=p>0,
D K_1(w_+)[Pi N(w_+)]=-p.
```

Here

```text
kappa=8378830290697834010855134831649203
       /2185042298515980655752000000000000000,
p=460211189638875086695980591914234514986595679
   /339619162444930160775671256243535860000000000000000,
D(w_-)=28714885428973207/909543690000000.
```

Thus neither the current stretching nor these two successive forecasts

This does not preclude a conservative bound covering BOTH signs.

For the actual datum u0=A w_- with A=512nu, R_nu(w0)=A^4 kappa/nu^2>0.

Clipping R to its positive part cannot repair this example. No perpetual

## Nonnegative source storage and an energy-cube repair

`receiver_source_square.py` tests a globally nonnegative completion of
the preceding receiver correction. It fails a universal differential
payment despite its positivity. A higher power of the FULL kinetic
energy then repairs both tested hidden phases at every amplitude and
integer harmonic dilation. The repair has a strict initial margin and
therefore pays on a short interval of each actual smooth solution.
Persistence beyond that interval remains open. All PDE conclusions in
this section are analytic; the checker certifies exact finite algebra.

### Completing the signed forecast to a square

Keep the normalized 2pi torus, nu>0, M=average_z u, w=u-M,
Pi=I-average_z, N(u)=-P[(u.grad)u], A=-Delta and S_s=exp(-nu s A).
Use the actual nonlinear solution only on its available smooth prefix.
Let D_w=||Aw||2^2 and D=||Au||2^2. Define

```text
C_nu(w)=(1/nu) integral_0^infinity ||Pi N(S_s w)||2^2 ds,
V_nu(w)=Z(w)/2+H_nu(w)+C_nu(w)
       =(1/nu) integral_0^infinity
           ||nu A S_s w+Pi N(S_s w)||2^2 ds >=0.          (195)
```

This uses the complete ADVECTIVE Leray source. It differs from the
inverse-curl stretching source used in `caloric_force.py`. Both constructions
retain heat rates, but their capacities and derivatives are different.

To verify the square, the pure linear integral is Z(w)/2 by Fourier
heat decay, and the cross term is H_nu(w) because
<Av,Pi N(v)>=<Av,N(v)>=g(v) for a zero-vertical-mean solenoidal v.
The remaining term is C_nu. Exponential heat decay and Sobolev product
estimates make these functionals continuously differentiable on, for
example, periodic H^m with m>=5. Differentiation along a sufficiently
smooth NS prefix is justified in the same spaces. The auxiliary heat
integral is not an assumption about infinite nonlinear lifespan.

The semigroup property and the actual equation give

```text
D C_nu(w)[-nu Aw]=-||Pi N(w)||2^2/nu,
d_t V_nu(w)+2g(w)
 =-nu D_w-||Pi N(w)||2^2/nu+<Aw,Pi N(u)>
   +D H_nu(w)[Pi N(u)]+D C_nu(w)[Pi N(u)].              (196)
```

Thus positivity of storage does not eliminate nonlinear renewal.
The full u in both differentiated terms retains the evolving mean,
all parents, all phases and pressure. It is not replaced by w.

### Positive storage does not alone pay the next return

Use the explicit w_- and w_+ of (194). They have equal positive energy,
enstrophy, D, C_1 and V_1, and g=H_1=0. Define the common values E_*,
Z_*, D_* and the following coefficients, computed exactly by the checker:

```text
b=D H_1(w_-)[Pi N(w_-)]-||Pi N(w_-)||2^2
 =D H_1(w_+)[Pi N(w_+)]-||Pi N(w_+)||2^2 <0,
p=D C_1(w_-)[Pi N(w_-)]
 =-D C_1(w_+)[Pi N(w_+)] >0.                            (197)
```

Their exact values include

```text
E_*=1000598841218897/909543690000000,
Z_*=5249427801854603/909543690000000,
D_*=28714885428973207/909543690000000,
b=-382373288285148495431151591994675913
   /29656662809696737448634000000000000000,
p=20098105310454878385748474602187144764763499
   /355120248771863575260309700871220000000000000000.
```

For u0=a w_- the initial value of (196) is
-nu a^2 D_*+a^4 b/nu+a^5 p/nu^2. At a=512nu its ratio to
(nu/2)D(u0) is strictly greater than 265. Consequently

```text
V_nu(w(t))+2 integral_0^t g(w)
  <= V_nu(w0)+(nu/2)integral_0^t D
```

fails for every sufficiently small positive t of the actual solution.
Local smooth existence and continuity transfer the strict initial
defect to such an interval. No forced dynamics, truncated evolution or
negative reserve is involved. This rejects this particular certificate;
it does not reject a larger original-data allowance or global regularity.

### A correction using an inviscid invariant

The polynomial design principle is established in
[Goulart and Chernyshenko, Sections 1.2 and 3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.1043):
highest-degree terms must be compatible with the inviscid nonlinearity.
Here a direct amplitude argument states the precise necessary condition.
If a fixed polynomial storage has highest homogeneous part V_d, d even,
and every other term in its universal differential inequality has degree
at most d, the coefficient D V_d(u)[N(u)] must vanish. Otherwise the leading
degree d+1 is odd: one sign of arbitrarily large amplitude violates the
inequality. This conclusion does not classify inviscid invariants or
exclude nonpolynomial, restricted-domain or datum-dependent certificates.

For (195), D C_nu[N] is the nonzero quintic term. Appending lower-degree
terms cannot cancel it. A suitable higher-degree invariant can change
that conclusion. In particular, use the FULL energy E=||u||2^2 and set

```text
gamma=1/100000000,
J_nu(u)=V_nu(u-average_z u)+gamma E(u)^3/nu^4 >=0,
d_t(gamma E^3/nu^4)=-6gamma E^2 Z(u)/nu^3.              (198)
```

The last identity follows from the unforced energy law E'=-2nu Z(u).
There is no seventh-degree nonlinear term because <u,N(u)>=0. This
would not hold for the energy of the receiver alone: it exchanges energy
with the mean.

For u0=a w_-(ell x), a!=0 and integer ell>=1, equations (196)--(198)
give the exact initial cost

```text
J_nu'(0)+2g(w0)
 =-nu a^2 ell^4 D_*
   +(a^4 ell^2/nu)[b+p r-q ell^2 r^2],
r=a/(nu ell), q=6gamma E_*^2 Z_*>0.                    (199)
```

For w_+ replace p by -p. Exact rational arithmetic gives
p^2+4qb<0. Completion of the scalar square proves
b+/-p r-q r^2<0 for every real r. Since ell^2>=1, (199) is
strictly less than -nu D(u0) for either initial phase at every nonzero
amplitude and harmonic dilation, with the SAME gamma.

For EACH such datum and nu>0, continuity therefore gives an epsilon>0
on its actual smooth NS lifespan such that

```text
J_nu(u(t))+2 integral_s^t g(w)
 <=J_nu(u(s))+(nu/2)integral_s^t D,
                     0<=s<=t<=epsilon.                (200)
```

This is a positive local repair of the two adversarial phases, not just
a sign check on a projected dynamical system. In particular it includes
the datum that defeats (195). The actual solution may immediately leave
these initial-data rays; no invariance of this family, prescribed
epsilon, arbitrary-horizon payment or global existence follows.
The initial stock contains gradient and source information in V, so
this is not a uniform energy-only arbitrary-data estimate.

### What the control construction must retain next

All intermediate seams in (200) use the same actual state and its
remaining J. Taking successive heat forecasts and choosing a fresh
allowance at each seam is not justified. A continuation certificate
requires control of the complete right-hand side of (196), together
with the energy-cube derivative, after geometry and parent modes change.
It must handle concentration and arbitrary simultaneous modes, not just
harmonic dilation of a fixed profile. Optimizing a constant for the
initial shape does not bound its later reachable shapes.

With external body force f, the derivative acquires
D V_nu(w)[Pi P f]+6gamma E^2<u,f>/nu^4. Incompressibility alone
does not erase these terms. Neither the local repair nor the polynomial
design argument excludes the imported forced singular construction.

and retains a nonzero mean in the actual evolution identity. It checks

## Source-square payment through an actual refeeding history

`receiver_history_payment.py` and `MettapediaNS.EnergyCubeReceiverReserve`
extend the preceding local calculation to a specified actual interval.
The SAME reserve J_nu from (198) pays the receiver stretching through
the full feed--return--feed event of (140). Strengthening original-data
smallness also makes it pay through any prescribed finite number of
the previously constructed approximate pattern cycles. All nonlinear
outputs, the generated mean and the original remaining reserve persist.
This is a controlled-neighborhood result, not arbitrary-data regularity.

### Bounding the complete nonlinear derivative

Use the same normalized period-2pi torus and notation as (195)--(198).
In this section H^j denotes the Fourier Bessel norm
`sum_k (1+|k|^2)^j |u_k|^2`, followed by a square root. Write

```text
B=||u||H3, W=||Pi u||H3, h=Pi N(u), H=||h||H1,
C=32, gamma=1/100000000, E=||u||2^2, Z=||grad u||2^2.
```

The constant C can be fixed independently of the field or frequency
support. Here is one explicit justification. Cubical lattice shell n>=1
has 24n^2+2 points. Integral comparison gives
`sum_(n>=1)n^(-p)<=1+1/(p-1)` for p>1. Therefore

```text
sum_k (1+|k|^2)^(-3) <=1+24(4/3)+2(6/5)<36,
sum_k |k|^2(1+|k|^2)^(-3) <=24(2)+2(4/3)<64.
```

Fourier Cauchy--Schwarz bounds velocity supremum by 6 times its H3
norm and both gradient Frobenius supremum and curl supremum by 8 times
that norm. For the ordered product Bcal(v,q)=-P[(v.grad)q], differentiating
once and using the H1 contraction of P gives
`||Bcal(v,q)||H1 <=(6+8+6)||v||H3||q||H3`.
The same bounds give
`||Bcal(v,h)+Bcal(h,v)||2<=2C||v||H3||h||H1`.
Thus C=32 suffices for all these estimates without an L-infinity bound
on the Leray projection.

Each of the three slots in the variation of g is bounded by
`C||v||H3^2||h||H1`: use gradient supremum in the outer-curl slots,
and curl supremum in the middle-gradient slot. Both w=Pi u and h have
zero vertical mean, so their H3 and H1 heat norms decay at least as
exp(-nu s). Consequently

```text
|D H_nu(w)[h]| <= (2C/nu) W^2 H,
|D C_nu(w)[h]| <= (C^2/nu^2) W^3 H.                    (201)
```

The first bound integrates the three differentiated cubic slots with
decay exp(-3nu s). The second pairs the quadratic source with both
differentiated parent slots and integrates exp(-4nu s), retaining the
outer 1/nu in C_nu. The tangent h is the COMPLETE nonlinear source,
including all interactions with M=average_z u.

Since Pi N(M)=0, the H1 product bound gives
`H<=C(2||M||H3+W)W<=3CBW`. Dropping only the two nonpositive terms
in (196), and using ||Aw||2<=W, now yields

```text
d_t V_nu(w)+2g(w)
 <=W H [1+CW/nu]^2
 <=3CB W^2 [1+CW/nu]^2.                               (202)
```

This controls the full evolution defect. It does not require a sign
for the transfer, frozen geometry, or mean motion remaining zero.

### A region in which one energy-cube reserve pays

Fix an ORIGINAL amplitude A>0. Suppose on an actual smooth interval

```text
A>=256nu, B<=5A, CW<=nu, E>=A^2/9, Z>=A^2/9.           (203)
```

Then (202) is at most 60A nu^2: first use (1+CW/nu)^2<=4,
then CW^2<=(CW)^2<=nu^2, since C>=1. Meanwhile the energy-cube
loss in (198) obeys

```text
6gamma E^2 Z/nu^3 >=(2gamma/243)A^6/nu^3 >=60A nu^2.
```

The last inequality follows from
`(2/(243*100000000))*256^5>60`. Thus, throughout that interval,

```text
d_t[J_nu(u(t))]+2g(Pi u(t))<=0,
J_nu(u(t))+2 integral_s^t g(Pi u)<=J_nu(u(s)).           (204)
```

Nonnegativity follows from
the heat square and full energy, independent of (203). Further, the
initial heat integrals have explicit bounds

```text
|H_nu(w0)| <=(2C/(3nu))W0^3,
C_nu(w0) <=(C^2/(4nu^2))W0^4,
J_nu(u0) <=(17/12)W0^2+gamma E0^3/nu^4.               (205)
```

For the last line use CW0<=nu, Z(w0)<=W0^2 and
1/2+2/3+1/4=17/12. This is a finite initial-data allowance; it contains
the receiver H3 size and is not an energy-only arbitrary-data estimate.
Its signed integral controls the remaining cost in (171) on the stated
interval. The construction's separate H3 stability theorem already
supplies existence in this restricted class.

Retain the earlier reference U=(a v,A rho theta),
v=(sin y,-sin x,0), a=A exp(-nu t), the original clock sigma and the

```text
Ktheta(S)=||theta0||H4,multi exp(228S),
```

```text
3rho Ktheta(S)<=1, Delta<=nu/96,
```

For 0<=sigma<=S, a=A-nu sigma>=A/2. With alpha=<u,v>,

Since ||v||2=||grad v||2=1 and -Delta v=v, projection gives BOTH

```text
0<=t<=t(S)=-log(1-nu S/A)/nu.
```

In particular, take S=3/4 and retain (139), (148)--(150) for the

It does not infer self-stretching's sign from either of those sign words.

For any prescribed finite N pattern cycles, take S=N P0 and retain

The required perturbation may be extremely small and the initial

Only the first feed--return--feed word is certified; it is not asserted

## Source transport cancellation and the evolving covariance interface

`receiver_transport_covariance.py` isolates the signed highest-degree term
in (196). It cancels transport before estimating norms, identifies the
remaining heat commutator with a covariance stress, and retains the actual
physical evolution of that stress. An exact smooth example has negative
source-deformation work but positive complete nonlinear renewal. Thus a
control rule based only on the deformation sign loses necessary information.
This is a refinement of the existing reserve, not a new regularity theorem.

The covariance identity is standard Gaussian-filter mathematics: see
[Johnson, equations (2.44)--(2.46)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2102.06844).
There the filter variance is the auxiliary variable; here it is `2nu s`.
The periodic identity below follows directly from the torus heat semigroup.
The present consumer is the source-square reserve, whose observer differs
from the resolved strain used for ordinary filtered kinetic-energy flux.
No statistical stationarity or turbulence closure is assumed.

### A cancellation valid for the complete nonlinear source

Work on the normalized 2pi torus with a smooth unforced solution on an
available smooth interval, nu>0, M=average_z u, w=Pi u and Pi=I-average_z.
Let P be the Leray projector, Q=Pi P, B(a,b)=-P[(a.grad)b], N(a)=B(a,a).
At each physical time t, use a separate auxiliary heat variable s:

```text
v_s=S_s w, S_s=exp(nu s Delta), n_s=Pi N(v_s), h=Pi N(u),
r_s=S_s Pi N(w)-n_s,
p_s=S_s Pi[N(u)-N(w)],
S_s h=n_s+r_s+p_s.                                     (207)
```

All these vector fields are solenoidal and have zero vertical mean.
In particular n is already pressure-corrected. Differentiating C from
(195), self-adjointness of Q and periodic integration by parts give

```text
D C_nu(w)[h] = Dgeom + Ccov + Pparent,
Dgeom = -(2/nu) integral_0^infinity <n_s,(n_s.grad)v_s> ds,
Ccov  =  (2/nu) integral_0^infinity <r_s,K_s> ds,
Pparent=(2/nu) integral_0^infinity <p_s,K_s> ds,
K_s=Q[(v_s.grad)n_s-(grad v_s)^T n_s].                  (208)
```

Indeed, the differentiated source is
`-Q[((S_s h).grad)v_s+(v_s.grad)(S_s h)]`.
Its part `<n_s,(v_s.grad)n_s>` is exactly zero, since div v_s=0.
For a remainder a=r_s or p_s, move the derivative in
`<n_s,(v_s.grad)a>` onto n_s. The other term contributes
`-(grad v_s)^T n_s`. Pairing with a permits projection of the complete
observer to K_s. This derives (208) without an L-infinity estimate on P.
Dgeom depends only on the symmetric part of grad v_s, but need not be
negative. It is the geometry of the nonlinear SOURCE, not an assertion
that the actual vorticity stretching has the same sign.

### The retained stochastic covariance and its actual evolution

For vector fields a,b define
`Cov_s(a,b)=S_s(a tensor b)-(S_s a) tensor (S_s b)` and put

```text
Tau_s=Cov_s(w,w),
r_s=-Q div Tau_s,
Tau_s=2nu integral_0^s S_(s-a)
             [sum_j partial_j v_a tensor partial_j v_a] da.   (209)
```

The tensor is positive semidefinite pointwise. Equivalently, it is the
covariance of w(x+sqrt(2nu) B_s), with the SAME Brownian displacement in
both factors and coordinates taken modulo the torus. Separate independent
displacements instead give the product of means and omit Tau. These are
auxiliary free-heat probes of the current fluid, not the actual stochastic
Lagrangian trajectories or a Schrödinger-bridge identification.

Tau is not an independently available input. At fixed s its derivative
in actual physical time, from w_t=nu Delta w+h, is

```text
partial_t Tau_s = nu Delta Tau_s - 2nu Gamma_s
                   + Cov_s(h,w)+Cov_s(w,h),
Gamma_s=sum_j Cov_s(partial_j w,partial_j w) >= 0.       (210)
```

To check the diffusion terms, apply the product rule for Delta to each
of `S_s(w tensor w)` and `v_s tensor v_s`. The cross-gradient difference
is precisely -2nu Gamma_s. The remaining terms are the displayed cross
covariances with the FULL h=Pi N(u), including evolving mean motion and
pressure. The nonlinearity can replenish covariance; (210) is not a closed
second-moment model. Its anisotropic part obeys the anisotropic projection
of the same equation. The trace and anisotropic evolution have different
uses and neither may be silently reset at an interface.

The isotropic part `(tr Tau_s/3) I` generates only a pressure gradient.
Thus both the force in (209) and its work are unchanged on replacing Tau
by `Tau_dev=Tau-(tr Tau/3)I`. More precisely,

```text
Ccov=(2/nu) integral_0^infinity <Tau_dev,sym grad K_s> ds,
|Ccov| <= (2/nu) integral_0^infinity
                       ||Tau_dev||2 ||sym grad K_s||2 ds.     (211)
```

The isotropic term pairs to zero because div K_s=0. This is an exact
reduction of the force observation; it does not permit discarding trace
energy from the resource ledger. For example,
`integral tr Tau_s = E(w)-E(v_s)` remains a useful nonnegative quantity.
A positive covariance matrix does not make its pairing with a traceless
symmetric observer positive or negative. In particular, the negative
matrix term in (210) alone does not fix the sign of (211).

### Adverse covariance despite depleting source geometry

Use the real four-mode seed r in the parent-refeeding construction and set
`w_*=r-Pi N(r)/10`. It is smooth, real, solenoidal and has zero vertical
mean. It is a full initial datum; all subsequent nonlinear outputs are
retained. At nu=1 the exact rational checker gives

```text
Dgeom = -0.00017613808742723402...,
Ccov  = +0.00019684919239252254...,
Pparent=0,
D C_1(w_*)[Pi N(w_*)] = +0.00002071110496528852... .     (212)
```

The signs are proved by rational arithmetic, not rounded decimals.
Changing the input to `r+Pi N(r)/10` reverses all three nonzero signs.
For every positive amplitude a and viscosity nu, replacing w_* by a w_*
multiplies these three terms by a^5/nu^2, so the same sign obstruction
holds without an amplitude smallness restriction.
For comparison, the matched data (194) have both Dgeom and Ccov positive
in the adverse phase, and both negative in the other phase. Adding the
actual mean part in `r+/-N(r)/10` also contributes nonzero Pparent;
the checker tests these full fields at nu=2/7.

Consequently, the assertion that positive heat covariance cannot reverse
an integrated depleting source-geometry contribution is false, even with
zero initial mean. For the actual unforced smooth solution from w_*,
continuity preserves Dgeom<0 and D C_1(w)[Pi N(u)]>0 for some positive
short interval; the subsequently generated mean stays in h. This does
NOT say that C increases after viscosity is included, that the full J
payment fails, or that this datum blows up. The rejected assertion concerns
one proposed cancellation in the complete reserve derivative.

There is another diffusion term that must remain when using (208).
Write `G_s=sum_j Pi B(partial_j v_s,partial_j v_s)`. In auxiliary heat time,
`partial_s n_s=nu Delta n_s-2nu G_s`, so

```text
||n_0||2^2/nu = 2 integral_0^infinity ||grad n_s||2^2 ds
                  +4 integral_0^infinity <n_s,G_s> ds.       (213)
```

The second term has no asserted sign. The endpoint loss in (196) cannot
be replaced by pure source-gradient dissipation without retaining it.
The checker verifies both this identity and
`(partial_s-nu Delta)r_s=2nu G_s, r_0=0` independently by heat-rate blocks.

### The precise remaining Bellman estimate

Keep the nonnegative J from (198), its original gamma, and full energy.
Combining the exact identities gives

```text
J'(t)+2g(w) = A_nu(u),
A_nu(u)=-nu D_w-||n_0||2^2/nu+<Aw,h>+D H_nu(w)[h]
        +Dgeom+Ccov+Pparent-6gamma E(u)^2 Z(u)/nu^3.      (214)
```

Thus an actual-history estimate `A_nu(u)<=nu D(u)/2`, or a nonnegative
original-datum-funded correction paying its excess, would discharge the
receiver budget (171). This is the named open physical estimate. The
constructed history class (201)--(206) remains paid, but its small H3
hypothesis has not been removed. A positive bound on (211) involving an
unknown future observer norm would merely relocate that obligation.

A trajectory interface may use the exact force quotient Tau_dev while
retaining the trace for energy accounting and a compatible full-fluid
witness for h. Existing `BoundaryBellman.CostedRelation.Bounds.comp` then
composes proved interval payments with the same intermediate state and
remaining stock. Neither (210) nor tensor positivity supplies the missing
payment. Allowing arbitrary independent covariance inputs would enlarge
the admissible histories and require a separate domination bound.

Run `python3 -O labs/receiver_transport_covariance.py`. Six exact fixtures
check direct differentiation, transport cancellation, covariance-force
reconstruction, anisotropic-force preservation, pressure-corrected stress
work, the physical covariance equation, auxiliary Duhamel generation and
complete source diffusion. Both adverse phases and nonunit viscosity are
retained. The analytic identities apply to arbitrary smooth periodic fields
and smooth NS prefixes; the strict-sign witnesses and their local PDE
interpretation do not establish arbitrary-horizon control. No Lean

## A covariance--Poisson correction and its complete physical defect

`covariance_poisson_corrector.py` tests an explicit correction for the
work isolated in (208)--(214). The two principal diffusion terms pay that
work exactly, but the complete derivative can increase the cost by more
than viscosity and the fixed energy cube pay. This occurs for actual
smooth unforced initial data with purely horizontal velocity and an
entire spectrum inside a thin horizontal belt. The original J remains
unchanged; the correction below is a tested, rejected universal extension.

### Candidate and exact cancellation

Retain every definition in (207)--(214), including the full h=Pi N(u).
Write A=-Delta, with A^-1 on nonzero modes, and define the bilinear
projected observer

```text
L(v,n)=Q[(v.grad)n-(grad v)^T n],   K_s=L(v_s,n_s),
T_nu(w)=(1/nu^2) integral_0^infinity
               <Tau_s,sym grad A^-1 K_s> ds,
Jtrial(u)=J_nu(u)+T_nu(Pi u).                           (215)
```

K_s has zero vertical mean, so its inverse Laplacian is well defined.
Smoothness and exponential decay of v_s and n_s justify these integrals
and their derivatives. The nondecaying spatially constant part of Tau
pairs to zero with a gradient. The isotropic part also has zero pairing.
T is a signed homogeneous quintic, not an independently nonnegative stock.
The candidate requires both a nonnegative total Jtrial and its sufficient
payment inequality along each actual history.

The operator L is the projected adjoint of the linearization of N,
already appearing in (160), here with v_s as its velocity and n_s as
its test field. A^-1 is a fixed elliptic operator; it is not the inverse
of the full physical evolution or an adjoint trajectory propagator.

Define, with B(a,b)=-P[(a.grad)b],

```text
G_s=sum_j Pi B(partial_j v_s,partial_j v_s),
O_s=sum_j L(partial_j v_s,partial_j n_s)+L(v_s,G_s),
z_s=S_s h,
m_s=-Q[(z_s.grad)v_s+(v_s.grad)z_s],
Kdot_N=L(z_s,n_s)+L(v_s,m_s),
Xi_s=Cov_s(h,w)+Cov_s(w,h).
```

The actual covariance equation is (210). The observer's physical
viscous derivative and nonlinear derivative are, respectively,

```text
Kdot_heat=nu Delta K_s-2nu O_s,    Kdot_nonlinear=Kdot_N. (216)
```

This follows from the Laplacian product rule and
`D n_s(w)[nu Delta w]=nu Delta n_s-2nu G_s`.
In particular the product-gradient terms in O_s cannot be discarded.
For a tensor U and vector V abbreviate
`[U,V]=integral_0^infinity <U,sym grad A^-1 V> ds`.
Differentiating the COMPLETE T gives

```text
T_nu'(t)+Ccov = Bcov+Bobs+Qcov+Qobs,
Bcov=-(2/nu)[Gamma,K],    Bobs=-(2/nu)[Tau,O],
Qcov=(1/nu^2)[Xi,K],      Qobs=(1/nu^2)[Tau,Kdot_N].     (217)
```

Each principal Laplacian contributes `-Ccov/2`, since
`Delta A^-1 K=-K`, derivatives commute and the domain is periodic.
The two remaining viscous terms and two nonlinear terms in (217) are
exact. The adjoint changes with the source and the velocity; it is not
frozen while the covariance evolves. All pressure and generated mean
motion enter through the same physical h.

For the matched minus phase (194), at nu=1,
`Bcov=-0.0000552365758...` and `Bobs=-0.0000286018641...`.
The matched plus phase reverses both signs. Although Gamma is positive
semidefinite, its pairing with the inverse-Laplacian strain is not
one-signed. On both of these earlier test data the sum Qcov+Qobs is
negative. That favorable restricted evidence does not persist for all
planar configurations.

### A complete budget failure inside positive storage

Let the four horizontal wave vectors and real coefficients be

```text
p_1=(1,0), p_2=(1,-1), p_3=(2,0), p_4=(2,-1),
c=(4/5,3/5,-1/5,2/5).
```

For an integer ell>=1 define the real field by its positive Fourier
coefficients at `k_j=(ell p_j,1)`:

```text
w_hat_ell(k_j)=c_j*(-(p_j)_y, (p_j)_x, 0),
w_hat_ell(-k_j)=w_hat_ell(k_j),
all other coefficients zero.                          (218)
```

Thus w_ell is solenoidal, has zero vertical mean and zero vertical
velocity, and every input satisfies `|k_z|/|k|<=1/ell`.
The Fourier coefficients, not the cosine amplitudes, are c_j times the
stated vectors. No nonlinear outputs are truncated after choosing these
initial data. In particular the full nonlinearity generates a mean and
an actual positive initial derivative of full vorticity stretching.

At the tested ell=2,16,32, let h_ell=Pi N(w_ell) and define

```text
E_ell=||w_ell||2^2, Z_ell=||grad w_ell||2^2,
D_ell=||A w_ell||2^2,
b_ell=D H_1(w_ell)[h_ell]-||h_ell||2^2<0,
r_ell=D T_1(w_ell)[h_ell]>0,
q_ell=6gamma E_ell^2 Z_ell, gamma=1/100000000.           (219)
```

Since every input has vertical frequency +/-1, the degree-three and
relevant degree-five scalar observations vanish. Exact arithmetic
confirms `g=H=T=0`, `D C_1[h_ell]=0`, and `D T_1[-A w_ell]=0`.
For the actual solution starting at u0=a w_ell, a>0, nu>0, the initial
complete corrected cost is therefore as follows. The powers of viscosity
follow from auxiliary heat-time rescaling: T_nu(a w)=a^5 T_1(w)/nu^3,
and its nonlinear derivative scales as a^6/nu^3.

```text
Jtrial'(0)+2g(w0)
 =-nu a^2 D_ell+(a^4/nu)b_ell
                    +(a^6/nu^3)(r_ell-q_ell).         (220)
```

The initial trial reserve is strictly positive: T=0 and the original
J is its nonnegative source square plus positive full-energy cube.
Representative coefficient values are below; signs and ratios are
certified with the exact fractions printed by the checker.

| ell | r_ell | q_ell | sign of r_ell-q_ell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | 0.003329380483... | 0.0000754397184 | positive |
| 16 | 0.013726589878... | 0.00445053001728 | positive |
| 32 | 0.013907566446... | 0.0177841385472 | negative |

For ell=16,
`E=116/25`, `Z=86132/25`, `D=85631092/25` and
`b=-1844296720901247052794036224/9081619947966623687004375`.
Taking a=256nu gives the strict exact bound

```text
[Jtrial'(0)+2g(w0)] / [(nu/2)||A u0||2^2] > 13.        (221)
```

For ell=2, a=64nu instead gives a ratio greater than 88. These conclusions
hold for every positive viscosity by (220); they are not inviscid tests.
The checker additionally computes the full physical tangent at nonunit
viscosity for ell=16. The original full stretching has
`Dg(w_16)[N(w_16)]=54618599424/333720625>0`; this is an actual generated
stretching example, not just an artificial covariance tensor.

Smooth local existence and continuity now give a positive interval on
which Jtrial stays positive but

```text
Jtrial(u(t))+2 integral_0^t g(Pi u)
  <= Jtrial(u0)+(nu/2) integral_0^t ||A u||2^2
```

fails for every sufficiently small t>0 in that interval. The evolving
mean remains in the full solution. Clipping a negative trial reserve
cannot remove this example because the trial reserve is positive there.

The failure is caused by the NEW correction: deleting r_ell from (220)
leaves the original J with strictly negative initial cost for all a,nu
on these same three profiles. Likewise, the thinner tested profile
ell=32 has r_ell<q_ell and hence strictly negative corrected initial cost
for every amplitude and viscosity. Neither conclusion supplies a time
interval uniform in the parameters, invariance of these profiles, or an
arbitrary-history result. The example does not refute all sufficiently
thin geometries, an increased energy-cube coefficient, a datum-dependent
allowance or another coupled correction.

The accepted identity (217) retains a useful principal cancellation.

## Filtered-source histories paid from full energy

`coarse_receiver_history.py` accompanies a fixed-resolution payment for
every available smooth unforced periodic history. No smallness, planar
polarization or favorable sign of the hidden transfer is assumed. A
nonnegative full-energy reserve pays the complete coarse nonlinear source
renewal. This removes a named part of (214), but its coefficient diverges
as the heat cutoff tends to zero. The remaining fine-scale estimate is
not supplied by the construction.

### Actual source evolution and its moving adjoint

Work on normalized period-2pi T3. Fix nu>0 and a smooth unforced solution
prefix u. Retain Pi, Q=Pi P, w=Pi u, h=Pi N(u), and E=||u||2^2,
Z=||grad u||2^2. In this section the heat parameter is a SPATIAL parameter:
write H_r=exp(r Delta), so H_r=S_(r/nu) in the previous convention.
