It is distinct from physical time t. Set

```text
v_r=H_r w, n_r=Pi N(v_r), z_r=H_r h,
L_v y=-Q[(v.grad)y+(y.grad)v],
L_v^* psi=Q[(v.grad)psi-(grad v)^T psi],
G_r=sum_j Pi B(partial_j v_r,partial_j v_r),
f_r=L_(v_r)(z_r-n_r)-2nu G_r.

partial_t n_r=nu Delta n_r+L_(v_r)n_r+f_r.            (222)
```

This is an equation for the ACTUAL filtered nonlinear source. It follows
by differentiating Pi N(v_r), with
`partial_t v_r=nu Delta v_r+z_r`, and using the Laplacian product rule.
In particular z_r-n_r is the covariance-plus-parent term r_s+p_s of
(207), with s=r/nu. It is not a freely chosen control. Its covariance
still obeys (210), including Xi and both nonlinear parents. Neither
that constraint nor the product-diffusion term G_r is deleted here.

For each fixed r>0 and prefix endpoint T, consider the backward linear
adjoint with a smooth solenoidal, zero-vertical-mean terminal test:

```text
-partial_t psi_r=nu Delta psi_r+L_(v_r)^* psi_r.
<psi_r(T),n_r(T)>-<psi_r(0),n_r(0)>
 =integral_0^T [<L_(v_r)^*psi_r,z_r-n_r>
                         -2nu<psi_r,G_r>] dt.        (223)
```

Both endpoints are retained. On a given smooth prefix the coefficients
are smooth; reversing time gives a linear parabolic equation. No
existence beyond that prefix is assumed. The Leray projection is part
of the operator. It disappears only in its legitimate solenoidal
pairing. This is the existing projected adjoint (160), applied to the
filtered source equation, not a new reconstruction of the full NS flow.

Define explicit lattice constants, summing over k in Z3 with k_z!=0:

```text
alpha_r^2=sum exp(-2r|k|^2),
beta_r^2 =sum |k|^2 exp(-2r|k|^2),
chi_r^2  =sum |k|^-2 exp(-2r|k|^2).                  (224)
```

All are finite for r>0. Fourier Cauchy--Schwarz gives
`||grad v_r||F,infinity<=alpha_r sqrt(Z)`.
In reversed physical time sigma, the exact adjoint norm identity is

```text
(1/2) partial_sigma ||psi_r||2^2
 =-nu||grad psi_r||2^2-<psi_r,(grad v_r)^T psi_r>
 <=alpha_r sqrt(Z) ||psi_r||2^2.
```

The coefficient is evaluated along the reversed actual history.
For any physical a<=b within that history, the full energy identity
`E'=-2nu Z` and Cauchy--Schwarz yield

```text
||psi_r(a)||2
 <=exp(alpha_r sqrt((b-a)(E(a)-E(b))/(2nu)))
       ||psi_r(b)||2
 <=exp(alpha_r sqrt(H E(0)/(2nu))) ||psi_r(b)||2,
       0<=a<=b<=H.                                  (225)
```

Thus this genuinely moving observer has a fixed-resolution growth price
from original resources, without a future H4 bound or a small receiver.
The estimate allows amplification. The exact shear
`u=(A exp(-nu t) sin(z),0,0)` and the terminal test
`psi=(cos(y)cos(z),-2sin(y)sin(2z),-cos(y)cos(2z))`
have `||psi||2^2=3/2`, `||grad psi||2^2=27/4` and instantaneous reversed
half-norm rate `-27nu/4+A exp(-r)/8`. At r=log(2), A=128nu this is
`5nu/4>0`. Both fields belong to the receiver subspace. This shows why
contractivity cannot replace the finite growth price.

Composition does not restart the energy allowance. For interval lengths
delta_j and energies actually spent e_j=E(t_j)-E(t_(j+1)),
`sum sqrt(delta_j e_j)<=sqrt((sum delta_j)(sum e_j))`.
The exponent in the product of adjoint bounds is therefore paid by the
same original E. This is the dissipation-root observation already treated
by `FullEnergyParentReserve`, used here to bound the physical adjoint.
The remaining forcing f_r in (223) must still be paid.

### Payment of the complete coarse renewal

Choose a fixed rho>0 before evaluating future history. Define

```text
C_(nu,rho)(w)=(1/nu^2) integral_rho^infinity ||n_r||2^2 dr,
K_r=L_(v_r)^* n_r,
P_(nu,rho)(u)=(2/nu^2) integral_rho^infinity <K_r,H_r h> dr.

partial_t C_(nu,rho)
 =-||n_rho||2^2/nu+P_(nu,rho).                       (226)
```

C_(nu,rho) is precisely the coarse part of the previous C_nu, after the
change of auxiliary variable r=nu s. The heat derivative in (226) spends
its lower endpoint. The nonlinear part retains every generated mode.
Self-adjointness and integration by parts give the additional exact form

```text
P_(nu,rho)=(2/nu^2) integral_rho^infinity
                      <u tensor u,grad H_r K_r> dr. (227)
```

The u here is the FULL fluid, including the evolving mean. This identity
does not freeze K_r or omit its dependence on the source: 2K_r is the
gradient with respect to v_r of ||Pi N(v_r)||2^2 at the current state.
No separate signed correction T is added or differentiated.

Here is a quantitative bound with no unobserved norms. For
`W_j(v)=sum |k|^j |v_hat(k)|`, projections Q contract each coefficient,
and the complete convolutions give

```text
W_0(n)<=W_0(v)W_1(v),
W_1(n)<=W_1(v)^2+W_0(v)W_2(v),
||K||2<=W_0(K)<=2W_0(v)W_1(v)^2+W_0(v)^2W_2(v).

W_0(v_r)<=alpha_r sqrt(E),
W_0(v_r)<=chi_r sqrt(Z),
W_1(v_r)<=alpha_r sqrt(Z),
W_2(v_r)<=beta_r sqrt(Z).
```

Consequently, with explicit functions depending only on the heat scale,

```text
j(r)=2 alpha_r^3 beta_r+alpha_r chi_r beta_r^2,
I_rho=integral_rho^infinity j(r) dr,
||grad H_r K_r||F,infinity<=j(r) sqrt(E) Z,
|P_(nu,rho)(u)|<=(2I_rho/nu^2) E^(3/2) Z.            (228)
```

The constants are finite. For an entirely elementary closed upper bound,
put q=exp(-rho), R=q^2 and

```text
Lbar_rho=(1+R)^3(1+4R+R^2)/(1-R)^5.
I_rho<=(3/4)Lbar_rho^2.
```

Indeed all three squared lattice constants are bounded by
`sum_(k_z!=0)(1+|k|^2)exp(-2rho|k|^2)<=Lbar_rho`.
Enlarging this last sum to all Z3, factor its three coordinates and use
`exp(-2rho m^2)<=R^|m|` to sum the geometric series and its second moment.
For r>=rho, each lattice constant decays by at least exp(-(r-rho));
the four factors in j give the integral factor 1/4. At rho=log(2),
`Lbar_rho=1375/81`. This closed bound is conservative; I_rho is the
more precise constant used below.

The required reserve now follows from the ACTUAL energy equation:

```text
R_(nu,rho)(E)=(2I_rho/(5nu^3)) E^(5/2)>=0,
partial_t R_(nu,rho)=-(2I_rho/nu^2) E^(3/2) Z,
partial_t R_(nu,rho)+|P_(nu,rho)|<=0.                 (229)
```

The fifth power is the fifth power of ||u||2, not of E. Its nonlinear
derivative vanishes because all internal kinetic transfers cancel in E.
The function E^(5/2) has a continuous derivative at E=0, so no singular
zero-energy convention is needed. Integrating over ANY compatible
subinterval [a,b] gives both payments

```text
integral_a^b |P_(nu,rho)|<=R_(nu,rho)(E(a))-R_(nu,rho)(E(b)),
C_(nu,rho)(w(b))+R_(nu,rho)(E(b))
 +(1/nu) integral_a^b ||n_rho||2^2
 <=C_(nu,rho)(w(a))+R_(nu,rho)(E(a)).                 (230)
```

This is valid for arbitrary smooth periodic histories at the chosen
fixed rho. There is no perturbative H3 assumption, preferred phase,
invariant planar family or restriction on the number of returns.
At a seam the full velocity must match and the same rho and reserve
remain in use. The scalar energy does not reconstruct an interior fluid
or certify compatibility of two arbitrary pattern labels.

### The precise remainder and the price of refining resolution

Let P_less be the same integral as P_(nu,rho), but over 0<r<rho.
Retain the original nonnegative J of (198), with its unchanged gamma.
Adding R_(nu,rho) to J removes only the coarse quintic work from (214):

```text
(J+R_(nu,rho))'+2g(w)
 <=-nu D_w-||Pi N(w)||2^2/nu+<Aw,h>+D H_nu(w)[h]
                  +P_less-6gamma E^2 Z/nu^3.        (231)
```

The sufficient remaining task is to bound this right side by
`(nu/2)D(full u)`, or to pay its excess with a further nonnegative,
original-data correction. The initial allowance has increased by the
explicit finite R_(nu,rho)(E(0)). The small-r part is exactly where an
additional geometric or history estimate is still needed. No part of
the source endpoint loss is spent twice: the coarse boundary
`-||n_rho||2^2/nu` cancels the opposite endpoint in the fine heat integral.

Refining resolution is also an exact, testable operation. If rho=rho(t)
is differentiable, the complete derivative of C_(nu,rho)+R_(nu,rho)
has the extra terms

```text
-rho'(t) ||n_rho||2^2/nu^2
 -(2rho'(t)/(5nu^3)) j(rho) E^(5/2).                 (232)
```

Both are nonnegative when rho decreases. In particular one cannot apply
(230) with a new finer cutoff at each seam without paying this change.
The actual I_rho tends to infinity as rho tends to zero: for small r,
count lattice points with all three coordinates of order r^(-1/2).
They give `alpha_r>=c r^(-3/4)` and `beta_r>=c r^(-5/4)`, hence
`j(r)>=c r^(-7/2)` and a divergent integral. This is a limitation of
the supplied bound, not a proof that the actual signed fine-scale work
diverges or that a full-datum allowance is impossible.

For a body force F, (226) additionally contains
`(2/nu^2) integral_rho^infinity <K_r,H_r Pi P F> dr`, and (229)
additionally contains `(2I_rho/nu^3) E^(3/2)<u,F>`.
The theorem is unforced; a forced application must retain these terms.
Its fixed-resolution scope alone does not exclude a forced singular
construction or prove arbitrary-data unforced regularity.

There is also an actual concentration test for a stronger possible claim
about the adjoint, independently of the lattice upper bound. On R3 use
the full Leray adjoint (160), without the periodic projection Pi. Choose
a compactly supported smooth solenoidal U equal to `(-x,-y,2z)` on a
ball: one construction is `curl(chi*(-yz,xz,0))`, with chi equal to one
there. Choose a nonzero `Psi=curl(0,0,eta)` supported strictly inside that
ball. Then `-<Psi,(grad U)^T Psi>=||Psi||2^2>0`.
Normalize both L2 norms to one. By heat convergence in C1, some fixed
rho_*>0 still gives
`a_*=-<Psi,(grad H_(rho_*) U)^T Psi>>0`.

Set U_lambda(x)=lambda^(3/2)U(lambda x),
Psi_lambda(x)=lambda^(3/2)Psi(lambda x), and
rho_lambda=rho_*/lambda^2. Both L2 norms remain one. Heat scaling and
the solenoidal pressure pairing give the EXACT instantaneous adjoint rate

```text
<Psi_lambda,[nu Delta+L_(H_(rho_lambda)U_lambda)^*]Psi_lambda>
 =lambda^(5/2) a_*-nu lambda^2 ||grad Psi||2^2.        (233)
```

It tends to positive infinity at every fixed nu>0. These are admissible
smooth unforced initial velocities, not a constructed forcing or a
finite-dimensional surrogate. Local smooth existence and continuity let
one put the terminal test at a sufficiently short positive time and
retain positive backward norm growth on the actual prefix. Thus a
uniform INSTANTANEOUS adjoint-growth coefficient depending only on
kinetic energy and nu cannot replace the scale price. This does not
refute a full-datum bound, an integrated bound with transient cancellation,
or (229). The latter keeps its prescribed positive cutoff; the family
in (233) refines it with lambda. The compact-support and local-PDE
argument is analytic, separate from the periodic Fourier fixtures.

### Verification and relation to existing tools

The projection and Gaussian-covariance framework is the one already
derived in (207)--(214), reusing the filtering identities discussed by
[Johnson](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.06844). The present original-energy
price follows directly from the displayed Fourier estimates and energy
equation. The scalar dissipation-root reserve is already Lean-certified
in `FullEnergyParentReserve`; its identification with this filtered
adjoint and the new spatial estimates remain analytic.

Run `python3 -O labs/coarse_receiver_history.py`. Exact rational heat
weights check (222)--(223), the adjoint norm identity, the three forms
of coarse renewal, lower-endpoint diffusion and the fine/coarse
cancellation. The six full-source fixtures cover both hidden phases,
a nonzero generated mean, nonunit viscosity and the three planar belts
of (218). Independent exact quartic polarization checks the physical
capacity derivative. The decaying-shear test verifies positive transient
adjoint growth, and squared rational inequalities test the explicit
payment bound. Every convolution and pressure output is retained.
The checker does not prove the infinite lattice estimates, parabolic
construction or arbitrary-history PDE conclusions. Those are analytic
arguments above; no Lean declarations or axioms change.

## Concentration and the limits of kinetic-energy corrections

`receiver_concentration.py` tests the unpaid fine part of (231). The
result rules out a universal differential payment by the particular
joint storage (195) plus any fixed C1 function of kinetic energy. It
does not rule out a continuation allowance depending on the full initial
datum, a different geometric storage, or an integrated history argument.
The fixed-resolution payment (229) remains valid.

### The assertion being tested

Fix nu>0 and a nonnegative C1 function F of kinetic energy, chosen before
the datum. F may depend on nu and a prescribed horizon or heat cutoff.
The proposed assertion is that every smooth unforced periodic solution
satisfies

```text
partial_t [V_nu(Pi u)+F(E(u))]+2g(Pi u)
                       <=(nu/2)||Delta u||2^2.        (234)
```

The energy cube in (198), with ANY fixed coefficient, and its sum with
the coarse reserve (229) are particular choices. The counterexample
below has E(u0)=1 exactly. It gives arbitrarily large positive initial
violations of (234), persisting on actual short smooth solution
intervals. No forcing or closed finite-mode evolution is used.

### A positive full-source coefficient

Localization must retain outputs removed by the periodic vertical-mean
projection: a localized packet around a zero-vertical-frequency output
need not remain on the zero-frequency plane. First perform the calculation
with the FULL advective Leray source. Use the spatial heat H_r=exp(r Delta)
and put

```text
Ctilde_nu(U)=nu^-2 integral_0^infinity ||N(H_r U)||2^2 dr,
Ptilde(U)=D Ctilde_1(U)[N(U)].
```

For the periodic matched data w_- and w_+ in (194), the exact full-source
calculation gives

```text
Ptilde(w_-)=
 85124461354557274284120223753665783495727
 /812632148219367449108260185060000000000000000 >0,
Ptilde(w_+)=-Ptilde(w_-).                             (235)
```

Both have the same energy and full initial source capacity. Their actual
nonlinear directions generate a vertical mean, and that mean is retained
in (235). The checker independently verifies the nonnegative full heat
square, the pure-heat endpoint loss, kinetic cancellation and an exact
quartic polarization of the full physical derivative. This is the
advective source capacity, not the earlier inverse-curl stretching
capacity of `caloric_force.py`.

### Solenoidal localization with a positive coefficient

Use the same measure normalization on R3 as on the torus: dmu=(2pi)^-3 dx.
Let A_per=curl(-Delta)^-1 w_- be a periodic vector potential. All its
Fourier modes have nonzero vertical coordinate. Choose a nonzero
nonnegative Schwartz function phi with compact Fourier support, and set

```text
U_L=curl[phi(x/L) A_per(x)].
```

Such a phi can be obtained by squaring the real inverse Fourier transform
of a real even smooth compactly supported function. The field U_L is
Schwartz and exactly solenoidal. For large L its Fourier support lies
in finitely many narrow packets around the original centers, separated
both from zero and from the plane xi_z=0. The envelope derivative in
the curl is retained; its leading contribution is O(1/L).

Expand the quintic functional Ptilde into its finite packet integrals.
Nonresonant combinations vanish for large L. In a resonant term rescale
the packet offsets by L. Away from zero the Leray multipliers converge
to their central values. At a zero intermediate output, use divergence
form: P(k) i k_j is bounded by |k| and extends continuously as zero
there. Such zero-output source terms are lower order; no pressure
singularity is discarded. The auxiliary heat denominator stays bounded
away from zero because the pairing contains original nonzero input
frequencies, including when N(U_L) has a low-frequency output.
Thus the heat integrals have a common integrable exponential bound.
Dominated convergence gives

```text
L^-3 Ptilde(U_L) -> Ptilde(w_-) integral phi^5 dmu >0,
L^-3 ||U_L||2^2 -> ||w_-||2,per^2 integral phi^2 dmu >0.
```

Fix a sufficiently large L and normalize by the exact L2 norm. This
gives a fixed Schwartz solenoidal U with E(U)=1, a vertical Fourier gap,
and c_*=Ptilde(U)>0. Normalization preserves this strict sign. The checker
tests a finite one-coordinate periodic envelope, including its curl
correction and fifth moment; it does not certify this R3 packet limit.

### Unit-energy concentration and the actual periodic receiver

On R3 set U_lambda(x)=lambda^(3/2)U(lambda x). Its energy remains one.
The complete scaling laws, with the volume factor included, are

```text
Z(U_lambda)=lambda^2 Z(U),
D(U_lambda)=lambda^4 D(U),
g(U_lambda)=lambda^(9/2)g(U),
||N(U_lambda)||2^2=lambda^5 ||N(U)||2^2,
D H_nu(U_lambda)[N(U_lambda)]
                  =lambda^5 D H_1(U)[N(U)]/nu,
Ctilde_nu(U_lambda)=lambda^3 Ctilde_1(U)/nu^2,
D Ctilde_nu(U_lambda)[N(U_lambda)]
                  =lambda^(11/2)c_*/nu^2.            (236)
```

These are concentration laws, not the fixed-amplitude harmonic dilations
of (199). In particular the quartic source loss is only order lambda^5,
whereas the positive quintic renewal has the larger exponent 11/2.

For an actual datum on the original period-2pi torus, periodize:

```text
v_lambda(x)=lambda^(3/2) sum_(m in Z3) U(lambda(x+2pi m)),
u_(0,lambda)=v_lambda/||v_lambda||2,per.
```

With Fourier transform Uhat(xi)=(2pi)^-3 integral U(x)exp(-i xi.x)dx,
vhat_lambda(k)=lambda^-3/2 Uhat(k/lambda). Parseval and Riemann sums give
||v_lambda||2,per ->1. The original vertical gap implies Pi u_(0,lambda)
=u_(0,lambda) exactly. The data are finite Fourier polynomials because
Uhat is compactly supported, but their NS evolution is never truncated.

Riemann sums of the multilinear Fourier formulas give the same leading
constants in (236). The projections on generated outputs require a
separate check: the removed plane k_z=0 is codimension one in the
rescaled sums, and its bounded integrands have vanishing normalized
contribution. All initial frequencies have a uniform rescaled gap, so
the heat-time domination used above applies here as well. Thus the
actual receiver, with h=Pi N(u_(0,lambda)), satisfies

```text
D C_nu(u_(0,lambda))[h]
          =lambda^(11/2)(c_*+o(1))/nu^2,
D H_nu(u_(0,lambda))[h]=O(lambda^5/nu),
||h||2^2=O(lambda^5),
Z=O(lambda^2), D=O(lambda^4), g=O(lambda^(9/2)).       (237)
```

The generated mean is retained in the physical equation. Its projection
in this initial receiver derivative is exactly the one in (196), not an
assumption that the mean remains zero during evolution.

Because E(u_(0,lambda))=1, the energy correction contributes exactly
-2nu F'(1)Z, of order lambda^2. Substitution into (196) shows

```text
partial_t[V_nu(Pi u)+F(E)]+2g(Pi u)-(nu/2)D(u)
          =lambda^(11/2)(c_*+o(1))/nu^2 >0            (238)
```

at the initial time for every sufficiently large lambda. For each such
smooth datum, local unforced NS existence and continuity preserve the
strict inequality on some positive interval. Integrating over a smaller
interval violates (234)'s proposed storage payment with its original
initial reserve. No interval uniform in lambda is asserted by this
periodic argument.

At any fixed rho>0 the coarse renewal is O(lambda^2), directly by (228).
Hence the fine term P_less has the same positive lambda^(11/2) leading
coefficient as (237). Adding the coarse energy reserve pays the part it
was designed to pay; it cannot remove this concentrating fine remainder.

### A whole-space burst and what it does not refute

There is also a common rescaled-time interpretation on R3. Let V^epsilon
solve the actual unforced equation from the fixed datum U with viscosity
epsilon, and take epsilon=nu/sqrt(lambda). Standard local H^m energy
estimates for m sufficiently large give a common interval [0,tau0] and
uniform smooth bounds for 0<=epsilon<=1. This does not assume global Euler
or NS regularity: the transport estimate and nonpositive viscous term
give a local lifespan from ||U||_(H^m) alone. Higher initial regularity
gives a uniform bound on the time derivative in the norms used here.

Ptilde is continuous on these bounded smooth sets. On heat times below
one this follows from Sobolev product estimates; above one, Fourier heat
estimates bound its integrand by O(r^(-7/2)) times bounded energy and
enstrophy. Reduce tau0 so that Ptilde(V^epsilon(tau))>=c_*/2 uniformly.
Rescale the ACTUAL solution by

```text
u_lambda(t,x)=lambda^(3/2)
                 V^(nu/sqrt(lambda))(lambda^(5/2)t,lambda x).
```

It has viscosity nu and unit initial energy. The leading renewal
integrated to tau0 lambda^(-5/2) is at least
c_*tau0 lambda^3/(2nu^2). The integrated quartic terms are
O(lambda^(5/2)/nu), cubic stretching O(lambda^2), and viscous
dissipation O(nu lambda^(3/2)). The energy loss is only
O(nu lambda^(-1/2)), so any fixed C1 energy correction changes by that
order near E=1. Consequently the integrated excess of the analogous
full-space joint storage payment is positive and unbounded as lambda
increases. This is an actual unforced burst, not a prescribed force.

However, the ORIGINAL full-source capacity already has size
lambda^3 Ctilde_1(U)/nu^2. The burst does not exceed every possible
allowance based on the full datum. It refutes the particular monotone
storage inequality, not the signed stretching criterion itself, and
does not construct indefinite renewal or a singular NS solution.
Allowing F to depend on concentration information from the original
datum is outside the fixed-energy-correction claim (234).

The next physical resource must therefore control the concentrating
source geometry or its actual renewal history; positivity of the
current heat square and a fixed kinetic-energy supplement do not
supply that control. This retains the distinction between a finite
burst and unbounded repeated renewal.

### Verification

Run `python3 -O labs/receiver_concentration.py`. The exact fixtures check
the full-source coefficient, its opposite phase, all nonlinear outputs,
the heat-square identity, endpoint diffusion, independent quartic
polarization, concentration exponents with the volume factor, and the
fine/coarse split. Periodic envelopes at lengths 32 and 128 have positive
coefficients within respectively 0.000100 and 0.00000624 of their
predicted fifth-moment limit in relative error. The actual comparisons
are rational, not rounded floating-point sign tests.

The Schwartz localization, Riemann-sum passage, local PDE intervals and
uniform rescaled-time argument are analytic. They are not newly
Lean-certified, and the finite checker does not prove them. No Lean
declarations or axioms change.


## Normalized storage and an actual first-generation obstruction

`normalized_receiver.py` tests whether normalizing the auxiliary source
stock repairs (234). The first weight fails immediately. A common-weight
repair pays a whole family of initial states, but the actual flow can leave
that payment region. The latter conclusion is an analytic whole-space
history argument, supported by exact finite Fourier fixtures. It is not an
arbitrary-data regularity result or a construction of indefinite renewal.

### Two weights and their complete physical derivatives

Write A=-Delta, w=Pi u, h=Pi N(u), n=Pi N(w), Z=||grad w||2^2,
H=H_nu(w) and C=C_nu(w) as in (195). The heat-square pairing gives
H^2<=2ZC. The proposed square-root normalization is

```text
theta=sqrt[Z/(Z+8C)],
W_sqrt=Z/2+theta H+theta^2 C,
theta'=4theta(C Z'-Z C')/[Z(Z+8C)].                 (239)
```

For u0=100r, nu=1, with r the seed of `cellular_parent_refeeding.py`,
g(r)=H(r)=0. Nevertheless the complete initial excess
W_sqrt'+2g-(1/2)D(full u) is greater than D(full u)=315500.
An exact squared-rational comparison certifies this strict radical
inequality. The forecast derivative carries theta while the negative
source loss carries theta^2; the initial test exposes this mismatch.

Instead use the SAME weight for forecast and source stock. For beta>=8,

```text
chi=Z/(Z+beta C),
W_beta=Z/2+chi(H+C),
Z/4<=W_beta<=7Z/8,
chi'=beta(C Z'-Z C')/(Z+beta C)^2.                  (240)
```

Indeed |chi H|/Z<=sqrt(2C/Z)/(1+beta C/Z)<=1/sqrt(2beta),
and 0<=chi C/Z<=1/beta. These inequalities also give a continuous
extension W_beta=0 at Z=0. Differentiability there is not asserted or
used below. All tested histories have Z>0.

The physical rates, including the surrounding fluid, are

```text
Z'=-2nu D_w+2<Aw,h>,
H'=-2g(w)+D H_nu(w)[h],
C'=-||n||2^2/nu+D C_nu(w)[h],

W_beta'=[1/2+beta C(H+C)/(Z+beta C)^2]Z'
       +chi H'+Z(Z-beta H)C'/(Z+beta C)^2.          (241)
```

Equivalently W_beta'=Z'/2+chi(H'+C')+chi'(H+C).
The checker tests both forms and independently obtains Z', H', C' by
exact polynomial polarization in the full physical NS direction.
Its fixture has both an existing and an evolving vertical mean.
The weight changes the observation; it applies no force to the fluid.

### A positive initial certificate at all amplitudes

Take a mean-free periodic seed with vertical frequencies only +1 and -1.
Then g=H=D C_nu(w)[Pi N(w)]=0 initially, by odd-degree frequency parity.
Set C1=C_1(w), R=D H_1(w)[Pi N(w)], N2=||Pi N(w)||2^2 and c=C1/Z.
For u0=a w(ell x), a nonzero, integer ell>=1, put r0=(a/(nu ell))^2.
The complete half-dissipation excess, divided by nu a^2 ell^4 and
multiplied by (1+beta c r0)^2, is

```text
 -(3/2)D
 +r0 [R-N2-3beta cD]
 +r0^2 [beta cR-beta(3beta/2+2)c^2D].                (242)
```

Thus the strict inequalities R-N2-24cD<0 and R<14cD imply strict
initial payment for EVERY amplitude, positive viscosity, integer
dilation and beta>=8. They hold exactly for r and for each of the
three planar belts of lengths 2, 16 and 32 in (218). The values of
RZ/(C1 D) are respectively about 3.050, 0.447, 0.00859 and 0.00216.
The claim covers all scalings of these four seeds, not every belt length.
Continuity gives a positive payment interval for each actual smooth
solution. No common duration or invariant payment region follows.

### Zero initial stretching that the full fluid regenerates

For the following whole-space construction, replace Pi by the identity
EVERYWHERE in (240)--(242), including the nonlinear source capacity.
This full-source convention retains every generated output. The seed is

```text
r(x)=(1/10) sum_(k,v) v cos(k.x),
(k,v)=((1,0,1),(1,-2,-1)), ((1,-1,1),(-4,-2,2)),
      ((2,0,1),(-3,-5,6)), ((2,-1,1),(4,10,2)).
```

Each polarization is transverse. The full pressure-projected nonlinearity
N(r)=-P div(r tensor r) obeys the exact identities

```text
g(r)=H_1(r)=D Ctilde_1(r)[N(r)]=0,
Dg(r)[-Ar]=0,
Dg(r)[N(r)]=892051/1092000>0.                       (243)
```

The full-source initial certificate (242) also holds, with
RZ/(Ctilde_1 D) approximately 0.303. The field's own evolution therefore
generates positive stretching from a state with zero stretching and
strict initial payment. This uses all NS outputs, not a closed mode model.

Localize this seed by U_L=curl[phi(x/L)curl(-Delta)^-1 r], with the
bandlimited nonnegative Schwartz envelope used above. Choose L so that
the vertical packet width delta is less than 1/5. No sum of three or
five packets centered at vertical frequencies +1 and -1 can equal zero.
Consequently the three odd-degree zeros in (243) persist EXACTLY on R3,
as does Dg(U_L)[-AU_L]=0. The quartic packet limit instead gives

```text
L^-3 Dg(U_L)[N(U_L)]
       ->(892051/1092000) integral phi^4 dmu>0.
```

The divergence-form Leray multiplier at zero intermediate output is
O(|k|), as in (235). Nonzero inputs retain the heat denominator gap.
Dominated convergence applies to the quartic coefficients R, N2 and
Ctilde_1, with common leading envelope factor integral phi^4; Z and D
have factor integral phi^2. Thus both strict inequalities for (242)
survive for sufficiently large L. Normalize the resulting fixed U to
E(U)=1. Homogeneity preserves these strict signs and the zero identities
in (243), rather than its original periodic numerical coefficient.

### The payment fails on the actual positive-viscosity history

Fix nu>0 and beta>=8. Let V^epsilon solve the full unforced R3 equation
from this U with viscosity epsilon, including the local Euler solution
V^0. On a common short interval, high Sobolev transport estimates give
bounds uniform for 0<=epsilon<=1. The difference equation, with forcing
epsilon Delta V^0 and zero initial difference, gives convergence
V^epsilon->V^0 in any fixed required Sobolev norm after taking enough
initial derivatives. This is only a local smooth inviscid-limit argument;
it assumes neither global Euler regularity nor global NS regularity.
For the classical smooth inviscid-limit framework see
[Constantin (1986)](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01211598).

By (243), g(V^0(0))=0 and its derivative is strictly positive. Choose
a fixed sufficiently small tau*>0 such that
DeltaZ=Z(V^0(tau*))-Z(U)>0, using Z'=2g for Euler.
Also reduce the interval so that Ctilde_1(V^epsilon) is bounded below
by a fixed positive constant. Continuity of this functional follows
from Sobolev products for heat times below one; above one,
||N(exp(r Delta)v)||2 is O(r^(-5/4)) on bounded L2 sets, giving an
integrable squared tail. H_1 is continuous by the analogous heat
pairing. These controls retain the newly generated low frequencies.

For large lambda put epsilon=nu/sqrt(lambda) and

```text
u_lambda(t,x)=lambda^(3/2)
                 V^epsilon(lambda^(5/2)t,lambda x),
t_lambda=tau* lambda^(-5/2).
```

These are actual smooth, finite-energy, unforced solutions with positive
viscosity nu, E(u_lambda(0))=1 and g(u_lambda(0))=0. Their initial
payment is strict: concentration changes r0 in (242) to lambda/nu^2,
with normalization factor nu lambda^4. No geometry is frozen later.

On the common rescaled interval the complete scaling laws give

```text
lambda^-2 W_(beta,nu)(u_lambda(t))
          ->(1/2+1/beta) Z(V^0(tau)),
2lambda^-2 integral_0^t_lambda g(u_lambda)dt -> DeltaZ,
lambda^-2 nu integral_0^t_lambda D(u_lambda)dt ->0.
```

Here chi C/lambda^2->Z/beta and chi H/lambda^2->0. The strictly
positive capacity lower bound justifies both limits. If F is any fixed
C1 function of current kinetic energy, chosen before the datum, its
endpoint change is O(nu lambda^(-1/2)); it cannot alter the limit.
Therefore

```text
lambda^-2 { [W_(beta,nu)+F(E)](t_lambda)
             -[W_(beta,nu)+F(E)](0)
  +2 integral_0^t_lambda [g(u_lambda(t))-g(u_lambda(0))]dt
  -(nu/2) integral_0^t_lambda D(u_lambda)dt }
       ->(3/2+1/beta) DeltaZ>0.                    (244)
```

Every fixed beta>=8 fails this integrated storage payment, even though
its initial rate pays. A fixed F also preserves strict initial payment
for sufficiently large lambda, since its initial derivative is only
order lambda^2, while the negative initial margin is order nu lambda^4.
For any prescribed positive horizon, these intervals eventually lie
inside it. The theorem here concerns the full R3 storage; no periodic
Pi history limit is claimed by this argument.

### A reserve from the original heat history pays this burst

There is a concrete positive repair on the SAME actual histories. Retain
h(t)=exp(nu t Delta)u0, fixed from the original datum, and put

```text
B_(u0,nu)(t)=Ctilde_nu(h(t))
           =(1/nu) integral_t^infinity ||N(exp(nu s Delta)u0)||2^2 ds,
B_(u0,nu)'(t)=-||N(h(t))||2^2/nu,
J_beta(t)=W_(beta,nu)(u(t))+B_(u0,nu)(t)>=0.         (245)
```

This is an auxiliary observer trajectory, not a replacement for the actual
NS solution. B decreases and cannot acquire credit from newly generated
fluid structure. At a later segment it retains the original heat age;
restarting it from the actual segment endpoint would be a different rule.

For the concentrating histories above, write C1=Ctilde_1(V^epsilon)
and H1=H_1(V^epsilon). In the rescaled variables,

```text
lambda^-2 W_(beta,nu)(u_lambda)
        =Z/2+Z(epsilon H1+C1)/(epsilon^2 Z+beta C1).
```

The uniform Sobolev bounds and positive lower bound for C1 give a constant
M, independent of sufficiently large lambda, such that the actual
W'+2g-(nu/2)D is at most M lambda^(9/2) on the entire controlled interval.
This uses the complete derivative, including the weight derivative. The
heat-functional derivatives are uniformly bounded by the same product
estimates and integrable tails used above.

Meanwhile N(U) is nonzero, by (243). Since
h_lambda(t)=lambda^(3/2)[exp(epsilon tau Delta)U](lambda x),
continuity gives a fixed m>0 with ||N(exp(epsilon tau Delta)U)||2^2>=m
for 0<=tau<=tau* and sufficiently small epsilon. Thus throughout this
actual positive-viscosity interval,

```text
J_beta'+2[g(u_lambda(t))-g(u_lambda(0))]-(nu/2)D
       <=M lambda^(9/2)-(m/nu)lambda^5<=0           (246)
```

for sufficiently large lambda. The constants come from the fixed smooth
U and its uniform local existence estimates, not from an assumed global
bound on an unknown solution. Equations (245)--(246) give a nonnegative,
original-datum reserve that pays the complete first generated burst which
violates (244).

This payment lasts through tau* lambda^(-5/2), where the original heat
age is only epsilon tau*. It does not control later interacting parents,
or prove payment through a full diffusion time of order 1/(nu lambda^2).
The latter corresponds to rescaled time of order 1/epsilon, outside the
common local interval used in this argument.

### What the obstruction requires of a repair

Equation (244) is a finite first-generation burst of order lambda^2.
The ORIGINAL source capacity is already of order lambda^3/nu^2.
Equations (245)--(246) explicitly spend that credit on the first burst.
This calculation does not refute a datum-dependent allowance K, the signed-renewal
continuation criterion, or global regularity. Nor does it construct
unlimited recurrent amplification. It rejects the stated normalized
monotone storage rule and shows why initial payment alone is insufficient.

A history repair must keep track of that larger initial resource and
justify how it is spent as new geometry appears. Recomputing a fresh
capacity from each evolved state would allow the credit itself to grow;
calling it the same original reserve would not establish a payment.
The fixed-resolution bound (229) continues to pay its coarse component.
The finer coupled-history estimate remains open.

### Verification

Run `python3 -O labs/normalized_receiver.py`. Exact checks include the
square-root failure, complete changing-weight derivatives, independent
physical-tangent polarization, the initial polynomial at several scales,
its coefficient certificates for four seed families, the full-source
positive stretching derivative (243), and the exact original-heat-bank
loss at three distinct heat ages. Two finite curl envelopes at
lengths 32 and 128 preserve all odd-degree zeros and positive generation;
the relative errors from their fourth-moment limit are approximately
0.000237 and 0.0000148. Signs are checked with rational arithmetic.

The Schwartz localization, uniform smooth local existence, inviscid
limit and positive-viscosity solution-history argument are analytic.
The checker does not certify these infinite-dimensional steps, and no
Lean declarations or axioms change.

## Original heat parents and the generated remainder's critical cost

`heat_remainder_payment.py` isolates what an original-heat reserve can
pay on EVERY available smooth prefix, without assuming a small residual.
The setting is unforced NS on R3 with smooth solenoidal data having the
finite Sobolev norms used below, or smooth periodic NS on T3. Viscosity
nu is positive. Every coefficient and remaining reserve is fixed from
the full original datum and a prescribed horizon H.

The heat-flow/remainder decomposition is classical. For its use with
nonlinear smallness conditions and large data, see
[Chemin--Gallagher, Wellposedness and stability results (2009)](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0611044).
Here it identifies a paid part of the physical history and an explicit
unpaid critical cost. No nonlinear smallness assumption or global
existence conclusion from that paper is imported without its hypotheses.

### The actual generated component

Let P be the Leray projection, A=-Delta, and N(v)=-P[(v.grad)v]. Define

```text
h(t)=exp(nu t Delta)u0, b(t)=u(t)-h(t), b(0)=0,
L_h b=-P[(h.grad)b+(b.grad)h],
b_t=-nu A b+N(b)+L_h b+N(h).                         (247)
```

This is the actual residual of the full NS solution, not an independent
forced fluid. Its source and coefficients all come from the SAME original
heat path. In particular they are not arbitrary controls. Pressure and
all newly generated modes remain in (247). The heat path exists for the
whole prescribed horizon even when only a shorter NS prefix is available.

Put Y=||grad b||2^2, D_b=||Delta b||2^2 and E_b=||b||2^2. Since Ab is
solenoidal, pressure gradients cancel in the integrated pairing, giving

```text
Y'+2nu D_b=2g(b)+2M(h,b)+2<Ab,N(h)>,
M(h,b)=<Ab,L_h b>.                                  (248)
```

Writing partial_i b_j=b_(j,i), integration by parts gives the complete
mixed term (all repeated indices summed and all terms integrated):

```text
M=-integral [b_(j,i) h_(k,i) b_(j,k)
            +b_(j,i) b_(k,i) h_(j,k)
            +b_(j,i) b_k h_(j,ki)].
```

The last term is the changing strain of the original heat parent. It
cannot be removed by transport cancellation. Define G(t)=||grad h||infinity
and L(t)=||grad^2 h||infinity, using pointwise Frobenius tensor norms.
Then |M|<=2G Y+L sqrt(E_b Y). For any fixed length ell>0,
2sqrt(E_b Y)<=ell Y+E_b/ell. Also
2<Ab,N(h)><=(nu/2)D_b+(2/nu)||N(h)||2^2.
Consequently

```text
Y'+(3nu/2)D_b
 <=2g(b)+(4G+ell L)Y+(L/ell)E_b+(2/nu)||N(h)||2^2.    (249)
```

These estimates do not assume the residual's size, alignment, scale
support, or sign of stretching. They retain all mixed work rather than
inferring its sign from the direction of energy exchange.

### A finite original-data price for the original parents

Write E0=||u0||2^2. Unforced kinetic-energy dissipation and heat contraction
give E_b<=2||u||2^2+2||h||2^2<=4E0. There is a sharper source-funded
bound. Pairing (247) with b cancels its self-advection and transport by h:

```text
(1/2)E_b'+nu Y=-<b,(b.grad)h>+<b,N(h)>.
```

Consequently ||b(t)||2<=M_h(t), where

```text
M_h(t)=integral_0^t exp[integral_s^t G(r)dr]||N(h(s))||2 ds.
```

The norm inequality follows by regularizing sqrt(E_b), using b(0)=0,
applying the integrating factor and letting the regularization vanish.
The entire comparison path is determined by u0. In particular, if the
original heat source N(h) vanishes, then b=0 throughout every prefix.
Put Ehat(t)=min(4E0,M_h(t)^2), so E_b<=Ehat.

Heat contraction also gives G(t)<=G0=||grad u0||infinity and
L(t)<=L0=||grad^2 u0||infinity. Fix ell once, and set
kappa0=4G0+ell L0. Define FROM THE ORIGINAL DATUM

```text
a_H(t)=exp[kappa0(H-t)]>=1,
f0(t)=Ehat(t)L(t)/ell+(2/nu)||N(h(t))||2^2,
R_H(t)=integral_t^H a_H(s)f0(s)ds>=0,
J_H(t)=a_H(t)Y(t)+R_H(t)>=0.
```

Multiplying (249) by a_H and using a_H'=-kappa0 a_H gives

```text
J_H'+(3nu/2)a_H D_b<=2a_H g(b),
J_H(t)+(3nu/2)integral_0^t a_H D_b
       <=R_H(0)+2integral_0^t a_H g(b).              (250)
```

The original-heat source is paid by precisely the capacity in (245):
nu^-1 integral_0^H ||N(h)||2^2<=Ctilde_nu(u0). Thus the price is finite
and admits the entirely initial-data upper bound

```text
R_H(0)<=exp(kappa0 H)[4E0 H L0/ell+2Ctilde_nu(u0)]
       <=exp(kappa0 H)[4E0 H L0/ell+U0^2 E0/nu^2],   (251)
U0=||u0||infinity.
```

More sharply, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
M_h(t)^2<=t exp(2G0 H)nu Ctilde_nu(u0). Thus the SAME allowance obeys

```text
R_H(0)<=exp(kappa0 H)
       [2+nu L0 H^2 exp(2G0 H)/(2ell)]Ctilde_nu(u0).
```

The allowance is therefore entirely source-funded, and vanishes when
the original heat source does. It does not charge a nonzero curvature
price to a residual that is identically zero.

For the second inequality in (251), Leray is an L2 contraction and
||N(h)||2<=||h||infinity||grad h||2<=U0||grad h||2.
The heat energy identity bounds integral_0^infinity ||grad h||2^2
by E0/(2nu), on either domain. A periodic constant mean causes no
problem: only the decaying part contributes to this dissipation.
For the admissible whole-space smooth fields with all derivatives in
L2, the initial supremum norms above are finite by Sobolev embedding.
The bound may be very large. Its finiteness uses no future solution norm.

On adjacent actual intervals, h keeps the same age, a_H keeps the same
horizon, and R_H keeps the same remaining integral. Equation (250)
telescopes at a shared physical endpoint. Matching a pattern label and
replacing h by the new fluid state would not preserve this reserve.

### The exact sufficient history estimate still missing

The outstanding claim is now a bound, fixed from u0, nu and H, on

```text
2 integral_0^t a_H(s)g(b(s))ds
  <=nu integral_0^t a_H(s)D_b(s)ds+K(u0,nu,H)         (252)
```

for EVERY available smooth unforced prefix from that datum and every
t in that prefix with t<=H. This is a signed history estimate, not
an asserted pointwise depletion law. The remainder is zero initially,
but its parents and source continue to evolve by (247).

If (252) holds, (250) yields Y(t)<=R_H(0)+K. Since u=h+b,

```text
||grad u(t)||2^2<=2||grad u0||2^2+2R_H(0)+2K.
```

This has exactly the uniform-prefix quantifiers required by the existing
whole-space Lean theorem
`WholeSpaceViscousFlow.hasNSEvolution_of_orderOne_bound` in
`MettapediaNS.WholeSpaceEnstrophyContinuation`. The physical identification
and estimates (247)--(252) are analytic, not an additional certified
instance of that theorem. The same analytic enstrophy bound is sufficient
for smooth periodic continuation. Neither domain is closed here.

All work involving the ORIGINAL heat parent has a finite price in
(250). The self-interaction of the GENERATED remainder has not been paid.
Describing that remainder as externally forced would lose the essential
constraint that its source and coefficients come from the original heat
history. Conversely, the constraint alone does not establish (252).

### The generated remainder can have either sign of self-stretching

For any smooth datum, the actual short-time expansion of (247) is
b(t)=t N(u0)+O(t^2) in sufficiently strong Sobolev norms. Hence

```text
g(b(t))=t^3 g(N(u0))+O(t^4).                         (253)
```

The coefficient is independent of positive viscosity: the same heat
term cancels from u_t(0)-h_t(0). The seed r of (243) gives the exact
negative value g(N(r))=-75009477/773500000. In contrast, set

```text
v(x)=(1/10) sum_(k,p) p cos(k.x),
(k,p)=((1,0,1),(3,1,-3)), ((1,-1,1),(-1,-3,-2)),
      ((2,0,1),(-2,9,4)), ((2,-1,1),(3,9,3)).
```

Every polarization is transverse, E(v)=233/200, and

```text
g(N(v))=706789431/24752000000>0.
```

Both examples are genuine smooth periodic initial data. Local existence
and (253) give actual positive-viscosity histories with the respective
strict signs on sufficiently short positive intervals. These are signs
of the GENERATED remainder, not signs inferred from an arbitrary later
Fourier state. The full source includes its generated vertical mean.

The positive value rejects automatic depletion g(b)<=0. It does not
refute (252): initially D_b is order t^2 whereas g(b) is order t^3, and
a full-datum allowance can pay finite bursts. No indefinite renewal or
positive-viscosity singularity follows from this fixture.

### Verification

Run `python3 -O labs/heat_remainder_payment.py`. Exact rational checks
verify the full remainder direction, all three integrated mixed terms,
the exact kinetic remainder cancellation, the source/diffusion estimate,
and the complete relative enstrophy identity for two nonzero viscosities
and both remainder phases. The
cubic source coefficients are computed independently via vorticity
stretching and the Laplacian/Leray pairing. Generated means are retained.
The off-trajectory identity fixtures verify algebra applicable to every
smooth state; only the analytic expansion (253) identifies actual
solution intervals. The heat contraction, Sobolev estimates, integration
and continuation implication are analytic. No Lean declarations or axioms
change, and the central history estimate (252) remains open.

## A single original-heat reserve for all time

`heat_parent_lifetime.py` sharpens (250): the original heat parents have
one finite allowance for their ENTIRE lifetime. The weight and allowance
no longer grow with the prescribed horizon. This is a bound for the
original-parent and mixed terms, not payment of the generated remainder's
self-stretching. The setting and full-source definitions remain those of
(247): smooth unforced NS on R3 or the 2pi-periodic cube, nu>0, h the
original heat solution, b=u-h, and b(0)=0.

### The original parent has finite accumulated strain

Choose nonnegative original-data envelopes Gbar,Lbar such that

```text
||grad h(t)||infinity<=Gbar(t),
||grad^2 h(t)||infinity<=Lbar(t),
Gamma(t)=integral_t^infinity Gbar(s)ds<infinity,
Lambda(t)=integral_t^infinity Lbar(s)ds<infinity.     (254)
```

These are available without knowing any future NS solution. On the torus,
write u_k for the normalized Fourier coefficients of u0. One choice is

```text
Gbar(t)=sum_(k!=0) |k| |u_k| exp(-nu t |k|^2),
Lbar(t)=sum_(k!=0) |k|^2 |u_k| exp(-nu t |k|^2),
Gamma(t)=nu^-1 sum_(k!=0) |u_k| exp(-nu t |k|^2)/|k|,
Lambda(t)=nu^-1 sum_(k!=0) |u_k| exp(-nu t |k|^2).
```

Vector and frequency norms here are Euclidean; pointwise derivative norms
are Frobenius. Smoothness makes every displayed sum finite. On R3 use
(2pi)^-3 times the corresponding integrals of |u0_hat(k)|. At zero
frequency the Gamma integral is finite by Cauchy--Schwarz, since
integral_(|k|<1) |k|^-2 dk is finite in three dimensions. At high frequency,
H2 regularity suffices for the two tail integrals; the stronger smooth
hypotheses also make the pointwise envelopes finite at t=0.
Thus neither a spectral gap nor a positive minimum whole-space frequency
has been assumed. The periodic constant mean contributes to neither
parent derivative envelope.

Let n(t)=N(h(t)), B(t)=Ctilde_nu(h(t)) as in (245), and define

```text
S0=integral_0^infinity ||n(s)||2 ds<infinity,
E_star=min(4E0, exp(2Gamma(0)) S0^2).                (255)
```

S0 is also finite from the original datum. On R3, for any fixed tau>0,
heat contraction and the Gaussian kernel give

```text
S0<=tau U0 sqrt(Z0)+4c3 E0 nu^(-5/4) tau^(-1/4),
c3=(8pi)^(-3/4)(2e)^(-1/2),
U0=||u0||infinity, Z0=||grad u0||2^2.
```

Indeed ||N(h)||2<=||h||infinity||grad h||2. Before tau use the initial
norms; after tau use ||h||infinity<=(8pi nu t)^(-3/4)sqrt(E0) and
||grad h||2<=(2e nu t)^(-1/2)sqrt(E0). The latter follows by maximizing
r exp(-nu t r^2). The resulting t^(-5/4) is integrable at infinity.
On the normalized torus, with mean mu and
F0=sum_(k!=0)|u_k|, one may instead use
S0<=sqrt(Z0)(|mu|+F0/2)/nu. This follows from the separate exponential
decay of the nonconstant velocity and its gradient.

The kinetic comparison preceding (250) now gives E_b(t)<=E_star on every
available prefix. This uses the whole original heat history; S0 is not
an integral over an unknown future nonlinear solution.
Using the larger 4E0 in place of E_star is also valid, but loses the
zero-source normalization of the sharper allowance.

### An explicit remaining reserve

Fix ell>0 once. Define

```text
kappa(t)=4Gbar(t)+ell Lbar(t),
a(t)=exp[4Gamma(t)+ell Lambda(t)]>=1,
F(t)=E_star Lambda(t)/ell+2B(t)>=0,
f(t)=E_star Lbar(t)/ell+2||n(t)||2^2/nu,
J(t)=a(t)[Y(t)+F(t)], Y=||grad b||2^2.              (256)
```

Here a'=-kappa a and F'=-f. Substituting (249) and E_b<=E_star gives

```text
J'+(3nu/2)a D_b <= 2a g(b)-kappa a F,
J(t)+(3nu/2)integral_0^t a D_b
       +integral_0^t kappa a F
 <= J(0)+2integral_0^t a g(b),                     (257)
J(0)=exp[4Gamma(0)+ell Lambda(0)]
       [E_star Lambda(0)/ell+2Ctilde_nu(u0)]<infinity.
```

The extra -kappa a F is the cooling of still-unspent credit. Dropping it
is allowed in an upper bound; changing the weight while forgetting its
derivative is not. Every object on the right of the formula for J(0)
is determined by u0 and nu. There is no prescribed horizon in that price.
Moreover a(t) tends to1 and F(t) tends to0 as t tends to infinity.
If N(h) is identically zero, S0=B=E_star=F=0, and the kinetic comparison
gives b=0; nonzero original strain alone does not create a charge.

The same a,F and original heat age persist across adjacent actual solution
segments. The storage difference telescopes, and the three time integrals
in (257) add. The equation for b still contains N(b), both mixed terms,
and the original source n; it has not become an arbitrary forced fluid.

For every prescribed H, a bound

```text
2 integral_0^t a g(b)<=nu integral_0^t a D_b+K(u0,nu,H)
```

on every available prefix with t<=H implies Y(t)<=J(0)+K. This supplies
the same gradient-energy continuation target as (252), now with the
horizon-independent original-parent allowance J(0). The required bound
on generated self-stretching is STILL OPEN. Finiteness of S0 and J(0)
does not imply it: finite forcing costs alone do not establish arbitrary
three-dimensional regularity.

### A delayed source, zero at the initial instant

The whole original heat history is essential even in a globally smooth
triangular example. On the normalized periodic cube, take arbitrary real
amplitudes A,B and

```text
u0=(A sin y, -A sin x, B[(cos x+cos y)^2-1]).        (258)
```

The vertical component is constant along the initial horizontal
streamlines. The horizontal nonlinearity is a pressure gradient, so
N(u0)=0 exactly. Nevertheless, write q=exp(-nu t). The two horizontal
components of h have heat rate1, while its vertical component has rates2
and4. Direct calculation gives

```text
n(t)=(0,0,2AB q^3(q^2-1) sin x sin y(cos x-cos y)),
||n(t)||2^2=(A^2 B^2/2)q^6(1-q^2)^2,
B(t)=A^2 B^2/(2nu^2)[q^6/6-q^8/4+q^10/10],
Ctilde_nu(u0)=A^2 B^2/(120nu^2),
S0=sqrt(2)|AB|/(15nu).                            (259)
```

For AB!=0, the later source and total source capacity are strictly positive
although the initial source is zero. Thus a reserve that declared this
whole history free merely because N(u0)=0 would discard a real interaction.
The source is created by unequal viscous heat rates; it is not supplied by
an external forcing term.

In particular n'(0)=-4nu AB sin x sin y(cos x-cos y) in the vertical
component. Since b(0)=b_t(0)=0, the actual equation gives b_tt(0)=n'(0).
Thus the generated remainder starts at second order in physical time,
even though the initial projected nonlinearity vanishes.

The ACTUAL NS solution has horizontal velocity
v_H(t)=Aq(sin y,-sin x), pressure -A^2 q^2 cos x cos y, and a vertical
component theta solving

```text
theta_t+v_H.grad theta=nu Delta theta,
theta(0)=B[(cos x+cos y)^2-1].
```

This smooth linear advection--diffusion problem gives the solution for
all time; no smallness restriction on A or B is required. Its usual
backward stochastic representation gives the actual vertical remainder:

```text
dX_s=-v_H(t-s,X_s)ds+sqrt(2nu)dW_s, X_0=x,
b_z(t,x)=E[integral_0^t n_z(t-s,X_s)ds].
```

No auxiliary fluid force or freely chosen drift is used here. The
remainder b is vertical and independent of z, so
N(b)=g(b)=0 throughout the ACTUAL history. Its horizontal parent stays
independent of theta, while theta may change shape and develop gradients.

In this class the mixed estimate is sharper: only the horizontal strain
acts on grad b. Its symmetric operator norm is at most |A|q. Thus set

```text
a_tri(t)=exp(2|A|q/nu),
J_tri(t)=a_tri(t)[Y(t)+2B(t)].
```

The same Young estimate for the source pairing gives

```text
J_tri'+(3nu/2)a_tri D_b <= -4|A|q a_tri B(t)<=0,
Y(t)<=(A^2 B^2/(60nu^2))exp(2|A|/nu)               (260)
```

for the entire actual history. The kinetic comparison additionally gives
||b(t)||2^2<=2A^2 B^2/(225nu^2). This is a concrete all-time consumer of
the original-source reserve, not a new general regularity class. It uses
the same autonomous-horizontal-parent structure as the earlier mixing
examples. Allowing the generated components to feed back into that
parent, and paying their subsequent self-stretching, remains the central
obligation for arbitrary three-dimensional data.

### Normalized trial and verification

The next tested storage replaces Y in (256) by the already defined
normalized W_8(b). Its COMPLETE payment defect, divided by a, is

```text
Q_trial=DW_8(b)[-nu Ab+N(b)+L_h b+n]
        +2g(b)-(nu/2)D_b-kappa[W_8(b)+F]-f.         (261)
```

A universal nonpositive sign along actual prefixes would imply the needed
history bound with K=J_trial(0). The next section refutes that universal
sign for each fixed ell, using an actual oscillatory-parent release.
Every derivative of the normalization and both mixed interactions is
retained. This failure does not refute the integrated history bound.

For the ENTIRE actual triangular class (258), the remainder has zero
self-source at every auxiliary heat age, so H_nu(b)=Ctilde_nu(b)=0 and
W_8(b)=Y/2, including its continuous value at zero. Equation (249) then
gives Q_trial<=-(5nu/4)D_b-f/2-kappa F<=0 for all time. Thus this trial
does have an actual-history consumer at arbitrary amplitudes. The same
pointwise rule does not cover all mutually interacting parents.

Run `python3 -O labs/heat_parent_lifetime.py`. Exact checks verify the
parent-tail derivatives, original-source spending, full coupled remainder
estimate including the -kappa a F term, and the complete normalized-trial
derivative on two finite states, using the valid 4E0 kinetic envelope.
Independent polynomial polarization checks the three observer derivatives.
The checks also verify (259) at three heat ages and its initial derivative
by independent polarization of the full nonlinearity,
for two parameter choices, retaining every Fourier output and pressure
projection. A nonconstant planar heat solution checks that an identically
zero heat source gives zero source-funded allowance. The actual-history,
heat-integrability, stochastic and all-time estimates are analytic, not
Lean-certified by these finite checks. No Lean declarations or axioms change.

## An oscillatory parent releases a self-stretching descendant

The universal pointwise sign proposed in (261) fails on an actual smooth
unforced periodic history, for each fixed ell>0. Rapid oscillations in
an initially horizontal velocity generate a slower three-dimensional
field, which survives after the original heat parents decay. An
initial-layer estimate and local stability identify the actual descendant;
its complete normalized-storage defect is positive. The PDE argument is
analytic, with exact algebra in `oscillatory_parent_release.py`, not
newly Lean-certified.

This rejects the pointwise sign, NOT the integrated allowance in (257),
even with its original large reserve. It gives a finite smooth release
and a short later interval, not indefinite renewal or a singularity.

High-frequency interactions producing a low-frequency response, with the
actual nonlinear error retained, are classical tools; see
[Bourgain--Pavlovic, *Ill-posedness of the Navier--Stokes equations in a
critical space in 3D*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.0882), especially its
heat/first-response/remainder decomposition. Their norm-inflation theorem
does not identify the particular descendant below. The layer and error
estimate here supply that separate identification.

### Data, pressure and the complete layer

Use the normalized torus of period 2pi. Let V be a smooth horizontal,
divergence-free trigonometric polynomial: V_3=0, with x_3 dependence
allowed. For any fixed nu>0 and finite real epsilon, set

```text
B=(V.grad)V, w=N(V)=-P B,
u_N(0,x)=epsilon N cos(Nx_3)V(x),
tau=N^2 t, theta=Nx_3, delta=1/N.                 (262)
```

The carrier N is a sufficiently large integer. Each datum is exactly
divergence-free, smooth and finite energy. No smallness of epsilon is
assumed; the required N can depend strongly on epsilon, nu and V.
All Fourier outputs are retained.

On T3_x times T_theta define

```text
D_N=(delta partial_1,delta partial_2,
                    delta partial_3+partial_theta),
P_N(k,l)=P(k+Nl e_3),
U_tau=nu D_N^2 U-P_N[(U.D_N)U],
U(0,x,theta)=epsilon cos(theta)V(x).              (263)
```

At zero physical frequency take the identity projector. P_N is an
orthogonal Fourier multiplier, commutes with derivatives, is uniformly
bounded on every H^m(T4), and projects onto D_N-solenoidal fields.
The pullback u_N(t,x)=N U(N^2 t,x,Nx_3) solves the ACTUAL unforced 3D
NS equation: physical derivatives become N D_N. The pressure projection
commutes with pullback, since indices with equal k+Nl e_3 have the same
projector. The extra coordinate separates phase; it is not an extra
physical fluid dimension or an auxiliary force.

The exact lifted original heat field is
H_N=exp(nu tau D_N^2)[epsilon cos(theta)V]. Its leading profile is
H_0=epsilon exp(-nu tau)cos(theta)V. The limiting projector P_infinity
is P(k) on l=0 and diag(1,1,0) on l!=0. In particular the slow pressure
can create vertical velocity from a horizontal source.

With q=exp(-nu tau) and T=(w_3 V_1,w_3 V_2,0), the complete first layer is

```text
R=m w+c2 cos(2theta)B+c1 sin(theta)T,
m=epsilon^2(1-q^2)/(4nu),
c2=-epsilon^2(q^2-q^4)/(4nu),
c1=epsilon^3 q[tau-(1-q^2)/(2nu)]/(4nu).          (264)
```

Its three components start at zero and solve

```text
R_tau=nu partial_theta^2 R
      -P_infinity[H_0.grad_x H_0+R_3 partial_theta H_0],
R_3=m w_3,
m'=epsilon^2 q^2/2,
c2'+4nu c2=-epsilon^2 q^2/2,
c1'+nu c1=epsilon q m.                            (265)
```

The last channel is essential: the generated vertical motion advects
the original fast phase. A first Duhamel response alone omits this
order-one physical correction. It decays like a polynomial times
exp(-nu tau), leaving b_*=epsilon^2 w/(4nu). Thus this layer includes
feedback into the original carrier, beyond the triangular class (258).

### Uniform control of the actual initial layer

Fix an integer m>=6. All norms here are on T4. Constants depend on
m,V,epsilon,nu, but not N. For l!=0, elementary projection geometry gives

```text
|P_N(k,l)-P_infinity(k,l)| <= C min(1,|k|/N).
```

For |k|<N|l|/2 use the angle with e_3; outside that region use boundedness
of both projectors. On l=0 they coincide. Their difference therefore maps
H^(m+1) to H^m with norm at most C/N, including modes of zero physical
frequency. R is P_infinity-solenoidal; only its decaying oscillatory part
contributes to P_N R-R. The finite Fourier support of V also gives

```text
||H_N||_(H^(m+2)) <= C exp(-nu tau/2),
||H_N-H_0||_(H^(m+2)) <= C delta tau exp(-nu tau/2)
```

for sufficiently large N, by the exact rates |l e_3+delta k|^2, l=+-1.
Use the exactly solenoidal approximation

```text
U_app=H_N+delta P_N R,
Res=partial_tau U_app-nu D_N^2 U_app
                     +P_N[(U_app.D_N)U_app].
```

Equation (265) cancels every term of order delta. H_N has zero third
component, so its self-interaction is delta H_N.grad_x H_N. The other
leading term is delta(P_N R)_3 partial_theta H_N. Their limit is exactly
the source F_0 in (265). Moreover P_N P_infinity F_0=P_N F_0: its
oscillatory coefficients are horizontal and its mean uses the same
pressure projection. The remaining terms are:

- the differences H_N-H_0 and P_N R-R in these two sources;
- nu delta P_N(2delta partial_3 partial_theta+delta^2 Delta_x)R;
- the two slow mixed derivatives, each with coefficient delta^2;
- delta^2 P_N[(P_N R)_3 partial_theta(P_N R)] and
  delta^3 P_N[(P_N R).grad_x(P_N R)].

Every order-delta^2 term decays integrably. Only order delta^3 can persist,
through slow derivatives of the mean. For a fixed polynomial p,

```text
||U_app||_(H^(m+1)) <= C(exp(-nu tau/2)+delta),
||Res||_(H^m) <= C delta^2 p(tau)exp(-nu tau/2)+C delta^3.
                                                               (266)
```

The Sobolev energy argument for (263) is uniform in N. Its transport
vector on T4 is (delta U_1,delta U_2,delta U_3,U_3), with zero ordinary
divergence; its norms are bounded by those of U. P_N is self-adjoint
and commutes with derivatives. Galerkin approximation, transport
cancellation and the H^m product/commutator estimates give local
solutions and continuation while the H^m norm is bounded. No inverse
ellipticity constant is used for the degenerate operator D_N^2.

For E=U-U_app, both fields are D_N-solenoidal and E(0)=0. The same
energy estimates give, using an upper derivative when the norm is zero,

```text
d||E||_(H^m)/d tau
 <= C[||U_app||_(H^(m+1))+||E||_(H^m)]||E||_(H^m)
       +||Res||_(H^m).
```

Set tau_N=4 log(N)/nu. The integrated approximation coefficient is
bounded independently of N and the integrated residual is at most C/N^2.
A bootstrap of the quadratic term gives

```text
sup_(0<=tau<=tau_N)||U-U_app||_(H^m) <= C/N^2.     (267)
```

All constants are fixed before choosing N and involve no unknown future
solution norm. This estimate also continues U through tau_N. Higher
regularity propagates by the tame energy estimates, giving a smooth
physical pullback.

The embedding H^m(T4) into continuous functions controls values on the
diagonal without derivative loss. For t_N=tau_N/N^2, the formulas give

```text
||u_N(t_N)-b_*||_infinity <= C/N.                  (268)
```

Indeed N H_N tends to zero, both oscillatory channels of R decay, its
mean tends to b_*, and N E=O(1/N). This asserts uniform convergence of
velocities, NOT their physical derivatives at t_N: differentiation of
the diagonal would introduce powers of N.

For the stronger convergence used below, let v(s) be the ordinary smooth
local NS solution from b_*. All velocities at t_N are uniformly bounded.
The periodic mild formulation has
||exp(nu s Delta)P div||_(L-infinity to L-infinity)<=C_nu s^(-1/2)
on a fixed bounded interval. Contraction and local stability therefore
give a common positive interval [0,s_0] on which
u_N(t_N+s)->v(s) uniformly. Away from s=0, parabolic smoothing gives
convergence in every fixed C^j norm. Only local existence at b_* is
used, not its global regularity.

### A reachable descendant with strictly positive defect

Choose

```text
k1=(1,0,1), k2=(1,-1,1), k3=(2,0,1), k4=(2,-1,1),
(c1,c2,c3,c4)=(-2,2,-2,3),
V=sum_j c_j (-(k_j)_2,(k_j)_1,0) cos(k_j.x).
```

This V depends on all three coordinates, with ||V||2^2=73/2. Its full
source w=N(V) has a nonzero vertical component and nonzero w_3 V. Exact
calculation gives

```text
Z(w)=443, D(w)=4767, g(w)=14040/119>0,
H_1(w)=13403/1785,
Ctilde_1(w)=4759369226919706030857271/8265219767113767658200.
```

Set nu=1, epsilon=12, hence b_*=36w. Retaining all weight, forecast and
capacity derivatives, the checker verifies the rational inequality

```text
Q_free(b_*)=DW_8(b_*)[-A b_*+N(b_*)]
                +2g(b_*)-D(b_*)/2 > 7,000,000 > D(b_*).
                                                               (269)
```

Its decimal value is approximately 7,136,339.346; the proof uses the
strict rational margin. By smooth local continuity Q_free(v(s)) stays
positive on some interval starting at zero. Fix s>0 in that interval.

The ORIGINAL heat field h_N and all fixed spatial derivatives at t_N+s
decay exponentially in N^2 s, with polynomial prefactors in N. The
Fourier envelopes in (254) do too. Since E_star<=4E0 and
E0=73 epsilon^2 N^2/4, the same holds for F,f,kappa, while a tends to1.
No heat age or reserve is reset. Strong convergence after (268) gives
b_N=u_N-h_N->v(s), including its full physical tangent and all
derivatives needed for W_8. The heat functionals and their derivatives
are continuous in sufficiently high Sobolev norms on this mean-zero
periodic class, and Z+8C remains positive. Consequently

```text
Q_trial[b_N,h_N](t_N+s) -> Q_free[v](s)>0.
```

For every fixed ell>0, (261) fails for sufficiently large finite N on
a nonempty interval of a genuine smooth unforced solution. The argument
does not certify a particular small N, or refute an existential choice
of ell depending on the datum and hence on N. It rejects the universal
sign at each fixed choice, for example ell=1.

Each datum has one finite reserve, although its energy grows like N^2
across the family. All effective forcing is internal. The argument does
not show that the accumulated cost exceeds the initial reserve. It
shows that cooling the original-parent allowance and retaining only
W_8 of the descendant loses the local payment property. The reserve
must follow what the parents created, as well as their own decay.

### Verification and remaining physical obligation

Run `python3 -O labs/oscillatory_parent_release.py`. It checks complete
carrier sources, low difference and high sum outputs, divergence and
energy; all three profile coefficient equations; the nonzero vertical
feedback; lifted pressure projections; the descendant's kinetic and
enstrophy identities; and the full normalized derivative, including
the changing weight. Exact checks at alpha=1,16,32,36 distinguish the
negative and positive state defects.

The estimates (266)--(268), local stability and actual failure interval
remain ANALYTIC. Python does not certify them. No new Lean declarations
or axioms are introduced, and no whole-space localization is asserted.

The open task remains the full-original-datum payment of generated
self-stretching in (257). A transferred resource must follow generated
parents after their original suppliers decay, without being replenished
when histories compose. The explicit release map
V -> epsilon^2 N(V)/(4nu), retaining pressure and the return channel,
provides a controlled physical test of such a rule.

## Descendant capacity renewal and a fixed-band force payment

Keeping the full source capacity of a generated descendant repairs the
sign at some states, but does not give a universal decreasing reserve.
The actual release mechanism (262)--(268) produces descendants whose
enstrophy and full source capacity BOTH increase after viscosity is
included. One input phase reversal changes both signs while preserving
every initial modal energy. Exact algebra is in
`descendant_capacity_transfer.py`; the actual-history interpretation
uses the analytic release theorem above.

There is also an unconditional payment for a specific part of the
effective forcing: high-frequency parents feeding a fixed lower band.
It reuses kinetic-energy dissipation and Fourier Cauchy--Schwarz, and
applies to every available smooth unforced prefix without a perturbative
assumption. Its loss when the observed band moves to finer scales is
explicit. This payment and the capacity obstruction concern different
observations; neither is the missing arbitrary-data continuation bound.

### The proposed transfer and an actual sign reversal

The tested repair retains the generated capacity without normalizing it:

```text
J_(beta,sigma)=a[W_beta(b)+sigma Ctilde_nu(b)+F],
beta>=8, sigma>=0,
Q_(beta,sigma)=DW_beta(b)[b_t]+2g(b)-(nu/2)D_b
             -kappa[W_beta(b)+F]-f
             +sigma[DCtilde_nu(b)[b_t]-kappa Ctilde_nu(b)].    (270)
```

Here b=u-h starts at zero, h is the ORIGINAL heat field, and a,F,kappa,f
remain those of (254)--(256). Parameters beta and sigma are constant
along a history; changing them would introduce additional derivatives.
The initial value is still a(0)F(0), without new credit at a later release.
Sigma=1 is the full-capacity repair, while sigma=0 includes the previous
normalized trial.

Keep the four waves from (262), but take two horizontal envelopes

```text
V_g: coefficients (3,1,3,-3),
V_d: coefficients (3,1,3, 3),
V=sum_j c_j (-(k_j)_2,(k_j)_1,0) cos(k_j.x),
w_g=N(V_g), w_d=N(V_d).                            (271)
```

Only the fourth wave changes phase by pi. Both envelopes have energy 46
and identical modal energies at every wavevector. Consequently their
original heat trajectories have identical quadratic Fourier energy
curves, including every homogeneous Sobolev energy. The same is true
of the modulated initial data epsilon N cos(Nx_3)V for large N. Their
pointwise geometry and nonlinear source capacities need not agree.

The exact generated quantities at nu=1 are:

| Observation | Growing phase w_g | Depleting phase w_d |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Z | 846 | 657 |
| D | 10620 | 7623 |
| g | 1755/28 | -585/476 |
| Ctilde_1 | 827.76864... | 1168.77554... |
| DCtilde_1(w)[N(w)] | 1976.97835... | -3791.94282... |

The signs use exact rational arithmetic, not the displayed decimals.
Set epsilon=32, so the released fields are b_g=256w_g and b_d=256w_d.
Along the FULL unforced tangent -Ab+N(b), exact calculation gives

```text
at b_g:
 Z'=4978114560/7>0,
 C'=DCtilde_1(b_g)[-Ab_g+N(b_g)]>2*10^15,
 Q_free,8=DW_8(b_g)[-Ab_g+N(b_g)]+2g(b_g)-D_b/2>2*10^9;
at b_d:
 g(b_d)<0, Z'<0, C'<0.                            (272)
```

Thus viscosity has already been subtracted in both comparisons. This
is stronger than a sign computation for the Euler part alone. The
analytic release and subsequent local smoothing give two actual
unforced histories on which these strict signs persist after the
original heat parents are arbitrarily small. They are short smooth
intervals, not assertions of persistent growth or singularity.

### A whole family of pointwise repairs fails

The growing phase defeats every constant beta>=8 and sigma>=0, not just
the choices in (272). For any physical tangent write Z,H,C for the full
enstrophy, signed heat forecast and full source capacity, with their
complete derivatives Z',H',C'. Put r=2g-(nu/2)D. Direct differentiation gives

```text
(Z+beta C)^2[W_beta'+r]=A0+beta A1+beta^2 A2,
A0=Z^2(Z'/2+H'+C'+r),
A1=C Z'(Z+H+C)+Z C H'-Z H C'+2r Z C,
A2=C^2(Z'/2+r).                                   (273)
```

Every coefficient A0,A1,A2 is strictly positive at b_g. The checker
computes them exactly, including the negative term -Z H C' and every
changing-weight contribution. Hence the free defect is positive for
all beta>=8. The complete capacity derivative C' is positive too.

To retain the original parent cooling in an ACTUAL history, replace
the three rates in (273) by Z'-kappa Z, H'-kappa H, C'-kappa C,
and r by r-kappa F-f. This is exact because W_beta is homogeneous of
degree one under simultaneous scaling of Z,H,C. After release these
three coefficients converge to their strictly positive values at a
small positive time in the evolution from b_g. Also C'-kappa C stays
positive. For each fixed ell>0, sufficiently large finite N therefore
gives a single actual smooth interval on which

```text
Q_(beta,sigma)>0 for ALL constant beta>=8 and sigma>=0.
```

The interval can be chosen simultaneously for all these parameters:
strict positivity of the three numerator coefficients and C'-kappa C
is an open condition involving finitely many continuous observations.
Thus selecting beta or sigma from the initial datum does not repair
this family if they remain constant during the history. The assertion
does not rule out a datum-dependent ell, evolving parameters with their
full derivative costs, a different history reserve, or an integrated
allowance that tolerates finite positive defects.

At this descendant the source capacity is a growing forecast of its
own future heat-source work. It is not a conserved stock left over from
the original parents. A nonnegative function can grow as the geometry
changes; nonnegativity alone does not make it a payable reserve.

### A positive bound for high parents feeding a fixed output band

Let u be ANY smooth unforced incompressible NS prefix, nu>0, and fix
M,Lambda>0. Let Q_(>=Lambda) be the orthogonal Fourier projection on
frequencies of magnitude at least Lambda and P_(<=M) the low-output
projection. Include the complete Leray pressure projection in

```text
v=Q_(>=Lambda)u,
F_(M,Lambda)=P_(<=M)N(v), q_(M,Lambda)=||F_(M,Lambda)||2,
E=||u||2^2, Z=||grad u||2^2.
```

On the normalized torus put K_M^2=sum_(0<|k|<=M)|k|^2. The convolution
formula, the norm-one Leray projection and Cauchy--Schwarz give

```text
|N(v)_k|<=|k| sum_p |v_p| |v_(k-p)|<=|k| ||v||2^2,
q_(M,Lambda)<=K_M ||v||2^2<=K_M Z/Lambda^2.         (274)
```

No sharp Fourier projection is asserted bounded on L-infinity. The
input projection is used only in L2 and its gradient energy. All high
input pairs, their phases and their pressure contributions remain.
The zero output vanishes by divergence form. For example K_5^2=7650.

On R3, use the unitary Fourier transform. The convolution factor is
(2pi)^(-3/2), and integration over the output ball gives the same bound
with K_M=M^(5/2)/(sqrt(10)pi). Indeed
(2pi)^(-3) integral_(|k|<=M)|k|^2 dk=M^5/(10pi^2).
There is no whole-space minimum-frequency assumption.

The actual kinetic identity E'=-2nu Z now supplies the nonnegative
reserve and every compatible interval payment

```text
R_(M,Lambda)(t)=K_M E(t)/(2nu Lambda^2),
R_(M,Lambda)' + q_(M,Lambda)<=0,
R_(M,Lambda)(b)+integral_a^b q_(M,Lambda)
                         <=R_(M,Lambda)(a).        (275)
```

The initial price is finite, depends only on the original kinetic
energy, viscosity and the fixed observation cutoffs, and is independent
of the horizon. Parents may be regenerated and exchange energy with
the remaining fluid; (275) still holds because it uses their current
contribution to the FULL dissipation. No renewal resets the energy.
Adjacent intervals use the same intermediate R, so the payments telescope.
Pairing the force with any compatible time-dependent L2 observer of norm
at most one is also absolutely paid by q. An observer of uncontrolled
norm would require its own bound.

This specializes the existing full-energy ledger. Its whole-space
kinetic identity is already Lean-certified as
`FullEnergyParentReserve.actual_kinetic_rate`; the Fourier identification
(274) and this particular reserve's application are analytic here.
No new generic ledger or assumed NS history is introduced.

The scaling matches the release example: its initial energy is
epsilon^2 N^2 ||V||2^2/2, while its parent frequencies are asymptotic
to N. Thus the fixed-band price stays of order epsilon^2/nu, consistent
with the finite released amplitude epsilon^2/(4nu). Growth after release
is a separate interaction among the slower descendants.

### The remaining scale and history cost

Bound (275) does not pay arbitrary vorticity stretching. It pays the
L2 size of one fixed-band force. If the observation follows finer
scales, write rho=K_M/Lambda^2. Whenever rho is differentiable,

```text
R=rho E/(2nu),
R'+q<=rho' E/(2nu).                              (276)
```

Positive jumps in rho cost E Delta rho/(2nu) as well. On R3, when M and
Lambda grow proportionally, rho grows like M^(1/2), rather than decaying.
The periodic lattice constants have the same large-scale order.
Neither energy nor the fixed-band payment controls this refining cost,
the receiver's growing derivative norms, or the remaining interactions.
These are reasons to retain geometry and complete histories, not to
interpret a bounded force impulse as a general regularity criterion.

### Direct payment inside the generated-stretching target

The force estimate also pays a named part of the OPEN budget (257).
Keep its actual b=u-h and original weight a. Define

```text
T_(M,Lambda)(b)=<P_(<=M)Ab,P_(<=M)N(Q_(>=Lambda)b)>,
g_rem(b)=g(b)-T_(M,Lambda)(b),
E_h=||h||2^2, Z_h=||grad h||2^2, E0=||u0||2^2.
```

Although b has effective forcing, the two actual fields u and h satisfy
E_u'=-2nu Z_u and E_h'=-2nu Z_h. Also
||b||2<=2sqrt(E0) and Z_b<=2(Z_u+Z_h). Therefore

```text
|T_(M,Lambda)|
 <=2M^2 sqrt(E0) K_M Z_b/Lambda^2
 <=4M^2 sqrt(E0) K_M (Z_u+Z_h)/Lambda^2,
R_paid=a(t) [2M^2 sqrt(E0) K_M/(nu Lambda^2)] (E_u+E_h),
R_paid'+a |T_(M,Lambda)|<=-kappa R_paid<=0,
R_paid(0)=4a(0)M^2 K_M E0^(3/2)/(nu Lambda^2).       (277)
```

Here the low-band observer was bounded by M^2||b||2; its derivative
cost was not silently discarded. All parameters and the initial a(0)
are fixed by the original datum, viscosity and chosen cutoffs. This is
an all-prefix physical bound, on either domain, not a reachability
assumption for arbitrary states or an energy identity falsely imposed
on the forced remainder. The energies of u AND its original heat
reference pay together. The same heat age persists at every seam.

Consequently it suffices to prove

```text
2 integral_0^t a g_rem <= nu integral_0^t a D_b + K_rem(u0,nu,H).
                                                               (278)
```

Then (257) follows with K=K_rem+2R_paid(0), and its gradient-energy
continuation consumer is unchanged. The residual g_rem retains all
other input pairs and output bands, including every interaction between
the released descendants. It has not been replaced by a closed system
of selected modes. At both released seeds (271), Q_(>=7)w=0, so
T_(5,7)=0 and g_rem=g: the adverse descendant remains wholly in the
unpaid core. On comparable moving cutoffs the prefactor
M^2 K_M/Lambda^2 grows like M^(5/2); this stronger observation still
needs a genuine scale/history mechanism.

The next physical task is to control renewal at the moving receiving
scale, after subtracting the work actually paid by (277).
The phase pair (271) and its full tangent are mandatory tests: matching
modal energies cannot identify the direction of later stretching, and
carrying a growing source forecast alone does not pay it.

Run `python3 -O labs/descendant_capacity_transfer.py`. The checker
verifies the matched spectra, both full physical descendant tangents,
the positive coefficient certificate for every beta, exact cooling of
the three observer slots, the full kinetic identity, three rational
fixed-band force bounds and the exact residual in (278). The analytic
release, all-prefix integral payment and whole-space Fourier estimate
are not Lean-certified by these checks. No Lean declarations or axioms change. The arbitrary-data
signed history estimate and global regularity remain open.

## Descendant source geometry and all-scale separated absorption

`descendant_geometry_separation.py` identifies the adverse renewal in
(271) using the COMPLETE source capacity, including the vertical mean.
It also checks an analytic bound absorbing an unbounded collection of
sufficiently separated frequency interactions into viscosity. Both results
serve the remaining generated-stretching budget. Neither assumes that a
favorable initial geometry persists or that a truncated set of modes
obeys an independent fluid equation.

The frequency argument uses standard convolution, Bernstein-type bounds
and viscous absorption. Frequency separation is also central to
[Cheskidov and Shvydkoy's dissipation-range regularity criteria](https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.1944).
Their solution-dependent dissipation wavenumber and regularity theorem
are not asserted to be the datum-fixed triad selector constructed below.
The present bounds are derived explicitly for this lane's remainder and
continuation consumer; no new arbitrary-data regularity criterion is claimed.

### What renews the descendant's source capacity

Use the full Leray projection, without the vertical-mean removal Pi of
(207). For a smooth solenoidal field w put H_r=exp(r Delta),

```text
v_r=H_r w, n_r=N(v_r), z_r=H_r N(w), c_r=z_r-n_r,
C1(w)=integral_0^infinity ||n_r||2^2 dr,
G(w)=-2 integral_0^infinity <n_r,(n_r.grad)v_r> dr,
M1(w)=-2 integral_0^infinity <n_r,(c_r.grad)v_r> dr,
M2(w)=-2 integral_0^infinity <n_r,(v_r.grad)c_r> dr.

DC1(w)[N(w)]=G(w)+M1(w)+M2(w).                       (279)
```

The omitted source-transport term is exactly zero, since div v_r=0.
All other terms remain. Here G observes source deformation, not directly
vorticity deformation. The covariance is still the SAME-displacement
Gaussian covariance of the current field. With
Tau_r=H_r(w tensor w)-v_r tensor v_r and
K_r=P[(v_r.grad)n_r-(grad v_r)^T n_r],
c_r=-P div Tau_r and M1+M2=2 integral <Tau_r,grad K_r>.
Its isotropic part contributes only pressure. These identities remain
