valid with the generated vertical mean; removing that mean would change
the observer and the quantities being compared.

For the two raw descendants w_g,w_d from (271), exact rational arithmetic
gives the following rounded values:

| Work in (279) | Growing phase | Depleting phase |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Source deformation G | 1670.484765... | -3254.705347... |
| Covariance deformation M1 | 249.272706... | -122.294405... |
| Covariance transport M2 | 57.220886... | -414.943077... |
| Complete nonlinear renewal | 1976.978357... | -3791.942828... |

More than four fifths of the adverse renewal comes from G; both covariance
terms reinforce it. Consequently a correction that only removes covariance
work would leave positive source-deformation work in this example.
The full projected tensor pairing independently checks the split.

The next actual derivative is retained too. Let w(t) solve unforced NS
with viscosity mu=1/256 from either raw seed. C1 remains the fixed
auxiliary observer above, not C_mu. Write d=-mu Aw+N(w),
e=-mu Ad+DN(w)[d], and differentiate every slot. In particular

```text
C1'=-mu ||N(w)||2^2+G+M1+M2,
C1''=-2mu <N(w),DN(w)[d]>+DG(w)[d]+D(M1+M2)(w)[d].   (280)
```

At the growing seed, DG[d]=5662.649635...,
D(M1+M2)[d]=11403.402929..., C1'=1869.462238...,
and C1''=16794.143027... are all strictly positive. Viscosity and the
source-square derivative have been included. At the depleting seed,
C1'<0 and C1''<0, although its covariance contribution is changing upward.
An independent differentiation of the complete heat square gives
C1''=2 integral(||n_r'||2^2+<n_r,n_r''>), with
n_r''=B(H_r e,v_r)+B(v_r,H_r e)+2B(H_r d,H_r d),
and checks the same exact rational answer.

Smooth local evolution preserves the growing seed's strict signs on a
positive interval. Rescaling b(t)=256w(256t) gives viscosity one, as in
(272), and preserves their signs. The preceding analytic release theorem
then transfers them to actual descendants of oscillatory parents after a
small fixed positive smoothing time. Thus source-capacity growth need not
immediately decelerate after release. No sign is extrapolated beyond the
local interval, and neither indefinite renewal nor a singularity follows.

### A fixed rule paying complete separated triads at every scale

Consider either normalized period-2pi T3 or R3 with the unitary Fourier
transform. Fix nu>0, an original datum of energy E0>0, and 0<delta<1/2.
For the ACTUAL b=u-H_(nu t)u0, the two energy inequalities give
||b||2<=B0=2sqrt(E0) on every available smooth prefix.
Define constants and a parent-dependent radius by

```text
c_domain=sqrt(27) on T3,   c_domain=1/(sqrt(10)pi) on R3,
m(p)=[delta nu/(3 c_domain B0)]^(2/5) |p|^(4/5).

S={ triads k+p+q=0: the smallest magnitude L is positive,
     L<=P/2 and L<=m(P), where P is the middle magnitude }. (281)
```

Here m(P) means the same radial function evaluated at magnitude P.
Every parameter is fixed from the original datum and viscosity, before
observing the future solution. The selector is invariant under EVERY
permutation and simultaneous negation of the three frequencies. Thus it
keeps all three receiving roles of a selected interaction, including
feedback into the two higher-frequency modes. It selects triads from
arbitrarily large frequencies, not a finite cutoff. The required relative
separation becomes stronger at increasing frequency.

Let N_S(b) retain precisely these pairs in the COMPLETE Fourier formula
for N(b), including its Leray multiplier, and put T_S=<Ab,N_S(b)>.
The mask sees the triple formed by a pair and its negative output. Then,
with D_b=||Ab||2^2,

```text
                         |T_S| <= delta nu D_b.             (282)
```

First, the symmetry of the mask preserves the vorticity-stretching
identity: T_S is exactly the similarly selected integral of
omega_i omega_j partial_j b_i, where omega=curl b. To verify this, move
one curl from Ab onto N_S, use the symmetrized curl identity for the
advective nonlinearity, and cancel the selected transport term. The
transport cancellation interchanges the two vorticity inputs while
keeping the transporting velocity fixed. The sum of their derivative
frequencies is the negative velocity frequency, whose contraction
vanishes by incompressibility. Permutation invariance keeps both terms
in the same selected region. Leray pressure disappears legitimately
under curl. This argument would not justify an arbitrary nonsymmetric
selection of receiving roles. The checker independently evaluates both
masked cubic expressions on all three carrier fixtures.

For the remaining summation, each vorticity-stretching term is bounded
by |k||p||q| |b_hat(k)||b_hat(p)||b_hat(q)|, with the Fourier convolution
normalization. Partition the sum according to which frequency is the
smallest. Each of the three parts has the same upper bound. In the part
where k is smallest, apply

```text
2 |p||q| |b_hat(p)||b_hat(q)|
                    <= |p|^2 |b_hat(p)|^2+|q|^2 |b_hat(q)|^2.
```

Symmetry between p and q makes the two contributions equal. For each
fixed p, enlarge the permitted k to the ball 0<|k|<=m(p).
Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the sum or integral of |k| |b_hat(k)| by
c_domain B0 m(p)^(5/2). Thus the three choices together give

```text
|T_S| <= 3 c_domain B0 sum_p |p|^2 |b_hat(p)|^2 m(p)^(5/2)
       = delta nu sum_p |p|^4 |b_hat(p)|^2.
```

On the torus, for M>=1, the number of lattice points in the ball is at
most (2 floor(M)+1)^3<=27M^3, so sum |k|^2<=27M^5.
For M<1 there is no nonzero lattice point. On R3 the unitary convolution
factor gives
(2pi)^(-3) integral_(|k|<=M) |k|^2 dk=M^5/(10pi^2).
These are the constants used in (281). There is no factor for the number
of scales and no unbounded sharp projection acting on L-infinity.
Absolute convergence follows from the same bound for smooth fields with
finite D_b. In particular this estimate retains the interchanges needed
to account for the complete interaction, not just its low-output term.

This is a spatial estimate, so it does not pretend that b satisfies an
unforced energy equation. Only its L2 envelope comes from the two actual
energy inequalities. The changing field and every internal parent are
retained in T_S. Since the selector is fixed, following a history creates
no derivative or seam cost for this observation. The case E0=0 has the
zero solution and is handled separately, without dividing by B0.

For exact torus computation put B2=B0^2. The fractional-power condition
in (281) is equivalently

```text
59049 B2^2 (L^2)^5 <= (delta nu)^4 (P^2)^4,
4L^2<=P^2,   L>0.
```

Here 59049=3^4*(sqrt(27))^4. Thus the checker selects every pair using
rational arithmetic. Fixtures with carriers64,128,256 retain nonzero
paid work, pressure and all remaining outputs. They check the inequality,
the masked vorticity identity and exact source reconstruction; the
summation argument, not those finite fixtures, proves the unbounded-family
statement.

### Disjoint payments and the smaller continuation obligation

Fix also M,Lambda as in (277). Let F be its pair region
|k|<=M, |p|,|q|>=Lambda. Use F\S for the fixed-band payment and S for
viscous absorption, so an interaction is never removed twice. Define

```text
T_fixed=<Ab,N_(F\S)(b)>,
g_core=g(b)-T_S-T_fixed.                              (283)
```

The proof of (274) also applies to a coefficientwise selection of any
subset of those input pairs: its absolute convolution is no larger.
Consequently (277) pays a|T_fixed| with the SAME R_paid and its SAME
original allowance. Both selected sources are only observations of the
full equation; the residual includes every pair not assigned to them.

Take delta=1/8. The next sufficient target is now

```text
2 integral_0^t a g_core
       <= (3nu/4) integral_0^t a D_b + K_core(u0,nu,H).       (284)
```

Adding (282) spends the remaining nu/4, and adding the fixed-band payment
gives (257) with K=K_core+2R_paid(0). The existing gradient-energy
continuation consumer is unchanged. This accounts for the entire
viscosity allocation; it does not spend the same dissipation twice.
K_core must still be finite from the original datum, viscosity and
horizon, uniformly over every available smooth prefix.

For both released seeds256w_g,256w_d, with their own energy as E0, the
checker finds no selected pair in either region at M=5,Lambda=7.
Increasing the energy envelope only shrinks S. Their adverse stretching
therefore remains in the core, including when the original oscillatory
parent datum has the larger energy needed for the release construction.
The new bound does not resolve renewal among these comparable scales.

Run `python3 -O labs/descendant_geometry_separation.py`. It checks the
full geometry/covariance split, mean retention, independent second
physical derivative, exact pair selection, nonzero absorption fixtures,
disjoint source reconstruction and the retained adverse core. All new
physical statements are analytic, not Lean-certified by the finite
checks. No Lean declarations or axioms change. Arbitrary-data regularity
and the uniform core-history estimate (284) remain open.

## An actual source-capacity return with positive core cost

`capacity_return_cycle.py` supplies a test of an interval reserve for the
remaining cost (284). On a genuine smooth unforced periodic history, the
FULL source capacity of the generated remainder returns to an earlier
value while its enstrophy increases and its integrated core cost is
strictly positive. This is a return of one observation, not a periodic
orbit of the full fluid. Its kinetic energy decreases, and the returning
states differ. All Fourier outputs, pressure and generated mean motion
are retained. Exact calculation supplies the initial jets; uniform local
existence, the return interval and its realization after parent release
are analytic arguments below, not Lean-certified results.

### A strict capacity turning point under the full equation

Work on normalized period-2pi T3. Write A=-Delta and N(v)=-P[(v.grad)v].
Use the four wavevectors of (271), but a new coefficient tuple:

```text
k1=(1,0,1), k2=(1,-1,1), k3=(2,0,1), k4=(2,-1,1),
(c1,c2,c3,c4)=(1,1,-4,3),
V=sum_j c_j (-(k_j)_2,(k_j)_1,0) cos(k_j.x),
w=N(V),  C1(v)=integral_0^infinity ||N(exp(r Delta)v)||2^2 dr.
```

V is horizontal and exactly divergence-free, with ||V||2^2=56.
The full pressure projection creates a vertical component in w. Both
w and N(w) have nonzero vertical averages; neither is removed.
The global spatial mean is zero. Exact rational arithmetic gives

```text
E(w)=140876/1071,  Z(w)=1345/2,  D(w)=20769/2,
g(w)=11895/68,
P0=DC1(w)[N(w)]=432.6120639436...,
N2=||N(w)||2^2=30466.9519509665...,
mu_*=P0/N2=0.01419938773789... >0.                   (285)
```

The displayed decimals only abbreviate exact rationals printed by the
checker. Here E=||v||2^2, Z=<v,Av>, D=||Av||2^2 and g=<Av,N(v)>.
For viscosity mu, the actual tangent and acceleration are

```text
d=-mu Aw+N(w),    e=-mu Ad+DN(w)[d],
C1'=P0-mu N2,
C1''=2 integral_0^infinity (||n_r'||2^2+<n_r,n_r''>) dr,
n_r=N(H_r w),    n_r'=DN(H_r w)[H_r d],
n_r''=DN(H_r w)[H_r e]+2B(H_r d,H_r d),
B(v,z)=-P[(v.grad)z],    H_r=exp(r Delta).         (286)
```

Here P0 denotes a scalar production rate; P in N and B is the Leray
projector. At mu=mu_* the checker establishes

```text
C1'=0,  C1''=-kappa < -45000,
Z'=z_*=2g-2mu_*D >50,
q_*=2g-mu_*D >200,
E'=-2mu_*Z <0.                                    (287)
```

Numerically kappa=45896.49629143... and z_*=54.94585724....
An independent quartic-polarization calculation checks C1'': if
S_j=C1(w+jd)+C1(w-jd)-2C1(w), then
D^2 C1(w)[d,d]=(16S_1-S_2)/12. Adding DC1(w)[e] gives exactly
the value in (286). Thus the second derivative includes the acceleration
of the full fluid, not a frozen-parent or straight-line surrogate.

### From the turning point to an actual return interval

Let v_theta(t) be the ACTUAL local NS solution starting from w with
mu_theta=(1-theta)mu_*, for small theta>=0. Its initial capacity slope is
alpha_theta=theta P0. Uniform smooth local existence holds for viscosities
in [mu_*/2,mu_*]. Smooth dependence follows, for example, by subtracting
the two NS equations: the viscosity difference contributes
(mu-mu_*)Delta v as a source in the usual high-Sobolev difference estimate.
Local bounds and Gronwall give convergence as mu tends to mu_*.
The smooth trigonometric datum supplies all the regularity required.

There is no unknown global bound in this step. One may first choose a
common local H^12 existence interval and then shrink it. On mean-zero
periodic fields, the heat semigroup decays exponentially. Product bounds
therefore make C1 and the derivatives in (286) continuous in sufficiently
high Sobolev norms, with integrable domination of the auxiliary heat
integrals. The equation controls the two physical time derivatives.
Consequently there exist T>0 and theta_0>0, fixed from w and mu_*, such
that, for 0<=theta<=theta_0 and 0<=t<=T,

```text
-3kappa/2 <= d^2 C1(v_theta(t))/dt^2 <= -kappa/2,
dZ(v_theta(t))/dt >= z_*/2.                         (288)
```

For theta>0 put alpha=alpha_theta. Integrating (288) gives

```text
alpha t-3kappa t^2/4 <= C1(v_theta(t))-C1(w)
                         <= alpha t-kappa t^2/4.
sigma=alpha/(8kappa), t1=alpha/kappa, t2=5alpha/kappa.     (289)
```

Choose theta still smaller so t2<=T. The exact brackets are

```text
C1(v_theta(sigma))-C1(w) >= 29alpha^2/(256kappa),
C1(v_theta(t1))-C1(v_theta(sigma)) >= 33alpha^2/(256kappa),
C1(v_theta(t2))-C1(v_theta(sigma)) <= -349alpha^2/(256kappa).
```

Continuity and strict concavity give a unique later return
t_ret in (t1,t2), with capacity equal at sigma and t_ret and strictly
larger between them. Also C1'(sigma)>0. The duration satisfies

```text
7alpha/(8kappa) < t_ret-sigma < 39alpha/(8kappa).            (290)
```

Enstrophy rises throughout this interval by (288). Full kinetic energy
strictly falls because Z stays positive and E'=-2mu_theta Z.
The positive starting time sigma is useful for the physical parent
realization below. The exact fixtures theta=1/100 and 1/1000 verify
the corresponding initial signs, but are not claimed to supply an
explicit value of theta_0 or a certified numerical return time.

### The return has positive cost after both previous payments

Keep the disjoint regions S and F\S from (281)--(283), delta=1/8,
M=5 and Lambda=7. For any field v to which the absorption bound applies,
the absolute convolution argument for any subset of F gives

```text
|T_(F\S)(v)| <= M^2 ||v||2 K_M ||Q_(>=Lambda)v||2^2,
2g_core(v)-(3mu/4)D(v)
 >= 2g(v)-mu D(v)
             -2M^2 ||v||2 K_M ||Q_(>=Lambda)v||2^2.  (291)
```

This uses |T_S|<=mu D/8, allocating its entire possible adverse sign.
It does not assume continuity of the selected mask as the viscosity or
original energy changes. All frequencies of w have magnitude less than7,
so the last term initially vanishes. At theta=0 the right side is q_*>200
from (287). By continuity, shrink the common interval and theta_0 so this
right side is at least q_*/2 for every v_theta under consideration.
Thus the core cost, not merely the unpartitioned stretching, is positive.
The integral over the return is larger than
7q_*P0 theta/(16kappa)>0. A positive weight at least one preserves this
lower bound. The same interval has enstrophy increase larger than
7z_*P0 theta/(16kappa).

The checker also verifies that both paid regions are empty at each
initial seed with energy envelope B0=2||w||2. The interval conclusion
uses (291), allowing all new modes and selected interactions to appear;
it does not assume these regions remain empty.

### A return of the actual remainder from one original datum

The independent solution above is a step in the construction, not a
substitute for the remainder that must start at zero in (284).
First convert to viscosity one by

```text
U_theta(t)=mu_theta^(-1) v_theta(t/mu_theta).
```

Direct substitution gives U_t=-AU+N(U). Capacity is multiplied by
mu_theta^(-4), enstrophy by mu_theta^(-2), and the unweighted integrated
core cost by mu_theta^(-2) when the corresponding absorption region is
scaled with its energy envelope. The strict return and cost signs persist.
The cost lower bound (291) is also valid for every larger admissible
energy envelope, so the construction does not require equality of masks.

Apply the analytic oscillatory-parent realization (262)--(268) with the
present V, viscosity one and epsilon=2/sqrt(mu_theta). Its limiting
descendant is epsilon^2 N(V)/4=mu_theta^(-1)w. The original data are

```text
u_(0,N)=epsilon N cos(Nx_3)V(x),
h_N(t)=exp(t Delta)u_(0,N),   b_N(t)=u_N(t)-h_N(t),
b_N(0)=0,   t_N=4log(N)/N^2.                        (292)
```

Fix a sufficiently small positive theta FIRST. Then choose N sufficiently
large. The actual solutions exist through the required interval, and
u_N(t_N+t) converges to U_theta(t), in every fixed spatial C^j norm on
compact time intervals away from zero. This is precisely the positive-time
stability and smoothing step after (268). The original h_N and its
derivatives vanish there, so b_N has the same convergence, including the
time derivatives supplied by its actual equation. No heat age is reset.

At the three positive times mu_theta*sigma, mu_theta*t1 and
mu_theta*t2, the strict capacity gaps in (289) persist for large N.
The intermediate value theorem therefore gives an EXACT return of
C1(b_N), starting at t_N+mu_theta*sigma and ending between
t_N+mu_theta*t1 and t_N+mu_theta*t2. Its enstrophy is strictly increasing.
Bound (291) stays strictly positive throughout this interval by the same
strong convergence. Use S with the ORIGINAL E0_N and use the original
weight a(t)>=1 from (254). The energy envelope is valid on every smooth
prefix; no convergence of S itself is required. It follows that

```text
C1(b_N(t_plus))=C1(b_N(t_minus)),
integral_(t_minus)^(t_plus)
  a(t)[2g_core(b_N(t))-(3/4)D(b_N(t))] dt >0.       (293)
```

Every datum in this construction is smooth, solenoidal and finite energy.
Its energy grows with N across the family. There is no claimed explicit
small N, whole-space localization, infinite sequence of returns or blowup.
The finite reserve of the full original datum may pay this finite cost.

### The precise reserve architecture this excludes

For a fixed original datum, viscosity and horizon, let Psi be any finite,
single-valued, time-independent function of C1 alone. Suppose it were to
pay every compatible interval's remaining core cost by

```text
Psi(C1(b(t_plus));u0,nu,H)
 + integral_(t_minus)^(t_plus) a[2g_core-(3nu/4)D_b]
 <= Psi(C1(b(t_minus));u0,nu,H).                    (294)
```

The actual history (293) contradicts (294): the endpoint values of Psi
are identical and the intervening cost is positive. Neither monotonicity
nor differentiability of Psi is needed. Allowing its parameters to depend
on the full original datum cannot change this equality for the SAME
history. This excludes a scalar-only remaining reserve, beyond the
constant-multiplier family already tested in (273).

It does not exclude explicit time dependence, a changing weight on Psi,
additional state or memory, a separate original allowance, or using slack
from another reserve. It does not refute (284). A compatible-history
summary that keeps only this capacity loses information needed for
interval payment. The observation's return cannot be pasted into an
indefinite physical cycle: the enstrophy, full state and resources spent
are different at the two endpoints.

Run `python3 -O labs/capacity_return_cycle.py`. The checker verifies the
full Fourier jets, an independent second-derivative calculation,
viscosity-one rescaling, the empty initial paid regions, retained mean
motion and exact return brackets. Local existence, the interval theorem
and its parent realization remain analytic. No Lean declarations or
axioms change. The next physical estimate must track resources beyond
this returning scalar while controlling the same open core budget (284).

## Source-direction reserves, transport and Schur elimination

`source_time_direction_reserve.py` tests whether retaining the source's
physical time direction repairs the remaining reserve. It gives a local
payment for the return in (293), but another actual released descendant
defeats every constant positive quadratic form in the source and either
of two directions. Exact Schur elimination preserves the instantaneous
minimum without making that minimum a decreasing history reserve.
The new physical intervals use the preceding analytic release theorem;
they are not newly Lean-certified.

### Full remainder derivatives and two retained directions

Keep the ORIGINAL h=exp(-nu t A)u0, b=u-h and full N=-P div(u tensor u).
The remainder's tangent and acceleration are exactly

```text
h_t=-nu Ah,
d=b_t=-nu Ab+N(b+h),
e=b_tt=-nu Ad+DN(b+h)[d-nu Ah].                    (295)
```

The checker independently expands the last line into the derivative of
N(b), the two mixed terms and N(h). A nonzero parent fixture verifies
that dropping those terms changes the acceleration. In particular b is
not assigned an independent unforced equation before release.

For auxiliary H_r=exp(r Delta), let v_r=H_r b, n_r=N(v_r). The first
direction is z_r=partial_t n_r=DN(v_r)[H_r d]. Its time derivative is
DN(v_r)[H_r e]+2B(H_r d,H_r d). The second direction is

```text
m_r=partial_t n_r+(v_r.grad)n_r,
partial_t m_r=partial_t^2 n_r+(H_r d.grad)n_r
                                      +(v_r.grad)partial_t n_r.
```

This is transport along the FILTERED remainder v_r, not an identification
of v_r with the full fluid velocity. No projection is applied to m_r,
which need not be solenoidal. Pressure remains in n_r, d and e.
Since div v_r=0, the transport contribution to integral <n_r,m_r>
cancels exactly. Its time derivative cancels only after retaining the
changing velocity H_r d, which the checker verifies separately.

For either choice z=n_t or z=m, form the integrated Gram matrix and its
FULL physical derivative, including integration over space and r:

```text
G = integral [[ |n|^2, <n,z> ], [ <n,z>, |z|^2 ]],
L = G',
G00=C1, G01=C1'/2, L00=C1', L01=C1''/2,
G11=integral |z|^2, L11=2 integral <z,z_t>.

J_W(t)=a(t) trace(W G(t)),
J_W'=a trace(W [L-kappa G])  when W is constant,
a'=-kappa a.                                      (296)
```

Here W is a fixed real symmetric positive semidefinite two-by-two
matrix. Its entries are constants over space and auxiliary heat time,
as well as physical time, but may be chosen from the original datum.
Thus J_W is a nonnegative sum of squares of real linear combinations
of n and z. The proposed square integral |n+eta z|^2 is included for
EVERY real eta, not only positive eta. No spatially varying or nonlinear
quadratic weight is included in this test.

### A growing descendant defeats all these constant weights

Use the growing and depleting seeds w=N(V) from (271), evolved with
physical viscosity mu=1/256. First compute G and L in these raw variables,
with no original-parent cooling. The two choices of z have the same
L00 and L01. Rounded values are:

| Seed | L00 | L01 | L11, time direction | L11, transport-adjusted |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Growing | 1869.462238 | 8397.071514 | 6613430.620087 | 107522.613480 |
| Depleting | -3907.722076 | -7263.478872 | -9428937.432829 | -28403.886378 |
| Return turning point (285) | 0 | -22948.248146 | 1080828.973326 | -54658.166739 |

The final row uses its own mu_* from (285). The checker uses exact
rationals, not the rounded table. At the growing seed, for BOTH directions,

```text
                         G > 0,    L-(1/2)G > 0.            (297)
```

Positive definiteness follows by checking the first diagonal and the
determinant. The determinants of L-G/2 are respectively
8621653475.0838... and 23162996.4920..., both strictly positive.
For a symmetric matrix K with K00>0, square completion gives
x^T K x=K00(x0+K01 x1/K00)^2+(det K/K00)x1^2.
This proves the claim for all real coefficients, beyond sampled mixtures.
At the depleting seed both L are negative definite. Source phase affects
the full matrix of rates, not just a single diagonal observation.

Removing transport substantially reduces both the direction's squared
norm and its growth, but the remaining matrix is still positive definite.
The failure is therefore not explained entirely by advection past a
fixed observer. Neither direction supplies a universally decreasing
reserve for the generated source.

To obtain an ACTUAL original-remainder statement at viscosity one,
scale U(t)=mu^(-1)w(t/mu), as before. With
D_mu=diag(mu^(-2),mu^(-3)), the two matrices become

```text
G_phys=D_mu G D_mu,  L_phys=mu^(-1) D_mu L D_mu.
```

Hence (297) gives L_phys-128G_phys>0 at the growing seed.
Continuity preserves this on a sufficiently short smooth interval.
Apply (262)--(268) with its original oscillatory parents, epsilon=32.
At fixed positive post-release times, b_N, its two time derivatives
and the required spatial derivatives converge to this physical solution.
The original kappa_N tends to zero. For sufficiently large finite N,
one common interval therefore has, for BOTH directions,

```text
L_N-kappa_N G_N >= 64G_N >0,
q_core=2g_core(b_N)-(3/4)D(b_N) >0.                 (298)
```

The second inequality uses the mask-independent lower bound (291),
which is already positive at this seed. It retains the original E0_N,
the all-scale region S, the disjoint fixed-band region F\S and all new
modes. The full actual field remains unforced; b_N(0)=0 and its original
heat age is unchanged.

For any nonzero W>=0, trace(W G_N)>0, so (296)--(298) imply
J_W'>=64J_W>0 while the core cost is positive. W=0 fails to pay the
positive cost too. The interval is common to ALL constant W>=0,
including weights selected from the original datum, since matrix
positivity is an open condition independent of those choices.
This is an obstruction to the stated differential payment, not to an
integrated allowance that permits finite positive defects.

### The same correction does pay the capacity return locally

At the turning point (285), fix xi=1/50 in the raw variables. For either
direction, exact arithmetic gives

```text
L00+2xi L01+xi^2 L11
             +mu_*^2[2g(w)-(mu_*/2)D(w)] < -400.   (299)
```

At viscosity one the corresponding coefficient is eta=mu_*/50,
not 1/50. The square's rate scales by mu_*^(-5), whereas the physical
cost scales by mu_*^(-3), explaining the factor mu_*^2 in (299).
The upper estimate complementary to (291) is

```text
q_core(v) <= 2g(v)-(nu/2)D(v)
                  +2M^2||v||2 K_M||Q_(>=Lambda)v||2^2.
```

The high input vanishes at the seed. Continuity thus preserves strict
payment for small theta>0, on the entire shrinking return interval
constructed in (289)--(290), using the fixed eta=mu_theta/50 for that
history. After parent release the same estimate holds for the actual
b_N by positive-time smoothing. Original cooling contributes the
favorable term -kappa_N J_W. It follows that this nonnegative square
pays every subinterval of that local capacity return from its value
at the subinterval's beginning.

This does not pay the earlier creation of that value from b_N(0)=0,
nor establish its replenishment budget over arbitrary histories.
It explains why a correction can repair the return example yet fail
the different growing descendant in (298).

### Exact elimination and the cost of changing the observer

On a tested interval with G>0, put C=G00, x=G01 and K=G11>0.
At each time in that interval one can minimize the INTEGRATED square
over one scalar eta. Exact square completion gives

```text
integral |n+eta z|^2 = S+K(eta-eta_*)^2,
eta_*=-x/K,   S=C-x^2/K>0,
S'=L00-2x L01/K+x^2 L11/K^2
   =(1,eta_*) L (1,eta_*)^T.                       (300)
```

S is the Schur complement of the direction block; eta_* reconstructs
the minimizing coefficient. This is the same linear-elimination pattern
used by `GSLT.Dynamics.LinearBoundaryReduction`, applied here analytically
to a quadratic norm. No new Lean connection is claimed. Differentiating
the optimum introduces no missing eta_*' term because the derivative
with respect to eta vanishes at eta_*.

At the actual growing interval, (298) gives (a S)'>=64a S>0.
Even this freely recomputed instantaneous minimum therefore fails to
pay q_core. At the return turning point, x=0 and S'=0 while the cost
is positive; the fixed non-minimizing direction in (299) pays instead.
Minimizing a reserve's current size and minimizing its payment defect
are different operations. This does not rule out Bellman optimization
over compatible histories, or all nonlinear functions of G.

For a differentiable time-dependent W(t)>=0, the exact additional term is

```text
J_W'=a trace(W[L-kappa G])+a trace(W'G).
```

Consequently payment J_W'+a q_core<=0 on (298) would require

```text
-trace(W'G) >= 64 trace(WG)+q_core.                 (301)
```

Changing the observation can decrease its reported reserve, but that
work must be supplied and accounted for. Jumps require their endpoint
cost as well. Equation (301) is a necessary local cost, not an estimate
controlling it from the original datum. Spatially varying weights bring
further derivative terms, also outside the constant-matrix obstruction.
The full-data core budget (284) remains open.

Run `python3 -O labs/source_time_direction_reserve.py`. It checks every
parent term in (295), transport cancellation and its derivative, both
complete Gram matrices, exact positivity certificates, direct square
derivatives, the local return-payment margin and Schur reconstruction.
Python compilation and finite algebra do not certify the local PDE or
release arguments. No Lean declarations or axioms change.

## The frame inherited from an oscillatory parent

`inherited_frame_release.py` follows the existing transported-frame
observable through the ACTUAL parent-release construction (262)--(268).
The mean frame can lose the visible fast shear while its second moment
retains a nonzero covariance. This identifies the frame carried into the
descendant and gives a finite strain allowance through the release.
An explicit physical example then separates decreasing weighted vorticity
from increasing ordinary vorticity. The uniform PDE estimates below are
analytic; symbolic checks verify the profiles and physical derivatives.

### Original initialization and retained covariance

Fix nu>0, finite epsilon, and a horizontal divergence-free trigonometric
V(x), with arbitrary dependence on x3, as in (262). Use the same actual
unforced solution u_N with original datum epsilon N cos(Nx3)V.
For D=partial_t+u_N.grad-nu Delta and B=grad u_N, construct the smooth
matrix fields on its available smooth prefix by

```text
D F_N=B F_N,                  F_N(0)=I,
D M_N=B M_N+M_N B^T,          M_N(0)=I.             (302)
```

These are the first- and second-frame moment equations used in the earlier
transported-frame construction. Here their PDE solutions are constructed
along the same u_N; the auxiliary fields do not change the fluid equation.
Linear parabolic evolution gives existence on each smooth prefix.
The matrix maximum principle preserves symmetry and positive definiteness
of M_N. More explicitly, comparison with
exp(-2 integral_0^t ||sym B||_infinity) I gives a positive lower bound
on each such prefix. No bound up to an unknown singular time is assumed.

The covariance Sigma_N=M_N-F_N F_N^T satisfies exactly

```text
D Sigma_N=B Sigma_N+Sigma_N B^T
                       +2nu sum_j (partial_j F_N)(partial_j F_N)^T,
Sigma_N(0)=0,   Sigma_N>=0.                        (303)
```

The source is positive semidefinite, so the same comparison proves the
last assertion. Replacing M_N by the square of its mean would discard
this diffusion-generated information. This use of the moment equations
does not newly formalize a Brownian path construction in Lean.

### The complete leading frame in the fast layer

Use delta=1/N, tau=N^2 t and theta=Nx3. The lifted velocity U_N and
derivatives D_N are exactly those of (263); u_N=N U_N on the diagonal.
The lifted strain is B_N=D_N U_N, with component convention
(B_N)_ij=(D_N)_j(U_N)_i. The lifted frame equations are

```text
(partial_tau+U_N.D_N-nu D_N^2) F_N^lift=B_N F_N^lift,
(partial_tau+U_N.D_N-nu D_N^2) M_N^lift
                           =B_N M_N^lift+M_N^lift B_N^T.
```

There is no amplitude rescaling for the frame. The leading velocity
H0=epsilon exp(-nu tau)cos(theta)V is horizontal, so its leading fast
transport vanishes and its strain is
B0=-epsilon exp(-nu tau)sin(theta) V tensor e3.
Treating x as a parameter, put

```text
q=exp(-nu tau),  b=-epsilon tau q sin(theta),
I0=[1-(1+2nu tau)q^2]/(4nu^2),
I2=[(2nu tau-1)q^2+q^4]/(4nu^2),
c=epsilon^2[I0-I2 cos(2theta)],
F0=I+b V tensor e3,
M0=I+b(V tensor e3+e3 tensor V)+c V tensor V.      (304)
```

Direct differentiation gives F0_tau-nu F0_thetatheta=B0 F0 and
M0_tau-nu M0_thetatheta=B0 M0+M0 B0^T, with both initial values I.
All off-diagonal correlations remain. In particular

```text
M0-F0 F0^T=(c-b^2) V tensor V,
(partial_tau-nu partial_theta^2)(c-b^2)=2nu b_theta^2>=0,
det M0=1+(c-b^2)|V|^2.
```

Comparison gives c-b^2>=0. Also I2>=0, since
(exp(4nu tau)I2)'=tau exp(2nu tau), and
I0+I2=(1-q^2)^2/(4nu^2). Write beta=epsilon^2/(4nu^2).
It follows that 0<=c<=beta and

```text
trace M0<=3+beta |V|^2,
lambda_min(M0)>=1/(2+beta |V|^2),
F0 -> I,     M0 -> M_*=I+beta V tensor V.           (305)
```

For the lower bound, in the plane spanned by V and e3 the determinant
is at least one and the trace is at most 2+beta|V|^2; the orthogonal
eigenvalue is one. The limit retains covariance even though the mean
frame tends to I. These formulas reuse the earlier exact shear calculation
with the full spatially varying parent envelope kept as a parameter.

### Uniform comparison with the actual frame

Fix a sufficiently large integer m, for example m>=8; norms in this
paragraph are on T4. Constants depend on m, V, epsilon and nu, not N.
The actual velocity estimate (267), applied at the needed higher derivative
orders, and the complete approximation (264) give, for a fixed polynomial p,

```text
||B_N-B0||_(H^m)
 <= C delta p(tau)exp(-nu tau/2)+C delta^2.
```

The nondecaying mean in R contributes only order delta^2 to B_N.
The pressure-generated vertical motion is retained: its transport of
F0 or M0 is order delta times an integrably decaying theta derivative.
The slow transport of their limiting x-dependent parts is order delta^2.
For either profile, substitution into its COMPLETE lifted equation has
residual bounded by

```text
C delta p(tau)exp(-nu tau/2)+C delta^2.             (306)
```

To see all terms in (306), compare D_N^2 with partial_theta^2, giving
2delta partial_3 partial_theta+delta^2 Delta_x. The order-delta term
acts only on the decaying oscillatory channels. In U_N.D_N, horizontal
transport carries delta, while U_N,3=O(delta); the latter again meets
a decaying theta derivative. The remaining mean transport is order
delta^2. Reaction errors are (B_N-B0)F0 or (B_N-B0)M0 and its transpose.
The actual velocity error and its derivatives are O(delta^2) in the
lifted norms. Products with the bounded smooth profiles have the same
residual bound. In particular the vertical return channel is not set to zero.

The two frame errors start at zero. The H^m energy estimate for their
linear equations has coefficient bounded by
C(||U_N||_(H^(m+1))+||B_N||_(H^m)). Its integral through
tau_N=4log(N)/nu is bounded independently of N, by (266)--(267).
The transport vector (delta U_1,delta U_2,delta U_3,U_3) on T4 is
divergence-free. Diffusion gives a nonpositive quadratic contribution;
the estimate uses no inverse ellipticity constant for D_N^2.
Gronwall and the integrated residual therefore give

```text
sup_(0<=tau<=tau_N)
 [||F_N^lift-F0||_(H^m)+||M_N^lift-M0||_(H^m)] <= C/N.
```

Pullback is bounded in C0 by Sobolev embedding on T4. At
t_N=4log(N)/(nu N^2), this proves the physical limits

```text
||F_N(t_N)-I||_infinity+||M_N(t_N)-M_*||_infinity <= C/N,
M_*=I+epsilon^2/(4nu^2) V tensor V.                 (307)
```

No convergence of physical spatial derivatives at t_N is claimed.
On the whole fast interval, (305) and the uniform error also give,
for sufficiently large N,

```text
[2(2+beta||V||_infinity^2)]^(-1) I <= M_N
                              <= (4+beta||V||_infinity^2) I.
```

The actual integrated strain and vorticity have the sharper frequency-
uniform allowance

```text
integral_0^(t_N) ||grad u_N||_infinity dt
 <= |epsilon| ||V||_infinity/nu+C/N,
integral_0^(t_N) ||curl u_N||_infinity dt
 <= |epsilon| ||V||_infinity/nu+C/N.                (308)
```

The gradient norm here is the matrix operator norm. Indeed grad u_N=N^2 B_N
on the diagonal, so the time rescaling cancels N^2. The leading strain
has norm |epsilon|q|sin(theta)||V|; its curl vector has the same magnitude.
Integrating the B_N-B0 bound contributes C/N in either norm.
Thus the full nonlinear parent release has a finite BKM cost with no
factor growing in N. Epsilon is not assumed small; the threshold on N
may depend strongly on it. This pays the release interval, not all later
descendant evolution or repeated releases.

### The frame travels into the descendant without a reset

Let U(s) be the smooth local NS solution from
U(0)=epsilon^2 N(V)/(4nu). Evolve its frame equations (302) from
F(0)=I and M(0)=M_*, the limits supplied by (307).
This is the limiting post-release pair; the actual F_N,M_N still have
their single original initialization at physical time zero.

The velocity stability argument after (268) gives a common positive
interval and uniform C0 convergence of u_N(t_N+s) to U(s).
The same local mild estimates give
||grad u_N(t_N+s)||_infinity<=C s^(-1/2) and a difference bound
C N^(-1)s^(-1/2), after reducing the common interval if needed.
These follow by differentiating the mild equation, moving the spatial
derivative onto its product, and using the integrable convolution of
(s-r)^(-1/2) with r^(-1/2). The initial C0 difference is O(1/N).

For the linear frame equations, write advection in divergence form.
Its heat-kernel factor is integrable, and the reaction coefficient
grad u_N has the preceding integrable bound. The resulting mild
contraction and difference estimates, together with (307), give uniform
C0 convergence of the two frames to F,M. On intervals s>=s1>0,
parabolic smoothing gives convergence in every fixed C^j norm, and the
equations then give the required time derivatives. Positive definiteness
is uniform there, either by matrix comparison or convergence to M>0.
Only local existence at the fixed descendant is used.

Consequently any strict finite-order comparison below at s=0 first
persists to a small fixed positive s, then transfers to sufficiently
large finite N. This order of choices avoids inferring derivative
convergence from the C0 assertion at t_N.

### Sharp conversion and actual growth after inheritance

For the inherited tensor let Q_*=M_*^(-1). Its exact inverse is

```text
Q_*=I-beta V tensor V/(1+beta|V|^2),
q=omega^T Q_* omega,
1 <= |omega|^2/q <= 1+beta|V|^2       when omega!=0. (309)
```

The lower bound uses M_*>=I; the upper bound is its largest eigenvalue.
For a fixed eta>0 the regularized quotient (|omega|^2+eta)/(q+eta)
has the same upper bound and is defined at vorticity zeros. For the
ACTUAL frame at t_N, the upper bound is at most
1+beta||V||_infinity^2+C/N, regardless of the unresolved derivatives
of u_N at precisely that time. Thus the regularized log conversion
has a finite original-parent allowance through the layer. This is the
initial value to retain when composing the existing logarithmic/HJB
representation across the release. It is not reset to zero, and the
later coupled potential in that representation remains unpaid.

For an explicit family take coordinates (x,y,z) and

```text
V=cos(z)(cos(y),-cos(x),0),  phi=sin(x)sin(y),
p=-phi/2-phi cos(2z)/6,
w=N(V)=-(cos(2z)partial_x phi,
          cos(2z)partial_y phi, sin(2z)phi)/3,
zeta=curl w=sin(2z)(-sin(x)cos(y),cos(x)sin(y),0).
```

The checker verifies divergence, w=-(V.grad)V-grad p and the full
pressure Poisson equation. On x=y=z=h, 0<h<pi/2, zeta is nonzero
and parallel to V, so the directional factor for omega=epsilon^2 zeta/(4nu)
is exactly 1+2beta cos(h)^4. Its spatial supremum is 1+2beta;
the bound (309) is sharp. The supremum approaches a vorticity zero,
but every nearby point used for the lower bound has nonzero vorticity.
Large conversion is therefore possible in this inherited physical
geometry, not just in an independently chosen matrix example.

Set nu=1, epsilon=16, so U(0)=64w and M(0)=I+64 V tensor V.
At x=y=z=pi/6, exact rational computation gives, with
D_t=partial_t+U.grad denoting the MATERIAL derivative,

```text
s=|omega|^2=1152,      q=1152/73,      k=s/q=73,
D_t s=10752>0,
D_t q=-760320/5329<0,
D_t k=4024/3>0.                                   (310)
```

The calculation uses the actual equations
D_t omega=Delta omega+(grad U)omega and
D_t M=Delta M+(grad U)M+M(grad U)^T, including every spatial derivative
of the inherited tensor. Independent inverse differentiation verifies
(D_t-Delta)q=-2D_cov, where
D_cov=sum_j |partial_j omega-(partial_j M)M^(-1)omega|_(M^(-1))^2>=0.
The Eulerian q rate has the opposite sign here; it is not substituted
for the material rate in (310).

There is also a strict increase of the whole frame bound. Initially
sup_x lambda_max(M)=129, attained at the origin. There U=0, and for
e=(1,-1,0)/sqrt(2), the exact Rayleigh rate is
partial_t(e^T M e)=4992>0. Thus the inherited upper bound 129 cannot
be kept unchanged even for the local descendant evolution.

By the positive-time convergence above, the strict signs in (310)
occur on a short material interval of actual finite-N unforced flows,
with the frame initialized at I at their ORIGINAL time zero. Weighted
depletion and ordinary-vorticity amplification coexist on the same
history. Each datum is finite energy; no indefinite amplification or
failure of a full-data allowance follows.

The remaining physical task is the time-integrated conversion through
interacting descendants, with their inherited frame and covariance.
The cancellation in `TransportedFrameMetric.production_nonpos` does not
supply that comparison, as its exact Lean statement explicitly retains.
The BKM/gradient-energy continuation hypotheses and the core budget
(284) are still open for arbitrary data.

Run `python3 -O labs/inherited_frame_release.py`. It checks the two fast
frame equations, covariance, exact inherited inverse, projected physical
source, sharp conversion and complete material derivatives. The uniform
lifted estimates, matrix comparison, smoothing and actual-history passages
remain analytic. No Lean declarations or axioms change.

## Joint parent covariance and ordered release histories

`joint_parent_boundary.py` checks the coefficients and physical boundary
algebra for a finite family of simultaneous parents. Their cross-covariance
determines both the released velocity and the inherited frame. The same
calculation allows a nontrivial incoming frame, so successively released
parents need not erase earlier geometry. Different release orders can
have the same limiting velocity and different limiting frame tensors.

The following release and composition statements are analytic, with
uniform error estimates as in (262)--(308). The checker verifies their
finite algebra, not existence intervals. These are limiting boundary
laws with controlled finite-frequency errors, not exact replacements
of finite-frequency NS histories by smaller graphs.

### Joint data and a compatible boundary response

On the normalized period-2pi torus fix nu>0, a smooth solenoidal background
W(x), and finitely many horizontal solenoidal trigonometric fields V_i(x).
Dependence on x3 is unrestricted. Let f_i(theta) be real mean-zero
trigonometric polynomials, with arbitrary finite amplitudes. Set

```text
H_i(tau,theta)=exp(nu tau partial_theta^2)f_i(theta),
H0=sum_i H_i V_i,
u_N(0,x)=W(x)+N sum_i f_i(Nx3)V_i(x),
Gamma_ij=integral_0^infinity mean_theta(H_i H_j) d tau
        =(1/(2nu)) sum_(k!=0) fhat_i(k) conjugate(fhat_j(k))/k^2,
S(x)=(1/nu) sum_ij Gamma_ij V_i(x) tensor V_j(x).    (311)
```

All data are exactly divergence-free. Fourier coefficients and L2 norms
here use normalized theta measure. Pairing k with -k shows that Gamma is
real symmetric. For any real vector z, z^T Gamma z is the integral of
mean_theta(sum_i z_i H_i)^2, so Gamma>=0 and S(x)>=0. No cross term is
replaced by a product of separate parent averages.

Let B(a,b)=-P[(a.grad)b], with the full periodic Leray projection, including
its action on the slow mean. The joint velocity increment is

```text
J=sum_ij Gamma_ij B(V_i,V_j)=-nu P div S.           (312)
```

For the second equality, use div V_i=0 and symmetry of Gamma; the two
indices can be interchanged after differentiating V_i tensor V_j.
Thus the same covariance field that records the parent geometry produces
the slow velocity through a pressure-projected stress divergence.
It is not an independently chosen effective force.

Allow fixed smooth incoming matrices F_in,M_in, with M_in symmetric,
uniformly positive definite and M_in-F_in F_in^T>=0. Evolve the actual frame PDEs
(302) with these initial values. The incoming fields can be the boundary
values of an earlier compatible segment. They are held fixed in the
single-stage N limit. Put m33=e3^T M_in e3. The release law is

```text
u_N(t_N) -> W+J,
F_N(t_N) -> F_in,
M_N(t_N) -> M_in+m33 S,
t_N=4log(N)/(nu N^2),                             (313)
```

uniformly in space, with error at most C/N in all three fields. Constants
depend on the fixed data, not N. The original case F_in=M_in=I gives
M_out=I+S. In general the covariance increment is m33 S; it depends on
the incoming full second moment, not just its covariance or trace.
One can recover the released velocity from this increment as
J=-nu P div[(M_out-M_in)/m33]. Spatial derivatives of m33 are retained.
This formula describes the limiting response; no interior-history
reconstruction from S alone is asserted.

### Complete velocity layer, including every vertical return

Use the lifted derivatives D_N and projection P_N from (263). The exact
initial heat carrier is H_N=exp(nu tau D_N^2)sum_i f_i(theta)V_i.
The initial background is part of the first response, not an added
external force. Write R=r+R_osc, where mean_theta R_osc=0 and

```text
r(tau)=W+sum_ij [integral_0^tau mean_theta(H_i H_j) ds] B(V_i,V_j),
R_osc(0)=0,  (R_osc)_3=0,
(partial_tau-nu partial_theta^2)R_osc
 =-sum_ij [H_i H_j-mean_theta(H_i H_j)] (V_i.grad)V_j
   -r_3 sum_i (partial_theta H_i)V_i.              (314)
```

Every raw oscillatory source is horizontal. The limiting projector is
therefore the identity on those sources, whereas its mean is the full
P used in r. Equation (314) is precisely
R_tau=nu R_thetatheta-P_infinity[H0.grad_x H0+R_3 partial_theta H0]
with R(0)=W. The last term includes both W_3 and the vertical motion
generated by every ordered parent pair, acting on every carrier. Omitting
it leaves an order-delta residual and changes the physical approximation.
It has zero theta mean, so r is nevertheless computed by the displayed
joint quadratic integral.

All nonzero theta frequencies have positive heat rate. Finite Fourier
convolution and elementary forced heat equations show that R_osc and
r-(W+J) decay like a polynomial times exp(-nu tau), at each fixed spatial
derivative order. Resonant heat rates add polynomial factors; no growing
or nondecaying oscillatory mode is omitted.

The exactly solenoidal approximation is again
U_app=H_N+delta P_N R, with delta=1/N, and it has the exact initial value.
The estimates (266)--(267) apply with the finite carrier set replacing
{+1,-1}: H_N-H0 is bounded by C delta tau exp(-nu tau/2), and
P_N-P_infinity maps H^(m+1) to H^m with norm C delta. All order-delta
terms cancel by (314). The complete residual is bounded by
C delta^2 p(tau)exp(-nu tau/2)+C delta^3. Only slow derivatives of r can
persist, and their coefficient is delta^3. The divergence-free T4 energy
estimate and bootstrap give ||U-U_app||_(H^m)<=C delta^2 through tau_N.
This constructs the actual unforced solution through the layer and proves
the velocity assertion in (313), without a smallness assumption on the
fixed parents or W. Large N can depend strongly on all those data.

### Incoming frame, covariance and finite price

Let a_i=tau partial_theta H_i, a=sum_i a_i V_i, and let the symmetric
scalar fields C_ij solve

```text
(partial_tau-nu partial_theta^2)C_ij
                 =2tau (partial_theta H_i)(partial_theta H_j),
C_ij(0)=0.
```

With x a parameter, the complete leading frame profiles are

```text
F0=(I+a tensor e3)F_in,
M0=M_in+a tensor(M_in e3)+(M_in e3)tensor a
                          +m33 sum_ij C_ij V_i tensor V_j.       (315)
```

The leading strain is B0=(sum_i partial_theta H_i V_i) tensor e3.
The identity (V_i tensor e3)(V_j tensor e3)=0 and
(V_i tensor e3)M_in(V_j tensor e3)^T=m33 V_i tensor V_j verify both
complete frame equations. The matrix C-aa^T in carrier indices satisfies

```text
(partial_tau-nu partial_theta^2)(C_ij-a_i a_j)
                    =2nu (partial_theta a_i)(partial_theta a_j).
```

This is a positive semidefinite covariance source, with zero initial
value. The inherited mean cannot substitute for the second moment.
Integrating by parts in tau gives

```text
mean_theta C_ij(tau)
 =(1/nu)[integral_0^tau mean_theta(H_i H_j) ds
                         -tau mean_theta(H_i(tau)H_j(tau))].
```

All nonconstant C modes decay. Consequently F0 tends to F_in and
M0 tends to M_in+m33 S. The actual frame comparison in (306)--(307)
then applies: derivatives of the incoming fields add only decaying
order-delta terms or persistent order-delta^2 terms. The complete
reaction and transport residuals have the same integrable bounds.
The leading frame stays uniformly positive by matrix comparison using
the finite integrated leading strain. This proves the remaining limits
in (313). It does not assert physical derivative convergence at t_N.

There is an explicit parent-only price. Define

```text
L=(1/nu) sum_i ||V_i||_infinity
                      sum_(k!=0) |fhat_i(k)|/|k|
 <=pi/(sqrt(3)nu) sum_i ||V_i||_infinity ||f_i||_L2.
```

The second inequality is Cauchy--Schwarz and sum_(k!=0)1/k^2=pi^2/3.
The leading strain and leading curl have norm at most
sum_i ||V_i||_infinity |partial_theta H_i|. Therefore the ACTUAL fluid
satisfies

```text
integral_0^tN ||grad u_N||_op,infinity dt <=L+C/N,
integral_0^tN ||curl u_N||_infinity dt <=L+C/N.       (316)
```

The fixed incoming W changes the error constant, not L: its fast-time
strain contribution vanishes as N grows. This does not assign zero cost
to W over a later macroscopic interval. The frame increment is bounded
by the same parent information:

```text
||S||_infinity <=L^2/2,
||M_out||_infinity <=||M_in||_infinity(1+||S||_infinity).           (317)
```

Indeed Gamma_ii=(1/(2nu))sum|fhat_i(k)|^2/k^2 and the Gram
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality bounds every Gamma_ij. Combine this with the
triangle inequality for V_i and the bound of the weighted l2 norm by
its l1 norm. Positive semidefiniteness gives the last inequality.
The conversion cost is finite for this stage, with its incoming frame
retained. No estimate for arbitrary regenerated parents follows.

### Equal individual powers, different joint output

Take nu=1 and

```text
V1=(cos z cos y,0,0),   V2=(0,-cos z cos x,0),
f1=cos theta,          f2=sigma cos theta+sin(2theta),
sigma in {-1,+1},
Gamma=[[1/4,sigma/4],[sigma/4,5/16]], det Gamma=1/64.             (318)
```

Each V_i alone has zero projected self-interaction. The full cross source
w=N(V1+V2) is the nonzero three-dimensional field used in (309)--(310).
The release is J=sigma w/4, with a nonzero vertical component. The
individual carrier powers and their separate heat-energy histories are
unchanged by sigma; their joint correlation changes sign. Removing off-diagonal
Gamma would incorrectly predict zero released velocity. For every integer
N>=3, both original data have exactly ||u0_N||_2^2=3N^2/8; all carrier
aliases relevant to this energy calculation are absent. The checker
verifies the identity directly at two finite N and the same orthogonality
argument proves the stated range.

It also solves every scalar coefficient in (314)--(315), including all
pair-to-carrier vertical returns, with exact rational/exponential algebra.
The source calculation uses the full Fourier pressure projection and
retains every output. This fixture supplies a concrete reason to carry
joint covariance rather than only the parents' individual energies.

### Different orientations make successive releases noncommutative

Coordinate permutations give the same law for carrier normals n=e1,e2,e3,
with every corresponding envelope tangent to its carrier planes. If S is
its joint tensor and J=-nu P div S, the limiting stage acts by

```text
(W,F,M) -> (W+J, F, M+(n^T M n)S).                (319)
```

The normal component of the incoming second moment matters. Starting
from M=I, two stages give

```text
M12=I+S1+(1+n2^T S1 n2)S2,
M21=I+S2+(1+n1^T S2 n1)S1.                       (320)
```

Both limiting velocities are W+J1+J2. These frame tensors can differ.
For a physical example take nu=1, single carriers f=2cos(theta), and

```text
n1=e3, V1=cos z(cos y,-cos x,0), S1=V1 tensor V1,
n2=e1, V2=cos x(0,cos z,-cos y), S2=V2 tensor V2.
```

Each envelope is solenoidal and tangent to its own carrier planes. At
the origin a=V1=(1,-1,0), b=V2=(0,1,-1), and

```text
M12=[[2,-1,0],[-1,4,-2],[0,-2,3]],
M21=[[3,-2,0],[-2,4,-1],[0,-1,2]].
```

The traces agree, but the tensors differ by b tensor b-a tensor a.
More importantly the SAME limiting physical vorticity detects the
difference. Set W=0. At x=0,y=z=pi/4,
omega=curl[J1+J2]=(0,1/sqrt(2),0), and exact computation gives

```text
|omega|^2=1/2,
omega^T M12^(-1)omega=65/232,
omega^T M21^(-1)omega=33/124.                     (321)
```

Thus even the ordinary-vorticity conversion differs. This is a statement
about full physical envelopes and the pressure-projected descendant,
not independently chosen matrix examples.

### Realizing the order without injecting later parents

Both stages can occur in one actual unforced history. Place BOTH packets
in the ORIGINAL initial datum:

```text
u0_(N1,N2)=W+N1 f1(N1 n1.x)V1+N2 f2(N2 n2.x)V2,
F(0)=M(0)=I.
```

For each fixed sufficiently large N2, let N1 tend to infinity first.
The second packet is a fixed smooth part of W for the first application
of (313). After that release the limiting state is
(W+N2 f2 V2+J1,I,I+S1). Next let N2 tend to infinity and apply (313)
with incoming frame I+S1 and background W+J1. This gives M12 and velocity
W+J1+J2. Exchanging the hierarchy gives M21. This is an iterated limit,
not a simultaneous limit with an unspecified frequency ratio.

For actual finite frequencies, choose the slower N2 first, then N1
sufficiently large. Local mild stability propagates the first C0 release
error over the second, already constructed smooth interval. Its gradient
error is integrable as s^(-1/2); the same linear frame argument following
(308) propagates the frame error. Thus both final velocity and frame can
be made arbitrarily close to the stated two-stage limits, and the total
integrated strain and BKM cost are at most L1+L2 plus an arbitrarily small
positive error. Every parent was present at time zero. No intermediate
frame reset, replenishment or external force is introduced.

For the two envelopes above the original energies also agree when the
frequency assignments are interchanged: for separated large N1,N2,
||u0_(N1,N2)||_2^2=N1^2+N2^2. Individual norms agree and the cross Fourier
supports are disjoint. Energy is not bounded uniformly as the carriers
tend to infinity. At a small fixed positive time after both releases,
parabolic smoothing transfers the strict difference in (321) to actual
finite-frequency histories. Their velocities can be arbitrarily close;
no exactly equal finite-frequency velocity states are asserted.

The same iterated construction works for every prescribed FINITE number
of stages, with all packets in the original datum and with every earlier
frame retained. Its limiting matrix bound is
||M_final||_infinity<=product_j(1+||S_j||_infinity), and its total release
price is at most sum_j L_j plus an arbitrarily small error. The constants
and frequency separations may grow strongly with the number of stages.
This is not an infinite-stage NS construction, a uniform bound for all
possible descendants, or proof that arbitrary histories have this form.

The boundary response now has a concrete physical consumer: it carries
the inherited frame and hence the nonzero initial conversion value into
the next segment of the existing logarithmic/HJB formula. The remaining
problem is to pay changing geometry when later parents are GENERATED by
the fluid, rather than supplied as a prescribed finite initial hierarchy.
The arbitrary-prefix core budget (284) and regularity theorem remain open.

Run `python3 -O labs/joint_parent_boundary.py`. The exact checks cover
joint heat rates, frame covariance, all vertical return coefficients,
pressure-projected outputs, finite initial-energy fixtures and ordered
physical frame comparisons. Uniform estimates, actual finite histories
and their composition remain analytic. No Lean declarations or axioms change.

## Evolving covariance compatibility and its pressure cost

`covariance_velocity_defect.py` follows the relation between the actual
fluid and its inherited covariance after a release. The complete physical
equation has a favorable anisotropic diffusion term. A four-wave family
shows that the associated pressure-Hessian work can exceed it, even on
an actual unforced history with increasing enstrophy. Thus the signed
history estimate must retain this work and its source of payment.

The PDE identities below are analytic identities for smooth solutions.
The checker verifies independent Fourier expansions and the exact physical
fixtures. Local solution intervals and transfer from original parent data
use (313) and positive-time stability; they are not new Lean certificates.

### The full evolving relation

Let u be an actual smooth unforced periodic NS solution with nu>0. Evolve
F,M by (302), with their original initialization or an incoming compatible
state. Define

```text
Sigma=M-F F^T,   K=sum_j (partial_j F)(partial_j F)^T,
B=grad u,   d=div Sigma,
C=u+nu P d,     grad chi=(I-P)d.
```

M is symmetric positive definite and Sigma>=0. The potential chi is chosen
with zero spatial mean. It is the gradient part of the covariance divergence;
it is not an independently specified pressure or an external control.
The actual fluid pressure remains in the full Leray projection P.
The covariance equation is

```text
(partial_t+u.grad-nu Delta)Sigma=B Sigma+Sigma B^T+2nu K.         (322)
```

A useful cancellation holds before projection:

```text
div[-u.grad Sigma+B Sigma+Sigma B^T]
                      =-u.grad d+div(Sigma grad u),
[div(Sigma grad u)]_i=sum_jk partial_j(Sigma_jk partial_k u_i).
```

To verify it, differentiating transport produces
-(partial_j u_k)(partial_k Sigma_ij). The matching term from
Sigma B^T cancels it after exchanging j,k; div u=0 removes its other
term. Differentiating B Sigma gives exactly the displayed divergence-form
operator. In particular this operator includes derivatives of Sigma.

Differentiate C using BOTH actual evolution equations. The self-advection
of u cancels against the u part of d=(C-u)/nu+grad chi. The result is

```text
C_t+P[(u.grad)C]
 =nu Delta C+nu P div(Sigma grad u)
       -nu P[(u.grad)grad chi]+2nu^2 P div K.       (323)
```

No stretching term is discarded: it is part of the anisotropic diffusion
operator. The mean-frame source K generally does not vanish. The checker
uses a nonconstant F and obtains ||P div K||_2^2=1/6144, so that omission
would fail an actual chain-rule fixture. The arbitrary incoming fixture
checks the identity; it is not used as a newly realized original-frame
counterexample.

Pair (323) with u, and the NS equation with C. Ordinary incompressible
transport cancels in their sum. With normalized spatial integrals, write

```text
m=integral u.C,
D_Sigma(u)=integral sum_ijk Sigma_jk partial_j u_i partial_k u_i >=0.

m'+nu D_Sigma(u)
 =-2nu integral grad u:grad C
       -nu integral u^T Hess(chi)u-2nu^2 integral B:K.           (324)
```

This is an identity along the complete physical history, not just at its
initial time. It isolates a nonnegative diffusion payment and three
remaining terms. In particular m need not be nonnegative, so (324) is
not itself a nonnegative reserve or a continuation bound.

### What the first descendant generates

For any horizontal solenoidal trigonometric parent V, let
w=N(V)=-P[(V.grad)V] and let p_V be its canonical envelope pressure:
w=-(V.grad)V-grad p_V. At the limiting single release with no background,

```text
u(0)=alpha w,  F(0)=I,
Sigma(0)=(alpha/nu)V tensor V,  C(0)=0,
chi(0)=-(alpha/nu)p_V,                 alpha>0.
```

These are precisely the physical inherited data from carrier amplitude
2sqrt(alpha nu), not a freely selected covariance. Since grad F=0 here,
K(0)=0. The viscous parts of u_t and nu P div Sigma_t cancel in C_t.
The entire remaining first derivative is

```text
C_t(0)=alpha^2 Z_V,
Z_V=P[(V.grad)^2 w+Hess(p_V)w].                    (325)
```

Thus nonlinear feedback regenerates the compatibility error after the
parent has decayed. The directional operator is unambiguous:
(V.grad)^2 w=(V.grad)((V.grad)w), including derivatives of V.
It comes from div[(V tensor V)grad w] and div V=0.

There is an independent verification. Let h=(V.grad)w-(w.grad)V. Then
Z_V=N(w)-DN(V)[h]. Expanding the bracket cancels the self-advection of w
and leaves exactly (325), with the pressure Hessian retained. Consequently

```text
integral w.Z_V = -L_V+P_V,
L_V=||(V.grad)w||_2^2,
P_V=integral w^T Hess(p_V)w.                       (326)
```

The term -L_V is always favorable. The pressure term is signed.
The simple parent V=cos z(cos y,-cos x,0) has
L_V=5/288, P_V=0 and ||Z_V||_2^2=26221/967680.
The earlier self-stretching parent (262) has
L_V=102543095/29988, P_V=-1464301/2499, and
integral w.Z_V=-7065571/1764<0. These are positive first-return comparisons
for those geometries, but the following family reverses the sign.

### A resonant family defeats the pressure-only absorption

For k in Z3 write v_k=(-k2,k1,0)cos(k.x). Set

```text
V_rho=v_(2,1,0)+v_(1,2,0)
                         -rho v_(1,0,1)+rho v_(0,1,1).         (327)
```

It is horizontal and divergence-free, and has three-dimensional dependence
when rho!=0. At rho=0 its projected source vanishes: the two planar modes
have the same Laplacian eigenvalue. Nevertheless small additional modes
produce a pressure cost exceeding the directional diffusion. Exact Fourier
calculation gives

```text
L(rho)=rho^2(55rho^4+20482rho^2+11601)/330,
P(rho)=6rho^2(507-55rho^2)/55,
P(rho)-L(rho)=rho^2(6651-22462rho^2-55rho^4)/330.                (328)
```

For every 0<|rho|<=1/2 the last quantity is strictly positive: the bracket
is at least 16513/16. In particular, at rho=1/10,

```text
L=23611651/66000000,
P=30387/55000,
P-L=12852749/66000000>0.
```

The polynomial verification uses their degree at most six, evenness under
rho->-rho (translation z->z+pi), and vanishing to order two at rho=0.
Thus three nonzero squared parameter values determine each polynomial.
The checker evaluates them independently at rho=1,2,3, and verifies the
rho=1/10 physical source directly. No floating-point search result is
used as evidence for (328).

This disproves the universal pointwise claim P_V<=L_V for these actual
released-parent geometries. It also disproves the stronger claim that the
same term always pays pressure with a fixed fraction below one. It does
not disprove payment with an additional full-datum allowance, or a reserve
retaining C, K and their later history.

To express the comparison physically, define the instantaneous covariance
prediction v_Sigma=-nu P div Sigma=u-C. It is an observer, not another
NS solution. At the matched release,

```text
d/dt [||u||_2^2-||v_Sigma||_2^2] at t=0
                          =2alpha^3(P_V-L_V).                  (329)
```

The simple and earlier self-stretching parents initially lie below that
prediction; the resonant family initially lies above it. Also
||C(t)||_2^2=alpha^4 t^2||Z_V||_2^2+O(t^3) when Z_V!=0. A homogeneous
heat-contraction law for this error would miss its nonlinear source.

### The same unpaid pressure term in an enstrophy-growing flow

The resonant example at rho=1/10 has g(w)=-423/275000. Its positive
pressure excess alone is therefore not a claim of positive initial
vorticity stretching for u=alpha w. The actual incoming-background law
(313) provides a direct test in that regime too.

Take nu=1, alpha=10000, the SAME V=V_(1/10), and put the background
W=-2alpha w in the original datum. With carrier amplitude 2sqrt(alpha),
its limiting released state is

```text
u=-alpha w, F=I, Sigma=alpha V tensor V,
C=-2alpha w, chi=-alpha p_V.
```

The two competing terms in (324) are still alpha^3 L and alpha^3 P,
so pressure strictly exceeds the covariance diffusion. At the same time,

```text
||(-Delta)w||_2^2=13239/2500,
d/dt ||curl u||_2^2
 =2alpha^2[-alpha g(w)-||(-Delta)w||_2^2]
 =22189680000/11>0.                               (330)
```

The background was present originally and evolves by unforced NS; it is
not a later force. The other terms of (324), including its nonzero C,
remain present. Thus (330) does not assert that pressure defeats all
viscous dissipation or every possible combined reserve. It shows that
restricting attention to enstrophy-growing flow does not rescue the
specific proposed pressure absorption.

### Actual intervals, literature connection and remaining payment

For each fixed nu, alpha and parent above, local smooth NS and linear
frame existence justify the displayed time derivatives. Strict signs
persist on a small positive descendant interval. The original release
(313), followed by its positive-time smoothing argument, transfers these
signs to sufficiently large FINITE carrier frequencies with F=M=I at
original time zero. In particular the strict energy comparison from (329) occurs on
actual short histories, and the pressure excess and enstrophy growth in
(330) coexist on an actual short interval. No frame is reset at release,
and derivative convergence is not inferred from the C0 endpoint limit.

The vector transport and stress-divergence structure has a useful precedent
in [Beekie, Friedlander and Vicol, *On Moffatt's magnetic relaxation
equations*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.14084), equations (1.1)--(1.2) and
(2.1). Their Darcy constitutive law uses +P div(V tensor V), with a
magnetic-energy dissipation identity. The released velocity here uses
-P div(V tensor V), and its subsequent evolution is actual NS. Those
constitutive dynamics and their energy estimate cannot be substituted
for (322)--(324). Their framework is useful for identifying the transport
and pressure terms, with that distinction retained.

The next physical estimate must pay the pressure-Hessian work jointly
with the changing compatibility error and mean-frame diffusion work.
A signed cross-work identity alone does not supply a nonnegative finite
reserve. The ordinary-vorticity conversion, arbitrary-prefix core budget
(284), and arbitrary-data regularity remain open.

Run `python3 -O labs/covariance_velocity_defect.py`. It checks the complete
moment chain rule with nonconstant mean frame, both discrepancy equations,
the integrated cross-work identity, independent parent-source expansions,
the rational parameter family, and the enstrophy-growing background.
The physical interval arguments remain analytic. No Lean declarations
or axioms change.

## A joint reserve with the evolving memory retained

`covariance_joint_payment.py` tests the positive quadratic completion of
(324). Keeping the actual mean-frame gradient gives a constructive result:
a nonnegative reserve pays a collection of weighted derivative costs along
every available smooth periodic NS history. The weights retain the largest
frame size reached so far. Their loss of coercivity as that size grows
remains an explicit obstruction to arbitrary-data continuation.

All PDE and norm estimates here are analytic. The checker verifies the
finite Fourier identities, independent moment derivatives, exact shear
formulas and scalar absorption squares. It does not certify the general
functional-analysis estimates or turn this into a Lean regularity theorem.

### Pressure as a compensated stress

Retain all the definitions and actual evolution equations in (322)--(324).
For fixed real theta and beta>0 put

```text
q=C-theta u,
R=1/2 ||q||_2^2+beta/2 ||u||_2^2,
T=B Sigma+chi B^T+2nu K.                                  (331)
```

Both u and q are divergence-free. Since
(u.grad)grad chi=grad(u.grad chi)-B^T grad chi and
B^T grad chi=div(chi B^T), incompressibility gives the exact full equation
and quadratic balance

```text
q_t+P[(u.grad)q]=nu Delta q+nu P div T,
R'+nu ||grad q||_2^2+beta nu ||B||_2^2
                                  =-nu integral grad q:T. (332)
```

The formula includes all derivatives of the covariance and the mean frame.
In particular the pressure potential occurs without derivatives in its
integrated work. This does not assert that chi itself has a bounded
L-infinity norm in terms of Sigma.

There is a further classical cancellation. Write

```text
Q=sum_ij (partial_j u_i)(partial_i q_j),
chi=-(-Delta)^(-1) div div Sigma,
I_chi=integral chi Q
     =-integral Sigma:Hess[(-Delta)^(-1)Q].                (333)
```

For each i, grad u_i is curl-free and partial_i q is divergence-free.
Also Q has spatial mean zero. The div--curl estimate bounds its Hardy
norm by a fixed constant times ||B||_2 ||grad q||_2. The zero-mode-removed
periodic Hessian inverse Laplacian maps this Hardy space to L1. Therefore,
for a finite constant c_*>=1 fixed by the dimension and torus,

```text
|integral grad q:(B Sigma+chi B^T)|
           <=c_* ||Sigma||_(op,infinity) ||B||_2 ||grad q||_2. (334)
```

This uses Coifman--Lions--Meyer--Semmes,
[*Compensated compactness and Hardy spaces*](https://benahou.github.io/pdfs/CLMS_Compensated%20compactness%20and%20Hardy%20spaces.pdf),
Theorem II.1(2), its local version in Remark II.1 and the proof of Lemma
II.1. On the fixed torus, apply the local maximal-function proof on small
coordinate balls; larger scales are controlled by the L1 product estimate.
For the elliptic operator, its L2 bound controls an atom near its support,
and the atom's cancellation plus the kernel derivative estimate controls
its far field. The smooth periodic remainder is bounded. These give a
constant independent of the fields, time or Fourier support. This is an
analytic application of the classical estimate, not a new div--curl theorem
or a formal-library import. No numerical value of c_* is claimed.

### Mean-frame diffusion pays the gradient product

Let A bound the pointwise Frobenius norm of F on a smooth interval, and set
X=||grad q||_2, Y=||B||_2 and Z=||Delta F||_2. An elementary periodic estimate is

```text
||K||_2 <= ||grad F||_4^2 <=3 A Z.                         (335)
```

For completeness, integrate div(sum_i F_i grad F_i |grad F|^2), treating
F as a vector of nine entries. The resulting two terms bound
||grad F||_4^4 by
A (||Delta F||_2+2||Hess F||_2) ||grad F||_4^2.
Periodic integration by parts gives ||Hess F||_2=||Delta F||_2; division
when the gradient norm is positive proves (335). The zero case is immediate.
No mean-zero hypothesis on F is needed.

For E_F=1/2||grad F||_2^2, its ACTUAL equation gives

```text
E_F'=-nu Z^2+integral Delta F:(u.grad F)
                   -integral Delta F:(B F)
     <=-nu Z^2+4 A Y Z.                                  (336)
```

In the transport integral, integrate by parts: incompressibility cancels
the derivative on |grad F|^2, leaving at most Y||grad F||_4^2. The second
integral is at most A Y Z. Thus pressure and frame derivatives have not
introduced an unaccounted second derivative of u.

For fixed bounds ||Sigma||_(op,infinity)<=S and |F|<=A, set

```text
a=c_* S, gamma=72 A^2, beta=a^2+1152 A^4+1,
E=R+gamma nu^2 E_F.
```

Here A>0, as in the original-frame setting. Equations (332)--(336) imply

```text
E'+nu/2 X^2+nu Y^2+gamma nu^3/4 Z^2<=0.                  (337)
```

Indeed its upper bound, in variables x=sqrt(nu)X, y=sqrt(nu)Y,
z=nu^(3/2)Z, is
-x^2-beta y^2-gamma z^2+a xy+6A xz+4gamma A yz.
Subtracting it from the claimed negative bound leaves the three squares
(x/2-a y)^2+(x/2-6A z)^2+gamma(z/2-4A y)^2.
The estimate is conditional on the fixed bounds S,A; choosing them from
a future supremum would not supply an original-data allowance.

### A reserve valid along every smooth original-frame history

There is an exact way to keep that dependence as an observed history
variable. Start the actual moment fields at F(0)=M(0)=I and define

```text
L(t)=max(1, sup_(0<=s<=t) ||M(s)||_(op,infinity)),
b=c_*^2+10368.
```

On every compact smooth prefix L is finite, nondecreasing and absolutely
continuous. The physical inequalities 0<=Sigma<=M and FF^T<=M give S=L
and A^2=3L. Substitute gamma=216L and beta=b L^2+1 in (337), divide by L^2,
and retain the derivatives of these weights. The resulting reserve is

```text
Rbar=(||q||_2^2+||u||_2^2)/(2L^2)
                     +b/2 ||u||_2^2+108nu^2/L ||grad F||_2^2,

Rbar'+nu/(2L^2)||grad q||_2^2+nu/L^2||B||_2^2
                          +54nu^3/L||Delta F||_2^2<=0.   (338)
```

The additional derivative is exactly
-L'(||q||_2^2+||u||_2^2)/L^3-108nu^2 L'||grad F||_2^2/L^2,
which is nonpositive. This is why adaptation is legitimate here; it is not
silently treated as a constant weight. The differential inequality holds
almost everywhere and integrates over the full smooth prefix.

For example theta=1 gives q=nu P div Sigma, initially zero, and

```text
Rbar(0)=(1+b)/2 ||u0||_2^2.                               (339)
```

Thus (338) pays the displayed weighted observations from a finite original
reserve on EVERY available smooth prefix, with no future supremum inserted
in (339). Compatible concatenation retains F,M and L; at a join the running
maximum is continued, not reset to one.

The limitation is the denominator. As L increases, the observations being
paid weaken. This controls neither L itself nor ordinary vorticity. The
existing nonpositive-production result for omega^T M^(-1)omega still needs
a finite original-data bound on its conversion, for example the periodic
integral of sqrt(||M||_(op,infinity)). The core budget (284) is also still
open. A bounded normalized reserve is not arbitrary-data regularity.

### Exact physical calibration: a decaying shear with inherited memory

A solvable incoming state shows why a memory-dependent weight is natural.
Take u(t)=a exp(-nu t)sin y e1, F(0)=I and
M(0)=I+lambda e2 tensor e2, lambda>=0. This is actual unforced NS with
zero pressure and zero vortex stretching. Its evolved moments satisfy

```text
F_12=a t exp(-nu t)cos y,
Sigma_22=lambda, Sigma_12=lambda F_12,
C=(1-lambda nu t)u,  chi=0, P div K=0.                   (340)
```

The other covariance component is retained in the checker: if
h_t-nu h_yy=2(partial_y u_1)F_12 and h(0)=0, then
M_11=1+(1+lambda)h. Moreover h-F_12^2 has nonnegative source
2nu(partial_y F_12)^2, which verifies covariance positivity.

For the unnormalized R in (331), put s=nu t and z=1-theta-lambda s. Then

```text
R=1/2 [z^2+beta] exp(-2s)||u(0)||_2^2,
dR/ds=-[(z+lambda/2)^2+beta-lambda^2/4]
                                      exp(-2s)||u(0)||_2^2. (341)
```

Hence beta>=lambda^2/4 pays the entire shear history for every theta.
When lambda>0 and theta<=1+lambda/2 this threshold is also necessary.
For any fixed theta,beta, sufficiently large lambda gives a strict growth
interval. That defeats coefficients uniform over these inherited memories,
not a coefficient selected from the full original datum.

The inherited state is physically approachable without resetting frames:
use original data a sin y e1+2nu sqrt(lambda)N cos(Nz)e2 with F=M=I and
apply (313). Its endpoint tends to this shear and covariance. This original
flow is triangular: its second component solves heat, and its first solves
linear advection--diffusion by the second. The release and positive-time
stability transfer strict growth intervals from (341) to sufficiently large
finite N. The exact all-time formula (340) describes the limiting incoming
shear; it is not asserted verbatim for finite N.

For this shear M e3=e3 and omega is parallel to e3, so
omega^T M^(-1)omega=|omega|^2 even when lambda is large. Thus the
full-frame maximum can greatly overestimate the conversion actually needed
by vorticity. This distinguishes memory growth in an observation from
physical stretching.
The favorable normalization in (338) is consistent with such harmless
transients. Controlling the deformation that changes that normalization,
while retaining the actual pressure and parent history, is the next task.

Run `python3 -O labs/covariance_joint_payment.py`. It checks the stress PDE,
the integrated and adjoint pressure identities, mean-frame gradient balance,
three released parents, the growing-background fixture, both ordered
histories, exact shear moments, and all coefficient/weight derivative
identities. The equal integrated rates of the ordered pair are consistent
with its coordinate symmetry; their pointwise frame observations still
need not agree. No Lean declarations or axioms change.

## Vorticity-direction payment and the concentration obstruction

`vorticity_direction_payment.py` retains the geometric diffusion in the
classical vorticity--energy estimate of
[Qian, *An estimate for the vorticity of the Navier--Stokes equation*,
Theorem 1 and equations (11), (16)](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.1016/j.crma.2008.11.007.pdf).
That paper proves monotonicity of
`||omega||_1+||u||_2^2/(2sqrt(2)nu)` on the periodic domain. The calculation
below keeps the nonnegative terms in its argument and compares their
payment with the existing transported-frame conversion equation. It is
reuse of a classical estimate, not a claim of a new regularity theorem.

### A physical reserve without frame normalization

Let u be an actual smooth unforced solution on an available compact time
interval, `nu>0`, `B=grad u`, `S=(B+B^T)/2`, `omega=curl u`,
`r=|omega|`, and `sigma=|S|_F`. The domain is the flat periodic torus,
or R3 with finite energy, initially integrable vorticity and sufficient
smoothness for the usual local strong solution and energy identity.
On a smooth whole-space prefix, temporary bounded-gradient estimates for
the linear vorticity equation preserve its L1 integrability. Spatial
cutoffs then justify the integrations below; the resulting allowance
does not contain that temporary bound. No transfer of (338) to R3 is
being asserted here.

Fix `delta>0`, constant in space and time, and put

```text
r_delta=sqrt(r^2+delta),
A_delta=sum_j [|partial_j omega|^2/r_delta
                  -(omega.partial_j omega)^2/r_delta^3],
J_delta=(r-sqrt(2)sigma)^2/(2sqrt(2))
                  +r sigma-omega.S omega/r_delta.             (342)
```

Both costs are nonnegative. The first follows from Cauchy--Schwarz;
the second uses `|omega.S omega|<=sigma r^2` and `r<=r_delta`.
The actual curl equation, including all internally generated parents, gives

```text
(partial_t+u.grad-nu Delta)r_delta
                  =omega.S omega/r_delta-nu A_delta.
```

The pointwise identity `|B|_F^2=|S|_F^2+r^2/2` and the actual
