kinetic-energy equation give the stronger local balance

```text
rho_delta=r_delta-sqrt(delta)+|u|^2/(2sqrt(2)nu),
partial_t rho_delta
 +div[u rho_delta+p u/(sqrt(2)nu)]-nu Delta rho_delta
                                  =-nu A_delta-J_delta.       (342a)
```

Pressure is retained as a flux. The nonnegative reserve

```text
R_delta(t)=integral (r_delta-sqrt(delta))
                          +||u(t)||_2^2/(2sqrt(2)nu)
```

therefore has the exact balance

```text
R_delta' +nu integral A_delta+integral J_delta=0,
R_delta(b)+integral_a^b integral(nu A_delta+J_delta)=R_delta(a).
                                                               (343)
```

Indeed expanding the square in J_delta gives
`r^2/(2sqrt(2))+sigma^2/sqrt(2)-omega.S omega/r_delta`;
its spatial integral is `||omega||_2^2/sqrt(2)` minus the stretching
production. This cancels the kinetic part of the reserve derivative.
Every compatible segment spends the same account. There is no reset,
smallness assumption, prescribed reference flow or future supremum in
its initial allowance, which is at most

```text
R_0(0)=||omega0||_1+||u0||_2^2/(2sqrt(2)nu).
```

At a point with `r>0`, let `n=omega/r`. Direct differentiation gives

```text
A_delta= r^2/r_delta |grad n|^2
                          +delta/r_delta^3 |grad r|^2.          (344)
```

Letting delta decrease to zero in (343), Fatou's lemma yields

```text
R_0(b)+nu integral_a^b integral_{r>0} r|grad n|^2
                   +integral_a^b integral J_0 <=R_0(a),
J_0=(r-sqrt(2)sigma)^2/(2sqrt(2))+r sigma-r n.S n,
J_0=sigma^2/sqrt(2) at r=0.                                  (345)
```

Only an inequality is asserted in this limit. Diffusion concentrated at
vorticity zeros can survive in (343) without appearing in the integral
over `r>0` in (345). The paid geometric cost measures spatial variation
of direction; it is not a bound on temporal rotation or accumulated
pointwise stretching. The radial-gradient coefficient in (344) vanishes
as delta tends to zero at nonzero vorticity.

For an actual force f the right side of (343)'s differential balance is

```text
integral omega.curl f/r_delta + <u,f>/(sqrt(2)nu).              (346)
```

Thus kinetic work alone does not account for forcing in this estimate.
Its vorticity source is retained separately. No special forced
construction or its hypotheses are changed by this identity.

A full-time calibration is the exact periodic solution
`u=A exp(-nu k^2 t)(0,sin(kx),cos(kx))`, with integer `k>0`.
Its nonlinearity and pressure gradient vanish, `omega=k u`,
`r=Ak exp(-nu k^2 t)`, and `|grad n|^2=k^2`.
Using normalized spatial measure, its all-time angular cost is `Ak`;
its all-time J_0 cost is `A^2/(2sqrt(2)nu)`. Together they spend exactly
the initial reserve. Keeping the same helix stationary requires the
force `f=nu k^2 u`; the two terms in (346) then pay those costs exactly.
This forced reference is not an unforced history or a blowup example.

### An original-data bound on flux through a fixed observation boundary

The local law also describes how surrounding unforced fluid supplies a
region. Fix a smooth compactly supported cutoff `0<=psi<=1` on R3,
constant in time, with
`|grad psi|<=C1/ell` and `|Delta psi|<=C2/ell^2`, `ell>0` prescribed
from the original datum. Integration of (342a) gives

```text
R_(delta,psi)=integral psi rho_delta,
R_(delta,psi)' +integral psi(nu A_delta+J_delta)
 =integral rho_delta[u.grad psi+nu Delta psi]
                         +integral p u.grad psi/(sqrt(2)nu).   (346a)
```

These are actual transport, diffusion and pressure fluxes, not external
forcing or free inputs at the interface. A spatially constant pressure
gauge contributes zero because `div u=0`.

Their total absolute contribution on ANY smooth prefix `T<=H` has an
original-data bound. Write `E0=||u0||_2^2`, `R0=R_0(0)`, use the canonical
whole-space pressure, and let fixed constants `C_P,C_G` satisfy the
standard Riesz-transform and Sobolev interpolation estimates

```text
||p||_(3/2)<=C_P||u||_3^2,
||u||_3^3<=C_G ||u||_2^(3/2)||grad u||_2^(3/2).
```

Set

```text
F_(ell,H)=C1/ell [E0 sqrt(H/(2nu))
        +(1+2C_P)C_G/(2sqrt(2)nu)
                    E0^(3/2) H^(1/4)/(2nu)^(3/4)]
                         +nu C2 H R0/ell^2.                  (346b)
```

Then the integral from zero to T of

```text
integral [rho_delta |u.grad psi|+nu rho_delta |Delta psi|
                              +|p u.grad psi|/(sqrt(2)nu)]
```

is at most F_(ell,H). To see this, use `rho_delta<=r+|u|^2/(2sqrt(2)nu)`,
`integral r|u|<=||omega||_2||u||_2`,
`integral |p||u|<=C_P||u||_3^3`,
`integral_0^T ||omega||_2^2<=E0/(2nu)`, and Holder in time with
exponents 2 and 4/3, respectively. Finally
`R_delta(t)<=R_delta(0)<=R0` pays the cutoff diffusion term.
This bounds absolute influx and outflux, including cancellations that
would disappear from a signed net balance. Subdividing the SAME history
at compatible seams does not replenish F_(ell,H).

This is a fixed-boundary estimate, not a bound uniform as ell tends to
zero. Its transport/pressure coefficient grows as ell^(-1) and its
cutoff-diffusion coefficient as ell^(-2). A moving or shrinking boundary
also introduces `integral rho_delta partial_t psi`. Paying the complete
flux while refining the observation to a concentrating region remains
open. This is the named spatial-history obligation left by the estimate;
an incompressible exterior need not supply zero pressure work.

### What remains in directional conversion

Keep the original transported tensor `DM=BM+MB^T`, `M(0)=I`, where
`D=partial_t+u.grad-nu Delta`. Set `Q=M^(-1)`,
`e=omega.Q omega`, and
`W=sum_j |partial_j omega-(partial_j M)Q omega|_Q^2`.
The earlier metric identity gives `De=-2nu W`. For the fixed positive
regularizer delta, the exact reaction for
`k_delta=(r^2+delta)/(e+delta)` is

```text
(D-2nu grad log(e+delta).grad) k_delta=V_delta k_delta,
V_delta=2 omega.B omega/(r^2+delta)
          +2nu [W/(e+delta)-|grad omega|^2/(r^2+delta)].
```

The unregularized expression, used only as a diagnostic where `r>0`,
makes the directional terms explicit. Write
`h=n.Q n`, `a_j=partial_j log r`, and
`d_j=partial_j n-(partial_j M)Q n`. Then

```text
V_0=2 n.B n+2nu sum_j [2a_j n.Q d_j/h
                         +d_j.Q d_j/h-|partial_j n|^2].       (347)
```

The two pure `a_j^2` terms cancel, but the mixed magnitude/frame term
remains. At the original frame `M=I`, all its spatial derivatives vanish
and the entire diffusion difference cancels: `V_0=2 n.B n`.
Thus (345) does not by itself absorb the conversion reaction, even
though it pays a genuine geometric cost. The cost is also spatially
integrated, whereas conversion follows a point or an auxiliary controlled
sampling history. Bounding the relevant sampling density and the
remaining mixed frame/strain terms is a further physical obligation.
The pressure remains implicit in the actual evolution of B; taking curl
does not remove that evolution or make B freely prescribable.

The checker also evaluates (347) with the actual inherited tensors in
the simple released-parent and resonant-parent/background fixtures.
It retains the complete Fourier source and all frame gradients. At
`x=y=z=pi/4` the simple released state has `n.B n=0`,
`|grad n|^2=2`, but `W/e-|grad omega|^2/r^2=2560/121>0`.
The resonant-background fixture has both positive directional strain
and positive diffusion difference. These are reactions in (347), not
claims about a material derivative with its Laplacian discarded. These
are derivatives of the limiting released states, with their existing
analytic original-parent realization; this test does not assert an
additional uniform long-time result for them.

For a direct connection to the existing conversion consumer, fix a
smooth compact periodic prefix and put `w=u-2nu grad log(e+delta)`.
Let psi be the nonnegative backward adjoint density with prescribed
smooth terminal value of mass one:

```text
partial_t psi+div(w psi)+nu Delta psi=0.
```

The same density observes the actual quotient and the physical reserve:

```text
<psi(T),k_delta(T)>=1+integral_0^T <psi,V_delta k_delta>,
R_(delta,psi)' +<psi,nu A_delta+J_delta>
 =2nu integral rho_delta div[psi grad log(e+delta)]
                         +integral p u.grad psi/(sqrt(2)nu).   (347a)
```

This follows by integration by parts in the two actual evolution
identities. The second line is the time-dependent version of (346a);
its extra density drift is retained. The density is generally compressible
even though u is incompressible. Its mass remains one, so
`R_(delta,psi)(0)<=||rho_delta(0)||_infinity`, an initial-data resource.
There is no uniform bound here on its spatial derivatives. The following
[metric-loss calculation](#metric-loss-bellman-payment-and-the-actual-sampling-density)
bounds its concentration at positive time separation from the terminal
observation; it does not give a bound uniform as that separation vanishes.
Nor has `V_delta k_delta` been dominated by the paid costs. The two signed
terms on the right and that domination are the precise remaining
obligations for this receiver. Taking terminal densities toward point
observations requires uniform estimates; smooth-prefix duality alone
does not provide them. This auxiliary adjoint is not a force on the fluid.

### A precise concentration test on actual whole-space flows

The following refutes a proposed universal linear conversion payment
from R_0 alone. Fix positive `nu,delta,H`. Choose any `a,b>0` and the
linear divergence-free field

```text
v=(-ax-by,bx,az),
A=(v cross x)/3.
```

For a smooth radial cutoff chi equal to one on the unit ball and zero
outside the ball of radius two, `u0=curl(chi A)` is a smooth compactly
supported admissible velocity and equals v on the unit ball. Its actual
local unforced NS solution has at `(0,0)`

```text
omega=(0,0,2b),  grad omega=0,  partial_t omega=(0,0,2ab),
M=I,  partial_t M=B+B^T,
partial_t e=0,
partial_t log k_delta=8ab^2/(4b^2+delta)>0.                    (348)
```

The vorticity derivative follows by taking curl of the actual initial
NS tangent. Pressure is the global pressure of the compact initial
field, not a pressure assigned from the linear core; its curl vanishes.
Smooth local existence and the smooth tensor equation supply an actual
interval. Continuity, uniformly for regularizers in `[0,delta]` at this
nonzero-vorticity point, gives fixed `tau>0,c>0` with
`log k_eta(tau,0)>=c` for every `0<=eta<=delta`.

Scale the complete actual solution and its original frame by

```text
u_lambda(t,x)=lambda u(lambda^2 t,lambda x),
M_lambda(t,x)=M(lambda^2 t,lambda x),
t_lambda=tau/lambda^2.
```

Viscosity is unchanged. Both `||omega0,lambda||_1` and
`||u0,lambda||_2^2` are their original values divided by lambda. Hence

```text
R_0,lambda(0)=R_0(0)/lambda,
log k_delta,lambda(t_lambda,0)
                  =log k_(delta/lambda^4)(tau,0)>=c.           (349)
```

For sufficiently large lambda, `t_lambda<=H`. Therefore no finite
constant `C(nu,delta,H)` can make
`sup_(0<=t<=H, t in the smooth prefix) sup_x (log k_delta)_+
 <=C(nu,delta,H) R_0(0)` hold for all such data. The same example rules
out any replacement right side depending only on R_0 that tends to
zero with R_0. It is an actual positive-time argument, not merely an
arbitrary collection of local matrix jets.

This does not refute a full-datum allowance, a different coercive reserve,
or the sufficient time-integrated conversion criterion. In particular
the time interval in (349) shrinks with concentration, and initial
higher derivatives grow. It proves neither indefinite renewal nor
unforced blowup. It identifies the concentration information omitted
by this particular direct payment proposal.

Run `python3 -O labs/vorticity_direction_payment.py`. The checker
independently differentiates magnitude jets, retains radial and angular
terms, checks the reserve's complete slack, the full-time helical flow,
forced bill, directional frame expansion, compact-core vector potential,
actual initial curl tangent and concentration exponents. General PDE
identities, integral estimates and positive-time realization here are
analytic, not newly Lean-certified. No Lean declarations or axioms change.

## Metric-loss Bellman payment and the actual sampling density

`metric_loss_bellman.py` checks two exact transformations of the physical
conversion equation (347). They give an analytic Bellman payment for its
nonnegative transported-metric loss, and a concentration estimate for its
uncontrolled backward receiver. They do not pay the remaining ordinary
stretching or prove arbitrary-data continuation.

### Actual histories and an original-data choice

Fix positive viscosity and a smooth unforced NS solution on an available
compact time interval, on the fixed periodic domain or on R3. In the latter
case assume the bounded spatial derivatives needed for the classical
comparison and stochastic arguments on this interval. These are local
smooth-prefix hypotheses, not bounds assumed uniformly up to an unknown
singular time. Every estimate below has constants independent of the sizes
of those future derivatives. Start the actual transported tensor at the
original initial time:

```text
D=partial_t+u.grad-nu Delta,  B=grad u,
DM=BM+MB^T,  M(0)=I,  Q=M^(-1),
e=omega.Q omega,
W=sum_j |partial_j omega-(partial_j M)Q omega|_Q^2 >=0,
De=-2nu W.
```

Positive definiteness of M follows on each such prefix from its linear
matrix evolution. The metric identity is the earlier physical derivation
whose algebra is certified in `TransportedFrameMetric.production_eq`;
the complete physical and stochastic construction here remains analytic.

Write `Omega0=||omega(0)||_infinity` and choose ONCE
`delta>0`, `delta>=Omega0^2`. The choice uses the original datum, not its
future evolution. Put

```text
h=e+delta,  a=2nu W/h >=0,
w=u-2nu grad log h,
L=partial_t+w.grad-nu Delta.
Dh=-a h,  delta<=h<=delta+Omega0^2<=2delta.                  (350)
```

The lower bound uses e>=0; the upper bound is the scalar maximum principle.
Let b be the passive scalar with `Db=0`, `b(0)=h(0)`. Comparison gives
`h<=b<=2delta`. Hence the original-history ratio g satisfies

```text
g=b/h,  1<=g<=2,  g(0)=1,  Lg=a g.
D(h f)=h(Lf-a f)  for every smooth scalar f.                (351)
```

The passive scalar and M retain their original initial data at every
later join. No new fluid is chosen and no parent is removed in (350)--(351).

### A finite Bellman allowance with control cost left over

Set `F=2g-1` and `Phi=(3/4)log F`. Direct differentiation gives

```text
1<=F<=3,  Phi(0)=0,  0<=Phi<=(3/4)log 3,
LF-(4/3)a F=(2/3)a(2-g)>=0,
LPhi-(4nu/3)|grad Phi|^2-a=a(2-g)/(2F)>=0.                 (352)
```

This is an explicit supersolution, rather than a value function defined
by an unbounded supremum over unknown solutions. For a fixed endpoint
`(t,x)`, use the auxiliary backward sampling process

```text
dY_s=[-w(t-s,Y_s)+beta_s]ds+sqrt(2nu)dB_s,  Y_0=x.
```

For bounded adapted controls beta on this fixed smooth prefix, Ito's
formula and completion of a square yield, for `0<=s0<=t`,

```text
E[Phi(s0,Y_(t-s0))
   +integral_0^(t-s0) (a(t-s,Y_s)-3|beta_s|^2/(16nu)) ds]
 <=Phi(t,x)<=(3/4)log 3.                                  (353)
```

Indeed the drift of `Phi(t-s,Y_s)` is
`-LPhi+beta.grad Phi<=-a+3|beta|^2/(16nu)`. Bounded coefficients
on the fixed prefix justify the stochastic integral, with spatial
localization if needed. This proves the stated inequality for the
specified controls; no assertion about arbitrary singular controls is
needed. Conditional versions of (353) telescope along compatible
subintervals, retaining the intermediate Phi. The rightmost constant is
used for the complete history, not assigned afresh to each subinterval.

Equivalently, with beta zero, F is a supersolution for the positive
reaction `(4/3)a`, so Feynman--Kac comparison gives
`E exp[(4/3) integral_0^t a(t-s,Y_s) ds]<=F(t,x)<=3`.
The stochastic control square completion is the classical entropy-control
mechanism; see Lehec, [Representation formula for the entropy and functional
inequalities](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.3028), Section 2.4. Equations
(350)--(353) identify its specific physical coefficients here. The control
changes how histories are sampled; it is not an external force on NS.

For clarity about the remaining consumer, let

```text
k=(|omega|^2+delta)/h,  G=log k,
v=(2 omega.B omega-2nu |grad omega|^2)/(|omega|^2+delta).
Lk=(a+v)k,  LG=a+v+nu |grad G|^2,  G(0)=0.
```

The usual verification on a fixed smooth prefix represents G as the
supremum of `E integral(a+v-|beta|^2/(4nu))`. Equality follows from the
bounded feedback `beta=2nu grad G` under the stated prefix hypotheses;
the upper inequality for each competing control follows by Ito's
formula. Splitting its penalty ONCE in (353) gives

```text
G(t,x)<=(3/4)log 3
 +sup_beta E integral_0^t [v(t-s,Y_s)-|beta_s|^2/(16nu)] ds. (354)
```

Thus the entire metric-loss reaction a is paid while leaving one quarter
of the original control penalty for v. This is not a payment for v.
Removing a instead by the product gauge recovers
`D(hk)=v(hk)` with `hk=|omega|^2+delta`: precisely the ordinary
vorticity equation. This agrees with the existing
`TransportedFrameDirection.gauge_barrier_iff`; the gauge alone does not
improve that physical equation. A bound on the remaining supremum from
the full datum would be sufficient: `|omega|^2+delta<=2delta exp G`.
Such a bound on every prefix up to a prescribed horizon is still open.
The [joint history transformation](#joint-history-change-of-measure-and-velocity-payment)
below subsequently preserves the full control penalty by changing the
sampling law and retaining its correlated endpoint term. It avoids the
separate allocation in (354); that estimate remains valid but is weaker.

### The receiver is a bounded weight times a killed fluid diffusion

For the actual UNCONTROLLED adjoint in (347a), put `psi=h phi`.
Its full equation transforms exactly as follows:

```text
psi_t+div(w psi)+nu Delta psi=0
  <=> phi_t+u.grad phi+nu Delta phi=a phi.                  (355)
```

After reversing time, phi is a positive scalar density transported by
the incompressible drift `-u(t-s)`, diffused with viscosity nu, and
killed at the nonnegative rate a. Dropping that killing gives an upper
bound. If psi has a nonnegative terminal value of mass one, then phi's
terminal mass is at most `1/delta`; multiplication by `h<=2delta`
costs at most a factor two. In kernel form, the receiver from a terminal
point x is `h(s,y)/h(t,x)` times this killed incompressible kernel.
This is a comparison with the actual advected kernel, not a pointwise
comparison with a Gaussian centered at x.

For R3, Hess-Childs, Raquepas and Rowan,
[Divergence-free drifts decrease concentration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16723),
prove a sharp concentration comparison for bounded measurable,
time-dependent divergence-free drifts. Their Theorem 1.7 and Corollary
1.10 in arXiv v1 apply in particular to a point mass and give the heat
kernel's L-infinity upper bound. Applying that result to the reversed
physical drift, rescaling viscosity, and then integrating over terminal
data gives

```text
||psi(s)||_infinity <=2[4pi nu(t-s)]^(-3/2),  0<=s<t.       (356)
```

The drift may be extended by zero outside the finite interval to fit
the cited theorem. The estimate is independent of its amplitude.
The same paper's Theorem 1.14 shows that its sharp concentration comparison
fails on the torus. We do not import that claim into the periodic case.
On a fixed torus, the weaker bound
`||psi(s)||_infinity<=2 C_T[1+(nu(t-s))^(-3/2)]` suffices here.
It follows from the torus Nash inequality, the passive-scalar energy
identity `d||f||_2^2/ds=-2nu||grad f||_2^2`, and duality on two consecutive
half-intervals. For short times the Nash inequality gives the L1-to-L2
factor `(nu s)^(-3/4)`; the reversed divergence-free adjoint supplies
the L2-to-L-infinity factor. L-infinity contraction extends the estimate
to long times. All constants depend only on the fixed torus.

These are bounds for beta=0. Arbitrary sampling controls need not be
incompressible, so (356) is not asserted for the controlled laws in (354).
Nor does (356) bound spatial derivatives of psi.

One direct connection to the previous physical reserve is now available.
Under its R3 integrability hypotheses, for a fixed delay `0<epsilon<t`,

```text
integral_0^(t-epsilon) <psi(s),nu A_delta+J_delta> ds
 <=2(4pi nu epsilon)^(-3/2) R0.                            (357)
```

This follows by applying (356) to its nonnegative paid density and using
the global reserve. The periodic counterpart uses the torus constant
above. It controls the receiver's observation of the earlier history;
the coefficient diverges as epsilon tends to zero. It neither bounds
the two derivative-dependent terms in (347a) nor dominates v by the
paid geometric density. Terminal concentration and the remaining signed
strain are concrete unpaid obligations.

The same density estimate also bounds an earlier portion of the ordinary
stretching directly from kinetic energy, without requiring initial
vorticity in L1. Let `E0=||u0||_2^2`. Since psi has mass one,
`||psi(s)||_2<=sqrt(2)[4pi nu(t-s)]^(-3/4)`. Using
`v_+<=2|grad u|` and `integral_0^t ||grad u||_2^2<=E0/(2nu)` gives

```text
integral_0^(t-epsilon) <psi(s),v_+(s)> ds
 <=4(4pi nu)^(-3/4) sqrt(E0/(2nu))
                  sqrt(epsilon^(-1/2)-t^(-1/2)).           (357a)
```

Here Cauchy--Schwarz in time integrates `(t-s)^(-3/2)` exactly.
This bound diverges as epsilon^(-1/4). It controls a first moment under
the uncontrolled sampling law, not the controlled supremum in (354)
or an exponential moment of the full stretching. Thus even this direct
energy payment leaves two explicit tasks: the last time interval and
the cost of changing the sampling law.

### Physical tests and the forcing distinction

The exact unforced periodic shear `u=(A exp(-nu t)sin y,0,0)` has
`e=|omega|^2=A^2 exp(-2nu t)cos^2 y` in its original frame. Writing
`q=exp(-2nu t)` and `c=cos y`, the passive scalar is

```text
h=delta+A^2 q c^2,
b=delta+(A^2/2)[1+q^2(2c^2-1)],
b-h=(A^2/2)(1-q)[1-q(2c^2-1)]>=0,
a=2nu A^2 q(1-c^2)/h,  v=-a,  k=1.                       (358)
```

The checker differentiates this complete history, including (352),
independently. Metric loss is genuinely present, but its cancellation
with ordinary vorticity diffusion leaves the full conversion constant.

The actual periodic initial datum used earlier,
`u0=(-a0 sin x cos z-b0 sin y,b0 sin x,a0 cos x sin z)`, has
at the origin, in its original frame,

```text
metric-loss rate a=0,
ordinary reaction v=8a0 b0^2/(4b0^2+delta)>0               (359)
```

for positive a0,b0. Its whole-domain vorticity satisfies
`||omega0||_infinity^2<=4(a0^2+b0^2)`. Choosing delta equal to that
upper bound preserves (359), giving `v=2a0 b0^2/(a0^2+2b0^2)>0`.
The calculation uses the curl of the actual NS initial tangent, including
transport and viscosity, not a prescribed time evolution of u0. This
rules out pointwise absorption `v<=C a`, even with the required datum
choice. It does not rule out a full-history allowance for v.

With external force f the metric identity instead reads
`Dh=-2nu W+2 omega.Q curl f`. The extra source spoils the unforced
comparison (350) unless it is separately controlled; it also remains
in the quotient and density transformations. No payment of forced
blowup histories follows. Internally generated motion is already part
of u and B in these equations; its ordinary stretching remains in v.

Run `python3 -O labs/metric_loss_bellman.py`. Independent spatial/time
jets check both gauges, the adjoint transformation and the retained
reaction. Exact checks also cover the control square, the penalty split,
the complete shear history and the physical initial obstruction.
Comparison, Ito verification, kernel estimates and the continuation
implication here are analytic, not new Lean-certified results. The
general arbitrary-history bound remains open; no Lean declaration or
axiom changes.

## Joint history change of measure and velocity payment

`joint_history_sampling.py` checks the exact joint change behind
(350)--(354). Retaining its correlated drift, loss and endpoint removes
the need to allocate three quarters of the control cost to the metric
term. The same construction composes along a complete original history.
It also gives an explicit payment for velocity observations. Stretching,
which observes a derivative of velocity, remains an open obligation.

### The complete path law, with its loss retained

Keep the smooth-prefix hypotheses and original-data regularizer of (350).
Fix `(t,x)`. Let P_u be the law of the auxiliary diffusion

```text
dX_s=-u(t-s,X_s)ds+sqrt(2nu)dB_s,  X_0=x,
Z_s=h(t-s,X_s)/h(t,x) exp[-integral_0^s a(t-r,X_r)dr].       (360)
```

The physical identity `Dh=-a h` gives
`dZ_s=Z_s sqrt(2nu) grad log h(t-s,X_s).dB_s`.
Thus Z is a positive local martingale. Since `delta<=h<=2delta` and
`a>=0`, it satisfies `0<Z_s<=2`; it is therefore a true martingale,
with `E Z_s=1`. Change measure by Z on the fixed prefix. Its sampling
drift is `-u+2nu grad log h=-w`, exactly the receiver's drift. Denote
that law by P_w. In particular, for every nonnegative path functional J,

```text
E_(P_w) J=E_(P_u)(Z_t J)<=2 E_(P_u)J.                     (361)
```

This controls complete histories, not only their one-time marginals.
It does not assert domination of arbitrary controlled laws by P_u.
The construction is a time-dependent Doob change with killing, a
classical change-of-measure method. Compare Leonard's
[survey of the Schrodinger problem](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0215),
Sections 3--4, for logarithmic drift changes and path measures. Here
(360) derives the actual coefficients and killing from NS. No claim
that an arbitrary Schrodinger bridge evolves as NS is used.

At an intermediate physical time s0, the endpoint factors compose as
`h(0,X_t)/h(s0,X_(t-s0))` times
`h(s0,X_(t-s0))/h(t,x)`. The common h cancels and the loss integrals
add. Over any finite compatible subdivision, the result is still (360).
The factor two is for the complete history, not a factor paid per join.
The original M and regularizer are retained at every join.

For bounded potentials on the fixed prefix, (360) gives in particular

```text
E_(P_w) exp integral_0^t (a+v)
 =E_(P_u)[h(0,X_t)/h(t,x) exp integral_0^t v].             (362)
```

The nonnegative loss cancels against the SAME path's density, before
either factor is bounded. Since k(0)=1, the left side is k(t,x).
Consequently

```text
(1/2) E_(P_u) exp integral_0^t v <=k(t,x)
                         <=2 E_(P_u) exp integral_0^t v,
|log k(t,x)-log E_(P_u) exp integral_0^t v|<=log 2.        (363)
```

This avoids the fourth exponential moment sufficient in (354) and
identifies the remaining value up to a bounded endpoint term.
It does not establish that the first exponential moment on the right
has a bound uniform over all prefixes before a possible singular time.
Indeed `h k=|omega|^2+delta` gives its usual scalar Feynman--Kac
representation with initial weight `h(0)=|omega0|^2+delta`.
The physical stretching is retained, not eliminated by a gauge.

### The full control penalty survives

On one fixed smooth prefix, write `p=grad log h` and change auxiliary
controls by `gamma=beta+2nu p`. The sampling paths then have the same
drift, `-w+beta=-u+gamma`. Ito's formula gives

```text
drift[log h(t-s,X_s)]=a-nu|p|^2+gamma.p,
a+v-|beta|^2/(4nu)
 =v-|gamma|^2/(4nu)+(a-nu|p|^2+gamma.p).                  (364)
```

Thus their expected integrated costs differ exactly by
`E log h(0,X_t)-log h(t,x)`, at most log 2. The map between bounded
adapted controls is invertible on the fixed prefix because p is bounded
there. No uniform bound on that future p enters the endpoint allowance.
The entire penalty `|gamma|^2/(4nu)` is available for v under the
incompressible reference diffusion. This is an exact identity of
auxiliary sampling problems for a fixed physical flow; neither control
is an applied fluid force.

`TransportedFrameDirection.sampling_control_shift` and
`sampling_cost_shift` certify the two algebraic identities in Lean for
arbitrary vectors in a real inner-product space and nonzero nu where
division is used. The identification of the supplied log rate, stochastic
construction, Ito integration and uniform endpoint bound remain analytic.

### A controlled velocity observation paid by initial energy

There is a concrete observation which this full entropy budget can pay
on arbitrary smooth unforced histories. On R3 set `E0=||u0||_2^2`.
The energy inequality gives `||u(s)||_2<=sqrt(E0)` throughout the prefix.
For the reversed physical diffusion, the L2 case of the
[Hess-Childs--Raquepas--Rowan concentration theorem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16723)
gives the kernel bound `(8pi nu s)^(-3/4)`, uniformly in the
time-dependent incompressible drift. Cauchy--Schwarz therefore yields,
from ANY starting time and position with the interval available,

```text
E_(P_u) integral_0^tau |u(t-s,X_s)| ds <=L tau^(1/4),
L=4 sqrt(E0)(8pi nu)^(-3/4).                              (365)
```

Fix an observation coefficient c>0 and E0>0. Choose
`tau_c=(2cL)^(-4)`. On every interval of length at most tau_c,
the conditional first moment of `c integral |u|` is at most 1/2.
Ordering the n time variables and using the Markov property bounds its
n-th moment by `n! 2^(-n)`. Summing the exponential series gives a
bound of 2 on each such interval. This is the classical Khasminskii
argument, here with explicit coefficients. For `0<T<=t`, conditioning
successively over a partition of the available duration T gives

```text
log E_(P_u) exp[c integral_0^T |u(t-s,X_s)|ds]
 <=ceil(T/tau_c) log 2
 <=[1+8 c^4 E0^2 T/(pi^3 nu^3)] log 2 =: B_vel.           (366)
```

For a single short interval with `cL T^(1/4)<1`, the same series gives
the sharper bound `-log[1-cL T^(1/4)]`. If c=0 or E0=0, the velocity
reward is zero and its allowance can be zero.

Relative-entropy duality and Girsanov, on this fixed smooth prefix,
now give for every bounded adapted gamma and its controlled law

```text
E_gamma integral_0^T [c|u|-|gamma|^2/(4nu)] <=B_vel.
```

For completeness, the entropy inequality is
`E_Q J-H(Q|P_u)<=log E_(P_u)exp J`, by Jensen. The path-law relative
entropy is at most the expected drift action
`E_gamma integral |gamma|^2/(4nu)`; allowing a control's extra randomness
does not increase that path-law entropy. Together with (364), this also
pays `a+c|u|` under the metric-adjusted controls beta, with allowance
`log 2+B_vel`. It is a bound for all these controlled histories, not just
their uncontrolled mean. Conditional composition retains one physical
datum and the original energy bound throughout.

On a fixed torus replace the sharp kernel bound by
`C_T[1+(nu s)^(-3/4)]` in L2. Choose any datum-fixed tau_c>0 satisfying
`c C_T sqrt(E0)[tau_c+4nu^(-3/4)tau_c^(1/4)]<=1/2`.
The same `ceil(T/tau_c)log 2` payment follows. The whole-space constant
in (366) is not asserted on the torus.

This pays bounded-speed transport observations, for example with c
fixed by a prescribed observation length. It does not pay an observation
whose coefficient grows without control as that length shrinks. Nor
does it bound v, which contains grad u. The proof uses the energy bound
and incompressibility; a forced flow with the same kinetic-energy bound
would also satisfy this velocity payment. It therefore does not by
itself distinguish a forced stretching mechanism from unforced renewal.

### Actual tests retain the stretching obstruction

The checker independently differentiates spatial/time jets for the
density martingale and full control cost. It checks the entire shear
history (358), where `v=-a` and the joint formula gives k=1 exactly.
It also checks the simple and resonant inherited-parent fixtures with
their complete M, first and second spatial derivatives, and actual NS
vorticity tangent. No inherited frame is reset. The simple fixture's v
is negative at the selected point, while the resonant one has positive v.
The cost identity holds in both cases and at two regularizer sizes.
These are coefficient checks. A datum-sized regularizer in an actual
finite-frequency release must be chosen from its ORIGINAL vorticity,
not from the later limiting descendant; the test values do not assert
that extra uniform identification.

There is also a useful actual initial-maximum test. For the periodic
datum in (359), let a0>nu and `b0^2>=2a0^2`. Its vorticity has

```text
|omega0|^2=4a0^2 sin^2 x sin^2 z+b0^2(cos x+cos y)^2,
||omega0||_infinity^2=4b0^2,
partial_t |omega|^2(0,0)=8b0^2(a0-nu)>0.                 (367)
```

To verify the global maximum, set `r=|cos x|` and bound `|cos y|<=1`.
The difference from 4b0^2 is at least
`(1-r)[(b0^2-2a0^2)(r+3)+2a0^2(1-r)]>=0`.
Equality occurs at the origin. The last line of (367) is computed
from the actual NS curl tangent, retaining viscosity. Local smooth
existence gives a positive interval on which the value at the origin
exceeds the ORIGINAL global maximum. For example nu=1,a0=2,b0=3 gives
initial maximum squared 36 and derivative 72; delta=36 is a valid
original-data choice in (350). Thus a uniform-in-time maximum principle
for ordinary vorticity is false even in this elementary admissible case.
This is a finite burst, not indefinite renewal or a failure of a
full-datum allowance. The pressure is the actual NS pressure; only its
curl cancels from the tangent calculation.

The same example rules out paying the remaining control value merely
by replacing its reward with a fixed multiple of velocity magnitude.
For delta=4b0^2 one has `u0(0)=0` but `v(0,0)=a0>0`. Define, using
the actual reversed physical diffusion from `(T,0)`,

```text
V_v(T)=log E_(P_u) exp integral_0^T v,
V_c(T)=log E_(P_u) exp[c integral_0^T |u|].
```

For every fixed finite c>=0, local smoothness and Feynman--Kac give
`V_v(T)=a0 T+O(T^2)` but `V_c(T)=O(T^(3/2))` as T decreases to zero.
For the second estimate, on the available local interval
`|u(s,x)|<=L|x|+Cs` in a periodic lift. Gronwall in the sampling SDE
bounds its maximum displacement by
`exp(LT)[C T^2+sqrt(2nu) sup_(s<=T)|B_s|]`.
Thus the velocity integral is bounded by a constant times
`T^2+T sup_(s<=T)|B_s|`. Brownian scaling and the finite exponential
moments of its unit-time maximum give the claimed order.

Consequently `V_v(T)<=V_c(T)` fails for sufficiently small positive T,
even if c was fixed using the complete initial datum. These are actual
local NS histories, not independently assigned potentials. The failure
concerns domination without an additional initial allowance. It does
not refute a datum-paid initial burst, a reserve for later geometric
renewal, or the intended full-horizon continuation bound.

Run `python3 -O labs/joint_history_sampling.py`. Exact fixtures and
the two Lean control identities support the stated algebra. The path
change of measure, energy-based occupation estimate and positive-time
realization are analytic. The remaining continuation obligation is the
signed-stretching exponential moment in (363), or the existing signed
renewal budget; neither has been bounded for arbitrary initial data.

## Signed-reaction renewal and gradient correction

`signed_reaction_renewal.py` follows the ordinary reaction left by the
joint change of measure. The bounded test is a derivative correction:
can adding a nonnegative multiple of the vorticity-gradient cost produce
a rate whose original maximum bounds every later smooth prefix? A second
test asks whether the complete pressure and diffusion source in that
rate has a favorable sign. Both assertions below are refuted for every
fixed nonnegative coefficient. An additional finite allowance from the
full original datum is retained as an open possibility.

If the proposed maximum bound held, then v<=q_kappa would bound the
exponential moment in (363) by `exp[H max(0,sup_x q_kappa(0,x))]` on every
available prefix up to H. This is the intended continuation consumer
for the bounded test; the counterexample prevents that particular use.

The calculation reuses the material stretching-vector identity already
certified in `LocalMaterialStretching`. Related directional dynamics
appear in [Galanti--Gibbon--Heritage, *Vorticity alignment results for the
three-dimensional Euler and Navier--Stokes equations*, Section 3](https://arxiv.org/abs/chao-dyn/9709003).
That work retains pressure and viscous direction derivatives; alignment
by itself does not supply their missing history bound. The identities
below apply a fixed positive regularization to the actual scalar reward,
including its negative gradient term. They do not assert a new classical
stretching-vector identity.

### The full reaction has a diffusion-renewal term

Work on any available smooth unforced periodic prefix, or on a smooth
whole-space prefix where the displayed derivatives exist. Let

```text
D=partial_t+u.grad-nu Delta,  B=grad u,  P=Hess p,
omega=curl u,  zeta=B omega,  g=omega.zeta,
J=sum_j |partial_j omega|^2,  H=sum_jk |partial_j partial_k omega|^2,
s=|omega|^2+delta,  delta>0 fixed from the ORIGINAL datum,
v=2(g-nu J)/s,  L_s=D-2nu grad(log s).grad.
```

The pressure is always the actual NS pressure. Write

```text
A=sum_j (partial_j omega).((partial_j B)omega),
T=sum_j (partial_j omega).B(partial_j omega),
C=sum_jk B_kj (partial_j omega).(partial_k omega).
```

In these contractions B and its derivative may equivalently be replaced
by their symmetric parts. The spin derivative cancels in A because
omega is the actual curl, rather than an independent transported vector.
The complete laws are

```text
Dg=|zeta|^2-omega.P omega-2nu T-4nu A,
DJ=2(A+T-C)-2nu H,   Ds=v s,

L_s v+v^2 = [2(|zeta|^2-omega.P omega)
                -4nu(3A+2T-C)+4nu^2 H]/s.              (368)
```

The last square is positive. This does not mean that viscosity creates
vorticity: v already subtracts its gradient loss, and removing some of
that loss can increase v. For example the exact shear
`u=(2 exp(-nu t) sin y,0,0)` has no stretching anywhere. With nu=1,
delta=4, at t=0,y=pi/2 its v is -2 and its time derivative is 4.
The reward is becoming less negative. Treating every positive derivative
of this reward as geometric amplification would misidentify this example.

### What the derivative correction pays, and what remains

For fixed kappa>=0, set

```text
q_kappa=2(g+kappa nu J)/s >= v.

L_s q_kappa+v q_kappa
 = [2(|zeta|^2-omega.P omega)
      +4nu((kappa-2)A+(kappa-1)T-kappa C)
      -4kappa nu^2 H]/s.                               (369)
```

The same identity also holds for kappa=-1, when q_kappa=v.
At kappa=1 the T contraction cancels, leaving

```text
L_s q_1+v q_1
 = [2(|zeta|^2-omega.P omega)-4nu(A+C)-4nu^2 H]/s.        (370)
```

This supplies a favorable highest-derivative square without dropping
pressure or a transport commutator. It does not sign the whole source.
The operator L_s is a quotient identity, not a newly paid sampling law.
In particular, the full control cost in (363)--(365) cannot be discarded
when trying to use (370) along controlled histories.

### An actual global-maximum test for every coefficient

Take a>0 and the smooth divergence-free periodic datum

```text
u0=a(-sin x cos z-2 sin y, 2 sin x, cos x sin z),
delta=16a^2=||omega0||_infinity^2,
p0=a^2(cos 2x+cos 2z)/4-4a^2 cos x cos y.               (371)
```

The pressure has zero mean and satisfies `-Delta p0=tr(B0^2)`.
Set X=cos x,Y=cos y,Z=cos z. Then

```text
d=(1-X^2)(1-Z^2)+(X+Y)^2+4,
j=2+Z^2-Y^2-2X^2 Z^2,
h=d-2XZ(X+Y)^2,
s0=4a^2 d,  J0=4a^2 j,
q_kappa(0)=[2a XZ(X+Y)^2+2kappa nu j]/d.
```

On the entire cube `X^2,Y^2,Z^2<=1`, one has d>0 and `0<=j<=h`.
There are two explicit nonnegative certificates for h-j. With
`w=(X+Y)^2` and `t=(1-X^2)(1-Z^2)`, they are

```text
w<=1: h-j=t+(1-w)+(1-Z^2)+Y^2+2X^2 Z^2+2(1-XZ)w,
w>=1: h-j=3t+(X-Y)^2+(X-Z)^2+(2-X^2-Y^2)+2(1-XZ)(w-1).
```

Consequently, if `a>=2kappa nu`, the GLOBAL initial maximum of q_kappa
is a, attained at the origin. The complete unforced tangent
`u_t=nu Delta u-Bu-grad p` gives, at that same point,

```text
q_kappa(0,0)=a,
partial_t q_kappa(0,0)=a(a-3nu), independently of kappa. (372)
```

For every prescribed nu>0 and kappa>=0, choose
`a=(2kappa+4)nu`. Smooth local NS existence and the strict derivative in
(372) give a positive interval on which
`q_kappa(t,0)>sup_x q_kappa(0,x)`.
This refutes the proposed original-maximum bound on actual unforced
histories, not only on freely assigned coefficient jets.
The quantifiers are `for every fixed kappa, there exists a datum`.
They do not refute choosing a different coefficient from each full datum.

There is an important interpretation limit: at the origin the ordinary
longitudinal strain `alpha=g/|omega|^2` has
`alpha(0)=a, alpha_t(0)=-2nu a`. Thus its initial rate is decreasing.
The increasing ratio in (372) includes activation of the fixed
regularizer as vorticity grows. It is a valid obstruction for q_kappa,
but not an example of increasing alpha or endlessly renewed stretching.
An initial allowance beyond the original maximum remains possible.

`MettapediaNS.SignedReactionRenewal` certifies six scalar results:
positivity of d, nonnegativity of j, j<=h, the whole-domain upper bound,
its attained value, and admissible parameters with positive stated rate.
Those Lean statements do not identify the polynomial with an NS field
or construct its subsequent evolution. Those steps remain analytic.

### A separate test creates genuine longitudinal strain

To distinguish physical pressure renewal from that normalization effect,
use the two opposing cellular strains in

```text
u0=a(-sin x cos z-2 sin y,
      2 sin x+sin y cos z,
      (cos x-cos y) sin z),
delta=16a^2=||omega0||_infinity^2,
p0=a^2(cos 2x+cos 2y+2cos 2z)/4
      -a^2 cos x cos y(9/2+cos 2z/6).                  (373)
```

The canonical pressure again satisfies its complete Poisson equation.
The initial vorticity maximum follows from

```text
|omega0|^2/(4a^2)=(2-X^2-Y^2)(1-Z^2)+(X+Y)^2,
4-|omega0|^2/(4a^2)=2(1-XY)+(2-X^2-Y^2)Z^2>=0.
```

At the origin, u0=zeta0=grad omega0=0, while omega0=4a e_z and
`P_zz=-4a^2/3`. The complete NS tangent gives

```text
alpha(0,0)=q_kappa(0,0)=0,
alpha_t(0,0)=(q_kappa)_t(0,0)=4a^2/3>0,
partial_t |omega|^2(0,0)=-32nu a^2,
(L_s q_kappa+v q_kappa)(0,0)=4a^2/3-3kappa nu^2.
```

Thus longitudinal strain is genuinely created by the fluid's internal
pressure even while its vorticity initially decays there. For any fixed
kappa the last expression is positive at large enough a; the proposed
nonpositive source in (369), even just where q_kappa>=0, is false.
Local smoothness yields a positive interval of positive alpha and
q_kappa at this receiver. It neither repeats the construction along
one history nor supplies an arbitrarily long renewal mechanism.

### Checks and remaining payment

The checker uses independently differentiated quotient, time and
spatial jets, rather than substituting only the proposed evolution law.
It keeps the canonical pressure, every Fourier convolution output and
the curl of the full NS velocity tangent. Fixtures include (371),
(373), the exact shear and both inherited parent velocities from (362).
The inherited tests use delta=10^12 as a coefficient check; this value
is not asserted to dominate the original finite-frequency release's
vorticity. Both explicit initial-data families use their true original
maximum. No frame or parent history is restarted.

Run `python3 -O labs/signed_reaction_renewal.py`. The scalar certificates
are Lean-checked, and the symbolic and exact Fourier checks pass. General
PDE identities, local existence and the positive-time implications are
analytic. This step pays no arbitrary-data continuation estimate.
It identifies the pressure and mixed-gradient work that a history
reserve must accommodate after the favorable correction in (370),
and rules out that correction's proposed original-maximum principle. The full
initial datum can still pay both finite bursts; control of repeated
renewal, using that same datum throughout, remains open.

## Passive-parent gradient payment and the pressure-impulse remainder

`passive_parent_bellman.py` supplies a positive payment for a derivative
channel, using the original passive parent already constructed analytically
in the pressure-impulse section. The bound holds on every available smooth
prefix; it does not assume a perturbative regime or a bound for the future
fluid gradient. It leaves a precise signed pressure-impulse history open.

### One bounded original parent on the actual fluid history

Let u be a smooth unforced NS evolution on an available finite prefix,
with positive viscosity nu, in the whole-space or periodic setting.
Use the lane's smooth class, with bounded spatial derivatives on each
compact smooth prefix, and choose a finite constant `M>0` such that
`||u0||_infinity<=M`. Retain the ORIGINAL componentwise passive field

```text
D=partial_t+u.grad-nu Delta,
D H=0,  H(0)=u0,
I=H-u,  D I=grad p,  I(0)=0,
B_H=grad H,  A=grad I,  B=grad u=B_H-A,
D B_H=-B_H B,  D A=P-AB,  P=Hess p.                    (374)
```

This H is a passive vector, not a divergence-free replacement velocity
or the stochastic Weber covector. Its construction uses the actual u
as drift. Classical linear parabolic existence, or the reversed diffusion
representation, gives H on each smooth prefix; comparison gives
`|H|<=M`. The future coefficient bounds used for that construction are
not part of the payment constant. The physical gradient laws and impulse
decomposition are already certified, with their stated hypotheses, in
`CovectorParentHistory` and `PressureImpulseHistory`.

For a fixed cost share theta>0, use the bounded potential

```text
Phi=theta (M^2-|H|^2)/(4M^2),        0<=Phi<=theta/4,
G=|grad H|_F^2,
D Phi=theta nu G/(2M^2),
grad Phi=-theta (grad H)^T H/(2M^2).                   (375)
```

For every sampling control gamma, completing all spatial squares gives

```text
D Phi-gamma.grad Phi+theta|gamma|^2/(4nu)
                      -theta nu G/(4M^2)
 =theta nu/(4M^2) sum_j |partial_j H+gamma_j H/nu|^2
   +theta|gamma|^2/(4nu)(1-|H|^2/M^2) >=0.             (376)
```

No pressure term has been removed from u: it is retained in I. The
comparison for H and the literal scalar product rule give (375); the
nonnegative right side of (376) uses only the original magnitude bound.
`MettapediaNS.PassiveParentBellman` certifies that range, the vector square,
its resulting inequality and the following conversion for every real c,y:

```text
c y <= theta nu y^2/(4M^2)+c^2 M^2/(theta nu).
```

Its difference is
`(theta nu y-2cM^2)^2/(4M^2 theta nu)`.
The one-coordinate vector square is summed over the actual three spatial
derivatives; the componentwise control penalty becomes |gamma|^2.
The continuous PDE and stochastic assembly are analytic here.

### Controlled histories and exponential moments

For a fixed available endpoint `(t,x)` and earlier time s, sample along

```text
dX_r=[-u(t-r,X_r)+gamma_r]dr+sqrt(2nu)dW_r,
0<=r<=t-s,  X_0=x.
```

The control is bounded and adapted on the fixed smooth prefix. It changes
which fluid history is sampled, not the velocity or pressure of that
fluid. Backward Ito applied to the SAME Phi gives, for fixed c>=0,

```text
E_gamma integral_0^(t-s)
       [c|grad H|_F-theta|gamma|^2/(4nu)](t-r,X_r) dr
 <=Phi(t,x)-E_gamma Phi(s,X_(t-s))
                         +c^2 M^2(t-s)/(theta nu)
 <=theta/4+c^2 M^2(t-s)/(theta nu).                     (377)
```

For c=2 this is the announced derivative-parent payment. Coefficients
and stochastic integrands are bounded on each fixed smooth prefix,
justifying the expectation step. The bound itself is uniform over all
such prefixes from the same datum. For consecutive compatible intervals,
condition on their shared state and add the first line: the intermediate
Phi terms telescope. The allowance theta/4 is charged once, and elapsed
times add. Restarting H or charging a new theta/4 at each seam would be
a different construction. Matching scalar endpoint costs alone does not
authorize joining unrelated fluid histories.

An independent exponential-moment derivation avoids needing a variational
representation theorem for this step. Set theta=1 and F=exp(Phi). From
(375)--(376),

```text
D F/F=D Phi-nu|grad Phi|^2 >=nu G/(4M^2),
1<=F<=exp(1/4).
```

Feynman--Kac comparison under the physical reversed diffusion P_u yields

```text
log E_(P_u) exp integral_s^t [nu|grad H|_F^2/(4M^2)] <=1/4,
log E_(P_u) exp integral_s^t c|grad H|_F
                                  <=1/4+c^2 M^2(t-s)/nu. (378)
```

The bounded terminal F(s) is at least one; it is not replaced by an
independent sample. These are derivative observations on actual drifting
paths, with neither a frame-coercivity factor nor an unknown gradient
norm in the allowance. They do not assert a pointwise bound for grad H.
The estimates use elementary parabolic comparison and Ito/Feynman--Kac
arguments, not a new arbitrary-data regularity theorem.

### The exact unpaid reaction and its continuation consumer

Keep the original regularizer `delta>=||omega0||_infinity^2`, delta>0,
and `s_omega=|omega|^2+delta`. The physical reaction now splits as

```text
v=v_H+r_I,
v_H=2omega.B_H omega/s_omega <=2|grad H|_F,
r_I=-2omega.A omega/s_omega-2nu|grad omega|^2/s_omega,
r_I(0)=-2nu|grad omega0|^2/s_omega(0)<=0.               (379)
```

The negative vorticity-gradient term remains in the unpaid reaction.
It is not discarded merely because the passive parent's derivative
was paid. For any theta in (0,1), Holder's inequality and (378) give

```text
log E_(P_u) exp integral_0^t v
 <=theta/4+4M^2 t/(theta nu)
       +(1-theta) log E_(P_u) exp integral_0^t r_I/(1-theta).
```

The same split in (377) spends theta of the quadratic sampling penalty
on the passive derivative, leaving the share 1-theta for r_I. The
increased exponential order belongs to this NEW pressure-impulse reward,
not to the original v. All factors are evaluated on the same physical
law; Holder's inequality does not assert independent histories.

For example choose theta=1/2 and a prescribed horizon T. If a finite
constant K, fixed from u0,nu,T, bounds

```text
log E_(P_u from (t,x)) exp[2 integral_0^t r_I] <= K
```

uniformly in x, t<=T and every available smooth prefix from u0, then
`B_T=1/8+8M^2 T/nu` and direct scalar Feynman--Kac give

```text
|omega(t,x)|^2+delta <=2delta exp(B_T+K/2),
integral_0^T ||omega(t)||_infinity dt
                  <=T sqrt(2delta) exp(B_T/2+K/4).
```

The time integral means the corresponding bound on each available
prefix, with its endpoint at most T. It would supply the existing BKM
continuation criterion. No such K is proved here. In particular, defining
K as a supremum over the unknown future would not discharge the obligation.
The derivation is analytic, not a newly certified stochastic consumer.

### Actual pressure activation and a forcing calibration

The remainder in (379) has a concrete source. Since I(0)=0, its first
gradient derivative is the ACTUAL initial pressure Hessian, `A_t(0)=P0`.
For (373) at the origin, with nu=1 and a=4, exact differentiation gives

```text
r_I(0,0)=0,   partial_t r_I(0,0)=64/3,
partial_t v_H(0,0)=0.
```

Thus the true pressure-created stretching from that example is entirely
in the unpaid channel at first order. Smooth local existence makes r_I
positive on a short actual interval. For (371) with the same a and nu,
the corresponding derivatives are `partial_t r_I=16` and
`partial_t v_H=-12`, adding to the previously checked `partial_t v=4`.
These finite activations do not refute an integrated full-datum allowance.

The passive payment also holds if u is forced; it cannot by itself
distinguish forced and unforced singularity mechanisms. With a physical
force f, the retained equations instead contain
`D I=grad p-f`, `D A=P-grad f-AB`, and the ordinary vorticity reaction
adds `2omega.curl f/s_omega`. All three changes must remain. The checker
uses a smooth manufactured calibration, the stationary shear
`u=(a sin y,0,0)`, `f=nu u`, `p=0`. Its original passive parent is
`H=(a exp(-nu t)sin y,0,0)`; the impulse source is exactly -f and the
curl-force reaction is nonzero. This is not a forced blowup construction
or a claim about internal realization of one.

### Verification and the remaining history task

The checker verifies full control squares, an exact all-time unforced
shear, the forced calibration, and two complete NS/passive time jets
for both explicit initial-data families. It also uses finite ORIGINAL
oscillatory carriers built from the simple and resonant parents, including
the resonant original background. H starts from each full carrier datum;
no descendant's state is used to reset it. Original Fourier bounds fix M
and delta before the jets are evaluated. Every convolution output and
the derivative of the actual drift are retained, together with the

Run `python3 -O labs/passive_parent_bellman.py`. The four new Lean

The next missing estimate is the pressure-impulse exponential history
bound in (379), with the full initial resource and retained parents.
Its source is constrained by actual unforced NS; it cannot be replaced
by an arbitrary control or presumed nonpositive from its zero initial
impulse. The favorable correction in (370) and the covariance reserve
(338) remain available, with their unproved conversions explicit.

## Pressure-impulse flux and the receiver's entropy

`impulse_receiver_flux.py` follows the exact remainder (379). It identifies
the spatial flux that a magnitude-only payment would omit, retains that
flux in a controlled density balance, and tests the proposed payment on
an actual unforced history. The general PDE, stochastic and interval
arguments below are analytic, with exact algebra and initial-jet checks.
No new Lean declarations or global regularity claim are made.

### The complete directional flux

Keep the SAME original passive H, pressure impulse I=H-u, positive
original-data delta, and s=|omega|^2+delta from (374)--(379). Define

```text
n=omega/sqrt(s),       W=grad omega/sqrt(s),
d=I.n,                R=Id-2n tensor n,
a=2d n,
r_I=-2n.(grad I)n-2nu|W|^2.
```

Here |n|<=1 and tr W=0, since div omega=0. The softened direction n
is generally NOT divergence free. In particular,

```text
grad n=W-n tensor(W^T n),
div n=-n.Wn,
r_I=-div a+2(RI).Wn-2nu|W|^2.                         (380)
```

Thus integration by parts changes the derivative observation into a
spatial flux and a directional gradient cost; it does not erase the
flux. R is a contraction, and is an actual reflection only when |n|=1.
All quantities remain on the same actual fluid history.

For any smooth real test function psi, set

```text
V=|n|^2 (|RI|^2+16d^2)/nu.
```

Completing the full spatial squares gives the POINTWISE identity

```text
2r_I psi^2-nu|grad psi|^2+2div(a psi^2)
 =V psi^2
  -4nu|psi W-psi (RI tensor n)/(2nu)|^2
  -nu|grad psi-4psi d n/nu|^2.                         (381)
```

The matrix norm is Frobenius. On the torus the divergence integrates
to zero. On a subregion its boundary contribution is retained with
outward normal; it cannot be dropped when joining spatial components.
Whole-space integration requires the stated terms to be integrable and
the boundary flux to vanish, for example with compactly supported psi.

Writing z=|n|^2, its magnitude bound has an exact nonnegative witness:

```text
17|I|^2-nu V
 =(1-z)(4z^2+16z+17)|I|^2
    +z(12+4z)(z|I|^2-d^2) >=0.
```

The last factor is a Gram determinant. Consequently V<=17|I|^2/nu.
The unsimplified V keeps directional information: when I.n=0 it is
|n|^2|I|^2/nu. This observation alone does not bound its future sampling.

### Actual controlled sampling and its density cost

For a fixed available smooth periodic prefix and endpoint time t, let
rho(r,y)>0 be the probability density of backward sampling with drift
`-u(t-r,y)+gamma(r,y)`, where gamma is a smooth Markov sampling control.
Use normalized torus volume and a smooth positive initial density rho0.
The fluid itself remains unforced. The density satisfies

```text
partial_r rho=nu Delta rho-div[(-u+gamma)rho],
psi=sqrt(rho),          Ent(r)=integral rho log rho,
Ent'=-4nu integral|grad psi|^2
                         +2integral psi gamma.grad psi.
```

Incompressibility cancels the actual velocity from this entropy rate.
It does not cancel the sampling control or make rho spatially uniform.
Adding half this rate to (381) and completing one further square gives

```text
integral rho[2r_I-|gamma|^2/(4nu)]+Ent'/2
 =integral rho V
  -4nu integral|psi W-psi (RI tensor n)/(2nu)|^2
  -nu integral|grad psi-4psi d n/nu|^2
  -1/(4nu) integral|psi gamma-2nu grad psi|^2.           (382)
```

The fluid fields are evaluated at (t-r,y), while rho and gamma use
(r,y). The identity retains their joint dependence. It does not replace
the receiver by an independent density or replace actual pressure by a
free fluid control. The spatial identity itself also holds in a forced
flow, but its full physical reaction includes the additional curl-force
term recorded after (379). Thus this identity alone does not distinguish
forced and unforced renewal. Integrating for 0<=r<=t and dropping only
squares gives

```text
E integral_0^t [2r_I-|gamma|^2/(4nu)]
 <=[Ent(0)-Ent(t)]/2+E integral_0^t V.                 (383)
```

On the normalized torus Ent(t)>=0. For compatible time segments the
entropy endpoints telescope, as do the potential endpoints in (377).
The original I and the incoming probability density must both be
retained. Their scalar costs alone do not authorize a new composition.

For example, if rho<=L on the whole sampling interval, the existing
passive and kinetic energy laws give ||I||_2^2<=4E0,
E0=||u0||_2^2. Then (383) is at most
`Ent(0)/2+68 L E0 t/nu`. This is a CONDITIONAL density bound; L is not
asserted to be controlled from arbitrary original fluid data.
For uncontrolled uniform sampling, rho=1 stays uniform and the sharper
direct completion of (380) gives
`integral_0^t integral 2r_I<=4E0 t/nu`. This pays a spatial average,
not its exponential moment or a pointwise continuation criterion.

Two obligations therefore remain in (383): control of the sampled V,
and a bound uniform as the initial receiver approaches a point. A
Dirac initial density has no finite Ent(0). Smooth densities of width
ell generally have entropy of order 3log(1/ell). This calculation does
not supply a uniform endpoint bound as ell tends to zero, even if the
bulk integral is finite. The analogous whole-space identity retains
both entropy endpoints when justified; there is no blanket nonnegative
lower bound for differential entropy on R3.

There is an exact relative-entropy alternative. Let q be the uncontrolled
physical sampling density with the SAME initial density and actual drift
-u, and put `h=grad log(rho/q)`, `k=grad log q`. Then
`Ent_rel=integral rho log(rho/q)` starts at zero and is nonnegative.
Its rate is `-nu integral rho|h|^2+integral rho gamma.h`. The full identity
becomes

```text
integral rho[2r_I-|gamma|^2/(4nu)]+Ent_rel'/2
 =integral rho[V+4d n.k]
  -4nu integral rho|W-(RI tensor n)/(2nu)|^2
  -nu/4 integral rho|h-8d n/nu|^2
  -1/(4nu) integral rho|gamma-nu h|^2.                 (383a)
```

Thus comparison with the physical kernel removes the common initial
entropy, but retains its score through `4(I.n)n.grad log q`. It does
not remove the concentrating receiver for free. Both laws use the same
fluid, and q is independent of the sampling control, not of u.
The identity is proved here for smooth positive initial densities; a
point-receiver conclusion needs uniform control of the complete right
side as those densities concentrate. Neither that control nor the
required passage is asserted. This identifies an alternative to paying
an infinite absolute-entropy endpoint, without hiding its replacement cost.

### Zero impulse at the receiver can coexist with positive stretching

Use the actual periodic pressure-start datum (373) with nu=1, a=4,
delta=256. It is odd under complete spatial inversion. Uniqueness of
the smooth NS solution preserves that symmetry, as does the original
passive equation. Consequently, throughout their common smooth interval,

```text
u(t,0)=H(t,0)=I(t,0)=0,
grad omega(t,0)=0,
a(t,0)=0,              V(t,0)=0,
r_I(t,0)=-div a(t,0)=(64/3)t+O(t^2)>0.               (384)
```

The vector flux vanishes at the centre, but its divergence does not.
This rules out `r_I<=C|I|^2/nu` there for any finite C, even with C
chosen from the full datum, and also rules out adding a nonnegative
multiple of |grad omega|^2/s to that right side. It does not rule out a
startup allowance, a spatially resolved reserve, or a history payment.

The actual stochastic histories give a stronger test than the pointwise
derivative. Let

```text
F(t,x)=E_(P_u from(t,x)) exp[2 integral_0^t r_I],
G_C(t,x)=E_(P_u from(t,x)) exp[(C/nu) integral_0^t |I|^2],
C>=0 fixed.
```

On the smooth periodic prefix these are classical Feynman--Kac solutions
`DF=2r_I F`, `DG_C=(C|I|^2/nu)G_C`, both initially one. The complete
initial jets at the centre give

```text
r_I(0,0)=0,       partial_t r_I(0,0)=64/3,
Delta r_I(0,0)=-3,
log F(t,0)=(55/3)t^2+O(t^3),
log G_C(t,0)=(11008 C/9)t^4+O_C(t^5).                (385)
```

The negative Laplacian contribution is included: Brownian sampling is
not frozen at the symmetry centre. For the second expansion, I(0)=0,
I_t(0)=grad p0, grad p0(0)=0, and the actual pressure Hessian is
`P0=diag(176/3,176/3,-64/3)`. Thus G_C's first three time derivatives
at the centre vanish, and its fourth is `4C|P0|^2`; taking log does
not change the displayed leading coefficient. Local smoothness gives
the stated remainders for each fixed C.

For every finite C, F(t,0)>G_C(t,0) for all sufficiently small positive
t. Therefore paying the remaining exponential moment solely from this
sampled impulse-magnitude potential fails, even when its coefficient
is selected from the original datum. The finite full-datum allowance
K in (379) remains open: these short bursts can be paid by an additional
initial reserve. Neither indefinite renewal nor blowup is constructed.

### Verification and the next physical obligation

The checker verifies the general flux identity using tr W=0 while
retaining div n, both spatial squares, and the complete entropy/control
square, including the relative-entropy kernel-score term. It independently
computes the physical and Feynman--Kac initial rates on both previous
datum families and the full original simple and
resonant carriers. Actual canonical pressure and its time derivative,
the original passive parent, and the changing velocity drift are kept.

A two-jet polynomial is also used as a nonzero-impulse spatial identity
test. It is explicitly a kinematic probe, not a claimed solution at its
evaluation parameter. Odd symmetry of the actual family uses PDE
uniqueness; finite jet checks alone do not prove symmetry for all time.
The exact all-time decaying shear has I=0 and retains only its favorable
vorticity diffusion.

Run `python3 -O labs/impulse_receiver_flux.py`. No Lean declarations
change. The positive identity gives a concrete receiver-concentration
obligation for the pressure-impulse history. To close (379), its density
and orientation costs must be paid uniformly for point receivers from
the full original fluid; neither zero initial impulse nor a magnitude
summary at a receiver provides that payment.

## Physical kernel entropy and the joint vorticity score

`kernel_score_budget.py` checks the algebra of a time-weighted payment
for the physical kernel score left in (383a). The payment holds on
arbitrary available smooth unforced prefixes, without a perturbative
restriction. It is an UNCONTROLLED first-moment estimate. The pressure
history's exponential moment in (379), and the corresponding controlled
receiver estimate, remain open. The kernel estimates, entropy limits and
positive-time PDE statements below are analytic, not Lean-certified.

### A point-source entropy balance with finite weighted cost

Fix an endpoint (t,x) in an available smooth prefix. Let q(r,y) be the
density of its physical backward diffusion

```text
dX_r=-u(t-r,X_r)dr+sqrt(2nu)dW_r,    X_0=x,
partial_r q=nu Delta q+u(t-r).grad q,
k=grad log q,       F_q(r)=integral q|k|^2,
E_q(r)=integral q log q.
```

On the torus use normalized volume; on R3 use Lebesgue measure. For
r>0 the kernel is positive and smooth. Incompressibility yields
`E_q'=-nu F_q`. First integrate on [epsilon,t], where every entropy is
finite. The bounds below imply epsilon E_q(epsilon) tends to zero, and
give the point-source identity

```text
nu integral_0^t r F_q(r)dr
 =-t E_q(t)+integral_0^t E_q(r)dr.                    (386)
```

Thus the singular initial entropy is not assigned a finite value. The
factor r removes its boundary contribution. Smooth bounded drift on
each fixed prefix justifies the kernel and integration identities; no
bound for its future derivatives enters the resulting allowances.
On R3 one may first localize and use the finite-prefix kernel tails to
remove spatial boundary terms.

On the canonical torus (R/2pi Z)^3, the fixed-domain Nash smoothing
estimate used in (356) gives, for C_T>=1 independent of the drift,

```text
||q(r)||_infinity <= C_T[1+(nu r)^(-3/2)],
0<=E_q(r)<=log[C_T(1+(nu r)^(-3/2))].
```

The finite-horizon consequence of (386) is

```text
nu integral_0^t r F_q(r)dr
 <=t{log[C_T(1+(nu t)^(-3/2))]+3/2}.
```

There is also a bound uniform in the duration of the available prefix.
Put tau=1/nu. The entropy integral before tau is at most
`[log(2C_T)+3/2]/nu`. If the prefix extends beyond tau, then
`||q(tau)-1||_2^2<=2C_T-1`. Incompressibility, scalar L2 dissipation
and the torus Poincare constant 1 give

```text
E_q(r)<=||q(r)-1||_2^2
       <=(2C_T-1)exp[-2nu(r-tau)],     r>=tau.
```

The first inequality follows from log q<=q-1. Integrating this tail
and dropping only the nonpositive term -t E_q(t) in (386) proves

```text
integral_0^t r F_q(r)dr
 <=[log(2C_T)+C_T+1]/nu^2 =: R_T.                   (387)
```

For t<tau use the truncated early integral. No extension of the fluid
beyond its smooth prefix is assumed. This bound holds for arbitrary
smooth incompressible drifts, including those supplied by forced flows;
it is not itself a mechanism distinguishing unforced renewal.

### Whole-space payment from original energy and displacement

For R3 let E0=||u0||_2^2. Reuse (365) and the
[Hess-Childs--Raquepas--Rowan concentration theorem, Corollary 1.10](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.16723v1).
After rescaling its unit diffusivity, the L-infinity and entropy
comparisons with a point-source heat kernel give

```text
||q(r)||_infinity<=(4pi nu r)^(-3/2),
E_q(r)<=-(3/2)[1+log(4pi nu r)].
```

The entropy comparison has this sign because E_q is negative Shannon
entropy. The sharp Euclidean bounds are not asserted on the torus.
The original energy inequality and (365) bound the first displacement:

```text
E|X_r-x|<=B(r):=sqrt(6nu r)+L r^(1/4),
L=4sqrt(E0)(8pi nu)^(-3/4).
```

Indeed Brownian motion contributes at most sqrt(6nu r), and the
integrated drift magnitude at most L r^(1/4). Compare q with the
normalized radial density
`g_r(y)=exp(-|y-x|/B(r))/(8pi B(r)^3)`. Nonnegativity of relative
entropy and the displacement bound yield

```text
E_q(r)>=-log(8pi B(r)^3)-1.
```

These upper and lower bounds justify both integrability of E_q near
zero and the vanishing boundary term in (386). Since the integral of
the sharp entropy upper bound is `-(3/2)t log(4pi nu t)`, (386) gives

```text
integral_0^t r F_q(r)dr
 <=(t/nu){log[8pi B(t)^3/(4pi nu t)^(3/2)]+1}
 =: R_R(t).                                         (388)
```

This is finite, explicit in E0,nu,t, and uniform in the endpoint and
the available prefix. Its limit at t=0 is zero. Taking its maximum
on a prescribed finite interval uses only this explicit function of
the original data, not a supremum over the unknown future solution.
Using only the L-infinity kernel bound instead of the sharper entropy
comparison would give the weaker additive constant 5/2 in (388).

### The pressure-score observation that this payment controls

Keep the original H and I=H-u from (374), and n,d,R,V from (380)--(383a).
The passive and kinetic energy laws give ||I(s)||_2^2<=4E0. Write
K_infinity(r) for the appropriate kernel upper bound and put

```text
A(t)=integral_0^t r K_infinity(r)dr
    =2(4pi nu)^(-3/2)sqrt(t)                    on R3,
    =C_T[t^2/2+2nu^(-3/2)sqrt(t)]              on T3.
```

All fluid fields in the following expectations are evaluated at
(t-r,X_r), on the SAME uncontrolled diffusion. With R(t)=R_R(t) or
R_T as appropriate, Cauchy--Schwarz and |n|<=1 give

```text
E_(P_u) integral_0^t r V dr <=68E0 A(t)/nu,
E_(P_u) integral_0^t r |4(I.n)n.k|dr
                         <=8sqrt(E0 A(t)R(t)).      (389)
```

For the second inequality, apply Cauchy--Schwarz to r q dr dy,
using `integral r E|I|^2<=4E0 A(t)` and (387) or (388).
This pays the absolute weighted first moment of both observations
remaining in (383a), even for a point initial receiver. It does not
pay their unweighted controlled expectations under rho. A bound under
q cannot simply be substituted into an integral under rho, nor does
a first-moment bound establish the exponential estimate (379).

Time weighting suppresses the short sampling interval closest to the
observation endpoint. Removing that weight needs additional structure.
The existing delayed whole-reaction first moment (357a) remains a
different paid observation; (389) is not a stronger continuation theorem.
Composition must retain the original passive field, incoming kernel
density and elapsed sampling time. Restarting the kernel or the weight
at every seam would change the observation being bounded.

### Fisher information can increase in an exact unforced shear

For any smooth positive initial receiver, direct differentiation gives

```text
F_q'=-2nu integral q|Hess log q|^2
                         +2integral q k.(grad u)k. (390)
```

In the notation of (392), its local balance is
`L|k|^2-(4nu/q)div(q Kk)=2k.(grad u)k-2nu|K|^2`;
integration removes precisely this spatial flux on the torus.

Thus decreasing entropy does not require decreasing Fisher information.
This failure occurs in an exact unforced periodic solution, not just
an arbitrary manufactured drift. Take

```text
u(s,y)=160nu exp(-nu s)sin(y_2)e_1,   p=0,
t=log(2)/nu,
phi=cos(y_1+y_3)+cos(y_1+y_2+y_3),
q(0,y)=exp(epsilon phi)/Z,           epsilon=1/100.
```

Here Z is the normalized-volume integral. The fluid has nonzero
viscosity, finite initial energy and no force. Its self-transport is
zero; its original passive field equals u and I=0 for all time.
At the endpoint u(t)=80nu sin(y_2)e_1. Uniform spatial averages are

```text
average[2cos(y_2)phi_1 phi_2]=1/2,
average[2|Hess phi|^2]=13.
```

Since |phi|<=2, `|q(0)-1|<=exp(1/25)-1<=1/24`.
For a shear amplitude A the absolute integrand in (390), after
dividing by epsilon^2, is at most 4A+50nu: use |phi_1|<=2,
|phi_2|<=1 and |Hess phi|<=5. Consequently

```text
F_q'(0)>=nu epsilon^2[40-13-370/24]
         =(139/12)nu epsilon^2>0.                  (391)
```

Smoothness gives a positive interval of increasing Fisher information.
The receiver is genuinely three-dimensional while the exact fluid
calibration is planar. This tests smooth-receiver monotonicity; it
does not refute a separate claim restricted to point-source kernels.
Although the sampler develops finer structure, the pressure-score
coupling in (383a) is zero here because I=0. A scalar score bound alone
therefore loses useful information about its actual fluid partner.

### A joint vorticity-score law cancels explicit strain

Let w(r,y)=omega(t-r,y), G=grad w, K=Hess log q, and c=w.k. Set
`L=partial_r-u.grad+nu Delta`, the backward-sampling generator acting
on time-dependent observations. For the actual unforced vorticity
equation and the uncontrolled density equation,

```text
Lw=-(grad u)w,
Lk=2nu Delta k+2nu Kk+(grad u)^T k,
Lc=2nu[w.Delta k+w.Kk+G:K].
```

The vector and covector deformation terms cancel. Retaining the full
diffusion product and spatial flux yields the local identity

```text
L(c^2)-(4nu/q)div(q c K w)
              =2nu[|G^T k|^2-|K w|^2].             (392)
```

For a smooth positive receiver on the whole torus, integration gives

```text
d/dr integral q(w.k)^2
      =2nu integral q[|(grad w)^T k|^2-|K w|^2].    (393)
```

The same identity holds for positive r along a point-source kernel;
no finite value for its directional cost at r=0 is asserted. Spatial
subregions retain the flux in (392). Whole-space integration additionally
requires integrability and vanishing boundary flux. This is a signed
identity, not a monotonicity theorem: the positive geometric derivative
term remains. An applied fluid force would also add
`-2integral q c(curl f).k` to (393), since w uses reversed physical time.

The checker uses the actual NS time derivative with canonical pressure
on the original pressure-start, vorticity-maximum, simple-carrier and
resonant-carrier data. All Fourier outputs are retained. It verifies
the local strain cancellation and complete flux identity at their
stated receivers. The simple-carrier fixture has strictly positive
`|(grad w)^T k|^2` and zero `|K w|^2` there, so simply discarding the
positive local term is not justified. This pointwise test makes no
claim about the sign of its whole-domain integral.

The directional equation supplies a concrete next obligation for
(383a): its vorticity direction and kernel score must be kept joint,
with the derivative of the normalization and the impulse included.
Replacing w by n or q by a controlled rho introduces further terms;
neither replacement is covered silently by (392). A payment for the
resulting controlled pressure history must still be uniform at the
point receiver and use a finite allowance from the full original datum.

### Verification scope

Run `python3 -O labs/kernel_score_budget.py`. The checker includes
the heat-kernel entropy identity, a positive periodic heat density,
the radial reference normalization, the budget constants, the exact
unforced shear and its strict Fisher-production margin, and four
complete actual-NS initial-jet fixtures for (392). Their prescribed
smooth receiver is not presented as a numerically evolved point kernel.
The kernel comparisons, entropy limit, positive-time shear statement,
and all general PDE inequalities are analytic. No Lean declarations or
axioms change, and no arbitrary-data continuation estimate is claimed.

## Normalized pressure-score histories and the point-kernel endpoint

`normalized_score_history.py` checks the normalized version of (392)
and the mixed pressure-score equation needed by (383a). Their full
controlled-density identity retains the spatial flux. An exact unforced
shear then tests a family of positive quadratic Bellman certificates
using its ACTUAL point-source sampling kernel. The family fails a
pointwise bounded-source test; this does not rule out integrated reserves
which retain the density and flux. The general PDE and kernel statements
here are analytic, with exact algebra and initial-jet checks, not new
Lean proofs. The arbitrary-data history estimate remains open.

### Normalization retains the physical growth rate

Fix an available smooth unforced prefix and its endpoint (t,x). Retain
the original passive H and impulse I=H-u. All fluid fields below are
evaluated at physical time t-r; q is the uncontrolled sampling density.
Use positive r for a point initial receiver, or a smooth positive initial
density. Define

```text
B=grad u,    A=grad I,    p_1=grad p,
s=|omega|^2+delta,       n=omega/sqrt(s),
W=grad omega/sqrt(s),   j=W^T n,
N=grad n=W-n tensor j, R=Id-2n tensor n,
k=grad log q,          K=Hess log q,
z=n.k,                d=I.n,
v=2n.Bn-2nu|W|^2,     chi=v/2+nu|j|^2,
L=partial_r-u.grad+nu Delta.
```

Here delta is the same positive original-data regularizer throughout.
The original equations, including pressure, give

```text
LI=-p_1,
Ln=-Bn+chi n-2nu N j,
Lk=2nu Delta k+2nu Kk+B^T k,
Lz=chi z-2nu k.Nj+2nu[n.Delta k+n.Kk+N:K].          (394)
```

The B terms still cancel in the scalar pairing. Unlike the unnormalized
pairing, normalization introduces chi and its complete diffusion terms.
In particular, v is the full normalized vorticity-growth rate already
split as v_H+r_I in (374). It is not a newly bounded coefficient.
Completing the geometric square gives

```text
L(z^2)-(4nu/q)div(q z K n)
 =v z^2+2nu|W^T Rk|^2-2nu|K n|^2 =: T_z.           (395)
```

For example, with an uncontrolled smooth periodic receiver,
`d/dr integral q z^2=integral q T_z`. The positive geometric term
and the signed growth factor are both retained. Neither may be erased
by invoking the unnormalized cancellation (392).

### Mixed pressure work and the complete controlled identity

Set `g_d=grad d=A^T n+N^T I` and `g_z=grad z=N^T k+K n`. Then

```text
Ld=-n.p_1-I.Bn+chi d-2nu I.Nj+2nu A:N,
L(dz)-(2nu/q)div(q d K n)=M_dz,
M_dz=2chi dz-2nu d k.Nj
     +z[-n.p_1-I.Bn-2nu I.Nj+2nu A:N]
     +2nu g_d.(N^T k).                              (396)
```

Thus actual pressure work, parent deformation and normalization remain
in the mixed term. In the initial-jet fixtures I=A=0 because the passive
field starts from the ORIGINAL u0; the mixed rate then includes
`-z n.grad p0`. The general formula retains nonzero inherited I and A.

For real constants alpha>=beta^2 define the candidate

```text
Q=|I|^2/nu+2beta dz+alpha nu z^2,
P(r,y)=r Q(r,y).
```

It is nonnegative, since

```text
Q=(|I|^2-d^2)/nu
   +(d/sqrt(nu)+beta sqrt(nu)z)^2
   +(alpha-beta^2)nu z^2 >=0.                       (397)
```

The first term is nonnegative because |n|<=1. Positivity alone is not
a payment theorem. Define the remaining source and flux explicitly:

```text
B_Q=-2I.p_1/nu+2|A|^2+2beta M_dz+alpha nu T_z,
F_Q=(4beta nu d+4alpha nu^2 z)K n,
LQ=B_Q+(1/q)div(q F_Q),
grad Q=2A^T I/nu+2beta(d g_z+z g_d)+2alpha nu z g_z.
```

Let rho be the density of sampling with drift -u+gamma in the SAME
fluid and let h=grad log(rho/q). For smooth positive periodic densities,
integration by parts yields the complete identity

```text
d/dr integral rho P
 =integral rho[Q+r(B_Q+gamma.grad Q-h.F_Q)].        (398)
```

Indeed `integral (rho/q)div(q F_Q)=-integral rho h.F_Q` on the
whole torus. A spatial subregion also retains its boundary integral.
This is exactly the relative-density gradient appearing in (383a),
not an independent free variable. Setting h=0 while retaining a general
controlled rho is invalid. Whole-space integration needs its own
integrability and vanishing-boundary hypotheses.

Equation (398) provides the complete terms that a density-integrated
reserve would have to combine with the three negative squares in
(383a). No sign or datum-fixed bound for its remaining source is
asserted. In particular, it is not a continuation theorem.

### An actual kernel defeats the pointwise quadratic certificate

A possible stronger route would seek finite coefficients C_0,C_H,C_u,
fixed from the original datum, viscosity and horizon, such that

```text
2r_I+LP+(nu/theta)|grad P|^2
 <=C_0+C_H|grad H|+C_u|u|,       0<theta<=1,        (399)
```

uniformly in positive sampling age and position. Completing the control
square shows that the left side is the supremum of
`2r_I+L_gamma P-theta|gamma|^2/(4nu)`, where
`L_gamma=L+gamma.grad`. A successful closure would reserve a positive
share of the original action to pay the right-side observations using
(366) and (377). The following obstruction already holds with theta=1,
the most generous allocation to P, and hence also for every smaller
positive theta.

For ANY nu>0 use the exact periodic unforced solution

```text
u(s,x,y,z)=2exp(-nu s)sin(y)e_x,   p=0,
```
