```text
H=u, I=0, delta=4,              t=log(2)/nu,
X_0=(0,0,0).
```

Its pressure impulse is zero everywhere and for all time. The fluid's
z drift is zero and its other components are independent of z. Thus
the actual reversed diffusion has density
`q(r,x,y,z)=q_xy(r,x,y) p_nu(r,z)`, where p_nu is the one-dimensional
periodic heat kernel. This is an exact factorization of the physical
sampler, not a replacement by an arbitrary smooth receiver.

Write `k_z=partial_z log p_nu` and
`kappa(r)=partial_zz log p_nu(r,0)`. The vorticity points in the
z direction, with

```text
n_z(r,y)=-exp(nu r)cos(y)/sqrt(exp(2nu r)cos(y)^2+4),
a(r):=n_z(r,0)^2=exp(2nu r)/(exp(2nu r)+4).
```

Every member of (397) with alpha>0, regardless of beta, becomes
`P=alpha nu r n_z^2 k_z^2`. Evenness of the heat kernel gives k_z(r,0)=0.
At the centre, P, its time derivative and its spatial gradient vanish,
and r_I=0 because grad omega=0 there. Its z Laplacian remains positive:

```text
[2r_I+LP+(nu/theta)|grad P|^2](r,0)
 =2alpha nu^2 r a(r) kappa(r)^2.                   (400)
```

The periodized Gaussian formula for the normalized-volume heat kernel is

```text
p_nu(r,z)=2pi/sqrt(4pi nu r)
                sum_(m in Z) exp[-(z-2pi m)^2/(4nu r)].
```

The series and its derivatives converge for r>0. It solves the periodic
heat equation, has mass one and tends to the unit point mass. At z=0,
with b=pi^2/(nu r), differentiation gives

```text
kappa(r)=-1/(2nu r)
 +pi^2/(nu^2 r^2)
       [sum m^2 exp(-b m^2)]/[sum exp(-b m^2)].
```

For b>=8 the quotient is at most `2h(1+h)/(1-h)^3`, h=exp(-b).
Indeed m^2>=m for integers m>=1 and
`sum_(m>=1) m^2 h^m=h(1+h)/(1-h)^3`. The elementary bounds
`h<=1/256`, `b h<=1/32` and `(1+h)/(1-h)^3<2` give
`b` times that quotient at most 1/8. In particular
`|kappa(r)|>=1/(4nu r)`. Since a(r)>=1/5, (400) implies

```text
[2r_I+LP+(nu/theta)|grad P|^2](r,0)>=alpha/(40r),
0<r<min(t,pi^2/(8nu)),
lim_(r->0) r[2r_I+LP+(nu/theta)|grad P|^2](r,0)
                                                    =alpha/10. (401)
```

The right side of (399) stays bounded: u=0 at the centre and
|grad H|=exp(nu r)<=2 for r<t. Hence no finite C_0,C_H,C_u make
(399) hold for this fixed smooth unforced datum when alpha>0, even if
all coefficients are chosen from that full datum. If alpha=0,
positivity forces beta=0 and the candidate contains no score term.
Allowing coefficients to vary with the sampling age is a different
candidate and requires their full derivative cost.

This failure is an endpoint defect of the certificate, not fluid blowup
or a counterexample to the integrated full-datum allowance. It occurs
even before using a nonzero control. The spatial flux in (395) is
essential: at the centre it outweighs the negative geometric square,
whereas its whole-domain q-weighted integral vanishes.

There is also a nonzero stochastic entrance cost. Independence of the
z component gives
`E P=alpha nu r E[n_z(r,Y_r)^2] integral p_nu k_z^2`.
The same periodized Gaussian formula gives
`r integral p_nu k_z^2 ->1/(2nu)`, while boundedness and continuity
give `E n_z^2 ->1/5`. Therefore `E P ->alpha/10` as r tends to zero.
Its pointwise value along the centre line is always zero. One cannot
replace the stochastic entrance value by that centre-line value, or
argue that multiplication by r makes every singular term vanish.

### The same shear has a positive controlled terminal payment

The failed pointwise certificate does not prevent paying this candidate
by a complete history argument. For this exact shear, the original
delta=4 and |omega|<=2 give |n|^2<=1/2 for all physical time. The
periodic heat score has a useful exact representation. If Z is a real
Gaussian with variance 2nu r and its reduction modulo 2pi is z, then

```text
k_z(r,z)=-E[Z | Z modulo 2pi=z]/(2nu r).
```

This follows directly by differentiating the periodized Gaussian sum.
Let G=Z/sqrt(2nu r), a standard Gaussian. For 0<alpha<2theta,
conditional Jensen applied to the convex function
`a -> exp[alpha a^2/(4theta)]` gives

```text
E_(P_u) exp[P(r,X_r)/theta]
 <=E exp[alpha G^2/(4theta)]
 =(1-alpha/(2theta))^(-1/2).                         (402)
```

The inequality first uses P<=alpha nu r k_z^2/2. Integrating the
conditional expectation restores the original Gaussian law. The other
fluid coordinates need no independence assumption beyond the exact
heat marginal already established. This estimate is uniform in positive
sampling duration and in the observation endpoint for the same shear;
it does not involve a future derivative norm.

Now let gamma be any bounded adapted sampling control, and retain the
same uncontrolled q in P. The relative-entropy argument in (366), with
the control share theta, turns (402) into

```text
E_gamma P(r,X_r)
 -theta E_gamma integral_0^r |gamma|^2/(4nu)
 <=-(theta/2)log[1-alpha/(2theta)].                  (403)
```

In particular, alpha=theta=1/2 pays the terminal quadratic by
`log(2)/4` while retaining half the original sampling penalty for other
observations. The coefficient beta can be any value allowed by (397),
since the actual impulse I is zero here. This is a payment for all
these controlled samplers on an actual unforced flow, not just an
uncontrolled average or a fitted receiver.

The auxiliary control changes the sampling law, not the fluid equation.
The kernel in the terminal functional remains the original physical
kernel; it is not replaced by the controlled density. Compatible
segments keep their incoming density, the original elapsed time and
the same q. Equation (403) supplies one allowance for the whole sampling
history, not a fresh allowance at every seam.

This is an exact calibration of the candidate's endpoint, not a bound
for the pressure reaction on arbitrary flows. In this shear r_I is
already nonpositive. The Gaussian conditional-score argument does not
identify the score of a general NS kernel. The latter would require
additional information about the evolving stochastic deformation.
Thus (403) repairs the endpoint accounting in the test where (399)
fails, while leaving the general mixed pressure history open.

### Verification and the remaining physical obligation

Run `python3 -O labs/normalized_score_history.py`. General symbolic
checks cover (395)--(398)'s product/flux algebra, positivity (397) and
the exact Bellman control square for every positive theta. Four actual
NS initial-jet fixtures independently compute normalization from the
literal vorticity and its time derivative, retaining canonical pressure
and all Fourier products. They use prescribed smooth receivers and are
not described as point-source kernels. The analytic shear example uses
the actual point-source kernel and needs no perturbative approximation.
Its kernel factorization, image-tail bound, stochastic entrance limit,
impossibility argument and controlled terminal payment remain analytic;
the constants and Gaussian moment have exact checks. No Lean
declarations or axioms change.

The next estimate must use the full density/flux identity (398), or a
different reserve with a justified point-source entrance law. It must
retain the normalized growth, actual pressure and inherited impulse,
and pay its controlled history from the original data. The weighted
uncontrolled payment (389) remains valid and is not promoted to this
stronger claim. The sufficient exponential target (379) remains open.

## Compatible score controls and stochastic pressure history

`score_compatibility.py` checks the algebra in this continuation of
(383a) and (394)--(403). The setting is a smooth unforced NS prefix on
R3 or the fixed flat torus, with positive viscosity and bounded spatial
derivatives on that prefix. H and I retain their original construction
(374); they are never restarted. Stochastic and PDE conclusions below
are analytic.

### The combined reserve and compatible density gradients

Fix a physical endpoint `(t,x)` and sampling age r. Let q be the actual
point-source density of drift `-u(t-r)`, and rho the density with added
sampling drift gamma. For r>0 retain

```text
k=grad log q, K=Hess log q, h=grad log(rho/q),
n=omega/sqrt(|omega|^2+delta), W=grad omega/sqrt(|omega|^2+delta),
R=Id-2nn^T, d=I.n, z=n.k, b=8dn/nu,
V=|n|^2(|RI|^2+16d^2)/nu,
Q=|I|^2/nu+2beta dz+alpha nu z^2, P=rQ,
J(r)=(1/2)Ent(rho|q)+E_rho P,
alpha>=beta^2, delta>0 fixed from the original datum.
```

Q and J are nonnegative. Set `D_Q=grad Q` and keep the full flux
`F_Q=(4beta nu d+4alpha nu^2 z)K n` and bulk `B_Q` from (398).
On the torus, for smooth bounded Markov sampling controls, combining
(383a) and (398) and completing the squares gives

```text
h_* = b+(2r/nu)(nu D_Q-F_Q),
C = V+4dz+Q+r B_Q+nu r^2|D_Q|^2
               +(r^2/nu)|nu D_Q-F_Q|^2+r b.(nu D_Q-F_Q),

E_rho[2r_I-|gamma|^2/(4nu)]+J'(r)
 =E_rho[C-4nu|W-(RI tensor n)/(2nu)|^2
            -(nu/4)|h-h_*|^2
            -|gamma-nu h-2nu r D_Q|^2/(4nu)].          (404)
```

r_I is the reaction in (378); r without a subscript is sampling age.
The control penalty occurs once. On R3, entropy and flux integrability
are additionally required to discard boundary terms; on a patch those
terms remain. Equation (404) does not authorize independent choices
of h and gamma: h is the gradient of a single scalar and rho must
evolve under the specified drift.

In the exact shear of (400), I=0 and `q=q_xy p_nu(r,z)`. At fixed r>0
write `m(y)=n_z(r,y)^2`, `ell(z)=(partial_z log p_nu(r,z))^2`.
Then `Q=alpha nu m ell` and

```text
(h_*)_y=2alpha nu r m_y ell,
(h_*)_z=-2alpha nu r m ell_z,
curl_x h_*=-4alpha nu r m_y ell_z,
closed_rectangle_integral h_*=-4alpha nu r Delta(m) Delta(ell).
                                                            (405)
```

All four edges are included. Choose y0=0, y1=pi/2, z0=0 and z1 with
ell(z1)>0. Such z1 exists at every finite age: the heat kernel's first
Fourier coefficient is nonzero. Since m(y0)>0, m(y1)=0 and ell(0)=0,
the circulation is strictly positive for alpha>0. This contractible
rectangle proves that no positive smooth periodic rho can satisfy
`h=h_*`. The test uses an actual point-source sampler in an exact
unforced solution, not an independently prescribed receiver.

There is also a quantitative retained square. For any smooth
divergence-free periodic test vector a, `integral h.a=0`, so weighted
Cauchy--Schwarz gives, when the denominator is positive,

```text
integral rho |h-h_*|^2
 >=(integral h_*.a)^2 / integral (|a|^2/rho).           (406)
```

For (405), choose `psi=m_y ell_z` and
`a=(0,partial_z psi,-partial_y psi)`. Then div a=0 and
`integral h_*.a=-4alpha nu r integral (m_y ell_z)^2` is nonzero.
Thus each fixed positive rho gives a strictly positive deduction in
(404). There is no uniform datum-controlled lower bound here: the
denominator in (406) can deteriorate as rho concentrates. Temporal
compatibility imposes further restrictions. Neither observation yet
pays C over a complete history.

### The actual diffusion score and its original passive contribution

We reuse terminal-shift integration by parts, specifically the
coupling-by-change-of-measure method in Feng-Yu Wang's
[Integration by Parts Formula and Shift Harnack Inequality for Stochastic Equations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.4023),
Theorem 2.1(2). This terminal derivative differs from the initial-point
derivative in the usual Bismut formula. Here is the specialization,
including its signs and transpose.

For `0<=s<=r<=t`, let

```text
dX_s=-u(t-s,X_s)ds+sqrt(2nu)dW_s, X_0=x,
B_s=grad u(t-s,X_s).
```

Translate the path by `epsilon (s/r)e`. Relative to b=-u, the derivative
of its added drift is `e/r-(s/r)(grad b)e=(Id+s B_s)e/r`.
Girsanov and differentiation at epsilon=0 give

```text
E partial_e f(X_r)
 =E f(X_r) [e . integral_0^r (Id+s B_s)^T dW_s]/(sqrt(2nu)r).
```

Bounded derivatives on the fixed prefix justify differentiating the
density change. Integration by parts against the positive transition
density identifies the terminal score:

```text
k(r,y)=-1/(sqrt(2nu)r)
         E[W_r+integral_0^r s B_s^T dW_s | X_r=y].     (407)
```

On the torus use a periodic lift and periodic test functions; W remains
real three-dimensional Brownian motion. The drift is the actual NS
velocity. Prefix derivative bounds justify the identity; they are not
proposed as a priori payment constants.

Let `Omega_s v=omega(t-s,X_s) cross v`, `A_s=grad I(t-s,X_s)`.
The identities `B-B^T=Omega` and `grad H=B+A` give
`grad H-B^T=A+Omega`. Passivity of H gives
`dH_s=sqrt(2nu)(grad H)_s dW_s`. Integrating s dH_s yields

```text
N_r=integral_0^r s(A_s+Omega_s)dW_s,
integral_0^r s B_s^T dW_s
 =(r H_r-integral_0^r H_s ds)/sqrt(2nu)-N_r,

k(r,y)=-E[W_r|X_r=y]/(sqrt(2nu)r)-G_H(r,y)
                              +E[N_r|X_r=y]/(sqrt(2nu)r),
G_H(r,y)=[H(t-r,y)-r^(-1)E[integral_0^r H_s ds|X_r=y]]/(2nu),
|G_H(r,y)|<=M/nu, M>=||u0||_infinity.                 (408)
```

The final bound uses the original passive maximum principle, with no
future gradient norm. N_r keeps the inherited pressure-impulse gradient
and rotation on the SAME path. In `n(t-r,X_r).N_r`, the terminal
direction is generally not adapted at earlier times. Moving it inside
an Ito integral as an adapted integrand would change the claim.

For planar flows `u=(u1,u2,0)` independent of z, H and I are horizontal
and omega is vertical. The terminal projections of G_H and N_r vanish,
recovering (402)'s heat direction. Arbitrary 3D flows need not have this
cancellation. With forcing, `D I=grad p-f`; (408)'s spatial split still
holds but inherits that forcing. The representation alone therefore
does not distinguish forced blowup from unforced history.

### Finite entrance on arbitrary smooth prefixes

Fix a smooth physical endpoint `(t,x)`. Set `Z_r=W_r/sqrt(r)` and
`R_r=r^(-1/2)integral_0^r s B_s^T dW_s`. Equation (407) and Ito
isometry give

```text
sqrt(2nu r) k(r,X_r)=-E[Z_r+R_r|X_r],
E|R_r|^2<=(sup |B|_F)^2 r^2/3.
```

The SDE gives `Z_r-(X_r-x)/sqrt(2nu r)=O(sqrt(r))` in L2 on R3.
Conditional expectation is the best L2 projection onto functions of
X_r, hence `Z_r-E[Z_r|X_r]` tends to zero in L2. On the torus use
the nearest lift relative to x; bounded drift and the Gaussian tail
make its wrap error tend to zero in L2. Continuity of n, |n|<=1 and
the fixed Gaussian fourth moment now give

```text
lim_(r->0) nu r E_q[(n(t-r,X_r).k(r,X_r))^2]
                                      =|n(t,x)|^2/2.  (409)
```

The conditional formula and the fourth-moment Ito estimate also bound
`sqrt(r)k(r,X_r)` in L4 at small age. Since I is bounded on the fixed
prefix, `r E|I|^2/nu ->0` and `r E|(I.n)(n.k)| ->0`. Thus
`E_q P ->alpha |n(t,x)|^2/2`.

For each FIXED bounded sampling control gamma, its Girsanov likelihood
tends to one in L2. The preceding estimate bounds P in L2, so its
controlled expectation has the same limit. Also
`Ent(rho|q)<=E_gamma integral_0^r |gamma|^2/(4nu)=O(r)`. In particular,
for the smooth Markov controls of (404),

```text
lim_(r->0) J(r)=alpha |n(t,x)|^2/2<=alpha/2.           (410)
```

Prefix and control bounds justify the limit but do not enter the
allowance alpha/2. No uniform convergence rate over controls or prefixes
is asserted, nor an entrance theorem for all unbounded finite-action
controls. One may integrate (404) from epsilon and take epsilon to zero
for each fixed bounded control; its remaining source still needs
payment. The shear entrance alpha/10 is recovered from |n(t,x)|^2=1/5.

### Two paid score contributions and the remaining noise moment

Decompose `sqrt(nu r)n.k=a_0+a_H+a_N` using (408). Under the actual
uncontrolled path law,

```text
a_0=-n.E[Z_r|X_r]/sqrt(2),
|a_H|<=M sqrt(r/nu),
a_N=n.E[N_r|X_r]/sqrt(2r), |n|<=1.
```

Use `(a_0+a_H+a_N)^2<=3(a_0^2+a_H^2+a_N^2)`, then Cauchy--Schwarz
and conditional Jensen. For `0<eta<1/6`, the Brownian factor is at most
`E exp(3eta|Z_r|^2)=(1-6eta)^(-3/2)`. The other factor retains the
joint terminal direction and the full stochastic integral. It follows
that

```text
log E exp[eta nu r(n.k)^2]
 <=3eta M^2 r/nu-(3/4)log(1-6eta)
       +(1/2)log E exp[(3eta/r)(n(t-r,X_r).N_r)^2].
                                                            (411)
```

All expectations refer to the SAME actual fluid kernel and history.
At eta=1/12, the path-entropy inequality with control share theta=1/2
gives, for each bounded adapted sampling control,

```text
E_gamma[(nu r/24)(n.k)^2]
 -(1/2)E_gamma integral_0^r |gamma|^2/(4nu)
 <=M^2 r/(8nu)+(3/8)log(2)
    +(1/4)log E exp[(n(t-r,X_r).N_r)^2/(4r)].           (412)
```

This is a finite bound only when its remaining exponential moment is
finite. No datum-controlled bound for that moment is proved here;
smoothness alone is not being used to promise the displayed exponential
coefficient at every age. The density q and physical fields stay
uncontrolled. The auxiliary sampling control spends part of the action
and is not a force on the fluid. This terminal estimate neither pays
the other terms of Q nor alone implies the integrated target (379).

The coefficient in (412) matches the score term of P at alpha=1/24
and beta=0. It does not pay the larger alpha=1/2 coefficient used for
the exact shear in (403), nor the impulse term at either coefficient.

### Verification and the next physical estimate

Run `python3 -O labs/score_compatibility.py`. It checks the combined
squares, complete shear circulation, projection algebra, Gaussian
constants and entrance coefficients. Four exact NS Fourier fixtures
retain canonical pressure and all convolution outputs when checking
`grad H-(grad u)^T=grad I+cross(omega)` and its actual first time
derivative. A non-normal linear Gaussian diffusion verifies the
terminal-score covariance and detects an omitted transpose. That
calibration has unbounded drift and is not a finite-energy NS example.
Stochastic identification, density arguments and limits remain analytic,
not Lean-certified. No Lean declarations or axioms change.

The entrance is finite without a perturbative assumption, and the
Brownian and original passive score contributions have explicit
payments. The next estimate must control the inherited pressure/rotation
noise and the signed source in (404), retaining endpoint alignment and
compatible histories. The denominator in (406) and moment in (412) are
unpaid obligations, not new assumed reserves. The arbitrary-data
continuation target (379) remains open.

## Projected score noise and conditioning on the endpoint

`projected_score_noise.py` tests the remaining moment in (412) on actual
unforced flows. It derives the joint projected-noise law and gives an
analytic counterexample to finiteness of that particular moment, even
with an allowance depending on the full datum. The counterexample is a
globally smooth flow. The actual conditional score has no corresponding
divergence. A rotating shear provides a positive controlled payment.

### The full joint law retains changing direction

Use the actual uncontrolled sampler of (407). Along it put
`A=grad I`, `Omega v=omega cross v`, `C=A+Omega`, `G=grad n` and
`N_s=integral_0^s a C_a dW_a`. All pressure impulse is inherited from
the original construction (374). From (394), the drift of n is

```text
a_n=-B n+chi n-2nu G j,
j=W^T n, chi=v/2+nu|j|^2,
v=2n.Bn-2nu|W|^2, W=grad omega/sqrt(|omega|^2+delta).
```

Here s is sampling age; W without a time index denotes the normalized
vorticity gradient, while W_s is the driving Brownian motion. The
diffusion coefficients of n and N are `sqrt(2nu)G` and `s C`.
The scalar `y_s=n_s.N_s` therefore satisfies

```text
dy_s=b_y ds+c_y.dW_s,
b_y=N_s.a_n+sqrt(2nu)s G:C,
c_y=s A^T n+sqrt(2nu)G^T N_s.                        (413)
```

The instantaneous term `Omega^T n` vanishes, but neither the change of
direction nor its quadratic covariation vanishes. In particular, for
s>0, the local Ito drift of `exp(y_s^2/(4s))`, divided by that
exponential, is

```text
y_s b_y/(2s)+|c_y|^2/(4s)-y_s^2/(4s^2)
                              +y_s^2|c_y|^2/(8s^2).
```

These are local, or stopped, identities. They do not justify removing
a local martingale from an expectation without the necessary
integrability. The next example shows why this distinction matters.

### An exact regular 3D flow with infinite unconditioned noise moment

Reuse the all-time Beltrami calibration already checked in
`transported_frame_metric.py` and `cubic_parent_renewal.py`. On
`(R/2pi Z)^3`, with nu=1, take

```text
U=(sin z+cos y, sin x+cos z, sin y+cos x),
u(t)=a exp(-t)U, p=-|u|^2/2, a=100, delta=12a^2.
```

Here div U=0, curl U=U, Delta U=-U, and
`(u.grad)u=grad(|u|^2/2)`. Thus this is a literal unforced NS solution
for all t>=0, including its nonconstant pressure. All three spatial
coordinates occur. Moreover `|U|<=sqrt(12)` and `|DU|_F^2=3`, so the
regularizer dominates the ORIGINAL vorticity maximum. Its normalized
mean squared velocity is `3a^2 exp(-2t)`, and
`integral_0^infinity ||omega(t)||_infinity dt<=sqrt(12)a`.
The fluid is decaying and satisfies continuation explicitly.

Fix physical endpoint `(t,x)=(1,0)` and sampling age r=1. The claim is

```text
E_phys exp[(n(0,X_1).N_1)^2/4]=infinity,
sup_y |n(0,y).grad log q(1,y)|<infinity.               (414)
```

The second assertion follows from the smooth positive transition
density on the compact torus for this fixed smooth drift. It proves
that the stronger unconditioned noise proxy can fail while every
exponential moment of the actual terminal score is finite.

Here is a probability lower bound for the first assertion. Lift the
sampler to R3 and let ell be the constant-speed, unit-period loop
around the rectangle `(x,z) in [0,pi]^2`, y=0, starting and ending
at the origin. Its orientation first increases x, then z, then
decreases x, then z. Its length is L=4pi. Put
`n_*=n(0,0)=(1,1,1)/sqrt(15)`. All four edges give

```text
integral_loop (DU n_*).dell=2pi/sqrt(15),
integral_0^1 s exp(s-1) ds=1/e.                      (415)
```

For an integer m>=1, set `h_m(s)=ell(ms)`, making m loops in unit
time. Periodic averaging of the loop integrand gives

```text
(1/sqrt(2)) integral_0^1
  s n_*.B(1-s,h_m(s))^T h_m'(s) ds = c m+O_a(1),
c=2pi a/(e sqrt(30)).
```

For completeness, the averaging error is bounded independently of m:
subtract the mean from the unit-period integrand, take its bounded
periodic primitive, and integrate by parts against `s exp(s-1)`.
The piecewise smooth corners cause no additional term; the loop is
absolutely continuous with speed L almost everywhere.

Under the auxiliary law Q_m, let
`X_s=h_m(s)+sqrt(2)Z_s`, with Z standard Brownian motion, and use the
bounded adapted sampling control
`gamma_m=h_m'+u(1-s,X_s)`. Under the original law P the process has
drift -u. Boundedness of gamma_m for EACH m permits Girsanov, with

```text
dP/dQ_m=exp[-M_m-(1/4)integral_0^1 |gamma_m|^2 ds],
M_m=(1/sqrt(2))integral_0^1 gamma_m.dZ_s,
integral_0^1 |gamma_m|^2/4
 <=4pi^2 m^2+C_a m+C_a,
E_(Q_m) M_m^2=O_a(m^2).
```

All constants C_a here are finite and independent of m. This control
changes only the measure on sampling paths; u and p are unchanged.
The resulting law P is the same original NS diffusion for every m.

It remains to bound the actual N on these paths, including its impulse.
Use (408) as a semimartingale identity under the equivalent law Q_m:

```text
N_1=(H(0,X_1)-integral_0^1 H(1-s,X_s)ds)/sqrt(2)
    -Y_m-(1/sqrt(2))integral_0^1 s B(1-s,X_s)^T gamma_m ds,
Y_m=integral_0^1 s B(1-s,X_s)^T dZ_s,
E_(Q_m)|Y_m|^2<=a^2.
```

The first term is bounded by the ORIGINAL passive maximum; the part
containing `B^T u` is bounded by C_a. Neither bound depends on m.
Thus no pressure term or original parent has been reset or discarded.
Only the `B^T h_m'` part can have leading size m.

Choose a fixed epsilon>0 so small that on the Brownian tube
`sup_s |sqrt(2)Z_s|<=epsilon` the combined errors from replacing X_s
by h_m(s) and n(0,X_1) by n_* contribute at most c m/8. This uses
the bounded derivatives of the explicit periodic fields and
`integral |h_m'|=Lm`. The tube has probability p_epsilon>0 independent
of m. Intersect it with

```text
|Y_m|<=c m/8,  M_m<=4pi^2 m^2.
```

Chebyshev and the two displayed second-moment bounds remove only
O_a(m^(-2)) probability, without any independence assumption. Hence
for sufficiently large m this event E_m has Q_m probability at least
p_epsilon/2. Absorbing the bounded drift and averaging errors for
large m gives

```text
|n(0,X_1).N_1|>=c m/2 on E_m,
P(E_m)>=(p_epsilon/2)
            exp[-8pi^2 m^2-C_a m-C_a].               (416)
```

Consequently, for every sufficiently large integer m,

```text
E_P exp[(n(0,X_1).N_1)^2/4]
 >=(p_epsilon/2)exp[(c^2/16-8pi^2)m^2-C_a m-C_a],
c^2/16-8pi^2
 =pi^2[a^2/(120e^2)-8]>(34/27)pi^2>0,  a=100.        (417)
```

The strict bound uses e<3. Letting m grow proves (414); disjointness
of the events is unnecessary. These loops are paths of the stochastic
sampler, not a claim of infinitely many physical fluid cycles.
The same fixed, globally smooth datum has been used throughout.

This refutes the proposed finite allowance for the last moment in
(412) with the displayed regularizer and exponent, even if the allowance
depends on the full datum, viscosity and horizon. A larger regularizer
or smaller exponent chosen from the datum is a different candidate;
its possible success is not excluded by this example.
It does not refute (411)--(412), which remain valid with infinite
right sides. Nor does it refute their conditional predecessor (408),
the reserve identity (404), or the sufficient continuation target (379).
Taking the exponential before averaging paths with the same endpoint
has removed cancellation essential to this example.

### A positive payment with spatially rotating vorticity direction

For comparison, take any a,nu>0 and the exact helical shear

```text
u(t,x,y,z)=a exp(-nu t)(cos z,sin z,0), p=0,
omega=-u, H=u, I=0, delta>=a^2.
```

Its vorticity direction varies with z. Nevertheless B has only its
third column nonzero, and every terminal n is horizontal. Thus for
each fixed terminal y, `B_s n(t-r,y)=0` along every sampling path.
Equation (407) gives

```text
n(t-r,y).k(r,y)
 =-E[n(t-r,y).W_r | X_r=y]/(sqrt(2nu)r).
```

The vertical sampler is free Brownian motion because u_z=0. Its
terminal angle determines the unit horizontal direction e_r, which
is independent of the horizontal Brownian displacement. Therefore
`G=e_r.(W_r^x,W_r^y)/sqrt(r)` is a scalar standard Gaussian. The
norm of n is spatially constant at the terminal time and at most
1/sqrt(2), by the original regularizer. Conditional Jensen now gives
the same finite payment as (402)--(403), despite rotating direction:

```text
P=alpha nu r(n.k)^2, 0<alpha<2theta,
E_phys exp(P/theta)<=(1-alpha/(2theta))^(-1/2),
E_gamma P-theta E_gamma integral_0^r |gamma|^2/(4nu)
 <=-(theta/2)log(1-alpha/(2theta)).                   (418)
```

At alpha=theta=1/2 this is log(2)/4 for every bounded adapted sampling
control, uniform in the endpoint and `0<r<=t`. The same uncontrolled
kernel remains in P. The control does not alter the fluid. Although
the terminal direction depends on the path, its independence from the
horizontal Brownian displacement is proved for this flow; it is not
assumed for arbitrary fluid histories.

### Verification and the revised physical target

There is an exact deterministic representation of the conditional
quantity that survived this test. Keep C=A+Omega and the original
physical density q. Define the vector density m weakly by
`integral f(y)m(r,y)dy=E[f(X_r)N_r]`. Applying Ito to the product of
f(X_r) and N_r, including their cross variation, gives

```text
partial_r m=nu Delta m+u(t-r).grad m
                         -sqrt(2nu)r div(q C),
m(0)=0, div(q C)_i=sum_j partial_j(q C_ij),
v_N=m/q=E[N_r|X_r=y],
partial_r v_N=nu Delta v_N+(u+2nu k).grad v_N
                         -sqrt(2nu)r[div C+C k].      (419)
```

This is a weak initial-value equation with the original point source
in q; its conditional quotient is used only for r>0. It retains the
same q in every term. On a fixed smooth periodic prefix, the parabolic
kernel construction gives a smooth m at every positive age: the source
is a spatial divergence of r q times smooth bounded C, and the
initial weighted source is integrable in the weak formulation.
Equivalently, the equation for the joint diffusion's first moment gives
that construction. Since q is positive, v_N is then smooth and bounded
at each fixed positive age. These regularity bounds depend on the
fixed prefix and are not the missing original-data allowance.

In deriving (411), retain this conditional mean instead of applying
Jensen once more to N. The other two steps are unchanged, yielding

```text
E_gamma[(nu r/24)(n.k)^2]
 -(1/2)E_gamma integral_0^r |gamma|^2/(4nu)
 <=M^2 r/(8nu)+(3/8)log(2)
    +(1/4)log integral q exp[(n.v_N)^2/(4r)].         (420)
```

This right side is finite for the fixed-age ABC test. Equation (419)
is closed for m once the actual NS fields and q are supplied; it is
not a closed finite-dimensional model of those NS fields. Estimating
its quotient without retaining q can again introduce artificial
concentration costs. A bound uniform over all available prefixes from
one datum is still unproved, as is the connection of this terminal
estimate to the complete integrated source (404).

At a compatible sampling seam, retain the incoming q, m and elapsed
age. The zero condition for m belongs only to the original sampling
origin; it is not a new allowance at each segment.

Run `python3 -O labs/projected_score_noise.py`. Exact checks cover the
joint Ito product and exponential drift, the full ABC NS equation with
pressure, its original regularizer, all four loop edges, the time
weight and strict exponent margin. The rotating-shear equation,
Gaussian constant and conditional-moment quotient are checked separately.
The probability lower bound, moment divergence and controlled payment
remain analytic. No Lean
declarations or axioms change.

The tested unconditioned-noise sub-target is rejected. The next
estimate must preserve the conditional expectation through (419)--(420)
or derive a different physical payment for (404). The joint law (413)
retains the orientation and pressure defects needed for that work; it
is not itself a bound. A successful correction must reproduce both
the finite rotating-shear payment and the finite actual ABC score
without demanding its infinite noise moment. The full integrated
arbitrary-data pressure-history estimate (379) remains open.

## Conditional deformation and an original-energy payment

The endpoint-conditional repair in (419)--(420) has a useful positive
consequence. A weighted gradient projection removes stochastic circulation
without changing its conditional first moment. On the fixed torus the
retained noise has an original-energy second-moment bound uniform in
sampling duration. This pays a terminal observation for a specified class
of sampling controls. The full exponential stretching budget (379) and
integrated reserve source (404) remain open.

### The physical history and its exact observable projection

Let u be any available smooth unforced NS prefix with viscosity nu>0 on
`T3=(R/(2pi Z))^3`, using normalized volume. Fix a physical endpoint
(t,x) and sample backwards in physical time:

```text
dX_s=-u(t-s,X_s)ds+sqrt(2nu)dW_s, X_0=x,
q(s,y)dy=Law(X_s), k=grad log q, B_s(y)=grad u(t-s,y),
E0=||u0||_2^2,  0<r<=t.
```

Here W_s is Brownian motion, not the normalized vorticity gradient used
in (379). Keep the actual u and q throughout. At each positive age q is
smooth and strictly positive. Define T_s rowwise by the weighted elliptic
problem, with periodic mean-zero potentials psi_i:

```text
T_ij=partial_j psi_i,
integral q grad psi_i.grad f = integral q (B^T)_i.grad f
                                for every periodic H1 function f.
Thus div_rows[q(B^T-T)]=0.                             (421)
```

Weighted coercivity and Poincare give existence and uniqueness of the
gradient at each positive age; smooth coefficients give spatial
regularity and smooth dependence on positive age. No lower bound for q
uniform down to age zero is assumed. The stochastic integrals below are
constructed from positive ages and extended to zero in L2 using (426).

For any smooth periodic terminal test f, let
`phi(s,y)=E[f(X_r)|X_s=y]`. Its backward equation gives
`f(X_r)-E f(X_r)=sqrt(2nu) integral_0^r grad phi(s,X_s).dW_s`.
Ito isometry and (421) therefore show

```text
E[f(X_r) integral_0^r s(B^T-T)(s,X_s)dW_s]
 =sqrt(2nu) integral_0^r s integral q(B^T-T)grad phi =0.
```

The same identity follows first on positive-age subintervals and then
by the L2 limit. Testing the resulting finite signed measures against
smooth functions proves equality of the endpoint-conditional means.
Consequently the terminal-shift formula (407) becomes exactly

```text
Z_r=integral_0^r s T_s(X_s)dW_s,
E[Z_r|X_r]=E[integral_0^r s B_s^T(X_s)dW_s|X_r],
k(r,y)=-(sqrt(2nu)r)^(-1) E[W_r+Z_r|X_r=y].           (422)
```

Only the conditional first moment is being preserved. The full noise
law, its unconditioned exponential moments, and its higher conditional
moments need not be preserved. A nonlinear function of the preserved
conditional mean is still exactly the same observation.

This projection keeps a cancellation in the actual physical fields.
With the original passive H, pressure impulse I=H-u, and
`Omega v=omega cross v`, one has

```text
C=grad I+Omega=grad H-B^T,
div_rows B^T=grad div u=0,
div_rows C=Delta H,  Pi_q C=grad H-T.                (423)
```

Thus the pressure and rotation terms should not be estimated separately
before this cancellation. The pressure in the fluid equation is retained;
the projection changes a representation of the observation, not u.
There is no derivative-of-projection term in (422): its preservation
follows directly by testing the additive stochastic integral.

### Projection energy, kernel smoothing and mixing

Write `||T||_q^2=integral q|T|_F^2` and
`epsilon_s=||q(s)-1||_infinity`. Orthogonality gives
`||T||_q^2=integral q B^T:T`. Incompressibility also gives
`integral B^T:T=0`, by periodic integration by parts. Hence

```text
||T_s||_q^2
 <= min(||q(s)||_infinity, epsilon_s^2/min q(s))
                                      ||B_s||_2^2.  (424)
```

The second bound follows by Cauchy--Schwarz in
`integral (q-1)B^T:T` and
`||T||_2<=||T||_q/sqrt(min q)`. At uniform q, T is exactly zero,
although B need not vanish.

An explicit kernel constant sufficient here is C_T=324:

```text
||q(s)||_infinity <= C_T[1+(nu s)^(-3/2)].
```

For completeness, this bound does not assume heat-kernel domination
on the torus. Fourier splitting at R>=1 gives, for any periodic f,

```text
X=||f||_2^2 <=27 R^3 m^2+R^(-2)||grad f||_2^2,
m=||f||_1.
```

When X>=54m^2, choose `R=(X/(54m^2))^(1/3)`. The gradient norm squared
is at least `X^(5/3)/(2*54^(2/3)*m^(4/3))`. Incompressible transport
cancels from the scalar L2 identity and its positive semigroup contracts
L1. With m fixed at the initial L1 norm, the resulting comparison yields

```text
||P_s||_(L1->L2)^2
 <=54 max(1,(3/(2nu s))^(3/2)).
```

This applies also to the time-reversed adjoint evolution: its drift is
again divergence-free. Compose the two half intervals by duality to
obtain `||P_s||_(L1->L_infinity)<=54 max(1,(3/(nu s))^(3/2))`.
Since `3 sqrt(3)<6`, C_T=324 suffices. Approximation of a point source
then proves the displayed q bound, on any time interval, independently
of the magnitude of the smooth time-dependent drift.

Set tau=1/nu. At age tau,
`||q-1||_2^2<=2C_T-1`. Mean-zero L2 energy and the torus Poincare
constant 1 give decay at rate nu. On a final interval of length tau,
the kernel bound and invariance of uniform volume give L2-to-L_infinity
norm at most `sqrt(2C_T)`. Therefore, for s>=2tau,

```text
epsilon_s <=sqrt(2C_T(2C_T-1)) exp(2-nu s)
          <=2C_T exp(2-nu s).
L=2+log(4C_T), sigma=L/nu,
s>=sigma => epsilon_s<=(1/2)exp[-nu(s-sigma)],
             min q(s)>=1/2.
```

Use the first estimate in (424) for s<=sigma and the second for
s>=sigma. Since `z^2 exp[-2(z-L)]` decreases for z>=L>=2,

```text
s^2 ||T_s||_q^2 <=(D_T/nu^2)||B_s||_2^2,
D_T=C_T(L^2+sqrt(L)).                               (425)
```

The early-age estimate uses
`s^2[1+(nu s)^(-3/2)]<=nu^(-2)(L^2+sqrt L)`;
the late-age coefficient is at most `L^2/(2nu^2)`.
All bounds use the same actual drift and its original point-source law.

### A payment from the original unforced energy

The actual unforced energy identity gives
`integral_0^t ||grad u(v)||_2^2 dv<=E0/(2nu)`. Combining it with
(425) and Ito isometry proves, for every endpoint and available prefix,

```text
E_phys |Z_r|^2
 =E_phys integral_0^r s^2 |T_s(X_s)|_F^2 ds
 <=K_T := D_T E0/(2nu^3)
 <=16848 E0/nu^3.                                  (426)
```

The final numerical constant follows from
`L=2+log1296<10` and `sqrt L<4`. For example e>5/2 and
`(5/2)^8>1296` prove the first strict bound. The raw integral with B^T
also exists in L2 on each finite interval, using the early kernel bound;
(426) improves its duration dependence by removing the invisible part.
Conditional Jensen gives
`integral q|E[Z_r|X_r=y]|^2<=K_T`. One further consequence of (422) is

```text
integral q|k(r)|^2
 <=(sqrt(3r)+sqrt(K_T))^2/(2nu r^2)
 <=3/(nu r)+K_T/(nu r^2).                           (427)
```

There is no smallness hypothesis on u0, no future derivative norm in
K_T, and no upper bound on r other than the available smooth prefix.
This is a mean-square estimate, not an exponential or stopping-time
conditional estimate. It does not contradict the ABC obstruction (414),
which concerned a different unconditioned exponential moment. A forced
flow with an independently bounded total dissipation would satisfy the
corresponding estimate too; this result alone does not distinguish all
forced and unforced singularity mechanisms.

### Controlled terminal observations with prescribed concentration

Let gamma be a bounded adapted sampling control, with the same physical
fluid drift and initial sampler position. Denote its terminal density by
rho and its path action by
`A_gamma=integral_0^r |gamma|^2/(4nu)`. Assume a constant Lrho>=1 is
prescribed in advance and that

```text
rho(r,y)<=Lrho q(r,y) almost everywhere.             (428)
```

Only the terminal ratio is required; the intermediate densities can
vary. Let n be the physical normalized vorticity direction, so |n|<=1.
Define `U(y)=E[W_r/sqrt r|X_r=y]` and `V(y)=E[Z_r|X_r=y]` under the
uncontrolled law. Equation (422) gives
`nu r(n.k)^2 <= |U|^2+|V|^2/r`.
For alpha=1/24 and theta=1/2, entropy duality, Girsanov and conditional
Jensen give

```text
E_gamma[alpha |U(X_r)|^2]-theta E_gamma A_gamma
 <=theta log E_phys exp[(alpha/theta)|U(X_r)|^2]
 <=-(3theta/2)log(1-2alpha/theta)=(3/4)log(6/5).
```

The last step uses the three-dimensional Gaussian W_r/sqrt r; it does
not assume that W_r and X_r are independent. The remaining term is paid
by (428) and (426), without spending another share of the action:

```text
E_gamma[(nu r/24)(n.k)^2]-(1/2)E_gamma A_gamma
 <=(3/4)log(6/5)+Lrho K_T/(24r)
 <=(3/4)log(6/5)+702 Lrho E0/(nu^3 r).               (429)
```

For r>=1/nu the final energy term is at most
`702 Lrho E0/nu^2`, uniformly in sampling duration. The apparent
small-age divergence of this bound does not replace the finite entrance
calculation (410) for each fixed bounded control. Nor does (429) prove
a uniform entrance bound over arbitrary controls.

The restriction (428) is material: relative entropy alone supplies no
uniform L_infinity bound on rho/q. Defining Lrho from the unknown future
controlled solution would not give the required original-data payment.
Thus (429) does not yet close the unrestricted Bellman problem.

### Whole-space counterpart

On R3, keep the raw integral
`Z_r^R=integral_0^r s B_s^T(X_s)dW_s` in (407). The point-source
L_infinity bound of Hess-Childs, Raquépas and Rowan,
[Divergence-free drifts decrease concentration, Theorem 1.7 and
Corollary 1.10](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16723), gives
`||q(s)||_infinity<=(4pi nu s)^(-3/2)`.
The cited result allows bounded measurable time-dependent divergence-free
drift. Apply it to -u on the fixed smooth bounded prefix, with viscosity
rescaled; it may be extended by zero outside that interval. Its bound
does not depend on the drift norm. This sharp Euclidean comparison is
not asserted on the torus, where the preceding Nash argument was used.

For finite-energy smooth unforced prefixes, Ito isometry and the original
dissipation ledger now give

```text
E_phys |Z_r^R|^2
 <=K_R(r):= E0 sqrt(r)/[2nu(4pi nu)^(3/2)].
```

Indeed `s^2||q(s)||_infinity<=sqrt(r)/(4pi nu)^(3/2)` for s<=r.
The same entropy calculation under the prescribed terminal ratio (428)
yields

```text
E_gamma[(nu r/24)(n.k)^2]-(1/2)E_gamma A_gamma
 <=(3/4)log(6/5)
    +Lrho E0/[48nu(4pi nu)^(3/2)sqrt(r)].            (430)
```

No whole-space weighted elliptic projection or periodic mixing is used
in this corollary. A prescribed lower age r0>0 makes the displayed
allowance uniform in r>=r0 within available prefixes. The same limits
concerning concentration and the complete integrated source apply.

### Verification and the remaining consumer

Run `python3 -O labs/conditional_deformation_payment.py`. The exact
checker verifies (423) on the initial field and first physical time jet
of four full NS fixtures, retaining their generated pressure. A separate
nonzero projection fixture has

```text
u=(5sin y,0,0), q=64/[5(5-3cos x)^2],
psi=(0,3sin x cos y,0), T=grad psi,
||T||_q^2=9/2, ||B^T||_q^2=25/2.
```

It verifies (421), normalization, the first cosine moment and projection
orthogonality exactly. This chosen positive receiver tests the elliptic
identity; it is not claimed to be an actual point-source kernel. The
Nash comparison constants, mixing threshold, decreasing late-age weight,
Gaussian action allocation and whole-space coefficient are also checked.
Weighted elliptic existence, observation preservation, probability
inequalities and the PDE payments (426)--(430) remain analytic, not
Lean-certified. No Lean declarations or axioms change.

At a compositional seam, retain the incoming physical q, elapsed age,
and conditional noise density. For the representation (422), the latter
satisfies `partial_r m_Z=nu Delta m_Z+u.grad m_Z-sqrt(2nu)r div(qT)`
with zero initial value only at the original sampling origin. Its source
equals that obtained from B^T by (421). Resetting q or m_Z would change
the observation and invalidate the proof.

The next consumer is the arbitrary-control version of this terminal
payment and its use in the complete source (404), with the signed
pressure-history continuation bound (379) unchanged. More precisely,
without (428), allocate one quarter of the action to each contribution
in (422). Entropy duality gives the exact sufficient reduction

```text
E_gamma[(nu r/24)(n.k)^2]-(1/2)E_gamma A_gamma
 <=(3/8)log(3/2)
   +(1/4)log integral q exp[(n.V)^2/(6r)],
V(y)=E[Z_r|X_r=y].                                  (431)
```

The Gaussian coefficient here uses `1-2*(1/24)/(1/4)=2/3`.
The remaining moment must retain endpoint conditioning; finite second
moments alone do not pay it. Its original-data bound, uniform over
endpoints and available prefixes at prescribed positive ages, is the
next precise sub-target. It is not asserted in (431). The original
energy payment above removes one duration-dependent deformation cost,
while the concentration of controlled observations and their integrated
physical stretching remain explicit open obligations.

## Original-data boundary smoothing and unrestricted controls

The exponential sub-target (431) has a positive answer at the boundary
of a complete backward history on the torus. A related estimate with a
capped age weight holds on both R3 and T3 for every bounded adapted
sampling control, without the terminal density restriction (428).
The construction uses the short smooth interval already available from
the original datum. Its kernel is composed with the actual incoming law;
no unknown later velocity bound or reset of the history is used.

This is an endpoint estimate. It does not pay the interior pressure
source in (404). In particular, the derivative of a kernel in its
terminal, original-data coordinate is different from its derivative
in the current observation coordinate needed to recover current fluid
gradients. All probability and PDE conclusions in this section are
analytic, not new Lean declarations.

### A certified interval from the original datum

Let u0 be admissible smooth solenoidal data, nu>0, on R3 or the fixed
normalized 2pi torus. One explicit local construction suffices here.
Fix constants C4,C_emb>=1 for the standard H4 multiplication, heat and
Sobolev estimates on the domain, with

```text
||exp(nu h Delta) Leray div(v tensor w)||_H4
 <=C4 (nu h)^(-1/2)||v||_H4||w||_H4,
max(||v||_infinity,||grad v||_(op,infinity))<=C_emb||v||_H4.
```

Set

```text
S=1+||u0||_H4, tau0=nu/(256 C4^2 S^2),
M0=b0=2 C_emb S, tau=min(tau0,1/b0)>0.             (432)
```

The mild equation on the radius 2S ball in `C([0,tau0];H4)` has
nonlinear displacement at most `8 C4 S^2 sqrt(tau0/nu)=S/2` and
Lipschitz constant at most `8 C4 S sqrt(tau0/nu)=1/2`.
Thus the usual contraction construction gives a unique local solution
with H4 norm at most 2S. Smooth initial data bootstrap to the smooth
solution. In particular, its velocity and deformation are bounded by
M0,b0 through tau, and b0 tau<=1. Uniqueness identifies every available
smooth prefix from u0 with this solution on their common interval.

The constants in (432) are chosen before considering a later prefix.
This supplies an analytic quantitative local bound; it is not asserted
to be the exact time or constant encoded by the existing Lean local
existence theorem.

### A terminal shift confined to that same initial interval

Fix any physical endpoint (t,x) on any available smooth unforced prefix.
Use the original sampler and its density

```text
dX_s=-u(t-s,X_s)ds+sqrt(2nu)dW_s, X_0=x,
q_t(y)dy=Law(X_t), k_t=grad_y log q_t,
ell=min(t,tau), s0=t-ell.
```

The interval `[s0,t]` of this sampler corresponds to physical times
`[0,ell]`, where (432) applies. Use a continuous terminal translation
with scalar weight

```text
phi(s)=0 for s<=s0, phi(s)=(s-s0)/ell for s0<=s<=t.
```

The terminal-shift argument in (407), based on Wang's
[change-of-measure integration by parts](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.4023),
now gives

```text
J_shift=integral_s0^t [Id+(s-s0)B_s]^T dW_s / ell,
B_s=grad u(t-s,X_s),
k_t(y)=-(1/sqrt(2nu)) E[J_shift|X_t=y].             (433)
```

Indeed the first variation of the added drift for translation by
`epsilon phi(s)e` is `phi'(s)e+phi(s)B_s e`. It vanishes before s0.
The incoming distribution of X_s0 remains exactly the one generated by
the full physical prefix. The formula can be proved conditionally on
that incoming state and then integrated, or directly by the single
piecewise smooth path translation. Continuity of phi leaves no impulse
at the seam. On the torus use periodic tests and the usual lifted SDE.

For each fixed deterministic vector v, the quadratic variation of
`v.J_shift` is at most `|v|^2 Q_shift`, where

```text
Q_shift=(1/ell^2) integral_0^ell (1+b0 s)^2 ds
       =1/ell+b0+b0^2 ell/3 <=7/(3ell).
```

The exponential martingale inequality therefore gives
`E exp(v.J_shift)<=exp(Q_shift |v|^2/2)`.
Integrating this inequality against an auxiliary standard Gaussian
proves `E exp(lambda|J_shift|^2)<=(1-2lambda Q_shift)^(-3/2)`
whenever `2lambda Q_shift<1`. The argument does not assume J_shift is
Gaussian. Conditional Jensen in (433), with lambda=ell/24, yields

```text
E_phys exp[nu ell |k_t(X_t)|^2/12]<=(36/29)^(3/2),
E_gamma[nu ell(n0.k_t)^2/24]
 -(1/2)E_gamma integral_0^t |gamma|^2/(4nu)
 <=(3/4)log(36/29),                                (434)
n0(y)=omega0(y)/sqrt(|omega0(y)|^2+delta), |n0|<=1.
```

Here gamma is any bounded adapted sampling control on the entire
interval `[0,t]`. Girsanov and entropy duality spend one half of its
original action, over that entire interval, once. The physical density
q_t remains in k_t. There is no bound assumed for the controlled
terminal density ratio, and no bound for u after physical time tau.
The first inequality in fact pays any terminal direction of norm at
most one. Both inequalities hold on R3 and T3, for arbitrarily large
available t. The data-dependent cap ell is essential to this assertion.

### The cap in the complete physical reserve

Use the quantities of (404), keeping the original H,I and delta.
Choose alpha=1/24 and beta with beta^2<=alpha. At every sampling age r
set

```text
a(r)=min(r,tau),
Q=|I|^2/nu+2beta(I.n)(n.k)+alpha nu(n.k)^2,
J_a(r)=(1/2)Ent(rho|q)+E_rho[a(r)Q].
```

Q and J_a are nonnegative. Denote `D_Q=grad Q` and retain the full
`B_Q,F_Q,b,V` from (398) and (404). Here V is the impulse potential
in (404), not the conditional noise mean of (431). Directly differentiating
aQ and completing the same compatible squares gives, almost everywhere
in r,

```text
h_*a=b+(2a/nu)(nu D_Q-F_Q),
C_a=V+4dz+a' Q+a B_Q+nu a^2|D_Q|^2
                +(a^2/nu)|nu D_Q-F_Q|^2+a b.(nu D_Q-F_Q),

E_rho[2r_I-|gamma|^2/(4nu)]+J_a'(r)
 =E_rho[C_a-4nu|W-(RI tensor n)/(2nu)|^2
             -(nu/4)|h-h_*a|^2
             -|gamma-nu h-2nu a D_Q|^2/(4nu)].       (435)
```

This identity is for the same smooth bounded Markov controls as (404).
The relative score h must still be `grad log(rho/q)`. The two parts of
a meet continuously at tau; there is no distributional jump or fresh
reserve. Its derivative is 1 before tau and 0 after tau. In particular,
the term a'Q cannot be retained as Q after the cap or discarded before
it. Near zero a=r, so the entrance law (410) remains
`lim J_a=alpha|n(t,x)|^2/2<=alpha/2` for each fixed bounded control.

At the full-history endpoint r=t the physical impulse is exactly zero:
`I(0)=H(0)-u0=0`. Thus Q there is just the score term in (434).
Since terminal relative entropy is at most the full sampling action,

```text
0<=J_a(t),
J_a(t)-E_gamma integral_0^t |gamma|^2/(4nu)
 <=(3/4)log(36/29).                                (436)
```

On R3 the entropy and flux integrability hypotheses of (404) remain
necessary for (435); (434) itself only uses the sampling law and its
finite action. This cap changes the candidate reserve and its full
source, not the NS equation or the signed physical reaction r_I.
It does not imply that C_a is favorable. Integrating (435) leaves its
complete interior source and deductions as the unpaid history estimate.

### The uncapped boundary exponential on the torus

Compactness gives a further result for (431) with its original age
weight. Let K(z,y) be the transition density, with respect to normalized
volume, of sampling through physical times tau down to zero. This is
one fixed kernel constructed entirely in the certified interval.
For t>=tau, the actual terminal law is
`q_t(y)=integral K(z,y) mu_t(dz)`, where mu_t is the actual incoming
probability law at physical time tau.

Here are explicit constants controlling K. Write D=pi sqrt(3) and

```text
m0=(2pi)^3(4pi nu tau)^(-3/2)
                         exp[-(D+M0 tau)^2/(4nu tau)].
```

Then K(z,y)>=m0 for every z,y. A direct lower-bound argument on the
periodic lift retains an incompressibility cancellation. For Brownian
motion Y of variance rate 2nu starting at z, Girsanov gives the lifted
kernel ratio against the Gaussian heat kernel as the Brownian-bridge
expectation of

```text
exp[ (1/(2nu)) integral_0^tau b(s,Y_s).dY_s
                   -(1/(4nu)) integral_0^tau |b(s,Y_s)|^2 ds ],
b(s,y)=-u(tau-s,y).
```

Under the Brownian bridge from z to y, let
`m_s=z+(s/tau)(y-z)` and `v_s=2nu s(tau-s)/tau`. Gaussian integration
by parts and div b=0 give

```text
E_bridge[b(s,Y_s).(y-Y_s)]
 =(y-m_s).E_bridge b(s,Y_s)-v_s E_bridge div b(s,Y_s)
 =((tau-s)/tau)(y-z).E_bridge b(s,Y_s).
```

The bridge drift is `(y-Y_s)/(tau-s)`. The martingale part has mean
zero, so the mean stochastic line integral is bounded below by
`-M0|y-z|`. Jensen consequently yields the lifted density bound

```text
K_lift(z,y)>=(4pi nu tau)^(-3/2)
                  exp[-(|y-z|+M0 tau)^2/(4nu tau)]. (437)
```

The bridge integrals are justified first short of tau and then in L1;
bounded drift makes the remaining bridge-drift singularity integrable.
This computes a kernel likelihood ratio, not the relative entropy of
two pinned path laws. Choose the nearest periodic image with
`|y-z|<=D` and convert to normalized volume to obtain m0.

For an upper derivative bound, the drift-independent Nash estimate
preceding (425) gives
`Q0=324[1+(nu tau/2)^(-3/2)]` at age tau/2.
On the last half interval let h be its elapsed time and f the evolving
kernel. The differential operator
`L0=partial_h-nu Delta-u.grad` satisfies

```text
L0(f^2)=-2nu|grad f|^2,
L0(|grad f|^2)<=2b0|grad f|^2-2nu|Hess f|^2.
```

The Bernstein combination
`h exp(-2b0 h)|grad f|^2+f^2/(2nu)` is a subsolution, hence

```text
||grad_y K||_infinity<=G0:=exp(b0 tau/2)Q0/sqrt(nu tau),
S0=G0/m0,
|grad_y log q_t(y)|<=S0, t>=tau.                    (438)
```

For the last step, the score of a mixture is the posterior-weighted
average of the individual kernel scores `grad_y K(z,y)/K(z,y)`.
No information about mu_t is discarded or replaced by an equilibrium
law. The constants M0,b0,tau,Q0,G0,m0,S0 all come from u0,nu and the
fixed domain. They can be large; no sharpness is asserted.

Now let `v_Z(y)=E[Z_t|X_t=y]` be the conditional mean in (431).
The exact score identity (422) gives
`v_Z=-sqrt(2nu)t k_t-E[W_t|X_t]`. For tau<=t<=H,
conditional Jensen and the Gaussian moment of W_t/sqrt(t) imply

```text
log integral q_t exp[(n0.v_Z)^2/(6t)]
 <=(2nu H/3)S0^2+(3/2)log(3).                       (439)
```

Indeed the exponent is at most
`(2nu t/3)|k_t|^2+|E[W_t|X_t]|^2/(3t)`.
For t<=tau, use instead the raw integral in (422): each directional
quadratic variation is at most `b0^2 t^3/3`. Its Gaussian-mixture bound
at coefficient 1/(6t), followed by conditioning, is
`(1-(b0 t)^2/9)^(-3/2)<=(9/8)^(3/2)`.
Thus (439)'s larger right side works for every 0<t<=H on every available
same-datum prefix. It proves the boundary case r=t of (431), including
arbitrarily small t; it does not prove all interior ages r<t.

The original uncapped score cost also has the direct bound

```text
E_gamma[(nu t/24)(n0.k_t)^2]
 -(1/2)E_gamma integral_0^t |gamma|^2/(4nu)
 <=(3/4)log(36/29)+nu H S0^2/24, 0<t<=H.            (440)
```

Use (434) for t<=tau and (438) for later t. Neither (438)--(440)
is transferred to R3 by compactness. The both-domain statement there
is the capped estimate (434), or a horizon-fixed smaller coefficient
`min(1,tau/H)/24` in place of 1/24 for the uncapped score cost.

### Scope, checks and the remaining physical question

Run `python3 -O labs/original_boundary_score.py`. Exact checks cover the
complete weighted reserve square, the local contraction constants,
the Gaussian margins, the Bernstein differential identity and the
mixture gradient identity. The bridge divergence cancellation is
checked mode by mode on four full NS fields and their first time jets,
retaining canonical pressure and every generated Fourier output.
A non-normal linear Gaussian probe checks the late shift's exact
terminal covariance independently of its inherited starting age; this
formula check is not asserted to be a finite-energy NS example.
A non-solenoidal calibration retains the divergence defect instead of
silently canceling it. The actual decaying ABC solution gives explicit
original-data bounds `M0=sqrt(6)a`, `b0=sqrt(3)a`; it is the same regular
flow on which the unconditioned noise moment (414) diverges. It obeys
the new boundary payment. No numerical approximation is used.

The local existence, stochastic representation, kernel lower bound,
comparison and controlled payments remain analytic. Symbolic scalar
PDE jets are labeled as such and are not claimed to be additional NS
solutions. No new Lean declarations or axioms are introduced.

This result isolates a limit of endpoint tests. Once the initial
interval is certified, the kernel arguments allow any smooth
incompressible continuation outside it, including one supported by an
external force. Accordingly, their success cannot by itself prevent
forced or internally sustained dangerous stretching. Also, the bounded
terminal-coordinate derivative in (438) is not a bound on differentiating
the current physical observation point x.

The full goal still requires payment of the interior, pressure-connected
source in (435), or a different estimate of the physical reaction in
(379). At interior ages, the sampler ends at an evolving fluid state;
its last interval need not lie in the original certified interval.
Extending (434) there by restarting with an unknown future norm would
reintroduce the missing estimate. The revised reserve keeps its incoming
q, rho, H, I and elapsed age. Its complete pressure, orientation and
relative-density terms are the next physical obligations, with the
boundary cost now explicitly separated.

## Physical forcing defects and compatible internal sources

The imported whole-space forced construction fails the exact exponential
pressure-impulse target (379), even after its direct normalized curl-force
contribution is paid by a finite constant. This is an analytic consequence
of the imported candidate's stated properties, not a new singular solution.
The distinction identifies a necessary limitation of a force-insensitive
history estimate. It does not refute the unforced target.

`forced_history_defect.py` also checks the force correction in the complete
reserve (435), a smooth rotating forced calibration, and the exact internal
sources obtained by splitting an actual unforced flow. The stochastic and
PDE arguments below are analytic; no new Lean declarations are introduced.

### The full force correction, including orientation

Use the same original passive H, impulse I=H-u, delta, physical point-source
sampler, densities q,rho, and spatial scores as in (374)--(435). Let the
physical equation have force f and put

```text
D=partial_t+u.grad-nu Delta, B=grad u,
D u=-grad p+f, D H=0, H(0)=u0,
D I=grad p-f, D omega=B omega+curl f,
s_omega=|omega|^2+delta, n=omega/sqrt(s_omega),
c_f=curl f/sqrt(s_omega), g_f=2n.c_f,
F_n=-(Id-nn^T)c_f.                                (441)
```

Here p is the actual forced pressure. In backward sampling time the
observation generator L gains +f in LI and F_n in Ln. The density's
equation still uses the actual drift -u; there is no additional explicit
force term in Lk. This is a comparison of generator formulas at identical
instantaneous fields, not a claim that forced and unforced flows have the
same fields or transition law.

Let d=I.n, z=n.k and keep the nonnegative quadratic Q from (397).
Differentiate Q directly in raw omega and I. Relative to the unforced
expression B_Q of (398), the extra source is

```text
E_f=2I.f/nu+2beta z(n.f)
       +(2beta z I+2beta d k+2alpha nu z k).F_n,
LQ=B_Q+E_f+(1/q)div(q F_Q).                        (442)
```

When evaluating B_Q, use the unforced algebraic reaction
`v=2n.Bn-2nu|W|^2` in chi and T_z. Substituting v+g_f there and also
adding E_f would double count part of the force. All fields, including
pressure and their spatial derivatives, are the actual forced ones.
The spatial flux F_Q and the control/gradient square completions retain
their formulas. In particular, if S_a denotes the sum of the three
nonnegative squares subtracted in (435), its full forced counterpart is

```text
E_rho[2(r_I+g_f)-|gamma|^2/(4nu)]+J_a'
 =E_rho[C_a-S_a+2g_f+a E_f].                       (443)
```

The hypotheses for integrated density identities and boundary flux are
unchanged. The reward here is explicitly r_I+g_f; the target (379) uses
r_I alone. Also, the time scale in an initial-interval argument for a
forced flow must be justified for that forced flow. The unforced Picard
constant (432) cannot be reused without its hypotheses.

A calibration shows why amplitude work alone misses orientation. On the
2pi torus let A,nu,Omega>0 and

```text
u=A exp(-nu t)sin(z)(cos(Omega t),sin(Omega t),0), p=0,
f=A Omega exp(-nu t)sin(z)(-sin(Omega t),cos(Omega t),0).
```

This is an exact smooth forced NS solution for all nonnegative time:
advection vanishes and f supplies only the rotating part of the time
derivative. Pointwise `u.f=0` and `omega.curl f=0`, but curl f is nonzero
and rotates the vorticity. The original passive field is
`H=A exp(-nu t)sin(z)(1,0,0)`; it is not reset to the rotating velocity.
There is no vortex stretching in this calibration, and
`r_I=-2nu|grad omega|^2/s_omega<=0`. Thus it verifies a force channel,
not growth or blowup. This smooth periodic force is not the force class
of the imported whole-space singular construction.

### The imported forced flow defeats the remaining history bound

Use precisely `NavierStokesR3.ProblemStatement.CandidateProperties` and
`NavierStokesR3.theorem_1_1_with_initial_rest` from the pinned
OpenAI/NavierStokesAndEuler package. The same whole-space u,p,f have:
positive viscosity; smooth velocity and pressure on every prefix before
1; a common compact spatial support; zero original velocity; globally
smooth force with compact spacetime support inside positive time; one
uniform kinetic-energy bound; and speed unbounded as t approaches 1.
The stronger imported theorem supplies initial rest through time 3/8.
No hypothesis on a manufactured or periodic substitute is used here.
The existing `ForcedCandidatePancake` and `ForcedSignedBudget` modules
connect these candidate properties to physical slices and other budgets;
the stochastic implication in this section is additional analytic work.

Fix ANY delta>0 once for this one candidate. Its original passive H is
identically zero by uniqueness, so I=-u and v_H=0. Compact support and
global smoothness of f imply
`F_curl=sup_(t,x)|curl f(t,x)|<infinity`. The elementary inequality
`2sqrt(delta)|omega|<=|omega|^2+delta` gives

```text
|g_f(t,x)|<=G_f:=F_curl/sqrt(delta).                (444)
```

Thus every path pays the absolute integral of g_f by G_f t. This also
bounds every fixed exponential order of that direct contribution.
It does not bound the work E_f in (442) or the history created by f.

On every fixed prefix [0,t], t<1, all spatial coefficients are bounded
by smoothness and the common compact support. The normalized scalar
vorticity equation and its ordinary backward Feynman--Kac formula give

```text
D s_omega=(r_I+g_f)s_omega, s_omega(0)=delta,
s_omega(t,x)=delta E_phys_(t,x) exp integral_0^t(r_I+g_f).
```

Using (444) and Cauchy--Schwarz on this SAME sampling law yields

```text
log E_phys_(t,x) exp[2 integral_0^t r_I]
 >=2log(s_omega(t,x)/delta)-2G_f t.                (445)
```

All moments in (445) are finite at each fixed endpoint before 1. The
claim concerns their failure to have one finite uniform bound through
the prescribed horizon 1, without restarting the initial datum.

For completeness, the imported unbounded speed really implies the
unbounded vorticity needed here. For any smooth compactly supported
solenoidal field on R3, curl omega=-Delta u, and for any R>0 the heat
identity gives

```text
u=exp(R^2 Delta)u+integral_0^(R^2) curl exp(s Delta)omega ds,
||u||_infinity <= (8pi)^(-3/4)R^(-3/2)||u||_2
                    +(4/sqrt(pi))R||omega||_infinity. (446)
```

The heat kernel has L2 norm `(8pi s)^(-3/4)` and its gradient has L1
norm `2/sqrt(pi s)`. Young's inequality proves (446), including the
integrable endpoint at s=0. Taking R=1 already shows that bounded L2
norm and bounded vorticity would bound the speed. Balancing the two
terms also gives the usual powers `||u||_2^(2/5)||omega||_infinity^(3/5)`.
No hypothetical regularity of a continuation is assumed.

Consequently the right side of (445) is unbounded over t<1 and x.
For this SAME imported forced candidate, every fixed delta>0 and every
finite K fail the uniform exponential inequality of (379). Allowing K
to depend on the entire fixed force does not change this conclusion.
The direct curl-force payment G_f is nevertheless finite. In fact the
original endpoint score cost in (434) vanishes because omega0=0.

This does not say that the explicit source 2g_f+a E_f alone must have
an infinite integral: the fields entering C_a change as the forced
history evolves. Nor is it a counterexample from a nonzero unforced
initial datum. Removing the force from this zero datum gives the zero
flow. Restarting at a later time with a nonzero datum produces a
different evolution and is not a proof of internal realization.
The result excludes a proposed argument that would pay (379) for this
forced class merely by also paying the bounded direct curl reaction.

### Effective internal sources must come from the same full evolution

There is a concrete compatibility condition when decomposing an unforced
flow. Let P be a fixed Fourier projector commuting with spatial derivatives,
eta=Pomega and zeta=(Id-P)omega. Keep the SAME full drift u and deformation
B=grad u in both equations. Directly applying P to the unforced vorticity
equation gives, throughout every smooth prefix,

```text
D eta=B eta+Xi_P,      D zeta=B zeta-Xi_P,
Xi_P=P(B omega)-B(Pomega)
          +u.grad(Pomega)-P(u.grad omega).         (447)
```

This is an observation of the full PDE, not a projected evolution. The
unobserved modes, all convolution outputs and the actual pressure remain
in u and its evolution. An arbitrary time series Xi_P cannot be inserted
without constructing the same full u satisfying (447).

Opposite vector sources do not cancel in separately squared observations.
Their source contributions are exactly

```text
in D(|eta|^2+|zeta|^2):      2(eta-zeta).Xi_P,
in D(2eta.zeta):           -2(eta-zeta).Xi_P.       (448)
```

The retained cross term restores the full |omega|^2 identity. Its
stretching and gradient-diffusion terms must also be retained. For a
normalized eta the backward orientation correction is
`-(Id-n_eta n_eta^T)Xi_P/sqrt(|eta|^2+delta_eta)`, with a fixed positive
delta_eta; the hidden component has the opposite unnormalized source
but a different normalization. These formulas expose the relevant
shared geometric information. They do not bound Xi_P or its history.
One must not substitute Xi_P for a physical force in every equation of
(441): eta is a component of vorticity transported by the full u, not
the vorticity of an independent fluid with its own NS drift and pressure.

The checker verifies (447) and its first physical time derivative on
four existing smooth NS data with cutoff-squared values 1,1,10,3 fixed
from the original data. It retains canonical pressure, viscosity and
all generated modes through two time derivatives. The nonzero sources
and (448) are checked exactly. Local smooth existence turns these data
into actual short histories; the general algebra proves (447) throughout
each such history. Finite jets do not establish a long-time payment.

Run `python3 -O labs/forced_history_defect.py`. Independent raw-variable
differentiation verifies (442)--(443); the literal rotating shear checks
the equation, passive field, work and orientation claims. Exact Gaussian
integrals check the constants in (446). The candidate's Feynman--Kac
obstruction and the general PDE consequences remain analytic, not
Lean-certified. No numerical approximation or new axiom is used.

The next physical task is to exploit the compatibility in (447), with
its cross geometry and evolving pressure, in a payment for the complete
bulk (435). The forced obstruction shows why a bounded external input
or an endpoint score alone is insufficient. The unforced arbitrary-data
exponential bound (379), and hence its continuation consequence, remain
open.

## Signed impulse geometry and a physical continuation allowance

The remaining history question has a geometric formulation with a direct
signed-renewal consumer. Only the impulse component contributing positively
to the Lamb-vector energy pairing needs to be measured. Impulse parallel
to vorticity, and transverse impulse with the opposite sign in that pairing,
are excluded. A finite original-data bound for the resulting time integral
would close the existing continuation argument. That bound is still open.

This uses the established geometric energy method of
[Chae--Lee, Theorem 1, beta=2](https://arxiv.org/html/1606.08126): their
criterion retains the positive part of a signed velocity--vorticity--curl
triple product. Below the bounded original passive parent is separated,
and vorticity is regularized without adding infinite constant mass on R3.
This adaptation and its physical source calculations are analytic, not a
new Lean formalization of the cited regularity theorem.

### The signed observation and its actual energy consumer

Work on an available smooth unforced prefix on R3 or the fixed 2pi torus,
with the regularity and decay needed for the usual energy identities.
Retain the SAME original passive H and impulse I=H-u. Fix delta>0 from
the original datum, once. Set

```text
omega=curl u, B=grad u, c=curl omega=-Delta u,
s=|omega|^2+delta, L=I cross omega, J=-L.c,
a_delta=J_+/(sqrt(s)|c|) if |c|>0, and 0 if c=0,
A(t)=||a_delta(t)||_infinity,
E0=||u0||_2^2, M=||u0||_infinity,
Z(t)=||omega(t)||_2^2, D_omega(t)=||grad omega(t)||_2^2,
g(t)=integral omega.Bomega.                         (449)
```

The stochastic meaning is unchanged. Along the actual backward diffusion
`dX_r=-u(t-r,X_r)dr+sqrt(2nu)dW_r`, starting at x,

```text
H(t,x)=E[u0(X_t)],
I(t,x)=E integral_0^t grad p(t-r,X_r)dr.
```

These formulas use the original datum and the full unforced pressure
history. They follow from the passive and impulse equations on each
smooth prefix. Subdividing that prefix does not discard the inherited
impulse or replace the drift by independently controlled parents.

The L-infinity norm can be read as essential supremum. The observation
is measurable and bounded by |I| on each smooth prefix. It need not be
continuous at c=0; the zero convention is sufficient for the estimates,
and no derivative of this positive-part quotient is taken below.
Its unnormalized numerator and both denominator fields have the full
evolution equations recorded later.

Incompressibility, integration by parts and curl omega=-Delta u imply

```text
Z'=2g-2nu D_omega,
g=integral(u cross omega).c,
||c||_2^2=D_omega,
(u cross omega).c=(H cross omega).c+J.
```

These are spatial integral identities; the Lamb and stretching integrands
are not asserted equal pointwise. On a proper subregion their boundary
fluxes must be retained. The original passive maximum principle and L2
energy identity give `||H||_infinity<=M`, `||H||_2<=sqrt(E0)` and hence
`||I||_2^2<=4E0`. No restarted passive field is used.

Since J<=J_+=a_delta sqrt(s)|c|, Cauchy--Schwarz gives

```text
g <=sqrt(D_omega)[M sqrt(Z)+sqrt(A^2 Z+4delta E0)].
```

Here the low-vorticity remainder is
`delta integral a_delta^2<=delta||I||_2^2<=4delta E0`.
Replacing it by `delta A^2 integral 1` would be invalid on R3.
Young's inequality, with half of full vorticity dissipation retained,
therefore gives on BOTH domains

```text
Z'+nu D_omega <=q(t) Z+F,
q(t)=(2/nu)(M^2+A(t)^2), F=8delta E0/nu.            (450)
```

In particular, suppose one finite number B_geo, fixed from u0,nu and a
prescribed horizon T, bounds `integral_0^t A(s)^2 ds` for every t<=T on
every available same-datum smooth prefix. Then

```text
Z(t)+nu integral_0^t D_omega
 <=(Z(0)+F t) exp[(2/nu)(M^2 t+integral_0^t A^2)].  (451)
```

One proof first drops dissipation and applies scalar Gronwall, then
integrates (450), using
`Z(s)<=(Z(0)+F t)exp(integral_0^s q)` for s<=t. All coefficients in
this conclusion are prescribed original resources except the explicitly
unpaid integral of A^2.

### A nonnegative reserve spending the geometric budget once

The consumer can be written as a reserve on compatible actual histories.
Under the stated hypothesis let

```text
ell(t)=B_geo-integral_0^t A(s)^2 ds >=0,
r(t)=(2/nu)[M^2(T-t)+ell(t)],
R(t)=exp(r(t))[Z(t)+F(T-t)]-Z(t) >=0.               (452)
```

ell records the unspent part of the one original geometric allowance.
It cannot be reset when histories are composed. With
`gap=qZ+F-(Z'+nu D_omega)>=0`, direct differentiation gives, almost
everywhere,

```text
R'+2g-nu D_omega
 =-exp(r)gap-nu(exp(r)-1)D_omega
                         -exp(r)qF(T-t) <=0.       (453)
```

Every sign follows from t<=T, ell>=0, nu>0, and the actual enstrophy
balance. Thus one explicit allowance for the original signed renewal is

```text
2 integral_0^t [g(s)-g(0)] ds
 <=nu integral_0^t D_omega ds+K,
K=exp[(2/nu)(M^2 T+B_geo)](Z(0)+F T)-Z(0)
                                      +2T|g(0)|.  (454)
```

On R3, `Z=orderEnergy 1` and `D_omega=orderEnergy 2` for solenoidal
fields, so this matches the hypothesis of
`JointCubicRenewal.hasNSEvolution_of_signed_renewal`. On the torus it
supplies the corresponding uniform H1 bound for the existing continuation
criterion. The spatial identification, integration and passive construction
in this section remain analytic. The existing Lean consumer does not
certify these new antecedents automatically.

This is a sufficient alternative geometric history target, not a proof
of its missing B_geo or a claim that it is equivalent to the exponential
pressure-history target (379). Defining B_geo by an unknown-future
supremum would not establish the needed estimate.

### Pressure and all generated parents remain in the source

Let the material diffusion operator be `D_u=partial_t+u.grad-nu Delta`,
and write `I_j=partial_j I`, `omega_j=partial_j omega`, `B_j=partial_j B`,
`u_j=partial_j u`. The exact unforced equations give

```text
D_u L=grad p cross omega+I cross(B omega)
                         -2nu sum_j I_j cross omega_j =: F_L,
D_u c=grad Delta p-B c+2 sum_j B_j u_j =: F_c,
D_u J=-F_L.c-L.F_c+2nu sum_j partial_j L.partial_j c. (455)
```

Thus pressure gradient, pressure Laplacian, strain and mixed diffusion
must all be retained. The actual pressure is determined by the full
velocity; these are not independently chosen coefficients. Along with
the actual normalized-vorticity equation, (455) specifies the fields
entering (449), including their changing alignment. It does not give
them a favorable sign or an original-data bound.

For the fixed Fourier split eta,zeta of (447), define
`L_eta=I cross eta`, `L_zeta=I cross zeta`. Their exact sources include
respectively `+I cross Xi_P` and `-I cross Xi_P`. They cancel in the
SUM L, but

```text
|L|^2=|L_eta|^2+|L_zeta|^2+2L_eta.L_zeta.           (456)
```

The shared denominator in (449) also uses the full omega=eta+zeta.
Taking independent positive parts or independently normalizing the two
components destroys these cancellations. Reconstructing (455) from
the joint components is an identity, not a new coercive estimate.
More explicitly, J is the sum of all four terms
`-(I cross omega_a).curl(omega_b)`, with a,b ranging over the two
components. Its positive part is taken only after that sum.

The signed observation can genuinely be created by an unforced flow.
For the earlier explicit pressure-start datum

```text
u0=(-4sin(x)cos(z)-8sin(y),
       8sin(x)+4sin(y)cos(z),
       4(cos(x)-cos(y))sin(z)),
```

at `x0=(0,pi/4,0)` the full canonical pressure yields

```text
I(0)=L(0)=J(0)=0,
partial_t J(0,x0)=(6400+2816sqrt(2))/3 >0,
|omega0(x0)|^2=(8+4sqrt(2))^2, |c0(x0)|^2=64.
```

Smooth local existence, with positive viscosity, makes a_delta(t,x0)
strictly positive on a short interval. For any fixed delta>0 its first
coefficient is the displayed J derivative divided by
`8sqrt(delta+(8+4sqrt(2))^2)`.
The corresponding small-time integral of A^2 has a positive contribution
of order t^3. Thus zero initial impulse does not imply a zero future
geometric cost. This finite burst does not refute a full-datum B_geo.

### Exact positive calibrations and the forced obstruction

The criterion retains a whole family with arbitrary amplitude. Let U be
a smooth divergence-free periodic steady Euler field with
`-Delta U=k^2 U`, k>0. Then
`u=a_* exp(-nu k^2 t)U`, with the correspondingly decaying steady pressure,
is an exact unforced evolution. Its curl observer satisfies `c=k^2 u`,
so `(u cross omega).c=0` pointwise. Consequently

```text
J=-(H cross omega).c,
a_delta<=|H|<=M, integral_0^t A(s)^2 ds<=M^2 t.
```

The original H is generally NOT u when
pressure is nonconstant. The proof uses its actual passive maximum
principle, not a false explicit formula for H. The checker verifies
both a three-dimensional ABC family and a planar cellular family with
nonconstant pressure. These are known regular solution families,
used to calibrate the history target rather than claim new regularity.

For the ABC family, omega=c=u, so a_delta is identically ZERO for every
actual H, a stronger statement than the displayed bound. In particular,
this observation does not reproduce the false obstruction of the
unconditioned noise moment (414) on that same regular flow.

The joint cancellation has a strict physical test. Write the standard
ABC field as `U1+U2`, where `U1=(0,sin(x),cos(x))` is its Fourier pair
at frequencies +/-e1. Both parts satisfy curl U_i=U_i. The diagonal
signed terms vanish and the off-diagonal terms are opposite at every
time, with the SAME inherited I. At `(0,pi/2,0)`, the actual initial
pressure gradient gives their first time derivatives

```text
partial_t J_12(0)=-a_*^4, partial_t J_21(0)=a_*^4.
```

Thus `[J_12]_++[J_21]_+=a_*^4 t+O(t^2)>0` on a short actual unforced
interval, while `[J_12+J_21]_+=0` for the entire flow. This is a strict
loss from charging parents separately. It does not refute every finite
budget for that larger observation; it identifies cancellation the
joint history should preserve before estimating a cost.

For the actual imported whole-space forced candidate, H=0 and I=-u.
Thus a_delta is exactly the positive normalized velocity Lamb triple.
Write `E_star=sup_t||u(t)||_2^2<infinity`. Its smooth compact force has
`F_star=sup_t||f(t)||_2^2<infinity`. The forced enstrophy balance, now
including `2 integral c.f`, gives

```text
Z'+nu D_omega <=(2/nu)A(t)^2 Z
                              +(2/nu)(delta E_star+F_star).
```

Allocate nu/2 of dissipation to each of the Lamb and force terms to
obtain this inequality. A finite integral of A^2 through time1 would
therefore bound Z uniformly. This contradicts the already certified
`ForcedCandidatePancake.no_uniform_gradient_energy` for this SAME
candidate, together with the solenoidal enstrophy identity. Hence its
new geometric integral must diverge for every fixed delta>0.
This argument uses the existing gradient-energy obstruction, not an
unsupported inference from unbounded speed to unbounded H1 norm.
It neither constructs internal realization nor excludes it in an
arbitrary nonzero-datum unforced flow.

### Verification and the remaining estimate

Run `python3 -O labs/signed_impulse_geometry.py`. The exact checker
verifies the reserve identity (453), dissipation allocation, both
all-time eigenflow calibrations, the integrated Lamb identity and its
first evolving derivative, and the complete source (455) on four full
NS data through the required time derivatives. Canonical pressure,
viscosity and all convolution outputs remain. It also verifies the
nonzero internal cross sources and the retained cross observation (456).
The explicit positive-creation fixture uses exact trigonometric values.
No numerical trajectory or finite closed cascade is substituted for NS.

The next estimate must pay the positive impulse geometry (449) from
the original fluid while respecting (455)--(456), or pay the previous
complete source (435) by another route. The new observation removes
irrelevant parallel and depleting components and has an explicit
continuation consumer. It leaves pressure-driven reorientation and
