repeated coupled renewal as the quantitative open obligation.

## Viscous creation of signed geometric cost

The positive signed observation (449) retains useful cancellations, but its
viscous chain-rule contribution need not be negative. An exact, globally
regular cellular flow violates that proposed sign for every amplitude,
positive viscosity and fixed vorticity regularizer. The example also defeats
adding any finite spatially constant multiple of the impulse's squared norm
as a repair of that particular sign. This does not refute the original-data
history allowance, nor say that increasing viscosity increases the full
solution's cost: all the other evolving terms remain in the equation.

### The precise local sign under test

Use the original passive H and I=H-u, with D_u I=grad p, as above. For
Y=(I,omega,c), c=curl omega, and delta>0 fixed from the original datum,
write, on the region J=-(I cross omega).c>0 and c!=0,

```text
Phi=F(Y)=J^2/[(|omega|^2+delta)|c|^2],
D_u Phi=F_I.grad p+F_omega.(B omega)+F_c.F_curl+V_nu,
F_curl=grad Delta p-Bc+2 sum_j B_j u_j,
V_nu=-nu sum_j Hess_Y F[partial_j Y,partial_j Y].    (457)
```

Here F_c means the derivative of F in its third vector argument, while
F_curl is the physical source of c. Pressure and the transport commutator
have not been classified as diffusion or discarded. Equation (457) is the
ordinary chain rule for the common Laplacian on the three actual fields.
The proposed local ingredient was V_nu<=0. It is false even on actual
unforced histories, as the following computation shows.

### An all-amplitude physical counterexample to the viscous sign

For any a,nu>0, on the fixed 2pi torus take the known exact solution

```text
u(t)=a exp(-2nu t)(sin x cos y,-cos x sin y,0),
p(t)=a^2 exp(-4nu t)(cos(2x)+cos(2y))/4.
```

This solves the full unforced equation for all time. Its actual vortex
stretching omega.Bomega is identically zero. Its full Lamb work
`(u cross omega).c` is also zero pointwise, since c=2u. The pressure is
nonconstant, so the original passive H cannot be replaced by u.

At x_*=(pi/4,pi/4,0), let G=grad p(0). Direct differentiation gives

```text
G=(-a^2/2,-a^2/2,0),       Hess p(0)=0,
omega0=(0,0,a),           c0=(a,-a,0),
partial_x omega0=partial_y omega0=(0,0,a),
partial_x c0=(a,a,0),     partial_y c0=(-a,-a,0).
```

The original impulse equation, with I(0)=0, gives
`I(t)=t G+O(t^2)` in all the needed spatial derivatives. Hence at this
fixed receiver `grad I(t)=O(t^2)`, while

```text
J(t,x_*)=a^4 t+O(t^2)>0,
Phi(t,x_*)=a^6 t^2/[2(a^2+delta)]+O(t^3),
V_nu(t,x_*)=
  2nu a^8(a^2+5delta)t^2/(a^2+delta)^3+O(t^3)>0.    (458)
```

The coefficient is positive for EVERY a,nu,delta>0. One independent
calculation differentiates F along the literal joint spatial directions
`(G,omega0,c0)+epsilon(partial_j G,partial_j omega0,partial_j c0)`.
Its second derivative in each of the x and y directions is
`-a^8(a^2+5delta)/(a^2+delta)^3`; the z contribution is zero.
Homogeneity in I and the actual short-time expansion then give (458).

For any finite spatially constant kappa, the additional viscous source
of kappa|I|^2 is `-2nu kappa|grad I|^2=O(t^4)`. It cannot cancel the
strict positive leading term in (458). The coefficient may depend on
the original datum, viscosity, regularizer and prescribed horizon; the
failure still holds for each such finite choice. This concerns the
viscous sign, not the full Bellman derivative or every possible reserve.
Gradient-dependent or nonlocal corrections are not excluded.

The failure is not confined to planar data. For the full three-dimensional
pressure-start datum in the preceding section, with delta=1, at
`(0,pi/2,pi/4)` the exact full pressure gives

```text
partial_t J(0)=7424,
V_nu(t)=nu (42181805312/8214057)t^2+O(t^3)>0.
```

Both interval conclusions use actual smooth local evolution and passive
transport. A finite Fourier jet is used to compute the coefficients;
it is not substituted for the subsequent nonlinear solution.

### A smooth joint direction and a paid part of its source

The observation can also be regularized at c=0. Fix mu>0 and define

```text
n=omega/sqrt(|omega|^2+delta),
m=c/sqrt(|c|^2+mu), b=n cross m,
q=-I.b, Phi_mu=(q_+)^2.                            (459)
```

The vector b is smooth in the primitive fields. The squared positive
part is C1 with a locally bounded weak second derivative; the following
identities hold on each sign region and almost everywhere in the weak
chain rule. No singular positive-part boundary term is omitted.
For each spatial direction set

```text
b_j=partial_j b,
K_b=sum_j Hess_(omega,c) b[
             (partial_j omega,partial_j c),
             (partial_j omega,partial_j c)].
```

K_b is the chain-rule Hessian term, not Delta b: the latter also contains
the first derivatives of b applied to Delta omega and Delta c. Thus the
viscous chain source of b is -nu K_b. The complete nonviscous source is
`S_b=(partial_omega b)(Bomega)+(partial_c b)F_curl`, and

```text
D_u Phi_mu=-2q_+[grad p.b+I.S_b]+V_nu,mu,
V_nu,mu+2nu|grad(q_+)|^2
 =2nu q_+ I.K_b+4nu q_+ sum_j I_j.b_j
 =2nu q_+ I.K_b+2nu|grad I|^2+2nu q_+^2|grad b|^2
                         -2nu sum_j |I_j-q_+ b_j|^2. (460)
```

The same actual fields occur in all terms. With |b|<=1 and
`q_+<=|I||b|`, put
`G_b=|b||K_b|+|b|^2|grad b|^2`. Cauchy--Schwarz yields the pointwise
bound and, using the existing original passive-history payment, its
spatially integrated consequence:

```text
(V_nu,mu)_+ <=2nu|grad I|^2+2nu|I|^2 G_b,
int_0^t int (V_nu,mu)_+
 <=4E0+2nu int_0^t int |I|^2 G_b.                  (461)
```

This reuses `PressureImpulseHistory.PassiveHistory.impulse_paid`: its
hypotheses include the literal passive PDE and original initial value,
and it proves `||I(t)||_2^2+2nu int_0^t||grad I||_2^2<=4E0` on R3.
The corresponding periodic estimate follows from the same two energy
balances. The new geometric chain rule and its spatial integration are
analytic, not newly Lean-certified. The allowance is spent across the
whole original history, not supplied afresh to each component or segment.

The first term in (461) therefore has a datum-only payment without a
smallness assumption. The weighted JOINT angular term remains open,
as does the physical pressure/strain source in (460). This is a spatial
integral bound, not the L-infinity-in-space history estimate required
by B_geo. Concentrated receivers need further control.

Joint geometry matters to the estimate. If omega=c as in the entire
ABC calibration, then b=0, b_j=0 and K_b=0 along its compatible spatial
variations. The angular cost in (461) is zero. Bounding the two directions
independently would obscure this exact cancellation.

For mu>0 the cellular calculation remains informative. Its viscous
coefficient, before multiplication by nu*t^2, is

```text
4a^8[2a^6+10a^4delta+3a^2delta mu-delta^2 mu]
 /[(a^2+delta)^3(2a^2+mu)^2].
```

At delta=a^2 this is `a^6(6a^2+mu)/(2a^2+mu)^2>0` for every mu>0.
Consequently the sign failure is not caused by a singular convention at
c=0. As mu decreases to zero, Phi_mu increases to Phi with its zero
convention. A bound uniform in mu for the ORIGINAL critical history norm
would pass to the limit. Neither such a bound nor uniform control of
K_b near c=0 has been proved by (461).

### Why a convex local replacement loses some aligned zeros

There is also a small algebraic obstruction to a particular repair.
Keep I=-e1 and compare the two joint states

```text
(omega,c)=(e2,e2),      (omega,c)=(e3,2e3).
```

Both have Phi_mu=0, since omega and c are parallel. At their midpoint,
J=1/4 and

```text
Phi_mu=1/[16(delta+1/2)(mu+5/4)]>0.                 (462)
```

A jointly convex local majorant of Phi_mu cannot be zero at both
endpoints: convexity would make its midpoint value nonpositive. This
is an obstruction to convexification on that joint state domain, not a
proof that these states are freely selectable NS histories or that all
history-dependent reserves fail. Reconstruction must retain which
orientations and amplitudes were paired before averaging.

### Verification and the next physical obligation

Run `python3 -O labs/geometric_diffusion_cost.py`. It checks the complete
unforced cellular PDE, vorticity and curl-observer equations; independent
Hessian calculations for all positive parameters; the smooth-regularizer
coefficient; the exact 3D source; the joint square in (460); and the strict
convexification gap. Python compilation is also checked. No new Lean
axioms, declarations, numerical trajectories or singular solutions are
introduced.

The failed assertion is nonpositivity of the LOCAL viscous chain source,
including its repair by a finite multiple of |I|^2. The global finite-datum
allowance is not refuted. A continuation proof must pay the combined
pressure and joint angular history, with spatial concentration controlled,
or use the earlier signed deformation target to avoid overcharging this
observation. The harmless cellular flow remains an essential calibration:
its geometric observation can grow although its actual stretching is zero.

## Physical enstrophy receiver and a diffusion feedback budget

The continuation argument can retain the flow's own spatial weighting
instead of replacing it by a maximum over all receivers. This keeps an
intermediate Cauchy--Schwarz estimate in the geometric energy method of
[Chae--Lee](https://arxiv.org/html/1606.08126), combined with the original
passive/impulse decomposition. It gives a different sufficient history
target and a precise diffusion-feedback allowance. The required
original-data bound is still open; this is not a new unconditional
regularity theorem.

### A finite global normalization

On an actual smooth unforced prefix on R3 or the fixed torus, retain
D_u H=0, H(0)=u0, I=H-u and D_u I=grad p. Set M=||u0||_infinity and
fix zeta>0 from the original datum, viscosity and prescribed horizon,
before considering any future prefix. Define

```text
e=|omega|^2, c=curl omega, J=-(I cross omega).c,
W=J_+^2/|c|^2 if c!=0, and 0 if c=0,
Z=integral e, Y=Z+zeta, D=integral |grad omega|^2,
Theta=(integral W)/Y, d=D/Y.                         (463)
```

The offset zeta is added to the FINITE global enstrophy; it is not
constant spatial mass on R3. Where omega,c are nonzero, put
`a_0=J_+/(|omega||c|)`, with zero elsewhere. Then
`Theta=integral a_0^2 rho`, where `rho=e/Y` is the actual subprobability
density. Also W<=|I|^2 e. No derivative of W or its positive part is
needed in the continuation argument below.

All interactions are summed before taking J_+. Original H, pressure,
phases and incoming impulse are retained through every segment. The
weight rho is fixed by the actual solution; it is not an independently
chosen concentrating control or a passively transported density.

### Direct continuation from the physical geometric history

The actual integrated Lamb identity and ||H||_infinity<=M give

```text
g=integral omega.(grad u)omega
 <=sqrt(D)[M sqrt(Z)+sqrt(integral W)]
 <=sqrt(Y D)(M+sqrt(Theta)),
Y'=2g-2nu D,
Y'+nu D <=2(M^2+Theta)Y/nu.                         (464)
```

Suppose B_phys is finite, fixed from the original resources, and bounds
`integral_0^t Theta` for EVERY available same-datum prefix and every
endpoint t<=T. Writing Y0=Z0+zeta, Gronwall gives
`Y(t)+nu integral_0^t D<=Y0 exp[2(M^2T+B_phys)/nu]`.
Equivalently the nonnegative reserve

```text
r(t)=2[M^2(T-t)+B_phys-integral_0^t Theta]/nu,
R(t)=(exp(r(t))-1)Y(t)
```

obeys `R'+2g-nu D<=0`. Thus an explicit original signed-renewal
allowance is

```text
K=Y0[exp(2(M^2T+B_phys)/nu)-1]+2T|g(0)|.
```

It matches the quantified hypothesis of
`JointCubicRenewal.hasNSEvolution_of_signed_renewal` on R3 and gives
the uniform H1 estimate used by periodic continuation. The spatial
identities and passive construction remain analytic. The existing
Lean consumer does not prove the new B_phys hypothesis.

The previous supremum criterion implies this target quantitatively.
For any fixed delta>0 in (449), `W=a_delta^2(e+delta)` and the existing
impulse-energy bound give

```text
Theta <= ||a_delta||_infinity^2 +4delta E0/zeta.
```

With the unregularized a_0, the sharper direct comparison is
`Theta<=||a_0||_infinity^2 Z/(Z+zeta)`. These comparisons explain the
smaller observation being requested. They do not assert a new class of
unforced singular solutions separating two sufficient criteria.

### Feedback below the full normalized dissipation

An allowance may also let the geometric cost use some of the same
physical diffusion. Fix 0<=alpha<1 and put kappa=1-alpha. The proposed
remaining estimate is

```text
C(t)=integral_0^t [Theta-alpha nu^2 d] <=B0           (465)
```

for all the same original-data prefixes, with one finite B0>=0 fixed
from the original resources. This is a substantive OPEN inequality,
not a definition of B0 by the unknown future. Neither alpha nor zeta
may be chosen adaptively from an unknown future solution.

To see why (465) suffices, let L=log Y. Retaining the passive term
linearly in (464), rather than combining it with Theta too early, gives

```text
L'+2nu d <=2M sqrt(d)+2sqrt(Theta d),
L'+kappa nu d <=C'/nu+2M sqrt(d).
```

The coefficient range alpha<1 follows from these actual inequalities.
It does not claim an optimal threshold for the fluid equation.
The complete logarithmic reserve is

```text
R_log=log(Y/zeta)+(B0-C)/nu+2M^2(T-t)/(kappa nu)>=0,
R_log'+(kappa nu/2)d<=0.                             (466)
```

Indeed, let
`gap=2(M+sqrt(Theta))sqrt(d)-(L'+2nu d)>=0` and
`S_Theta=(sqrt(Theta/nu)-sqrt(nu d))^2`. The exact remainder in (466) is

```text
R_log'+(kappa nu/2)d
 =-gap-S_Theta
       -[sqrt(kappa nu/2)sqrt(d)-sqrt(2/(kappa nu))M]^2.
```

Every term uses the same actual history. The expenditure C can decrease
when diffusion pays it, but no new B0 is issued at a join. The original
zeta, H and accumulated C persist across the join.

Set L0=log(Y0/zeta). It follows that

```text
integral_0^t d <=Q_star,
Q_star=2[L0+B0/nu+2M^2 T/(kappa nu)]/(kappa nu),
Y(t)<=Y_max=Y0 exp[(B0+M^2T/kappa)/nu].               (467)
```

For the second estimate use
`2M sqrt(d)-kappa nu d<=M^2/(kappa nu)` before integrating.
Consequently `integral_0^t D<=Y_max Q_star`, and one direct
signed-renewal allowance is

```text
K=(Y_max-Y0)+nu Y_max Q_star+2T|g(0)|.
```

This follows from `2 integral(g-g(0))=Z(t)-Z0+2nu integral D-2t g(0)`.
All constants are prescribed original resources IF (465) is proved.
The feedback assumption also supplies the earlier sufficient budget
`B_phys=B0+alpha nu^2 Q_star`.

### The physical receiver carries its own reaction and diffusion

The density rho=e/Y has mass Z/Y. The remaining scalar mass zeta/Y
can be recorded at an auxiliary point so that total mass is one; that
point is bookkeeping, not an additional fluid component. Put
`A=2omega.(Bomega)-2nu|grad omega|^2`, B=grad u. Directly from NS,

```text
D_u rho=A/Y-(Z'/Y)rho,
(d/dt)(zeta/Y)=-(Z'/Y)(zeta/Y),
Z'=integral A.                                      (468)
```

This equation retains local stretching, diffusion and the evolving
global normalization. It is nonsingular at omega=0 and is not the
passive diffusion equation. In particular, replacing rho by a convenient
heat kernel would change the observation being estimated.

There is an exact physical interpretation of the d paid in (466).
On omega!=0 let n=omega/|omega|. With the usual weak derivatives at
zeros, the norm-gradient identity gives

```text
d=(1/4)Fisher(rho)+integral rho|grad n|^2,
Fisher(rho)=integral_{rho>0}|grad rho|^2/rho.
```

To verify it, write
`|grad omega|^2=|grad |omega||^2+|omega|^2|grad n|^2`
where omega!=0. On its zero set the derivative of the smooth vector
field vanishes almost everywhere, so no spatial integral is lost.
Under the OPEN feedback hypothesis this yields
`integral_0^t Fisher(rho)<=4Q_star` and
`integral_0^t integral rho|grad n|^2<=Q_star`.
Thus concentration and direction variation spend the same normalized
dissipation. These conclusions are conditional; Fisher information
alone is not asserted to bound the density's spatial maximum in 3D.
The continuation argument uses the physical energy inequality directly.

The earlier unweighted impulse payment does NOT automatically pay
`integral rho|grad I|^2`. The normalized receiver's source and its
correlation with I still have to enter the estimate for (465).

### Entire eigenflow histories and the actual forced obstruction

Take any smooth periodic steady Euler field U with
`-Delta U=k^2 U`, k>0. The actual unforced solution
`u=a exp(-nu k^2t)U` has c=k^2u, so its full Lamb work vanishes
pointwise. Retaining its original passive H gives
`J=-(H cross omega).c`, hence W<=M^2 e. Its enstrophy is
`Z=Z0 exp(-2nu k^2t)`. Therefore, for all t>=0,

```text
integral_0^t Theta
 <=M^2/(2nu k^2) log[(Z0+zeta)/(Z0 exp(-2nu k^2t)+zeta)]
 <=M^2/(2nu k^2) log(1+Z0/zeta),
integral_0^t d=log[(Z0+zeta)/(Z(t)+zeta)]/(2nu).     (469)
```

This is an explicit finite payment over ALL time for this entire known
solution family, without small-amplitude assumptions or H=u. It improves
on charging M^2 once per unit time in the earlier coarse calibration.
For the decaying ABC family W=0 exactly, a stronger statement. For the
cellular family the actual stretching is zero while the geometric
observation need not be; (469) pays that harmless observation.
No payment for arbitrary mutually amplifying parents follows.

For the ONE actual imported whole-space forced candidate, H=0,I=-u,
and `F_star=sup_t||f(t)||_2^2<infinity`. Retain any fixed zeta>0.
The forced enstrophy equation and Cauchy--Schwarz give

```text
(log Y)'+2nu d
 <=2sqrt(Theta d)+2sqrt(F_star/zeta)sqrt(d).          (470)
```

Thus the same feedback proof applies with M replaced by
`sqrt(F_star/zeta)`. If C(t) in (465) had a finite upper bound through
time1 for ANY fixed alpha<1, it would give a uniform gradient-energy
bound. This contradicts the existing Lean theorem
`ForcedCandidatePancake.no_uniform_gradient_energy` on that SAME
candidate. Accordingly C(t) has no finite upper bound there; in
particular its integral of Theta is infinite. This uses the exact
imported force assumptions. It neither constructs internal realization
by unforced fluid nor excludes such realization by an arbitrary datum.

### Checks and the remaining physical estimate

Run `python3 -O labs/physical_geometric_receiver.py`. Exact checks cover
the direct reserve, the complete logarithmic reserve square, feedback
constants, full receiver equations through their first evolving derivative
on two genuine 3D NS data, mass preservation including the scalar remainder,
the concentration/direction identity, and the entire eigenflow integral.
Canonical pressure and every generated Fourier output are retained.
The earlier eigenflow checks establish the literal PDEs. No truncated
finite-mode dynamics is used as an evolution.

These calculations identify sufficient targets (463) and (465) and
positive calibrations. Their arbitrary-data payment, passive/stochastic
construction, PDE integration and continuation assembly remain analytic
obligations, not new Lean certificates. The next estimate should use the
ACTUAL reaction (468), original pressure impulse and compatible joint

available alternatives; no equivalence or completed regularity proof is
asserted by this reformulation.


## Solenoidal geometric observations and a complete two-coordinate payment

A geometric observation should discard fields that do no integrated
stretching work before charging their positive part. This can be done
exactly, using the Hilbert-space cone projection of
[Moreau](https://www.numdam.org/article/BSMF_1965__93__273_0.pdf).
The resulting observation has a complete original-data payment for the
known three-component, two-coordinate NS class. The arbitrary 3D
history payment remains open. The argument below and its physical
integration are analytic, not new Lean-certified regularity results.

### The actual curl imposes a compatibility constraint

On R3 or the fixed normalized 2*pi torus, let
`F=u cross omega=(H-I) cross omega`, `c=curl omega` and `Y=Z+zeta`
as above. All products belong to L2 on a smooth prefix. In the real
Hilbert space of L2 vector fields, set

```text
C_c={a c: a>=0 measurable, a c in L2},
S={v in L2: div v=0 distributionally},
K_c=C_c intersect S,
Q_c(F)=projection of F onto K_c,
Theta_Q=||Q_c(F)||_2^2/Y.                           (471)
```

Each ray cone C_c is closed and convex: use an almost-everywhere
convergent subsequence of any strongly convergent L2 sequence, with
zero value required where c=0. S is a closed linear subspace. Thus K_c
is a closed convex cone containing 0 and the actual c. Moreau's polar
decomposition gives

```text
<F,c> <= <Q_c(F),c> <= ||Q_c(F)||_2 ||c||_2,
||Q_c(F)||_2=sup{<F,v>: v in K_c, ||v||_2<=1}.
```

Here `<F,c>` is precisely the integrated vorticity stretching g. The
constraint is spatial and joint: for smooth a, `div(a c)=c.grad a=0`.
Thus admissible weights must agree along the actual c curves. They
are not independently selected positive weights in separate patches,
and these c curves are not asserted to be material trajectories.

There is also a constructive upper-bound form. Let G=S-perp be the
closed L2 space of gradients, and put

```text
P_c(V)=integral [(V.c)_+]^2/|c|^2, with value0 at c=0.
||Q_c(F)||_2^2=inf_{g in G} P_c(F-g).                (472)
```

Indeed, C_c's polar consists of fields r with r.c<=0. The polar of
K_c is the closure of G plus that polar cone. Distance to this closure
and Moreau's decomposition give (472). The sum need not be closed;
no minimizing smooth potential is assumed. Every explicit gradient
witness g gives a rigorous upper bound. A countable dense subset of G
suffices because the ray-cone projection is nonexpansive. This also
makes Theta_Q measurable along smooth prefixes, including changing
zero sets of c. The projection norm is bounded by ||F||_2, so the cost is locally
integrable on each smooth prefix. Derivatives involving its cumulative
cost are understood almost everywhere; the reserves are locally absolutely
continuous. No time derivative of the moving projection is used.

Both gradients and fields pointwise orthogonal to c can therefore be
removed. Plain Leray projection removes only the former. The exact
checker below includes an actual planar datum with nonzero Leray Lamb
energy but zero cost in (471).

The original passive/impulse split remains available. Applying (471)
to `-I cross omega` gives a cost no greater than Theta in (463), since
K_c is contained in C_c. For the FULL joint cost,

```text
sqrt(Theta_Q)<=M sqrt(Z/Y)+sqrt(Theta).
```

This is a quantitative comparison, not an assertion that every feedback
hypothesis with the same alpha transfers unchanged. Taking positive
parts of independent parents still loses their joint cancellation.

### The finite-history consumer

For an actual unforced prefix, g<=sqrt(Y D Theta_Q) and
`Y'=2g-2nu D`. Fix one 0<=alpha<1, write kappa=1-alpha and suppose

```text
C_Q(t)=integral_0^t[Theta_Q-alpha nu^2 D/Y]<=B_Q,
R_Q=log(Y/zeta)+(B_Q-C_Q)/nu>=0,
R_Q'+kappa nu D/Y<=0.                               (473)
```

The FIRST line is the OPEN arbitrary-data estimate; the remaining
lines follow from it. B_Q must be fixed from the original datum,
viscosity and prescribed horizon, uniformly over every available
same-datum prefix. It is not defined by an uncontrolled future supremum.
The exact derivative defect is
`-gap-(sqrt(Theta_Q/nu)-sqrt(nu D/Y))^2`, where
`gap=2sqrt(Theta_Q D/Y)-[(log Y)'+2nu D/Y]>=0`.

Consequently

```text
Y<=Y_max=Y0 exp(B_Q/nu),
integral D/Y<=Q_star=[log(Y0/zeta)+B_Q/nu]/(kappa nu),
integral D<=Y_max Q_star,
K=(Y_max-Y0)+nu Y_max Q_star+2T|g(0)|.
```

This K supplies the same signed-renewal consumer as (467). The analytic
R3 and periodic continuation connections are unchanged. The original
H, I, zeta, actual solution and accumulated expenditure remain the same
at every join; projecting an observation does not reconstruct or alter
the fluid. The new projection is not an additional stochastic control.

### An exact cancellation for every planar nonlinear flow

Work on the torus in the frame that removes the original constant
horizontal mean. For arbitrary smooth functions psi(x,y), v(x,y), let

```text
u=(psi_y,-psi_x,v), q=-Delta_h psi,
omega=(v_y,-v_x,q), c=(q_y,-q_x,-Delta_h v),
chi=-psi q+v^2/2,
F-grad chi=(psi q_x,psi q_y,-u_h.grad_h v),
(F-grad chi).c=(u_h.grad_h v) Delta_h v.              (474)
```

These are pointwise identities, with no assumption that psi is steady,
small, or confined to one Laplacian eigenspace. If v=0, the residual is
orthogonal to c everywhere. The explicit gradient witness in (472)
proves Theta_Q=0 for EVERY such planar state, and hence along its
entire actual nonlinear history. No artificial positive geometric
charge remains on the cellular example.

The checker uses
`psi=sin x sin y+(sin 2x)/3`. Its raw signed observation is nonzero,
its Leray-projected Lamb energy is 1/15, but its reduced cost is zero.
This distinguishes the joint cancellation from a mere pressure projection.

### Full payment for the three-component two-coordinate class

For an actual unforced flow of the form (474), u_h obeys autonomous
2D NS and v obeys its passive advection-diffusion equation. Write

```text
E_h=||u_h||_2^2, Z_h=||q||_2^2, D_h=||grad_h q||_2^2.
E_h'+2nu Z_h=0, Z_h'+2nu D_h=0,
Theta_Q<=||u_h||_infinity^2 ||grad_h v||_2^2/Y
       <=||u_h||_infinity^2.                        (475)
```

The first inequality uses the explicit witness (474) and
`|Delta_h v|<=|c|`, including zero sets. The existing Lean lattice
inequality `FourierAgmon.sq_sum_le_agmon` has constant104. Applied to
the nonzero Fourier amplitudes of u_h, then passed to the smooth
Fourier limit on the normalized 2*pi torus, it gives

```text
||u_h||_infinity^2<=104 sqrt(Z_h D_h),
integral_0^t Theta_Q
 <=104 sqrt[(integral_0^t Z_h)(integral_0^t D_h)]
 <=(52/nu)sqrt(E_h(0)Z_h(0))=:B_plane.              (476)
```

The Fourier limit and PDE application are analytic here; the lattice
inequality itself is already Lean-certified. This bound holds on every
available prefix, with the SAME constant independent of its length.
There is no smallness restriction on either horizontal motion or v.
Combining (473) at alpha=0 with (476) yields uniform enstrophy and a
finite total dissipation allowance; continuation closes this known
regular class. This is a new calibration of the observation, not a
claim to have newly discovered regularity of two-coordinate flows.

The vertical component need not have zero stretching. For the same psi
and `v=sin x-sin(2x+y)`, the actual initial g is 1/2. Thus (476) pays
real amplification as well as changing horizontal geometry. The exact
checker retains its evolving pressure and the first evolving identity
(474). No closed finite Fourier system is substituted for the NS flow.

### The precise defect when hidden modes feed the parent

For a genuine 3D flow, let U be its actual average in z, w=u-U,
Omega=curl U, eta=curl w, C=curl Omega and c_w=curl eta. Retain every
term in

```text
N=U cross eta+w cross Omega+w cross eta,
F(u)-grad chi_U=R_U+N,
(F(u)-grad chi_U).c
 =(U_h.grad_h U_3)Delta_h U_3+R_U.c_w+N.(C+c_w),    (477)
```

where R_U is the explicit residual in (474) for U. The last two terms
measure what the exact two-coordinate cancellation leaves on the
ACTUAL full curl observer. Projecting separately onto cones made from
C and c_w would change the observation.

Moreover U is not an autonomous solution. With Sigma=average_z(w tensor w),

```text
U_t+(U.grad)U+grad p_bar-nu Delta U=-div Sigma=:f_R,
E_h'+2nu Z_h=2 integral U_h.f_R,h,
Z_h'+2nu D_h=2 integral q (curl f_R)_3.             (478)
```

The sources in (478) are generated by the SAME unforced fluid. Their
payment is required before reusing B_plane; the pressure and source
cannot be dropped by calling U a known planar parent.

A small exact construction makes this obstruction active. Set

```text
p=sin(x+z), r=sin(y-z), w=(p+r,r,-p+r),
U_plus=(-sin(x+y),sin(x+y),0)/8,
U_minus=-U_plus, u_plus/minus=U_plus/minus+w.
```

These are smooth divergence-free NS initial data at nu=1, with zero
z-average of w. Both have E_h(0)=1/64 and Z_h(0)=1/32. The hidden stress
gives horizontal energy sources +1/8 and -1/8 and enstrophy sources
+1/4 and -1/4 respectively. Consequently the plus case has ACTUAL
`E_h'(0)=1/16` and `Z_h'(0)=1/8`: the parent grows while the whole
fluid's kinetic energy decreases. The return case has rates -3/16 and
-3/8. Continuity supplies genuine short intervals with these strict signs.
This is internal energy transfer, not external forcing or a singularity.

There is also actual creation of the improved geometric cost. Both data
satisfy c=2u initially, so F.c=0 pointwise and Theta_Q(0)=0. Nevertheless
the complete NS derivative gives `g'(0)=547/128>0` in both cases. With
zeta=Z0=161/32, the lower bound
`Theta_Q>=g_+^2/(D Y)` yields

```text
Theta_Q(t)>=(299209/1658944)t^2+O(t^3)
```

on their actual short histories. The zero-cost set is not invariant under
unforced evolution. The two cases even have the same initial onset of
stretching despite opposite energy transfers into the average. These are
finite bursts paid by their full datum; no failure of a finite integrated
allowance is inferred. Scaling the entire initial datum by A>0 gives
`g'(0)=A^4(547/128)` at every positive viscosity, since the initial cubic
g is zero and the viscous tangent is -2nu u. In the plus case the parent
energy rate is `A^2(2A-nu)/16`, positive whenever A>nu/2.

### Pressure is retained in the evolving physical state

For arbitrary unforced flow the literal equation is

```text
F=u_t+nu c+grad(p+|u|^2/2).                         (479)
```

A gradient is invisible to (471), but pressure still determines u and
c through their evolution. Removing a gradient from an observation does
not remove pressure, hidden memory or covariance from that evolution.
With an applied force, (479) has the additional term -f on its right.

For the one imported forced whole-space candidate, the enstrophy
inequality for (471) is (470), with Theta replaced by Theta_Q and
`F_star=sup||f||_2^2<infinity`. The same argument with the force term
retained shows that a finite bound for C_Q for any fixed alpha<1 would
contradict `ForcedCandidatePancake.no_uniform_gradient_energy` on that
candidate. Thus this improved observation still fails the necessary
forced test. No exclusion of arbitrary internal realization follows.

Run `python3 -O labs/solenoidal_geometric_cost.py`. Exact checks cover
the conditional reserve, constant52, planar and three-component witness
identities and their first evolving derivative, four complete 3D pressure
fixtures, Reynolds forcing, the planted transfers and the evolving
acceleration identity. The Hilbert reduction, general physical prefix
arguments, stochastic identification and arbitrary-data payment are not
certified by those finite checks. No Lean declarations are changed.

### The actual internally fed mean can still be absorbed

The loss of autonomy in (478) need not prevent a payment for U's
contribution. On the torus, keep the full three-component U=average_z u
in the once-fixed zero-mean frame. Let
`Z_U=||grad U||_2^2`, `D_U=||Delta U||_2^2`, and E=||u||_2^2.
Orthogonality of the coordinate average gives

```text
Z_U<=Z, D_U<=D, E'=-2nu Z,
integral_0^t Z_U<=E0/(2nu).
```

None of these statements assumes that U is autonomous or that its
own energy or enstrophy decreases. The planted example satisfies them.

A two-dimensional logarithmic Fourier estimate supplies the remaining
spatial step. It is a periodic version of the
[Brézis--Gallouët logarithmic estimate](https://doi.org/10.1016/0362-546X(80)90068-1).
For Z_U>0,

```text
||U||_infinity^2<=48 Z_U log(e+D_U/Z_U).             (480)
```

Here is a direct constant check for the normalized 2*pi torus. A square
Fourier shell of sup radius j contains 8j nonzero lattice points. A
cutoff at integer N>=1 gives

```text
(sum_low |U_hat|)^2<=8 Z_U(1+log N),
(sum_high |U_hat|)^2<=4 D_U/N^2,
||U||_infinity^2<=16 Z_U(1+log N)+8 D_U/N^2.
```

Take N=ceil(sqrt(D_U/Z_U)); D_U>=Z_U implies
`N<=2sqrt(D_U/Z_U)`. The right side is at most
`Z_U[24+16log2+8log(D_U/Z_U)]`, which is bounded by (480).
This applies to vector amplitudes and all three components of U.
If Z_U=0, the mean-zero U vanishes and the estimate is unnecessary.
The infinite Fourier passage is analytic, not a new Lean declaration.

Fix 0<=alpha<1 before considering any future prefix. Retain the SAME
full c and omega in the fluctuation cost

```text
w=u-U, theta_w=||Q_c(w cross omega)||_2^2/Y,
C_w(t)=integral_0^t[theta_w-alpha nu^2 d]<=B_w,
d=D/Y, kappa=1-alpha>0.                             (481)
```

The second line is the remaining OPEN original-data hypothesis, uniformly
on all same-datum prefixes. w is the actual fluctuation; it is not an
independently evolving fluid, and omega and c are not replaced by its
own vorticity or curl. Subadditivity of the support function in (471)
gives the physical inequality
`g<=sqrt(YD)(||U||_infinity+sqrt(theta_w))`.
This split can overcharge cancellation between U and w; no inequality
`theta_w<=Theta_Q` is asserted. The mean contribution is retained and
paid by the following estimate. Neither component is chosen independently.

Put h=log(Y/zeta), `ell=log(e+384zeta/(kappa^2 nu^2))` and
`A=96/(kappa nu)`. For every epsilon>0,
`log(e+r)<=epsilon r+log(e+1/epsilon)`. Applying this with
`epsilon=kappa^2 nu^2/(384Y)` in (480) yields

```text
||U||_infinity^2<=(kappa^2 nu^2/8)d+48 Z_U(ell+h),
h'+(kappa nu/4)d<=C_w'/nu+A Z_U(ell+h).             (482)
```

The second inequality uses the two Young squares for the fluctuation
and mean terms in the actual enstrophy equation. In particular, the
logarithmic factor has not been replaced by an assumed future norm.
It is paid by the explicit nonnegative reserve

```text
R=exp[48E/(kappa nu^2)] [ell+h+(B_w-C_w)/nu],
R'<=-(kappa nu/4)exp[48E/(kappa nu^2)]d.             (483)
```

To check the source sign, write b=(B_w-C_w)/nu>=0. After removing
the nonnegative gap in (482), the derivative divided by the exponential
is at most

```text
-(kappa nu/4)d-A[(Z-Z_U)(ell+h)+Z b].
```

Every bracket is nonnegative. This uses the ACTUAL full energy law;
it does not restart an energy reserve for the averaged parent or drop
its Reynolds stress. Thus the mean's contribution can be absorbed even
when hidden modes repeatedly feed it, subject to the remaining fluctuation
allowance. No independent bound on its future supremum is assumed.

All resulting constants are original resources IF (481) holds. Set

```text
R0=exp[48E0/(kappa nu^2)] [ell+log(Y0/zeta)+B_w/nu],
h_max=R0-ell, Y_max=zeta exp(h_max),
Q_star=4h_max/(kappa nu).
```

Since R>=ell, (483) gives `Y<=Y_max`, `integral d<=Q_star` and
`integral D<=Y_max Q_star`. The signed-renewal allowance K has the same
explicit form as after (473). This mean/fluctuation reduction is
periodic; no coordinate average over an infinite R3 axis is substituted.
The full-space criterion (473) remains a separate available target.

The checker retains the average/fluctuation orthogonality and full
energy identity on all four physical 3D fixtures, as well as the exact
reserve and its source signs. The generic logarithmic inequality,
PDE integration and continuation assembly remain analytic.

The next physical task is now sharper: pay the fluctuation budget (481)
from the original FULL fluid, retaining the actual interactions with U.
The mean contribution has been absorbed without an autonomous-parent
hypothesis. This does not pay theta_w or complete arbitrary-data
regularity; the full vorticity and curl in that remaining cost are
essential to its physical meaning.


## Fixed spectral bands and coherent generation of stretching

The mean payment extends to any fixed finite band of vertical frequencies,
even while those modes exchange energy with the rest of an actual NS flow.
The resulting tail cannot be assumed to start dissipatively: two elliptically
polarized parent waves generate positive signed tail stretching from an empty
tail. Separating their polarization contributions loses the term responsible
for that sign. A two-coordinate version has a complete finite-horizon payment;
adding a third-coordinate parent retains the positive onset, but its general
history payment remains open. The PDE results here are analytic, with exact
algebraic checks, not new Lean certificates.

### A fixed band can be paid without closing its dynamics

Keep the normalized 2*pi torus and the original zero-mean Galilean frame.
Choose an integer N>=0 before examining any future solution prefix. Let
P_N retain all frequencies with |k_z|<=N, set V=P_N u, w=u-V and m=2N+1.
This band has infinitely many horizontal frequencies; it is not a finite
Galerkin state. The actual equation for V retains every interaction with w.

Write Z_V=||grad V||_2^2, D_V=||Delta V||_2^2. Fourier orthogonality gives
Z_V<=Z and D_V<=D, while the FULL energy satisfies E'=-2nu Z. The periodic
logarithmic estimate used in (480) becomes

```text
||V||_infinity^2 <= 48m Z_V log(e+D_V/Z_V).          (484)
```

For completeness, a horizontal shell of sup radius j contains at most
8mj frequencies in this band. Frequencies on the vertical axis contribute
at most `2 sum_{j>=1}1/j^2<=4` to the inverse-square sum. Splitting at
horizontal radius L>=1 therefore gives

```text
(sum_low |V_hat|)^2 <= Z_V[8m(1+log L)+4],
(sum_high |V_hat|)^2 <= 4m D_V/L^2.
```

For Z_V>0, put r=D_V/Z_V>=1 and L=ceil(sqrt r). Twice the sum of these
bounds is at most `m Z_V[32+16log2+8log r]`, which is bounded by (484).
Indeed `48log(e+r)-8log r` is increasing for r>=1 and exceeds48 at r=1,
whereas `32+16log2<48`. If Z_V=0 the mean-zero V vanishes. This derivation
uses the same logarithmic Fourier mechanism as Brézis--Gallouët above.

With the FULL omega and c from (471), define

```text
theta_N=||Q_c(w cross omega)||_2^2/Y,
C_N(t)=integral_0^t[theta_N-alpha nu^2 D/Y],
0<=alpha<1, kappa=1-alpha.                         (485)
```

The remaining hypothesis is ONE finite B_N(u0,nu,T)>=0 with C_N<=B_N
for every available same-datum prefix through T. N, alpha and zeta>0
are fixed from original resources. There is no such arbitrary-data
bound proved here. Substituting (484) into the argument of (482) gives

```text
ell_N=log(e+384m zeta/(kappa^2 nu^2)), h=log(Y/zeta),
h'+kappa nu d/4 <= C_N'/nu + 96m Z_V(ell_N+h)/(kappa nu),
R_N=exp[48m E/(kappa nu^2)] [ell_N+h+(B_N-C_N)/nu],
R_N' <= -(kappa nu/4) exp[48m E/(kappa nu^2)] d.    (486)
```

After dividing the derivative by the exponential, the additional terms are
`-96m[(Z-Z_V)(ell_N+h)+Z(B_N-C_N)/nu]/(kappa nu)`, hence nonpositive.
Only the full energy law is used; the band's own energy can increase.
Putting h_max=R_N(0)-ell_N gives Y_max=zeta exp(h_max) and
Q_star=4h_max/(kappa nu). These bound Y, integral d and integral D exactly
as after (483), and supply the same explicit signed-renewal allowance K.
All constants depend on original resources IF the open B_N is supplied.
The factors grow with N. Letting N tend to infinity does not give a bound.

A weaker, directly signed observation also suffices in (485)--(486):
replace theta_N by
`sigma_N=(s_N)_+^2/(D Y)`, where `s_N=<w cross omega,c>` and sigma_N=0
when D=0. Indeed s_N<=sqrt(YD sigma_N), and sigma_N<=theta_N. This option
retains cancellation in the actual integrated work; no independent bounds
on spatial positive parts are necessary for this consumer. Its arbitrary
original-data payment is also open.

### A favorable isolated interaction and its exact limitation

Consider two nonparallel Fourier waves, each with a single REAL polarization,
`A cos(p.x)` and `B cos(q.x)`, with p.A=q.B=0. Common phase shifts do not
change the following coefficient calculation. The newly generated sum mode
has NS tangent `b sin((p+q).x)`, where
`b=P_{p+q}[(A.q)B+(B.p)A]/2` and P_k is the solenoidal Fourier projection.
Its first signed contribution to `<w cross omega,c>` is

```text
L=-[|q|^2 (b cross (p cross A)).B
    +|p|^2 (b cross (q cross B)).A]/4 <=0.          (487)
```

There is an explicit sum of squares. In an orthonormal basis for the
coefficient algebra, write p=(P,0,0), q=(Q,R,0), A=(0,a,b0),
B=(R c0,-Q c0,d0), K=(P+Q)^2+R^2 and M=Q+2P R^2/K. Then

```text
L=-(P^2 R^2/8) [(a d0+M b0 c0)^2
               +R^2(P^2-Q^2-R^2)^2(b0 c0)^2/K^2].
```

Choosing this basis only evaluates rotationally invariant coefficient
algebra; it does not rotate the periodic lattice into a different domain.
The parallel case has zero interaction. Replacing q by -q handles the
difference daughter. Viscosity contributes no initially absent mode, so
this first-order sign holds at every positive viscosity. It concerns this
signed work and this initial interaction, not the whole cone cost or later
returns. In particular, it does not cover elliptic polarization.

Here is the limitation on actual unforced data. Put P=2x+z and take

```text
u0=(cos z-cos P+epsilon cos y,
    -a sin P-b sin z,
    2 cos P).                                    (488)
```

This smooth mean-zero datum is divergence free. All its vertical frequencies
satisfy |k_z|<=1, so w(0)=0 for N=1. The complete pressure-projected equation
generates tail modes (+/-2,0,+/-2), with equal signs in those tuples. Exact
calculation gives, independently of epsilon and positive viscosity,

```text
s_1'(0)=-(a^2+8ab+5b^2)/2.
a=-2,b=1:  -2 -5/2 +8 = 7/2 >0.
a= 2,b=1:                  -25/2 <0.              (489)
```

The first two terms in the positive case are the separate polarization
contributions. The shared child's cross term is +8 and reverses their
combined sign. It is lost by adding separately estimated parent responses.
The two data have the same spectral kinetic energies at every frequency.
They nevertheless have opposite signed transfer into the stretching
observation. This is a finite, physical example of necessary joint phase
information.

For epsilon=1, both data depend on all three coordinates, with E0=6,
Z0=24 and D0=114. At nu=1 the positive case has s_1''(0)=-91,
||w'(0)||_2^2=3/2 and g'(0)=37/4. The second full velocity derivative
already generates |k_z|=3, so the calculation has not closed the band.
The negative case has g'(0)=85/4: the sign of this tail contribution is
not the sign of the complete stretching derivative. Smooth local existence
and continuity give actual intervals with s_1>0 or s_1<0, respectively.
For the positive case and zeta=Z0,
`theta_1(t)>=sigma_1(t)=(49/21888)t^2+O(t^3)`.
No differentiability of the moving cone projection is assumed here.

### Positive viscosity does not automatically pay newly generated modes

The initial calculation gives a genuine obstruction to a pointwise payment,
not merely a formal tangent. Fix the positive epsilon=1 datum Phi in (488).
For 0<mu<=1, standard local Sobolev energy estimates give a common interval
for the smooth NS solution v_mu starting at Phi. Their bounds are uniform
in mu: viscosity is dissipative in the velocity estimate. Choose sufficiently
many Sobolev derivatives, for example H^12, so the first two time derivatives
of s_1 are uniformly bounded as well. Thus there is a fixed small tau0>0
and an interval J=[tau0/2,tau0] on which s_1(v_mu)>=c0>0 and D(v_mu)<=D_*
for every 0<mu<=1. These constants come from the fixed smooth datum, not an
assumed future regularity bound. D stays positive after shortening tau0.

For any prescribed nu>0 and amplitude A>=nu, set
`u_A(t)=A v_{nu/A}(At)`. This is an ACTUAL unforced NS solution at viscosity
nu, with datum A Phi and the SAME initially empty N=1 tail. On J/A,

```text
theta_1/(nu^2 d) >= sigma_1/(nu^2 d)
                  =s_1(u_A)^2/(nu^2 D(u_A)^2)
                  >=A^2 c0^2/(nu^2 D_*^2).        (490)
```

Here the positive signed work scales as A^3 and D as A^2. The comparison
is independent of the choice of zeta>0. Consequently no fixed alpha<1
gives theta_1<=alpha nu^2 d on all these histories merely because the tail
was initially empty. The sharper signed observation fails that claim too.
The failure is in genuine three-dimensional unforced dynamics.

With zeta=Z(u_A(0))=24A^2, the same local bounds give constants c,C>0,
independent of A and nu, such that at t=tau0/A
`C_1(t)>=c A-C nu^2/A`. In obtaining this cumulative bound, integrate the
positive cost over J/A and bound the negative diffusion term on the ENTIRE
interval [0,tau0/A]. For any fixed positive horizon these endpoints lie
inside it once A is large. Thus an allowance based only on the empty initial
tail, the prescribed cutoff, viscosity and horizon cannot pay these bursts.
This does not refute an allowance depending on the FULL datum or a different
datum-chosen cutoff. It does not construct indefinite renewal or blowup.

### A full-data payment for the two-coordinate version

The epsilon=0 positive example has a useful complete payment. Its (x,z)
velocity is an autonomous planar NS flow; its y component is a passive
scalar. For the unscaled datum their planar energy and enstrophy are
E_h0=3 and Z_h0=13, and the passive supremum is at most3. The actual prefix
energy/enstrophy estimates used in (476) give
`integral ||u_h||_infinity^2<=52sqrt(E_h0 Z_h0)/nu`, while the passive
maximum principle gives ||u_y(t)||_infinity<=||u_y0||_infinity.

For any fixed N the Fourier projection obeys ||P_N||_{L-infinity->L-infinity}
<=m, by its Dirichlet kernel or the sum of its m coefficient projections.
Hence ||w||_infinity<=(m+1)||u||_infinity and theta_N<=||w||_infinity^2.
For N=1 and datum A Phi with epsilon=0 this proves, on every prefix through T,

```text
integral theta_1 <=16 A^2 [52sqrt(39)/nu+9T].       (491)
```

This supplies B_1 in (485), even with alpha=0, at EVERY amplitude. The finite
burst is paid by its original parents despite the failed pointwise diffusion
claim. This is a calibration in a known regular class, not new general
regularity. Adding epsilon cos y retains (489) but destroys this autonomous
planar/passive decomposition; no corresponding all-amplitude payment is
established here for that genuinely 3D case.

### The remaining history must keep the shared child

The exact tail equation can be written

```text
w(t)=exp(nu t Delta)w0
     +integral_0^t exp(nu(t-s)Delta)(1-P_N)P_sol[u(s) cross omega(s)] ds.
```

Its signed stretching uses this SAME w(t), omega(t) and c(t). In particular,
each source time is paired with the actual receiver at t; independent phase
averages do not reconstruct the observed +8 term. This is related to the
hidden-mode history addressed by [Hald--Stinis's t-model analysis](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.0700084104).
That work proves properties of a reduced model; it does not supply the
arbitrary NS tail payment used here. We retain the exact evolution and do
not substitute a first memory term for its later history.

The next physical estimate must pay the coherent cross term and subsequent
returns together, after the full band contribution has been absorbed by
(486). Neither isolated damping of polarization channels nor energy exchange
alone proves that estimate. The original-data allowance remains open on T3;
no infinite-axis average or finite-band argument on R3 is asserted.

Run `python3 -O labs/finite_band_renewal.py`. The checker verifies the general
linear-pair sum of squares, the elliptic-pair formula, four full NS jet
fixtures, their pressure and higher generated modes, the conditional reserve
and the normalization of (491). The local uniform PDE estimates, logarithmic
Fourier argument and physical continuation assembly are analytic obligations,
not proved by the finite checker. No Lean declarations or axioms change.


## Helical geometry, coherent children and a critical history reserve

Helical Fourier decomposition supplies a geometry-sensitive positive
quantity at the critical scaling. [Waleffe's triad analysis](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.858309)
describes the interaction coefficients. [Biferale--Titi](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.1215)
prove global regularity for an equation projected onto one helicity sign.
That projection changes the equation. The calculation below keeps the full
NS evolution, identifies its extra production term, and tests the first
return of generated modes. Helicity sign here is the sign of a curl Fourier
eigenvalue, not an assumption of aligned physical vorticity directions or
spatial helical symmetry. No regularity theorem for the decimated model is
asserted to apply automatically to full NS.

### The actual critical reserve and its unpaid source

On R3, or the mean-zero normalized 2*pi torus, let Lambda=sqrt(-Delta) and
P_+/-=(P_sol +/- curl/Lambda)/2. The zero mode is absent on the torus and
irrelevant to the R3 multiplier. For actual divergence-free u, define

```text
u_+=P_+ u, u_-=P_- u, omega=Lambda u_+-Lambda u_-,
M_+/-=||Lambda^(1/2)u_+/-||_2^2,
L_+/-=||Lambda^(3/2)u_+/-||_2^2,
M=M_++M_-, L=L_++L_-, H=M_+-M_-.
J=<Lambda u_-, u cross Lambda u_+>.                (492)
```

All fields come from the SAME solution. The full projected equation is
u_t=-nu Lambda^2 u+P_sol(u cross omega). Self-adjointness and orthogonality
of the fixed Fourier projections give the exact identities

```text
M_+'+2nu L_+=2J, M_-'+2nu L_-=2J,
M'+2nu L=4J, H'=-2nu(L_+-L_-).                    (493)
```

The integrated difference of the two sector balances is the critical-helicity
identity of [Lei--Lin--Zhou, Theorem 1.1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.00142).
Its signed difference and the nonnegative sum have different coercivity
properties. Their large-data constructions impose additional geometric
conditions; initial positive helicity alone is not their global theorem.

For example, pairing the negative sector with Lambda u_- eliminates the
term u cross Lambda u_- pointwise, leaving J. The positive-sector pairing
gives the same J by the scalar triple-product identity. Pressure is removed
only from these solenoidal pairings; the evolving velocity retains the full
pressure-projected equation. Signed helicity records the difference of the
two sectors. It does not bound their sum: the nonlinear source creates or
removes equal amounts in both sector balances.

There is an explicit sufficient history target. Fix 0<=alpha<1 and demand
ONE finite original-data allowance B_H>=0, uniformly on every available
same-datum prefix through the prescribed horizon, such that

```text
C_H(t)=4 integral_0^t J -2alpha nu integral_0^t L <= B_H,
R_H=M+B_H-C_H>=0,
R_H'=-2(1-alpha)nu L.                             (494)
```

The allowance in (494) is OPEN. Defining it by an uncontrolled supremum of
the future would not prove it. The identity alone is not a payment. If the
bound holds, put kappa=1-alpha and R0=M0+B_H. Then
`sup M<=R0` and `integral L<=R0/(2kappa nu)`.

Here is the direct connection to the existing gradient-energy continuation
consumer. Let S be a fixed homogeneous Sobolev constant for the domain,
valid for the mean-zero periodic velocity and vorticity when appropriate.
Retain Z=||omega||_2^2 and D=||grad omega||_2^2 from the preceding sections.
Fourier interpolation and Sobolev give

```text
Z^2<=M L, integral ||u||_6^4<=S^4 R0^2/(2kappa nu),
Z'+nu D <= [27 S^2/(16nu^3)] ||u||_6^4 Z,
Z_max=Z0 exp[27 S^6 R0^2/(32kappa nu^4)],
Z<=Z_max, integral D<=Z_max/nu.                    (495)
```

Indeed `|g|<=S^(1/2)||u||_6 Z^(1/4)D^(3/4)`. The stated Young constant
follows from the nonnegative polynomial
`x^4-2yx^3+27y^4/16=(2x-3y)^2(4x^2+4xy+3y^2)/16`.
The integrating factor for the Z inequality proves both bounds in (495).
Thus `K=2Z_max-Z0+2T|g0|` supplies the signed-renewal allowance. This
derivation applies to smooth prefixes before global existence is known;
M0 is finite for the admitted smooth data. It is analytic here, not a new
Lean-certified physical estimate.

The forced test remains discriminating. An applied force adds
`2<Lambda^(3/2)u,Lambda^(-1/2)f>` to the M balance. If its squared
H^(-1/2) norm has a finite time integral, Young's inequality leaves
`M+kappa nu integral L` bounded whenever (494) has a finite allowance.
Finite time-integrated ||f||_2^2 then also preserves a uniform Z bound in
the forced version of (495). The imported whole-space forced candidate
has these force bounds: its common compact support bounds ||f||_1 by
||f||_2, and splitting its Fourier norm at |xi|=1 bounds H^(-1/2) by
these two norms. On its shorter slabs beginning at time 1/2, a finite
uniform B_H would therefore contradict the exact Lean theorem
`ForcedCandidatePancake.no_uniform_gradient_energy`. This does not exclude
every possible internal realization of a forced pattern by surrounding fluid.

### An isolated forward interaction has a favorable helicity fraction

Consider two positive-helicity parent coefficients at nonparallel p and q,
and the solenoidal nonlinear coefficient b at k=p+q. Write P=|p|, Q=|q|,
r=|k|. The helical coupling identity gives, when the interaction is nonzero,

```text
||P_- b||^2/||P_+ b||^2 = ((P+Q-r)/(P+Q+r))^2.
If r>=max(P,Q),
||P_- b||^2 <= (1/10)||b||^2.                     (496)
```

This is a kinematic coefficient statement, not a statistical cascade
assumption. Equal-length or parallel parents may have zero interaction;
the inequality includes that case. One way to verify the identity is to
choose coefficient coordinates p=(P,0,0), q=(q1,q2,0), use helical vectors
(0,1,i) and (-q2,q1,iQ), and apply the solenoidal projection to their cross
product. If E=||b||^2 and h=Re(conj(b).(ik cross b)), the exact identity is
`h[(P+Q)^2+r^2]=2(P+Q)r^2 E`. For r<=P+Q<=2r, the fraction of total
energy in the negative sector is at most 1/10. The checker verifies both
the coefficient identity and this last scalar inequality.

### Two such pairs can create an entirely opposite-sign child

The favorable fraction (496) does not survive arbitrary coherent summation.
Here is an exact genuinely three-dimensional datum. Let R be rotation by pi/2 around the
z axis, R(x,y,z)=(-y,x,z), and choose four wave vectors and their
Fourier coefficients as follows:

```text
p=(12,0,16), A=(16,20i,-12), |p|=20,
q=(-12,0,9), B=(9,15i,12),   |q|=15,
u_hat(p)=A/2, u_hat(q)=B/2,
u_hat(Rp)=-i R(A)/2, u_hat(Rq)=R(B)/2.             (497)
```

Include the complex-conjugate coefficients at the negative wave vectors
and no others. Thus u is real, smooth, mean zero and divergence free.
Every original coefficient satisfies ik cross u_hat=|k| u_hat; there is
NO initial negative helicity. The original wave vectors span three-space.

Both pairs generate the same forward child k=(0,0,25). For the complete
nonlinear acceleration b=P_sol(u cross omega), the exact modal energies are

| Parents included | Positive-sector child energy | Negative-sector child energy | Negative fraction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| p,q | 405000 | 11250 | 1/37 |
| Rp,Rq, with the stated phase | 405000 | 11250 | 1/37 |
| All four parents | 0 | 45000 | 1 |

The positive outputs cancel; the negative outputs agree. Explicitly,

```text
b_hat(0,0,25)=(-150i,-150,0),
ik cross b_hat=-25 b_hat.                         (498)
```

All cross interactions and other children are retained: there are 12
nonzero source wave vectors. The datum has E0=1250, M0=H0=22750 and
L0=7918750. The full second velocity derivative has 60 wave vectors,
including a return to the original parents; the pressure and its first
time derivative used in those jets have 18 and 66 modes. This is not a closed
triad, a helicity projection imposed on the equation, or an externally
driven construction.

In a fixed helical basis at k, the two pair-amplitude products x,y, measured
before imposing the rotated pair's phase, are observed as `c_+(x-i y)` and
`c_-(x+i y)`, with nonzero constants c_+,c_-.
The choice x=1,y=-i erases the first observation but doubles the second.
Thus elimination that retains only the positive child output loses a
direction needed for reconstruction of the negative output. A compatible
boundary summary must retain the relevant joint phase information.

At any prescribed positive viscosity the actual smooth local solution has
u_hat(k,t)=t b_hat(k)+O(t^2), since k is initially absent. Its negative
sector energy is 45000t^2+O(t^3), whereas its positive sector energy is O(t^4).
The negative fraction therefore tends to 1. For ANY finite constant C, even
one chosen from this full datum, a bound of negative child energy by C times
positive child energy fails on sufficiently short actual intervals. The
parents' full resources can still pay an integrated allowance. This result
rules out compressing their joint state to the positive child output alone.

### The complete first return creates positive critical storage

Let b denote the entire nonlinear acceleration of (497), and put
`A_-=||Lambda^(1/2)P_- b||_2^2`. The mode in (498) and its conjugate alone
contribute 2250000 to A_-, so A_->=2250000>0. The exact full value is

```text
A_-=-15835500+190643400/sqrt(337)+462770100/sqrt(913).
M_-(t)=A_- t^2+O(t^3), J(t)=A_- t+O(t^2),
M(t)-M(exp(nu t Delta)u0)=2A_- t^2+O(t^3).         (499)
```

The last identity includes the evolving original parents, not only the
new children's energy. The complete second NS jet verifies that their
return gives exactly the stated coefficient. Initial signed-helicity
curvature agrees with the heat forecast; it does not see this increase
in the sum of the two helicity magnitudes. In particular M is not bounded
above by its original heat forecast, even on these initially one-sign data.

There is also a failure of the proposed monotone critical reserve at FIXED
positive viscosity. The same local Sobolev argument used for (490) gives a
common smooth interval for v_mu starting at (497), uniformly for 0<mu<=1.
For sufficiently many derivatives, the third derivative of M is bounded
there uniformly. Equations (493) and (499) give

```text
M(v_mu(tau))-M0
 =-2mu L0 tau+[2mu^2 ||Lambda^(5/2)u0||_2^2+2A_-]tau^2
   +O(tau^3),                                    (500)
```

with a uniform remainder. Choose a small fixed tau0, then sufficiently
small positive mu. The right side is positive. Rescaling
u_A(t)=A v_{nu/A}(At) gives actual unforced solutions at any prescribed
nu>0 for which M(u_A(tau0/A))>M(u_A(0)). It refutes both monotonicity of
M and the stronger inequality M'+nu L<=0 on all such histories. It does
not refute the open full-data allowance B_H in (494), nor exhibit repeated
unbounded creation or a singularity.

The useful remaining question is now explicit: can the ACTUAL joint
source J, including coherent opposite-sign creation and later returns,
be paid by an original-data allowance with the retained viscous fraction
in (494)? The decimated theorem supplies a positive calibration when its
opposite-sign sector is removed, but doing so is not a faithful repair of
the full equation. A correction must retain the shared parent phases and
the generated sector. The fixed-band payment (486) and signed tail
observation remain available alongside this critical-helicity test.

Run `python3 -O labs/helicity_renewal.py`. It checks the general isolated
triad identity, the full four-parent cancellation, every source mode,
two viscosities of complete NS return jets, and the conditional reserve
algebra. The local-time and continuation arguments remain analytic;
no new Lean declarations or axioms are introduced.

## Complete-source helicity and a paid changing geometry

The cancellation at a selected child in (498) leaves a natural question:
do the other children restore a favorable helicity balance for the ENTIRE
nonlinear source? This section tests the precise proposed inequality

```text
u=P_+u, b=P_sol(u cross curl u)
    ==> H(b):=integral b.curl b >=0.               (501)
```

Equivalently, the negative critical magnitude of b would not exceed its
positive critical magnitude. The assertion is false. The counterexample
below retains every source mode, and also has a known regular calibration
whose complete history pays the signed source J in (494). Helicity sign
continues to mean Fourier polarization, not the sign of physical stretching.

### An exact complete-field counterexample

Use normalized volume on the 2*pi torus. Let psi have the following real
Fourier coefficients at (kx,ky,0), invariant under exchange of kx,ky and
independent changes of their signs. All other coefficients are zero.
Repeated orbit elements are included once, rather than summed again.

| Representative (kx,ky) | psi_hat |
|---|---:|
| (0,1) | 1 |
| (0,2) | -2/7 |
| (0,3) | 1/20 |
| (1,1) | -9/14 |
| (2,2) | -1/6 |
| (1,3) | -3/40 |

There are 28 wave vectors. Write Lambda_h=sqrt(-Delta_h), and define

```text
v=(psi_y,-psi_x,Lambda_h psi),
h=(cos z,-sin z,0), U_epsilon=v+epsilon h.          (502)
```

Both v and h have positive helicity at every nonzero mode:
curl v=Lambda v and curl h=h. They are real, smooth, divergence free
and mean zero. For epsilon!=0 the initial Fourier support spans R3.

There is a short independent way to evaluate the entire source. Put
w=Lambda_h psi, q=-Delta_h psi, and A f=(psi_y,-psi_x).grad_h f.
For b_v=P_sol(v cross curl v), the two-coordinate equations give

```text
(b_v)_3=-A w, (curl b_v)_3=-A q,
H(b_v)=2 integral (A w)(A q).                       (503)
```

The horizontal pressure projection is retained. Integration by parts
identifies the horizontal contribution to H with the vertical one,
giving the factor 2. Positivity of Lambda does not fix the sign of this
correlation: the advecting operator A does not commute with Lambda.

Exact convolution over ALL output wave vectors gives

```text
H(b_v)=-350383 sqrt(2)/180075+378244847/864360000
                  +9824477 sqrt(10)/13720000 < -49/1000.
c=P_sol(v cross curl h+h cross curl v),
H(c)=-362501/44100+81 sqrt(10)/20+6946 sqrt(2)/441,
H(b_epsilon)=H(b_v)+epsilon^2 H(c),
b_epsilon=P_sol(U_epsilon cross curl U_epsilon).    (504)
```

Indeed h has zero nonlinear source. The sources b_v and c have disjoint
vertical frequencies, respectively 0 and +/-1, so their integrated
helicity cross terms vanish. At epsilon=1/100 the literal value is

```text
H(b_epsilon)=-210059623 sqrt(2)/108045000
           +524353257/1200500000+6143771 sqrt(10)/8575000
           < -47/1000.                             (505)
```

The two cases have respectively 80 and 128 full source wave vectors.
Their canonical pressures have 116 and 172 modes. Nothing is discarded
to produce the negative sign. In particular, for F=U cross curl U,
`integral P_sol F.curl(P_sol F)=integral F.curl F`; the omitted part
in this ONE integral is an orthogonal gradient, not absent pressure
in the evolving flow. The checker independently reconstructs
`b=-U.grad U-grad p`, with the canonical pressure solving
`-Delta p=div(U.grad U)`.

The strict inequalities use exact rational enclosures for sqrt(2) and
sqrt(10), verified by squaring their endpoints. Floating-point optimization
helped select the fixture but is not evidence for its final sign.

### Actual viscous histories and a finite-energy whole-space version

For every prescribed nu>0, smooth local NS existence from U_epsilon gives
an actual unforced solution. Keep the same original heat evolution and set

```text
r(t)=u(t)-exp(nu t Delta)U_epsilon,
r(t)=t b_epsilon+O_H1(t^2),
H(r(t))=t^2 H(b_epsilon)+O(t^3)<0                  (506)
```

for all sufficiently small positive t. The inequality is for the FULL
generated remainder, not one selected child or a closed collection of
modes. It says that the negative critical magnitude of that remainder
exceeds its positive magnitude. It does not say that the total velocity
has negative helicity, that either helicity sign alone is dangerous, or
that repeated unbounded production occurs. The original parents
and their later returns remain in the full equation. The finite-interval
conclusion uses local PDE regularity and Taylor's theorem, not merely a
finite Fourier computation.

The failure of (501) is not confined to infinite-energy whole-space
periodic fields. Choose a nonzero real Schwartz envelope chi whose
Fourier transform is smooth and supported in a ball of radius 1/10.
For L sufficiently large define on R3

```text
u_L=P_+[chi(x/L) U_(1/100)(x)].                    (507)
```

This is a real, finite-energy Schwartz field with EXACT positive helicity.
Its Fourier support is a union of small packets about the finitely many
nonzero modes in (502), separated from zero. On each packet the symbol
P_+ is smooth. Taylor expansion of that symbol, or Fourier inversion with
Schwartz seminorms, gives, for any fixed derivative order and 1<=p<=infinity,

```text
||partial^a[u_L-chi(x/L)U_(1/100)]||_p=O(L^(3/p-1)).
```

Let F_L=u_L cross curl u_L and F=U_(1/100) cross curl U_(1/100).
The product rule then gives
`||F_L-chi(x/L)^2 F||_H1=O(L^(1/2))`, while the leading term has
H1 norm O(L^(3/2)). Removing gradients only in the helicity integral gives

```text
H(P_sol F_L)
 =L^3 [integral_R3 chi^4] H(b_(1/100))+O(L^2)<0     (508)
```

for all sufficiently large L. In the leading product the derivative of
chi^2 contributes zero, since F.(grad chi^2 cross F)=0. Averaging the
remaining finite periodic polynomial against chi(x/L)^4 leaves its
normalized mean; every nonzero Fourier term decays faster than any
inverse power of L after rescaling. Local whole-space NS existence and
the same H1 expansion as (506) give actual unforced viscous histories
with this negative-helicity generated remainder. This localization is
analytic, not a finite-checker or Lean-certified result.

### The calibration pays its complete history despite the sign reversal

An unfavorable complete-source sign need not prevent a finite reserve.
For ANY mean-zero smooth two-coordinate torus datum u0=(v_h0,w0), write
u(t)=(v_h(t,x,y),w(t,x,y)), with no z dependence. The exact equations are
two-dimensional NS for v_h and
`w_t+v_h.grad_h w=nu Delta_h w`. Define

```text
E_h=||v_h||_2^2, Z_h=||curl_h v_h||_2^2,
D_h=||grad_h curl_h v_h||_2^2,
X=||grad_h w||_2^2, Y=||Delta_h w||_2^2.
E_h'+2nu Z_h=0, Z_h'+2nu D_h=0,
X'+nu Y<=nu^(-1)||v_h||_infinity^2 X.              (509)
```

For the last inequality, pair the passive scalar equation with -Delta w;
the advection is bounded by
`2||v_h||_infinity sqrt(X Y)<=nu Y+nu^(-1)||v_h||_infinity^2 X`.
The existing lattice theorem `FourierAgmon.sq_sum_le_agmon`, followed
by the smooth Fourier limit, gives the same bound used in (476):

```text
integral_0^t ||v_h||_infinity^2
 <=104 sqrt[(integral Z_h)(integral D_h)]
 <=52 sqrt(E_h0 Z_h0)/nu=:A0.
X_star=X0 exp(A0/nu),
X(t)<=X_star, integral_0^t Y<=X_star/nu.            (510)
```

The integrating factor proves BOTH conclusions in (510). These constants
are fixed by the full original datum and nu, independent of t and of
how a history is divided into compatible segments. They permit arbitrary
amplitude and actual changing geometry. With E0=||u0||_2^2, the full
vorticity and gradient quantities from (495) satisfy

```text
Z<=Z_star:=Z_h0+X_star,
integral D<=D_star:=(Z_h0/2+X_star)/nu,
integral Z<=E0/(2nu).
M<=sqrt(E0 Z_star),
integral L<=sqrt[(E0/(2nu)) D_star].               (511)
```

The last two steps are Fourier interpolation: M^2<=E Z and L^2<=Z D,
with M=||Lambda^(1/2)u||_2^2 and L=||Lambda^(3/2)u||_2^2 as before.
For any fixed 0<kappa<=1, alpha=1-kappa, define

```text
B_plane=sqrt(E0 Z_star)+kappa sqrt(E0(Z_h0+2X_star)).
C_H(t)=4 integral_0^t J-2alpha nu integral_0^t L
      =M(t)-M0+2kappa nu integral_0^t L<=B_plane.
R_H=M+B_plane-C_H>=0, R_H'=-2kappa nu L.            (512)
```

This proves the proposed allowance (494) for the ENTIRE compatible history
of this known regular class, uniformly over all available prefixes and
all horizons. Applying the existing continuation argument does not assume
global existence beforehand. No new regularity class is claimed. For the
specific v in (502), the original quantities are
`E_h0=221407/22050`, `Z_h0=X0=1246171/44100`, `E0=2E_h0`.
It is therefore a concrete paid history with the adverse sign in (504).
Its proof does not require source helicity to have a favorable sign.

This payment is not assigned to the 3D perturbation or the localized
whole-space fields. For general 3D flow, an actual coordinate average
receives the Reynolds source `-div average_z(w_fluc tensor w_fluc)`, where
`w_fluc=u-average_z u`. Equations (478) retain the resulting energy and enstrophy
work. One must pay that generated work before using (510) for the average.
The arbitrary-data joint history allowance in (494), or the alternative
fixed-band signed allowance in (485), remains open. The next correction
must control the complete signed creation and feedback; the sign of the
entire generated helicity is not a valid substitute.

Run `python3 -O labs/helical_source_balance.py`. It checks the exact
coefficients, all source modes, the independent scalar-bracket identity,
the canonical pressure, positive initial helicity, spatial rank, literal
kinetic-energy decay and rational sign certificates. It also checks the
algebra of the complete planar allowance. Local PDE evolution, packet
localization, Fourier-limit inequalities and the all-time payment are
analytic here. No new Lean declarations or axioms are introduced.

## Phase-sensitive second return of the complete helical flow

The helical calculation (497)--(500) creates negative-helicity mass from
positive-helicity initial data. The next question is whether its nonlinear
return depletes further creation. For an entire two-amplitude family the
answer is yes, relative to the first Picard forecast. Changing a single
joint phase gives another entire family with the opposite answer. All
initial spectral energies and helicity are unchanged by that phase change.
Both statements concern actual unforced viscous NS on the torus, on a
short interval supplied by smooth local existence. They do not assume that
the four original parents form a closed dynamical system.

### The physical family and the comparison

Use normalized volume on the torus with period 2 pi. Write
`N(v)=Psol(v cross curl v)`, `L=nu Delta`, `Lambda=sqrt(-Delta)` and
`M_minus(v)=<Lambda P_minus v,P_minus v>`. For the fixed rotation
`R(x,y,z)=(-y,x,z)`, take

```text
p=(12,0,16), q=(-12,0,9), A=(16,20i,-12), B=(9,15i,12),
U_hat(p)=a A/2,       U_hat(q)=b B/2,
U_hat(Rp)=a zeta RA/2, U_hat(Rq)=b RB/2,           (513)
```

with the conjugate coefficients at the negative modes, real `a,b`, and
`zeta=-i` or `zeta=+i`. Each mode has positive helicity. For `ab!=0`,
the support spans all three spatial directions. Both phases have

```text
||U||_2^2=800 a^2+450 b^2,
||Lambda^(1/2)U||_2^2=H(U)=16000 a^2+6750 b^2,
||Lambda^(3/2)U||_2^2=6400000 a^2+1518750 b^2.
```

Indeed every initial norm `||m(D)U||_2`, with m a scalar Fourier multiplier,
is the same in the two cases. These observations retain no relative parent phase.

For every fixed positive viscosity, let `u` be the actual local NS solution
with datum U. Define the original heat flow and its first generated field
without restarting either at a later time:

```text
v(t)=exp(tL)U,
r1(t)=integral_0^t exp((t-s)L) N(v(s)) ds,
u_first(t)=v(t)+r1(t).                              (514)
```

The forecast `u_first` is an auxiliary Picard iterate, not another claimed
unforced solution. The heat field remains exactly positive-helicity, so
`M_minus(u_first)=M_minus(r1)`.

The exact initial jets give

```text
M_minus(u(t))-M_minus(u_first(t))
  = a^2 b^2 [c42(zeta) a^2+c24(zeta) b^2] t^4
      + O(t^5).                                    (515)
```

The constants do not depend on viscosity. The following are strict rational
enclosures, not rounded sign tests; the entries are in units of one million:

| Parent phase | c42 / 10^6 | c24 / 10^6 | Actual negative-sector mass relative to its own first forecast |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-i` | `(-18662,-18661)` | `(-11474,-11473)` | Strictly smaller for all sufficiently small positive t |
| `+i` | `(77464,77465)` | `(65065,65066)` | Strictly larger for all sufficiently small positive t |

These inequalities hold for every fixed real `a,b` with `ab!=0` and every
fixed `nu>0`. The interval may depend on all three parameters. If either
amplitude is zero, the remaining single-shell field is Beltrami and its
evolution is exactly the heat flow. No amplitude-uniform time interval is
claimed.

In both families the negative-sector mass itself initially grows, with a
strictly positive t^2 coefficient. "Depleting" here means smaller than
the corresponding forecast, not a decreasing negative-sector mass.

### Complete return, including the new square

The coefficients in (515) have a short exact definition which makes clear
what the computation retains. With derivatives of N taken as maps of vector
fields, set

```text
b0=N(U),
c0=N'(U)b0,
d0=N'(U)c0+2N(b0),
C(U)=(1/3)<Lambda P_minus b0,P_minus d0>
         +(1/4)||Lambda^(1/2)P_minus c0||_2^2.       (516)
```

Then `C(U)=a^2 b^2(c42 a^2+c24 b^2)`. This finite Fourier expression,
with U given explicitly in (513), defines each radical coefficient exactly.
`helical_second_return.py` also prints the expanded rational combinations
of square roots and rational upper and lower certificates.

The two contributions matter separately. The table gives approximate
coefficients in units of one billion, only for interpretation; their signs
and the signs of their sums are checked by rational enclosures:

| Phase | Amplitude monomial | Mixed first/third jet | Positive second-jet square | Complete coefficient |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `-i` | `a^4 b^2` | -554.821419 | 536.159828 | -18.661590 |
| `-i` | `a^2 b^4` | -357.222738 | 345.749540 | -11.473198 |
| `+i` | `a^4 b^2` | -99.356173 | 176.821164 | 77.464991 |
| `+i` | `a^2 b^4` | -30.699918 | 95.765094 | 65.065176 |

Thus the mixed return is negative in both families. It is not sufficient
to establish depletion of the complete observation: the newly generated
second-order field carries its own positive square. In the second family
that square more than pays back the favorable mixed term.

For completeness, (516) can be derived without dropping viscosity from
the actual equation. The full initial time jets satisfy

```text
u^(n+1)(0)=L u^(n)(0)
  +Psol sum_(j=0)^n binomial(n,j)
       [u^(j)(0) cross curl u^(n-j)(0)].             (517)
```

The first forecast uses heat jets in the quadratic source in (517), and
its own previous jet in the L term. Since `P_minus U=0`, the fourth
derivative of negative-sector mass only needs velocity jets through order
three: its nonzero terms are
`8<Lambda P_minus u'(0),P_minus u'''(0)>`
and `6||Lambda^(1/2)P_minus u''(0)||_2^2`.

The checker represents each vector jet as a polynomial in a, b and nu
with exact Gaussian-rational Fourier coefficients. Subtracting the
forecast cancels the coefficients of orders zero through three. At order
four, every viscosity-dependent monomial vanishes and only `a^4 b^2` and
`a^2 b^4` remain. This proves a polynomial identity in all three
parameters; it is not an interpolation from chosen numerical samples.
Its viscosity-free coefficient is (516). The negative mixed term and
the new positive square are both retained.

Independently, the checker computes actual jets using the advective NS
equation and its canonical pressure, for positive viscosities 1, 3/2 and 2,
unequal amplitudes, a negative amplitude and a single-shell limit. For the
nondegenerate samples it retains 8, 20, 60 and 148 velocity modes at orders
zero through three, and 18, 66 and 152 pressure modes. Their jets equal the
polynomial recurrence exactly and satisfy the kinetic-energy identity.
No intermediate output is projected back onto the four-parent support.

Trigonometric-polynomial initial data give an actual local smooth viscous
solution with sufficiently many time derivatives in Sobolev spaces to
apply Taylor's theorem to this quadratic observation. The integral
forecast is also smooth there. Consequently the remainder in (515) is
bounded by a finite constant times t^5 on a sufficiently short interval.
Since the fourth-order coefficient is strictly nonzero whenever `ab!=0`,
its certified sign proves the strict short-time comparisons above. This
local PDE and remainder argument is analytic, not a new Lean theorem.

The comparison also reaches the signed production in (493)--(494).
Define the forecast production
`J_first=<Lambda P_minus r1,P_minus N(v)>` and
`L_minus(w)=||Lambda^(3/2)P_minus w||_2^2`. The actual and forecast balances
are respectively `M_minus(u)'+2nu L_minus(u)=2J(u)` and
`M_minus(r1)'+2nu L_minus(r1)=2J_first`. The same polynomial check shows
that `L_minus(u)-L_minus(r1)` vanishes through order three. Hence

```text
J(u(t))-J_first(t)=2 C(U)t^3+O(t^4).
```

Thus the opposite signs also hold for the first return of the actual
critical production relative to its own forecast. J_first is the source
work in (514); it is not asserted to equal J evaluated on u_first, since
u_first does not solve unforced NS. No all-time integral comparison follows.

### The joint phase and the remaining history question

The four wavevectors obey `p+q=Rp+Rq`. Relative to the explicitly fixed
polarizations in (513), their scalar amplitudes have the quartet product

```text
alpha_p alpha_q conjugate(alpha_Rp alpha_Rq)
      = a^2 b^2 conjugate(zeta).                    (518)
```

This product is unchanged by spatial translation: the four translation
phases cancel. It distinguishes the two families although their entire
initial scalar energy spectra agree. An interface intended to reconstruct
this return therefore cannot retain just the individual modal energies.
This is a concrete necessary observation, not a proof that one quartet
is a sufficient boundary state for subsequent evolution.

The positive family refutes automatic depletion of the first complete
return for arbitrary positive-helicity parents. It does not refute a
finite allowance depending on the full datum. The negative family supplies
a physical instance of nonlinear depletion despite initial negative-sector
creation. Neither result establishes payment from viscosity: viscosity is
present in both actual evolutions, but cancels from this leading difference.
Helicity sign alone is not the sign of physical enstrophy stretching.

The remaining target is still (494): control the accumulated actual
production J, with a fixed dissipation fraction and an allowance determined
by the original full datum. The next relevant phase equation must retain
the other modes which the quartet creates and the parents they feed back
into. Reapplying (515) as though the evolved state still had the form (513)
would reset its history and is invalid. An arbitrary-horizon payment and
an extension of this short-time comparison to whole-space fields are not
established here.

Run `python3 -O labs/helical_second_return.py`. It checks both full
amplitude/viscosity polynomial families, exact radical signs, the two
return contributions, independent pressure jets and the shared initial
resources. These algebraic checks support the analytic local comparison;
no Lean declaration or axiom changes.

## Actual quartet phase dynamics and a paid observation history

The two returns in (515) differ in their joint phase. To test whether the
actual dynamics automatically align the parents toward the depleting
configuration, keep the same four wavevectors and polarizations as (513)
but allow any `zeta=exp(i theta0)`. The calculation below retains every
generated mode and the canonical pressure. It gives both a favorable
amplitude effect and a failure of automatic favorable angular motion.
A separate estimate then pays a fixed quartet's complete observation
history for arbitrary unforced periodic flows, using the existing full
energy identity.

### Actual coefficients and their first nonlinear return

For any actual velocity field, define alpha_p as the coefficient of the
