orthogonal projection of its p Fourier coefficient onto A/2, and similarly
use B/2, RA/2 and RB/2 at q,Rp,Rq. These four complex observations do not
discard any modes from the evolving PDE. At the family datum their values
are `a,b,a*zeta,b`. Their product

```text
Q=alpha_p alpha_q conjugate(alpha_Rp alpha_Rq),
theta=-arg(Q), theta(0)=theta0,                    (519)
```

uses a continuous local branch when `ab!=0`. It is invariant under spatial
translation. In the following initial derivatives, theta means theta0.
All first nonlinear parent sources vanish at this datum. Consequently
`alpha_j'(0)/alpha_j(0)=-nu |k_j|^2` and `theta'(0)=0`.

Put `ell_j=(log alpha_j)''(0)`. The exact full return is

```text
ell_p/b^2 = -3392375616/307681
                   +(599616+2279700i) zeta/337,
ell_q/a^2 =  1689009840/307681
                   +(12960-2217960i) zeta/337,
ell_Rp=conjugate(ell_p), ell_Rq=conjugate(ell_q).    (520)
```

These identities hold for all nonzero real a,b, all unit phases and all
positive viscosities. They are Laurent polynomial identities in zeta and
ordinary polynomial identities in a,b. The viscosity terms cancel from
the logarithmic second derivatives: the second velocity jet consists of
the original heat curvature, terms supported on two-parent outputs, and
the full cubic return `N'(U)N(U)`. None of the two-parent outputs is an
original mode. Subtracting `(alpha_j'/alpha_j)^2` removes the heat curvature.
No inviscid evolution is substituted for the physical viscous solution.

In particular the actual joint angle satisfies

```text
theta''(0)=[(4435920 a^2-4559400 b^2) cos(theta)
                 -(25920 a^2+1199232 b^2) sin(theta)]/337.  (521)
```

The sign depends on the amplitude ratio as well as the phase.

### A favorable parent loss, but not automatic favorable alignment

The real part of the high-parent logarithmic curvature is

```text
Re ell_p = b^2 [-3392375616+547449408 cos(theta)
                              -2081366100 sin(theta)]/307681
          <= -763560108 b^2/307681 < 0.             (522)
```

Let E_high(t) count the full velocity energy at the four modes
`+/-p,+/-Rp`, including any subsequently generated polarization there.
For every fixed datum in this family and every fixed nu>0, actual smooth
local NS gives

```text
E_high(t)-800a^2 exp(-800nu t)
   =800a^2 Re(ell_p) t^2+O(t^3)<0                 (523)
```

for sufficiently small positive t. Thus the original higher-frequency
parents initially supply energy beyond their own heat loss for EVERY
phase, including phases which increase the critical production relative
to its first forecast. The finite remainder follows from smooth local
existence. The interval is not uniform over all amplitudes and viscosities.
Later refeeding from other modes is retained in the equation and is not
excluded by (523).

The corresponding angular-descent shortcut fails. Let C(a,b,theta) be
the complete fourth-order coefficient defined by (516), allowing a unit
phase. It is a degree-six translation-invariant polynomial in the initial
coefficients. The only primitive relation among the four positive input
wavevectors is `p+q-Rp-Rq=0`. A phase harmonic of order n needs at least
`4|n|` input factors, so

```text
C(a,b,theta)=C0(a,b)+Cc(a,b)cos(theta)+Cs(a,b)sin(theta).
```

This also rules out odd-degree zero-frequency contractions and justifies
the cancellation of viscosity-dependent return terms for every phase,
as in (515). For `a=2,b=1,theta=0`, exact computation gives

```text
theta''(0)=13184280/337>0,
partial_theta C(2,1,0)
   =[C(2,1,pi/2)-C(2,1,-pi/2)]/2 > 9*10^11.      (524)
```

The angular component of the actual return therefore moves toward a
larger production coefficient at this datum. This refutes the proposed
universal descent sign `theta'' partial_theta C<=0`. It does not freeze
the amplitudes or assert that C evaluated on the complete evolving field
obeys a closed angular equation. The favorable amplitude effect (522)
is present at the same time. Their joint history must be analyzed.

### A full-history reserve for a fixed quartet

Now allow ANY smooth mean-zero unforced NS prefix on the normalized
2*pi torus. The observations in (519) remain fixed; the velocity need
not lie in the four-parent family. Write `n_j` for the corresponding
linear observation of the COMPLETE nonlinear source N(u). Then

```text
alpha_j'=-nu |k_j|^2 alpha_j+n_j,
Q'+nu kappa Q=F, kappa=sum_j |k_j|^2,              (525)
```

where F is the sum of four product-rule terms, replacing each alpha by
its n and conjugating in the last two slots. It includes all modes of
the surrounding fluid and their pressure-projected interactions.

For a general fixed resonant quartet of nonzero modes, let s_j be the norm
of its scalar coefficient observation. With `E=||u||_2^2`,
`Z=||grad u||_2^2`, incompressibility,
the norm-one Leray projection and Fourier Cauchy--Schwarz give

```text
|N(u)_k|<=|k| sum_p |u_p| |u_(k-p)|<=|k| E,
|alpha_j|<=s_j sqrt(E), |n_j|<=s_j |k_j| E,
|F|<=K E^(5/2), K=(product_j s_j) sum_j |k_j|.     (526)
```

This is the same full-energy Fourier estimate used in (274), here applied
to the actual joint phase source rather than to an autonomous model of
the original parents. The nonlinear source is not a freely specified force.

The actual energy identity and the mean-zero Poincare inequality give
`E'=-2nu Z`, `Z>=E`. Hence the nonnegative reserve

```text
R=K E^(5/2)/(5nu),
R'=-K E^(3/2) Z <=-K E^(5/2)<=-|F|.               (527)
```

To count angular changes without dividing by a vanishing amplitude, define
`q=|Im(conjugate(Q)F)|/|Q|` when Q is nonzero and q=0 otherwise.
Where the phase is defined, `q=|Q| |theta'|`; always `q<=|F|`.
The absolutely continuous modulus satisfies
`(|Q|)'+nu kappa |Q|<=|F|` almost everywhere. Therefore

```text
S=|Q|+2R>=0,
S'+nu kappa |Q|+q<=0,
S(t)+integral_0^t [nu kappa |Q|+q] <= S(0).        (528)
```

This pays both maintenance against viscosity and the weighted absolute
phase motion on EVERY available prefix from the original datum, uniformly
over the horizon. It remains valid through zeros of Q; it does not bound
unweighted winding near such zeros. Adjacent compatible segments use the
same intermediate E,Q and telescope, without a new allowance at a seam.
For the observations in (519), `s_j=sqrt(2)/|k_j|`, so

```text
kappa=1250, K=7/2250,
S(0)=|Q(0)|+7 E0^(5/2)/(5625nu).                  (529)
```

A constant spatial mean can be removed by a Galilean change of coordinates.
Its four advection phases cancel in Q because `p+q=Rp+Rq`; the same bound
then uses the kinetic energy relative to that conserved mean.

For a prescribed threshold `q_star>0`, this gives two useful consequences
for actual histories. The total time with `|Q|>=q_star` is at most
`S(0)/(nu kappa q_star)`. If N disjoint intervals each contain a complete
phase turn, and `|Q|>=q_star` throughout those intervals, then

```text
2pi q_star N <= integral q <= S(0).                (530)
```

Thus the initial reserve bounds the number of these sustained, fixed-scale
phase cycles, with either winding direction. These are cycles of the
specified joint observation, not exact repetitions of the whole velocity.
Phase motion near zero amplitude, or cycles at changing frequencies, are
not excluded by this consequence.

### What the paid observation does and does not control

The bound (528) applies to arbitrary periodic unforced histories and to
their full internally generated feedback, including repeated parent
renewal. It supplies a physical Bellman upper bound for this fixed joint
observation. Its proof reuses the ordinary energy reserve; it does not
establish the critical continuation allowance (494).

In particular the original critical production J observes all frequencies,
with derivative weights, whereas (528) observes one prescribed quartet.
For unit-norm coefficient observations, K grows with the observed wave
numbers; summing all quartets requires additional summable weights. No
bound converting such a paid sum into (494) has been proved. Allowing
the observations or their weights to change also introduces derivative
and seam costs. Treating a newly selected quartet as a fresh reserve would
lose the resource already spent. Whole-space wave-packet observations
are a separate extension, not asserted here.

In particular, for successive fixed quartets along the SAME actual history,
let `S_old,S_new` be their reserves at a switch time. The segment bounds give

```text
S_last(t)+sum_segments integral [nu kappa |Q|+q]
  <= S_first(0)+sum_switches [S_new-S_old].         (531)
```

Any positive jump is an additional cost. No bound on the sum of these costs
for arbitrary refinement, and no critical-production consumer for that sum,
is asserted. The full velocity must supply both observations at the seam;
matching only a phase label would not establish that compatibility.

External forcing adds its own coefficient sources to F and work to the
energy identity; these terms cannot be discarded when applying (527).
This fixed-observation result neither refutes a forced singularity nor
excludes every internal realization of a forced pattern at refining scales.
The open task is to control the joint amplitude, phase and scale history
strongly enough to pay the complete critical production.

Run `python3 -O labs/quartet_phase_history.py`. Laurent coefficients prove
the full unit-phase identities; independent advective NS jets check
positive viscosity, canonical pressure and high-parent energy. Rational
enclosures verify the adverse angular direction. The scalar reserve
identities and explicit constants are also checked. The local PDE,
Fourier estimates and all-prefix payment above are analytic arguments;
no new Lean declaration or axiom is introduced.

## Fixed-energy concentration of the actual critical history

The fixed-quartet payments (527)--(531) are valid along arbitrary smooth
periodic unforced prefixes. Their payment, however, comes from kinetic
energy. A uniformly finite energy-funded sum of these observations cannot
dominate the complete critical cost (494). This obstruction concerns the
ACTUAL velocity and its critical history; it is distinct from the earlier
counterexamples for auxiliary caloric renewal functionals.

The analytic statement is: on R3 and on the fixed normalized 2*pi torus,
for any prescribed nu>0, horizon T>0 and 0<=alpha<1, there are smooth
divergence-free initial data with E0=1, exactly positive initial helicity,
and actual unforced smooth evolutions through times t_lambda<=T such that

```text
C_H(t_lambda)=4 integral_0^t_lambda J
                 -2alpha nu integral_0^t_lambda L >= c lambda,
t_lambda=tau0 lambda^(-5/2),
0<=1-E(t_lambda)<=C nu lambda^(-1/2).              (532)
```

Here c,tau0,C>0 are fixed independently of sufficiently large lambda;
J,L,M and C_H have exactly the meanings in (492)--(494). Each lambda
uses DIFFERENT original data. This proves neither indefinite renewal from
one datum nor an unforced singularity. It rules out an energy-only uniform
allowance for this particular sufficient criterion. The full-data allowance
in (494) remains open.

### A uniform physical interval with critical-mass growth

Reuse the localized seed (507)--(508), fixing its envelope size sufficiently
large, then normalizing its kinetic energy. This gives a real divergence-free
Schwartz field U on R3, with smooth compact Fourier support away from zero,
P_+U=U, E(U)=1, and H(N(U))<0, where N(U)=P_sol(U cross curl U).
In particular,

```text
b=N(U), A=||Lambda^(1/2)P_-b||_2^2>0.             (533)
```

The strict inequality follows from 2A=M(b)-H(b)>0; no sign of the
helicity of the total evolving velocity is assumed. For viscosity
0<mu<=1 let v_mu be the actual local unforced solution from U.
The usual differentiated H^m energy estimate, for a fixed sufficiently
large m (m=12 suffices), has a nonpositive viscous term and gives a common
existence interval and uniform H^m bound independent of mu. The projected
equation then bounds v_mu'' in H^(1/2) uniformly there: differentiating
twice costs at most four spatial derivatives and mu<=1. Consequently

```text
P_-v_mu(tau)=tau P_-b+e_mu(tau),
||Lambda^(1/2)e_mu(tau)||_2<=K tau^2,
L(v_mu(tau))<=L_star.                             (534)
```

The initial viscous derivative has no negative sector because P_-U=0.
All nonlinear outputs and pressure are retained in (534); this is not an
evolution on a closed set of modes. These local estimates can be obtained
directly from the transport energy inequality and local existence; no
global regularity or controlled future norm is assumed.

More generally suppose the initial negative-source norm squared is at
least a>0, with the constants in (534) uniform over a family. Choose one
tau0 in the common interval with K tau0<=sqrt(a)/2. Then

```text
M_-(v_mu(tau0)) >= a tau0^2/4,
H(v_mu(tau0))-H(U) >= -2mu L_star tau0,
M(v_mu(tau0))-M(U)
  >= a tau0^2/2-2mu L_star tau0 >= delta,
delta=a tau0^2/4>0,
provided mu<=a tau0/(8L_star).                    (535)
```

The second line uses the exact viscous helicity balance (493), and the
third uses M=H+2M_- and M_-(U)=0. Thus the initial critical mass can
increase on a common interval even though its initial derivative is
negative. For comparison, the complete initial derivatives are

```text
M'(0)=-2mu L(U),
M''(0)=4A-4mu <Lambda^3 U,b>
                 +4mu^2 ||Lambda^(5/2)U||_2^2.   (536)
```

The checker verifies the entire viscosity polynomial in (536), including
a fixture with <Lambda^3 U,b>=-72. Discarding the mixed viscous term is
unnecessary and would be incorrect for that fixture. The proof of (535)
uses the controlled interval (534), not the initial derivatives alone.

### Exact concentration on R3

Set mu=nu/sqrt(lambda) and rescale the full solution and pressure by

```text
u_lambda(t,x)=lambda^(3/2)
                  v_mu(lambda^(5/2)t,lambda x),
p_lambda(t,x)=lambda^3 p_mu(lambda^(5/2)t,lambda x).
E(u_lambda)=E(v_mu), M(u_lambda)=lambda M(v_mu),
L(u_lambda)=lambda^3 L(v_mu),
J(u_lambda)=lambda^(7/2) J(v_mu).                 (537)
```

Both the time derivative and the complete convection/pressure terms have
factor lambda^4; the viscous coefficient becomes nu as required. Thus
these are actual unforced solutions at the SAME prescribed viscosity.
Take lambda sufficiently large for (535) and t_lambda<=T. Integrating
(493) gives

```text
C_H(t_lambda)
 =lambda [M(v_mu(tau0))-M(U)
          +2(1-alpha)mu integral_0^tau0 L(v_mu)]
 >=delta lambda.                                 (538)
```

The kinetic balance gives the other part of (532): if Z(v_mu)<=Z_star
on the common interval, then
`1-E(u_lambda(t_lambda))<=2nu Z_star tau0/sqrt(lambda)`.
There is no replenishing force. A vanishing kinetic-energy expenditure
can accompany a large change in a norm which weights small scales more
heavily. The original critical mass itself is lambda M(U); this family
requires a critical-history allowance at least a fixed positive multiple
of that initial resource. It does not rule out such an allowance.

### The same obstruction on the fixed torus

To connect the result to the PERIODIC quartet payments, a whole-space
example alone does not suffice. Use the same Schwartz seed and define on
the torus of side 2*pi*lambda

```text
W_lambda(y)=rho_lambda sum_(n in Z^3) U(y+2pi lambda n),
rho_lambda>0 chosen so E(W_lambda)=1.             (539)
```

For this comparison, use the fixed measure density (2*pi)^(-3)dy on
R3 AND on every expanding torus, not the mean over each expanding box.
Normalize U in that convention. With
`U_hat(xi)=(2pi)^(-3) integral U(y)exp(-i xi.y)dy`, the coefficients
in (539) are `rho_lambda lambda^(-3) U_hat(k/lambda)`.
Parseval and Riemann sums give rho_lambda->1 and convergence of every
fixed Sobolev norm to its whole-space value. The initial data are finite
Fourier polynomials, real, exactly solenoidal, mean-zero and exactly
positive-helicity: the multiplier is evaluated at the same k/lambda as
the sampled coefficient, and U_hat vanishes near zero.

The full source also converges in the norm needed in (533). Its Fourier
convolution is a Riemann sum of smooth compactly supported factors.
The Leray multiplier is bounded uniformly. At zero output the divergence
form of the source contributes a factor |xi|; hence the source tends to
zero there. Applying the bounded helical projection and weighting by
|xi| in its squared norm introduces no low-frequency singularity.
It follows that
`||Lambda^(1/2)P_-N(W_lambda)||_2^2->A>0`.

The H^m local estimates used for (534) are uniform on these expanding
tori. For example, the Fourier proof of the Sobolev embedding uses

```text
lambda^(-3) sum_(k in Z^3)
    (1+|k/lambda|^2)^(-s)<=C_s, s>3/2, lambda>=1. (540)
```

Thus the Sobolev/product constants, the norm-one Leray projection and
the initial H^m bounds are all uniform. The same transport estimate
and projected-equation time derivatives give uniform K,L_star,Z_star
and a common interval. With a=A/2, (535) holds for all sufficiently
large lambda at sufficiently small mu, using the same tau0,delta.
This step only constructs local viscous solutions.

Solve from W_lambda at viscosity mu=nu/sqrt(lambda) on its expanding
torus, then apply (537). The resulting velocity lives on the ORIGINAL
2*pi torus, has exactly unit initial normalized energy, and obeys
(532) and (538). Its initial critical mass is
`lambda M(W_lambda)`, asymptotic to lambda M(U). This establishes the
fixed-domain obstruction rather than changing the domain in the final
claim. Periodization and the uniform PDE interval are analytic here,
not finite Fourier computation or Lean certification.

### Consequence for sums of paid phase observations

For quartet i in (527)--(530), write c_i=product_j s_ij and
K_i=c_i sum_j |k_ij|. Then its nonnegative accumulated observation cost
P_i(t)=integral_0^t [nu kappa_i |Q_i|+q_i] satisfies

```text
P_i(t)<=S_i(0)<=c_i E0^2+2K_i E0^(5/2)/(5nu).
For w_i>=0, A0=sum_i w_i c_i<infinity,
            A1=sum_i w_i K_i<infinity,
sum_i w_i P_i(t)<=A0 E0^2+2A1 E0^(5/2)/(5nu).    (541)
```

Tonelli justifies the countable sum. If A0,A1 have bounds depending
only on E0,nu,T, the right side is uniformly finite at E0=1. Therefore
there cannot be a universal estimate

```text
C_H(t)<=D(E0,nu,T)+C(E0,nu,T) sum_i w_i P_i(t)     (542)
```

with finite D and finite C>=0 and those uniform price bounds, for all
smooth unforced periodic data and available prefixes. Equation (532)
contradicts it. This conclusion allows weights selected from the datum
if their TOTAL price is still uniformly bounded by energy alone.

It does not exclude a joint observation with an initial price that grows
with the datum's critical mass or finer geometry, nor a different sufficient
regularity criterion. The next constructive obligation is a payment from
such a full-data resource that survives changing scales and interacting
parents. Merely summing more of the current energy-funded accounts cannot
supply that obligation. This is a restriction on one proposed bridge to
(494), not a disproof of arbitrary-data regularity.

Run `python3 -O labs/critical_history_concentration.py`. It checks the
full viscosity-polynomial identities against independent advective NS
jets, strictly positive source norms with rational radical enclosures,
and the scaling and scalar payment calculations. It reuses the localized
seed established analytically in (507)--(508). The uniform local interval,
Schwartz localization and expanding-torus limit remain analytic arguments.
No new Lean declaration or axiom is introduced.

## Critical amplification in a paid unforced mixing history

The concentration result (532) requires an allowance beyond kinetic energy
alone. A fixed multiple of the original critical mass M0 is still too
restrictive. Even globally regular unforced flows can amplify M by an
arbitrarily large factor. This section tests that precise stronger candidate
and gives a NONLINEAR original-data payment for the entire reference history.
All norms are on the normalized 2*pi torus; no R3 extension is claimed here.

Shear mixing and enhanced dissipation have an extensive theory, including
[Bedrossian--Coti Zelati](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.08098). Their stationary
shear semigroups are not the time-decaying fluid used below. The elementary
comparison here retains that time dependence and connects the mixing directly
to the critical NS criterion (494). No optimal enhanced-dissipation rate or
new general regularity theorem is claimed.

### An actual unforced history and its stochastic representation

For A,B>0 and nu>0, consider

```text
U(t,x,y,z)=(V(t,y),0,w(t,x,y)),
V=A exp(-nu t) sin y,
w_t+V w_x=nu(w_xx+w_yy), w(0,x,y)=B cos x.        (543)
```

This is an exact global smooth unforced 3D NS solution with zero pressure.
It has genuine vorticity stretching, although only two-coordinate spatial
dependence and no return from w into V. The global existence here follows
from the explicit shear and a linear parabolic equation, independently of
any arbitrary-data NS hypothesis.

Write `w=B Re[exp(ix) psi(t,y)]`. If W_s is standard one-dimensional
Brownian motion, the exact Feynman--Kac representation is

```text
psi_t=nu psi_yy-nu psi-i V psi, psi(0,y)=1,
psi(t,y)=exp(-nu t) Expectation exp(
  -i integral_0^t V(t-s,y+sqrt(2nu) W_s) ds),
zeta(t)=A(1-exp(-nu t))/nu,
|psi|<=exp(-nu t),
|psi_y|<=exp(-nu t) zeta(t).                      (544)
```

Differentiation under the expectation is justified by the bounded smooth
shear. The phase and its derivative stay in the SAME expectation; bounding
its absolute value does not replace it by independent expectations. This
is an auxiliary stochastic representation of the actual viscous equation,
not a force applied to the fluid. Higher y derivatives give bounds of the
form `exp(-nu t) P_j(zeta)` with finite polynomials P_j. Thus the reference
decays to zero in every fixed Sobolev norm.

### A positive-viscosity lower bound for critical amplification

The transported reference
`w_tr=B cos(x-zeta(t) sin y)` solves `w_tr,t+V w_tr,x=0`.
Let e=w-w_tr. Its forced linear error equation and the divergence-free
transport energy estimate give

```text
||e(t)||_2<=nu integral_0^t ||Delta w_tr(s)||_2 ds
 <=(B/sqrt(2)) nu [t+A^2 t^3/3].                 (545)
```

Indeed, direct integration gives
`||Delta w_tr||_2^2/B^2=1/2+3zeta^2/4+3zeta^4/16`
and hence `||Delta w_tr||_2<=(B/sqrt(2))(1+zeta^2)`;
also zeta(s)<=As. This controls the actual viscous solution on the
whole stated interval, not just its initial Taylor coefficients.

Let c_n be the Fourier coefficients of `exp(-i zeta sin y)`. Parseval gives

```text
sum |c_n|^2=1,
sum n^2 |c_n|^2=zeta^2/2,
sum n^4 |c_n|^2=zeta^2/2+3zeta^4/8.               (546)
```

Cauchy--Schwarz, after removing the contribution from |n|<zeta/2,
implies

```text
sum_(|n|>=zeta/2) |c_n|^2
 >=zeta^2/(8+6zeta^2)>=1/14>1/16, for zeta>=1.   (547)
```

For Re=A/nu>=8000 choose

```text
t_star=(1/(10nu)) Re^(-2/3),
Re^(1/3)/20<=zeta(t_star)<=Re^(1/3)/10,
||e(t_star)||_2/(B/sqrt(2))
 <=1/10+1/3000=301/3000<1/8.                     (548)
```

The phase lower bound follows from 1-exp(-r)>=r/2 for 0<=r<=1.
By (547), the high-y-frequency part of w_tr has norm at least
B/(4sqrt(2)). Equations (545)--(548) leave at least B/(8sqrt(2))
in the SAME projection of the actual w. On that projection |k|>=zeta/2,
so the actual critical mass satisfies

```text
M(U(t_star))>=B^2 zeta(t_star)/256
             >=B^2 Re^(1/3)/5120.                (549)
```

Set B=A. All initial modes have length one, and E0=M0=Z0=A^2.
Consequently M(t_star)/M0 is unbounded as A/nu grows at fixed nu.
Every prescribed positive horizon contains t_star for sufficiently large A.
Since `C_H=M-M0+2(1-alpha)nu integral L>=M-M0`, no finite constant
C(nu,T,alpha) can give `C_H(t)<=C(nu,T,alpha) M0` for all data and
available prefixes. The same example excludes fixed finite linear
combinations of initial Sobolev energies as the sole allowance: every
homogeneous Sobolev energy of this datum equals A^2.

This does NOT exclude a nonlinear function of M0 and nu, or an allowance
depending on the full datum. In contrast to (532), the initial energy
here grows with A. These are two different restrictions on proposed
payments, and neither constructs blowup.

### The entire reference history has an explicit finite payment

The same stochastic formula that permits large mixing supplies its payment.
Put E_w=||w||_2^2, Z_w=||grad w||_2^2 and D_w=||Delta w||_2^2. Equation
(544) gives

```text
E_w<=B^2 exp(-2nu t)/2,
Z_w<=B^2 exp(-2nu t)(1+zeta^2)/2,
M_w<=B^2 sqrt(1+Re^2)/2.                         (550)
```

The actual scalar energy and gradient-energy identities are

```text
E_w'+2nu Z_w=0,
Z_w'+2nu D_w=-2 integral V_y w_x w_y
             <=A B^2 zeta exp(-3nu t).
integral_0^infinity Z_w<=B^2/(4nu),
integral_0^infinity D_w<=B^2(1+Re^2/6)/(4nu),
integral_0^infinity L_w
 <=B^2 sqrt(1+Re^2/6)/(4nu).                      (551)
```

The D_w bound uses `integral zeta exp(-3nu t)=Re/(12nu)`.
The last bound follows from `L_w<=sqrt(Z_w D_w)` and time Cauchy--Schwarz.
The remaining shear has M_V(t)=A^2 exp(-2nu t)/2 and
`integral_0^infinity L_V=A^2/(4nu)`. Therefore, for kappa=1-alpha>0,
the FULL critical history of U satisfies, for every t>=0,

```text
C_H(t)<=B_mix,
B_mix=B^2/2 [sqrt(1+Re^2)-1]
       +kappa/2 [A^2+B^2 sqrt(1+Re^2/6)],
R_mix=M+B_mix-C_H>=0,
R_mix'=-2kappa nu L.                             (552)
```

This is a single reserve fixed by the original A,B,nu,alpha. Successive
segments use this SAME reserve and do not reset the original shear. It
pays the sufficient criterion (494) despite the arbitrarily large relative
amplification in (549). For B=A its leading allowance is of order A^3/nu,
whereas the demonstrated lower growth is of order A^2 Re^(1/3). These
upper and lower bounds are not asserted to be optimal or matching.

### Genuine three-dimensional feedback preserves the obstruction

The failure of the linear M0 allowance is not limited to zero feedback.
Take initial data

```text
U_epsilon(0)=(A sin y+epsilon cos z,
               epsilon sin z, A cos x).          (553)
```

For epsilon nonzero these data depend genuinely on all three coordinates;
E0=M0=Z0=A^2+epsilon^2. Let a(t) denote twice the negative imaginary
part of the x-component Fourier coefficient at (0,1,0), so a(0)=A.
The COMPLETE projected NS equation gives

```text
a(t)=A exp(-nu t)-A epsilon^2 t^2/4+O(t^3).       (554)
```

This is a nonzero return into the original shear. The pressure and all
generated modes are retained. The checker proves the entire A,epsilon,nu
polynomial identity and independently compares full advective NS jets at
positive viscosity. Equation (554) does not describe a closed scalar ODE
or assert the sign of all later returns.

For each fixed finite A and nu, choose epsilon sufficiently small. Reuse
the actual H^3 difference estimate (122)--(123) from the coupled-cycle
construction, now with the Fourier norm having weight (1+|k|^2)^3.
Equation (544) bounds the reference by `||U(t)||_H4<=Q exp(-nu t)`,
where Q is finite from A,nu; one may take `Q=C4 A(1+Re^4)` for a fixed
norm constant C4. Put d=U_epsilon-U, Y=||d||_H3^2 and
`K=C3 Q/nu`, where C3 is the fixed difference-estimate constant. Then

```text
Y'+2nu ||grad d||_H3^2
 <=C3 ||U||_H4 Y+C3 Y^(3/2),
sqrt(Y0) exp(K/2)<=nu/(2C3)
  implies Y(t)<=Y0 exp[K(1-exp(-nu t))-nu t].
Y0=8epsilon^2.                                   (555)
```

Poincare and the bootstrap `sqrt(Y)<nu/C3` absorb the COMPLETE self
interaction in (555), as in (123). Local existence and H^3 continuation
then construct the global smooth solution. Every constant comes from the
known reference and nu, not an assumed future bound for the perturbed
solution. This retains the pressure difference in the physical equation;
its solenoidal energy pairing cancels. The stability argument is analytic.

Put `ell=A^2 Re^(1/3)/5120`. By also requiring
`sqrt(Y0)exp(K/2)<=sqrt(ell)/4`, the H^(1/2) triangle inequality preserves
at least half the lower bound (549). Require |epsilon|<=A as well, giving
M0<=2A^2. Thus the genuine 3D globally regular solutions can satisfy

```text
M(U_epsilon(t_star))/M(U_epsilon(0))
                  >=Re^(1/3)/20480.              (556)
```

This ratio is arbitrarily large. The permissible nonzero epsilon depends
on A,nu and the reference history and may be extremely small.

The coupled solution also has a more conservative explicit history payment.
In the Fourier H^3 convention, M(d),L(d)<=Y. Consequently (555) gives
`sup M(d)<=Y0 exp(K)` and `integral L(d)<=Y0 exp(K)/nu`.
Use the squared triangle inequalities `M(U_epsilon)<=2M(U)+2M(d)`
and `L(U_epsilon)<=2L(U)+2L(d)`, and retain its exact initial mass
A^2+epsilon^2. Equations (550)--(552) imply

```text
C_H[U_epsilon](t)<=B_3D, for every t>=0,
B_3D=A^2+2B_mix+(2+4kappa)Y0 exp(K),              (557)
```

where B_mix is evaluated at B=A. This is a payment for ACTUAL coupled
histories, under the explicit perturbation condition (555). It includes
the original data's feedback through all times and all generated modes;
it does not assert a uniform large-perturbation payment. The sharper
B_mix itself is not transferred unchanged to the perturbed solution.
Uniqueness makes the same allowance apply to every available smooth prefix
from these initial data. No reserve is replenished at a segment boundary.

The remaining task is a nonlinear original-data reserve for unrestricted
mutually amplifying parents. This example requires such a reserve to permit
large transient amplification, retain the original parent's history, and
remain valid after that parent becomes dynamically coupled. A constant
multiplicative cap on the initial critical mass cannot meet that obligation.

Run `python3 -O labs/critical_shear_mixing.py`. Fourier moment identities,
the positive-viscosity error constants, the complete polynomial parent
return and the allowance algebra are checked exactly. The stochastic
identification, PDE comparison, all-time payment and small-perturbation
global stability remain analytic arguments, not Lean-certified statements.
No new Lean declaration or axiom is introduced.

## A change of self-interaction sign with finite history payment

The unsigned difference estimate (555) charges C3 Y^(3/2) for the
perturbation's complete self-interaction. This section tests a possible
geometric improvement: does an initially nonlinear-free perturbation keep
a favorable sign in the critical norm? It does not, even when it is
initially Beltrami. An actual positive-viscosity unforced history first
depletes, then produces, critical difference mass through this term.
Nevertheless, a commutator bound pays its absolute value over the entire
history. That payment extends to arbitrary smooth passive profiles in the
specified triangular class. It does not require a small passive amplitude.

All norms and inner products use the normalized 2*pi torus. Write
N(v)=P_sol(v cross curl v), Lambda=(-Delta)^(1/2), and

```text
u(0)=(A sin y+C cos z, D sin z, B cos x),
U(0)=(A sin y,0,B cos x), d=u-U,
Sigma_p(d)=<Lambda^p d,N(d)>.                    (558)
```

Here u and U are the ACTUAL unforced solutions from the displayed data;
U is the globally regular triangular solution (543). The reference is
not reset or replaced by its initial heat flow when B is nonzero.
The difference d is not an autonomous NS solution. Its equation contains
the two cross interactions with U as well as N(d), and

```text
(1/2) M(d)' + nu L(d)
 = Sigma_1(d)
   + <Lambda d,P_sol(U cross curl d+d cross curl U)>.       (559)
```

Thus the sign of Sigma_1 alone does not determine the sign of M(d)',
the full field's helicity transfer J, or its vorticity stretching g.
This is one specific cost in an actual-history estimate.

### The initial return distinguishes critical and high-norm work

Initially d=(C cos z,D sin z,0) and N(d)=0. If C=D, curl d=-d.
The complete A,B,C,D,nu polynomial jets of the projected NS equation give

```text
F=A^2 D^4+B^2 C^2 D^2,
Sigma_p(d(t))=F [2+5^(p/2)-3*2^(p/2)] t^3/32+O(t^4),
                 p=0,1,2,4,6,
Sigma_H3(d(t))=151 F t^3/32+O(t^4),
Sigma_H3=< (1-Delta)^3 d,N(d)>.                  (560)
```

Every coefficient through order two vanishes. The cubic coefficients
are independent of viscosity, but the viscosity terms have been retained
in the polynomial calculation and cancel. In particular
`2+sqrt(5)-3sqrt(2)<0`, whereas the enstrophy and H3 coefficients are
positive when F>0. The higher-norm bound can therefore hide a favorable
critical interaction. This local fact does not persist automatically.
The checker verifies the entire parameter polynomial and independently
compares the full advective NS recurrence, including canonical pressure
and all generated modes, at several positive-viscosity data.

### The same positive-viscosity history subsequently reverses sign

Set B=0 and A,D>0. The exact globally regular history is

```text
u=(C exp(-nu t)cos z+A f, D exp(-nu t)sin z,0),
f_t+D exp(-nu t)sin z f_y=nu(f_yy+f_zz), f(0)=sin y,
U=(A exp(-nu t)sin y,0,0), r=f-exp(-nu t)sin y,
Sigma_1(d)=-A^2 D exp(-nu t)<Lambda r,sin z r_y>. (561)
```

Pressure is identically zero for this exact triangular subclass. The
C component contributes no work in (561), by orthogonality of the
y frequencies. Choose C=D to keep the initial perturbation Beltrami.

Put sigma=Dt, mu=nu/D, and
`F_mu(sigma)=-<Lambda r_mu,sin z partial_y r_mu>`.
The zero-viscosity comparison is explicit:
`r_0=sin(y-sigma sin z)-sin y`. For
`q_n=(-1)^n J_n(sigma)-delta_(n,0)` and w_n=sqrt(1+n^2),
Fourier pairing gives

```text
F_0(sigma)=-(1/4) sum_(n in Z) (w_(n+1)-w_n) q_n q_(n+1)
 =-(sqrt(2)-1)(1-J_0(sigma))J_1(sigma)/2
  +(1/2) sum_(n>=1) (w_(n+1)-w_n) J_n(sigma)J_(n+1)(sigma).
1/100 < F_0(2) < 3/200.                          (562)
```

The classical generating function and power series are those in
[DLMF 10.12.1](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.12.E1) and
[DLMF 10.2.2](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.2.E2). At sigma=2,
`J_n(2)=sum_j (-1)^j/(j!(n+j)!)`. Alternating partial sums enclose
J_0,...,J_7 rationally. For n>=1,
`n/(n+1)! <= J_n(2) <= 1/n!`, so all omitted positive-index
pairs in (562) are positive. Keeping n=1,...,6 proves the lower
bound; the upper tail is at most
`[1/(2*7!*8!)]*72/71`. Rational square-root enclosures complete
the strict bounds. This is an infinite-series sign proof with a
controlled tail, not a floating-point or Galerkin observation.

To transfer it to POSITIVE viscosity, let e=f_mu-f_0 on 0<=sigma<=2.
Its exact equation is

```text
e_sigma+exp(-mu sigma)sin z e_y
 =mu Delta e+mu Delta f_0
   +(1-exp(-mu sigma))sin z partial_y f_0.        (563)
```

Pointwise differentiation of f_0 bounds
`||Delta f_0||_H1<26` and `||sin z partial_y f_0||_H1<4`
on this interval. For example the three components of the former
are bounded by 7,7,24, and those of the latter by 1,1,3.
Here H1 is the derivative norm, equal to the Fourier norm with weight
1+|k|^2. The forcing in (563) has H1 norm at most 34mu. In the H1
energy estimate the only transport commutator is
`-exp(-mu sigma)<e_z,cos z e_y>`, whose absolute value is at most
`(||e_y||_2^2+||e_z||_2^2)/2`. Therefore

```text
(||e||_H1)' <= (1/2)||e||_H1+34mu,
||e||_H1 <=68mu(exp(sigma/2)-1)<136mu,
||r_mu-r_0||_H1<138mu.                          (564)
```

The norm inequality at a zero norm follows by regularization. The final
2mu pays the difference of the heat baseline and the original sin y;
`||sin y||_H1=1`. Also `||r_0||_H1<4`. If mu<=1/138, then
`||r_mu||_H1<5`, and Cauchy--Schwarz in the defining bilinear pairing
gives `|F_mu-F_0|<1242mu`. Consequently

```text
D>=250000nu>0 implies F_mu(2)>1/200,
Sigma_1(d(2/D))>A^2 D exp(-2nu/D)/200>0.         (565)
```

Equation (560) makes Sigma_1 strictly negative for sufficiently small
positive t for these SAME data. Equation (565) proves a later positive
value on their actual unforced viscous history. The constants are
deliberately coarse and are not asserted to mark a sharp transition.
The failed assertion is persistence of favorable self-work from initial
Beltrami geometry. No integrated full-data allowance is refuted.

### Absolute self-work is paid for an unbounded class of profiles

Replace A sin y by any smooth real periodic w0(y,z). Let w solve
`w_t+D exp(-nu t)sin z w_y=nu Delta w` from w0 and let
`g=exp(nu t Delta)w0`. The actual unforced solutions

```text
u=(C exp(-nu t)cos z+w, D exp(-nu t)sin z,0),
U=(g,0,0), r=w-g,
K0=|| |partial_y|^(1/2) w0 ||_2^2              (566)
```

give the same identity (561), with A incorporated into r. Their difference
r has zero y-average, since the y-average of both w and g obeys the same
heat equation. In Fourier variables (m,n), let r_hat(m,n)=a_(m,n).
An exact adjacent-frequency pairing gives

```text
-<Lambda r,sin z r_y>
 =-(1/2) sum_(m,n) m [sqrt(m^2+(n+1)^2)-sqrt(m^2+n^2)]
                         Re(conj(a_(m,n)) a_(m,n+1)),
|<Lambda r,sin z r_y>| <=(1/2)|| |partial_y|^(1/2) r ||_2^2.  (567)
```

Indeed the absolute frequency-weight difference is at most one, by
the reverse triangle inequality. Apply `2|ab|<=|a|^2+|b|^2`
and sum; smoothness justifies every rearrangement. This estimate keeps
the signed interaction between adjacent coefficients before taking its
absolute value. It does not replace shared phases by separate averages.

The directional operator |partial_y|^(1/2) commutes with this actual
shear advection and with diffusion. The resulting field has |m|>=1,
so its exact energy identity and Poincare inequality imply

```text
|| |partial_y|^(1/2) w(t) ||_2^2 <=exp(-2nu t)K0,
|| |partial_y|^(1/2) g(t) ||_2^2 <=exp(-2nu t)K0,
|| |partial_y|^(1/2) r(t) ||_2^2 <=4exp(-2nu t)K0,
|Sigma_1(d(t))| <=2|D|K0 exp(-3nu t),
integral_0^infinity |Sigma_1(d)| <=2|D|K0/(3nu). (568)
```

Thus `R_rel(t)=2|D|K0 exp(-3nu t)/(3nu)` is a single nonnegative
reserve with `-R_rel'>=|Sigma_1|`. It pays both signs across every
compatible segment. It never resets the original directional resource
or the shear amplitude. For w0=A sin y, K0=A^2/2 and the allowance
is A^2|D|/(3nu), at arbitrary A,C,D and positive viscosity.

The positive result is a concrete bound for the critical difference
self-interaction. It does not on its own control the cross work in (559).
For the sinusoidal example, the full critical criterion is already paid
by (552), with shear amplitude D and passive amplitude A. The additional
C mode contributes exactly

```text
C_H[C exp(-nu t)cos z]=-alpha C^2(1-exp(-2nu t))/2<=0,
C_H[u](t)<=B_mix(D,A).                          (569)
```

Here 0<alpha<1 and B_mix(D,A) denotes the allowance in (552) with
that substitution. Thus the sign-reversing example pays the complete
continuation criterion as well as the isolated self-work account.

### Small genuine 3D feedback and the remaining obstruction

The strict later sign survives a sufficiently small nonzero B cos x
in (558). This follows from actual H3 continuous dependence on the
known global B=0 flow, and the explicit linear dependence on B of
the reference U. The cubic map d -> Sigma_1(d) is continuous in H3.
The negative initial coefficient in (560) also persists. All generated
modes and pressure are retained; there is no finite-mode closure.

More explicitly, use (555) around the B=0 actual flow with
`Y0=4B^2`, `Q=C4[|A|(1+(D/nu)^4)+|C|+D]` and K=C3Q/nu.
For D>0 the stochastic derivative bounds (544) justify this Q after
increasing the fixed norm constant C4. The stated smallness condition
constructs a global perturbed solution. Decrease |B| further until the
H3 continuity error in Sigma_1 at t=2/D is below half the positive
margin (565). All constants are from known references and the original
data. This gives genuinely three-coordinate unforced flows with the
same sign reversal. The admissible B may be extremely small.

The full history of that small perturbation is paid by the same
triangle-inequality argument as (557):

```text
M0_ref=(A^2+C^2+D^2)/2,
C_H[u_B](t)<=M0_ref+2B_mix(D,A)+(2+4kappa)Y0 exp(K).       (570)
```

In deriving this bound retain `M(u_B(0))=M0_ref+B^2/2`; dropping
the favorable subtraction B^2/2 gives (570). Uniqueness transfers the
same bounds to all smooth prefixes from that datum. Neither (568) nor
(570) supplies a payment for arbitrary three-dimensional coupling.

The structural reason (568) works is precise: the transported direction
commutes with the known parent flow, so its initial fractional variation
only decays. A general parent can generate variation in that direction,
and a moving direction has its own derivative cost. The next physical
obligation is to retain and pay these commutators and the parent's renewal
from original data. Assuming the same decay after the parent becomes
arbitrary would put the missing estimate into a hypothesis.

This defect can be stated directly on arbitrary smooth periodic NS flows,
without selecting a reference. For a fixed coordinate j, set
T_j=|partial_j|^(1/2), K_j=||T_j u||_2^2 and
Q_j=||grad T_j u||_2^2. Commutation with gradients and divergence removes
pressure from the integrated identity, while incompressibility cancels
the undifferentiated transport:

```text
K_j'+2nu Q_j=2W_j,
W_j=-<T_j u,[T_j,u dot grad]u>
   =<|partial_j|u,N(u)>,
M<=sum_j K_j<=sqrt(3)M,
L<=sum_j Q_j<=sqrt(3)L.                          (571)
```

The comparisons follow mode by mode from
`|k|<=|k_x|+|k_y|+|k_z|<=sqrt(3)|k|`. For the FULL actual family
(558), the complete polynomial calculation gives

```text
W_y(0)=0,
W_y(t)=A^2 B^2 t/4+O(t^2).                      (572)
```

Thus the nonzero B component supplies a positive nonlinear source to the
directional resource, whose evolution had only diffusion in (566). This
does not assert that the source already exceeds diffusion. The calculation retains
all C,D,nu terms; their cancellation in (572) is an identity, not an
assumption. A transient positive W_y does not refute an integrated payment.

There is a concrete continuation consumer for a successful repair. If a
finite allowance B_dir from the full original datum, nu and horizon bounds

```text
2 integral_0^t sum_j W_j-2alpha nu integral_0^t sum_j Q_j<=B_dir
                                                        (573)
```

on every same-datum smooth prefix, then (571) gives
`M(t)+2(1-alpha)nu integral L<=sum_j K_j(0)+B_dir`.
This pays (494) with allowance `sum_j K_j(0)-M0+B_dir`.
The allowance in (573) is OPEN for arbitrary data. Equation (568) pays
one specific relative self-work term in a commuting geometry; it is not
a proof of (573). The next test must control the actual commutator's
generation and return, rather than assume directional variation decays.

Run `python3 -O labs/relative_selfwork_history.py`. It checks the complete
jet polynomials, independent pressure-inclusive NS jets, strict rational
Bessel bounds, viscous comparison constants, adjacent-mode pairing and
reserve algebra, including the first generation of directional work.
The analytic PDE comparison, general commutator estimate,
all-time payment and continuous-dependence extension are not Lean-certified.
No Lean declaration or axiom changes.

## Material coordinates, critical diffusion and a paid physical metric

The directional resource in (568) only decays because its derivative
commutes with a particular parent flow. Following the ACTUAL fluid removes
advection more generally, but changes the diffusion operator. A fixed
Euclidean critical norm in the material labels need not decrease under
that diffusion. This section proves an increase ABOVE its initial value
on an actual unforced positive-viscosity flow with zero pressure.

Retaining the physical metric restores the correct negative diffusion
term. Its deformation then has a separate cost. For the shear class that
cost has an explicit original-data payment, giving a direct bound for
the COMPLETE critical continuation criterion and arbitrary smooth passive
profiles. For arbitrary interacting parents the metric cost remains open.

### The actual material flow and its diffusion operator

Consider the exact unforced NS solution on the normalized 2*pi torus

```text
u=(A exp(-nu t)sin y,0,w(t,x,y)),
w_t+A exp(-nu t)sin y w_x=nu Delta w, w(0)=w0,
theta(t)=A(1-exp(-nu t))/nu,
T_theta f(x,y)=f(x+theta sin y,y), h=T_theta w.   (574)
```

Its pressure is zero. The FULL material flow has
`Phi_x=x+theta sin y`, `Phi_y=y` and
`Phi_z=z+integral_0^t w(s,Phi_x(s),y) ds`.
The z coordinate is retained but does not enter these z-independent
velocity components. The flow preserves volume. The operator T_theta
is unitary on scalar L2, and the exact material equation is

```text
h_t=nu L_theta h,
L_theta=T_theta Delta T_theta^(-1)
 =partial_x^2+(partial_y-theta cos y partial_x)^2
 =Delta-2theta cos y partial_xy+theta sin y partial_x
        +theta^2 cos^2 y partial_xx,
<h,L_theta h>=-||h_x||_2^2-||h_y-theta cos y h_x||_2^2.    (575)
```

Thus kinetic energy still decreases. The diffusion matrix has determinant
one, but this does not make its pairing with the FIXED label operator
Lambda=(-Delta_label)^(1/2) negative. Viscosity in these coordinates has
the two noise directions displayed by the sum of squares in (575), not
an unchanged isotropic label Laplacian. This transformation introduces no
external force into the fluid.

### An exact negative multiplication form

Let

```text
h0(x,y)=cos x q(y),
q(y)=11-14cos(2y)+8cos(4y)-4cos(6y)+2cos(8y),
a_0=11, a_(+/-2)=-7, a_(+/-4)=4, a_(+/-6)=-2, a_(+/-8)=1,
P0=sum_n (1+n^2)^(3/2) a_n^2
  =121+490sqrt(5)+544sqrt(17)+296sqrt(37)+130sqrt(65),
P2=sum_n sqrt(1+n^2) a_n [a_n/2+(a_(n-2)+a_(n+2))/4]
  =22-(7/2)sqrt(5)-2sqrt(17)-sqrt(37),
-4/25<P2<-3/20,
<Lambda h0,L_theta h0>=-(P0+theta^2 P2)/2.        (576)
```

The coefficient linear in theta vanishes by Fourier parity. At theta=256
the last expression exceeds 1900. These are exact rational/radical
identities. All generated Fourier modes are retained. A positive value
at a selected field and metric alone would not establish an actual-history
counterexample; the next argument supplies that connection.

### The full viscous material velocity exceeds its initial critical mass

Fix nu>0, take A>0, set w0=A h0 and rescale sigma=At, mu=nu/A. Write
`h=A H_mu`. Then

```text
theta_mu(sigma)=(1-exp(-mu sigma))/mu,
partial_sigma H_mu=mu L_(theta_mu) H_mu, H_mu(0)=h0,
G(sigma)=integral_0^sigma L_s h0 ds,
H_mu(sigma)=h0+mu G(sigma)+O_H1(mu^2)             (577)
```

uniformly on the FIXED interval 0<=sigma<=S=512. The first variation
includes the actual viscosity dependence of theta; replacing it by
sigma contributes only to the controlled second-order remainder.

The complete velocity composed with its full material flow is
`A(exp(-mu sigma)sin y,0,H_mu(sigma))`. Hence its fixed-label critical
mass, including the decaying parent, obeys

```text
M_label(S/A)-M_label(0)=A^2[mu Gamma_S+O(mu^2)],
Gamma_S=-S(1+P0)-(S^3/3)P2>3000000, S=512.       (578)
```

This is an expansion in the viscosity/amplitude ratio on a controlled
interval, not a Taylor forecast in time of an unknown long trajectory.
Here is one explicit, deliberately coarse remainder bound. All functions
remain in the x frequencies +/-1. For 0<=theta<=S the H1 energy estimate
for `v_sigma=mu L_theta v+F` gives

```text
(||v||_H1)'<=mu c_S ||v||_H1+||F||_H1,
c_S=S+2S^2.                                    (579)
```

The only potentially positive derivative pairing comes from
`[partial_y,L_theta]v`. Its highest derivative term is
`2theta sin y partial_x partial_y v`, whose real pairing with v_y
vanishes. The remaining terms are bounded by
`(theta+2theta^2)||v_y||_2 ||v||_2`; the other diffusion pairings are
nonpositive. The x derivative commutes with L_theta. Regularizing the
norm justifies (579) at zero.

In Fourier Hm norms, multiplication by sin y or cos y has norm at most
2^m, and multiplication by cos^2 y at most 4^m. For m=1,3 these give

```text
a_S=1+24S+64S^2, b_S=12S^2+64S^3,
||L_theta f||_Hm<=a_S ||f||_H(m+2),
||[L_(theta_mu(sigma))-L_sigma]h0||_H1
 <=mu b_S ||h0||_H3.                            (580)
```

The second line uses
`0<=sigma-theta_mu(sigma)<=mu sigma^2/2` and
`|theta_mu(sigma)^2-sigma^2|<=mu sigma^3`. Let

```text
R=39*66^3, G_star=S a_S R,
C=3S R(b_S+S a_S^2),
E=(R+G_star+C)^2+S^2,
mu_star=1/[2(E+c_S S+1)].                        (581)
```

Since h0 has `1+|k|^2<=66` and Fourier l1 norm 39,
`||h0||_H5<=R`. Set e=H_mu-h0-mu G. Its exact forced equation is

```text
e_sigma-mu L_(theta_mu) e
 =mu[L_(theta_mu)-L_sigma]h0+mu^2 L_(theta_mu)G,
e(0)=0.                                        (582)
```

For mu c_S S<=1, (579)--(580) yield `||e||_H1<=C mu^2` on the
entire interval. Also `||G||_H1<=G_star`. Expanding the quadratic
critical mass and using Cauchy--Schwarz bounds its remainder by
`(R+G_star+C)^2 mu^2` for mu<=1. The remaining S^2 term in E pays
the second-order remainder of the parent's exponential decay. Thus

```text
0<mu<=mu_star implies
M_label(S/A)-M_label(0)>A^2 mu/2>0.              (583)
```

For EVERY fixed nu>0 choose a finite A>=nu/mu_star. This gives an
actual smooth global unforced NS history satisfying (583). No backward
parabolic reconstruction or Galerkin closure is used. The constants
are very conservative; they establish existence of a strict failure,
not its optimal amplitude threshold. The failed claim is contraction
of the fixed Euclidean critical norm in material labels. Neither
kinetic-energy decay nor the full-data continuation budget is refuted.

### Retaining the physical metric restores the correct cost

Define the nonnegative self-adjoint operator
`A_theta=T_theta Lambda T_theta^(-1)`. Unitary conjugation gives
`A_theta^2=-L_theta`. The PHYSICAL critical mass of the passive component
is `M_w=<h,A_theta h>`, not `<h,Lambda h>`. If X=sin y partial_x,

```text
A_theta'=theta'[X,A_theta],
M_w'= <h,A_theta' h>-2nu<h,A_theta^3 h>,
<h,A_theta' h>=-2theta'<Lambda w,sin y w_x>.      (584)
```

The diffusion term now has its correct negative sign. The deformation
of the metric has not disappeared. The adjacent-mode estimate (567),
with coordinates exchanged and applied to the ACTUAL w, gives

```text
K_x(t)=|| |partial_x|^(1/2) w(t)||_2^2,
K_x(t)<=exp(-2nu t)K_x(0),
|<h,A_theta' h>|<=|theta'|K_x(t)
                  <=|A|K_x(0)exp(-3nu t),
integral_0^infinity |<h,A_theta' h>|
                  <=|A|K_x(0)/(3nu).            (585)
```

This holds for ANY smooth real periodic w0(x,y), with no amplitude
smallness. The directional derivative commutes with the actual shear;
its nonzero x frequencies justify Poincare. Its zero x frequencies
contribute no metric work. This is an original-data payment for the
physical metric, not a replacement of the evolving w by heat parents.

For the FULL field, including the shear, the critical balance is
`M'+2nu L=<h,A_theta' h>`. Therefore, for 0<alpha<1, the complete
criterion (494) has the allowance

```text
C_H(t)=M(t)-M0+2(1-alpha)nu integral_0^t L
      <=B_metric:=|A|K_x(0)/(3nu), for all t>=0,
R_source(t)=B_metric exp(-3nu t)>=0,
-R_source'>=|<h,A_theta' h>|.                    (586)
```

No reserve is replenished between segments. The resulting critical
continuation reserve is also `R_H=M+B_metric-C_H>=0`, as in (494).
For w0=B cos x this gives `B_metric=|A|B^2/(6nu)`. For the fixture
w0=A h0 it gives `B_metric=87A^3/(2nu)`. These whole-history bounds
coexist with the material-norm increase (583). A sinusoidal receiver can
use the minimum of this bound and (552); the new bound is smaller in the
large-shear regime. No optimal constant is claimed. These estimates stay
within a known regular class and do not establish regularity for arbitrary
three-dimensional data.

### The exact arbitrary-flow bridge and its remaining obligation

The physical metric identity has a direct counterpart on EVERY available
smooth periodic unforced NS prefix. Let Phi_t be its actual volume-preserving
material flow, T_t f=f composed with Phi_t, V=T_t u and
`A_t=T_t Lambda T_t^(-1)`. These are actual fluid-derived operators.
Then

```text
A_t'=T_t[u dot grad,Lambda]T_t^(-1),
d/dt <V,A_t V>
 =<V,A_t' V>-2nu<V,A_t^3 V>,
<V,A_t' V>=-2<Lambda u,(u dot grad)u>=4J.        (587)
```

Indeed `V'=T_t(nu Delta u-grad p)`. The pressure term in this
pairing is `-2<Lambda u,grad p>=0` by physical incompressibility;
it is not removed from the underlying evolution. Differentiating the
unitary conjugation and using skew-adjointness of u dot grad proves
the last equality. All identities are understood on smooth fields on
that prefix; they do not assume a global material flow already exists.

Thus a full-data bound on the signed metric-deformation cost, after its
viscous payment, is exactly the remaining critical history obligation.
Equation (586) proves that bound in a commuting geometry. Arbitrary
parents regenerate the directional variation, as (572) already shows.
Following them removes advection from the material equation but does not
give (585) for free. Even a bound in fixed labels would need metric control
before becoming a physical continuation estimate. In the shear example,
interpolation of the unitary L2 bound with
`||grad T_theta f||_2<=(1+|theta|)||grad f||_2` gives
`(1+|theta|)^(-1) M(w)<=M_label(h)<=(1+|theta|)M(w)`.
For general material flows the corresponding distortion is itself part
of the unpaid history.

Run `python3 -O labs/material_critical_history.py`. It checks the actual
coordinate chain rule, factorized diffusion and L2 balance, complete Fourier
quadratic forms, strict rational sign bounds, interval remainder constants
including parent decay, and the full physical allowance algebra. The PDE
comparison, fractional interpolation, operator identities on smooth flows
and all-history estimates remain analytic, not Lean-certified. No Lean
declaration or axiom changes.

## Cubic velocity, pressure work and a Bernoulli reserve

The material-metric cost in (587) depends on the observation. Incompressible
pullback preserves the physical cubic velocity mass EXACTLY, without any
metric comparison. Its integrated nonlinear source is pressure work. A
Bernoulli correction supplies a nonnegative reserve and a full-history payment
in a nonzero-pressure, arbitrary-amplitude cellular class. Genuine 3D parents
can generate an adverse correction defect immediately. Thus the change of
observation removes one cost but does not establish an arbitrary-data bound.

### The physical budget and its continuation consumer

On an actual smooth unforced prefix on R3 with the stated decay, or on the
normalized 2*pi torus, write r=|u| and

```text
Y=integral r^3,
D=integral r |grad u|^2 + r |grad r|^2,
Pi=-integral r u dot grad p=integral p u dot grad r,
Y'+3nu D=3Pi.                                      (588)
```

At u=0 the expression `r |grad r|^2` is understood through
`sum_j (u dot partial_j u)^2/r`, with value zero. The Hessian of |u|^3 is
`3r I+3u tensor u/r`, extended continuously by zero at u=0. Multiplying
NS by `3r u`, incompressibility, and integration by parts give (588).
For every volume-preserving material map Phi,
`integral |u composed with Phi|^3=Y`. Unlike (575), no fixed fractional
operator on labels appears. Pressure remains in the actual equation.

A sufficient target, retaining half the diffusion, is

```text
C3(t)=3 integral_0^t Pi-(3nu/2) integral_0^t D
     =Y(t)-Y(0)+(3nu/2) integral_0^t D <= B3,
K=Y(0)+B3,
sup Y <= K, integral_0^t D <= 2K/(3nu).             (589)
```

For arbitrary-data continuation the quantifiers are essential: for each
original datum, nu>0 and prescribed H, choose a finite B3 BEFORE all available
smooth prefixes from that datum of duration at most H. No future norm may
supply this allowance. The existing `WholeSpaceCubicHistory` controls the
TIME INTEGRAL of Y from energy and viscosity; it does not establish (589).

The consumer of (589) has a short classical proof. Sobolev applied to r^(3/2)
gives `||u||_9^3 <= C D` on R3 and `<= C(D+Y)` on the fixed torus.
For E1=||grad u||_2^2 and E2=||Delta u||_2^2, the complete NS equation gives

```text
E1'+nu E2 <= C nu^(-2) ||u||_9^3 E1,
E1(t) <= E1(0) exp[C nu^(-2) K (nu^(-1)+chi H)],
chi=0 on R3, chi=1 on the fixed torus.               (590)
```

Indeed the convection pairing is at most
`||u||_9 ||grad u||_(18/7) ||Delta u||_2`, and interpolation bounds this
by `C ||u||_9 E1^(1/3) E2^(2/3)`. Young's inequality and Gronwall prove
(590). The constants depend only on the domain's Sobolev constants.
Thus (589) supplies the hypothesis of the existing whole-space Lean theorem
`WholeSpaceViscousFlow.hasNSEvolution_of_orderOne_bound` in
`MettapediaNS.WholeSpaceEnstrophyContinuation`; the periodic enstrophy
continuation argument applies likewise. This NEW derivation has not been
formalized in Lean. In particular, the already certified consumer does not
certify the missing payment.

This is the classical nonendpoint Serrin mechanism, with L3 in time and
L9 in space. The stronger endpoint result that sup_t ||u||_3 alone suffices
on R3 is due to Escauriaza--Seregin--Sverak; see Theorem 1.1 and the
quantitative refinement in [Tao, arXiv:1908.04958](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.04958).
We do not need to import that endpoint theorem to deduce (590), because
(589) also pays D.

### A nonnegative pressure completion and its exact defect

Let h be a specified smooth scalar along the SAME actual solution prefix,
with the integrability needed below. It is an observer correction, not a
force on the fluid. Suppose P=p+h>=0, and define

```text
e=|u|^2/2, Q=e+P,
L=partial_t+u dot grad-nu Delta,
S=(partial_t-nu Delta)p+Lh,
LQ=S-nu |grad u|^2,
Z=2sqrt(2) integral Q^(3/2), R=Z-Y>=0.               (591)
```

The energy equation is `Le=-u dot grad p-nu |grad u|^2`.
Adding p cancels its advective pressure derivative and leaves S. In
particular, replacing S by the material derivative of p alone would be
incorrect. The full entropy identity is

```text
Z'=3sqrt(2) integral sqrt(Q) S
   -3sqrt(2)nu integral sqrt(Q) |grad u|^2
   -(3sqrt(2)/2)nu integral |grad Q|^2/sqrt(Q).       (592)
```

Use positive regularization and passage to the limit at Q=0. On R3 also
use spatial cutoffs and the stated integrability; a nonzero constant h over
all R3 is not admissible because it makes Z infinite. Since
`D <= 2 integral r |grad u|^2 <= 2sqrt(2) integral sqrt(Q)|grad u|^2`,
(588)--(592) give the actual-history inequality

```text
R'+3Pi-(3nu/2)D <= 3sqrt(2) integral sqrt(Q) S,
C3(t) <= R(0)+3sqrt(2) integral_0^t integral sqrt(Q) S.   (593)
```

The last step retains R(t)>=0. This is useful only when positivity of P,
finiteness of R(0), and a full-data bound for the SIGNED right-hand defect
are established. Defining h or its allowance from an uncontrolled future
pressure is not a proof. For a spatially varying h, its advection and
viscosity in Lh must both be retained. Even a time-dependent pressure gauge
has the extra cost h'.

There is also a direct stochastic interpretation on a smooth periodic prefix.
For `dX_s=-u(t-s,X_s)ds+sqrt(2nu)dW_s`, X_0=x, the scalar representation is
`Q(t,x)=E[Q(0,X_t)+integral_0^t (S-nu|grad u|^2)(t-s,X_s)ds]`.
If S<=0, Jensen's inequality and preservation of volume imply Z(t)<=Z(0).
The differential identity (592) additionally retains the required diffusion
payment. These are actual fluid-driven paths; no independent replacement of
joint expectations or external fluid control is made. The representation
and entropy argument are analytic, not new stochastic Lean certificates.

### A complete payment with nonzero pressure and arbitrary amplitudes

Consider the exact periodic class

```text
a(t)=A exp(-2nu t),
u=(a sin x cos y,-a cos x sin y,w(t,x,y)),
p=(a^2/4)(cos(2x)+cos(2y)),
w_t+(a sin x cos y)w_x-(a cos x sin y)w_y=nu Delta w,
h=a^2/2, P=(a^2/4)(2+cos(2x)+cos(2y))>=0.          (594)
```

Here w(0) is ANY smooth real periodic profile. These are actual unforced
NS solutions: the horizontal Euler convection is exactly -grad p, the
horizontal field is a Laplace eigenfield of eigenvalue -2, and the vertical
component obeys the displayed scalar advection-diffusion equation. Its
smooth coefficients give a global smooth evolution. No amplitude smallness,
finite-mode closure, or reset of the passive component is imposed. This is
an already known regular class, not a new arbitrary-data regularity theorem.

Crucially `p_t-nu Delta p=0` and `h'=-2nu a^2`, so S=-2nu a^2<=0.
Consequently

```text
B3=R(0)=2sqrt(2) integral (|u0|^2/2+p0+A^2/2)^(3/2)-Y(0),
R(t)>=0, R'+3Pi-(3nu/2)D<=0,
C3(t)<=B3, all t>=0,
Y(t)+(3nu/2) integral_0^t D <= Z(0).               (595)
```

This bounds the COMPLETE criterion (589), not just one separated source.
A coarse explicit estimate is
`B3 <= 3A^2 integral |u0|+3sqrt(2)|A|^3`, since 0<=P0<=A^2 and the
torus volume is normalized to one. The same reserve passes through every
intermediate time; it is never replenished. Signed pressure work can be
positive during the history. Its absolute time integral is not claimed to
be controlled by B3.

### Cubic mass really can grow in that paid viscous class

Let v=(sin x cos y,-cos x sin y,0), p_*=(cos(2x)+cos(2y))/4 and

```text
F=v dot grad p_*=cos x cos y (sin^2 y-sin^2 x),
mean F=0, integral F^2=1/32,
integral |sin x| F^2=43/(840pi),
u0^-=A(v_x,v_y,16sin x(1-F)),
u0^+=A(v_x,v_y,16sin x(1+F)).                       (596)
```

Both fields are smooth, divergence-free and have ZERO spatial mean.
Reflection x -> pi-x preserves |v| and sin x, reverses F and exchanges
their speed fields. Thus they have equal initial Y and kinetic energy,
but opposite Pi. To prove strictness without numerical quadrature, use
`|v|<=1`, `|F|<=1` and
`0<=sqrt(|v|^2+w^2)-|w|<=|v|`. For w=16sin x(1-F), this gives

```text
Pi(u0^-)/A^4 >= 16*43/(840pi)-||v||_2 ||F||_2
             >179/1320>1/8,
D(u0^-)/A^3 <=2*33*(1+163)=10824,
A>=100000nu implies Y'(0)>0.                      (597)
```

The exact gradient square of sin x(1-F) is 163/256. The pressure-error
bound is 1/8 by Cauchy--Schwarz. The classical strict inequality pi<22/7
also follows from the positive integral
`integral_0^1 x^4(1-x)^4/(1+x^2) dx=22/7-pi`.
The constants are deliberately conservative. Continuity of the actual
smooth solution makes Y(t)>Y(0) on a nonzero interval. Nevertheless the
all-time budget (595) holds. This refutes cubic contraction, not the
pressure-corrected reserve or regularity. The opposite profile has strictly
negative initial pressure work; energy and speed-norm data alone cannot
identify that sign.

### Interacting 3D parents generate the unpaid defect

Take a different, genuinely three-dimensional periodic datum

```text
u0=(A sin y,B sin z,C sin x), A,B,C>0.
p0=0,
partial_t p(0)=-2ABC cos x cos y cos z.             (598)
```

These identities use canonical mean-zero pressure. In the complete NS
initial tangent,
`u_t(0)=nu Delta u0-(u0 dot grad)u0`; the pressure at time zero vanishes
because `trace((grad u0)^2)=0`. Differentiating
`-Delta p=trace((grad u)^2)` gives (598), including all generated modes.
The viscous part of this derivative cancels, not the nonlinear part.
Thus pressure is NOT automatically caloric in an unforced flow.

At (0,0,0), u0=0 and `partial_t(e+p)(0)=-2ABC<0`. The uncorrected
Bernoulli quantity, initially nonnegative, becomes negative there on the
actual short-time smooth history. At (pi,pi,pi),

```text
[L(e+p)](0,pi,pi,pi)=2ABC-nu(A^2+B^2+C^2).
A=B=C=a>3nu/2 makes this strictly positive.        (599)
```

It remains positive on a nonzero neighborhood in space and time by local
smooth existence and continuity. A constant positive gauge can repair
initial positivity but does not change this defect. A changing gauge can
change the sign only by contributing its own derivative to S.
These are pointwise failures of a proposed automatic correction, not a
counterexample to an integrated full-datum allowance, nor to NS regularity.

For reference the general pressure-defect equation is

```text
-Delta [(partial_t-nu Delta)p]
 =-2 sum_ij (partial_i u_j) partial_j[(u dot grad)u_i+partial_i p]
  -2nu sum_ijk (partial_k partial_i u_j)(partial_k partial_j u_i).   (600)
```

It follows by differentiating the same pressure Poisson equation. This
retains nonlinear parent interactions, pressure feedback and viscosity.
The next substantive obligation is to control the weighted SIGNED history
in (593), with a finite nonnegative completion initialized from the full
datum. The initial source (598) must be paid; suppressing it, assuming
pressure follows heat, or repeatedly rebuilding (595) from a fresh parent
would fail this test. The known cellular payment calibrates a proposed
repair but does not establish it for unrestricted 3D coupling.

### The imported forced construction fails this pressure budget

For forced NS the exact cubic balance gains the direct work

```text
J_f=integral |u| u dot f,
Y'+3nu D=3Pi+3J_f,
|J_f|<=||f||_infinity ||u||_2^2.                    (601)
```

Apply this to precisely the same whole-space fields satisfying the pinned
`NavierStokesR3.ProblemStatement.CandidateProperties`, supplied by
`NavierStokesR3.theorem_1_1_with_initial_rest`. They have positive viscosity,
smooth velocity and pressure on every prefix before time 1, common compact
spatial support, zero original velocity, globally smooth compactly supported
forcing, uniformly bounded kinetic energy, and speed unbounded toward time 1.
The stronger theorem retains initial rest through 3/8. No periodic substitute
or dropped force is used.

For this ONE candidate, sup ||f||_infinity and sup ||u||_2^2 are finite,
so the absolute integral of J_f on [1/2,1) is finite. Nevertheless

```text
sup_(1/2<=t<1) [3 integral_(1/2)^t Pi
                  -(3nu/2) integral_(1/2)^t D]=+infinity.   (602)
```

To see this, a finite upper bound would give bounded Y and finite integral D
by (601). The R3 Sobolev estimate above would give finite
`integral_(1/2)^1 ||u||_9^3`. The forced version of (590) is
`E1'+nu E2 <= C nu^(-2)||u||_9^3 E1+C nu^(-1)||f||_2^2`.
Its forcing term has finite integral, so Gronwall would bound E1 uniformly.
That contradicts the existing Lean theorem
`ForcedCandidatePancake.no_uniform_gradient_energy` in
`MettapediaNS.ForcedSignedBudget`, whose hypothesis is this exact
`CandidateProperties`. The new cubic implication and (602) are analytic;
the imported candidate and its gradient-energy obstruction are separately
kernel-checked results.

Thus finite DIRECT cubic force work cannot explain away the failed pressure
payment. This does not show that its history can be realized without forcing:
the same zero initial datum with no force remains zero, and restarting from
a nonzero later slice changes the subsequent equation and history.

For completeness, the pressure-completed reserve itself has an additional
weighted force term. With Q and S defined as in (591), its forced inequality is

```text
R'+3Pi-(3nu/2)D <= 3sqrt(2) integral sqrt(Q) S
                   +3 integral (sqrt(2Q)-|u|) u dot f.     (603)
```

The second term is not J_f and is not automatically bounded by the estimate
in (601). No assertion that this extra observer cost is finite is needed for
(602). Any proposed pressure completion must account for it when tested on
the forced construction. The unforced task remains a finite original-data
payment for the actual signed defect in (593).

Run `python3 -O labs/cubic_pressure_reserve.py`. The checker verifies the
complete cellular and cyclic NS initial equations, differentiated pressure,
exact Fourier norms, pressure-sign reflection, rational growth margins,
convex entropy Hessian and the reserve's diffusion remainder. The PDE
history inequalities, scalar stochastic representation and continuation
bridge remain analytic, not Lean-certified. No Lean declaration or axiom
changes. No new general regularity result is asserted.

## Pressure storage and the complete Bernoulli return

The defect in (593) can charge pressure storage even when the observed
velocity moment is depleting. This section tests two concrete completions
on the SAME actual three-dimensional history. Both completions increase,
but a regularized cubic velocity moment lies strictly BELOW its original
heat forecast. The conclusions hold at positive viscosity on a controlled
interval. They do not rely on a finite-mode trajectory or identify an
unforced singularity.

### Three observations and the exact proposed payment

Work on the normalized 2*pi torus. Fix h>0 from the original datum and keep
it constant throughout the history. With e=|u|^2/2, define

```text
Phi(s)=2sqrt(2) s^(3/2), rho=e+h,
Y=integral |u|^3,
V=integral Phi(rho),
Z=integral Phi(rho+p),
W=integral [Phi(rho)+Phi'(rho)p].                    (604)
```

Z is the previous Bernoulli completion. W removes its convex pressure
remainder: `Z-W=integral [Phi(rho+p)-Phi(rho)-Phi'(rho)p]>=0` whenever
rho+p>0. It is the exact tangent in pressure, not a truncation of the fluid
itself. If p>=-h/2, both Z>=Y and W>=Y. Indeed the density in W is
`2sqrt(2)sqrt(e+h)(e+h+3p/2)`, which is at least
`2sqrt(2)sqrt(e+h)(e+h/4)>=|u|^3`. This hypothesis will hold on the entire
constructed interval. Also V>=Y, so V retains the velocity observation
used in (588)--(589). The constant h is admissible here
because the torus has finite volume; no such whole-space claim is made.

For either completion J=Z or J=W, the proposed nonnegative reserve R_J=J-Y
would pay the same pressure budget (589) monotonically if

```text
R_J'+3Pi-(3nu/2)D<=0,
equivalently J'+(3nu/2)D<=0.                       (605)
```

This is the exact claim tested below. It is stronger than merely having
SOME finite full-datum allowance. A violation of (605) does not refute that
weaker target.

Subtracting pressure variance changes the evolution and cannot be done for
free. For `L=partial_t+u.grad-nu Delta`, G=|grad u|^2 and
`H_p=(partial_t-nu Delta)p`, the complete tangent identity is

```text
W'=integral Phi'(rho) H_p - p Phi''(rho) u dot grad p
   -nu integral [Phi'(rho)+p Phi''(rho)] G
   -nu integral [Phi''(rho)+p Phi'''(rho)] |grad e|^2
   -2nu integral Phi''(rho) grad e dot grad p.       (606)
```

Here h is constant, as specified. The last mixed diffusion term has no
prescribed sign. Equation (606) follows by applying L to both factors of
Phi'(rho)p; it retains the actual pressure, transport, velocity diffusion
and derivative cross term. The full Z identity remains (592), with both
of its nonnegative diffusion terms retained.

### The first complete returns for cyclic interacting parents

Use the dimensionless Euler solution v^0 on its smooth local interval,
with original datum `U=(sin y,sin z,sin x)`. Its use here is to establish
strict margins that will be transferred to actual viscous solutions below.
Write e_j and p_j for the j-th time derivatives at zero of e and canonical
pressure. The existing complete NS jet operator supplies all generated
modes; specialize viscosity to zero for these coefficients. In particular,

```text
e_0=(sin^2 x+sin^2 y+sin^2 z)/2, p_0=0,
p_1=-2cos x cos y cos z, integral p_1^2=1/2,
p_2=-(2/3)[sin(2x)cos y sin z+sin x sin(2y)cos z
                       +cos x sin y sin(2z)].       (607)
```

This reuses the pressure derivatives from `cyclic_pressure_history.py`.
It is not a new claim that those local pressure sources exist. The new
calculation pairs the COMPLETE evolving derivatives with the nonlinear
observation weights.

Set h=1 in (604). Reflection symmetries give
`integral F(e_0) p_1=integral F(e_0) p_2=0` and
`integral F(e_0) e_1 p_1=0` for every smooth F on the relevant interval.
Moreover translating all three coordinates by pi sends U to -U. Euler
uniqueness and time reversal therefore make V, W and Z even functions of
time on a common small interval about zero. Their first and third time
derivatives vanish. The full second derivatives satisfy

```text
V''(0)=W''(0)=0,
Z''(0)=integral Phi''(1+e_0) p_1^2
       >=3/(2sqrt(5))>2/3.                        (608)
```

For V, differentiate its pressure-work identity once and integrate by parts;
the surviving term is a function of e_0 times p_1 u_0.grad e_0, whose
integral vanishes by the same symmetry. For W, (606) at zero viscosity
leaves the weighted p_2 and e_1 p_1 terms, which vanish. Z additionally
retains the strictly positive variance in (608). Thus its first increase
is not an increase of the velocity-only quantity V. The same variance
argument works for any strictly convex C3 function of e+p+h: convexity
alone does not supply a dissipating Bernoulli observation.

Removing that variance does not settle the next return. Exact weighted
integration of the fourth derivatives gives

```text
-47/100 < V''''(0)/sqrt(7/2) < -46/100,
  9/20  < W''''(0)/sqrt(7/2) <  23/50.
In particular V''''(0)<-4/5 and W''''(0)>4/5.      (609)
```

Both quantities start with the same value, since p_0=0. The tangent
completion has removed the positive second-order pressure variance, but
now grows at fourth order while the velocity-only moment decreases.
These are full derivatives, including the fourth pressure derivative and
all generated velocity fields. Dropping the new squared terms or replacing
the pressure by its first jet would give a different calculation.

### Exact certification of the nonpolynomial weights

Here is the finite calculation behind (609). Let `r0=1+e_0`. Chain and
product rules give the fourth derivative as a sum of four weighted
polynomials. For W these polynomials are

```text
P0=e4+p4,
P1=4e1 e3+3e2^2+4e3 p1+6e2 p2+4e1 p3,
P2=6e1^2 e2+12e1 e2 p1+6e1^2 p2,
P3=e1^4+4e1^3 p1,
W''''/sqrt(2)=integral [3sqrt(r0) P0
 +(3/2)r0^(-1/2)P1-(3/4)r0^(-3/2)P2+(9/8)r0^(-5/2)P3].   (610)
```

For V remove all terms involving p_j. Every P_j is an exact rational
trigonometric polynomial. Since
`e_0-3/4=-(cos(2x)+cos(2y)+cos(2z))/4`, write
`r0=(7/4)(1+q)`, with |q|<=3/7. Expand each power `(1+q)^alpha`,
alpha=1/2,-1/2,-3/2,-5/2, through degree N=32.

Every retained moment is rational. For a Fourier mode with an odd coordinate
the integral is zero. For k=(2m1,2m2,2m3), the moment of `(e_0-3/4)^n`
is `(-1/4)^n n!` times the degree-n coefficient in the product of the three
exponential generating functions

```text
sum_(l>=|m|, l=m mod2) binom(l,(l+m)/2) t^l/(2^l l!).      (611)
```

Coordinate reflections allow |m| and coordinate permutations without losing
information, since this particular weight depends on the symmetric e_0.
If L_P bounds the Fourier l1 norm of P, the absolute omitted integral is at
most

```text
L_P |binom(alpha,N+1)| (3/7)^(N+1) /(1-r_alpha),
r_alpha=(3/7)(1+|alpha|/(N+1))<1.                         (612)
```

The ratio bounds every subsequent absolute binomial term. Applying (612)
with the actual polynomial norms certifies the strict rational intervals
in (609). This is an exact enclosure, not floating-point quadrature. The
checker also compares the low moments with independent direct Fourier
multiplication and verifies the symmetry cancellations in (608).

### A uniform interval at positive viscosity

The signs above persist for actual NS, rather than only for Euler. Let
v^mu solve unforced periodic NS with viscosity mu in [0,1], initial datum U,
and pressure q^mu. Choose m=16 and N0=||U||_Hm. The usual local Sobolev
energy estimate provides constants C_m and a positive time tau, depending
only on this fixed datum and Sobolev product constants, such that

```text
sup_(0<=sigma<=tau, 0<=mu<=1) ||v^mu(sigma)||_Hm <=2N0.     (613)
```

For example take tau no larger than `1/(4C_m(1+N0))` after enlarging C_m
in the standard estimate. Pressure is the order-zero multiplier applied
to v tensor v. Its time derivative and all the Euler time derivatives
through order five needed below consequently have finite bounds computed
from N0 and the product constants. No future solution norm defines those
bounds. This is the smooth local inviscid-limit argument; for classical
background see [Kato, 1972](https://doi.org/10.1016/0022-1236(72)90003-1).
The periodic estimates required here are described explicitly below.

These envelopes can be obtained recursively: start with B0=2N0, and for
Euler use `B_(j+1)=C_m sum_(r=0)^j binom(j,r) B_r B_(j-r)` to bound
the j+1 time derivative in H^(m-j-1), through j+1=5. The same products
bound pressure derivatives. The finitely many derivatives of Phi on the
resulting compact positive argument range then bound the scalar observation
derivatives. For q^mu_sigma also retain the term mu Delta v^mu; its
H^(m-2) norm is at most 2N0. Thus the constants below are a priori
functions of fixed Sobolev constants and N0, rather than assumed regularity
bounds on a future interval.

Let K1 bound ||partial_sigma q^mu||_infinity in (613). Reduce tau so that
`tau<=1/[4(1+K1)]`. Since q^mu(0)=0, this guarantees |q^mu|<=1/4 and
hence the positivity hypotheses for BOTH completions throughout the common
interval. Let M>=1 bound the third and fifth time derivatives of the three
Euler observations there. Reduce to
`s=min(tau,1/(1+M),1)>0`. Taylor's theorem, (608)--(609) and the vanishing
odd derivatives give

```text
Z^0(s)-Z^0(0)>=s^2/6,
W^0(s)-W^0(0)>=s^4/60,
V^0(s)-V^0(0)<=-s^4/60.                           (614)
```

All these constants can be chosen from the original profile's local Sobolev
bounds. In particular M is an a priori derivative envelope from (613),
not an unrestricted supremum of the unknown future.

For completeness, set d=v^mu-v^0. Its projected equation has source
mu Delta v^mu and convection `v^mu.grad d+d.grad v^0`. The H^(m-2) estimate
therefore gives
`(||d||_H(m-2))'<=C N0 ||d||_H(m-2)+2mu N0`, with d(0)=0.
Gronwall bounds d by `2mu N0 tau exp(CN0 tau)` uniformly on the interval.
The pressure multiplier and Sobolev embedding give the corresponding uniform
pressure bound. Since the observation arguments stay strictly positive,
there is a finite original-profile constant L such that each of V, W and Z
changes by at most L mu relative to its Euler value on that interval.
The heat forecast `v_heat^mu=exp(-mu sigma)U` likewise differs from its
initial velocity observation by at most L_heat mu.

Choose
`mu_* = min(1,s^4/[240(1+L+L_heat)]) >0`.
For every mu in (0,mu_*], (614) implies

```text
Z^mu(s)-Z^mu(0)>=s^2/12,
W^mu(s)-W^mu(0)>=s^4/80,
V^mu(s)-V(v_heat^mu(s))<=-s^4/80.                 (615)
```

This uses the complete positive-viscosity equations, not an inviscid answer
substituted for a viscous history. The small parameter is viscosity divided
by amplitude; the physical initial datum need not be small.

For ANY prescribed physical nu>0, choose A>=nu/mu_* and take the actual
datum A U. Then
`u(t)=A v^(nu/A)(At)`, `p(t)=A^2 q^(nu/A)(At)` and h=A^2.
At t_*=s/A, each observation in (604) is A^3 times its dimensionless value.
Consequently (615) is a strict, quantitative comparison on actual smooth
unforced NS prefixes with arbitrary fixed positive viscosity. Both reserves
remain nonnegative throughout the interval. Yet for J=Z and J=W,

```text
J(t_*)-J(0)+(3nu/2) integral_0^(t_*) D >0,        (616)
```

contradicting the proposed monotone payment (605). The diffusion is not
omitted: its contribution to the left side is nonnegative, and the actual
viscous comparison already includes its effect on J. Strict inequalities
also persist on a nonzero neighborhood of t_* by continuity.

The velocity comparison is specifically for the regularized moment V, not
a claim about the sign of every vorticity or stretching observable. The
heat forecast uses the ORIGINAL datum; no parent is reset. No global
regularity of this cyclic 3D family is assumed or proved.

### Consequence for the history reserve

This calculation rules out two specific passive pressure completions as
universally monotone payers. The convex completion charges pressure variance
before the velocity observation changes. Its tangent repair cancels that
first charge but still overestimates the next return in this example.
Neither failure establishes unforced blowup or disproves a finite allowance
