from the full initial datum. It also does not contradict the cellular
all-time payment (595), whose pressure has additional structure.

The next physical target is the signed pressure--velocity work itself,
with an evolving correction whose full defect is paid, rather than making
every pressure rearrangement a positive expense. The negative velocity
return (609), and the positive returns of both completed observations,
are discriminating tests for such a correction. Its positivity, pressure
lower envelope and cost under repeated 3D parent renewal must all remain
explicit. A successful cancellation at one return cannot be restarted
indefinitely without an actual-history estimate.

Run `python3 -O labs/bernoulli_pressure_return.py`. Full rational Fourier
jets, exact weighted-series enclosures, the complete tangent evolution and
comparison margins pass. The local Sobolev existence bounds, Taylor
remainder envelopes and inviscid comparison used to obtain (615)--(616)
remain analytic, not Lean-certified. No Lean declarations or axioms change.

## Cyclic entropy depletion and its scale boundary

The favorable velocity return in (609) extends to an entire family with
unequal amplitudes. It does not extend to arbitrary spatial scales, even
when all amplitudes are equal. Both conclusions use the complete physical
equation and the same regularized cubic velocity observation. Thus the
scale counterexample concerns actual velocity redistribution, rather than
the pressure-storage overcharge in (608)--(616).

### A uniform amplitude law at a common scale

On the normalized 2*pi torus, take the smooth Euler datum
`U=(a sin y,b sin z,c sin x)`, with a,b,c>0, and any fixed h>0. Define
`Phi(s)=2sqrt(2)s^(3/2)` and `V(t)=integral Phi(e(t)+h)`, where
e=|u|^2/2. The Euler calculation is a calibration for the actual
positive-viscosity comparison below. It proves

```text
V'(0)=V''(0)=V'''(0)=0,
V''''(0)<=-delta(a,b,c,h)<0,
delta=(7sqrt(2)/80) a^2 b^2 c^2 (a^2+b^2+c^2)
                 /sqrt(h+(a^2+b^2+c^2)/2).                (617)
```

In particular this applies to h=max(a^2,b^2,c^2), fixed from the original
datum. No smallness or comparability assumption on the amplitudes is used.
The fourth return is zero if any parent is removed. The family is not an
invariant class of solutions: its generated modes are retained, and (617)
cannot be restarted later by pretending the original geometry persists.

The proof simplifies in material coordinates without discarding pressure.
Let D_t=partial_t+u.grad, and write M_j=(D_t^j e)(0). The actual material
flow preserves volume. Initially p0=0, M1=0, and
`M2=-U.grad p1`, with `p1=-2abc cos x cos y cos z`. Consequently

```text
V''''(0)=integral [Phi'(e0+h) M4+3Phi''(e0+h) M2^2].       (618)
```

The new square in (618) has a positive coefficient and must be retained.
This is not the return obtained by following only the original parents.

Set X=sin^2 x, Y=sin^2 y, Z=sin^2 z and
`r=h+(c^2 X+a^2 Y+b^2 Z)/2`. Average the finite Fourier polynomials over
coordinate reflections and half-period translations, which leave r
unchanged. Denote that projection by an overbar. Complete symbolic
pressure and velocity jets give

```text
overbar(M2)=0,
overbar(M4)=(16/15)a^2 b^2 c^2 S,
overbar(M2^2)=4a^2 b^2 c^2 T,
S=30XYZ-27(XY+XZ+YZ)+11(X+Y+Z),
T=c^2 X(1-X) Z(1-Y)+a^2 Y(1-Y) X(1-Z)
                         +b^2 Z(1-Z) Y(1-X).              (619)
```

The coordinates and their weights remain ordered. Permuting unequal
weights would invalidate the calculation. The first and third integral
derivatives vanish by Euler time reversal and the translation of all
three coordinates by pi. The second vanishes by overbar(M2)=0.

Under normalized spatial integration, X,Y,Z are independent arcsine
variables on [0,1]. Integration by parts gives
`E[(X-1/2)G]=E[X(1-X) partial_X G]` for a smooth G. The boundary term
vanishes because sqrt(X(1-X)) vanishes at both endpoints. Since h>0,
all the weights below are smooth on the closed cube. Applying this
identity to the three terms in T combines the two terms of (618):

```text
V''''(0)=-(4/15)a^2 b^2 c^2 E[Phi'(r) P],
P=150XYZ-27(XY+XZ+YZ)+X+Y+Z.                              (620)
```

Although P has both signs, its weighted average here has a definite sign.
Write x=X-1/2, y=Y-1/2, z=Z-1/2. Then
`P=150xyz+48(xy+xz+yz)+(23/2)(x+y+z)`.
Put `d=(c^2,a^2,b^2)/2`, `t_i=d_i X_i(1-X_i)`,
`S1=sum t_i`, `S2=sum_(i<j) t_i t_j`, and `S3=t1 t2 t3`.
Repeated arcsine integration by parts, now applied to Phi'(r), yields

```text
E[Phi'(r)P]=3sqrt(2) E[r^(-5/2) B],
B=(23/4)r^2 S1-12r S2+(225/4)S3,
B-(7/4)r^2 S1
 =4r S1(r-S1)+2r sum_(i<j)(t_i-t_j)^2+(225/4)S3 >=0.      (621)
```

Every term on the right is nonnegative because
`r-S1=h+sum d_i X_i^2>0`. Thus (620) is at most
`-(7sqrt(2)/5)a^2 b^2 c^2 E[S1/sqrt(r)]`.
Finally `E[X(1-X)]=1/8`, so `E[S1]=(a^2+b^2+c^2)/16`, and
`r<=h+(a^2+b^2+c^2)/2`. This proves the quantitative bound (617).
The strict sign comes from the full pressure return and its new square
together; neither one was assigned a favorable sign separately.

### Different scales reverse the physical return

Now keep equal amplitudes but use
`U_*=(sin y,sin(4z),sin x)` and h=1. Its initial canonical pressure is
also zero. Its initial speed distribution, and hence every integral
depending only on that speed, is identical to the unit-frequency datum.
Its spatial derivatives and generated pressure are different. Computing
the COMPLETE Euler jets gives

```text
V_*'(0)=V_*''(0)=V_*'''(0)=0,
73/1000 < V_*''''(0)/sqrt(7/2) <74/1000,
in particular V_*''''(0)>1/8.                             (622)
```

The reflection projection again verifies the vanishing second derivative.
Translation by `(pi,pi,pi/4)` sends U_* to -U_*, giving the vanishing odd
derivatives by Euler uniqueness and time reversal. There is no discarded
Fourier output or imposed closed cascade.

For certification, all physical Fourier differentiation and pressure
inversion use wave numbers `(k_x,k_y,4k_z)`. Only AFTER generating the
complete jets are they pulled back to independent phase coordinates.
The integer phase covering preserves normalized spatial integration.
In those coordinates e0 is again the symmetric sum of three squared sines.
Therefore the exact rational weighted-series integration (611)--(612)
applies with h=1, center 7/4, radius 3/7 and degree 32. The checker bounds
the fourth derivative both by the Eulerian chain formula (610), with
pressure-observer terms removed, and independently by the complete
material formula (618). Both enclosures imply (622). Applying the old
unit-wave-number pressure operator after this change of coordinates would
be incorrect; the checker preserves the physical wave numbers throughout
the evolution calculation.

Thus changing only a spatial frequency reverses the signed physical
return. The amplitude law (617) is valid on its stated domain, while its
extension to all cyclic spatial scales is false. This is a statement about
the regularized cubic velocity moment, not a universal claim about
vorticity stretching or every measure of concentration.

### Actual positive-viscosity histories

Both strict signs transfer to actual unforced NS. Here are the quantifiers
and interval bounds. Fix either a common-scale profile U with its h>0 and
margin delta from (617), or U_* with h=1 and delta=1/8. Let v^mu solve NS
with that same datum and viscosity mu in [0,1]. The local H16 estimate
(613) supplies a common interval [0,tau] and an a priori bound from the
original profile. Because e+h>=h, finite product-rule recursions and the
derivatives of Phi on that positive range give an a priori fifth time
derivative bound M for the Euler observation. No pressure lower bound is
needed for this velocity-only observation.

Choose `s=min(tau,1,5delta/[2(1+M)])>0`. Let epsilon=-1 for (617) and
epsilon=+1 for (622). Taylor's theorem gives
`epsilon[V^0(s)-V^0(0)]>=delta s^4/48`.
The same H14 difference estimate as below (614) bounds
`|V^mu(s)-V^0(s)|<=L mu`, with L determined by the original profile,
h and the local Sobolev constants. The original heat forecast obeys
`|V(exp(mu s Delta)U)-V(U)|<=L_heat mu`. These are finite original-data
constants, not assumed control of an unknown future history.

For
`0<mu<=mu_*=min(1,delta s^4/[96(1+L+L_heat)])`, one obtains

```text
epsilon [V^mu(s)-V(exp(mu s Delta)U)]>=delta s^4/96,
and, for U_*, V^mu(s)-V(U_*)>=s^4/768>0.                  (623)
```

For ANY fixed physical viscosity nu>0 choose a finite amplitude
`A>=nu/mu_*`. The actual solution with original datum A U is
`u(t)=A v^(nu/A)(At)`. Use the constant original-data regularizer A^2 h.
At t_*=s/A all the entropy differences in (623) are multiplied by A^3.
The heat comparison is always with the ORIGINAL datum:
for U_* it is
`A(e^(-nu t)sin y,e^(-16nu t)sin(4z),e^(-nu t)sin x)`.
Strict inequalities persist on a neighborhood of t_*.

In the unequal-scale example, V initially decreases: p0=0 and the full
viscous derivative at zero is strictly negative. Yet (623) places V
strictly above its initial value later on the same smooth history. Kinetic
energy decreases throughout according to its usual viscous identity.
The pressure is generated internally and only redistributes energy;
no external force, reinitialization or negative-viscosity evolution is
used. The proof provides a local interval and a finite amplitude threshold,
not optimized numerical thresholds or global regularity for these 3D data.

### What the continuation reserve still has to pay

The physical meaning is visible directly in the complete identity for V.
Set `r=|u|`, `s_h=sqrt(r^2+2h)`, `G=|grad u|^2`, and

```text
Pi_h=-integral Phi'(e+h) u.grad p
    = integral p Phi''(e+h) u.grad e,
D_h=3 integral [s_h G+(r^2/s_h)|grad r|^2],
V'+nu D_h=Pi_h,       D_h>=3D,                            (624)
```

where D is the cubic diffusion from (588). These formulas hold along
every smooth unforced periodic prefix with constant h>0. The norm gradient
is understood almost everywhere; at zero velocity the multiplied terms
vanish. To verify the comparison, write
`D_h-3D=3 integral (s_h-r)[G-(r/s_h)|grad r|^2]>=0`, using
`|grad r|^2<=G`. All pressure and viscous terms remain present.

Consequently a finite full-datum bound B_h on every available prefix for

```text
integral_0^t Pi_h-(nu/2)integral_0^t D_h <= B_h
implies
Y(t)+(3nu/2)integral_0^t D <= V(0)+B_h.                   (625)
```

This feeds the SAME cubic/enstrophy continuation argument (588)--(591).
The allowance must be fixed by the full original datum, nu and horizon
before ranging over all its smooth prefixes. It cannot be defined by an
uncontrolled future supremum. Equation (623) rules out automatic monotone
payment `V'+(nu/2)D_h<=0` even for cyclic initial geometry. It does not
refute SOME larger original-data allowance in (625).

The common-scale law is a useful geometric calibration; scale imbalance
is an explicit obstruction to iterating that law indiscriminately.
Neither an increasing velocity moment nor a sequence of isolated initial
jets constructs a singularity. Whether repeated, changing, interacting
parents have a finite allowance in (625) remains open. Constant h has
infinite background integral on R3, so this particular regularized
observation and new family results are periodic statements; the original
unregularized whole-space criterion remains unchanged.

Run `python3 -O labs/cyclic_entropy_depletion.py`. The symbolic full jets,
ordered reflection projection, arcsine polynomial identities, nonnegative
remainder and two exact weighted enclosures pass. The integration-by-parts
argument, common local interval, derivative envelopes and positive-viscosity
comparison are analytic, not Lean-certified. No Lean declarations or
axioms change.

## Stochastic pressure histories, entropy and a coercive moment

`kinetic_pressure_entropy.py` checks a pressure-history lift of actual
unforced periodic NS. It reuses the pressure-compensated stochastic
representation and its viscous covariance, rather than identifying an
arbitrary stochastic control with a fluid. Two choices of reference
measure distinguish a paid entropy from a coercive one. The first has an
exact original-energy allowance but is too weak for continuation. The
second controls a sufficient regularity norm, but actual internal pressure
can increase it despite its complete Fisher dissipation.

These are analytic statements on each available smooth solution prefix.
The checker certifies their finite Gaussian-moment algebra, complete NS
jets and a non-Gaussian shear fixture; it does not certify the PDE or
stochastic interval arguments in Lean. No global arbitrary-data estimate
is asserted. The stochastic fluctuation-dissipation background includes
[Drivas and Eyink, 2017](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.00729); the existing
Constantin--Iyer reconstruction and pressure-impulse identities retain
their separate hypotheses. The auxiliary velocity below is a history
variable, not the velocity driving particle positions.

### Identification with the actual fluid

Use normalized spatial measure on the 2*pi torus. Let u,p solve unforced
NS with viscosity nu>0 on a smooth prefix, and fix eta>0 from the original
datum. Write G_eta for the centered three-dimensional Gaussian density
with covariance eta I. With a uniform initial label a and an independent
Gaussian zeta, define

```text
dX_t=u(t,X_t)dt+sqrt(2nu)dW_t,       X_0=a,
dV_t=-grad p(t,X_t)dt,              V_0=u_0(a)+zeta,
zeta ~ N(0,eta I),

partial_t f+u.grad_x f-grad p.grad_v f=nu Delta_x f,
f(0,x,v)=G_eta(v-u_0(x)).                                  (626)
```

The flow in x is volume preserving for every common Brownian realization:
its spatial derivative solves the usual variational equation with trace
zero. Its law, with the independent initial Gaussian spread, constructs
f. In particular f is positive and smooth in x,v on every such prefix.
The pressure impulse and its spatial derivatives are bounded there, so
Gaussian tails justify the following integrations by parts, first with
velocity cutoffs and then by passage to the limit. This construction uses
an already available smooth prefix and does not assume its continuation.

Let D=partial_t+u.grad_x-nu Delta_x and g=grad p. Integrating (626) gives
D rho=0 for rho=integral_v f, with rho(0)=1; hence rho=1. The first moment
m=integral_v vf satisfies Dm=-rho g with m(0)=u_0. The actual NS velocity
satisfies Du=-g. Uniqueness for this linear parabolic equation proves m=u.
Thus the lift reconstructs the actual velocity and retains its canonical
pressure. No auxiliary control or force is applied to the fluid.

Define the raw moments and covariance

```text
L=integral_v v tensor v f,   T=integral_v |v|^2 v f,
K=integral_v |v|^4 f,        Sigma=L-u tensor u,
B=grad u,

D L=-u tensor g-g tensor u,
D T=-(2L+tr(L)I)g,          D K=-4g.T,
D Sigma=2nu B B^T,          Sigma(0)=eta I,
integral_x tr L(t)=E_0+3eta,  E_0=||u_0||_2^2.             (627)
```

The last identity uses integral u.grad p=0. Sigma is eta I plus the
already identified viscous-memory covariance. The augmented second
moment is conserved while the mean fluid loses energy: that loss appears
in the covariance. This is not replenishment of the physical energy.
The equations through K retain all their lower moments; they do not
impose a Gaussian closure.

At a joining time the entire evolved f, or a proved sufficient collection
of joint moments for a specified consumer, must be retained. Restarting
with G_eta(v-u(t,x)) discards generated covariance and higher moments.
The linear transition kernels for the same actual u,p compose with the
evolved density as their input. Matching only their means does not give
that compatibility or preserve the entropy history.

### An entropy paid by energy, and why it is insufficient

All entropies below integrate over x and v. Set

```text
H_G=integral f log(f/G_eta),
I_x=integral f |grad_x log f|^2,
H_G(t)+nu integral_0^t I_x = E_0/(2eta).                   (628)
```

Indeed the phase-space drift in (626) is divergence free, so
`(integral f log f)'=-nu I_x`. The Gaussian cross-entropy depends only on
the conserved augmented second moment (627). The initial translated
Gaussians give H_G(0)=E_0/(2eta), and H_G>=0. Thus (628) pays the full
spatial Fisher information on every available prefix from original data,
without taking a future supremum.

There is also an exact connection to the existing covariance reserve.
Let q_x be the Gaussian with the SAME mean u(x) and covariance Sigma(x)
as f(x,.). Moment matching gives
`H_G=integral_x KL(f(x,.) || q_x)+R_eta/(2eta)`, where
`R_eta=integral_x [|u|^2+tr(Sigma-eta I)-eta log det(Sigma/eta)]`
is the previous viscous-memory entropy. The remainder is nonnegative;
its vanishing would require the Gaussian closure tested below. This
identity does not assert that the remainder decreases on its own.

Nevertheless H_G cannot control a quartic velocity moment using this
allowance alone. Choose an odd smooth nonzero function phi supported in
(-1,1), I_j=integral phi^j for j=2,4, and a small epsilon>0. The periodic
shear datum
`u_epsilon(y)=A_epsilon phi(y/epsilon)e_1`, with
`A_epsilon^2=2pi/(epsilon I_2)`, has

```text
||u_epsilon||_2^2=1,
||u_epsilon||_4^4=(2pi I_4/I_2^2)/epsilon.
```

It evolves globally by the one-dimensional heat equation with p=0.
Every datum has the same Gaussian entropy 1/(2eta), whereas its fourth
moment is unbounded along the family. This refutes energy-only coercivity,
not an allowance depending on the full initial datum. It also illustrates
why a finite entropy budget is useful only after its physical observation
has been identified.

### A coercive entropy and its exact pressure defect

Instead fix kappa>0 from the original datum and use
`g_kappa(v)=Z_kappa^(-1)exp(-kappa|v|^4)`, where
`Z_kappa=pi Gamma(3/4) kappa^(-3/4)`. Its relative entropy obeys

```text
H_kappa=integral f log(f/g_kappa)>=0,
H_kappa'=-nu I_x-4kappa integral_x g.T,

H_kappa(0)=kappa[||u_0||_4^4+10eta E_0+15eta^2]
           -(3/2)log(2pi eta)-3/2+log Z_kappa.            (629)
```

The initial Gaussian moments are
`L_0=u_0 tensor u_0+eta I`,
`T_0=(|u_0|^2+5eta)u_0`, and
`K_0=|u_0|^4+10eta|u_0|^2+15eta^2`.
All constants in H_kappa(0) are finite original-data quantities.
Pressure no longer cancels: it couples to T, not just to the mean u.

The Gibbs variational inequality with test `(kappa/2)|v|^4` gives
`H_kappa>=(kappa/2)integral_x K-(3/4)log2`, since
`Z_(kappa/2)/Z_kappa=2^(3/4)`. Conditional Jensen and rho=1 then give

```text
||u(t)||_4^4 <= integral_x K(t)
             <= (2/kappa)[H_kappa(t)+(3/4)log2].          (630)
```

This has a concrete continuation consumer. If H_kappa<=B uniformly on
all available prefixes of a prescribed horizon H, put
`K_4=(2/kappa)[B+(3/4)log2]`. For E_1=||grad u||_2^2 and
E_2=||Delta u||_2^2, the periodic enstrophy estimate gives

```text
E_1'+nu E_2 <= C nu^(-7)||u||_4^8 E_1,
E_1(t) <= E_1(0) exp(C nu^(-7) H K_4^2).
```

For completeness, convection is at most
`C||u||_4 E_1^(1/8)E_2^(7/8)` by Holder and the periodic
Gagliardo--Nirenberg estimate for grad u. Its zero spatial mean removes
the constant-mode term. Young's inequality absorbs diffusion and leaves
the displayed power eight. This is the usual nonendpoint continuation
argument, not a new Lean theorem. The genuinely missing input is the
uniform bound B from original data, rather than finiteness on each
already smooth prefix.

### The third central moment is real history

Let C_ijk be the third central velocity moment and let c_i=sum_j C_ijj.
Without assuming f Gaussian, product differentiation in (627) gives

```text
T=(|u|^2+tr Sigma)u+2Sigma u+c,
D C_ijk=2nu sum_l [ (partial_l u_i)(partial_l Sigma_jk)
                  +(partial_l u_j)(partial_l Sigma_ik)
                  +(partial_l u_k)(partial_l Sigma_ij) ]. (631)
```

The third central moment starts at zero but need not remain zero.
Explicit pressure terms cancel in the centered equation; pressure still
influences the evolving u and Sigma. Every cross-gradient term in D's
product rule is retained. The checker verifies this identity for arbitrary
symbolic u, one arbitrary spatial gradient, and symmetric raw second
moments and covariance gradients. Summing over spatial directions gives
(631).

There is an exact positive-viscosity example, not merely an initial jet.
Take the globally regular shear
`u=A exp(-nu k^2 t)sin(ky)e_1`, p=0, with integer k>=1. The conditional
law in (626) is a mixture of Gaussians centered at
`A sin(k(y+sqrt(2nu)W_t))e_1`. At ky=pi/6, write
q=exp(-nu k^2 t). The first three moments of the sine center, divided by
A, A^2 and A^3 respectively, are
`q/2`, `(1-q^4/2)/2`, and `(3q/2-q^9)/4`.
At the positive time `nu k^2 t=log2`, their third central moment is

```text
c_1=-297 A^3/2048,     c_2=c_3=0,     for every eta>0.
```

Independent Gaussian spread changes neither this third central moment
nor its sign. Thus a Gaussian replacement for f loses actual history
already on a regular decaying flow. This shear has zero pressure work;
its role is to test the proposed closure, not to produce amplification.

### Actual pressure can overcome the full entropy dissipation

Use the unequal-scale cyclic datum U_*=(sin y,sin(4z),sin x), with
eta=kappa=1. For the Euler calibration, let F=integral |u|^4. Full
canonical-pressure time jets give

```text
F'(0)=F''(0)=F'''(0)=0,     F''''(0)=7184/15015>1/3.
For U=(sin y,sin z,sin x), F''''(0)=-23/5.                 (632)
```

The checker computes both the raw-moment system (627) and the complete
material derivatives of the physical quartic observation. For Euler,
`f(t,x,v)=G_1(v-u(t,x))`: the pressure-compensated velocity follows the
same deterministic material equation as u, plus its independent constant
Gaussian offset. Hence `H_1(t)-H_1(0)=F(t)-F(0)` in this calibration.
The integrated raw fourth moment starts at 261/8, and its first three
derivatives vanish. Every generated Fourier output is retained. The
pressure derivatives have respectively 0,8,24,68 modes. Positive-viscosity
moment fixtures at nu=2/7 provide a separate algebra check; the interval
argument below does not substitute Euler for viscous evolution.

Apply the uniform local H16 estimate (613) to this fixed U_* and viscosity
mu in [0,1]. It supplies a common interval [0,tau], bounds for the velocity,
pressure and their spatial derivatives, and a fifth-derivative envelope M
for the Euler F, all from the original profile. With delta=1/3 and
`s=min(tau,1,5delta/[2(1+M)])`, Taylor gives
`F^0(s)-F^0(0)>=delta s^4/48`.

Here is a bound for the FULL Fisher loss of the kinetic law. Use a common
Brownian motion for all labels and define
`Z_t(a)=U_*(a)-integral_0^t grad p^mu(r,X_r(a))dr`.
For the inverse spatial flow A_t, put z_t(x)=Z_t(A_t(x)). Pathwise volume
preservation gives
`f^mu(t,x,v)=E G_1(v-z_t(x))`. Let K_u bound ||grad u^mu||_infinity,
P bound ||Hess p^mu||_infinity and U_1 bound ||grad U_*||_infinity, using
compatible operator/Frobenius norms. Then

```text
||grad X_t||, ||grad A_t|| <= exp(K_u tau),
||grad z_t||_F <= L_z=exp(K_u tau)[U_1+tau P exp(K_u tau)],
I_x(f^mu(t)) <= L_z^2.                                   (633)
```

The last inequality follows from convexity of Fisher information under
mixtures and the exact shifted-Gaussian formula
`integral_v G_eta(v-z)|grad_x log G_eta(v-z)|^2
 =||grad z||_F^2/eta`.
These are pathwise bounds, since the common additive noise disappears
from the spatial variational equation. Their constants are furnished by
the common local estimate, not by an unknown long-time solution bound.

Couple X^mu with the deterministic Euler flow from the same label. The
H14 inviscid estimate below (614), the uniform pressure-gradient bounds,
and Brownian maximal estimates give
`E sup_(t<=tau)|X_t^mu-X_t^0|<=C sqrt(mu)` and the same bound for
`E|Z_t^mu-Z_t^0|`. This may be evaluated on periodic lifts. The centers
Z_t are uniformly bounded; integrating their Gaussian fourth moments
therefore yields
`|integral K^mu(s)-integral K^0(s)|<=C_4 sqrt(mu)`.
Here and in (633), C_4,L_z depend only on the original profile and the
chosen local interval. In particular all stochastic spreading and
viscous pressure changes are retained.

The exact Boltzmann-entropy loss from (629) now gives

```text
H_1^mu(s)-H_1^mu(0)
 >= delta s^4/48-C_4 sqrt(mu)-mu s L_z^2
 >= delta s^4/96>0                                      (634)
```

whenever
`0<mu<=min(1,[delta s^4/(192(1+C_4))]^2,
                 delta s^4/[192(1+s L_z^2)])=:mu_*`.
At the initial time p=0, so H_1'(0)=-mu I_x(0)<0. Thus it first falls
and later lies strictly above its initial value on the SAME actual
unforced smooth history. The full Fisher dissipation, not merely its
initial value, has been subtracted in (634).

For any prescribed physical viscosity nu>0 choose a finite A>=nu/mu_*.
The actual datum A U_* and solution `u(t)=A u^(nu/A)(At)` have this same
behavior using original-data parameters eta=A^2 and kappa=A^(-4).
The density is `f_phys(t,x,v)=A^(-3)f^(nu/A)(At,x,v/A)`, and its reference
quartic density scales by the same factor. Relative entropy is invariant
under that velocity change, so (634) holds at t=s/A. These parameters are
fixed once and retained across the entire history. No external force,
parent reset, backward viscous solve or finite-mode trajectory is used.
The conclusion concerns a local smooth interval; it is not a proof of
global regularity or singularity for the cyclic datum.

### The remaining finite-history payment

The exact sufficient target supplied by this lift is

```text
-4kappa integral_0^t integral_x grad p.T
       -nu integral_0^t I_x <= A(u_0,nu,H,eta,kappa)
for every available smooth prefix and 0<=t<=H.            (635)
```

A finite allowance chosen from the full original datum and prescribed
horizon gives H_kappa<=H_kappa(0)+A and hence (630)'s continuation bound.
This allowance remains OPEN. Equation (634) refutes zero allowance or
automatic monotonicity, not every finite full-data payment. Equation
(631) identifies a specific piece of history that a Gaussian closure
would discard. It does not assign all the adverse pressure work to that
piece: the mean and covariance terms in T must also be retained.

In particular a nonnegative correction R with R(0)=0 cannot make
H_kappa+R nonincreasing on the witness (634). Such a repair would imply
H_kappa(t)<=H_kappa(0), contradicting the actual burst. A successful
reserve therefore needs an initially funded allowance, a different
coercive observation, or signed cross terms whose total positivity and
evolution are proved. Simply adding positive generated-memory costs
without initial funding cannot repair this candidate.

This construction places the physical identification and the observation
needed for continuation on the same probability law. It does not establish
an optimal-control or Schrodinger-bridge identification, nor a Bellman
supersolution paying (635). The new entropy argument uses a uniform
spatial probability measure on the torus. It makes no whole-space claim
with an infinite constant spatial background. Neither one entropy burst
nor independently concatenated initial jets demonstrates infinite renewal.

Run `python3 -O labs/kinetic_pressure_entropy.py`. The exact checks pass
with Python assertions disabled. Density construction, entropy balance,
Gibbs coercivity, the local positive-viscosity comparison and the
continuation consumer remain analytic. No Lean declarations or axioms
change.

## A Bellman payment for complete stochastic pressure histories

`pressure_parent_bellman.py` checks an explicit Bellman bound and its
identification with the physical pressure histories (626). It supplies an
all-time payment for entire exact flow families, including genuine 3D
Beltrami parents. A separate example has increasing quartic entropy but
still satisfies this payment. The argument does not assume that its
stochastic histories are Gaussian or that amplification is absent.

The Bellman verification method is classical; see
[Nazarov, Treil and Volberg](https://www.math.brown.edu/streil/papers/Name/name1.pdf)
for its relation to stochastic control and martingale inequalities.
The ABC family is also classical; see
[Dombre et al., 1986](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0022112086002859).
The calculations below identify the particular physical history, original
resource and remaining arbitrary-flow obligation. They do not claim new
regularity for these already known global solution families.

### A direct continuation target in the actual pressure impulse

Keep the actual forward spatial flow X of (626), with uniform initial
label a, and define the pressure impulse without auxiliary Gaussian noise:

```text
P_t=integral_0^t grad p(s,X_s)ds,  Z_t=u_0(a)-P_t,
E[Z_t | X_t=x]=u(t,x),
E|Z_t|^2=E_0,                    E|P_t|^2<=4E_0,
||u(t)||_4 <= ||u_0||_4+(E|P_t|^4)^(1/4).                 (636)
```

The conditional mean solves the same linear advection-diffusion equation
as the actual NS velocity. The spatial marginal stays uniform. Thus
`(E|Z|^2)'=-2 integral u.grad p=0`; the pressure-impulse second-moment
bound follows by the triangle inequality in L2. This recovers the existing
pressure-history energy payment. The last line is conditional Jensen and
Minkowski, with no Gaussian hypothesis.

Consequently an original-data bound B_P(u_0,nu,H) for E|P_t|^4, uniform over
all available prefixes and t<=H, would give the enstrophy continuation bound

```text
E_1(t)<=E_1(0) exp(C nu^(-7) H [||u_0||_4+B_P^(1/4)]^8).
```

The physical Sobolev argument is the same nonendpoint estimate following
(630). This is an analytic sufficient criterion, not a new Lean consumer.
The fourth moment of the ACTUAL signed pressure impulse is the unpaid
input. An integral of absolute pressure-gradient norms is a stronger
sufficient assumption, but would discard the time cancellations retained
in P. Its second-moment bound alone does not supply its fourth moment.

### Why subtracting stored pressure is not automatically a payment

An initially tempting correction is
`J_gamma=H_kappa-gamma kappa ||p||_2^2`, for 0<gamma<1/2.
The canonical pressure projection is an L2 contraction from u tensor u:
Fourier Cauchy--Schwarz at every nonzero wave number gives
`||p||_2^2<=integral |u|^4<=integral K`. Thus (630) proves

```text
J_gamma+(3/4)log2 >= kappa(1/2-gamma)integral K>=0.         (637)
```

This is a coercive observation, but its pressure credit can disappear.
For equal-amplitude ABC initial data of amplitude L and wave number k,
eta=kappa=1, the exact viscous solution below has
`||p_0||_2^2=3L^4/4` and `integral |grad u_0|^2=3k^2 L^2`.
Its initial integrated quartic pressure work is zero. Therefore

```text
J_gamma'(0)=3nu k^2 L^2(gamma L^2-1).
For gamma=1/4 and L=3: J_gamma'(0)=(135/4)nu k^2>0.       (638)
```

The field is globally regular and its physical kinetic energy decays.
This refutes automatic monotonicity for the stated fixed correction and
parameters. It does not refute every datum-dependent choice of eta,kappa,
gamma, a time-dependent correction with its derivative accounted for,
or a finite allowance for J_gamma. The positive result below pays history
with an explicit initial stock instead.

### The Bellman function, its exact drift and compatible composition

Let N be a vector martingale with dN=sigma dW. Let q>=0 be its unspent
variance allowance, with dq=-a dt, where a>=tr(sigma sigma^T). Set
C=sigma sigma^T and d=a-tr C>=0. Define

```text
B(m,q)=|m|^4+6q|m|^2+3q^2,
(partial_t+generator) B(N,q)
 =-4 sum_(ell,i<j)(N_i sigma_jell-N_j sigma_iell)^2
   -6d(|N|^2+q) <=0.                                    (639)
```

The left side denotes the finite-variation drift in Ito's formula;
its martingale term is omitted only after taking conditional expectations.
The displayed equality is a polynomial identity for arbitrary sigma, N
and q. In particular it retains diffusion in every component and arbitrary
adapted rotations of the noise. The squares measure transverse variation
relative to N; they are not asserted to be vorticity-direction coherence.

There is an exact control interpretation. The Hessian is
`8m tensor m+(4|m|^2+12q)I`, whose largest eigenvalue is
`12(|m|^2+q)`. Hence

```text
partial_q B = sup_(C>=0, tr C<=1) (1/2) C:Hess_m B,
B(m,0)=|m|^4.                                           (640)
```

The supremum is attained by rank-one noise in the direction of m (any
unit direction at m=0). Equivalently, from a given m, keeping that noise
on the line through m for variance time q gives expected terminal fourth
power B(m,q). Thus the finite polynomial realizes the martingale control
bound; it is not an unproved future supremum. The controlled noises form
a relaxation containing the physical noise identified below. They are
not forces applied to the fluid, and no claim that every controller is
an NS evolution is needed.

Localization of Ito's formula and nonnegativity give, for s<=t,
`E[B(N_t,q_t)|F_s]<=B(N_s,q_s)`. The deterministic trace bounds used below
also give the required finite moments on finite intervals. In particular,
if N_0=-zeta for a centered three-dimensional Gaussian zeta with covariance
eta I, and q_0=Q_0,

```text
E|N_t|^4 <= E B(N_t,q_t)
          <= R_0=15eta^2+18eta Q_0+3Q_0^2.               (641)
```

With N_0=0 the initial stock is instead 3Q_0^2. Joining successive
segments retains N_s and the SAME unspent q_s. Resetting either one would
change the process and its funding. Conditional expectations compose this
bound without requiring independent segments. This certifies a cost for
a specified observation; it does not identify full physical histories
from the two summary variables alone.

### Identification and payment for exact viscous parents

Let U,p_* be a smooth periodic steady Euler field and canonical pressure,
with lambda>0 and
`div U=0`, `-Delta U=lambda U`, `U.grad U+grad p_*=0`.
Then the complete unforced NS evolution is

```text
u(t)=exp(-nu lambda t)U,
p(t)=exp(-2nu lambda t)p_*.                                (642)
```

Let L_0=||U||_infinity and L_1=||grad U||_(infinity,F).
On the actual spatial flow dX=u dt+sqrt(2nu)dW, set

```text
M_t=sqrt(2nu) integral_0^t grad u(s,X_s)dW_s,
q_t=(L_1^2/lambda)exp(-2nu lambda t),  Q_0=L_1^2/lambda,
a_t=2nu L_1^2 exp(-2nu lambda t),
D_t=u(t,X_t)+2nu lambda integral_0^t u(s,X_s)ds.
```

The noise covariance satisfies tr C_t<=a_t=-q_t'. Forward Ito sampling
adds nu Delta to the material NS equation. It gives
`du(t,X_t)=(-grad p+2nu Delta u)dt+sqrt(2nu)grad u dW`.
Using (642) yields the EXACT decompositions

```text
Z_t=D_t-M_t,       V_t=D_t-N_t,       N_t=M_t-zeta,
|D_t|<=L_0[2-exp(-nu lambda t)]<=2L_0.                   (643)
```

The factor 2 in the viscous integral is essential; a backward sampler
would require a different derivation. All pressure is retained through
the actual equation, rather than discarded or independently averaged.
Applying (641) and Minkowski gives the full kinetic fourth-moment bound
and, separately, a pressure-impulse bound without Gaussian noise:

```text
integral_x K(t)=E|V_t|^4 <= K_*=[2L_0+R_0^(1/4)]^4,
(E|P_t|^4)^(1/4) <= ||U||_4+2L_0+3^(1/4)sqrt(Q_0),
H_kappa(t)+nu integral_0^t I_x
 <= H_kappa(0)+kappa[K_*-K_0],       all t>=0.            (644)
```

Here K_0=integral_x K(0) is the original Gaussian fourth moment in (629).
The last inequality is the exact entropy identity, using
`H_kappa(t)+nu integral I_x=H_kappa(0)+kappa[integral K(t)-K_0]`.
Thus it pays the complete signed pressure history (635), and retains its
full Fisher loss. Since K_*>=K_0, its allowance is nonnegative and finite
from original data. There is no amplitude smallness, future solution norm,
Gaussian closure or renewal of q at an intermediate time.

### A genuine three-dimensional family, uniform across common scales

For any real A,B,C and integer k>=1, take the classical ABC field

```text
U=(A sin(kz)+C cos(ky),
   B sin(kx)+A cos(kz),
   C sin(ky)+B cos(kx)),
S=A^2+B^2+C^2,
curl U=kU,  lambda=k^2,  p_*=(S-|U|^2)/2,
|grad U|_F^2=k^2 S,  |U|^2<=2S,  Q_0=S.                 (645)
```

With all three amplitudes nonzero this depends on all three coordinates.
The identities give (642) directly, including its pressure and nonlinear
convection. The gradient-square identity is pointwise, not an average.
The checker verifies it symbolically for arbitrary amplitudes and physical
k derivatives, as well as by complete Fourier NS fixtures. The speed
bound follows by adding the three squared differences complementary to
the three squared sums in |U|^2.

Consequently (644) has the explicit bound
`K_*=[2sqrt(2S)+(15eta^2+18eta S+3S^2)^(1/4)]^4`.
It is independent of nu>0 and k, for fixed amplitudes and eta. The stronger
noise gradient at higher k is paid by its shorter viscous lifetime;
smaller viscosity gives a longer lifetime but a smaller noise rate. These
are exact cancellations in q, not an estimate extrapolated from samples.
The family has a fixed decaying spatial profile. Its existence does not
show that newly generated, interacting profiles have the same allowance.

### A paid history whose stronger entropy actually increases

The same mechanism applies to the cellular class (594) with ANY smooth
periodic w_0(x,y). Its horizontal parent is
`a(t)v`, where a=A exp(-2nu t) and
`v=(sin x cos y,-cos x sin y)`, with A>0. Its pressure is independent of
w. For the two-component horizontal martingale,
`Q_0=A^2`, `|D_h|<=2A`, and the initial Gaussian stock is
`R_h=8eta^2+12eta A^2+3A^4`.
The vertical history is exactly `V_3=w_0(a)+zeta_3` because partial_z p=0.
No independence between that history and the horizontal history is used.
Minkowski supplies

```text
K_*=[2A+R_h^(1/4)
       +(integral w_0^4+6eta integral w_0^2+3eta^2)^(1/4)]^4. (646)
```

Equation (644)'s entropy and Fisher payment follows for all t>=0. The
pressure impulse is horizontal and satisfies the simpler bound
`(E|P_t|^4)^(1/4)<=(3+3^(1/4))A`, independent of w_0 and nu.
This is a three-component flow with two-coordinate dependence; the passive
component does not feed the horizontal parent. It is distinct from the
fully three-dimensional family (645).

To test that the payment allows real production, reuse the explicit
profile in (596). Put p_*=(cos(2x)+cos(2y))/4, F=v.grad p_*, and
`w_0=16A sin x(1-F)`. Exact spatial integration gives

```text
integral sin^2(x)F^2=3/256,
-4 integral |u_0|^2 u_0.grad p_0=24A^5,
integral |grad u_0|^2=164A^2.
```

Choose the fixed original-data parameters eta=A^2, kappa=A^(-4).
The COMPLETE initial entropy derivative (629) is

```text
H_kappa'(0)=24A-164nu.
At A=7nu it equals 4nu>0.                               (647)
```

Continuity of the globally smooth actual solution gives an interval of
strict increase. Nevertheless (646) pays its entire history, without
resetting the initial stock. The physical flow has nonzero pressure and
transport, and every generated passive mode is retained. This tests an
actual viscous evolution; it is not a Gaussian closure or a finite-mode
approximation. The vertical moments at unit A are respectively 131 and
110751/4, so every constant in this fixture's allowance is explicit.

### The arbitrary-parent obligation remains physical

The controller in (640) already allows arbitrary adapted changes in noise
orientation. The unproved step for general NS is furnishing a finite
original-data allowance for the evolving parent history. In (642), both
the remaining trace variation and the drift in (643) are explicit. Under
mutually regenerating parents, neither the exponential law nor its drift
identity can simply be restarted. Assuming a future bound on
`nu integral ||grad u||_infinity^2` would already assume strong regularity
control; it is not a derivation of the missing estimate.

The direct arbitrary-flow target (636) avoids imposing that particular
pointwise cap: bound the fourth moment of the actual signed pressure
impulse, retaining its correlations and cancellations. The existing
second-moment payment is genuinely weaker. Whether concentrated histories
can repeatedly produce large fourth-moment contributions without a finite
full-data allowance remains open. A proposed correction must be tested on
these actual histories, including the entropy increase (647), and retain
whatever original resource it spends.

Run `python3 -O labs/pressure_parent_bellman.py`. The exact Bellman drift,
Gaussian initial stocks, symbolic ABC family, Fourier pressure identities,
viscous clock and both entropy-derivative fixtures pass. The stochastic
identification, conditional composition, all-time physical payment and
continuation consumer are analytic, not Lean-certified. No Lean declarations
or axioms change. These new statements use normalized periodic measure;
no whole-space uniform-probability claim is made.

## Pressure-impulse returns and the failure of local funding

`pressure_impulse_return.py` tests two concrete questions about the
pressure-history target (636). Can a local reserve, transported from the
original velocity, pay for pressure arriving at that location? Does the
complete fourth moment of the pressure impulse have a favorable first
feedback correction on the cyclic examples that challenged earlier
entropy estimates? The first answer is no for the precise rule below;
the second is yes for the two stated families. Both conclusions concern
actual smooth unforced periodic NS histories on a positive local interval.

### The observation and its complete evolution

Use normalized measure on the period-2pi torus and the actual solution u.
For a uniform original label a, let
`dX_t=u(t,X_t)dt+sqrt(2nu)dW_t` and
`P_t=integral_0^t grad p(s,X_s)ds`, with the canonical mean-zero pressure.
The marginal law of X_t stays uniform. Write g=grad p and
`D=partial_t+u.grad-nu Delta`. Conditional on X_t=x, define

```text
I=E[P], Q=E[P P^T], T=E[|P|^2 P], J4=E[|P|^4].
DI=g,
DQ=I tensor g+g tensor I,
DT=(2Q+tr(Q) Id)g,
DJ4=4g.T;                  I(0)=Q(0)=T(0)=J4(0)=0.       (648)
```

These follow by multiplying the joint forward equation for (X,P) by
the indicated polynomial in P. Every preceding level retains transport
and diffusion. Only after spatial integration at the final level do
their contributions vanish. No independence or Gaussian closure is used.
The global observation is `Phi(t)=integral J4(t,x)dx=E|P_t|^4`.
Its connection to an L4 velocity bound and continuation is (636).

### A local transported reserve cannot pay incoming pressure

Consider the proposed rule

```text
Dh4=0, h4(0,x)=|u0(x)|^4,
J4(t,x) <= C(u0,nu,H) h4(t,x)                            (649)
```

for all available smooth prefixes t<=H and all x, with one finite
constant chosen from the full original datum. This is a specific local
funding hypothesis. It is stronger than the global original-data
allowance sought in (636).

One fixed smooth mean-zero divergence-free datum refutes (649). Put

```text
F(y)=(1-cos y)^3(cos y+3/4),
G(z)=sin z(1-cos z)^2, H(x)=sin x(1-cos x)^2,
U=(F(y),G(z),H(x)),
gamma=1178750/28129101>0.                               (650)
```

All three coordinates occur. For any cyclic field of this form,
`tr((grad U)^2)=0`, so its canonical initial pressure is identically
zero. If p_1 denotes the actual first time derivative of pressure,
the full NS tangent gives

```text
Delta p_1=6 F'(y)G'(z)H'(x),
grad p_1(0)=(0,-gamma,0) for (650).
```

Indeed `u_1=nu Delta U-U.grad U`, and
`tr((grad U)(grad u_1))=-3F'G'H'`; all viscosity terms cancel
in this pressure derivative. The checker solves the complete Fourier
Poisson equation and verifies the rational value above, including all
generated frequencies.

At the origin U vanishes to order at least five. Its first two time
derivatives therefore satisfy `u_1(0)=0` and
`u_2(0)=-grad p_1(0)`, for every fixed nu>0. The terms in
`nu Delta u_1-u_1.grad U-U.grad u_1` vanish there; they have not
been discarded from the equation. Consequently

```text
u(t,0)=(gamma/2)t^2 e_y+O(t^3),
|u(t,0)|^4=(gamma^4/16)t^8+O(t^9),
J4(t,0)=(gamma^4/16)t^8+O(t^9),
h4(t,0)=5244976800 nu^10 t^10+O(t^11).                  (651)
```

To derive the conditional moment coefficient, write `g(t)=t g_1+O(t^2)`
in (648). In the spatially smooth topology the leading terms are
`I=t^2 g_1/2`, `Q=t^4 g_1 tensor g_1/4`,
`T=t^6 |g_1|^2 g_1/8` and `J4=t^8 |g_1|^4/16`.
Transport and diffusion contribute at subsequent orders.

The passive reserve calculation uses its ACTUAL advecting velocity.
For a smooth time-dependent drift, the nth initial time derivative of
the passive solution is a differential operator on h4(0) of order at
most 2n. Its principal part is `nu^n Delta^n`; all other terms have
order at most 2n-1. This follows inductively by differentiating
`partial_t h4=nu Delta h4-u.grad h4`, retaining every time derivative
of u. Here all spatial derivatives of h4(0) of order below twenty
vanish. Its leading homogeneous term is

```text
(x^20+2x^10 z^10+z^20)/256.
```

Thus its initial time derivatives through order nine vanish. At order
ten, only the principal Laplacian contributes, and
`Delta^10 h4(0,0)/10!=5244976800`. The checker verifies this both
from the full Fourier datum and from its leading homogeneous polynomial.
This does not replace the actual advecting flow by free heat.

For each fixed nu>0 the ratio in (649) diverges like
`gamma^4/(16*5244976800*nu^10*t^2)` as t decreases to zero.
Hence for this single U, every prescribed H>0 and every finite
C(U,nu,H), there is an actual positive local time at which (649)
fails. Replacing J4 by the actual `|u|^4` also fails. At any such
strict violation, continuity gives a spatial neighborhood of violation;
this is not an ambiguity of conditional expectation at a null point.

The remainders in (651) are controlled by local smooth existence, not
by extending a formal series past its validity. For example choose
L=1+||U||_{H^40} and a sufficiently large fixed Sobolev constant C_40.
The usual differentiated energy estimate gives an interval
`tau<=min(1,(4 C_40 L)^(-1))` with `||u||_{H^40}<=2L`.
Time differentiation of the NS equation and of the linear triangular
moment system bounds the required derivatives on a smaller closed
interval by finite functions of L and nu. Taylor's theorem then
gives the remainders above. The passive equation is smooth to the
eleventh required time derivative; its coefficients and initial datum
come from the same U. In particular the leading positive t^8 terms
and the upper t^10 bound yield the strict inequality on a sufficiently
short positive interval. No claim about numerical resolution is needed.

This obstruction is spatial redistribution. Pressure is elliptic and
can accelerate a quiet region because of interactions elsewhere. Its
global kinetic work still cancels exactly:
`integral u.grad p=-integral p div u=0`.
There is no external force and no new energy supply. A positive
globally funded stock, a nonlocal initial reserve, or an explicitly
accounted transfer between regions is not refuted by (651).

### A favorable complete return with matched viscosity

Now take the previous cyclic seeds
`U_k=(sin y,sin(kz),sin x)`, for k=1 and k=4. Write N=k^2+2.
Their initial pressure is zero and

```text
p_1=-(6k/N)cos x cos y cos(kz).
```

There is a natural fixed-original-data forecast to compare against.
In the amplitude expansion starting from epsilon U_k, the linear
parents decay by their heat factors. Their first quadratic velocity
outputs are
`-t exp(-nu(lambda_i+lambda_j)t) U_j partial_j U_i`;
the inputs occupy different coordinate directions, so the Laplace
eigenvalues add. The cubic pressure generated by these parents is
exactly `t exp(-nu N t)p_1`.

Use that generated pressure on Brownian paths with uniform initial
label, keeping the SAME viscosity:

```text
g_gen(t,x)=t exp(-nu N t) grad p_1(x),
dB_t=sqrt(2nu)dW_t,
Pbar_t=integral_0^t g_gen(s,B_s)ds,
Phibar(t)=E|Pbar_t|^4.                                 (652)
```

This is a diagnostic first-generation forecast, not a second NS
solution. It omits the subsequent nonlinear parent feedback and fluid
advection; those remain in the actual Phi. Its entire allowance is
explicit: for nu>0,
`Phibar(t)<=||grad p_1||_infinity^4/(nu N)^8` for all t.
This inequality alone says nothing about the actual Phi after the
proved comparison interval.

The complete actual moment equations (648), with canonical pressure
jets through p_3, give

```text
Phi(t)    = a_k t^8+b_k nu t^9+(c_k nu^2-d_k)t^10+O(t^11),
Phibar(t) = a_k t^8+b_k nu t^9+ c_k nu^2     t^10+O(t^11).
                                                               (653)
```

| k | a_k | b_k | c_k | d_k |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 99/512 | -297/160 | 29203/3200 | 20641/152064 |
| 4 | 199/72 | -796/5 | 3183262/675 | 907148604883/196886722032 |

Every d_k is strictly positive. These are identities over the
polynomial ring QQ(i)[nu], not coefficients interpolated from sample
viscosities. The checker retains the full convolutions, checks each
velocity jet is divergence-free, and rejects a product if a needed
nonzero derivative has not been computed. It separately reproduces
the nu=0 coefficients by integrating the full evolving material
pressure jets along particle paths. A rational-viscosity specialization
also agrees with the existing complete NS jet implementation.

Local smooth existence and the triangular moment equations justify
the actual time derivatives. Their next derivatives have bounds from
the original smooth datum and fixed viscosity, as in the local
argument above. Thus for every fixed nu>0 there is tau_k(nu)>0 with

```text
Phi(t)-Phibar(t) <= -(d_k/2)t^10 < 0,
0<t<=tau_k(nu), k in {1,4}.                            (654)
```

For example, if the two Taylor remainders together are bounded by
M t^11 on an original-data local interval, restrict to
`t<=d_k/(2(1+M))`. This keeps the whole comparison on the SAME
actual history. No inviscid limit or a posteriori choice of viscosity
is necessary.

The statement extends to arbitrary overall amplitude A>0 and common
integer spatial multiplier ell>=1. The actual NS scaling is
`u(t,x)=A v(A ell t,ell x)` with v's viscosity `nu ell/A`.
Both pressure impulses scale by A and their fourth moments by A^4.
Therefore the first difference for datum `A U_k(ell x)` is

```text
-d_k A^14 ell^10 t^10+O(t^11), k in {1,4}.              (655)
```

The local interval may shrink with the datum and viscosity. This
proves two unbounded families of local comparisons, not an
amplitude-independent time window or a statement about all frequency
ratios and all independent parent amplitudes.

The k=4 datum was adverse for the earlier quartic kinetic-entropy
return (632). Its first pressure-impulse correction in (654) is
nevertheless favorable. Changing the observed history changes which
cancellation is visible. Phi itself initially increases from zero;
(654) is depletion relative to the explicitly matched forecast,
not a monotonicity theorem.

### What the next payment must retain

The local failure (651) and the averaged depletion (654) can coexist.
Pressure exchanges acceleration between regions without external
kinetic work. A reserve sufficient for (636) must retain this
exchange or fund it globally. The passive pointwise rule (649)
cannot do that, even with a datum-dependent multiplicative constant.

The open target remains one finite B_P(u0,nu,H), controlled from the
original datum, with `E|P_t|^4<=B_P` for every same-datum smooth
prefix t<=H. The generated forecast in (652) cannot be restarted
after each return: existing parents, accumulated impulse and their
joint distribution are already nonzero. Proving a signed correction
for those subsequent returns, or finding an actual adverse return,
is a concrete next test. Neither result here constructs blowup or
rules out an initial allowance with nonlocal pressure transfer.

Run `python3 -O labs/pressure_impulse_return.py`. The exact Fourier
and viscosity-polynomial checks pass with assertions disabled.
Conditional stochastic identification, local PDE intervals, scaling
and the failed pointwise inequality are analytic arguments, not
new Lean certificates. No Lean declarations or axioms change.

## Whole-time cyclic pressure depletion and a funded continuation

`pressure_impulse_payment.py` follows the pressure history beyond its
initial return. The calculation uses the existing full viscous amplitude
recurrence and exact exponential-polynomial algebra in
`paired_stretching_history.py`. No numerical time grid, frequency cutoff,
frozen parent or restarted pressure impulse occurs.

The result is an all-time pressure-history payment for two families of
actual nonlinear flows with sufficiently small, independently varying
parent amplitudes. Small-data existence is established theory, already
represented by `FourierSmallDataOne.nonempty_globalSolution_of_small_one`.
The additional assertion here is the strict comparison to the original
generated-pressure forecast, including its joint amplitude dependence.
The analytic dependence and stochastic remainder argument below are not
new Lean certificates.

### The actual-flow statement

First set nu=1 on the normalized period-2pi torus and prescribe
`U_{a,b,c,k}=(a sin y,b sin(kz),c sin x)`, k in {1,4}. There exists a
positive radius rho_k, determined from this original family and the
estimates below, such that if `r^2=a^2+b^2+c^2<=rho_k^2`, then the
actual global smooth unforced solution satisfies

```text
Phi_{a,b,c,k}(t)=E|integral_0^t grad p(s,X_s)ds|^4
 <= (abc)^4 F_{0,k}(t) <= (abc)^4 L_k,    all t>=0,

L_1=27539587/384072192000,
L_4=97150482506203/145010906352284544000000.               (656)
```

Here F_{0,k} is exactly the unit-amplitude Brownian forecast Phibar
in (652), with nu=1. The first comparison is strict for t>0 if all
three amplitudes are nonzero. Its proof retains all subsequent parents,
transport, pressure, viscosity and stochastic correlations. It is not
an assertion that the actual solution remains in its initial Fourier
support. A numerical value of the sufficient radius is not supplied;
the proof gives a conservative radius in terms of fixed Sobolev and
analytic majorants. No large-amplitude extension is inferred.

### Why the common joint factor is exact

If one amplitude is zero, the remaining two parents form a triangular
pressure-free flow. For example, when c=0 the second component is
`b exp(-k^2 t)sin(kz)`, the first component solves the corresponding
passive advection-diffusion equation in y,z, and the third stays zero.
Its gradient is strictly triangular, its divergence is zero, and its
canonical pressure is zero. Cyclic permutations cover a=0 and b=0.
This statement is exact for those triangular flows, without smallness.

In the small analytic neighborhood, the pressure gradient is therefore
divisible by abc as a function of the initial amplitudes. The successive
conditional moment equations (648) show divisibility by abc, (abc)^2,
(abc)^3 and (abc)^4 at their respective levels. Consequently Phi/(abc)^4
has an analytic extension across the coordinate planes; it is not a
singular quotient near a missing parent.

Translating one coordinate by a half-period reverses exactly one initial
amplitude. Spatial integration and uniform stochastic sampling are
translation invariant. The quotient is thus even in each amplitude.
Its expansion is

```text
Phi_{a,b,c,k}(t)/(abc)^4
 =F_{0,k}(t)+a^2 F_{a,k}(t)+b^2 F_{b,k}(t)+c^2 F_{c,k}(t)
    + E_k(a,b,c,t),
E_k starts at total amplitude degree four.               (657)
```

At k=1, cyclic coordinate symmetry makes the three F_i equal. At k=4,
the three coefficients are recovered exactly from amplitudes (1,1,1),
(2,1,1) and (1,2,1); the sample (1,1,2) is an unused check. This finite
coefficient identification is justified by the proved polynomial basis
`(abc)^4(a^2 F_a+b^2 F_b+c^2 F_c)`. It is not extrapolation from
numerical samples or an assumption about finite-amplitude solutions.

### Complete time evolution of the amplitude coefficients

Write `u= sum_{n>=1} epsilon^n u_n` and similarly for pressure at a
fixed initial amplitude triple. Coefficients have no factorials.
The full projected NS recurrence determines u_1,...,u_5 and p_3,...,p_5.
The first three pressure-impulse moment levels are then retained through
degrees 5,8 and 11, giving the integrated fourth moment through degree14.
All pressure convolution outputs are kept. The advecting velocity is
expanded at the same time; it is never replaced by its first parent.

For each spatial Fourier mode the resulting scalar coefficients have
the form `sum c_{lambda,j} t^j exp(-lambda t)` with rational c and
nonnegative integer lambda,j. Heat convolution, including resonance,
is performed exactly. Every moment field is checked against its full
heat-source equation and zero original history. The implementation
represents an order-r moment coefficient as i^r times a real coefficient;
this retains the sign in both pressure forcing and advective transport.
Independent Gaussian-rational NS time jets check the velocity and
canonical pressure reconstruction.

The whole-time result is stronger than a sign of the tenth initial
derivative:

```text
F_{0,k}'(t)>0,
F_{i,k}'(t)<0 for i=a,b,c,              every t>0.
F_{i,k}(t)=-d_{i,k} t^10+O(t^11),
F_{0,k}(0)=F_{i,k}(0)=0.                              (658)
```

| k | d_a | d_b | d_c |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 20641/456192 | 20641/456192 | 20641/456192 |
| 4 | 408649/1364688 | 34518739/57953313 | 15515401/4179357 |

The constants in (656) are the exact integrals of F_0' over the full
half-line. They are not inferred from a late-time numerical plateau.

### A finite certificate proves each sign for every time

For an exponential polynomial f, list each decay rate lambda with
multiplicity one greater than its largest polynomial degree, in
descending order. Define a finite differential cascade

```text
f_0=f, f_{j+1}=(d/dt+lambda_j)f_j.
The final f_N vanishes identically.
f_j(t)=exp(-lambda_j t)f_j(0)
       +integral_0^t exp(-lambda_j(t-s)) f_{j+1}(s)ds.    (659)
```

If every f_j(0) is nonpositive, backwards induction proves f<=0 for
all t>=0. A strictly negative datum at any level gives f(t)<0 for
all t>0. The same argument applies to nonnegative data. It uses
positive heat kernels and exact identities, with no interval sampling.

The checker applies this certificate to each derivative in (658).
The k=1 negative cascades have 53 levels; the k=4 negative cascades
have 98,85,98 levels. The positive F_0' cascades have 19 and25 levels.
Every oriented initial value has the required sign, and the last
field is checked to vanish exactly. The first nonzero datum for
F_i' is at level9 and equals `-10! d_i`.

Let Lambda_k be any common upper bound on their decay rates: 26 for
k=1 and292 for k=4 suffice. Formula (659), retaining just the first
strict datum and using positivity of the remaining kernels, gives

```text
F_{i,k}'(t)<=-10 d_{i,k} t^9 exp(-Lambda_k t).
F_{i,k}(t)<=-delta_k min(t^10,1),
delta_k=min_i d_{i,k}/3^Lambda_k >0.                    (660)
```

For t<=1 integrate the derivative bound and use exp(-Lambda)>=3^(-Lambda).
For t>=1 use monotonicity. The deliberately coarse constant will make
the sufficient amplitude radius small, but provides a uniform margin
both near t=0 and over the infinite time tail.

### A uniform remainder makes this an actual-flow comparison

This step is necessary: signs of finitely many amplitude coefficients
alone do not imply (656). Here is a quantitative analytic construction
of the required uniform remainder, using only the original family.
It uses the classical Fujita--Kato fixed-point strategy; see
[Monniaux's account](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0511213) for the
semigroup construction of local strong solutions. The weighted
periodic estimates below supply the particular global bounds needed here.

Choose an integer m=40 and the complex mean-zero solenoidal space
`X_m` with norm `sup_{t>=0} exp(t/2)||u(t)||_{H^m}`. The periodic heat
semigroup and Sobolev product estimate bound the usual NS bilinear
Duhamel operator by `B_m||u||_{X_m}||v||_{X_m}`. One may use
`C(1+s^(-1/2))exp(-3s/4)` as its differentiated heat kernel bound;
after the time weight the remaining kernel is integrable. B_m is a
fixed operator constant, not a quantity read from the evolving solution.

For a sufficiently small complex polydisc of initial amplitudes,
Picard iteration is a contraction in X_m. Equivalently the homogeneous
coefficients are bounded by the corresponding Catalan majorant.
This gives a unique global solution, holomorphic dependence on the
three amplitudes, and uniform exponential decay of the H^m norm.
The pressure gradient is holomorphic in the associated integrable
time-weighted H^(m-1) space.

For the moment equations use `Y_m=L_infinity([0,infinity);H^m)`.
Heat convolution maps an exponentially decaying H^(m-1) source into
Y_m. The operator `M -> integral heat[-u.grad M]` has norm less
than one half after shrinking the same original polydisc if needed.
Thus its inverse is a convergent Neumann series, uniformly over the
whole half-line. Applying it successively to (648) proves holomorphy
and uniform bounds for all four moments. This also retains their
zero spatial modes; persistent accumulated memory is not discarded.
On the real amplitudes the moments coincide with the actual stochastic
ones by the joint forward equation and uniqueness. The complex
extension uses the polynomial `(P.P)^2`; it is not a stochastic
process with a complex physical velocity.

Differentiating these equations ten times on [0,1] gives a second
uniform bound from the same H^40 majorant and the smooth original
datum. There is ample spatial regularity for the derivatives lost
to the Laplacians. After the analytic division by (abc)^4 described
above, let M_0 and M_10 denote the resulting bounds for the quotient
and its tenth time derivative on a closed polydisc of radius R>0.
They are finite majorants obtained from the fixed-point, product and
differentiated-equation estimates, not unproved future-solution bounds.
The radius can be shrunk once to put that closed polydisc inside the
convergence domain.

Cauchy's coefficient estimate and evenness in each amplitude now give,
for `r^2=a^2+b^2+c^2<=R^2/2`, a degree-four remainder bounded by
`2 M_0 r^4/R^4` for all t. The same estimate with M_10 controls
its tenth time derivative on [0,1]. Its initial time derivatives
through order9 vanish: since g starts at time order1 and amplitude
degree3, the fourth moment starts at time order8 and amplitude
degree12; one additional time derivative adds at most one amplitude
degree, whose odd contribution vanishes by translation symmetry.
The remaining degree12 term is exactly F_0. Therefore

```text
|E_k(a,b,c,t)| <= C_k r^4 min(t^10,1),
C_k=2 R^(-4) max(M_0,M_10/10!).                         (661)
```

This estimate remains uniform when any amplitude tends to zero because
the quotient was analytically extended before applying Cauchy's estimate.
It does not divide an uncontrolled error by a tiny parent amplitude.

Choose, for example,

```text
rho_k=min(R/2,sqrt(delta_k/(2(1+C_k)))).
Phi/(abc)^4-F_0
 <= -(delta_k/2) r^2 min(t^10,1),   0<r<=rho_k.         (662)
```

For abc=0 use the exact pressure-free triangular evolution. Equations
(660)--(662) establish the actual-flow assertion (656), including strict
depletion for nonzero parents. The construction proves a positive radius
and gives its dependence on fixed analytic constants. It does not offer
an optimized numerical threshold or remove the smallness assumption.

### Viscosity, physical scales and one shared reserve

For any nu>0 and integer ell>=1, NS scaling transfers the result to
initial datum `(A sin(ell y),B sin(k ell z),C sin(ell x))`, provided
`A^2+B^2+C^2 <= rho_k^2 nu^2 ell^2`. Use amplitudes
`(a,b,c)=(A,B,C)/(nu ell)` at viscosity1, time `nu ell^2 t` and
velocity multiplier `nu ell`. The actual pressure impulse has the
same velocity multiplier. In particular

```text
E|P_t|^4 <= (ABC)^4/(nu^8 ell^8) L_k,     all t>=0.     (663)
```

This is a bound from the original datum, positive viscosity and fixed
frequency pattern. It is small in the relevant amplitude-to-viscosity
and spatial-scale ratio, even when a spatial rescaling makes individual
dimensional amplitudes large. It does not enter the arbitrary-data regime.

Let B_P be the right side of (663), and set R(t)=B_P-Phi(t).
Its nonnegativity is now proved by (656), rather than assumed from a
formal ledger. The exact fourth-moment balance gives every compatible
continuation of this SAME original history the signed payment

```text
4 integral_s^t integral grad p.T = Phi(t)-Phi(s)
                               = R(s)-R(t) <= R(s).    (664)
```

At a seam, retain the actual fluid state and its existing conditional
moments I,Q,T,J4. Their equations compose without replenishing B_P or
setting the impulse to zero again. These moment summaries suffice for
this polynomial observation given a compatible actual fluid evolution;
they do not replace the full NS state or identify arbitrary auxiliary
controls with physically possible fluids. The bound feeds the periodic
L4/enstrophy consumer (636). Small-data regularity itself is not a new
claim; the pressure allowance and relative depletion are the added
quantitative information.

The arbitrary-data problem remains controlling the higher corrections
without the small radius used in (661)--(662). The finite certificates
prove that the first feedback remains favorable throughout time. They
do not justify restarting the initial geometry after a return.

### The next feedback reinforces the pressure history

There is an exact obstruction to claiming that all successive nonlinear
corrections have the favorable sign. At equal parent amplitudes epsilon
and k=1, retain the pressure through amplitude degree7 and the first
three moment levels through degrees7,10,13. The complete next term is

```text
Phi_epsilon(t)=epsilon^12 F_0(t)+epsilon^14 F_14(t)
               +epsilon^16 F_16(t)+O(epsilon^18),
F_14=F_a+F_b+F_c<0,
F_16'(t)>0 and F_16(t)>0 for every t>0,
F_16(t)=(106168693607/2059433164800)t^12+O(t^13).        (665)
```

The derivative sign again has a finite certificate (659): 101 levels,
maximum rate38, all initial values nonnegative, with the first strict
one at level11. Its infinite-time value is the positive rational

```text
152490621712563288522860694365656656374065925339476309
/35951541890842638215113438256286222765113462489088000000000.
```

This is a complete coefficient of the evolving fluid and stochastic
history. It includes the new parents and existing moments; it is not
a sum of separately restarted first returns. At any fixed t_*>0,
the same holomorphic solution and moment bounds give a controlled
O(epsilon^18) remainder. Consequently, for all sufficiently small
nonzero epsilon, the ACTUAL flow satisfies

```text
Phi_epsilon(t_*) > epsilon^12 F_0(t_*)+epsilon^14 F_14(t_*),
while Phi_epsilon(t_*) <= epsilon^12 F_0(t_*).
```

Thus the two-term expression is not automatically an upper
bound, although the original allowance (656) still pays the actual
history in its proved small regime. The positive coefficient does
not show that the full pressure cost exceeds that allowance at large
amplitude: a truncated amplitude series is not such evidence. Nor
does it assert a temporal cycle in which each coefficient is a
separate flow stage. It identifies competing contributions within
the same complete history, and the higher-order payment that the
arbitrary-data argument must control.

Run `python3 -O labs/pressure_impulse_payment.py`. It checks the complete
amplitude evolution, conditional moment recurrences, independent time
jets, joint-amplitude coefficient identification, whole-time sign
cascades and exact infinite-time stocks. The fixed-point estimates,
uniform analytic remainder and actual all-time physical payment remain
analytic arguments. No Lean declarations or axioms change.
Use `python3 -O labs/pressure_impulse_payment.py --next-coefficient`
to check the complete degree-sixteen calculation and its positive
whole-time certificate separately.

## A combined pressure bound beyond the first return

`pressure_impulse_envelope.py` tests whether the favorable and adverse
returns in (665) can be paid together. It reuses the complete viscous
amplitude recurrence and conditional pressure moments. The resulting
comparison is proved analytically for all time at sufficiently small
amplitude, and on an initial nonlinear time interval without amplitude
smallness. Its extension to arbitrary amplitude over arbitrary horizons
remains open. The calculation also gives an actual-flow obstruction to
proving this comparison by domination of instantaneous rates.

### One candidate keeps both signs

For a nonzero real amplitude epsilon and initial datum
`u_0=epsilon (sin y,sin z,sin x)` at viscosity one, keep the actual
stochastic pressure impulse P and Phi=E|P|^4 of (656). Write
`a(t)=F_0(t)`, `b(t)=F_14(t)` and `c(t)=F_16(t)` for the complete
coefficients already computed in (665). In particular a>0, b<0 and
c>0 at positive times. Define the original-data envelope

```text
B_epsilon(t)=epsilon^12 a(t)^2/[a(t)-epsilon^2 b(t)],
B_epsilon(0)=0,
0<B_epsilon(t)<=epsilon^12 a(t)<=epsilon^12 L_1.          (666)
```

Its denominator is positive. This is a proposed upper bound for the
actual pressure history, not a new fluid evolution or a freedom to choose
its pressure. It matches the first two amplitude terms of Phi, while
including a positive degree-sixteen term. The first unmatched difference is

```text
Phi_epsilon-B_epsilon
 =epsilon^16 G(t)+O(epsilon^18),
G=c-b^2/a=H/a,                 H=ac-b^2.                 (667)
```

The complete degree-sixteen coefficient must be used: replacing it with
independent repetitions of the first return would discard generated
parents and existing conditional moments.

### Exact combined depletion over the whole clock

The finite exponential-polynomial certificate (659) gives

```text
H'(t)<0, H(t)<0, G(t)<0,                    every t>0.
a(t)=a_0 t^8+O(t^9), b(t)=-d_0 t^10+O(t^11),
c(t)=c_0 t^12+O(t^13),
a_0=99/512, d_0=20641/152064,
c_0=106168693607/2059433164800,
q=d_0^2/a_0-c_0=2972406502169/67961294438400>0.           (668)
```

Thus the positive correction is strictly smaller than the amount
provided by this particular combined expression. The H' certificate
has 247 levels, maximum rate 56, and first strict datum at level 19.
That datum equals `-20! a_0 q`. No time sampling is used to prove
these signs. The pressure and all generated moment fields entering
this calculation are checked against their complete coefficient equations.
A separate Euler material-path calculation, using the full evolving velocity
and pressure time jets, independently reproduces a_0,d_0,c_0. It does not
use the stochastic moment recurrence or the exponential-polynomial evolution.

The certificate supplies a quantitative margin. With
`eta=a_0 q/3^56`, the argument of (660) gives
`H<=-eta min(t^20,1)`. The forecast pressure gradient is
`t exp(-3t)grad[-2 cos x cos y cos z]`; its norm is bounded by
`2 sqrt(3)t`. Hence `a(t)<=9t^8`, and its exact infinite-time stock
also satisfies `L_1<9`. Consequently

```text
G(t)<=-delta min(t^12,1),  delta=eta/9>0.                (669)
```

### Actual all-time comparison in a small neighborhood

As in (661), the global complex small-data solution and the complete
conditional moment equations depend analytically on epsilon. The ratio
`b/a` is bounded over the whole half-line: near zero it is O(t^2),
and away from zero use a's positive monotonicity and b's finite limit.
Thus the denominator in (666) also stays nonzero in a sufficiently small
complex amplitude disc, uniformly in time.

After subtracting the exactly matched degree-twelve and degree-fourteen
terms, analytic division gives

```text
Phi_epsilon-B_epsilon=epsilon^16 G+epsilon^18 W_epsilon,
|W_epsilon(t)|<=C min(t^12,1).                           (670)
```

Here C is obtained from the same fixed-point and differentiated-equation
majorants, using twelve time derivatives on [0,1]. The H^40 estimates
leave enough spatial derivatives. The needed lower time jets vanish:
a pressure coefficient of amplitude degree n>=3 starts no earlier than
time order n-2; each impulse integration increases time order by one.
Every fourth-moment contribution of degree n therefore starts no earlier
than time order n-4. The odd total amplitude terms vanish by translation
symmetry. The rational expression has the same property, since b/a is
O(t^2). In particular the remainder in (670) has zero time derivatives
through order eleven. Cauchy estimates and Taylor's integral remainder
then give the stated uniform bound. This argument does not divide a
bare uncontrolled error by epsilon or by a small value of a(t).

Choose a positive epsilon_0 within that convergence disc and with
`C epsilon_0^2<=delta/2`. For every `0<|epsilon|<=epsilon_0`,

```text
Phi_epsilon(t)<=B_epsilon(t)
              -(delta/2)epsilon^16 min(t^12,1), t>=0.   (671)
```

This is an actual nonlinear stochastic-history comparison. The smallness
threshold is conservative and not numerically evaluated. It strengthens
the envelope for this family; it does not establish new small-data
regularity or an arbitrary-data theorem.

### A strong-amplitude initial interval

There is also a comparison without smallness of the dimensional amplitude.
For the unit cyclic datum at viscosity mu>=0, let Phi_mu denote the actual
pressure-impulse fourth moment. At mu=0 the paths are deterministic Euler
paths. Define

```text
a_mu(t)=mu^(-8)a(mu t), b_mu(t)=mu^(-10)b(mu t),
B_mu(t)=a_mu(t)^2/[a_mu(t)-b_mu(t)]       when mu>0,
a_0(t)=(99/512)t^8, b_0(t)=-(20641/152064)t^10,
B_0(t)=(99/512)^2 t^8/[(99/512)+(20641/152064)t^2].       (672)
```

The subscript-zero functions in (672) refer to zero viscosity, whereas
the constants a_0,d_0 in (668) are leading Taylor coefficients.
The apparent singularities at mu=0 are removable. These functions can
also be constructed directly from the finite coefficient heat equations,
whose solutions are smooth in mu on any bounded time interval.

Complete initial jets, including viscosity, give

```text
Phi_mu(t)-B_mu(t)=-q t^12+O(t^13).                       (673)
```

The leading coefficient is independent of mu. Terms of amplitude degree
at least eighteen cannot enter before time order fourteen. The viscosity
terms at lower amplitude degrees are already retained exactly in a_mu
and b_mu; they are not silently omitted to obtain (673).

This has a uniform actual-flow interpretation. Local existence on a
viscosity-independent interval is classical; see
[Kato's whole-space result](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0022123672900031).
For the periodic datum here, the Sobolev energy estimate gives the needed
bound directly. With Y=||u||_(H^40), the dissipative viscous term and
Sobolev embedding give `Y'<=C_40 Y^2`, uniformly for 0<=mu<=1.
Thus `T_loc=1/(2 C_40 ||U||_(H^40))` supplies `Y<=2||U||_(H^40)`
on one common interval. The fixed constants and original norm determine
this bound before the future flow is known.

The moment equations have uniform H^39 transport-diffusion estimates
with the actual H^40 coefficients and H^39 pressure gradients. Their
triangular source terms and Gronwall bounds use that same original-data
majorant. Their differentiated equations, through thirteen time derivatives,
have uniform bounds on a smaller common interval. At mu=0 they are the
deterministic moment equations.
After factoring t^8 from the denominator in (672), its remaining factor
is uniformly positive near zero. Taylor remainders for the difference
in (673) are therefore bounded by one fixed C_* t^13 with C_*>0. Taking
`tau_0<=q/(2C_*)` within the common interval proves
`Phi_mu-B_mu<=-(q/2)t^12` for 0<t<=tau_0, uniformly for 0<=mu<=1.
These are local smooth-solution estimates, not an assumption about an
unknown long-time solution.

For physical data `A(sin(ell y),sin(ell z),sin(ell x))`, with A>0,
integer ell>=1 and viscosity nu>0, put `mu=nu ell/A` and `tau=A ell t`.
The pressure impulse scales by A. Thus, whenever A>=nu ell, the actual
flow satisfies

```text
Phi_physical(t)<=A^4 B_mu(A ell t),
0<=t<=tau_0/(A ell),
Phi_physical(t)-A^4 B_mu(A ell t)
 <=-(q/2)A^16 ell^12 t^12.                              (674)
```

The dimensionless nonlinear interval tau_0 is independent of A, nu and
ell in this range. It need not contain a complete pattern cycle, and
its numerical length has not been optimized. In particular it is not
an arbitrary-horizon bound. The entire initial interval has the finite
allowance `9A^4 tau_0^8`, since a_mu(t)<=9t^8 uniformly in mu>=0.
Its shrinking physical duration is essential and cannot be discarded
when attempting to compose subsequent intervals.

### The instantaneous-rate proof fails on actual flows

Even the all-time small-amplitude comparison (671) cannot be justified
by requiring `Phi_epsilon'<=B_epsilon'` at every time. Differentiating
the complete next difference gives

```text
G'=K/a^2,
K=a^2 c'-2ab b'+b^2 a',
3*10^(-41)<K(12)<4*10^(-41).                            (675)
```

The last enclosure is rational. The checker bounds exp(12) by a positive
Taylor sum and a geometric tail, reciprocates the bounds, then evaluates
each signed term of the exponential polynomial K with exact rational
endpoints. It does not infer a sign from floating-point cancellation.

Analytic dependence and its differentiated remainder now imply that,
for all sufficiently small nonzero epsilon, the actual unforced
positive-viscosity history has

```text
Phi_epsilon(12)<B_epsilon(12),
Phi_epsilon'(12)>B_epsilon'(12).                         (676)
```

The effect is very late and small; it is a counterexample to the stated
instantaneous-rate verification, not evidence of singularity. In terms
of the nonnegative slack `S(t)=B_epsilon(t)-Phi_epsilon(t)`, earlier
returns have accumulated savings and S is decreasing at this time.
The compatible signed balance is

```text
integral_s^t [4 integral grad p.T - B_epsilon']
 =S(s)-S(t)<=S(s).                                      (677)
```

Retain the original clock, actual fluid and pressure moments at the
seam. Setting S(s)=0 or restarting the pressure impulse would erase the
resource that pays this interval. This is a concrete reason to allow
withdrawals from a history-dependent reserve. It refutes the stronger
instantaneous comparison, not the proposed value bound (666).

### Numerical adversarial checks and the remaining boundary

The optional prefix mode evolves all three velocities, three first
moments, six second moments, three third moments and the spatially
integrated fourth moment. It reuses the existing dealiased Fourier
operations and Lawson RK4 step. Canonical pressure and generated modes
within the retained grid evolve together. The output reports the energy
balance, high-mode fractions and the minimum eigenvalue of `Q-I I^T`.
These are numerical diagnostics, not certified continuum error bounds.

The strong-advection tests use the unit-amplitude nonlinear clock and
viscosities 0.05,0.25,1, with comparisons to zero viscosity as a diagnostic.
A low-resolution zero-viscosity run loses moment positivity; it cannot
certify a physical stochastic distribution or be counted as a rigorous
inequality test. Resolution and step refinement are required even when
the scalar comparison has a large favorable margin.

At nonlinear time two, the following approximations stay below the envelope:

| viscosity | grid | time step | Phi | Phi/B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.05 | 48^3 | 0.005 | 2.203688882 | 0.4138902900 |
| 0.25 | 32^3 | 0.0025 | 0.1292751102 | 0.6338462627 |
| 1 | 32^3 | 0.005 | 0.000054028835 | 0.9787254505 |

For viscosity 0.05 the final Phi changes relatively by 6.2e-8 from 32^3
to 48^3. The latter run has positive conditional covariance at every sampled
