## A rational pressure allowance is not preserved by pooling rotating cores

`pressure_envelope_mixture.py` tests a possible extension of the combined
pressure envelope (666): use the first two nonzero amplitude coefficients
of the actual pressure-impulse fourth moment to form a rational upper bound.
Two smooth rotating cores show that this rule is not valid for arbitrary
initial data. Each isolated core passes its initial comparison, while the
combined initial datum fails on an actual unforced positive-viscosity
interval. The failure occurs in planar flows, whose vortex stretching is
identically zero. It refutes this particular pressure allowance, not global
regularity, the sufficient pressure-moment criterion, or every allowance
which depends on the full initial datum.

The preceding cyclic tests remain favorable. Complete material pressure
jets for frequencies `(1,k,1)`, k=1,2,4,6, for each placement of amplitudes
4:1:1 at k=4,8, and for an added third harmonic of amplitude +/-1/2 or +/-1
all retain a negative first unmatched envelope coefficient. These fourteen
checks do not establish the cyclic envelope at later times. The two-core
construction below tests a different, precise generalization.

### The proposed rule and the actual observation

On the normalized period-2pi torus, let u be the actual unforced solution
from epsilon U at viscosity nu>0. The forward stochastic flow has drift u
and diffusivity nu, and starts from a uniform label. Keep the original
pressure impulse and its fourth moment:

```text
P_t=integral_0^t grad p(s,X_s)ds,  Phi_epsilon(t)=E|P_t|^4.
Phi_epsilon=epsilon^8 F_8+epsilon^10 F_10
                         +epsilon^12 F_12+...,
a=F_8, b=F_10,
B_epsilon=epsilon^8 a^2/(a-epsilon^2 b).                (746)
```

The even expansion will follow from an exact reflection of these data.
Here pressure starts at amplitude degree two, unlike the cyclic seed of
(666), where it starts at degree three. Thus F_8 and F_10 are the relevant
complete coefficients. They are obtained from the same heat/Duhamel and
conditional-moment recurrences, retaining every generated mode and the
actual pressure. They are not fitted constants or coefficients from a
frozen-pressure dynamics. Parameter expansions of the periodic NS equation
use the established framework of
[Morosi and Pizzocchero](https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.2972); the pressure-moment
extension and the counterexample here are derived below. No claim about
convergence on arbitrary horizons is needed.

### Smooth physical data with two different rotation scales

Choose a smooth function phi on [0,infinity), between zero and one, equal
to one on [0,15/16], and identically zero on [1,infinity). It can be chosen
flat at both transition endpoints using the usual exp(-1/s) smooth cutoff.
For a disc of radius R_i centered at (c_i,0), put

```text
r_i^2=(x-c_i)^2+y^2,
omega_i(r)=Omega_i phi(r/R_i),
U_i=omega_i(r_i)(-y,x-c_i,0),
p_i(r)=-integral_r^(R_i) s omega_i(s)^2 ds  for r<R_i,
p_i=0 outside the disc.                                (747)
```

Both fields extend smoothly. U_i is divergence free and mean zero;
`(U_i.grad)U_i=-grad p_i`. Choose c_1=-1, c_2=1 and R=1/4, with the
radii below. Their supports are disjoint and lie inside one periodic
coordinate chart. The sum U=U_1+U_2 is an exact steady Euler datum, with
pressure p_1+p_2 up to its mean. Cross advection vanishes by disjoint
support. The datum is independent of z and has zero vertical velocity.

This is not a superposition of separately evolved viscous solutions.
At nu>0 there is one actual NS solution from epsilon(U_1+U_2); viscosity
and the resulting common pressure are retained in the argument below.
Planarity is preserved. The standard two-dimensional global theory applies;
the existing `FourierPlanarRegularity` module proves planarity preservation
and `stretchingDensity_planar` in its periodic Fourier setting. Directly,
`omega.grad u=0` on this whole evolution. In particular the signed
vortex-stretching budget itself has zero cost here. The new pressure-moment
counterexample is not already a consequence certified by that module.

For Euler a particle in one disc keeps its radius and rotates at angular
speed omega_i(r). Its exact pressure impulse is the difference between its
original and current velocity, so

```text
|P_t|^4=16 r^4 omega(r)^4 sin^4(omega(r)t/2)
 =r^4[omega^8 t^4-omega^10 t^6/6
                         +omega^12 t^8/80]+O(t^10).    (748)
```

Let `M_j=integral_0^1 rho^5 phi(rho)^j drho` for j=8,10,12.
Normalized integration over each disc and over z gives the three Euler
coefficients

```text
A=(M_8/(2pi)) sum_i R_i^6 Omega_i^8,
B=-(M_10/(12pi)) sum_i R_i^6 Omega_i^10,
D=(M_12/(160pi)) sum_i R_i^6 Omega_i^12.                 (749)
```

Cauchy--Schwarz and the cutoff plateau give

```text
M_10^2<=M_8 M_12,
(15/16)^6/6<=M_j<=1/6,
1<=M_8 M_12/M_10^2<20/9,                               (750)
```

where the strict upper bound follows from `(16/15)^12<20/9`.
For each isolated core, its first unmatched rational-envelope coefficient
is therefore strictly negative:

```text
Delta_i=R_i^6 Omega_i^12/(2pi)
                  [M_12/80-M_10^2/(36M_8)]<0.           (751)
```

### The combined profile reverses that sign

For any integer L>=3, take speeds Omega_1=1, Omega_2=L and radii

```text
x=(2L^2-3)/(L^2-1), y=1/[(L^2-1)L^8],
R_1=R x^(1/6), R_2=R y^(1/6), C=R^6/(2pi).
x+y L^8=2, x+y L^10=3, x+y L^12=L^2+3.
A=2C M_8, B=-C M_10/2, D=C M_12(L^2+3)/80.             (752)
```

The first two Euler coefficients A,B are exactly fixed across this
family. The third increases without bound. These are leading time
coefficients; the full viscous functions F_8(t),F_10(t) are not asserted
to be identical across L. The actual next difference from (746) is

```text
Delta=D-B^2/A
 =C[(L^2+3)M_12/80-M_10^2/(8M_8)]
 >=C(M_10^2/M_8)(L^2-7)/80>0.                           (753)
```

The individual signs (751) thus do not survive the pooled rule.
The initial speeds are nevertheless uniformly bounded: R_1<2R and
L R_2<R imply `||U||infinity<=2R`, hence a uniform kinetic-energy bound
on the normalized torus. Derivatives of the small core grow with L.
An unbounded Taylor coefficient does not imply an unbounded observation
at a fixed positive time; the controlled initial interval may shrink.

### Why this is a positive-viscosity counterexample

Fix L, epsilon!=0 and any nu>0. Reflection in y=0, with the corresponding
reflection of vector components, sends U to -U and preserves the scalar
pressure-history observation. Uniqueness and invariance of Brownian motion
under this isometry give `Phi_epsilon=Phi_(-epsilon)`. The odd amplitude
coefficients vanish, including their complete viscous corrections.

The finite heat/Duhamel coefficient equations give velocity degree n
starting at time order n-1 and pressure degree n starting at n-2.
The raw pressure moments satisfy the identified triangular transport-
diffusion equations. Their fourth amplitude coefficient F_n starts no
earlier than time order n-4. At that first time order all available
operations raise amplitude degree; diffusion cannot contribute there.
Consequently (749) gives, at every fixed viscosity,

```text
F_8(t)=A t^4+O(t^5), F_10(t)=B t^6+O(t^7),
F_12(t)=D t^8+O(t^9),
Phi_epsilon(t)-B_epsilon(t)
                  =epsilon^12 Delta t^8+O(t^9).        (754)
```

One can obtain (754) from finite time jets without assuming an infinite
amplitude series converges at the prescribed epsilon. The j-th velocity
time jet has amplitude degree at most j+1, the pressure jet at most j+2,
and the fourth-moment jet at most j+4. Through time order eight, the
complete even coefficients below degree twelve are exactly F_8 and F_10;
the degree-twelve leading coefficient is the Euler one. Expanding the
rational expression in `epsilon^2 F_10/F_8=O(t^2)` produces B^2/A.
All higher terms start later. The lower-degree viscous terms are retained
in the entire functions F_8,F_10, not omitted from the comparison.

For completeness the remainder is controlled on an actual smooth interval.
Local Sobolev existence from the fixed smooth datum supplies a common
short interval and high spatial bounds for u, pressure and the finite
moment hierarchy. Differentiating these equations nine times, starting
with sufficiently high initial Sobolev regularity, supplies a finite
Taylor remainder constant. The coefficient heat equations supply the
same regularity for F_8,F_10. Factoring t^4 out of the denominator leaves
a smooth function with positive initial value A. Thus there are constants
T>0 and M<infinity, obtained from these initial-data local estimates, with
absolute remainder at most M t^9 on [0,T]. Reduce T to ensure the positive
denominator. With
`tau=min(T,epsilon^12 Delta/[2(1+M)])`, (753)--(754) imply

```text
Phi_epsilon(t)-B_epsilon(t)
       >=(epsilon^12 Delta/2)t^8>0,       0<t<=tau.      (755)
```

The same argument with (751) proves the favorable initial comparison for
each isolated core. No inviscid limit is substituted for a viscous
trajectory, and no unknown long-time bound is assumed. The size of tau
has not been numerically optimized. The PDE regularity, coefficient grading
and remainder argument are analytic, not newly Lean-certified.

As an independent viscosity check, the script also computes the exact
solid-rotation SDE. Its pressure impulse has isotropic noise variance
`v=4nu Omega(Omega t-sin(Omega t))`. With deterministic mean square
`m2=2r^2 Omega^2(1-cos(Omega t))`, its fourth moment is
`m2^2+8v m2+8v^2`. Nonzero viscous corrections are present, while the
highest-amplitude leading coefficients in (754) remain (748). This is
an algebraic local fixture, not a claim that unbounded solid rotation
is admissible periodic initial data.

### The exact lost cost and a compatible repair obligation

For positive a_i and nonnegative d_i, pooling before division loses

```text
sum_(i=1,2) a_i^2/(a_i+d_i)
 -(a_1+a_2)^2/(a_1+a_2+d_1+d_2)
 =(a_1 d_2-a_2 d_1)^2/
       [(a_1+d_1)(a_2+d_2)(a_1+a_2+d_1+d_2)]>=0.       (756)
```

The leading loss is a weighted variance of the component ratios. Two
pooled numbers do not retain it. Keeping the component ratios or adding
the exact missing term preserves the sum of already proved component
allowances. It does not by itself prove those allowances under interacting
NS dynamics.

There is a physically identified way to retain component histories without
superposing independent fluids. Label particles once from their original
positions, with a finite smooth partition of nonnegative probabilities.
Use the SAME actual velocity, pressure and Brownian flow for every label.
Let rho_i be its transported density and I_i,Q_i,T_i,K_i its unnormalized
first, second, contracted third and fourth pressure-impulse moments. With
`D_u=partial_t+u.grad-nu Delta` and g=grad p, they satisfy

```text
D_u rho_i=0,                        sum_i rho_i=1,
D_u I_i=rho_i g,
D_u Q_i=I_i tensor g+g tensor I_i,
D_u T_i=2 Q_i g+(tr Q_i)g,
D_u K_i=4g.T_i,                     Phi=sum_i integral K_i. (757)
```

Each impulse starts at zero only at the original initial time. These
identities follow by integrating the joint spatial/impulse Fokker--Planck
equation against the indicated polynomials. Keeping unnormalized moments
avoids discarding derivatives of a normalization by rho_i. Sums preserve
the complete original moment equations; pressure still couples all labels.
At every time seam carry rho_i and every existing moment forward. Dividing
into new independent fluids or resetting a label's impulse would invalidate
(757).

For this two-core witness, retaining labels also repairs the initial
actual-flow comparison. Choose smooth radial label functions chi_1,chi_2 equal to one
on the respective closed velocity supports, with disjoint slightly larger
supports, and chi_0=1-chi_1-chi_2. Let a_i,b_i be the complete amplitude
coefficients of degree eight and ten of `Phi_i=integral K_i`, using the
same evolving u,p and transported label density in (757). Define

```text
B_label=epsilon^8 a_0+epsilon^10 b_0
          +epsilon^8 sum_(i=1,2) a_i^2/(a_i-epsilon^2 b_i).
Phi_epsilon-B_label
 =epsilon^12 C(L^2+3)[M_12/80-M_10^2/(36M_8)]t^8
                                                   +O(t^9)<0. (758)
```

The subscript zero here denotes the exterior label. Its first two complete
coefficients are retained as a signed term. Its degree-twelve leading
Euler coefficient is zero, because those original particles have zero
velocity and pressure gradient and stay outside the cores. The two core
labels have exactly the leading coefficients in (749). All lower even
amplitudes match because the labelled moments sum to the full moment;
(751) then gives the negative coefficient in (758). The same finite-jet
and local remainder argument used for (755) makes (758) an actual
positive-viscosity initial-interval inequality. In particular B_label is
nonnegative there because it bounds Phi_epsilon. These labelled coefficient
functions come from the full coupled fluid, not from independently evolved
single-core solutions. No later-time comparison is asserted.

The next physical obligation is to pay the evolution of these retained
conditional costs, including cross-component pressure and renewed parents.
Equation (756) repairs a specific loss of information, and (758) verifies
its initial physical use. They do not supply the arbitrary-data continuation
allowance. They also do not refute the original equal-scale cyclic
envelope (666).

Run `python3 -O labs/pressure_envelope_mixture.py` for the exact radial,
viscous-fixture, mixture and moment-source identities, or add
`--cyclic-probes` to reproduce the fourteen complete initial jet tests.
Python compilation and the exact checks are distinct from the analytic
actual-solution argument. No Lean declarations or axioms change.

## A retained label can pass its initial payment and fail later

`labelled_pressure_return.py` tests the next obligation after (758).
Retaining an original label repairs the pooling error there, but does
not make a component's two-coefficient allowance valid on every later
prefix. The example below starts with a favorable comparison and then
crosses the allowance at a strictly positive time. It persists on actual
unforced positive-viscosity three-dimensional flows with reciprocal
nonlinear feedback. No history is restarted at the crossing.

The failed assertion is the componentwise extension of (758). This is
not a failure of the sum after all other labels' savings are included,
nor of an arbitrary finite allowance depending on the full datum. The
reference flow is explicitly globally regular. The result identifies
a later-history defect in this particular proposed payment.

### The precise component candidate and its full derivative

Work on the normalized period-2pi torus. Choose one smooth original
particle label `0<=chi<=1`, of mass m>0. Its complement is another
label, so the full spatial marginal remains uniform. Use the actual
velocity, canonical pressure and diffusivity nu for both labels. For
initial datum epsilon U, set

```text
Phi_chi(epsilon,t)=(1/m) E[chi(a)|P_t|^4],
P_t=integral_0^t grad p(s,X_s) ds,
F_n(t)=(1/n!) partial_epsilon^n Phi_chi(0,t),
a=F_8, b=F_10, B(epsilon,t)=epsilon^8 a^2/(a-epsilon^2 b).
                                                               (759)
```

The division is by the constant ORIGINAL label mass, not by its evolving
spatial density. Multiplying all expressions by m gives the unnormalized
convention of (757). The label, density and every accumulated moment
persist throughout the evolution. The example has an exact symmetry
removing odd amplitude coefficients; pressure starts at degree two.
Both a and b are the complete viscous coefficient functions, including
pressure renewal, transport and the evolving label. They are not just
their first time monomials.

For epsilon=1 the exact later-time comparison defect is

```text
(Phi_chi-B)' = (4/m) integral grad p . T_chi
              -[(a^2-2ab)a'+a^2 b']/(a-b)^2.             (760)
```

Here T_chi is the unnormalized contracted third moment in (757).
Integrating transport and diffusion in the fourth-moment equation gives
the first term; diffusion still acts in the complete equations for
rho,I,Q,T and the coefficient functions. Formula (760) omits none of
those effects. At a seam s, the value gap at t is its existing value
at s plus the integral of (760). An initially negative gap cannot
be reset to zero or used repeatedly as a fresh reserve.

### An explicit reference with a later value crossing

Take the classical cellular velocity and its canonical pressure

```text
U=(sin y,sin x,0), p_0=cos x cos y,
U.grad U=-grad p_0, Delta U=-U.
u_nu(t)=exp(-nu t)U, p_nu(t)=exp(-2nu t)p_0.              (761)
```

Thus (761) is an exact unforced viscous solution, not a forced
stationary flow. Begin the calculation at nu=0, and below transfer
the strict inequalities to the complete nu>0 histories.

Let theta satisfy `cos theta=c=5/9`, with `0<theta<pi/2`.
Start a reference particle at `(theta,theta,0)` on the separatrix
x=y. Its equation is x'=sin x, so

```text
sin x(t)/sin theta = h_+(t)=1/(cosh t-c sinh t).
```

The translated point `(theta,theta,0)+(pi,pi,pi)` follows the reversed
cellular velocity. Its speed ratio is
`h_-(t)=1/(cosh t+c sinh t)`. Along a steady Euler trajectory,
`P_t=U(a)-U(X_t)` exactly. Averaging these two original particles gives

```text
phi(t)=4 sin(theta)^4 f(t),
f(t)=[(1-h_+(t))^4+(1-h_-(t))^4]/2
    =A t^4+B t^6+D t^8+O(t^10),
A=c^4,
B=c^2(60c^4-56c^2+9)/6,
D=(2800c^8-4800c^6+2416c^4-340c^2+5)/80.
For c=5/9:
A=625/6561, B=-140425/1062882,
D=124769021/688747536,
D-B^2/A=-1433735/688747536<0.                           (762)
```

The common factor `4 sin(theta)^4` multiplies both the actual moment
and its rational allowance. The initial comparison is strictly
favorable. For this Euler reference, amplitude scaling gives
`Phi(epsilon,t)=epsilon^4 phi(epsilon t)`, so the COMPLETE first two
amplitude coefficients are precisely the multiples of A t^4 and B t^6.

Now take T=log4. This time has exact hyperbolic values
`cosh T=17/8`, `sinh T=15/8`, hence

```text
h_+(T)=12/13, h_-(T)=6/19,
f(T)=[(1/13)^4+(13/19)^4]/2=407930521/3722098081.
```

The normalized candidate `A t^4/(1-(B/A)t^2)` is increasing for t>0.
The first six positive terms of exp(7/5) already sum to more than four,
so T<7/5. Therefore

```text
A T^4/(1-(B/A)T^2) < 3001250/30495123,
f(T)-A T^4/(1-(B/A)T^2)
 >1268944547747833/113505838798158963 >1/100.              (763)
```

These are exact rational bounds; no sampled time or floating-point
sign decides the crossing. The same component that saves initially
has spent more than its proposed allowance by T. In physical terms,
particles at different phases move through the same cellular geometry;
the later change of speed is not paid by this first-return forecast.

### Smooth labels and positive viscosity, with an actual solution

The paired atoms above are only a reference calculation. Replace them
by two identical nonnegative smooth bumps, supported in small disjoint
balls about the stated points, and let chi be their sum. Choose their
height at most one, and use chi_0=1-chi as the exterior label. Then
`chi(x+(pi,pi,pi))=chi(x)`. Normalized integration against chi converges
to the paired reference as the balls shrink.

All material coefficients in (762), and the reference observation at T,
are smooth functions of the original particle position. Consequently
one can FIX a positive bump radius, using only the explicit reference,
for which A_chi>0, B_chi<0,
`D_chi-B_chi^2/A_chi<0`, and the later strict gap in (763) remains
positive. No label is chosen from a subsequent unknown NS solution.
The constant initial normalization commutes with these limits.

Next use (761) at nu>0. The actual forward stochastic paths have drift
`exp(-nu t)U` and noise `sqrt(2nu)dW`; their pressure is
`exp(-2nu t)p_0`. Coupling them to the reference Euler paths from the
SAME initial positions gives convergence on [0,T]. For example the
bounded Lipschitz constants of U and grad p_0, Brownian maximal-moment
bounds and Gronwall give an L4 path/impulse error at most
`C_T(sqrt(nu)+nu)`. The fourth moments converge as well, since the
pressure gradients on this fixed interval are uniformly bounded.

The complete coefficient functions also converge, not only the actual
observation. Differentiate the finite heat/Duhamel velocity equations
and the labelled hierarchy (757) through amplitude degree ten. This
gives finitely many triangular, smooth transport/diffusion source
equations, with the fixed initial U and chi. Their difference from the
nu=0 equations is bounded by `C nu` on [0,T] in sufficiently high
spatial norms. One proves this by induction on amplitude degree,
retaining each pressure projection and every generated product.
The needed extra derivatives of U and chi are finite from the outset.

Their time grading gives continuous extensions of a/t^4 and b/t^6 at
zero. The same integral equations show convergence of these factored
coefficients uniformly on [0,T]. In particular, for sufficiently small
positive nu, a>0 and b<0 on the entire interval 0<t<=T. Their quotient
in (759) converges at T to the reference quotient. Thus the later
crossing survives with its full viscous coefficients and Brownian
history. Choosing nu after fixing the smooth label is essential; no
uniform assertion as the bump radius tends to zero is used.

The initial favorable sign survives too. Finite time jets of a smooth
NS solution give velocity amplitude degree at most j+1 at time order j,
and pressure degree at most j+2. The labelled fourth moment of degree n
starts no earlier than time order n-4. The leading terms at that time
contain no diffusion. Translation by (pi,pi,pi) reverses the initial
velocity and preserves chi, so uniqueness makes the observation even
in epsilon, including at nu>0. Consequently, with COMPLETE a,b,

```text
Phi_chi(1,t)-B(1,t)
 =[D_chi-B_chi^2/A_chi]t^8+O(t^9)<0
                   on a sufficiently short positive interval, (764)
Phi_chi(1,T)-B(1,T)>0.
```

This is a value crossing on one physical history. The remainder in
(764) is bounded by local high-Sobolev estimates for the actual
solution and the finite labelled moment equations. It is not an
assumption that an infinite amplitude expansion converges at epsilon=1.
Here the reference solution itself is explicit for every nu, so no
long-time regularity premise enters this step.

### Persistence with genuine reciprocal three-dimensional parents

The crossing is not confined to a flow with identically zero vortex
stretching. Perturb the original velocity to

```text
U_delta=(sin y+delta sin z, sin x, delta sin x),
p_delta=cos x cos y+delta^2 cos x cos z,
N_delta=-U_delta.grad U_delta-grad p_delta
       =(0,-delta sin z cos x,-delta sin y cos x).        (765)
```

This is smooth, mean-zero and divergence-free. For delta!=0 its
nonzero spatial frequencies span all three directions. It preserves
the translation symmetry used for the SAME smooth paired label.
Neither the velocity nor the pressure is held to the reference
evolution after the initial time. Complete unforced jets give

```text
partial_t p(0)=-2nu p_delta
 +(2/3)sin x[delta^2 sin y cos z+delta sin z cos y],
partial_t^2 u_1(0)-nu^2 (U_delta)_1
 =(delta/3)cos x[delta sin y cos z+sin z cos y].          (766)
```

The first generated parent outputs in (765) therefore return into
the first component at the next step. The canonical pressure
derivative in (766) is retained in that calculation. In addition,
writing `g(t)=integral omega.grad u.omega`, exact integration gives

```text
g(0)=0,                  g'(0)=delta^2/2>0.              (767)
```

The equality holds at every viscosity: the initial velocity has one
Laplacian eigenvalue, and the viscous contribution is -3nu g(0)=0.
Thus these actual smooth histories have positive integrated vortex
stretching for a short positive interval. This says nothing by itself
about exceeding the viscous or full-datum renewal allowance.

To justify the finite interval, fix the positive viscosity chosen
above and compare the perturbed NS solution to the explicit smooth
reference (761). For any sufficiently high Sobolev order s, the
standard difference energy estimate, retaining the favorable viscous
term, bounds their difference y on a bootstrap region y<=1 by
`y'<=C_s(U,nu,T)y`. Hence choosing the original
`|delta| ||(sin z,0,sin x)||_{H^s} exp(C_s T)` sufficiently small
gives existence and closeness throughout [0,T]. Local existence and
this bound extend the prefix; existence up to T is not assumed.
The pressure gradient and the finite moment/coefficient equations
depend continuously on this prefix in their required norms.

The strictly negative initial coefficient, strictly positive later
gap, and the signs a>0,b<0 therefore persist for all sufficiently
small nonzero delta. Local derivative bounds supply the remainder in
(764) for this perturbed flow as well. These are ONE full NS solution
and its original histories, not independently evolved components
superposed at a seam. The perturbation size has not been optimized.

The construction applies at any prescribed viscosity nu_target>0
after increasing initial amplitude. If the above witness has viscosity
mu, choose A=nu_target/mu and use `u(t,x)=A v(A t,x)` with initial
`A U_delta`. Its pressure impulse and fourth moment scale by A and
A^4, respectively. Its complete amplitude coefficients a,b also
scale by A^4 after evaluating at A t, so both comparison signs are
preserved and the crossing time is T/A. This is not a uniform time
or amplitude claim over all data.

### The surviving payment and the remaining physical obligation

For the exact planar reference (761), `||grad p_0||infinity<=1`.
Every stochastic path therefore satisfies the entirely explicit bound

```text
|P_t| <= (1-exp(-2nu t))/(2nu),
Phi_chi(t) <= (2nu)^(-4)                  for all t>=0.  (768)
```

This finite initial-data payment coexists with the rational-envelope
failure. For initial A U the corresponding bound is `(A^2/(2nu))^4`.
It uses autonomous decay of this exact reference; it is not asserted
for the perturbed parents or arbitrary flows. The perturbed crossing
has only the fixed-interval statement proved above.

The example refutes propagation of the particular component payment
from its favorable initial return. It does not refute the original
two-core local repair (758), the equal-scale cyclic envelope (666),
the sum of allowances after exterior savings are retained, or the
existence of a larger full-datum budget. Its practical constraint on
a later Bellman control is precise: original labels and the first
two complete amplitude coefficients do not certify that a component
can pay every subsequent geometry change with this formula. The
unpaid term is the integral of the physical defect (760), with the
actual third moment and inherited impulse. A useful repair must pay
that term or transfer a certified existing reserve to it.

Run `python3 -O labs/labelled_pressure_return.py` for the exact
reference, rational margins, complete three-dimensional pressure and
velocity jets, positive stretching derivative and allowance derivative.
The smooth-label limit, positive-viscosity persistence, fixed-interval

## Balanced reciprocal parents defeat the joint rational allowance

`joint_pressure_return.py` tests whether summing component savings repairs
the failure in (764). The answer is negative for this particular rational
payment. An interval of genuinely three-dimensional initial data has a
favorable first complete return and an adverse next return in the TOTAL
pressure fourth moment. An explicit nonconstant partition into original
labels has equal costs by physical symmetry, so its joint sum has exactly
the same deficit. There is no pooling loss in this example.

This is an obstruction to the specified two-coefficient allowance, not
to arbitrary finite full-datum allowances. It does not construct a
singularity. Unlike (764), the rational comparison here already fails
on a sufficiently short initial interval. The favorable first return
means depletion relative to the coarser heat forecast, not an initially
valid rational comparison that is later reversed.

### An interacting physical family

On the normalized period-2pi torus use the complete unforced NS evolution
from epsilon U_delta, with epsilon>0, nu>0 and

```text
U_delta=(sin y+delta sin z, sin x, delta sin x),
3/4<=delta<=4/3.
p_delta=cos x cos y+delta^2 cos x cos z,
N_delta=(0,-delta sin z cos x,-delta sin y cos x).         (769)
```

Here p_delta is the initial canonical pressure and N_delta the initial
Euler part of the velocity derivative, at epsilon=1. The nonzero
frequencies span all three spatial directions. The generated pressure,
return into the first velocity component and positive initial growth
of integrated stretching are the full identities (766)--(767).
At amplitude one, `g(0)=0`, `g'(0)=delta^2/2`; for epsilon U_delta
the latter is `epsilon^4 delta^2/2`. Neither pressure nor velocity is
subsequently held to its initial spatial profile.

Let X be the actual forward stochastic flow from a uniform original
position, and use its original pressure impulse throughout. Define

```text
Phi(epsilon,t)=E|integral_0^t grad p(s,X_s)ds|^4,
a(t)=F_8(t), b(t)=F_10(t),
F_n(t)=(1/n!) partial_epsilon^n Phi(0,t),
R(epsilon,t)=epsilon^8 a(t)^2/[a(t)-epsilon^2 b(t)].       (770)
```

These are COMPLETE viscous amplitude coefficients. Translation by
(pi,pi,pi) changes U_delta to -U_delta, so the uniform observation
is even in epsilon. The pressure starts at degree two, rather than
degree three as in the cyclic seed of (666).

### The full first two returns have different signs

Write x=delta^2. Complete Euler time jets of the pressure integral give

```text
Phi(1,t)=A(x)t^4+B(x)t^6+D(x)t^8+O(t^10),
A(x)=(5x^4+14x^2+5)/16,
B(x)=-(x+1)(90x^4+105x^3+323x^2+105x+90)/1728,
D(x)=[94022775x^6+311313856x^5+2842006625x^4
      +1021570593x^3+2842006625x^2+311313856x+94022775]
                                                   /14370048000. (771)
```

All canonical pressure and velocity time jets are generated by the
full Fourier convolution. Material differentiation also retains every
advecting parent. No Galerkin closure or truncation of generated outputs
is used. In particular the two new reciprocal outputs in (769) and
their subsequent pressure are present in D.

There is a finite exact way to verify the entire ratio family. At Euler
time order n the fourth pressure moment is homogeneous of degree n+4
in the initial velocity. Thus its degree in delta is at most n+4.
Reflection in z, with reflection of vector components, changes delta
to -delta and preserves the integrated observation. The coefficients
of orders 4,6,8 are therefore polynomials in x of degrees at most
4,5,6. The checker computes exact Gaussian-rational Fourier jets at
delta=0,1/4,1/2,1,2,4,8 and interpolates within those proved degree
bounds. This determines (771) exactly; it is not a fit to numerical data.

The first return B is strictly negative for every nonnegative x.
However its predicted next saving B^2/A is too small. At balance,

```text
A(1)=3/2, B(1)=-713/864, D(1)=71583401/136857600,
D(1)-B(1)^2/A(1)=85044709/1231718400>0.                  (772)
```

The sign holds uniformly across the whole interval in (769). Substitute
`x=9/16+(16/9-9/16)s` into `A D-B^2`, for 0<=s<=1. Every coefficient
in its degree-ten Bernstein representation is at least

```text
6309914825996461177/802541453597422387200 > 1/128.
```

The checker reconstructs that polynomial exactly from the Bernstein
coefficients. Their basis functions are nonnegative and sum to one.
Also A is increasing for x>=0 and
`A(16/9)=650789/104976<25/4`. Hence
`D-B^2/A>1/800` throughout `3/4<=delta<=4/3`.

### Actual positive viscosity and a uniform short interval

The passage from (771) to the physical viscous comparison retains the
entire functions a,b. The same time/amplitude grading used in (754)
gives, at each fixed positive viscosity,

```text
a(t)=A t^4+O(t^5), b(t)=B t^6+O(t^7),
F_12(t)=D t^8+O(t^9),
Phi(epsilon,t)-R(epsilon,t)
 =epsilon^12 (D-B^2/A)t^8+O(t^9).                        (773)
```

Lower-degree viscous terms are already included in the COMPLETE a,b
and cancel from this difference. At the first time order for a given
amplitude degree, all operations raise that degree; diffusion cannot
contribute there. Higher amplitude degrees start later. Finite time
jets suffice; convergence of an infinite amplitude expansion at the
chosen epsilon is not assumed.

For fixed epsilon,nu>0 the initial high-Sobolev norms are uniformly
bounded over the compact ratio interval (769). Local smooth existence
and differentiated NS/moment equations consequently give a common
time T>0 and a finite original-data bound M for the absolute remainder
in (773), at most M t^9. The finite coefficient heat equations have the
same regularity. The factored denominator at t=0 is A>0, uniformly in
delta; decrease T so that a>0 and b<0 for every ratio and 0<t<=T.
Taking, for example, a further restriction
`tau<=epsilon^12/[1600(1+M)]` gives the ACTUAL inequality

```text
Phi(epsilon,t)-R(epsilon,t) >= epsilon^12 t^8/1600>0,
0<t<=tau, 3/4<=delta<=4/3.                               (774)
```

Thus the failure holds at every prescribed nu>0 and epsilon>0, with
a common short interval across these parent ratios. The interval may
depend on epsilon and nu. It is obtained from local initial-data
estimates, not an unknown long-time bound.

As a separate check of the physical diffusion terms, the script evolves
the COMPLETE conditional first, second and contracted third pressure
moments over the polynomial ring QQ(i)[epsilon], at nu=1/2 and delta=1.
Spatial integration cancels transport and diffusion only at the final
fourth-moment level; they remain in every preceding equation. It gives

```text
[t^4]Phi = (3/2)epsilon^8,
[t^6]Phi = -(713/864)epsilon^10+(2057/360)epsilon^8,
[t^8]Phi = (71583401/136857600)epsilon^12
           -(7402001/1451520)epsilon^10+(30547/6720)epsilon^8.
                                                               (775)
```

In particular these are not inviscid trajectories relabelled as viscous
ones. The highest-degree terms agree with the independent material
calculation. The interval and remainder argument remains analytic.

There is also a genuine favorable comparison, with a coarser allowance.
Because B<0, the same grading gives
`Phi(epsilon,t)-epsilon^8 a(t)=epsilon^10 B t^6+O(t^7)<0`
initially. Here a is the fourth moment of the first pressure generated
by the heat-evolved original velocity, sampled on Brownian paths.
Since that pressure is `exp(-2nu t)p_delta` and
`||grad p_delta||infinity<=1+delta^2`, its entire forecast stock obeys
`a(t)<=[(1+delta^2)/(2nu)]^4` for all t>=0.
The later rational sharpening over-credits that initial depletion.
No all-time comparison with the coarser forecast is proved or refuted.

### A joint labelled sum with exactly zero pooling loss

Use the fixed nonconstant original partition

```text
chi_+(x,y,z)=1/2+sin x/4,
chi_-(x,y,z)=1/2-sin x/4,        m_+=m_-=1/2.             (776)
```

Both weights lie between 1/4 and 3/4. They are passive original labels
of the SAME fluid and Brownian histories, not two independent fluids.
Carry their transported densities and all moments according to (757).

Spatial inversion is a physical symmetry: `U_delta(-x)=-U_delta(x)`.
Uniqueness preserves the velocity equivariance and even pressure.
Inverting the original position and Brownian path sends P to -P,
preserves its fourth power, and exchanges chi_+ with chi_-. Therefore
their unnormalized observations satisfy
`Phi_+=Phi_-=Phi/2` at every available time, for every amplitude and
viscosity. Their complete amplitude coefficients likewise satisfy
`a_+=a_-=a/2`, `b_+=b_-=b/2`. Hence the SUM of their allowances is
exactly

```text
epsilon^8 sum_(i=+,-) a_i^2/(a_i-epsilon^2 b_i)
 =epsilon^8 a^2/(a-epsilon^2 b)=R.
```

Inequality (774) defeats this joint sum as well. The mixture correction
in (756) is zero, since the two coefficient ratios coincide. This
failure is consequently distinct from the loss caused by pooling
unequal rotation scales. Merely retaining these labels and adding
their scalar allowances cannot pay the next full nonlinear return.

The precise remaining task is to control the actual generated-parent
work beyond that first depletion, or supply a different joint reserve
whose nonnegativity and finite initial stock can be proved. The defect
(760), summed with the true component masses, retains the necessary
third moments and inherited impulse. Kinetic pressure-work cancellation
does not cancel this fourth-moment work. None of the results here shows
that repeated renewal is unbounded on a finite interval or that the
full original fluid lacks a larger finite resource.

Run `python3 -O labs/joint_pressure_return.py` and
`python3 -m py_compile labs/joint_pressure_return.py`. The checks cover
the exact family polynomials, their uniform sign, all generated jets,
the separate viscous moment recurrence, and the label algebra. Local
PDE existence, time grading, uniform remainder and stochastic symmetry
identification are ANALYTIC, not new Lean certificates. No Lean
declarations or axioms change.

## Whole-time heat payment for reciprocal parents

`reciprocal_pressure_payment.py` tests the coarser heat forecast left open
by the joint rational obstruction (774). The complete first nonlinear
correction has a favorable sign for every time and every parent ratio.
A uniform analytic remainder turns this into an actual all-time pressure
comparison in a small two-amplitude disk. Strong-amplitude histories are
tested numerically; their continuum comparison remains open.

### Actual histories and the fixed original forecast

On the normalized period-2pi torus, first set viscosity equal to one and
take the actual unforced solution from

```text
U_(a,b)=(a sin y+b sin z, a sin x, b sin x).
p(0)=a^2 cos x cos y+b^2 cos x cos z.
N(0)=(0,-ab sin z cos x,-ab sin y cos x).                (777)
```

Here N is the projected nonlinear velocity derivative. When ab is
nonzero, all three coordinate frequencies are present and the flow
immediately generates parents outside its initial Fourier support.
The preceding full jets give g(0)=0 and g'(0)=a^2 b^2/2 for the integrated
vortex stretching. This is not a superposition of independently evolved
planar flows.

Let X be the actual forward process with drift u and Brownian variance
2, with uniform original position. Retain
`P_t=integral_0^t grad p(s,X_s)ds` and `Phi=E|P_t|^4`.
The reference process Y has Brownian motion only, with the same viscosity
and uniform initial position. Its pressure source is the quadratic heat
forecast `exp(-2t)grad p(0)`. Define

```text
H_(a,b)(t)=E|integral_0^t exp(-2s)grad p(0,Y_s)ds|^4
          =(a^8+b^8) A0(t)+a^4 b^4 A1(t).              (778)
```

Y is an auxiliary forecast, not an independently forced fluid. It is
identified with the full degree-eight coefficient of the actual history.
The actual process continues to use the evolving NS velocity and pressure.
No pressure impulse, conditional moment, original label or time origin is
restarted at a later return.

The two complete heat functions are

```text
A0=11/2048 +(5/1024-t/16)exp(-4t)
   +(-23/2048+t/256+t^2/32)exp(-8t)+exp(-12t)/1024,

A1=427/30720 +(-15/256-3t/32)exp(-4t)+exp(-6t)/6
   +(-301/2048-17t/256+t^2/64)exp(-8t)+exp(-10t)/40.
                                                               (779)
```

Both start at zero and have strictly positive derivative for t>0.
Thus the entire forecast is paid by the finite original stock
`(11/2048)(a^8+b^8)+(427/30720)a^4 b^4`. In the balanced unit case the
stock is 757/30720. These are exact infinite-time integrals, not fitted
numerical plateaux.

An independent check expands the fourth Brownian moment over its 24 time
orderings. For four ordered pressure Fourier modes k1,...,k4 with zero
sum, the Brownian characteristic function and exp(-2s) source give the
four gap decay rates
`8, 6+|k1|^2, 4+|k1+k2|^2, 2+|k4|^2`.
Integrating that simplex exactly, with all three vector pairings and
their multiplicity eight, reproduces (779). This check does not use the
conditional-moment PDE recurrence.

### The complete first correction is favorable for every time

The next homogeneous coefficient of the ACTUAL Phi is

```text
J_(a,b)=(a^10+b^10) B0
       +(a^8 b^2+a^2 b^8) B1
       +(a^6 b^4+a^4 b^6) B2.
Bi(0)=0, Bi'(t)<0 for every t>0, i=0,1,2.              (780)
```

The full exponential polynomials are emitted by the checker. Their
initial and final data are:

| function | -[t^6]Bi | limit as t tends to infinity | sign-cascade levels |
|---|---|---|---|
| B0 | 5/96 | -50593/276480000 | 13 |
| B1 | 65/576 | -16312927/26671680000 | 18 |
| B2 | 107/432 | -2287499437/2133734400000 | 23 |

All velocity, pressure and moment coefficients are obtained from the
complete viscous equations through degree ten of Phi. In particular the
calculation keeps the generated velocity modes, their canonical pressure,
and the transport of all lower moments. The exact exponential-polynomial
and heat-convolution operations are reused from `paired_stretching_history.py`
and `pressure_impulse_payment.py`. Independent full Gaussian-rational time
jets check the velocity and pressure; the lower-amplitude viscous moment
terms also match the separate calculation in the preceding section.

The ratio identification is algebraic. Reflection in y or z changes the
sign of the corresponding original amplitude, preserving the integrated
fourth moment. Interchanging y and z exchanges a and b. Degree-ten
homogeneity therefore leaves exactly the three symmetric monomial pairs
in (780). Exact full-output evaluations at (a,b)=(1,0),(1,1),(1,2)
determine their coefficient functions; (1,3/4) is an unused exact check.
This is not an extrapolation from floating-point samples. At degree eight,
the auxiliary Brownian forecast has only a^8, a^4 b^4, b^8: translation in
y or z changes the sign of one of its two pressure sources and removes
the odd mixed terms. This extra cancellation is specific to that coefficient.

Each derivative sign in (779)--(780) has the finite differential certificate
(659). Every oriented initial datum in the cascade has the required sign,
and the final function vanishes identically. The largest decay rate in the
negative cascades is 18. Retaining the first strict datum of B0 and using
positive convolution kernels gives the deliberately conservative bound

```text
-B0(t)>=c min(t^6,1), c=5/(96*3^18)>0.
16(a^10+b^10)>=(a^2+b^2)^5.
J_(a,b)(t)<=-(c/16)(a^2+b^2)^5 min(t^6,1).             (781)
```

For the first inequality, `-B0'(t)>=(5/16)t^5 exp(-18t)` follows directly
from the positive cascade. Integrate on [0,t] when t<=1, use exp(18)<3^18,
then use monotonicity for t>=1. The second inequality follows from the
checked identity
`16(x^5+y^5)-(x+y)^5=5(x-y)^2(x+y)(3x^2+2xy+3y^2)` with x=a^2,y=b^2.

The sharper rational comparison can still fail: the positive next return
in (771) exceeds that rational formula's predicted correction. Statements
(780)--(781) concern the saving relative to the unsharpened heat forecast.
They do not discard or change the preceding counterexample.

There is also a useful operator-level separation at equal parents. Tag
each extra fluid-nonlinearity insertion by alpha and each moment-advection
insertion by beta. A pressure coefficient of degree n receives
alpha^(n-2); transport by velocity degree n receives beta alpha^(n-1).
The complete degree-ten correction becomes
`alpha^2 S + alpha beta C + beta^2 T`. These are bookkeeping tags within
the equations, not three independently realizable fluid histories.

| contribution | coefficient of t^6 | derivative sign for every t>0 |
|---|---|---|
| evolving pressure source S | -259/432 | negative |
| transport with the original heat pressure T | -35/96 | negative |
| shared source/transport work C | 5/36 | positive |

All three whole-time signs have exact differential certificates. An unused
tag pair (alpha,beta)=(2,3) checks the degree-two decomposition independently.
The physical case alpha=beta=1 retains the positive mixed work, and its sum
is still negative. Adding the two isolated savings while dropping their
shared work would overstate depletion. This identifies a concrete cost
that a compositional reserve must carry even in this favorable family.

### A uniform remainder pays actual small-amplitude histories

Here is the analytic step from the finite coefficient calculation to
actual flows. It reuses the global weighted periodic fixed-point and
moment estimates in (661), an application of the classical
[Fujita--Kato method](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0511213).
The specific comparison below is not a theorem imported from that paper.

Take the complex mean-zero solenoidal space with norm
`sup_(t>=0) exp(t/2)||u(t)||_(H^40)`. The heat semigroup and the fixed
Sobolev product constants bound the NS bilinear Duhamel map there.
For a sufficiently small fixed polydisc in (a,b), contraction gives a
global holomorphic solution with uniform exponential decay. The pressure
gradient is holomorphic with integrable time decay. On
`L_infinity([0,infinity);H^40)`, heat convolution against `-u.grad M`
has norm less than one half after shrinking this same polydisc.
Successively solving the complete moment equations by the resulting
Neumann inverse gives uniform holomorphic bounds. All accumulated zero
Fourier modes are retained. For real amplitudes, the joint forward
equation identifies these moments with the actual stochastic observation.
The complex extension uses the polynomial `(P.P)^2` only.

Choose a closed polydisc of radius R strictly inside this contraction
region. Let M0 bound the fourth moment there for all time, and M8 bound
its eighth time derivative on [0,1]. The differentiated equations and
the smooth initial trigonometric fields give these finite bounds from
the same fixed H^40 majorants, before the future solution is known.
Eight time derivatives use at most sixteen extra spatial derivatives;
the remaining Sobolev regularity controls the products and observation.

Set r^2=a^2+b^2. Individual evenness in a,b and Cauchy estimates on the
polydisc bound the remainder after homogeneous degree ten by
`2 M0 R^(-12) r^12` for r<=R/2. The same estimate applies to its eighth
time derivative with M8. Its first eight initial time jets vanish:
the pressure coefficient of amplitude degree n starts at time order n-2,
and the fourth-moment coefficient of degree n starts no earlier than
time order n-4. In particular every remaining degree is at least 12
and its time order is at least 8. Hence

```text
Phi_(a,b)=H_(a,b)+J_(a,b)+E_(a,b),
|E_(a,b)(t)|<=C r^12 min(t^8,1),
C=2 R^(-12) max(M0,M8/8!).                            (782)
```

There is no division by a possibly vanishing parent amplitude. The
Cauchy estimate sums `sum_(i+j=k)|a|^(2i)|b|^(2j)<=r^(2k)` and a
geometric tail. The time grading uses the actual equation; it does not
assume that higher generated modes are absent.

For example choose
`rho=min(R/2,sqrt(c/[32(1+C)]))>0`. Combining (781)--(782) proves

```text
Phi_(a,b)(t)<=H_(a,b)(t)-(c/32)r^10 min(t^6,1),
0<r<=rho, t>0.                                        (783)
```

This is an actual all-time unforced comparison, with both parent
amplitudes varying independently and with every subsequent return kept
in the controlled remainder. The radius is conservative and not
numerically evaluated. Small-data regularity itself is established
theory; the additional result is this particular pressure-history
payment and its strict geometric saving. It does not leave the
small-amplitude region.

For positive viscosity nu and integer common frequency ell>=1, apply
NS scaling to `nu ell v(nu ell^2 t,ell x)`. For physical initial
amplitudes A,B with `sqrt(A^2+B^2)<=rho nu ell`, the entire actual
pressure fourth moment is at most

```text
[(11/2048)(A^8+B^8)+(427/30720)A^4 B^4]/(nu ell)^4.
```

This stock uses the original amplitudes, scale and viscosity. It is
never replenished when the evolving geometry changes.

### A finite tail target for stronger parents

The optional prefix test retains all three velocity components and the
complete first, second and third conditional pressure moments, together
with the integrated fourth moment. It uses dealiased Fourier products
and the existing Lawson RK4 step. Energy balance, high-mode fractions,
conditional covariance and a fourth/second-moment Jensen check diagnose
the computation; they do not bound the continuum error.

For balanced unit parents, the completed discovery prefixes give:

| nu | grid | time step | final time | Phi | Phi/H |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.25 | 32^3 | 0.005 | 12 | 1.449071257 | 0.229747832 |
| 0.05 | 48^3 | 0.01 | 8 | 19.82699708 | 0.0231232492 |

Every reported quarter-time sample stays below the heat forecast and has
positive conditional covariance and Jensen gap. For nu=0.25, comparison
with 24^3 and time step 0.01 changes the final Phi relatively by 4.2e-10;
the largest relative change at matched reported times is 1.2e-7. For
nu=0.05, comparison with 32^3 at the same step changes final Phi by 5.9e-6
and all matched reported values by at most 6.6e-6. The maximum reported
high-moment fractions on the refined runs are 2.4e-11 and 1.8e-6 respectively.
The latter comparison refines space only. Neither these diagnostics nor
the small kinetic-energy balance errors certify the PDE history.

There is a concrete sufficient tail condition for the balanced datum
(a,b)=(1,1) at nu=1/4. If the ACTUAL history at time 12 satisfies

```text
sum_(k!=0)|u_hat(12,k)|<=1/8, Phi(12)<=2,               (784)
```

the previously proved Fourier tail reserve gives future impulse radius
`R<=log(2)/4-1/8<1/20`. Minkowski retains all inherited/future mixed costs:
`Phi(t)^(1/4)<=Phi(12)^(1/4)+R<6/5+1/20=5/4`.
The complete heat forecast is increasing and exceeds 6 at time 12;
the checker verifies that lower bound with rational exponential
enclosures. Thus `Phi(t)<625/256<6<=H(t)` for every t>=12.
This is conditional on the actual seam (784). Neither the preceding
continuum comparison nor that seam is certified by a numerical prefix.

The stronger-amplitude task is now finite and specific: bound the actual
history up to such a tail seam while retaining the accumulated saving.
The exact sign of one complete correction does not pay all higher
returns at large amplitudes. Nor is the quadratic heat forecast a proposed
universal allowance for every datum: the earlier cyclic datum has zero
initial pressure and creates nonzero pressure through its generated parents.
Any extension must include those parents' pressure resources as well.

Run `python3 -O labs/reciprocal_pressure_payment.py` for exact family,
independent time-jet and conditional-tail checks. Use
`python3 -O labs/reciprocal_pressure_payment.py --prefix --n 32 --nu .25 --dt .005 --final 12`
for a numerical discovery history. The actual stochastic identification,
uniform analytic remainder and scaling argument are ANALYTIC, not new
