## Pressure-history comparison from velocity-error dissipation

`pressure_history_control.py` supplies a concrete consumer for the preceding
velocity validation: an error estimate for the original pressure impulse
along actual stochastic paths. It retains all inherited moments. This is an
analytic comparison theorem and a numerical feasibility tool; the new
sampled runs do not certify an actual finite prefix.

The general strategy of proving regularity from a checked approximation is
established in [Chernyshenko, Constantin, Robinson and Titi,
*A posteriori regularity of the three-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations
from numerical computations*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0607181), alongside
the control-inequality work cited above. Here the additional consumer is the
pressure-history fourth moment, including its trajectory error.

### Spatial pressure error uses the available dissipation

Work on the normalized period-2pi torus. Let u be any available smooth
mean-zero unforced NS prefix at viscosity nu>0. Let v be a prescribed smooth
mean-zero solenoidal reference with the SAME original datum; v may have a
nonzero NS residual. Its canonical pressure is determined by v, not by an
independently fitted pressure field. Write

```text
w=u-v, X=||w||2, Y=||grad w||2, Z=||Delta w||2,
g_u=grad p_u, g_v=grad p_v,
V0>=||v||infinity, V1>=||grad v||infinity,
V2>=||D^2 v||infinity.                                (785)
```

Use Frobenius norms for derivatives. The Fourier sums
`sum |vhat|`, `sum |k||vhat|`, `sum |k|^2|vhat|` suffice for V0,V1,V2.
The existing mean-zero Agmon inequality gives
`||w||infinity<=C_A sqrt(Y Z)`, with `C_A=sqrt(26pi)<10`.
Two further elementary bounds are

```text
||f||4<=3||grad f||2       (mean-zero scalar or vector f),
||grad w||4^2<=3||w||infinity Z.                       (786)
```

For the first, Hausdorff--Young and Holder give the fourth root of
`sum_(k!=0)|k|^(-4)` as a constant. Grouping by `|k|infinity=n` bounds this
sum by `24 sum n^(-2)+2 sum n^(-4)<=24*2+2*(4/3)<81`.
The vector version follows by applying the scalar bound to each component
and using Minkowski for the sum of their squares. For the second, integrate
one derivative in `integral |grad w|^4`. The Laplacian term costs
`||w||infinity Z ||grad w||4^2`; differentiating `|grad w|^2` costs at most
twice that amount. On the torus `||D^2 w||2=||Delta w||2`.

The gradient projection `Q=I-P_Leray` is an H1 contraction and

```text
g_u-g_v=-Q[v.grad w+w.grad v+w.grad w].
```

Differentiating the three products, and using (786) also on this mean-zero
pressure difference, proves

```text
||g_u-g_v||4
 <=3[V0 Z+2 V1 Y+V2 X+40 sqrt(Y) Z^(3/2)].             (787)
```

Every derivative of the unknown error is either X, Y or Z. In particular,
(787) does not assume a Lipschitz bound on the unknown actual flow.

Let `Sminus>=sup lambda_max(-sym grad v)`, and let epsilon0,epsilon1
bound the L2 and homogeneous H1 norms of the full solenoidal NS residual
of v. The previously derived comparison gives, with
`kappa=27(26pi)^2/(32nu^3)`,

```text
X' <=(Sminus-nu)X+epsilon0,
Y' <=(2Sminus-nu/2)Y+V2 X+kappa Y^5+epsilon1,
(1/2)(Y^2)' +(nu/2)Z^2
 <=2Sminus Y^2+V2 XY+kappa Y^6+epsilon1 Y.              (788)
```

Let x(t),y(t) be finite nonnegative supersolutions for X,Y starting at
zero. They are obtained from the reference and its residual, not from the
unknown solution. Set

```text
E(t)=(2/nu) integral_0^t
       [2Sminus y^2+V2 xy+kappa y^6+epsilon1 y],
A0(t)=integral_0^t V0^2,
A1(t)=integral_0^t [2V1 y+V2 x],
A2(t)=integral_0^t y^2.
```

Integration of (788) proves `integral_0^t Z^2<=E(t)`. Cauchy--Schwarz
and Holder in time then turn (787) into

```text
integral_0^t ||g_u-g_v||4
 <=3[sqrt(A0 E)+A1+40 A2^(1/4)E^(3/4)].               (789)
```

This cumulative account uses the one original zero error. It does not
charge a fresh initial gradient on every subinterval. An alternative valid
bound sums local versions of (787), using
`integral_s^(s+h) Z^2 <=[y(s)^2+2 integral_s^(s+h)(...)]/nu`.
The minimum of the cumulative and local bounds is available; neither
restarts the physical pressure impulse.

### Couple paths, then compare the retained moments

Start actual and reference stochastic paths at the same uniform point,
and drive them with the SAME Brownian motion:

```text
dX_t=u(t,X_t)dt+sqrt(2nu)dW_t,
dY_t=v(t,Y_t)dt+sqrt(2nu)dW_t.
```

Both spatial marginals remain uniform by incompressibility. Use continuous
lifts to R3 with identical initial lifts to measure their displacement.
The common noise cancels in that displacement. With
`Splus>=sup lambda_max(sym grad v)`,

```text
d(t)=||X_t-Y_t||_(L4 probability),
d'<=Splus d+3y, d(0)=0.                               (790)
```

Indeed, split the velocity difference as `w(X)+v(X)-v(Y)`, use the
one-sided strain bound for the second term and (786) for the first.
No derivative of actual u is used in (790). If dbar is a supersolution
and `G1>=||grad g_v||infinity`, Minkowski gives

```text
|| integral_0^t g_u(s,X_s)ds
   -integral_0^t g_v(s,Y_s)ds ||4
 <= B(t)+integral_0^t G1 dbar =: b(t),                 (791)
```

where B is either pressure bound from (789) or its local variant. The
first term pays changed pressure; the second pays changed paths. The
reference is an auxiliary comparison process, not an independently
controlled physical fluid or an external force inserted into u.

The EXACT conditional reference moments satisfy, with
`D_v=partial_t+v.grad-nu Delta`,

```text
D_v I=g_v,
D_v Q=I tensor g_v+g_v tensor I,
D_v T=2Q g_v+(tr Q)g_v,
Phi_v'=4 integral g_v.T.                              (792)
```

All start at zero at the original time. Let prescribed approximations
Ibar,Qbar,Tbar,Phibar have residual norms rI,rQ,rT,rPhi in (792), where
the first three are L2, Q uses the full symmetric Frobenius norm, and
rPhi is scalar absolute value. For `G0>=||g_v||infinity` and
`G2>=||g_v||2`, their errors are bounded by the triangular system

```text
e1'<=rI,
e2'<=2G0 e1+rQ,
e3'<=4G0 e2+rT,
e4'<=4G2 e3+rPhi,       e1(0)=...=e4(0)=0.             (793)
```

Transport cancels and diffusion has favorable sign in each L2 comparison.
The third inequality uses `2+sqrt(3)<4` for
`2(Q-Qbar)g_v+tr(Q-Qbar)g_v`. There is no blanket exponential
amplification of all moment errors.

Combining (791)--(793) gives the actual-history consumer

```text
Phi_u(t)^(1/4)<=max(0,Phibar(t)+e4(t))^(1/4)+b(t).      (794)
```

A complete implementation must bound all coefficients and residuals over
ENTIRE time slabs and enclose arithmetic. Finite velocity controls then
also extend the actual smooth prefix by the existing H1 continuation
criterion. This is an a posteriori sufficient condition, not a proof that
arbitrary data satisfy it. Conversely, an exploding comparison control is
not evidence that the physical solution blows up.

The pressure observation remains physically relevant: the conditional
transport representation gives `||u(t)||4<=||u0||4+Phi_u(t)^(1/4)`.
Together with the established enstrophy estimate this supplies continuation
on a finite horizon when the right side is bounded. This argument uses the
conditional transport equation. It does not use the false forward-path
identity `du(t,X_t)=-grad p dt`: that Ito derivative also contains viscosity
and a stochastic term.

### The small-gradient tail pays pressure as well

There is a second tail consumer that avoids a pointwise Wiener-error
estimate. Suppose the ACTUAL mean-zero flow at time s has
`Ys=||grad u(s)||2` and `theta=2kappa Ys^4/nu<1`.
The existing gradient-energy argument gives

```text
integral_s^infinity ||Delta u||2^2
 <=Ds=Ys^2/[nu(1-theta)],
integral_s^infinity ||grad u||2^2<=Ds.
```

Apply (787) with zero reference and Holder over the whole remaining
interval. The future L4 pressure-impulse radius is at most

```text
R_pressure<=12 C_A Ds<=120 Ds,
Phi_u(t)^(1/4)<=Phi_u(s)^(1/4)+R_pressure, t>=s.       (795)
```

Thus the original impulse and all mixed inherited/future costs stay in
the bound. For nu=1/4 and Ys<=1/64 the conservative constants give
`theta<3/10`, `Ds<=5/3584`, and `R_pressure<=75/448`.
If additionally `Phi_u(s)<=4`, then

```text
Phi_u(t)<(99/70+75/448)^4
 =157574018016801/25176309760000
 <63/10<757/120.                                      (796)
```

The last number is the complete original heat stock for balanced unit
reciprocal parents. If s>=12, the increasing heat curve itself exceeds
63/10, checked using rational exponential enclosures. This pays the entire
tail from such an ACTUAL seam. It does not certify arrival at that seam
or comparison with the sharper heat curve before it.

### Feasibility checks and their limits

The default checker verifies the exact constants, the conditional tail,
and the polarization formula for the complete cubic joint vector field.
An independent Gaussian-rational Fourier recurrence supplies both velocity
jets and the first two derivatives of ALL conditional moments; the numerical
interpolation derivatives agree within 1.0e-15 relatively. This checks the
pressure sign and the complete generated outputs at the original datum.
It is not a validation of later time slabs.

The prefix tool uses a shared quintic reference for velocity and the
retained moments. Products are evaluated without filtering on a doubled
spatial grid; cubic outputs fit because each retained frequency satisfies
`|k_j|<n/3`. The three time samples per comparison interval do NOT bound
unsampled residuals. The scalar Phibar has a Bernstein bound over the slab,
but its floating arithmetic and the other controls are not enclosed.

For balanced unit parents at nu=1/4, an initial 24^3 run with comparison
step 1/8 loses its gradient-error bootstrap at time 3. A 32^3 run at the
same comparison step loses it at time 10.875. The latter occurs after the
computed physical pressure moment has nearly stabilized, while the error
majorant is still growing. These are failures of validation bounds, not
counterexamples to the heat payment or regularity.

A separate residual test locates a real spatial truncation cost: at time
1.5, the endpoint H1 residual is about 1.6e-7 at 32^3 and 3.8e-10
at 40^3 with the same integrator step. Decreasing only the interpolation
interval does not remove the spatial cost. Spatial refinement and full-time
residual enclosure are separate remaining obligations.

Run `python3 -O labs/pressure_history_control.py` for the algebra and
independent Fourier-jet checks. The optional command
`python3 -O labs/pressure_history_control.py --prefix --n 40 --nu .25 --dt .0078125 --h .0625 --final 18`
produces sampled feasibility data, not a continuum certificate. The analytic
comparison (785)--(796), stochastic coupling and tail derivation are not new
Lean theorems. No Lean declarations or axioms change. The arbitrary-data
pressure-history payment remains open.

## A pressure-history residual needs its complete time polynomial

`pressure_history_slabs.py` addresses the next obligation in (794): bounds
on the entire reference interval, retaining every pressure and moment
source. The coefficient formulas are exact finite polynomial identities.
The present array implementation still uses unenclosed floating arithmetic,
so its numerical output is feasibility evidence, not a continuum certificate.

### An actual decaying NS shear exposes the sampling defect

Three residual samples cannot certify a time interval, even if both endpoint
first and second time derivatives agree with the physical equation. On the
periodic torus at viscosity one, take the exact globally regular unforced
flow

```text
u(t,x,y,z)=(-386 exp(-t) sin y,0,0), p=0.              (797)
```

Its transport nonlinearity vanishes. Consider the quintic reference
`v=(a(t)sin y,0,0)` on [0,1], where

```text
a(t)=2t^5-15t^4+64t^3-193t^2+386t-386,
a'(t)+a(t)=r(t)=t^2(1-t)^2(2t-1).                    (798)
```

Thus v has the SAME original datum as u. Its complete NS residual is
`(r(t)sin y,0,0)`, which vanishes at times 0,1/2,1. Moreover r' vanishes
at both endpoints, so `a'=-a` and `a''=a` there. These are precisely the
first and second heat-equation jets used in the shared quintic reference.
Nevertheless the residual at time 1/4 has amplitude -9/512. The final
reference amplitude is -142, whereas the true amplitude is -386/e.
An exact rational Taylor upper bound verifies `e<193/71`, so these differ.

The construction is transparent: start with the displayed r, and solve
`a'+a=r` within degree-five polynomials by
`a=sum_(j=0)^5 (-1)^j r^(j)`. All identities in (798) are checked exactly.
There is also a direct sign proof of the endpoint error:
`a(1)-a(0)e^(-1)=e^(-1) integral_0^1 e^t r(t)dt>0`, by pairing t with
1-t. The residual is antisymmetric about 1/2, while the exponential gives
its positive half more weight.

This is an actual NS solution compared with an inaccurate reference, not
an NS blowup or a failure of the pressure payment. Its pressure is zero.
It refutes the proposed inference from three zero residual samples to a
correct physical history. The preceding scripts classified their samples
as discovery evidence; none used this inference as a proof premise.

The same defect occurs with nonzero pressure. Take
`U=(sin x cos y,-cos x sin y,0)` and
`p_U=(cos(2x)+cos(2y))/4`. Exact differentiation gives
`div U=0`, `U.grad U+grad p_U=0` and `Delta U=-2U`.
At viscosity 1/2, the actual flow is
`u=-386e^(-t)U`, `p=386^2 e^(-2t)p_U`. The reference
`v=a(t)U`, `p_v=a(t)^2 p_U` has the same residual `r(t)U` and
the same three vanishing samples. Its final canonical pressure differs
from the actual pressure because `142^2!=386^2/e^2`. The checker verifies
these full incompressible NS identities as well. These examples are
independent of the third coordinate; they test the validation premise,
not a claim about three-dimensional singularity formation.

### Retain all time coefficients and all generated spatial outputs

For a slab [t0,t0+h], put `xi=2(t-t0)/h-1`. Write the shared quintic
reference state as

```text
V(xi)=sum_(j=0)^5 C_j xi^j, -1<=xi<=1.               (799)
```

The state has three velocity entries, three first moments, six symmetric
second moments, three third moments and the integrated fourth moment.
The latter is a spatial scalar; the other moments retain their zero
Fourier modes. All moments still refer to the original start time.

The complete transport term is a degree-ten polynomial. The canonical
pressure gradient determined by the velocity has degree ten as well.
Multiplying it by a first, second or third moment raises the corresponding
source degree to fifteen. Hence the complete velocity and first-moment
residuals have degree at most ten; the second, third and integrated-fourth
residuals have degree at most fifteen. Differentiation in time uses
`partial_t=(2/h)partial_xi`; diffusion is applied to every relevant field.

The implementation constructs each coefficient of those operators before
forming a bound. With retained spatial support `|k_j|<n/3`, all cubic
outputs fit strictly inside the doubled Fourier grid. The complete pressure
is used in the moment sources; it is not filtered back to the velocity
storage box. No generated mode or temporal coefficient is discarded.

For a residual block R, a valid first bound is
`sup_|xi|<=1 ||R(xi)|| <= sum_j ||R_j||`. However this can pay repeatedly
for coefficients which cancel as time passes. The sharper bound retains
their joint information:

```text
||R(xi)||^2 = sum_(k=0)^30 p_k xi^k,
p_k=sum_(i+j=k) Re <R_i,R_j>.                         (800)
```

For velocity H1 residuals the inner product includes the Fourier weight
`|k|^2`; for the symmetric second moment it includes twice each off-diagonal
entry. The scalar fourth-moment residual uses its absolute square. These
are the same norms required by (788) and (793).

On any subinterval [a,b] of [-1,1], convert the scalar polynomial (800)
using `xi=a+(b-a)tau`. If its resulting power coefficients are d_j, then
its degree-30 Bernstein coefficients are

```text
B_k=sum_(j=0)^k [binom(k,j)/binom(30,j)] d_j,
sup_(a<=xi<=b) ||R(xi)|| <=sqrt(max_k B_k).            (801)
```

The Bernstein basis is nonnegative and sums to one on [0,1], proving the
bound. Subdivision changes only the enclosure of the SAME reference
polynomial. It does not create separate histories or replenish the
original reserve. The method keeps signed cross terms between temporal
coefficients until after their complete physical norm has been formed.

### What the bounded probes show

For balanced unit reciprocal parents at nu=1/4, retained grid 40^3,
integrator step 1/128 and comparison interval 1/16, four interval probes give
the following velocity H1 residual figures:

| interval ending at | largest endpoint/midpoint sample | sum of coefficient norms | joint polynomial bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.0625 | 5.25494e-9 | 6.18412e-7 | 4.54911e-8 |
| 1 | 1.64919e-9 | 4.15755e-8 | 2.87031e-9 |

At the interior points `xi=+/-1/sqrt(5)` of the first interval, direct
polynomial evaluation gives a residual norm as large as 4.53561e-8.
Thus the missing error is present between the three sample times; it is
not merely an artifact of the coefficient-sum bound. Retaining the cross
terms makes the interval bound about 13.6 times smaller than that sum and
within 0.3 percent of this interior observation.

The intervals ending at 2 and 4 were also checked. Their joint H1 bounds
are respectively about 1.018 and 1.306 times their three-node samples.
All six residual groups (velocity L2/H1 and four moment levels) retain
the full polynomial; the largest joint-bound/sample ratio among these
four probes is below 9.34. This finite set of probes is not a uniform
multiplier for other intervals.

An independent fixture varies the time coefficients through different
quarter-period spatial translations and uses nonzero entries in every
moment block. Reconstructing the full residual at independently selected
times agrees with a direct complete-operator evaluation within 3.8e-16
relatively. Independent Gaussian-rational Fourier fixtures check that
operator, including pressure. Exact algebra checks the time conversion
and the decaying-shear counterexample. These checks support the formulas;
they do not replace rounding or the full-prefix obligations.

Run `python3 -O labs/pressure_history_slabs.py` for those checks and
`python3 -O labs/pressure_history_slabs.py --probe` for the four probes.
The optional full-history run is
`python3 -O labs/pressure_history_slabs.py --prefix --n 40 --nu .25 --dt .0078125 --h .0625 --final 18`.
It propagates (788)--(794) using complete time-polynomial bounds instead
of three residual samples. Its floating coefficient arithmetic remains
unenclosed. Passing that run would still not certify the actual seam.

A final certificate must reconstruct exactly solenoidal, Hermitian
velocity references with shared endpoints, preserve every inherited
moment, and enclose the Fourier products, inner products and signed
polynomial conversions. The existing radix-two arithmetic proof does
not cover the sampled grid 80 transform; an appropriate supported grid
or a separately proved transform enclosure is required. No Lean
statements or axioms change. The arbitrary-data history estimate remains
open.

## Outward arithmetic for correlated pressure residuals

The complete-time residual construction (797)--(801) has two distinct
arithmetic obligations: generate enclosures of the physical residual
coefficients, then bound the norm of their polynomial on a whole interval.
`pressure_polynomial_enclosure.py` supplies the second consumer and the
shared-reference reconstruction needed by the first. It does not yet
supply the complete physical coefficient enclosures or certify a stronger
pressure-history prefix.

### A continuous reference across interval boundaries

Let b_0,...,b_5 be stored, normalized Fourier arrays, interpreted as exact
binary rationals. The reference is the degree-five Bernstein curve after
one fixed linear reconstruction: Hermitian symmetrization followed by
Leray projection and mean removal for velocity, Hermitian symmetrization
for the conditional moments. The integrated fourth moment is a real scalar.
The other moments retain their zero modes. Adjacent intervals sharing the
same stored endpoint therefore share the same exact reconstructed state.

The computational centered-power coefficients enclose that reference;
they do not redefine it. This distinction prevents a concrete seam error.
For scalar Bernstein control points

```text
(1,0,0,0,0,2^-54),
```

rounding each exact centered-power coefficient separately to binary64 gives
a polynomial whose value at the right endpoint is exactly zero, instead
of 2^-54. Joining that polynomial to the constant next interval would
introduce a jump. A piecewise smooth continuous reference suffices for the
physical differential comparisons, but such unpaid jumps do not.

The exact change of basis used in the enclosure is

```text
B_i^5((1+s)/2) = binom(5,i)(1+s)^i(1-s)^(5-i)/32.       (802)
```

The existing projection and linear-combination ball routines bound its
rounding errors. Independent rational Fourier fixtures check every field
block, including nontrivial Leray denominators and retained moment means.

### A norm enclosure that retains cancellation

For supplied residual centers a_i and certified radii r_i in the required
weighted, normalized Hilbert norm, write the exact coefficients as a_i+e_i,
with ||e_i||<=r_i. On -1<=s<=1,

```text
||sum_i (a_i+e_i)s^i||
  <= sqrt(sup_s sum_(i,j) Re<a_i,a_j>s^(i+j))
       + sum_i r_i.                                   (803)
```

The signed inner products are enclosed before conversion to Bernstein
form. The implementation explicitly computes real/imaginary products and
a sum, instead of assuming an unspecified BLAS dot-product error. With M
complex entries, exact nonnegative integer weights and unit roundoff
u=2^-53, it uses the conservative enclosure

```text
|computed inner product - exact inner product|
  <= gamma * A + 10^-290,
gamma = 8(M+1)u / (1-8(M+1)u),                         (804)
```

where A bounds the sum of the absolute weighted real and imaginary
products. Guards restrict M<=2^28, weights<=2^30 and exclude overflow.
The absolute allowance exceeds the accumulated subnormal error in this
domain. Both the Fourier H1 weights and symmetric-tensor multiplicities
are retained. Fourier normalization is divided out as an exact rational.

Every subsequent signed polynomial conversion uses rational intervals.
For each subinterval, an exact matrix converts centered powers to
Bernstein coefficients. Multiplying a negative matrix entry uses the
opposite interval endpoint. Bernstein convexity then gives (803), with
its final square root checked by an exact rational square comparison.
No assumption about a transcendental library's square-root accuracy is
needed for that returned bound. This is an explicit arithmetic argument
and executable check, not a new Lean kernel certificate.

### Bounded test and remaining physical work

For the first interval of the balanced unit reciprocal flow at nu=1/4,
retained grid 40^3, step 1/128 and interval length 1/16, the signed arithmetic
enclosure adds less than seven parts per billion to each of the six
stored-polynomial norm bounds. The velocity H1 residual bound remains
about 4.54911e-8. Thus enclosing these inner products and scalar conversions
does not erase the previously observed benefit of retaining correlations.
The separate shared-reference coefficient balls are also computed; the
largest velocity coefficient radius is below 3.2e-14 in normalized L2.

These figures enclose the stored residual polynomial ONLY. The probe's
rescaling, Fourier transforms and physical nonlinear operator still need
error propagation from the reference coefficient balls. Setting zero
radii in this probe means that its stored coefficients are its exact
input; it does not assert that the physical residual has zero arithmetic
error. The required remaining pieces are the full operator/pressure
coefficient balls, outward reference-field bounds, and outward propagation
of all pressure-history scalar controls. The earlier three-sample run and
the complete-time floating run cannot substitute for these obligations.

Default checks include exact cancellation, subnormal products, rational
reconstruction of every degree-30 monomial, weighted complex fixtures,
shared endpoints and all reconstructed field balls. Run
`python3 -O labs/pressure_polynomial_enclosure.py` for these checks and
`python3 -O labs/pressure_polynomial_enclosure.py --probe` for the bounded
physical-interval arithmetic test. No Lean declarations or axioms change.
The arbitrary-parent renewal estimate remains open.

## Full operator balls for shared pressure histories

`pressure_operator_enclosure.py` connects the shared Bernstein reference
of (802) to the residual-norm consumer (803). It encloses the complete
Navier--Stokes and conditional pressure-moment operator, including every
quadratic and cubic spatial output. The reference-field majorants and
complete pressure-history scalar propagation are separate requirements;
this operator enclosure alone does not certify a physical prefix.

### The same reference, with complete Fourier support

Let the exact reconstructed reference coefficients have coordinatewise
Fourier support |k_j|<=b. Velocity, first, second and third conditional
moments each have time degree five. The canonical pressure gradient is
computed from that same velocity:

```text
g_v = -Q_grad(v.grad v),                               (805)
```

where Q_grad is the orthogonal projection onto gradients. Transport and g_v
have spatial support at most 2b and time degree ten. The second/third
moment sources and the fourth-moment rate have support at most 3b and
time degree fifteen. An explicit radix-two transform on a grid N>6b
retains every generated frequency. The products' exact discrete Fourier
coefficients therefore equal their continuous Fourier coefficients.

For retained grid 40, b=13, the transform grid is 128 and final coefficient
storage is 80. Cropping beyond the proved support projects the numerical
error orthogonally; it removes no true operator output. In particular,
pressure is not projected back to the original input band. Conditional
moment means are retained throughout.

### Propagating field errors through the physical sources

A field ball consists of a midpoint and a radius in normalized L2, either
in Fourier coordinates or on the complete physical grid. Suppose a and b
have midpoint maxima A and B, radii r_a,r_b, and a pointwise bilinear map
has Euclidean bound L. Its product error is at most

```text
L (A r_b + B r_a + N^(3/2) r_a r_b)
  + the enclosed arithmetic error.                    (806)
```

The last term inside parentheses uses the exact finite-grid inequality
||e||infinity<=N^(3/2)||e||2. It is an error estimate on this computational
grid, not a new continuum Sobolev claim. Each Fourier transform then uses
the explicit butterfly enclosure from `pressure_prefix_certificate.py`.

The physical maps and sufficient constants are:

| map | stored inputs | L |
|---|---|---|
| one transport direction | v_d and partial_d field | 1 |
| symmetric second-moment source | I and g | 2 |
| third-moment source | six symmetric Q entries and g | 5 |
| fourth-moment source | T and g | 4 |

The third source is 2Qg+tr(Q)g. Its bound follows from
2sqrt(2)+sqrt(3)<5 when the six stored entries use their unweighted norm.
The final residual consumer restores the Frobenius norm by weighting
off-diagonal entries twice. All tensor contractions, additions and
projection errors are included; the same g_v enters every source.

Time differentiation, viscous diffusion and transport are then assembled
coefficient by coefficient. There are sixteen coefficients for the joint
residual; velocity and first-moment coefficients above degree ten vanish
exactly. If r is an L2 error radius for a velocity residual coefficient,
its support gives

```text
H1 error <= 2sqrt(3)b r.                               (807)
```

This support bound includes the quadratic generated modes. The scalar
fourth-moment source is integrated with an enclosed signed sum. Its
spatial mean is exact quadrature for the full cubic source, and its
reference time derivative is retained. No history is restarted.

### Independent check of every time coefficient

A separate Gaussian-rational Fourier calculation reconstructs the exact
reference from the stored Bernstein control points and solves its pressure
Poisson equation. It expands every convolution without using the FFT
implementation. All sixteen time coefficients, all spatial outputs and
all six requested residual norms are compared against their returned
balls. The fixture includes changing phases, a nontrivial Leray projection
and nonzero tensor means. Each residual group has a nonzero coefficient
at its highest possible time degree, including the fourth-moment source.
Its auxiliary moment fields are an operator
fixture, not asserted to be realizable conditional moments of a fluid.

These comparisons pass, as does a retained-grid-12 physical interval
probe. Run `python3 -O labs/pressure_operator_enclosure.py` for the exact
fixtures, and `python3 -O labs/pressure_operator_enclosure.py --probe --n 40`
for the first reciprocal-flow interval. The arithmetic claim uses the
stated IEEE model and analytic transform/product estimates. It is not
newly Lean-certified and does not establish the arbitrary-history budget.

For the first balanced unit reciprocal interval, nu=1/4, h=1/16 and
integrator step 1/128, the complete grid-40 operator enclosure gives:

| residual norm | stored-polynomial bound | full coefficient-ball bound |
|---|---|---|
| velocity L2 | 1.36733770e-8 | 1.37210758e-8 |
| velocity H1 | 4.54910868e-8 | 4.76391232e-8 |
| first moment L2 | 6.73931047e-8 | 6.74028838e-8 |
| second moment Frobenius L2 | 1.97112107e-7 | 1.97115604e-7 |
| third moment L2 | 2.45646053e-7 | 2.45646783e-7 |
| scalar fourth-moment rate | 4.09634685e-8 | 4.09660238e-8 |

The largest inflation is about 4.72 percent, in the H1 residual. Its
coefficient-error contribution is 2.14803640e-9. All six norms therefore
meet the bounded test's factor-two acceptance criterion. The full bound
covers this whole interval and the complete spatial operator under the
stated arithmetic model; it is not inferred from residual samples.
This does not extrapolate the measured inflation to later intervals.
The stronger finite-prefix pressure payment still needs the other field
majorants and its controls enclosed over the complete original history.

## Enclosed pressure controls with inherited history

`pressure_history_certificate.py` connects the complete residual balls to
the physical comparison (785)--(794). The exact target remains the one
shared reconstructed Bernstein reference. Every accepted interval now
includes its field bounds and the scalar arithmetic, retaining the
original moments, path displacement and accumulated error dissipation.
The result is an analytic/computational certificate under the explicit
arithmetic assumptions above; it is not a new Lean theorem.

### Field bounds for that same reference

For a Fourier coefficient ball with error radius r and support
|k_j|<=b, Cauchy--Schwarz gives, for derivative orders j=0,1,2,

```text
W_j(target) <= W_j(midpoint)
               + sqrt(sum_(|k_i|<=b) |k|^(2j)) r.     (808)
```

The three support sums are exact integers. Writing m=2b+1,
a=sum_(-b)^b k^2 and c=sum_(-b)^b k^4, they are
m^3, 3am^2 and 3cm^2+6a^2m. The implementation checks these formulas
against independent integer enumeration. H1 error is at most sqrt(3)b r.
Velocity uses bandwidth b; its canonical pressure gradient uses bandwidth
2b. Summing the six velocity or eleven pressure time-coefficient bounds
covers the complete centered time interval |s|<=1.

Both signs of strain matter. Let S0 be the symmetric velocity gradient
of centered time coefficient zero. At each physical grid point an
outward Sylvester test bounds its largest eigenvalue. To cover the
continuum and other time coefficients, add

```text
grid reconstruction error
 + 11 W_2(v_0)/(4N)
 + (1/2) sum_(j=1)^5 W_1(v_j).                       (809)
```

The spatial margin uses the gradient Lipschitz bound, nearest-grid-point
distance and sqrt(3)pi<11/2. Exact solenoidality of the reconstructed
velocity gives ||sym(ik tensor vhat)||op<=|k||vhat|/2.
The same argument with -S0 bounds compression. Each result can also be
replaced by the smaller valid bound W_1(v)/2. Rounded Fourier midpoints
are not presumed exactly solenoidal; their reconstruction errors are
included before using these target-field facts.

The code also returns G0>=||grad p_v||infinity,
G1>=||D grad p_v||infinity and G2>=||grad p_v||2.
The scalar reference fourth moment is bounded by the maximum of its
stored real Bernstein control points. The final H1 estimate comes from
the shared endpoint ball, not an independently rounded polynomial value.

An exact affine shear checks normalization and signs: for
v=((13+5s)sin(y)/16,0,0), |s|<=1, pressure is zero,
W0=W1=W2=9/8 as interval bounds, maximum strain in either sign is 9/16,
and final H1 is 9/(8sqrt(2)). The returned intervals enclose all of these.
This shear is a prescribed reference used to test the field estimates;
its affine amplitude is not asserted to solve unforced NS.

### Scalar arithmetic pays both changed pressure and changed paths

The existing outward bootstrap supplies interval velocity-error bounds
x,y. For interval length h, define

```text
R = 2h(2 Sminus y^2+V2 xy+kappa y^6+epsilon1 y),
D_local = (old_y^2+R)/nu,
D_total = (old_energy_rhs+R)/nu.                      (810)
```

Here old_y is the previously carried error bound. The cumulative account
starts from zero only at the original datum. Subsequent intervals retain
that account, together with the integrals A0,A1,A2 in (789). The local
pressure estimate uses D_local; the cumulative estimate uses D_total.
The smaller of these two valid bounds is added to the accumulated
trajectory term. A cheaper local estimate never resets the global history.

All additions, products and quotients for these controls are performed
as exact rational operations on the supplied binary64 upper bounds.
Square-root proposals are verified by exact squaring; applying that
operation twice gives a fourth-root bound. The path exponential is
bounded by the existing Taylor series with its explicit remainder.
Its step-domain condition is checked. Unsupported large scalar steps
are rejected, not accepted on the basis of ordinary floating exponentials.

The triangular moment bounds use the updated interval upper e1 when
bounding e2, then the updated e2 for e3 and e3 for e4. Consequently,

```text
Phi_u(t) <= (max(0, Phi_reference_upper+e4)^(1/4)
              +pressure_error+trajectory_error)^4    (811)
```

holds throughout each accepted interval. The program records the maximum
over the entire prefix. Exact stored endpoints are compared for all
sixteen fields at every seam; matching hashes are additional diagnostics.
The exact original analytic velocity is checked before the first interval,
and all original conditional moments are zero. Later moments and their
means are carried forward.

Independent 100-digit calculations check all fourteen new propagated
scalar quantities and the fourth-moment output. A two-step fixture begins
with nonzero inherited costs and verifies that replacing them by zero
would discard a nonzero history. These tests supplement the analytic
inequalities and exact outward implementation; high precision alone is
not the justification for the error bounds.

### First complete physical intervals and the remaining decision

For the actual unforced normalized-period-2pi datum

```text
u0=(sin(y)+sin(z), sin(x), sin(x)), nu=1/4,
```

the retained-grid-12 run accepts two complete intervals of length 1/16,
using reference integration step 1/128. The resulting upper bounds are:

| time | actual pressure fourth moment | actual final H1 |
|---|---|---|
| 1/16 | 2.510376e-5 | 1.392943 |
| 1/8 | 3.466982e-4 | 1.373186 |

The displayed decimals are rounded upward. The bounds retain all spatial
outputs, the complete time polynomials and their arithmetic errors. The
shared endpoint comparison passes, and the second interval inherits both
nonzero path error and moment error. These are short physical prefixes;
they do not establish the all-time pressure allowance.

Run the checks and two-interval example from this package with:

```text
python3 -O labs/pressure_operator_enclosure.py
python3 -O labs/pressure_history_certificate.py
python3 -O labs/pressure_history_certificate.py --prefix --n 12 --final .125
```

The stronger grid-40 run is testing the complete prefix to time 18.
At viscosity 1/4 the fixed tail consumer requires actual H1<=1/64 and
an inherited pressure fourth-moment bound at most 4. If accepted, its
remaining fourth-root cost is at most 75/448, including mixed costs with
the past. Formula (796) then gives a full bound below 63/10<757/120,
the original heat stock for this particular datum. Until every required
interval and that seam pass, this stronger payment is unproved.

The universal obligation is different: establish a finite initial-data
reserve for arbitrary concentration and mutually renewing parents.
Finding an approximation that passes this comparison for a particular
initial field does not prove that such a search terminates for every
initial field. A rejected scalar bootstrap would refute the proposed
certificate, not establish singularity of the actual flow. The general
heat forecast is already known to miss pressure generated by cyclic
parents with zero initial pressure; this example tests a specific
nonzero-pressure class, not a universal replacement for the history bound.

## A complete pressure return depletes across unequal scales

`pressure_impulse_scale_return.py` tests the first complete pressure-history
correction at the scale ratios where the parent-energy reserve (709)
fails. The result extends the initial comparison (654) from two frequency
patterns to every positive integer frequency ratio and all independent
parent strengths. It retains the full pressure and material evolution.
The actual positive-viscosity comparison below is analytic, supported by
exact symbolic identities; it is not newly Lean-certified.

This distinction between mixing, amplification and the complete nonlinear
interaction also appears in [Bedrossian, Germain and Masmoudi's Couette
analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.03720). Their background flow and
perturbation hypotheses differ from the finite-energy periodic datum
here; no Couette stability theorem is used to assert this comparison.

### Fixed original forecast and actual-flow statement

On the normalized period-2pi torus prescribe

```text
U=(a sin(y), b sin(kz), c sin(x)),
k a positive integer, a,b,c real, nu>0.
```

Let u be its actual local unforced smooth NS solution, with canonical
pressure p. Start X uniformly and use
`dX=u(t,X)dt+sqrt(2nu)dW`. The pressure observation is the original one:

```text
Phi(t)=E|integral_0^t grad p(s,X_s)ds|^4.
```

The complete initial pressure is zero, while its first derivative is

```text
p1=-(6abc k/(k^2+2)) cos(x)cos(y)cos(kz).              (812)
```

Use the same fixed original first-generation forecast as in (652):
`g_gen(t)=t exp[-nu(k^2+2)t] grad p1`, sampled on Brownian paths with
viscosity nu and uniform starting point, without the fluid drift. Denote
its fourth impulse moment by Phibar. This is an auxiliary observation,
not an externally forced fluid. Its full initial-data stock is finite:

```text
Phibar(t)<=||grad p1||infinity^4/[nu(k^2+2)]^8.
```

For every such datum with abc nonzero, there exists tau>0, determined
from that datum and viscosity, such that

```text
Phi(t)-Phibar(t)
 <= -(1/2)(abc)^4 [a^2 d_a(k)+b^2 d_b(k)+c^2 d_c(k)] t^10 <0,
                                                0<t<=tau. (813)
```

All three d_i are strictly positive. No smallness of the three amplitudes
is required for this initial interval. The interval is not uniform as
amplitudes, frequency or viscosity vary. If a parent amplitude vanishes,
the corresponding triangular NS flow has identically zero pressure and
both moments vanish for all time.

### An explicit frequency law and its sign certificate

Put z=k^2 and define

```text
A(z)=655z^5+9098z^4+35023z^3+53980z^2+81856z+67080,
B(z)=1620z^5+11052z^4+13893z^3+20474z^2+12684z+2200,
C(z)=495z^5+7018z^4+30063z^3+52860z^2+86976z+70280.

d_a = 9z^2 A(z) / [512(z+2)^5(z+5)^2(z+10)],
d_b = 9z^3 B(z) / [512(z+2)^5(2z+1)^2(9z+2)],
d_c = 9z^3 C(z) / [512(z+2)^5(z+5)^2(z+10)].           (814)
```

Every numerator and denominator has nonnegative coefficients and is
strictly positive for z>0. This certifies the whole frequency range;
it is not an extrapolation from a finite list of integers. At k=1 the
three coefficients all equal 20641/456192, recovering the equal-scale
law. At k=4 they recover the three independent values in (658).
For large scale separation,

```text
k^2 d_a -> 5895/512,   d_b ->405/512,   d_c ->4455/512. (815)
```

Thus one parent direction has a weakening margin. The positive sign does
not supply a uniform positive lower bound on all d_i as k grows.

The checker works in rational functions of k with integer Fourier phase
labels (n1,n2,n3), representing the physical frequency (n1,n2,kn3).
Every derivative and inverse Laplacian uses that physical frequency.
The phase map is injective for k>0; no generated mode is identified with
another or discarded. The complete Euler velocity and pressure jets
through the orders used in (813) are reconstructed symbolically.
At k=2 and k=7 the entire fields, not only their final scalar integrals,
are checked against the independent physical Fourier recurrence.

Why four amplitude evaluations suffice is an analytic algebra fact.
When any one amplitude is zero, the triangular flow has pressure zero.
Each pressure time jet is therefore divisible by abc. The fourth impulse
moment is divisible by (abc)^4. Translating x, y or z by the appropriate
half-period reverses exactly one original amplitude and leaves the
integrated stochastic observation unchanged. Its amplitude dependence
is even in each variable. Finally the Euler t^10 coefficient is homogeneous
of degree fourteen in the original velocity. It therefore has exactly
the basis `(abc)^4(a^2,b^2,c^2)`. Three evaluations determine this basis;
a fourth is an unused exact check. No arbitrary function of amplitudes
is being inferred from four samples.

### Which signed contribution pays the positive terms

At zero viscosity, expand the actual pressure impulse along its evolving
material paths as `P=t^2 A+t^3 B+t^4 C+O(t^5)`. These vector fields include
the generated velocity and pressure, not just transport by the original
three waves. The complete t^10 coefficient is

```text
4 integral |A|^2 A.C
 +2 integral |A|^2 |B|^2
 +4 integral (A.B)^2.                               (816)
```

The last two terms are nonnegative. For equal unit strengths, write
L for the negative of the first term and Ppos for their sum. The exact
frequency calculation proves

```text
L>0,           0<=Ppos<(2/3)L,         every k>=1,
Ppos/L ->2/5 as k->infinity.                         (817)
```

The strict margin is certified by the positive numerator and denominator
of `(2/3)L-Ppos`. It leaves at least one third of the signed contribution
after paying BOTH positive terms. These are joint contributions to one
history coefficient, not separately composable fluid stages. In particular
(817) does not assert that each interaction has a favorable sign.

### Viscosity is retained, not sent to zero

The Euler calculation supplies exactly the viscosity-independent part
of the first difference. Here is why that is enough for every fixed
positive viscosity in (813).

The degree-three pressure in the amplitude expansion is exactly
`t exp[-nu(k^2+2)t]p1`. Each first quadratic velocity output comes from
two waves in orthogonal coordinate directions, so its Laplace eigenvalue
is the sum of the two input eigenvalues; its heat convolution is the
resonant factor t times that common exponential. Pairing it with the
remaining heat parent gives the stated cubic pressure. The leading
amplitude-degree-twelve fourth moment has no velocity transport factor
and is exactly Phibar on Brownian paths with the SAME viscosity.

The t^n coefficient has joint degree n+4 when original amplitudes and
viscosity are scaled together. Its amplitude degree is at least twelve.
At time orders eight, nine and ten, the only possible amplitude degrees
are therefore twelve, thirteen and fourteen. Odd amplitude degrees
vanish by the translations above. All degree-twelve terms, including
the viscous ones, are already in Phibar. Consequently,

```text
Phi(t)-Phibar(t)
 = -(abc)^4(a^2 d_a+b^2 d_b+c^2 d_c)t^10+O(t^11),      (818)
```

and the displayed coefficient contains no viscosity. The checker also
computes the full conditional-moment PDEs over QQ(i)[nu] independently
at k=3 with amplitudes (1,2,3), and k=6 with amplitudes (2,1,1).
In both cases all lower coefficients cancel against the matched forecast
and the complete t^10 difference is exactly (818), for every viscosity.
Those specializations check the degree argument; they do not replace it.

Local smooth existence makes (818) a statement about actual solutions.
For each fixed datum and viscosity, a standard H40 energy estimate gives
an initial interval and norm bound fixed before the solution is known.
The pressure equation and the triangular conditional-moment equations
then bound the required eleven time derivatives on a smaller interval.
The explicit forecast has bounded derivatives there as well. If their
combined Taylor remainder is bounded by M t^11 and
`D=(abc)^4(a^2 d_a+b^2 d_b+c^2 d_c)>0`, choosing
`tau<=D/[2(1+M)]` inside that interval proves (813).
For a fixed datum the same local estimates are uniform for nu in [0,1].
No unknown future-solution bound is assumed.

### Growing parent energy can coexist with this history depletion

For k>=6 and equal strengths, (708) gives actual small-positive-viscosity
intervals on which both retained concentration J and pressure-parent
energy H exceed their initial values. Choose its interval small enough
also to lie inside the viscosity-uniform interval for (818), then choose
viscosity in the range required by (708). The SAME actual history has

```text
J(t)>J(0),       H(t)>H(0),       Phi(t)<Phibar(t).     (819)
```

Thus the earlier adverse norm return does not imply an adverse return
for the continuation-relevant pressure observation. The joint path and
pressure terms retain a cancellation which those two scalar energies
cannot express. Physical amplitude scaling gives the same coexistence
at any prescribed positive viscosity, with a correspondingly shorter
interval and larger original datum.

This is an unbounded-family initial-return law, not an arbitrary-horizon
payment. The existing moment state must persist beyond tau; the proof
cannot be restarted with a newly favorable original geometry. Later
returns, interacting additional frequency families and concentration
remain the central unpaid obligations. Neither (813) nor failure of a
different reserve constructs an unforced singularity.

Run `python3 -O labs/pressure_impulse_scale_return.py`. It checks the
symbolic frequency law, all amplitude coefficients, positive-polynomial
certificates, the signed margin, independent full physical Fourier jets
and the complete viscosity-polynomial moment fixtures. Local PDE
intervals and stochastic identification remain analytic.

## Oblique parents reverse the pressure-history correction

The law (813) depends on more than initial zero pressure and a cyclic
arrangement of parents. `pressure_oblique_return.py` gives a smooth
periodic unforced example with those two properties for which the matched
pressure-history comparison has the opposite sign. The forecast retains
the complete heat evolution of the oblique waves. Its failure is not an
artifact of applying the orthogonal resonance formula in new coordinates.

### The physical datum and its matched original forecast

On the normalized period-2pi torus take

```text
U=(sin y-4 sin z, sin z, sin(x+4y)).                    (820)
```

This is the pushforward of a cyclic field by an integer linear shear
of determinant one. It is divergence-free and has initial canonical
pressure zero. That shear is not a symmetry of the Euclidean NS equation:
both the physical inverse Laplacian and diffusion must be recomputed.
All calculations below use their ordinary Euclidean values. In particular,

```text
p_t(0)=-(1/9) cos(x+5y)cos z-(3/11) cos(x+3y)cos z.    (821)
```

For any fixed nu>0 define from the ORIGINAL datum

```text
H(t)=exp(nu t Delta)U,
V_t-nu Delta V=-P[(H.grad)H],       V(0)=0,
-Delta p3=div div(H tensor V+V tensor H),
integral p3=0,                    g_gen=grad p3.       (822)
```

P is the solenoidal projection. For this datum H has pressure zero for
every time, so the quadratic source in (822) is already solenoidal.
H and V are the first two homogeneous amplitude terms of the actual NS
solution, and p3 is its entire cubic pressure term. They are explicitly
computable finite Fourier heat convolutions. No later state is substituted
for U. In general `g_gen` is not `t exp(nu t Delta)grad p_t(0)` here,
because the input and generated Laplace eigenvalues do not always add.

Let Phi be the fourth pressure-impulse moment of the actual local unforced
solution, sampled along `dX=u(t,X)dt+sqrt(2nu)dW` from uniform initial
position. Let Phibar use g_gen along uniform Brownian paths with the SAME
viscosity and no fluid drift. This auxiliary forecast is not a forced
fluid. The conditional moments of both histories start at zero once.

The forecast has a finite original-data stock. For example, let Mj be
the initial Fourier Wiener sum `sum_q |q|^j |Uhat(q)|`, j=0,1,2.
The mean of V is zero. Heat decay and contraction of P give

```text
W0(H)<=M0 exp(-nu t),      W1(H)<=M1 exp(-nu t),
W0(V)<=M0 M1 t exp(-nu t),
W1(V)<=(M1^2+M0 M2)t exp(-nu t).
```

The Fourier pressure multiplier then gives

```text
||g_gen(t)||infinity<=C(U)t exp(-2nu t),
C(U)=4M0 M1^2+2M0^2 M2,
Phibar(t)<=[C(U)/(4nu^2)]^4.                          (823)
```

This supplies a finite forecast without assumptions about the unknown
future fluid. The counterexample below concerns its time-dependent
comparison curve, not violation of the larger stock (823).

### Complete positive-viscosity comparison failure

The full moment equations, computed over QQ(i)[nu], give

```text
Phi(t)-Phibar(t)=delta t^10+O(t^11),
delta=388474522689518625902918581
      /128553647224867666773083481600 >0.              (824)
```

The coefficients through order nine cancel exactly. At order ten the
complete viscosity-squared term also cancels; the remaining delta is
independent of viscosity. To check the matching, the cubic forecast jets
are derived directly from (822), separately from the full NS recurrence.
They agree with the entire cubic-amplitude part of those full pressure
jets. The independent rational-viscosity Fourier recurrence also checks
the full velocity and canonical pressure fields.

Local H40 bounds from U and nu, followed by the triangular conditional
moment equations, bound eleven time derivatives on an original-data
interval. If the difference remainder is at most M t^11, choose a
smaller tau<=delta/[2(1+M)]. Then the ACTUAL solution satisfies

```text
Phi(t)-Phibar(t)>=(delta/2)t^10>0,       0<t<=tau,      (825)
```

for every fixed positive viscosity. This is an analytic local-solution
argument supported by exact algebra, not a formal Lean interval theorem.

The failure does not require the previously favorable contribution to
turn positive. In the full material expansion `P=t^2 A+t^3 B+t^4 C+...`,
write

```text
L=-4 integral |A|^2 A.C,
Ppos=2 integral |A|^2 |B|^2+4 integral (A.B)^2.
```

Here L>0 and both terms in Ppos are strictly positive, but

```text
Ppos/L=3097380746164991847708492620
        /2708906223475473221805574039 >1.              (826)
```

Thus the positive contributions exceed the signed payment by about
14.34 percent. In contrast, (817) paid both terms with a uniform margin
in the orthogonal family. For the tested shears 1,2,4,8 at k=1, the
complete initial correction is respectively negative, negative, positive,
negative. No monotone dependence on the shear is asserted. The pressure
source and its material paths evolve together throughout this calculation.

### The same failure occurs with a global diffusion payment

For initial datum lambda U, lambda>0, rescaling amplitude and physical
time gives the exact relation

```text
Phi_(lambda,nu)(t)-Phibar_(lambda,nu)(t)
 =lambda^4 [Phi_(1,nu/lambda)(lambda t)
            -Phibar_(1,nu/lambda)(lambda t)].          (827)
```

The first adverse coefficient is therefore delta lambda^14. It persists
for arbitrarily small nonzero amplitudes at each positive viscosity.
These small copies have an explicit GLOBAL positive payment from the
existing gradient-energy argument (733) and pressure tail (795).
Their original resources are

```text
||lambda U||2^2=(19/2)lambda^2,
||grad(lambda U)||2^2=(35/2)lambda^2.
```

If `0<lambda<=nu/128`, the first-exit parameter in (733) obeys, using pi<4,

```text
theta=2 kappa_nu ||grad(lambda U)||2^4/nu
 <5589675/268435456<1/40.
```

Consequently the actual unforced solution is globally smooth, its gradient
decays, and its entire original pressure history satisfies

```text
Phi_(lambda,nu)(t)^(1/4)
 <=(28000/13) lambda^2/nu,                 every t>=0. (828)
```

Indeed the total squared-Laplacian cost is at most
`(40/39nu)*(35/2)lambda^2`; multiply by the conservative pressure factor
120 from (795). The initial impulse is zero, so no past cost is omitted.
This supplies an explicit finite reserve for the same geometry that
violates the sharper forecast comparison. These examples have neither
external forcing nor a singularity.

The failed assertion is the extension of the orthogonal initial
domination law to all pressure-free cyclic geometries. Neither the
unbounded orthogonal-family theorem nor the possibility of a larger
full-datum allowance is refuted. Subsequent general histories require
payment of the positive geometric terms after parents change direction;
one cannot reuse (817) solely because the interaction graph is cyclic.
The small-gradient payment (828) does not solve that arbitrary-data task.

## An adverse return consumes additional original pressure stock

`pressure_oblique_stock.py` follows the oblique datum (820) through the
whole viscous clock. The complete first nonlinear pressure correction is
positive and increasing for every time. Thus the initial excess in (825)
does not disappear after later heat decay. For actual sufficiently small
flows, it eventually exhausts the exact cubic forecast's total stock.
An additional, original-data stock pays the full history in that regime.

This statement concerns the exact forecast stock computed below. It does
not assert failure of the larger Wiener majorant (823), and it does not
construct an unforced singularity. The small-data hypothesis will remain
explicit in the physical transfer.

### Complete coefficients on one original clock

Set viscosity to one for the calculation and initial velocity to epsilon U,
where U is (820). Define Phi from the actual pressure and actual advecting
paths, and retain all its conditional moments from time zero. The complete
amplitude expansion has the form

```text
Phi_epsilon(t)=epsilon^12 A(t)+epsilon^14 B(t)
                         +epsilon^16 W_epsilon(t).    (829)
```

Here epsilon^12 A is exactly the matched cubic-pressure Brownian forecast
(822). B includes the velocity and pressure through amplitude degree five,
the first conditional moment through degree five, the second through degree
eight, and the third through degree eleven. Every convolution output is
retained. B is not obtained by independently repeating the initial return
or multiplying uncorrelated parent expectations.

The implementation reuses `pressure_impulse_payment.history_from_fields`.
Its supplied physical fields solve the complete projected heat-source
recurrence; independent Gaussian-rational NS time jets check their
velocity and canonical pressure. The same moment routine still produces
the previous orthogonal-family certificates.

Both A and B are finite exact sums of `c t^j exp(-r t)`. Their coefficients
are rational and their rates are nonnegative integers. The checker proves

```text
A(0)=B(0)=0,     A'(t)>0, B'(t)>0,      every t>0,
alpha=lim A(t)>0,       beta=lim B(t)>0,
4.604e-12<alpha<4.606e-12,
6.608e-13<beta<6.610e-13.                            (830)
```

The displayed brackets are exact terminating rationals, not numerical
quadrature tolerances. Full rational alpha and beta and all exponential
polynomials are emitted by the checker. A has 96 terms and its derivative
sign certificate has 95 levels; B has 450 terms and 449 derivative levels.
The largest rates are respectively 162 and 334. The first strict cascade
data occur at derivative orders seven and nine, agreeing with

```text
A(t)=(708361715/49182515712)t^8+O(t^9),
B(t)=delta t^10+O(t^11),                             (831)
```

where delta is the positive rational in (824). Each sign certificate
applies a finite chain of operators `(d/dt+r)` with nonnegative initial
data, ending at zero. Solving that triangular chain proves the sign for
every time, without a time grid. Keeping its first strict datum gives

```text
B(t)>=b min(t^10,1),       b=delta/3^334>0.            (832)
```

For t<=1 this follows from the sharp leading term times exp(-334t),
using e<3; for t>=1 use monotonicity and the value at one. The small
constant in (832) is a conservative analytic margin.

### Independent Brownian verification of the forecast stock

The eight cubic-pressure modes are `(+-1,+-3,+-1)` and
`(+-1,+-5,+-1)`, with the x and y signs matched. Their squared lengths
are r=11 or r=27. Each Fourier pressure coefficient is

```text
p3_hat(q,t)=-[2t exp(-19t)+K_r(t)]/(4r),
K_r(t)=[exp(-rt)-exp(-19t)]/(19-r)>0,     t>0.         (833)
```

These are checked against the full heat-Duhamel recurrence, not assumed
from the wave labels. For four modes a,b,c,d with zero sum, set

```text
S=(a.b)(c.d)+(a.c)(b.d)+(a.d)(b.c).
```

There are exactly 216 ordered zero-sum quartets in this support. Every S
is positive, and the minimum is 283. Writing `h_q=-p3_hat(q)>0`, the
Brownian characteristic function expresses A as a sum of positive ordered
time integrals with factor 8S. The three nontrivial Brownian gap rates are
`|a|^2`, `|a+b|^2`, `|d|^2`. In particular A is strictly increasing.

The checker independently evaluates the entire half-line integral by
three exact heat convolutions at those gap rates, followed by a scalar
exponential-polynomial integral against h_d. Summing all quartets gives
the same rational alpha as the conditional-moment PDE calculation.
This verification uses none of the first, second or third moment fields.
Thus epsilon^12 alpha is a certified total stock for the matched FORECAST.

### Actual histories fit a larger stock and exceed the old one

The standard complex small-data fixed-point estimate supplies a radius
r0>0, chosen from the fixed shape U and viscosity one, with uniform
decaying H40 bounds on the solution for complex |epsilon|<r0. The pressure
and triangular conditional-moment equations then have uniform analytic
bounds on the whole half-line. These bounds come from the fixed-point
and equation majorants, not a presumed bound on an arbitrary future flow.
On this complex disc the moment is extended by its polynomial conditional
moment equations; it is not defined using a nonholomorphic complex modulus.

Translation by `(pi,pi,pi)` reverses U, so the integrated observation is
even in epsilon. Its first amplitude degrees are twelve and fourteen.
Cauchy bounds on a smaller disc give (829) with a uniformly bounded W.
The same differentiated equations give twelve time derivatives on [0,1].
A velocity coefficient of degree n starts at time order n-1; a pressure
coefficient of degree n starts at order n-2; a fourth impulse coefficient
of degree n starts at order n-4. Consequently the degree-sixteen remainder
has zero time jets through order eleven. One finite majorant C gives

```text
|W_epsilon(t)|<=C min(t^12,1),       every t>=0.        (834)
```

This is the same analytic mechanism used in (670), applied to the complete
oblique fields. The radius and C are determined before the future solution
is known. They are not evaluated numerically here.

Choose epsilon0>0 inside that disc, with `C epsilon0^2<=b/2` and within
the global small-gradient range of (828). Equations (829)--(834) imply
the ACTUAL all-time comparison

```text
epsilon^12 A(t)+(1/2)epsilon^14 B(t)
 <=Phi_epsilon(t)
 <=epsilon^12 A(t)+(3/2)epsilon^14 B(t)
 <=K_epsilon=epsilon^12 alpha+2epsilon^14 beta,
                  0<|epsilon|<=epsilon0, t>=0.        (835)
```

The original nonnegative stock K_epsilon is finite and explicit once the
datum is specified; it covers both the complete first correction and its
uniform remainder margin. The small-amplitude threshold may be extremely
small. This argument does not extend that threshold to arbitrary data.

Conversely, the exact uncorrected forecast stock is genuinely insufficient.
Choose an integer N from the explicit A,B functions such that

```text
alpha-A(N)<=epsilon^2 beta/8,       B(N)>=beta/2.
```

Such a finite N exists by their proved limits; it depends on the original
datum and computable coefficient functions, not on the unknown actual
history. The lower bound in (835) yields

```text
Phi_epsilon(N)>=epsilon^12 alpha+(1/8)epsilon^14 beta
               >epsilon^12 alpha.                   (836)
```

This strengthens the initial comparison failure to failure of the exact
whole-time cubic forecast stock, on globally regular unforced flows.
It does not refute K_epsilon or the coarser stock in (823).

For arbitrary viscosity nu>0 and original datum lambda U, use
epsilon=lambda/nu and the clock nu t. The full fourth moment is nu^4
times the viscosity-one moment, so (835) supplies

```text
K_(lambda,nu)=lambda^12 alpha/nu^8
                       +2lambda^14 beta/nu^10,
                  0<|lambda|<=epsilon0 nu.            (837)
```

The lesson for the arbitrary-data reserve is specific: positive returns
need additional resources even after complete viscous history is included.
For this small-data class the higher returns are absorbed by (834).
Removing that smallness requirement, while retaining all accumulated
moments and generated parents, remains the open physical estimate.

Run `python3 -O labs/pressure_oblique_stock.py`; the existing

## A fast receiver leaves a slower pressure parent

`pressure_oblique_slow_parent.py` identifies a later physical interaction
that the original cubic pressure forecast cannot represent. The same
oblique datum as (820) generates a slow velocity mode, which interacts
with an original parent to produce a slow pressure tail. The coefficient
identities are exact. A uniform small-data decay argument below transfers
them to actual globally regular unforced solutions. This is an analytic
result, not a new Lean certificate.

The conclusion is deliberately different from the integrated stock result
(837). No fixed multiple of the original **instantaneous** pressure forecast
bounds the actual pressure gradient for all time. Nevertheless the finite
corrected **integrated** allowance in (836)--(837) remains valid in its
proved small-amplitude range. Neither conclusion decides arbitrary-data
regularity.

### The complete equation generates a descending chain

Use viscosity one and the normalized period-2pi torus. The original field is

```text
u(0)=epsilon U,
U=(sin y-4 sin z, sin z, sin(x+4y)).
```

Write the actual viscous amplitude expansion as `u=sum epsilon^m U_m`.
For `q_j=(1,4-j,0)`, let `i c_j(t)` be the vertical Fourier coefficient
of `U_(j+1)` at q_j. The full NS recurrence gives

```text
c_0(t)=-(1/2)exp(-17t),
c_j'+[1+(4-j)^2]c_j=(1/2)exp(-t)c_(j-1),
c_j(0)=0,                                  1<=j<=4.    (838)
```

No lower amplitude degree contains q_j. Both other velocity components
at this first degree vanish. These assertions are checked against the
complete velocity, including pressure projection and every generated
mode. The scalar chain is the resulting identity, not a replacement of
NS by a passive model. In particular c_j<0 at every positive time, by
successive positive heat convolutions. The diffusion rates are
17,10,5,2,1.

At the last step the exact field is

```text
c_4(t)=-exp(-t)/92160+exp(-3t)/46080-exp(-7t)/64512
       +exp(-13t)/184320-exp(-21t)/1290240,
lim_(t->infinity) exp(t)c_4(t)=-1/92160.                (839)
```

An independent full physical time-jet calculation gives
`partial_t^4 uhat_3(0,(1,0,0))=-i epsilon^5/32`, agreeing with
(838). The new mode has a much longer lifetime than the original receiver.

### Its pressure is a genuine subsequent return

Pressure degree six needs only velocity degrees one through five:
`p_6=sum_(a+b=6) P(U_a tensor U_b)`, where P is canonical pressure
recovery. At `q=(1,0,1)` the checker finds

```text
p_m(q)=0 for m<6,
lim_(t->infinity) exp(2t) p_6(t,q)=-1/46080.            (840)
```

It independently recovers this coefficient from the first-eigenmode
limits of all the velocity coefficients. There are exactly four nonzero
pressure coefficients at rate two, at `(+-1,0,+-1)`, all equal to
`-1/46080`. In real form their leading contribution is
`-epsilon^6 exp(-2t) cos(x)cos(z)/11520`.

This return pairs the generated vertical `sin x` with the original
horizontal `-4 sin z`. The original cubic pressure has frequencies
`(+-1,+-3,+-1)` and `(+-1,+-5,+-1)`, with the x/y signs matched,
and all of its time rates are at least eleven. Thus a history summary
retaining only that cubic source misses a slower descendant of the very
same unforced datum.

### Transfer to actual solutions, uniformly in late time

Here is the analytic obligation that prevents a finite Taylor polynomial
from being mistaken for the actual late-time flow. Fix a sufficiently
large integer Sobolev index, for example s=40, and use the mean-zero
solenoidal mild equation at viscosity one. Its heat estimate has the form

```text
||exp(t Delta) P_Leray div F||_(H^s)
 <= C (1+t^(-1/2)) exp(-t) ||F||_(H^s).
```

The H^s algebra estimate makes the mild map a contraction in
`sup_(t>=0) exp(t)||u(t)||_(H^s)` on a fixed small complex ball of
initial data. The bound is uniform on a smaller ball, and the solution
is holomorphic in epsilon there. This uses initial norms and the heat
kernel estimate; it assumes no future bound for the target solution.
It is the same small-data mechanism used in the preceding stock result.
For example, the time-convolution factor is bounded by four:
`integral_0^t [1+(t-s)^(-1/2)]exp(-s)ds<=4`. Splitting at t-s=1
proves this bound. If C is four times the heat and algebra constants,
the weighted solution ball of radius 1/(4C) is contractive for initial
norm at most 1/(8C). This specifies a sufficient amplitude radius from
the fixed norm of U alone; a smaller radius gives uniform Cauchy bounds.

Let Pi_1 project onto the six frequencies with |q|^2=1 and write
`N(u)=-P_Leray div(u tensor u)`. The convergent expression

```text
V(epsilon)=Pi_1 u(0)+integral_0^infinity exp(s)Pi_1 N(u(s))ds
```

defines the first-mode asymptote. The mild equation then gives

```text
u(t)=exp(-t)V(epsilon)+O((1+t)exp(-2t)) in H^s.         (841)
```

Indeed N(u)=O(exp(-2t)) in H^(s-1). In the first eigenspace the
remaining source integral costs O(exp(-2t)); on its complement the heat
rate is at least two, so the convolution costs at most
O((1+t)exp(-2t)). All estimates are uniform on a smaller amplitude disk.
Consequently V is holomorphic and its amplitude coefficients are the
limits of the complete coefficient equations. Translation by (pi,pi,pi)
reverses U, so V is odd in epsilon.

Equations (839)--(841), together with canonical pressure recovery, imply

```text
Vhat_3(epsilon,(1,0,0))=-i epsilon^5/92160+O(epsilon^7),
lim_(t->infinity) exp(2t) phat(t,(1,0,1))
                    =-epsilon^6/46080+O(epsilon^8).    (842)
```

Pressure recovery is a continuous quadratic map on H^s; thus the limit
in (842) follows from (841) for the full pressure, not a pressure series
truncated at degree six. The exact lower-degree calculation and uniform
holomorphy identify its leading coefficient. For all sufficiently small
nonzero real epsilon it is nonzero. The amplitude threshold is supplied
by the small-data estimates and the analytic remainder; it is not
numerically evaluated here.

Let `g_gen=epsilon^3 grad p_3` be the original matched Brownian cubic
forecast of the preceding section. For every such fixed epsilon,

```text
||grad p(t)||_2 >= c_epsilon exp(-2t)  for large t,
||g_gen(t)||_2 <= C |epsilon|^3 exp(-11t) for t>=1,
||grad p(t)||_2 / ||g_gen(t)||_2 -> infinity.            (843)
```

The first inequality uses just the nonzero Fourier coefficient in (842).
The second follows directly from the explicit eight cubic coefficients.
Their faster terms are a polynomial times exp(-19t), so they are bounded
by a constant times exp(-11t) on t>=1. Rescaling to arbitrary positive
viscosity replaces t by nu*t and multiplies pressure by nu^2.
The same obstruction holds for the L4 pressure-gradient norm used in
impulse estimates: the actual L4 norm dominates its L2 norm, whereas
the finite Fourier forecast also has an L4 upper bound of rate eleven.

Thus even an arbitrarily large constant depending on the full datum and
viscosity cannot repair this particular all-time pointwise decay profile.
A constant also depending on a prescribed finite horizon is not refuted.
Nor is a larger integrated pressure stock: these actual small flows are
already paid by (837). The conclusion identifies lost history, not a
singularity or an endlessly regenerated energy source.

The numerical consumer evolves all three velocities, the original
conditional impulse, all six second moments, the three contracted third
moments and the integrated fourth moment. It reuses the full physical
operator in `reciprocal_pressure_payment.make_flow`; no amplitude series
is used to evolve these numerical histories.

The first coarse screen exposed a specific observation error. A grid of
24 retains |q_j|<8. Every original cubic pressure mode fits, but some

| --- | ---: | ---: |
| abs(q_j)<8 | 156 of 216 | 0.9585102736093485 |
| abs(q_j)<12 | 216 of 216 | 1 exactly |

Every omitted quartet has a strictly positive time integral. The lost
modes have y-frequency eight or ten. Therefore the first row's apparent
depletion is an exact projection loss, even as the amplitude tends to

leading quartets does not certify later nonlinear moments; spatial and

The first and third partial frequency sums are already pressure modes;
the intermediate pair sum is the extra information needed here.

At viscosity one, numerical histories were tested through time 1.5 against

| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1/8 | 0.99776842 | 1.00224326 | 1/256 |

### Reproduction and remaining boundary

Run the exact slow-parent check with
`python3 -O labs/pressure_oblique_slow_parent.py`. It verifies the full
chain, the independent physical time jet and the pressure recovered from
all first-mode limits. Run `python3 -O labs/pressure_oblique_stock.py` for

pass it as `--coefficients` to
`python3 labs/pressure_oblique_slow_parent.py --prefix`. Optional flags

The physical lesson is that generated parents can outlive the geometry
that produced them. A compositional reserve must retain those parents and
the original impulse across transitions. The present result supplies an
explicit physical transition and a failed decay-profile bound. Uniform
payment under repeated interacting transitions, concentration and arbitrary
original data remains the missing estimate.

## Relative vorticity controls a retained pressure history

`pressure_vorticity_control.py` supplies a second physical comparison for
(788), and passes its dissipation bound into the existing pressure-history
consumer (789)--(794). It uses the complete velocity difference, including
its curvature work, viscosity and residual. The identities and scalar
arithmetic have independent exact and high-precision checks. The transfer
to actual solutions is analytic; no new Lean theorem is claimed here.

This is an application of the a posteriori strong-solution framework of
[Chernyshenko, Constantin, Robinson and Titi](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0607181).
Their robustness result explains how a sufficiently accurate approximation
can certify an actual strong solution. It does not make every approximation
accurate enough, or supply a bound for every initial datum. The comparison
below retains the extra pressure-history account needed by this laboratory.

### Complete relative-vorticity identity

Work on the normalized period-2pi torus. Let u be an actual smooth,
mean-zero, unforced NS solution at viscosity nu>0. Let v be a smooth,
mean-zero, solenoidal reference, with the full projected residual

```text
r = v_t + P_Leray(v.grad v) - nu Delta v.
w=u-v, eta=curl w, Omega=curl v,
X=||w||2, Y=||grad w||2=||eta||2, Z=||Delta w||2.
```

The residual is an error of the reference, not a force inserted into u.
Let epsilon0 and epsilon1 bound its L2 and homogeneous H1 norms. Let
Sminus and Splus bound the largest eigenvalues of -sym grad v and
sym grad v, respectively, and set

```text
V2 = sum_k |k|^2 |vhat(k)|.
```

In particular `||grad Omega||infinity,Frobenius<=V2`. Taking curl of the
full error equation gives

```text
eta_t + (v+w).grad eta
 = eta.grad v + Omega.grad w + eta.grad w
   - w.grad Omega + nu Delta eta - curl r.             (844)
```

The two curvature terms cannot simply be discarded. Write

```text
I = integral eta.(Omega.grad w),
J = integral eta.(w.grad Omega).
```

Periodic integration by parts, self-adjointness of curl, and
`div Omega=0` give the exact cancellation

```text
2 I = integral sum_(i,j,k,l)
        w_i epsilon_ijk (partial_j Omega_l)(partial_l w_k).
|I| <= (1/2)V2 X Y,       |J| <= V2 X Y.               (845)
```

Indeed, moving curl from w to `Omega.grad w` produces the displayed
commutator plus `integral w.(Omega.grad eta)=-I`. For the bound, fix l:
the contraction in i,j,k is a cross product of w with `partial_l w`.
Its norm is at most `|w| |partial_l w|`. Cauchy--Schwarz in l and space
proves (845), with no separate uncontrolled derivative of eta.

Transport by v+w cancels in the enstrophy integral. Reference stretching
costs at most Splus Y^2. The error's own stretching equals
`integral (w.grad w).Delta w`; the same Agmon/Young estimate used in
(788) bounds it by `nu Z^2/2+kappa Y^6`, where
`kappa=27(26pi)^2/(32nu^3)`. The residual work is at most epsilon1 Y.
Consequently

```text
(1/2)(Y^2)' + (nu/2)Z^2
 <= Splus Y^2 + (3/2)V2 X Y + kappa Y^6 + epsilon1 Y,
Y' <= (Splus-nu/2)Y + (3/2)V2 X + kappa Y^5 + epsilon1. (846)
```

The norm comparison at Y=0 follows by the usual regularization of Y.
The original L2 comparison `X'<=(Sminus-nu)X+epsilon0` is unchanged.
This trades the doubled compression rate in (788) for the stretching
rate, at the price of a larger explicit curvature coefficient. Either
inequality may be better. In particular it is not valid to take Splus
from (846) and retain the smaller curvature coefficient from (788).

### The same dissipation pays the same pressure account

For nonnegative comparison bounds x,y, retain both complete sources:

```text
M(x,y) = min(2Sminus y^2+V2 xy,
             Splus y^2+(3/2)V2 xy) + kappa y^6+epsilon1 y.
E(t) = [Y(0)^2+2 integral_0^t M(x(s),y(s)) ds]/nu.
integral_0^t Z^2 <= E(t).                              (847)
```

Each source is a valid upper bound at the same physical time. Taking their
minimum therefore preserves the bound. Both are increasing in x,y, so
supersolutions can be inserted without choosing incompatible coefficients.
The comparison starts with Y(0)=0 when reference and actual datum coincide.
A test initialized with a nonzero gradient error must retain its Y(0)^2
contribution as well.

Insert this E into (789). All integrals A0,A1,A2, the stochastic trajectory
error, conditional moments I,Q,T and fourth-moment error still inherit
their original values across every seam. No pressure impulse is reset.
`pressure_history_certificate.propagate` accepts the two new physical
comparison callbacks. Its default complete scalar output is exactly
unchanged from the preceding implementation.

On each scalar subinterval, the implementation obtains a supersolution
from either complete linear branch after bounding the nonlinear term by
kappa B^5. It accepts B only if the resulting endpoint and initial value
are both strictly below B. The linear upper expression is monotone or
convex in time, so its maximum is at an endpoint. This closes the
whole-subinterval bootstrap. Scalar subdivisions are powers of two and
cover the same exact time interval. All arithmetic in the pressure account
is rational on the supplied bounds; exponentials and final conversions
are rounded outward as before.

G_ij = sum_planes Re <r_i, W r_j>_plane / m^6,
||sum_j s^j r_j||_W^2 = sum_(i,j) s^(i+j) G_ij.

No cross term or generated mode is removed. The floating reduction order

Here the raw Fourier coefficients are normalized stored dyadics, H is
